Wouldn’t it then be the case that—in systems of the Middle Way which hold that functional things exist by definition, as well—there would be both a belief that the tendency to hold to a self-nature of things was wrapped up with negative thoughts, and a belief that it was not?


[1867]
‘DI LA GSAL BAR BSHAD PA MI SNANG YANG, RANG RGYUD PA DE DAG GIS NYAN RANG LAM DE LTAR SGOM PA LA, CHOS KYI BDAG ‘DZIN MNGON GYUR RE ZHIG SPANGS PA ‘ONG YANG, TSOGS MTHA’ YAS PA BSAGS PA’I GROGS MED PAR CHOS KYI BDAG ‘DZIN GNYIS PO GANG GI YANG SA BON SPANGS PA MI ‘ONG ZHES BZHED DGOS PAS, SHES SGRIB MNGON GYUR BA RE ZHIG LA SPANGS PA NYAN RANG LA SRID KYANG, SA BON SPANGS PA MI SRID PAR SMRA DGOS SO,,

I haven’t observed a clear explanation of this point; but we can say that those who belong to the Independent group would have to agree that—if a person were to meditate in this way upon the paths of the listener or self-made buddha—then they would come to eliminate, for the time being, the manifest form of the tendency to hold to a self-nature to things.  But they would also have to say that—without the additional assistance provided by accumulating unlimited masses of good karma—it is an impossibility that they could ever eliminate the seeds of either one of the two forms of the tendency to grasp to a self-nature of things.  As such, one would have to declare that—even though it was possible for listeners and self-made buddhas to eliminate manifest forms of obstacles to omniscience for the time being—it would be impossible for them to have eliminated the seeds themselves.


[1868]
SLOB DPON ‘DI’I BZHED PAS NI CHOS KYI BDAG ‘DZIN NYON MONGS YIN PAS, DE’I SA BON SPANGS PA LA TSOGS MTHA’ YAS PA GSOG PA’I GROGS MI DGOS LA, GNYIS SNANG ‘KHRUL PA’I BAG CHAGS KYI SHES SGRIB SBYONG BA LA NI, GROGS DE LTA BU MED PAR SBYONG MI NUS PAR BZHED DO,,

The position taken by the current master is that the tendency to grasp to a self-nature to things is a negative emotion; and as such, it is not necessary—if we seek to eliminate the seeds for this tendency—to have the additional help offered by accumulating unlimited masses of good karma.  This master would though say that—if we seek to clean ourselves of obstacles to omniscience in the form of deep seeds causing a mistake in the form of the discrepancy—we could not successfully accomplish this purification without just such additional assistance.


[1869]
SNGAR BSHAD PA DE DAG GI GO BA CHAGS NA KHYAD SHIN TU CHE BAR SNANG BAS BSHAD DO,,

I have taken the time here to go through the explanations you see just up to this point because it seems to me that they can make a very big difference in getting a clear understanding of these points.



The root text on how karma
connects to consequence

[1870]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to the second part we promised above: explaining the words of the root text on these particular points.


[1871]
DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR ‘DOD PA’I PHYOGS LA, KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS MA BLANGS KYANG LAS ‘BRAS KYI ‘BREL PA ‘THAD TSUL JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA,

One may begin with the following question:

Just how is it—in the case of those who assert that there is nothing at all which exists through any nature of its own—that we can we can say that the connection between karma and its consequences is all perfectly acceptable, even without accepting concepts such as foundation consciousness?


[1872]
LAS DANG DE’I ‘BRAS BU’I BAR DU YUN RING POR CHOD PA’I DGE MI DGE’I LAS LAS KYANG, BDE BA DANG SDUG BSNGAL SOGS KYI ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA NI RANG GI SDE PA GONG ‘OG THAMS CAD ‘DOD LA, DE [f. 140b] LA LAS DE ‘BRAS BU ‘BYIN PA’I SNGA LOGS BAR DU GNAS NA NI RTAG PAR ‘GYUR LA, RTAG PAS DON BYED PAR MI NUS PAS LAS LAS ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA’I ‘BREL PA MI ‘THAD DO,,

The fact is that something is going on between an action and the consequences of that action; which is to say—according to all Buddhist schools, be they higher or lower ones—a person can commit a good or bad deed, and then the result of pleasure or pain and the like can come back to them, even in a case where an extended period of time has passed between this karma and its consequence.  But if, in such a circumstance, the karma somehow remains somewhere during the interim—up to the point at which it gives forth its consequence—then that karma would have to be an unchanging entity.  We all know though that an unchanging entity is incapable of performing a function; as such, the supposed connection between karma and its consequences is an untenable concept.


[1873]
LAS DE BYAS PA’I SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR ZHIG NA NI, MTSAMS DE NAS ‘BRAS BU DNGOS SU ‘BYIN PA’I SNGA LOGS KYI BAR DU LAS DE MED LA, LAS ZHIG PA YANG DNGOS POR MED PAS LAS LAS ‘BRAS BU JI LTAR ‘BYUNG BAR ‘GYUR ZHES BRTZAD PA’I

Someone might then come and make the following argument:

And suppose, rather, that this karma—in the second instant of committing it—comes to a stop.  From this juncture, up to the moment before the karma gives forth its consequence, the karma would not have existed.  And a karma which has already stopped could never exist as a functioning thing; how then could the karma give forth its result?


[1874]
LAN DU, LAS BYAS PA’I SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR ‘GAGS ZIN PA’I SNGA LOGS KYI LAS ‘GAG PA LA MNGON DU PHYOGS PA’I TSE, LAS KYI NUS PA GZHAG PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR KHA CIG KUN GZHI RNAM PAR SHES PA RTOG PAR BYED LA, KHA CIG BU LON GYI DBANG RGYA STE DE’I YI GE DANG ‘DRA BA’I LAS GNYIS LAS DON GZHAN PA, CHUD MI ZA BA ZHES PA LDAN MIN ‘DU BYED DU GYUR PA CIG ‘DOD DO,,

In response to this, some people point to the karma which is approaching stopping: that karma just previous to the point at which the karma has stopped, in the second instant of the commission of the karma.  In this moment, they say, there must be a place where the potential of the karma is deposited; and so it is that some people imagine that there must be a type of awareness known as “foundation consciousness.”  And there are also some who say that there is some other entity, distinct from the two karmas, similar to a letter of credit or receipt for a loan; something—a separate changing entity that is neither physical nor mental—which consists of the fact that the karma will never just fade away.


[1875]
KHA CIG NI LAS GNYIS KYI THOB PA ZHES PA DE GNYIS LAS DON GZHAN DU GYUR PA’I LDAN MIN ZHIG RTOG PAR BYED DO,,

Some other people talk about the “retention for the two karmas,” which they imagine to consist of a changing entity which is neither physical nor mental, and which enjoys an existence of its own, apart from the two.


[1876]
KHA CIG NI LAS KYI BAG CHAGS KYIS BSGOS PA’I RNAM SHES KYI RGYUN RTOG PAR BYED LA, DE’I PHYIR LAS ‘GAGS KYANG LAS KYIS PHYIS YUN RING PO NAS ‘BRAS BU ‘BYIN PA MI ‘GAL PAR ‘DOD DE, LAS KYIS KUN GZHI LA BAG CHAGS ‘JOG PAS BAG CHAGS DE LAS KYI ‘BRAS BU YIN LA, DE’I RIGS ‘DRA BRGYUD PAS MTHAR ‘BRAS BU ‘BYIN PAS DANG PO’I LAS KYI ‘BRAS BU BRGYUD PA LAS ‘BYUNG BAR ‘DOD PA’O,,

Others have an idea about a stream of awareness which is imbued by the deep seed of the karma; as such, they say, there is no contradiction incurred by when we say that a karma gives forth a consequence much, much later, even though the karma itself has stopped.  That is, the karma deposits a deep seed in the foundation consciousness; and thus the consequence of the karmic action is that very deep seed.  The stream of similar cases of the gives forth, finally, a result.  And thus, they believe, the consequence of the original karma is produced from the continuation.


[1877]
DE BZHIN DU GZHAN GSUM LA YANG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

And then we can understand the other three cases in a similar way.


[1878]
DE’I DANG PO NI SEMS [f. 141a] TZAM PA ‘GA’ ZHIG GO ,GNYIS PA NI BYE BRAG TU SMRA BA YIN PAR SPYAN RAS GZIGS BRTUL ZHUGS KYIS BSHAD DE, KHA CHE BYE BRAG TU SMRA BA LAS GZHAN PA ZHIG GO ,GSUM PA YANG BYE BRAG TU SMRA BA’I NANG TSAN GCIG GO ,BZHI PA LA GSAL KHA MA BYUNG YANG MDZOD ‘GREL GYI GNAS DGU PA DANG BSTUN NA MDO SDE PA DANG KHA CHE BYE BRAG TU SMRA BA’I YANG ‘DOD PA YIN PA ‘DRA’O,,

The first of these three is a position of a number of followers of the Mind Only school.  The second is described by Master Avalokita Vrata as belonging to members of the Detailist school: “It is a group within the Detailists different from the Kashmiris.”  The third also belongs to a particular group within the Detailist school.  As for the fourth, the case is not exactly clear; but since it accords with the ninth chapter of the autocommentary to the Treasure House of Higher Knowledge, it would seem to be a belief of the Sutrists, in addition to the Kashmiri section within the Detailists.


[1879]
KHA CHE BAS THOB PA KHAS LEN KYANG THOB BYA’I CHOS LAS GNYIS KYIS THOB PA SKYED PAR MI ‘DOD LA ‘DIR NI DE LTAR ‘DOD PA CIG STE GANG GI LTAR NA ZHES PA’I DON NO,,

What this is saying is that “The Kashmiris accept the idea of a retention; but they do not accept that the retention can be created by that which is retained: by the two kinds of karma.  And so we can describe them as ‘having the single belief’—and this then is the reason.”


	[1880]
[VI.39]
Yasmāt svarūpeṇa na tan niruddhaṃ
ciraṃ niruddhād api karmaṇo’taḥ,
Kvacid vinaivālayam asya śakteḥ
phalaṃ samutpadyata ityavaihi.

,GANG PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS DE MI ‘GAG PA,
,DE PHYIR KUN GZHI MED KYANG ‘DI NUS PHYIR,
,LA LAR LAS ‘GAGS YUN RING LON LAS KYANG,
,’BRAS BU YANG DAG ‘BYUNG BAR RIG PAR GYIS,

	For this reason,
	Neither does it stop
	Through any nature
	Of its own.

	As such, it has
The power for this,
Even refusing
A foundation consciousness.

In particular ones,
Karma can stop,
And a very long time
Can pass; but even then,

You should understand,
The exact consequence
Will be given forth.


[1881]
DBU MA THAL ‘GYUR BA GANG GI LTAR NA, LAS RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS MA SKYES PA DE’I LTAR NA NI, GANG GI PHYIR LAS DE RANG BZHIN GYIS TE MI ‘GAG PA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA ‘GAGS PA LAS KYANG ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA MI ‘GAL BA DE’I PHYIR KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS MA BLANGS KYANG, LAS LAS ‘BRAS BU ‘DI ‘BYUNG BAR NUS PA’I PHYIR,

According to those who belong to the Consequence group within the Middle Way school, karma cannot start by itself.  Due to that—for this same reason—neither can it stop through any nature of its own.  But even though it does not stop through any nature of its own, it’s no contradiction to say that a consequence can be given forth by it.  As such, the karma does indeed have the power to give forth this consequence, even if we refuse to accept that there is a foundation consciousness, or anything of the like.


[1882]
SEMS CAN GYI RGYUD LA LAR LAS GNYIS BYAS PA ‘GAGS NAS YUN RING PO BSKAL PA MANG PO LON PA LAS KYANG, LAS LAS ‘BRAS BU YANG DAG PA STE RGYU LA ‘BRAS BU MI ‘KHRUL BAR ‘BYUNG BAR RIG PAR GYIS SHIG ,DE LTAR NA PHYOGS ‘DI LA NI LAS DANG ‘BRAS BU’I ‘BREL PA CHES SHIN TU ‘THAD PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

In the minds of particular living beings then, the two kinds of karma can be committed, and stop; and then a very long time—even many eons—can pass.  But even then, you should understand, the exact consequence will be given forth from the karma: which is to say, the result will come unerringly from its cause.  As such, the whole idea of a connection between karma and its consequences is—in this particular way of thinking—something which is entirely correct.


[1883]
DE RNAMS KYI DON NI SNGAR BZHIN BRTZAD PA’I LAN SMRA BA PO BZHI GAS KYANG, LAS LA SKYE BA DANG ‘GAG PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHAS LEN ZHING, LAS BYAS PA’I ‘OG TU ‘GAGS PA DE RANG [f. 141b] BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR ‘DOD DO,,

The import of all these points is to provide an answer to the arguments presented earlier, as all four presenters here accept the idea that karma can start & stop, by definition; and that when karma stops after we have committed it, this is something which occurs by nature.


[1884]
DE LA SLOB DPON ‘DIS DE ‘DRA BA’I ‘GAGS PA YIN KYANG KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS LEN PAS SKYON MED CES LAN ‘DEBS PA MI RIGS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I TSUL GYIS LAS SKYE BA DANG ‘GAGS PA MED PA’I PHYIR RO ZHES ‘GOG PA YIN NO,,

And what this master is saying here is that it would be wrong to reply, at this point, that—even though it is true that the stopping of the karma is happening the way it was described—nonetheless there is no problem, since we accept concepts such as foundation consciousness and the like.  That is, he is denying that there could exist any such thing as karma starting and stopping in a way where things existed through some nature of their own. 


[1885]
LAN ‘DEBS TSUL DE NYID ‘PHAGS PA’I BZHED PA YIN PAR STON PA LA,
,GANG PHYIR LAS NI SKYE BA MED,
,’DI LTAR RANG BZHIN MED DE’I PHYIR,
,GANG PHYIR DE NI MA SKYES PA,
,DE PHYIR CHUD ZAR MI ‘GYUR RO,
ZHES RTZA SHER GSUNGS PA DRANGS TE, LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA’I PHYIR RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS SKYE BA MED DO,,

In order to show that this exact way of responding reflects the viewpoint of the Realized One, our master at this point cites the following lines from Wisdom:

Karma never starts;
And for this reason,
It has, as we have seen,
No nature of its own.

And for the reason too
That it never started,
It can never be that it
Simply fades away.

What this is saying is that—because there is no such thing as karma which exists through some nature of its own—there is no such thing as karma which starts in and of itself.


[1886]
DE’I PHYIR LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS ‘GAG PA MI SRID PA’I PHYIR, LAS BYAS PA’I ‘OG TU ‘GAGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BZUNG NAS CHUD MI ZA BAR RTOG PA RIGS PA MIN NO, ZHES PA’I DON NO,,

As such—for the reason that it is impossible for karma to come to a stop through some nature of its own—what’s being said here is that it’s illogical to imagine that karma never just fades away, if you are still holding that the stopping of karma subsequent to its commission is something that does exist through some nature of its own.


[1887]
RIGS PA DE NI CHUD MI ZA BA ‘GOG PA LA GSUNGS KYANG GZHAN GSUM ‘GOG PA LA YANG KHYAD PAR MED DE RGYU MTSAN KUN NAS MTSUNGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

With this particular line of reasoning, they refer to “stopping where it doesn’t just fade away”; but the stopping in the case of the other three too isn’t any different—since the reason is exactly the same.


[1888]
YANG MDO LAS,
,MI YI TSE TSAD LO BRGYA STE,
,DE SRID ‘TSO ZHES BRJOD MOD KYI,
,LO LA PHUNG POR SPUNGS PA MED,
,SGRUB PA DE YANG DE DANG MTSUNGS,

,ZAD PA MED CES GANG SMRAS DANG,
,LAS ZAD CES NI GANG SMRAS PA,
,STONG PA’I TSUL DU ZAD PA MED,
,THA SNYAD TSUL DU ZAD PAR BSTAN,

We can quote the following sutra—

The span of a human life
May be a hundred years,
And people may talk about
Staying alive for that long;

But years are not things
That you can pile upon each other;
And doing practice
Is something the same as that.

When it was said that
There was no ending,
And when they said
That karma did end,

It was in the sense of emptiness
That there was no ending;
And in the sense of expression
That things were said to end.


[1889]
ZHES GSUNGS PA DRANGS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I ZAD PA’AM ‘GAG PA MED PA DANG, DE GNYIS THA SNYAD KYI DBANG GIS BZHAG PA’I KHUNGS SO,,

This is a source for saying that there is no such thing as an ending, or a stopping, which could exist through any nature of its own; and for saying that these two are established nominally.


[1890]
NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS,
,LO RNAMS [f. 142a] PHUNG POR SPUNGS PA NI,
,MED PA DE BZHIN YANG DAG PAR,
,TSOGS PA ‘DI YANG BLTA BAR BYA,
ZHES ‘BYUNG NGO,,

Naktso’s translation of the same sutra reads—

There is no such thing
As piling the years
One on top the other;

And a person should view
Any kind of perfect collection
As being the same.


[1891]
DE RNAMS NI RANG BZHIN GYIS TE MI ‘GAG PA ZHES DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA’I STENG NAS BSHAD PA’O,,

When these deny that things could stop through some nature of their own, they are speaking with reference to predicating the object which emptiness is empty of.



A reason not to accept
foundation consciousness

[1892]
GSUM PA LA GNYIS, ‘GAG PA RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PA KUN GZHI KHAS MI LEN PA’I RGYU MTSAN DU ‘GRO TSUL DANG, KUN GZHI KHAS MI LEN KYANG BAG CHAGS KYI GZHI ‘JOG PA’O,,

This brings us to our third step: explaining additional points that the issues we’ve discussed here raise, themselves.  We proceed in two sections—the way in which the fact that the stopping here does not exist through any nature of its own can actually end up serving as a reason not to accept the concept of foundation consciousness; and the how to posit a foundation for deep seeds even if we don’t accept foundation consciousness.


[1893]
DANG PO NI, GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I ‘GAG PA MED KYANG RANG GI LUGS LA YANG LA LAR LAS ‘GAGS ZHES DANG, ‘GAGS SHING RANG BZHIN YOD MIN PA’I, ZHES GSUNGS PAS, THA SNYAD TSUL DU ZAD PAR BSTAN, ZHES PA LTAR

Here is the first.  One may begin with the following question—

Now in your presentation, you say that even though there is no such thing as the karma stopping through some nature of its own, nonetheless “In particular ones, karma can stop,” and one “which is not something that exists with any nature of its own can stop.”  And thus you have quoted “In the sense of expression, things were said to end.”


[1894]
LAS BYAS PA’I ‘OG TU LAS DE ‘GAGS PA NI ‘DOD DGOS LA, DE’I TSE ‘GAGS PA NI DNGOS POR MED CING LAS ‘BRAS KYI ‘BREL PA’I RTEN DU KUN GZHI SOGS KYANG MI ‘DOD NA,

In the end though you would have to agree that a particular karma ends subsequent to the commission of that karma.  And at that point, the stopping does not exist as an entity; but still you refuse to accept ideas like that of a foundation consciousness which could act as the basis for a connection between the karma and its consequence.


[1895]
LAS ‘GAGS NAS YUN RING DU LON PA LAS, ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA MI ‘THAD PAR BRTZAD PA SON {%SO NA} GNAS PAS, SNGAR GYI LAN DE DAG GIS MI CHOG GO ZHE NA,

As such, our original argument that it would be wrong then to say that a consequence could be put forth a long time after the karma had already stopped remains a valid one.  So too we can say that your replies thus far are not sufficient.


[1896]
SKYON MED DE, GANG PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS DE MI ‘GAG PA, DE PHYIR ZHES PA’I RGYU MTSAN NYID KYIS LAS ZHIG PA’I ZHIG PA LAS PHYIS KYI ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA ‘GRUB PAS LAN ZUR PA MA GSUNGS SO,,

And yet there is no such problem.  Remember, “For the reason that it never stopped through any nature of its own; and for that reason too.”  This is expressing the very reason why we can say that—from the stopping of a karma which has stopped—a later result can be given forth; as such, no further, separate reason is offered.


[1897]
DE YANG DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR ‘DOD PA’I PHYOGS THAMS CAD LA, ZHIG PA DNGOS POR MI RUNG LA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PAR ‘DOD PA’I DBU MA’I PHYOGS LA ZHIG PA DNGOS [f. 142b] POR GRUB PA’I GNAD DO,,

Beyond that—according to the views of all those groups which accept the idea that a functional object could exist through some nature of its own—it would be incorrect to say that the stopping could itself be a functional thing; whereas according to the views of the followers of the Middle Way school, the stopping itself is proved to be a functional thing.  This is the crucial point here.


[1898]
LUGS DANG PO LA NI, MYU GU LTA BU’I DNGOS PO CIG ZHIG PA NA, MYU GU’I CHA SHAS KYI DNGOS PO THAMS CAD NI LOG LA, MYU GU LAS GZHAN PA BUM PA LA SOGS PA’I DNGOS PO GZHAN GANG YANG MA THOB PAS, ZHIG PA DE DNGOS PO GTAN MIN PAR ‘DOD DE, SNGON PO LA SOGS PA SKYE MCHED RE RE BA’I DNGOS PO DANG, BUM PA LA SOGS PA RANG GI CHA SHAS KYI DNGOS PO TSOGS PA GANG YANG ZHIG PA DE’I MTSAN GZHIR MI RUNG BA’I PHYIR DNGOS PO MIN NO SNYAM PA’O,,

According to the first of these two positions, when a functional thing like a sprout comes to an end, all the functional entities which constitute component parts of the sprout are cancelled.  At the same time, no entity other than the sprout—nothing like a water pitcher or the like—is thus actualized; and, as such, they have to say that there cannot be the slightest functional thing left here.  What they are thinking is that there is nothing at all that would be fitting to point to as a classical example of this kind of stopping—neither the functional things represented by the individual doors of sense such as blue or the like; nor functioning things which are conglomerates of their components, as in the case of pitchers or the like.  As such, they would say, the stopping could never itself be a functional thing.


[1899]
LUGS PHYI MA LA NI, DPER NA NYER SBAS KYI PHUNG PO LNGA RE RE BA DANG TSOGS PA GNYIS KA DANG, DE GNYIS LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GCIG NYER SBAS KYI MTSAN GZHIR ‘JOG RGYU MED CING, NYER SBAS KYANG DE GSUM GYI MTSAN GZHIR MI RUNG LA, RANG GI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS NYER SBAS SU BTAGS PA DNGOS PO YIN PAR MI ‘GAL BA BZHIN DU, ZHIG PA YANG ZHIG RGYU’I DNGOS PO DANG, DE DANG RIGS MTHUN PA’I DNGOS PO GANG YANG MTSAN GZHIR MED KYANG, ZHIG RGYU’I DNGOS PO LA BRTEN NAS SKYES PA’I PHYIR DNGOS PO’O,,

Now let’s consider the latter of the two positions.  They would say that—as an illustration—we cannot find any classical example of something that we point to as being Mary, neither in any one of the five individual parts that make her up, or in the combination of these five; nor in any one thing which is essentially distinct from these two.  And they would say that there is no contradiction in saying that Mary as something ascribed to her component parts is itself a functional thing.  Similarly, they would say, there is a stopping which arises based on the entity which is to stop—despite the fact that neither the functional entity to stop, nor any functional entity of the same type as it, can be pointed to as the stopping itself.  As such, they say, we can say that the stopping is itself a functional thing.


[1900]
DE SGRUB PA LA LUNG RIGS GNYIS TSIG GSAL LAS GSUNGS PA’I DANG PO NI,

A Clarification of the Verses presents both scriptural reasoning and logical support which corroborate this position; let’s speak about the first.


[1901]
SA BCU PA LAS, SKYE BA’I RKYEN GYIS RGA SHI ZHES GSUNGS PA STE, SHI BA NI GANG SHI BA’I SEMS CAN DE ZHIG PA YIN LA, DE SKYE BA’I RKYEN GYIS SKYED PAR GSUNGS PA DANG,

Ten Levels speaks of “aging & death, due to the factor of birth.”  Death here refers to the stopping of the living being who dies; and what this is saying is that this happens due to the factor of being born.


[1902]
YANG DE NYID LAS ‘CHI BA YANG BYA BA GNYIS SU NYE BAR GNAS PA YIN TE ‘DU BYED ‘JIG PAR YANG BYED PA DANG, YONGS SU MI SHES PA RGYUN MI ‘CHAD PA’I RGYU YANG ‘BYIN PA’O,

The same teaching describes how “Death consists of the proximity of two conditions: the creation of the destruction of factors; and the failure to shut off the flow of total misunderstanding—these causes will bring it forth.”


[1903]
ZHES ‘CHI BAS BYA BA GNYIS [f. 143a] BYED PAR GSUNGS TE, SHI BA RGYUS BYED PA DANG, SHI BAS MA RIG PA SKYED PAR YANG GSUNGS PAS, ZHIG PA LA SKYED PA’I RGYU YOD PA DANG, ZHIG PAS ‘BRAS BU SKYED NUS PA YIN TE,

What this is saying is that death performs two functions: it’s expressing the idea that death is accomplished by a cause; and that, furthermore, death triggers misunderstanding.  And what this is saying is that there does exist such a thing as a cause which triggers a stopping; and furthermore that a stopping has the ability to trigger a result.


[1904]
‘DI NI RGYUN GYI ZHIG PA YIN YANG SKAD CIG MA DANG PO DUS GNYIS PAR ZHIG PA LA YANG ‘DRA LA, SKAD CIG MA DANG PO DUS GNYIS PAR ZHIG PA’I RGYUR YANG BSTAN NO,,

All this refers to the stopping of a flow; but still we would have to say that the stopping of the first instant in the second instant of time is the same.  It is, at the same time, indicating that this is a cause for the stopping of the first instant at the second point in time.


[1905]
DES NA SEMS CAN SKYES PA DANG SHI BA GNYIS DANG SKAD CIG MA GNYIS PAR MI SDOD PA DANG, SKAD CIG MA GNYIS PAR MA BSDAD PA RNAMS LA DNGOS POR ‘JOG MI ‘JOG DANG, RGYUS SKYED MI SKYED KUN NAS MTSUNGS SO,,

Thus we can say that these questions are all the same: that is, whether we can say that the pair of living beings having taken birth, or dying; and things failing to remain into their second instant; and the failing itself to remain in the second instant—whether we can say that these themselves are functional entities, or not; and whether they have been generated by causes, or not.


[1906]
‘DI LA DGONGS NAS RTZA SHE LAS, DNGOS DANG DNGOS MED ‘DUS BYAS YIN, ZHES DANG,

It’s with these questions in mind that Wisdom includes that line about how “Those things that are actual, and those that are not, are all products.”


[1907]
RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG,
,RGYU ZAD NYID LAS ZHI BA NI,
,ZAD CES BYA BAR DMIGS PA STE,

The Sixty Verses on Reasoning says, as well,

We observe what we call
The wearing out,
Or coming to a rest,

From the simple wearing out
Of the cause.


[1908]
ZHES MYU GU SOGS KYI DNGOS PO DANG, DE ZHIG PA DE’I DNGOS POR MED PA GNYIS KA ‘DUS BYAS DANG, SNUM LTA BU’I RGYU ZAD PA NI MAR ME LTA BU’I ‘BRAS BU ZAD PA’I RGYUR GSUNGS PAS, ‘PHAGS PA’I BZHED PAR GDON MI ZA BAR ‘DOD PAR BYA’O,,

What this is saying is that both entities like sprouts and the like—and the non-entitying of the the same objects, their stopping—are produced things; that the exhaustion of the causes for something, such as the oil in a lamp, is itself a cause for the stopping of the result of something like the lamp.  And beyond any shadow of a doubt, a position taken by the Realized One is a position that we would all have to agree with.


[1909]
SKAD CIG DANG PO DUS GNYIS PAR ZHIG PA NI DNGOS SU DGAG BYA BCAD NAS RTOGS DGOS PAS, DGAG PA NI YIN LA MED DGAG NI MA YIN PAS MA YIN DGAG STE, ZHIG RGYU DE BCAD PA TZAM MIN GYI DE BCAD PA’I DNGOS PO ZHIG ‘PHANGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

The fact that the first instant stops at the point of the second is something we comprehend by cancelling—directly—what the statement denies.  Therefore what we have here is a denial, but not the kind of denial where something is absent; rather, it is a denial of the type where something is not something else.  Which is to say, it is not that we are simply cancelling the thing it is that is coming to an end; rather, a functional entity represented by the cancellation of this thing is, further, being suggested.


[1910]
SGRUB BYED LHAG MA NI RGYAS PAR RTZA SHE’I t’IKKA LAS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

The remaining logical argument in support of this idea is something that you can learn by studying the commentary on Wisdom.


[1911]
‘DI NI LUGS ‘DI’I RIGS PA PHRA LA DON CHE BA CIG TU ‘DUG GO ,,

By the way, this is a logical argument of this school which is very subtle, and very important.



Sesame & petals:
deep seed storage

[1912]
[f. 143b] GNYIS PA NI,

Here then is our second section from above: how to posit a foundation for deep seeds even if we don’t accept foundation consciousness.


[1913]
GAL TE KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KHAS MI LEN KYANG DGE MI DGE’I BAG CHAGS ‘JOG PA DANG, BAG CHAGS DE SMIN PA LAS ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BAR ‘DOD DGOS TE, ‘JUG ‘GREL LAS, THOG MA MED PA’I ‘KHOR BAR DNGOS PO’I BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA YONGS SU SMIN PA, DNGOS PO LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA, ZHES DANG, DE ‘DRA BA GZHAN YANG MANG DU ‘BYUNG BA’I PHYIR RO,,

Even if we don’t accept the idea of a foundation consciousness, we still have to agree that virtuous and non-virtuous deep seeds can be planted; and that as these seeds ripen, they give forth results.  As the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way puts it,

In the cycle of suffering with no beginning, the deep seeds of things have been planted, and have ripened.  And we have had a deep belief in those things…

And we see many other such references as well.


[1914]
DE YANG BAG CHAGS ‘JOG PA’I GZHI MED PAR MI RUNG BAS GZHI DE GANG YIN ZHE NA,

Here though one might ask—

And yet it would be wrong to say that there was no place at all where the deep seeds are planted; what then would that place be, according to you?


[1915]
JI LTAR KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KHAS LEN PA RNAMS KYI LTAR NA, NYON YID KYIS NGA’O SNYAM DU DMIGS PA’I GZHIR GYUR PA’I KUN GZHI RNAM SHES BAG CHAGS KYI GNAS SU ‘DOD PA DE BZHIN DU LUGS ‘DIS KYANG NGA’O SNYAM PA TZAM GYI BLO LHAN SKYES KYI DMIGS PA DE NYID BAG CHAGS SGO BA’I GZHIR BZHED DO,,

In response, we can say that those who accept the idea of a foundation consciousness would assert that there is a foundation consciousness which functions as the place that negative consciousness focuses upon, and thinks, “This is me.”  In the same way, those who follow the present system assert that there is a location that an inborn tendency to think, simply, “me” focuses upon; and that this is the place which is imbued with our deep seeds.


[1916]
‘O NA ‘JUG ‘GREL LAS, SEMS KYI RGYUN BAG CHAGS KYI GZHIR GSUNGS PA JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA,

“Well then,” one may ask, “what about that reference in the autcommentary to Entering the Middle Way, where it says that the flow of the mind is the location for the deep seeds?”


[1917]
NGA TZAM DE NYID SEMS RNAM SHES LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA’I RGYUD YIN PAS, SEMS KYI RGYUD CES KYANG BYA LA, SEMS NYID KYI RIGS ‘DRAL {%’DRA LA} DE’I RGYUD CES PA LTAR NA, DE YANG RES ‘GA’ BA’I BAG CHAGS SGO BA’I GZHIR ‘GYUR RO,,

The simple me is itself the “flow” that we talk about relative to the mind, to consciousness.  This is why we can even talk about “a flow of the mind.”  The mind itself tends to continue on in a series of similar cases; and thus we can speak of its “flow.”  From this point of view, this is what provides a place which is imbued with deep seeds, whose own nature is one of coming and going.


[1918]
MA RIG PA’I BAG CHAGS KYI TSUL NI, ‘JUG ‘GREL LAS,

Here is how the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way describes how the deep seeds of misunderstanding work.


[1919]
GANG GIS SEMS KYI RGYUD ‘GAG {%Teng, correct: ‘BAG} PAR BYED CING SGO BAR BYED LA, RJES SU BGROD PAR BYED PA NI BAG CHAGS TE, NYON MONGS PA’I MUR THUG PA DANG, GOMS PA DANG RTZA BA DANG BAG CHAGS ZHES BYA BA NI RNAM GRANGS DAG GO ,

That thing which functions to infect, or imbue, the flow of the mind—that thing which follows behind it—is the deep seeds.  They continue on as long as our condition of negativity continues; and they are known by many different names: “the habit,” or “the root,” or “deep seeds.”


[1920]
DE NI ZAG PA MED PA’I LAM GYIS [f. 144a] NYON MONGS PA SPANGS SU ZIN KYANG, NYAN THOS DANG RANG SANGS RGYAS KYIS SPANG BAR MI NUS TE, TIL MAR DANG ME TOG LA SOGS PA BSAL DU ZIN KYANG, BUM PA DANG SNAM BU LA SOGS PA RNAMS LA DE {Teng: de dag} DANG PHRAD PAS YON TAN PHRA MO DMIGS PA BZHIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

Now we may have accomplished the elimination of negativity by utilizing the path that is free of impurity; and yet these deep seeds are not something that listeners and self-made buddhas are able to eliminate.  Suppose for example that we have been storing sesame seed, or flower petals, or anything of the like in a clay vase, or a fold of cloth, or such.  We can take the seed or petals out of where we’ve been storing them, but due to the contact that these objects have been sharing with their containers, we can still detect some subtle trace of them in those receptacles.


[1921]
DGE MI DGE’I BAG CHAGS LA SOGS PA’I BAG CHAGS GZHAN LA YANG GZHI GNYIS SU ‘GYUR BA JI LTAR RIGS PAR SBYAR RO,,

You can apply this same sort of thinking to other specifics of deep seeds; for example, to deep seeds of virtue or non-virtue; to where you would have a dual location.


[1922]
‘O NA MTHONG LAM BAR CHAD MED LAM GYI DUS SU DE’I SPANG BYA MTHONG SPANG MED MOD KYANG, SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL YOD DGOS LA,

One might come then with the following thought:

We would have to say that—at the point where we are in the uninterrupted stage within the path of seeing—those deep seeds which are eliminated by the path of seeng are no longer present; nonetheless, those which will be eliminated by the path of habituation would have to still be present, in a dormant state.


[1923]
DE’I TSE YID KYI SHES PA NI GNYIS SNANG ‘KHRUL BA’I BAG CHAGS KYIS MA BSLAD PA’I ZAG MED YIN PAS, DE’I NGO BOR BAG LA NYAL DE GNAS PA MI RIGS LA, DBANG SHES KYANG DE’I RTEN DU MED CING GZUGS KYANG DE’I RTEN DU MI RIGS LA

At this point though, the awareness of our thought is unstained, in the sense that it is not infected by the deep seeds for the error of the discrepancy.  As such, it would be incorrect to say that the seeds were remaining in a dormant state as part & parcel with this awareness.  Neither could there be any sense consciousness which were acting as their basis; and it would be illogical to say that physical form itself were providing the base.


[1924]
KUN GZHI YANG MI ‘DOD PAS DE’I RTEN MED PAR ‘GYUR RO SNYAM NA,

And since, finally, you deny the existence of foundation consciousness, aren’t you saying then that there is in fact no basis at all where the deep seeds can be located?


[1925]
SKYON MED DE DE’I TSE NGA TZAM ZHIG SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL GYI RTEN YIN PA’I PHYIR TE, SPANG GNYEN GZHAN LA YANG DE BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA’O,,

And yet there is no such problem.  At that particular point, the simple “me” is providing the basis for the deep seeds which are to be eliminated by the path of habituation, and are staying at this juncture in a dormant state.  And you can understand the situation with other examples of qualities to be eliminated, and their antidotes, as being the same.


[1926]
LUGS ‘DI’I GANG ZAG GI ‘JOG TSUL THUN MONG MA YIN PA SHES NA NAM MKHA’ DANG RNAM SHES MTHA’ YAS DANG CI YANG MED PA GSUM DU SKYES PA’I ‘PHAGS PA’I RGYUD LA, ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA ZAG MED KYI SEMS MNGON DU GYUR PA NA, ‘JIG RTEN PA’I SEMS GZHAN MED PAS DE RNAMS KYI ‘GRO BA LDOG PAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES PA DANG,

If we can come to an understanding of the unique manner in which this particular system posits the person, then it would appear that our position could no longer be challenged by arguments such as the following.  The first here would be where someone asks us to consider the mind stream of a realized being who has taken birth into one of the three levels of Limitless Space; Limitless Awareness; or Nothing At All.  When a state of mind which transcends the normal world—an unstained state of mind—manifests itself, then since there can be no other, worldly states of mind, their functioning is said to be suspended.


[1927]
SRID RTZER SKYES PA’I ‘PHAGS PA LA [f. 144b] CI YANG MED PA’I SAR GTOGS PA’I ZAG MED KYI SEMS MNGON DU GYUR PA NA, SRID RTZE DANG CI YANG MED PA GNYIS KA’I SAS BSDUS PA’I ‘GRO BA LDOG PAR ‘GYUR TE, ZAG MED KYI SEMS DE’I GNAS NI ‘GRO BA DE GNYIS DANG, MYANG NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA’I ‘GRO BAR MI RUNG BA’I PHYIR RO, ZHES GSUNGS PA’I

Or else we can consider the case where a realized being has taken birth into the level known as Peak of Existence, but they have manifested an unstained state of mind taken in by the level of Nothing At All.  This then blocks any possibility of them passing to a state subsumed by either the Peak of Existence or by Nothing At All, since it would be inappropriate to describe the location of an unstained state of mind as either one of these two types of existence, or as a state of existence within the state of nirvana.


[1928]
RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG MI GNOD PAR MNGON TE, ZAG BCAS DANG ZAG MED KYI SEMS GANG YANG ‘GRO BA DE DAG GI MTSAN GZHIR MA BZHAG KYANG ‘GRO BA BZHAG PAS CHOG PA’I PHYIR RO,,

The reason that these arguments would no longer be a challenge is that—even though there is no state of mind either stained or unstained which we could point to as a typical example for any of these states of existence—we can nonetheless posit such states.


[1929]
PHYOGS SNGA MA’I LUGS NI, LAM MA ZHUGS DANG SLOB PA RNAMS KYI ‘GRO BA’I NGO BO MA SGRIBS LUNG MA BSTAN GYI DBANG DU MDZAD PA’O,,

The previous position here is taken relative to the idea that the content of states of existence for those who are not entered upon a path—and those who are still learning—is neutral karma of the type that does not act as an obstacle.


[1930]
LAN DE DAG KYANG BDAG ‘DRA BAS LUGS CHEN PO RNAMS LA RANG STOBS KYIS BRJOD PAR GA LA NUS, ‘ON KYANG MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYI DGONGS PA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RDZOGS PAR ‘JOG SHES PA’I SHING RTA CHEN PO DAG GI LUGS LA BRTEN NAS SMRAS PA YIN NO,,

As for these responses, how could anyone like me ever display my own capacity to speak to the positions of the great ones?  I have though made my comments here relying upon the system of those magnificent innovators who possess themselves the knowledge of how to set forth, in their entirety, positions which represent the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna.


[1931]
DE RNAMS LA DPAGS NA KUN GZHI SGRUB PA’I RIGS PA LHAG MA RNAMS KYIS KYANG LUGS ‘DI LA MI GNOD PAR MNGON TE, BLO GROS CHE ZHING ZHIB LA RNO BA RNAMS KYIS RTZAD GCAD PAR BYA’O,,

It would seem that we can extrapolate from the points we have covered here what we need to show that remaining arguments in favor of a foundation consciousness in no way challenge the present system; and so those of you who possess a great degree of understanding—a detailed degree, and sharp—can go ahead and dissect those accordingly.



Karma in a dream

[1932]
GNYIS PA NI, SNGAR LAS ‘GAGS PA LAS ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BAR BSHAD PA’I DON DE NYID DPE’I SGO NAS BSHAD PA,

This brings us to the second of our more general topics from above: the presentation of a metaphor to illustrate the point of how a karmic consequence can come from the karma itself having stopped earlier.


	[1933]
[VI.40]
Svapnopalabdhān viṣayān avetya
bodhe’pi mūḍhasya yathaiva saṅgaḥ,
Saṃjāyate tadvad asat svabhāvāt
phalaṃ niruddhād api karmaṇo’sti.

,RMI LAM DMIGS PA’I YUL DAG MTHONG NAS NI,
,SAD KYANG BLUN LA CHAGS PA SKYE ‘GYUR BA,
,DE BZHIN ‘GAGS SHING RANG BZHIN YOD MIN PA’I,
,LAS LAS KYANG NI ‘BRAS BU YOD PA YIN,

		One may see certain objects
		Perceived inside a dream;

		And then foolish people
		Might awake,
		And begin to feel desire.

		Just so,
		A karma which is not
		Something that exists
		With any nature of its own

		Can stop,	
		And there can be
		A consequence from it.


[1934]
RMI LAM NA BUD MED BZANG MO DMIGS PA’I YUL DAG MTHONG NAS NI, DE NAS GNYID SAD KYANG SAD PA’I TSE NA YANG SKYE BO BLUN PO LA DA LTA ‘GAGS SHING MED PA LA DMIGS NAS CHAGS PA DRAG PO SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA

Someone may see certain objects—such as a beautiful woman—that they perceive inside a dream.  And then certain foolish people might wake up, and—even though they have awoken—focus on something that has now already stopped, and is no longer there, and begin to feel intense desire for it.


[1935]
DE BZHIN [f. 145a] DU RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN PA’I LAS ‘GAGS PA LAS KYANG NI, LAS KYI ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA YOD PA YIN NO, ZHES LAS ZHIG PA LAS ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BAR BSTAN NO,,

Just so, it can also happen that a karma which is not something that exists through any nature of its own can stop, and there can be a consequence of that karma which comes forth from it.  What all this is indicating is that a consequence can issue forth from the stopping of a karma.


[1936]
DE’I SHES BYED DU SRID PA ‘PHO BA’I MDO LAS RGYAL PO CHEN PO ‘DI LTA STE DPER NA MI ZHIG NYAL BA’I RMI LAM NA YUL GYI BUD MED BZANG MO DANG LHAN CIG SPYOD PAR RMIS LA, DE NYAL BA LAS SAD NAS YUL GYI BUD MED BZANG MO DRAN NA,

Support for this illustration is found in the sutra entitled Moving Between Lives:

This, great king, is how it is.  Take for example a man who goes to sleep, and then in his dreams he sees something: he dreams that he is enjoying himself with a beautiful woman.  And then, when he wakes from his sleep, he recalls the beautiful woman he had perceived.


[1937]
RGYAL PO CHEN PO ‘DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS, ‘O NA GANG RMI LAM GYI YUL GYI BUD MED BZANG MO DANG LHAN CIG YONGS SU SPYOD PAR RMIS LA, DE NYAL BA LAS SAD NAS YUL GYI BUD MED BZANG MO DRAN PA’I MI DE CI MKHAS PA’I RANG BZHIN CAN YIN NAM,

And what, o great king, do you think on this?  What about this man who was enjoying himself with that beautiful woman who was only an object in a dream?  Who wakes up from his sleep, and can’t stop thinking about this thing in the dream—the beautiful woman.  Would we say that he was, by nature, a person who was wise?


[1938]
GSOL PA BCOM LDAN ‘DAS DA NI MA LAGS TE, DE CI’I SLAD DU ZHE NA, BCOM LDAN ‘DAS RMI LAM GYI BUD MED BZANG MO YANG MA MCHIS SHING, MI DMIGS PA LAGS NA, DE DANG YONGS SU SPYOD PA LTA GA LA MCHIS TE, ‘DI LTAR MI DE NI PHONGS SHING DUB PA’I SKAL BA CAN DU ‘GYUR LAGS SO, ZHES DRANGS PA NI DPE STON PA’O,,

And the king replied,

O Conqueror, this would not be the case.  And why would we say that?  Because, o Conqueror, this beautiful woman in the dream does not even exist; there is no such woman.  And what need then to mention the time spent enjoying her?  The man in this case is just a poor fellow of little fortune, who is exhausting himself.

This then is the section of the sutra which provides us a metaphor for our current question.


[1939]
DE DON DANG SBYOR BA NI, RGYAL PO CHEN PO DE BZHIN DU BYIS PA SO SO’I SKYE BO THOS PA DANG MI LDAN PA YANG MIG GIS GZUGS RNAMS MTHONG NAS YID BDE BAR ‘GYUR BA’I GZUGS RNAMS LA MNGON PAR ZHEN TE, MNGON PAR ZHEN PAR GYUR NAS CHAGS PA SKYED PAR BYED DO,,

And then the sutra relates this metaphor to its referent—

O great king, infants who have no learning are the same.  With their eyes they see certain forms, and then they begin to feel attraction for those forms which are pleasing.  And once the attraction starts, then that incites in them desire.


[1940]
CHAGS NAS ‘DOD CHAGS LAS BYUNG BA DANG, ZHE SDANG LAS BYUNG BA DANG, GTI MUG LAS BYUNG BA’I LUS DANG NGAG DANG YID KYIS MNGON [f. 145b] PAR ‘DU BYED DO,,

Once the desire has begun, then they start to undertake physical, verbal, and mental actions; and these spring from ignorant liking, ignorant disliking, and dark ignorance itself.


[1941]
LAS DE MNGON PAR ‘DU BYAS PAR GYUR NAS ‘GAG GO ,’GAGS PA NA SHAR PHYOGS SU BRTEN TE GNAS PA MA YIN PA NAS, PHYOGS MTSAMS RNAMS SU MA YIN NO ZHES BYA BA’I BAR DANG, ZHES GSUNGS TE

And once they have undertaken these karmas, then those karmas come to a stop.  But once they do stop, it’s not as if they remain somehow over to the east…

From here the citation continues up to: “Neither do the karmas remain in any of the ordinal directions.”


[1942]
THOS PA DANG MI LDAN PA NI DE KHO NA NYID STON PA THOS PA LAS DE NYID RTOGS PA MED PA’O,,

When the sutra mentions “those who have no learning,” what it’s referring to is those who have heard teachings on suchness, but who have failed to realize it.


[1943]
MNGON PAR ZHEN PA NI BDEN ZHEN NO,,

And when it speaks of “attraction,” what this means is an attraction to seeing things as existing in reality.


[1944]
CHAGS PA LAS BYUNG BA’I LAS GSUM LA NI, DGE MI DGE’I LAS GNYIS KA DANG, ZHE SDANG LAS BYUNG BA’I LAS NI MI DGE BA DANG, GTI MUG LAS BYUNG BA LA YANG LAS GNYIS KA GSOG PA YOD DO,,

When the sutra mentions three kinds of karma that come from desire, it is talking about both virtuous and non-virtuous karma [that come from ignorant liking]; about non-virtuous karma that comes from ignorant disliking; and again the fact that we can collect both types of karma, from dark ignorance.


[1945]
LAS BYAS MA THAG TU ‘GAGS PA NI THA SNYAD DU DANG, LHAG MAS NI ‘GAG PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA BKAG GO

When the sutra mentions karma stopping just after its commission, this is meant in a nominal sense.  And then the remainder is denying that the stopping could occur through some essential nature of its own.


[1946]
,DE NAS DUS GZHAN CI TZAM ZHIG NA ‘CHI BA’I DUS DANG TSOD NYE BAR GNAS PA’I TSE, DE DANG SKAL BA ‘DRA BA’I LAS DE’I TSE ‘PHEN BYED ZAD NAS, RNAM PAR SHES PA THA MA ‘GAG PA’I TSE ‘DI LTA STE, DPER NA NYAL NYAL BA LAS SAD PA’I MI’I YUL GYI BUD MED BZANG MO LTA BUR YID LAS DE NYID {%Kangyur: LTA BUR LAS DE YID} LA MNGON DU PHYOGS PAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES GSUNGS TE,

And then,

A certain amount of time passes and the karma stops; and then later comes a point where we are fairly close to the time of death.  At this juncture, the projection of karma of the same likeness is exhausted, and the final moment of consciousness draws to a close.  At this point, it’s similar for example to the point at which that man has woken from his deep sleep, and brings to mind the beautiful woman: the karma too is brought to mind.


[1947]
SKAL BA ‘DRA BA STE PHUNG PO RIGS MTHUN TSE ‘DIR GNAS PA’I LAS ZAD NAS, TSE ‘DI’I RNAM SHES THA MA ‘GAG PA’I TSE, CHAGS LDAN SAD MA THAG TU RMI LAM GYI MDZES MA DRAN TE,

When they speak about “karma of the same likeness” here, what they’re referring to is karma for the continuation of the parts of the person in their same form, over the length of this life.  And then the final moment of this life’s awareness comes to a stop; and at this point it’s similar to where the man with desire first wakes up, and immediately recalls the beautiful woman from the dream. 


[1948]
YID DE LA PHYOGS PA BZHIN DU ‘CHI KHA’I TSE TSE PHYI MAR GANG SMIN PA’I LAS KYI NUS PA SAD PA’I LAS DE LA YID PHYOGS PAR ‘GYUR GYI DRAN PA MIN NO,,

Just as he directs his mind in this manner, at the moment of death we direct our thoughts to the karma that is about to ripen in the life to come: to the karma whose potential is now awakening.  Again, this is a directing of our thoughts, and not actually a remembering, as it was with the dream woman.


[1949]
DE LTAR RNAM PAR SHES PA THA MA ‘GAG CING, SKYE BA’I CHAR GTOGS PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA [f. 146a] DANG PO YANG NA NI LHA DAG GI NANG DU ZHES BYA BA NAS, YANG NA NI YI DVAGS RNAMS SU ‘BYUNG BAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES BYA BA’I BAR DANG, ZHES GSUNGS TE THA MA ‘GAG PA NI TSE ‘DI’I ‘O,,

Thus then “the final moment of awareness comes to a stop”; and we have our first moment of awareness subsumed by our new birth.  This can come, as the sutra puts it, “among the pleasure beings,” on up to, alternately, “among the craving spirits.”  The “final moment” that stops here refers to the final moment of this current life.


[1950]
SKYE BA’I CHAR GTOGS PA’I RNAM SHES DANG PO ‘BYUNG BA LA LHA DAG GI NANG DU ZHES SOGS GSUNGS SHING, BAR SRID ‘GRO BA DRUG PO MIN PAS SKYE SRID KYI RNAM SHES YIN TE,

When they are referring here to the first moment of awareness taken in by our new birth, they mention “among the pleasure beings” and so forth.  What they are talking about here is the awareness of the being at rebirth; since the being during the period between death and rebirth is not technically counted among the six types of rebirth.


[1951]
SKYE ‘CHI GNYIS KYI BAR NA BAR SRID YOD KYANG MA GSUNGS PA MANG BAR SNANG BAS, GTZO BOR SKYE ‘CHI’I DBANG DU BYAS PA’I LAS ‘BRAS BU DANG ‘BREL TSUL GTAN LA DBAB PAR BZHED PA’O,,

That is, there does exist an intermediate being between death and rebirth, but we see many instances in scripture where it is not specifically mentioned.  Which is to say, Lord Buddha primarily wishes here to describe the manner in which karma is connected to its consequences, with reference to the process of death and rebirth.


[1952]
DE NAS RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG PO DE ‘GAGS MA THAG TU GANG LA RNAM PAR SMIN PA MYONG BAR ‘GYUR BAR MNGON PA DE DANG SKAL PA ‘DRA BA’I SEMS KYI RGYUN ‘BYUNG NGO,,

And then “when that first moment of consciousness has stopped, just after that we undergo whatever karmic ripening is meant to manifest for us; and then the mind flows on in matching moments of the same form of consciousness.”


[1953]
RGYAL PO CHEN PO DE LA CHOS GANG YANG ‘JIG RTEN ‘DI NAS ‘JIG RTEN PHA ROL TU ‘PHO BA YANG MED LA, ‘CHI ‘PHO BA DANG SKYE BAR MNGON PA YANG YOD DE, RGYAL PO CHEN PO DE LA GANG RNAM PAR SHES PA THA MA ‘GAGS PA DE NI ‘CHI ‘PHO BA ZHES BYA, GANG RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG PO ‘BYUNG BA DE NI SKYE BA ZHES BYA’O,,

And,

O great king, you should understand that there is no entity at all which moves from this world to the world beyond; and yet, nonetheless, the actions of dying, and moving on, and being reborn can all make their appearance.  The point is, great king, that whatever we say is the stopping of the final moment of awareness—the dying and the moving on—is what we say is the starting of the first moment of awareness: the being born.


[1954]
RGYAL PO CHEN PO RNAM PAR SHES PA THA MA ‘GAGS PA’I TSE YANG GANG DU YANG MI ‘GRO’O,,

When the final moment of awareness, great king, comes to a stop, it’s not as though anything goes on to anywhere.


[1955]
RNAM PAR SHES PA SKYE BA’I CHAR GTOGS PA ‘BYUNG BA’I TSE YANG GANG NAS KYANG ‘ONG BA MED DO,,

And when it happens that we count some point of consciousness as being part of rebirth, it’s not as though something came from somewhere else.


[1956]
DE CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA, RANG BZHIN GYIS DBEN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And why is that?  It’s because these things are totally devoid of any nature of their own.


[1957]
RGYAL PO CHEN PO DE LA RNAM PAR SHES PA THA MA NI RNAM PAR SHES PA THA MAS STONG NGO,,

That is, great king, the final moment of consciousness is empty of being the final moment of consciousness.


[1958]
‘CHI ‘PHO NI ‘CHI ‘PHO BAS STONG NGO,,

And dying and moving on is empty of dying and moving on.


[1959]
LAS NI LAS KYIS STONG NGO,,

And karma is empty of karma.


[1960]
RNAM PAR [f. 146b] SHES PA DANG PO NI RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG POS STONG NGO,,

And the first moment of awareness is empty of the first moment of awareness.


[1961]
SKYE BA NI SKYE BAS STONG LA LAS RNAMS CHUD MI ZA BAR YANG MNGON NO,,

And birth is empty of birth; and yet still we can see the truth that the actions we commit—our karma—never just fades away.


[1962]
ZHES GSUNGS TE SKYE SRID DU NYING MTSAMS SBYAR BA’I SNGON LAS KYI ‘BRAS BU BDE SDUG CIG MYONG BAS, DE MYONG BA’I RNAM SHES KYI RGYUN SKYE SEMS DANG PO LAS SKYE BA DANG, ‘CHI ‘PHO BA DANG SKYE BA THA SNYAD DU YOD LA, DON DAM PAR MED PA DANG

What this is saying is that we are experiencing the combined consequence of pleasure and pain from the karma that was previous to the point where we crossed over into the being at rebirth.  As such, the flow of the awareness which experiences these things is born from the first moment of the mind at rebirth; while the dying, the moving on, and the being reborn all do exist, nominally—but they do not exist in an ultimate sense.


[1963]
DE’I RGYU MTSAN RANG BZHIN GYIS DBEN ZHES PA NI, DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA STE RNAM SHES THA MA SOGS RANG RANG GIS STONG PAR GSUNGS PA LA SBYAR BAR BYA’O,,

And the reason for this last is that they are “totally devoid of any nature of their own.”  In this case the object denied by emptiness is being qualified; and Lord Buddha begins describing the final moment of consciousness and so forth as each being empty of themselves.


[1964]
DE LTAR BSTAN PA NA LAS ‘BRAS YOD PA MIN PAR BZUNG GIS DOGS NAS LAS RNAMS CHUD MI ZA BAR GSUNGS SO,,

Fearing that—if he describes things this way—people will start to hold the idea that the very principles of karma and its consequences do not exist at all, Lord Buddha wraps up by mentioning the fact that “karma never just fades away.”



Overthinking karma

[1965]
GSUM PA LA GNYIS, RNAM SMIN THUG MED DU ‘BYIN PA’I RTZOD PA SPANG BA DANG, KUN GZHI YOD PAR GSUNGS PA’I LUNG DANG ‘GAL BA’I RTZOD PA SPANG BA’O,,

This brings us to our third point from above: disproving any debate that may arise about the previous presentation.  Here we will cover two topics—disproving debate which argues that never-ending ripenings would be given forth; and disproving debate which argues that our position contradicts scriptural statements that a foundation consciousness does exist.


[1966]
DANG PO NI, GAL TE LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA LA RANG BZHIN GYIS ZAD PA MED PAS RNAM SMIN ‘BYUNG BAR ‘DOD NA DE BZHIN DU RNAM PAR SMIN ZIN PA LAS KYANG YANG RNAM PAR SMIN PAR ‘GYUR BA’I PHYIR THUG PA MED PA’I SKYON DU ‘GYUR RO SNYAM NA,

Here is the first.  Suppose the following thought occurs to someone:

If we accept the idea that a karmic ripening which cannot end through any nature of its own has arisen—again, not through any nature of its own—then similarly we would have to say that, after it has finished ripening, it would have to ripen once again.  And then there arises the problem that it would have to keep happening like that, endlessly.


	[1967]
[VI.41]
Tulye’pyasattve viṣayasya yadvat
keśākṛtiṃ taimirikaḥ paraiti,
Na sarva bhāvākṛtim ityavaihi
tathā vipakvān na punar vipākam.

,JI LTAR YUL NI YOD NYID MIN MTSUNGS KYANG,
,RAB RIB CAN GYIS SKRA SHAD RNAM PAR NI,
,MTHONG GI DNGOS GZHAN RNAM PAR MA YIN LTAR,
,DE BZHIN SMIN LAS SLAR SMIN MIN SHES KYIS {%GYIS},

		It’s also like objects
		Equivalent in the way
		They’re not really there;

		Those with cataracts
		Are sure they see
		Strands of hair,

		But other things
		That we don’t even see.

		Similarly,
		You should understand
		That it’s not as if
		What has ripened
		Will ripen once again.
		

[1968]
JI LTAR TE DPER NA YUL NI YOD PA NYID MIN PAR MTSUNGS BZHIN DU, RAB RIB CAN GYI MIG GIS YOD PA MIN PA’I SKRA SHAD LA SOGS PA’I RNAM PAR NI MTHONG GI ,DE LAS GZHAN PA’I DNGOS PO’I RNAM PA BONG BU’I RVA DANG, MO GSHAM GYI BU LA SOGS PA’I RNAM PAR MTHONG BA MA YIN PA LTAR,

It’s like, for example, how specific objects might be equivalent in the way that they are not really there.  Eyes affected by cataracts are sure they see strands of hair or the like which don’t even exist; but there are other appearances of things that we don’t even see—things like the horns on a rabbit’s head, or the child of a barren woman.


[1969]
DE BZHIN DU LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MIN PAR MTSUNGS [f. 147a] BZHIN DU, SMIN MA ZIN PA LAS SMIN PA DANG, SMIN ZIN PA LAS SLAR YANG SMIN PA MIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG

Similarly, karma is equivalent in that it is not something which can exist through any nature of its own.  You should understand that—when the karma has not yet ripened—it can go on to ripen; but it’s not as if karma which has already ripened is going to go ahead and ripen once again.


[1970]
,DPE ‘DI LAS LAS RNAMS KYI ‘BRAS BU NGES PAR ‘GRUB PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, DGE MI DGE’I LAS LAS YID DU ‘ONG MI ‘ONG GI ‘BRAS BU YANG SO SOR NGES SO ZHES BSHAD PA,

This example serves not only to inform us about how consequences come, with certainty, from karma.  Rather, we also hear about how either pleasant or unpleasant consequences respectively come, with certainty, from virtuous and non-virtuous karma.


	[1971]
[VI.42]
Ato hi kṛṣṇād aśubho vipākaḥ
śubhād vipākaḥ śubha eva dṛṣṭaḥ,
Śubhāśubhābhāvadhiyaś ca mokṣaś
cintāniṣedhaḥ phala karmaṇāṃ ca.

,DE PHYIR RNAM SMIN MI DGE NAG PO’I LAS,
,RNAM SMIN DGE NYID DGE LAS YIN MTHONG ZHING,
,DGE MI DGE MED BLO CAN THAR ‘GYUR TE,
,LAS ‘BRAS RNAMS LA SEMS PA’ANG DGAG PA MDZAD,

		As such, we can see
		That a non-virtuous ripening
		Is black karma,

		While that virtuous ripening
		Is from a good deed.

		And also intelligent ones
		Who understand
		There exists no virtue
		Nor non-virtue
		Come to be freed.

		And they undertake
		To prevent overthinking
		Karma & its consequences.


[1972]
RAB RIB CAN GYI MIG GIS SKRA SHAD SOGS MTHONG BA DANG, BONG BU’I RVA LA SOGS PA MI MTHONG BA’I NGES PA DE’I PHYIR RNAM SMIN YID DU ‘ONG BA NI MI DGE BA LAS MI ‘BYUNG LA, RNAM SMIN YID DU MI ‘ONG BA NI DGE BA LAS MA YIN PA’I PHYIR, RNAM SMIN MI DGE BA STE YID DU MI ‘ONG BA NI, NAG PO’I LAS LAS YIN LA, RNAM SMIN DGE BA STE YID DU ‘ONG BA NI DGE BA LAS ‘BYUNG BA YIN PAR MTHONG ZHING,

Eyes affected by cataracts see things like strands of hair; but it is definite that they do not see things like horns on top of the head of a rabbit.  As such, it is not the case that a pleasant ripening of karma can come from a non-virtuous deed; and neither can an unpleasant ripening come from a virtuous deed.  We can see then that a non-virtuous ripening—an unpleasant one—is something that comes from a black karma; while a virtuous ripening—a pleasant one—is something that comes from a good deed.


[1973]
DGE BA DANG MI DGE BA’I LAS MED PA’I BLO CAN TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MI DMIGS PAR RTOGS PA NI ‘KHOR BA LAS THAR BAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And also, those intelligent ones who understand that there exists no virtuous karma, nor non-virtuous karma—that is, those who realize that it is an impossibility for karma to exist through any nature of its own—come to be freed from the cycle of suffering.


[1974]
DE’I PHYIR RGYAL BAS SO SO SKYE BO LAS KYI KHYAD PAR ‘DI DANG ‘DI LAS ‘BRAS BU’I KHYAD PAR ‘DI DANG ‘DI ‘BYUNG BA’I RGYU MTSAN ‘THAD SGRUB KYI RIGS PAS ZHIB PAR NGES PAR DPYOD PAR BYED PA RNAMS LA, LAS DANG ‘BRAS BU LA SKUR PA BTAB PA LAS KUN RDZOB ‘JIG PAR ‘GYUR DU ‘ONG SNYAM STE, LAS RNAMS KYI ‘BRAS BU RNAM PAR SMIN PA NI BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB BO, ZHES LAS DANG ‘BRAS BU RNAMS LA BRTEN PA’I SEMS PA STE DPYAD PA’ANG DGAG PAR MDZAD DO,,

And so the Victors have undertaken to prove the correctness of karma to common beings, with reasons such as “You will get this or that particular kind of consequence from committing this or that particular karma”; for they know that, on a conventional level, it will be the destruction of these individuals if they discount the laws of karma & its consequences.  And so they undertake to prevent these types of people from overthinking things—from overanalyzing them—with regard to the laws of karma & its consequences; they tell them, “Oh, the way that consequences ripen from karma is simply inconceivable.”


[1975]
GZHUNG ‘DIR DE ‘DRA BA’I SGO MANG PO NAS LAS ‘BRAS KYI NGES PA STOR DU DOGS NAS [f. 147b] SGO DU MA NAS LAS ‘BRAS KYI NGES PA SKYED THABS MDZAD PA ‘DI SHES PAR GYIS LA, STONG PA NYID KYI LTA BAS KYANG DE’I NGES PA BRTAN PA’I GROGS BYAS PA’I STENG NAS, DA RES RIN PO CHE’I GLING DU PHYIN PA STONG LOG TU MI ‘GRO BA LA ‘BAD PAR BYOS SHIG

We have to understand then how—in this classic—the author has a fear that, in many different ways, his readers might react by having their certainty about the laws of karma & its consequences shattered; and so he undertakes different methods to inspire in them this confidence in karma & consequences.  And he sees moreover that a correct view of emptiness acts as an aid in making this confidence even more firm.  I urge you then not on this occasion to labor in a journey to the Isle of Jewels, only to return empty-handed.



An intent of self-correction

[1976]
,GNYIS PA LA GSUM, LUNG ‘GAL SPONG BA’I TSIG DON DNGOS, YID SHES LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I KUN GZHI BSHAD MA BSHAD KYI TSUL, DGONGS PA’I DBANG GIS GSUNGS PA’I DPE BSTAN PA’O,,

This brings us to the second topic here—disproving debate which argues that our position contradicts scriptural statements that a foundation consciousness does exist.  We cover this in three different steps: a presentation of the actual meaning of the wording which denies that we contradict scripture; the way in which a foundation consciousness essentially separate from consciousness of the thought is either explained, or not explained; and the presentation of a metaphor to demonstrate that statements in this regard were only figurative.


[1977]
DANG PO NI, GAL TE DA {%DE} LTAR KUN GZHI MED KYANG LAS ‘BRAS KYI ‘BREL PA RNAM PAR ‘JOG NUS NA, ‘O NA LANG KAR GSHEGS PA DANG, LA SOGS PAS DGONGS ‘GREL DANG, THEG PA CHEN PO’I CHOS MNGON PA’I MDO LAS, KUN GZHI RNAM PAR SHES PA ZHES PA,

As for the first, one may begin with the following question:

Suppose it is, as you have described, the case that—even in the absence of a foundation consciousness—we can still posit a connection between karma and its consequences.  But then what about mentions of foundation consciousness in A Journey to Langka and “the rest”—a reference to What I Really Meant, and the classic text upon higher knowledge according to the higher way?


[1978]
DNGOS PO’I CHOS MTHA’ DAG PA’I NUS PA’I KHYAD PAR GYI GZHI SA BON THAMS CAD PA, RGYA MTSO LAS RLABS RNAMS ‘BYUNG BA LTAR, PHYI NANG GI DNGOS PO THAMS CAD SKYE BA’I RGYUR GSUNGS PA DE, RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU DE’I RNAM GZHAG ‘JOG PA MED ZHIG GAM ZHE NA,

In those places, this consciousness is described as a foundation which includes within it all of the mental seeds there are—a foundation which is responsible for all the different potential of each & every functioning entity there is.  It is said to be the cause behind the birth of each & every functional thing, whether outside of us or within—just as the ocean itself is where all waves rise from.  Is it then the case that we can in no manner at all posit such a thing?


[1979]
DE LTAR NI MA YIN TE, DE SKAD DU KUN GZHI YOD PAR BSTAN PAS ‘DUL BA RNAMS LA DE YOD PA NYID DU BSTAN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

In reply we can say that this is not the case; when works like this thus describe the existence of a foundation consciousness, it’s only that this presentation is being made to certain disciples.


[1980]
‘DIS NI DGOS PA’I DBANG GIS KUN GZHI GDUL BYA’I NGOR KHAS LEN PAR BSTAN PAS, RANG GI LUGS LA DGONGS PA CAN DU STON PA NA,

What this is meant to indicate is that the presentation where we seem to accept a foundation consciousness is only something made to certain disciples, with a specific special purpose in mind.  And what this means is that—according to what is actually our own position—this description is in fact figurative.


[1981]
GANG LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS PA’I DGONGS GZHI NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA’I STONG PA NYID KHO NA LA DGONGS NAS, KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KYI SGRAS BSTAN PAR RIG PAR BYA’O,,

What is it our real intention to say, when we make such references?  What we only ever intend to refer to with these statements is emptiness: the fact that existence is devoid of anything that could exist through some nature of its own.  You should understand then that we are only using the expression “foundation consciousness” to say this very thing.


[1982]
[f. 148a] DE LA KUN GZHIR GSUNG BA NI, RANG BZHIN DE NI DNGOS PO THAMS CAD KYI RJES SU ZHUGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And why do we use here this specific wording, calling it “foundation” consciousness?  The point is that this nature follows upon each & every entity that exists.


[1983]
DGOS PA’I DBANG GIS KUN GZHI RNAM SHES YOD PAR STON PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, GANG ZAG KYANG RDZAS SU YOD PAR STON TE, DES ‘DUL BA’I SKYE BO LA DE YOD PAR BSTAN PAS RJES SU ‘DZIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And it’s not just foundation consciousness which is, figuratively, taught to exist.  There is also a teaching which says that the person can exist substantially; but only as a stratagem to attract disciples who might respond to such a presentation.


[1984]
JI SKAD DU DGE SLONG DAG PHUNG PO LNGA NI KHUR RO, ,KHUR ‘KHUR BA NI GANG ZAG GO ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

This presentation is reflected is reflected in statements from scripture such as:

O monks, the five parts to a person are the load.
And the one who carries this load is the person.


[1985]
‘DI NI GANG ZAG RANG RKYA THUB PA’I RDZAS YOD DU ‘DZIN PA RNAMS KYIS ZHUS PA’I NGOR DE MED PAR MA BSTAN PAR KHUR ‘KHUR BA’I GANG ZAG YOD PAR GSUNGS PAS, TSIG LA DNGOS SU MED KYANG DON NI RDZAS YOD DO,,

This statement that there does exist a person who carries that particular load was presented to disciples who had requested a teaching and who were holding that there is a person who exists substantially, in a self-standing way.  As such, even though it is not included in the actual wording, the meaning is meant to refer to substantial existence.


[1986]
YANG GDUL BYA KHA CIG LA NI GANG ZAG RDZAS SU MED PA’I PHUNG PO TZAM ZHIG BSTAN PAR MDZAD DE, SEMS ZHES BYA BA’AM, YID CES BYA BA’AM, RNAM PAR SHES PA ZHES BYA BA DE NI DUS RING POR DAD PA DANG TSUL KHRIMS LA SOGS PAS YONGS SU BSGOS SHING, GONG DU ‘GRO BA NA PHYI MA LA MTHO RIS SU ‘GRO BAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES BSHAD PA’O,,

Lord Buddha also taught, to a certain number of disciples, the person as being only a collection of the parts to a person—but parts that did not exist substantially.  That is, he spoke about how what we call “the mind,” or what we call “the thoughts,” or else “consciousness,” has over a long period of time become completely imbued with attributes such as faith and ethical behavior.  And then this has led to the fact that the person moved up, and in their future lifetime came to the higher rebirths.


[1987]
‘DI YANG MTHO RIS DANG BYANG GROL DU ‘GRO BA’I TSUL LA BDEN PAR ‘DZIN PA CAN RNAMS, JI TZAM ZHIG KHAS BLANG BAR BYA SNYAM PA LA, DE’I BDEN ZHEN GYIS YUL MA BKAG PAR PHUNG PO TZAM ZHIG YIN PAR BSTAN PA NA PHUNG PO BDEN PAR DON GYIS STON PA’O,,

This presentation was made for those who held that things existed in truth, as a method for travelling to the higher rebirths and liberation.  It incorporates an estimation of what they are able to accept; and so the person is described as being simply the parts to a person, without any refutation being made—at this point—about the objects that these students believe to exist in truth.  By implication, then, the teaching is saying that the parts to the person exist in truth.


[1988]
‘DI DAG THAMS CAD NI DGONGS PA’I DBANG GIS GSUNGS PA YIN NO,,

The fact though is that all these types of statements were made only figuratively.


	[1989]
[VI.43]
Evaṃ hi gambhīratarān padārthān
na vetti yas taṃ prati deśaneyam,
Astyālayaḥ pudgala eva cāsti
skandhā ime vā khalu kevalāś ca.

,KUN GZHI YOD CING GANG ZAG NYID YOD LA,
,PHUNG PO ‘DI DAG ‘BA’ ZHIG NYID YOD CES,
,BSTAN PA ‘DI NI DE LTAR CHES ZAB DON,
,RIG PAR MI ‘GYUR GANG YIN DE LA’O,,

	Statements as thus—
That there does exist
	One of the foundation,

	And there does exist
	A very essence of the person

	Which is only
	In and of these parts
	To the person—

	Were for those particular
	Ones who could not comprehend
	Extraordinarily deep points.


[1990]
‘DIR GDUL BYA GANG LA DGONGS TE GSUNGS PA YIN ZHE NA,

One might ask, at this point, “What particular disciples did Lord Buddha have in mind, when he made these kinds of statements?”


[1991]
DE’I LAN BRJOD PAR BYA STE, KUN GZHI RNAM [f. 148b] SHES YOD CING GANG ZAG NYID RDZAS SU YOD LA, PHUNG PO ‘DI DAG ‘BA’ ZHIG STE DE TZAM NYID BDEN PAR YOD CES BSTAN PA ‘DI NI, SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR TE DE LTA BU’I CHES ZAB PA’I DON RE ZHIG RIG PA STE RTOGS PAR MI ‘GYUR BA’I GDUL BYA GANG YIN PA DE LA DGONGS TE GSUNGS SO,,

And then the verse here is a response to this inquiry.  Let’s consider this teaching, where Lord Buddha states that there does exist a foundation consciousness—and that the very essence of the person themselves is to exist substantially; where he says that the person is contained in and of these parts to the person: only just that, existing in truth.  What’s being said in our lines here is that the statement as we read it thus above here was made intended for those particular disciples who could not, for the time being, comprehend or realize the extraordinarily deep points of these matters.


[1992]
GDUL BYA GANG DAG YUN RING POR MU STEGS KYI LTA BA LA GOMS PAR BYAS PAS CHOS NYID ZAB MO LA ‘JUG PAR MI NUS SHING, RIN CHEN ‘PHRENG BA LAS,
,BDAG YOD MA YIN YOD MI ‘GYUR,
,BDAG GI YOD MIN MI ‘GYUR ZHES,
,BYIS PA DAG NI DE LTAR SKRAG

Those disciples who have become accustomed to the viewpoints of the River Schools over a long period of time find themselves unable to enter into the profound presentation of suchness.  And then we also have those lines from The String of Precious Jewels, where it says—

	There is no self,
	And there will be no self.

	There is nothing of the self,
	And neither will there be.

	Those who are infants
	Are terrified of these facts.


[1993]
,CES GSUNGS PA LTAR CHOS NYID THOG MAR BSTAN PA NA SKRAG NAS, SANGS RGYAS KYI BSTAN PA LA G-YANG SA DANG ‘DRA BAR SEMS PA DE DAG BSTAN PA LA RGYAB KYIS PHYOGS SHING MI ‘JUG PAS DON CHEN PO SGRUB PAR MI ‘GYUR RO,,

As this is pointing out, people will be terrified if—from the very beginning—we teach them the true nature of things.  They will perceive the teachings of the Buddha as if they were a high cliff that a person might fall from.  And then they turn away from those teachings, and refuse to enter into them.  As such there is no great meaning thus served.


[1994]
DE RNAMS LA CHES THOG MAR ZAB MO’I GNAS MTHAR THUG PA MA BSTAN PAR KUN GZHI RNAM SHES DANG, PHUNG PO BDEN PA SOGS BSTAN PAS NI DE LA BRTEN NAS MU STEGS KYI LUGS BSAL NAS,

If though from the very beginning we avoid teaching such people those most profound points—the ultimate points; and instead impart to them teachings about things like foundation consciousness, or parts to the person that exist in reality, they will be able to utilize these lessons to clear their minds of the systems of the River Schools.


[1995]
DE DAG GI DON CHEN PO ‘DREN PAR ‘GYUR ZHING PHYI NAS GSUNG RAB KYI DON LEGS PAR RIG PA RNAMS RANG NYID KYIS KUN GZHI LA SOGS PA YOD PAR ‘DZIN PA SPONG BAR ‘GYUR BAS, DE LTAR BSTAN PA LA YON TAN KHO NA ‘BYUNG GI SKYON NI MA YIN NO,,

By doing so, we lead them to a place of great meaning; and then later on they come to a good understanding of the meaning of the high words of the Buddha.  And then they are able—by themselves—to give up these types of viewpoints where, for example, they hold that there exists a foundation consciousness.  As such, only good things happen if we start out teaching them as we’ve described it here; and nothing untoward.


[1996]
RIM PA DE LTAR BYA BA LA DGONGS NAS BRGYA PA LAS,
,GANG ZHIG GANG GANG LA DGA’ BA,
,DE YI DE DE SNGAR SPYAD BYA,
,NYAMS PAR GYUR PA DAM CHOS KYI,
,SNOD NI CIS KYANG MA YIN NO,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

The 400 Verses has this graduated approach in mind when it says,

Let people start out doing
Whatever it is that they
Might first be attracted to;

When it fails them,
Why then wouldn’t they
Become worthy vessels
For the highest teachings of all?


[1997]
TSOGS DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I KUN [f. 149a] GZHI BSTAN DGOS PA LA NI, PHYI ROL DGAG DGOS PAS GZUNG ‘DZIN RDZAS GZHAN GYIS STONG PA’I DE KHO NA NYID TZAM ZHIG GI SNOD DU RUNG LA,

Now to serve what purpose do we teach people that there is a foundation consciousness which is essentially separate from the collection of six different kinds of consciousness?  Our goal is to deny outside objects; and there are certain people who are worthy vessels only for the idea of suchness in the form of things being empty of any situation where the objects held by consciousness—and the consciousness which holds to them—could ever be such that to be one was not to be the other.


[1998]
SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KHAS MA BLANGS KYANG, LAS ‘BRAS KYI ‘BREL PA ‘JOG SHES PA MIN PAS, CHES ZAB PA’I DON RIG PAR MI ‘GYUR BA LA GSUNGS PA YIN NO,,

That is, this is a teaching which is presented to those who will not be able to understand the very most profound presentation; since—as we described the situation above—they cannot grasp how to posit a connection between karma & its consequences if they do not accept a foundation consciousness.



On foundation consciousness, or not

[1999]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second step from above: the way in which a foundation consciousness essentially separate from consciousness of the thought is either explained, or not explained.


[2000]
SHER PHYIN ‘BUM PA SOGS MANG POR RNAM SHES KYI GRANGS STON PA NA, RNAM SHES TSOGS DRUG BSHAD KYI DE LAS MANG BA MA BSHAD PA’I MDO SDE DU MA ZHIG YOD PAS, MDO SDE LAS KUN GZHI RNAM SHES BZHAG MA BZHAG GI TSUL GNYIS BKA’ STZAL PA BZHIN DU,

In many sources such as the Perfection of Wisdom in 100,000 Lines, when they present the number of different types of consciousness, they describe only the collection of six different kinds of consciousness—and say nothing about there being more kinds than that.  There are many teachings in the collection of sutras like this; and so we can say that Lord Buddha described two different systems in the sutras here: one where he did describe a foundation consciousness, and one where he did not.


[2001]
RJE BTZUN BYAMS PAS KYANG DE DAG GI DON RNAM PAR ‘GREL BA NA, DBUS MTHA’ DANG MDO SDE RGYAN DANG, CHOS NYID RNAM ‘BYED DU KUN GZHI RNAM PAR BZHAG PA DANG PHYI ROL MED PA’I PHYOGS BSHAD LA, MNGON RTOGS RGYAN DANG, RGYUD BLA MA LAS KUN GZHI RNAM SHES RNAM PAR MA BZHAG PA DANG PHYI ROL MA BKAG PA’I PHYOGS BSHAD DO,,

And it was similar when the high & holy Loving One, Maitreya, commented upon these matters.  In Distinguishing between the Middle and the Extremes, and in the Jewel of the Sutras, and Distinguishing Things from the Very Nature of Things, he set forth the idea of a foundation consciousness, and described the position that there are no outer objects.  In the Jewel of Realizations and The Higher Line though, he did not set forth any foundation consciousness; and described a position which did not deny outer objects.


[2002]
SLOB DPON CHEN PO THOGS MED KYIS KYANG RGYUD BLA MA’I DGONGS PA RNAM RIG TZAM GYI LUGS SU YE MA BSHAD PAR, DBU MA’I LUGS SU BSHAD LA,

Neither did the great master Asanga say anything about the true intent of The Higher Line being the system of those who say it is all just awareness; rather, he glossed it as presenting the system of the Middle Way school.


[2003]
THEG BSDUS SU KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KYI SGRUB BYED DU DRANGS PA’I CHOS MNGON PA’I LUNG, RGYUD BLA MA’I ‘GREL PA LAS, SEMS CAN LA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA’I KHAMS GRUB PA SNYING POR GYUR PA YOD MOD KYI, SEMS CAN DE DAG GIS SHES PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

In A Compendium of the Greater Way, we do see citations from teachings on higher knowledge used in support of the idea of foundation consciousness.  And in the commentary to The Higher Line we read:

It is said that, admittedly, living beings do possess what is the essence of attainment, the element of the Ones Gone Thus; but it is not something that they are even aware of.


[2004]
[f. 149b] DE SKAD DU,
,THOG MA MED PA’I DUS KYI KHAMS,
,CHOS RNAMS KUN GYI GNAS YIN TE,
,DE YOD PAS NA ‘GRO KUN DANG,
,MYA NGAN ‘DAS PA’ANG THOB PA YIN, 
ZHES SEMS CAN LA CHOS NYID KYI RIGS YOD PA’I SGRUB BYED DU DRANGS PAS,

We also see the following lines quoted in support of the idea that living beings do possess the nature of the very essence of all things:

It is an element
That has been there
For time with no beginning;

It is a place
Of all the things there are;

Because it is here,
We have all the different
Types of beings,

And can attain nirvana
As well.


[2005]
SLOB DPON ‘DIS KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KYI DGONGS GZHI STONG NYID DU BSHAD PA DANG MTHUN PA’I PHYIR, TSOGS DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I KUN GZHI GDUL BYA ‘GA’ ZHIG GI NGOR, DGOS PA’I DBANG GIS GSUNGS PAR BZHED DO,,

This master explains the intent behind foundation consciousness as referring to emptiness; as such, it is his position that a foundation consciousness essentially separate from the collection of six types of consciousness was taught to a certain number of disciples, but intended only in a figurative sense.


[2006]
‘O NA BYANG CHUB SEMS ‘GREL DU,

“Well then,” you may ask.  “How do you interpret then the following statement from A Commentary on the Wish for Enlightenment which describes how it is foundation consciousness which takes us to another existence?”


	[2007]
,JI LTAR KHAB LONG DANG NYE BAS,
,LCAGS NI MYUR DU YONGS SU ‘KHOR,
,DE LA SEMS NI YOD MIN TE,
,SEMS DANG LDAN BZHIN SNANG BAR ‘GYUR,

The needle of a compass
Set close to a lodestone
Will quickly turn to face it;
Even though it has no mind,
It would seem as though it did.


	[2008]
,DE BZHIN KUN GZHI RNAM SHES NI,
,BDEN MIN BDEN PA BZHIN DU NI,
,GANG TSE ‘GRO ‘ONG G-YO BAR ‘GYUR,
,DE TSE SRID PA ‘DZIN PAR BYED,

Foundation consciousness
Is just the same;

Even though it is not real,
It seems as if it’s real,
As it shifts with coming & going,

And at that time it acts
For us to take existence.


	[2009]
,JI LTAR RGYA MTSO LA NI SHING,
,SEMS NI MED KYANG G-YO BAR ‘GYUR,
,DE BZHIN KUN GZHI RNAM SHES NI,
,LUS LA BRTEN NAS G-YO BA YIN,
ZHES KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KYIS SRID PA ‘DZIN PAR GSUNGS PA JI LTAR DRANG ZHE NA,

The ocean, and a tree,
May not have a mind,
But still they make to move.

Foundation consciousness
Is the same, as it shifts
All based on the body.


[2010]
DE NI SEMS LAS DON GZHAN PA’I PHYI ROL BKAG NAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA BKAG PA’I SEMS TZAM GSUNGS PA NI, BYIS PA THAMS CAD STONG PAR BSTAN PA LA SKRAG PA SPANG BA’I PHYIR YIN GYI, NGES DON GYI DE NYID MIN PA DANG,

Let’s consider this statement, where we talk about a way in which things are mind only, in the sense of denying that there could exist external objects that were not part & parcel with the mind itself.  This description is made only with the intention of avoiding any panic that infants might feel when we describe emptiness; it is not though describing a nature of things which is meant to be taken literally.


[2011]
RNAL ‘BYOR SPYOD PA BA RNAMS KYIS GNAS GYUR PA’I SEMS KYI DAG PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CIG, SO SO RANG GIS RIG PA’I SPYOD YUL DU GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS PA BKAG PA’I TSE,

Let’s consider the point at which we deny the position of those who belong to the school of deep practice, as they assert an adventitious purity of the mind which could exist through some nature of its own, and which could serve as the sphere of activity for the state of mind which could perceive itself, in the same moment that it perceives other objects.


[2012]
[f. 150a] SEMS BDEN PA MED NA ‘JIG RTEN SNGA MA NAS ‘DIR ‘ONG BA DANG, ‘DI NAS PHYI MAR ‘GRO BA’I G-YO BA’I BYA BA MI ‘THAD DO SNYAM PA’I RTZOD PA KHONG NA GNAS PA’I LAN DU,

They would say that—if the mind were indeed not something real—then the argument remains, where we consider it incorrect to say then that one could act to shift from the world they were in before, to this one; or to shift from this one to the next one.


[2013]
LCAGS DANG SHING LA SEMS MED KYANG YOD PA LTAR G-YO BA BZHIN DU, KUN GZHI BDEN PAR MED KYANG BDEN PAR YOD PA LTAR ‘GRO ‘ONG GI G-YO BA DANG BCAS PAR SNANG NGO, ZHES STON PA YIN PAS GZHUNG GZHAN NAS BSHAD PA LTAR GYI KUN GZHI RNAM SHES RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHAS LEN PA NI MIN NO,,

And then what’s being indicated here is that—even though foundation consciousness is not something that exists in truth—it can appear to be involved with the shifts of going & coming as if it did exist in truth; it’s just like the way that the iron or a tree could shift here & there, as if they had a mind, despite the fact that they do not.  As such, it is not that in this case a kind of foundation consciousness is—as we see it described in other texts—being accepted as existing by definition.


[2014]
GAL TE KUN GZHI RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR KHAS MI LEN KYANG, TSOGS DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I SGYU MA LTA BU KUN BYANG GI CHOS KUN GYI SA BON THAMS CAD PA KHAS LEN NO SNYAM NA,

Which may lead one to the following thought—

Even if it is the case that foundation consciousness is not being accepted here as something which could exist by definition, don’t we still accept it as something that is essentially separate from the combination of six kinds of consciousness; as being like an illusion; and as the combination of all the seeds there are?


[2015]
DE ‘DRA BA’I KUN GZHI KHAS LEN NA KUN GZHI’I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS GZUGS SGRA SOGS SU SNANG BA TZAM DU ZAD KYI, PHYI ROL GYI DON MED PAR KHAS BLANG DGOS NA, DE NYID LAS,

If we were to accept a foundation consciousness like the one you have described, then we would have to agree to the idea that there exist no outer objects; we would have to say that things like visible form, and sounds, were nothing but phantoms appearing out of the ripening of deep seeds inside of foundation consciousness.  And then it would be as the same work describes it:


	[2016]
,SHES PAS SHES BYA RTOGS PA STE,
,SHES BYA MED PAR SHES PA MED,
,DE LTA NA NI RIG BYA DANG,
,RIG BYED MED CES CIS MI ‘DOD,

	Awareness perceives
	Something to be aware of;
	If there is nothing
	To be aware of, then
	There is no awareness.

	As such, why would anyone
	Disagree with the idea
	That there is nothing
	To be known, and
	Nothing to know it?


[2017]
