,CES PHYI’I SHES BYA DANG NANG GI SHES PA GNYIS YOD MED MTSUNGS PAS GCIG MED NA CIG SHOS MED PAR GSUNGS LA,

What this is saying is that outer objects to be aware of, and the inner awareness of these objects, are equal in that either they both exist, or they both don’t exist.  If one is absent, then the other is absent.


[2018]
‘DI NI GZHUNG ‘DIR DON SHES GNYIS DON DAM DU MED MNYAM DANG THA SNYAD DU YOD MNYAM YIN PAS, BDEN GNYIS GANG DU YANG DE GNYIS LA YOD MED KYI KHYAD PAR ‘BYED PA MI ‘THAD PAR GSUNGS PA DANG KHYAD MED PAS NA, PHYI ROL MED PA’I SHES PA YOD PA SLOB DPON GYI BZHED PA MIN NO,,

This point in the context of the current work is that object and awareness are equivalent in not existing in any ultimate way; and they are equivalent in existing nominally.  This is no different than the statement that—whichever of the two realities we are talking about—it would be incorrect to draw a distinction between them, as to whether they exist or do not.  As such, it is not something that the Master would accept to say that there could be an awareness devoid of an outer world.


[2019]
DE’I PHYIR YID KYI SHES [f. 150b] PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I KUN GZHI MI BZHED PAS KUN GZHI ZHES GSUNGS PA NI, SPYIR SEMS RIG CING GSAL TZAM LA KUN GZHIR BZHAG PA DANG, KHYAD PAR DU YID KYI SHES PA LA YIN TE,

As such, neither would he agree to the idea of a foundation consciousness which was essentially separate from the awareness of the thought.  And so when we use the expression “foundation,” we can say in general that the mind itself—this simple knowing and clearness—is itself the foundation; and, more particularly, the awareness of our thoughts is.


[2020]
SEMS SPYI TZAM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA’I LAN DU, SEMS BDEN PAR MED PA LA BYA BYED RUNG BA’I TSUL YIN PA’I PHYIR DANG, SRID PAR SKYE BA ‘DZIN PA’I SEMS YID SHES YIN PA’I PHYIR DANG, YID KYI SHES PA NI KUN NAS NYON MONGS DANG RNAM BYANG THAMS CAD KYI GZHI YIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

That is, as we reply by denying that the mind in general could exist through any nature of its own, we are describing a way in which all the workings of things is something completely consistent with the idea of a mind which cannot exist in truth; and where the mind that takes a new birth in the cycle of pain is our awareness of our thoughts; and how our awareness of our thoughts is the foundation of everything there is, in both the side of life which is entirely negative, and the side which is totally enlightened.


[2021]
DBU MA SNYING POR YANG KUN GZHI SGRA JI BZHIN PA BKAG LA, SLOB DPON YE SHES SNYING PO YANG, PHYI ROL BZHED PAS KUN GZHI MI BZHED DO,,

In Heart of the Middle Way, a foundation consciousness which is taken literally is denied; Master Jnanagarbha too accepts the idea of outer objects, and thus does not accept the concept of a foundation consciousness.


[2022]
PHYI ROL GYI DON ‘GOG PA’I SEMS TZAM PA LA YANG KUN GZHI RNAM SHES ‘DOD MI ‘DOD GNYIS SNANG LA, PHYI ROL GYI DON MI BZHED PA’I SLOB DPON K’A MA LA SH’I LAS KYANG, YID KYI BLO KHO NA NI SKYE BA GZHAN DANG NYING MTSAMS SBYOR BA’I NUS PA CAN YIN NO,,

Even among those of the Mind Only school who deny outer objects, there appear to be two groups: those who accept the idea of a foundation consciousness, and those who do not.  Even Master Kamalashila, who denies the existence of outer objects, says that the mind in the sense of thought itself is an entity which possesses the capacity to take us over the border to a next life.


[2023]
JI SKAD DU YANG,
,CHAD DANG MTSAMS SBYOR ‘DOD CHAGS BRAL,
,NYAMS DANG ‘CHI ‘PHO SKYE BA NI,
,YID KYI RNAM SHES KHO NAR ‘DOD,
CES MDZOD LAS GSUNGS PA DRANGS PAS, SLOB DPON CHEN PO ZHI ‘TSO YANG KUN GZHI RNAM SHES MI BZHED PAR GSAL LO,,

It is evident as well that the great master Shanta Rakshita denies the concept of a foundation consciousness, as he quotes the following lines from The Treasure House:

Severing, reconnecting,
Freedom from desire,
Degenerating,
Dying and moving on,

And rebirth too
Are accepted as being
Only consciousness
Of the thought.


[2024]
AA BHY’A {%BHA Y’A} KA RA YANG DE DANG ‘DRA’O,,

Master Abhayakara’s position is the same.


[2025]
THEG PA CHEN PO’I GSUNG RAB GZHAN DU KUN GZHI RNAM SHES ZHES GSUNGS PA YANG, MING TZAM MA RTOGS PA NGOS ‘DZIN GSAL BAR MI SNANG LA, DON LA DPYAD PA TSOGS DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA MI BZHED PA KHO NAR SNANG ZHING, LUGS DE YANG PHYI ROL KHAS [f. 151a] LEN PA’I PHYOGS SU SNANG BAS YID KYI RNAM SHES LA MING DE LTAR BTAGS PA’O,,

In other works of the greater way, we do see the expression “foundation consciousness” used; but except for the name itself, there doesn’t appear to be any clear identification of what this refers to.  In actual fact as well, all we do see are refusals to accept the position that there could exist a consciousness by this name which was essentially distinct from the collection of six types of consciousness.  These systems too would appear to be ones in which outer objects were accepted; as such, the expression “foundation consciousness” itself would appear to be just something applied to the consciousness of the thought.


[2026]
‘DI RNAMS RGYAS PAR GTAN LA ‘BEBS DGOS MOD KYANG MANGS PAS ‘JIGS NAS MA BRIS SO,,

We really should pause here to nail down these points in detail; but I have not written more here because I fear that our work would then go on too long!



Just like me & mine

[2027]
GSUM PA NI,

Which brings us to our third step here: the presentation of a metaphor to demonstrate that statements in regard to foundation consciousness were only figurative.


	[2028]
[VI.44]
Ahaṃ mametyeva yathā dideśa
satkāya dṛṣṭer vigame’pi Buddhaḥ,
Tathā’svabhāvān api sarva bhāvān
astīti neyārthatayā dideśa.

‘JIG TSOGS LTA DANG BRAL YANG
SANGS RGYAS KYIS,
,JI LTAR NGA DANG NGA YI BSTAN PA LTAR,
,DE BZHIN DNGOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN MED MOD KYI,
,YOD CES DRANG DON NYID DU BSTAN PA YIN,

	It’s like how
The Buddha is free
	From the view
	Of the destructible collection,

	But did still give teachings
	Using “me” and “mine.”

	This is a similar case:
	Things admittedly have
No nature of their own,

And yet only
In a figurative sense
It was stated
That things did exist.


[2029]
GDUL BYA GZHUG PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR DANG PO KUN GZHI RNAM SHES LA SOGS PA BSTAN PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, ‘ON KYANG JI LTAR TE DPER NA ’JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA DANG BRAL BAS, 

Concepts like foundation consciousness are presented at first only for the purpose of inducing disciples to enter the teachings.  But in the end it’s like, for example, the case with the point at which we free ourselves from the view of the destructible collection, along with the deep seeds for this view.


[2030]
NGA DANG NGA YIR ‘DZIN PA’I RTOG PA THAMS CAD SPANGS KYANG, NGA DANG NGA YI ZHES BSNYAD PA ‘JIG RTEN GYIS CHOS KYI DON KHONG DU CHUD PA’I THABS YIN PA’I PHYIR,

That is, at this point we have been able to eliminate all of those ideas where we hold to a “me,” or to a “mine.”  But speaking still of “me” or “mine”—using these terms—can be employed as a means of helping people of the everyday world to begin to grasp the meaning of the teachings.


[2031]
SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS NGA DANG NGA YI ZHES JI SKAD BSTAN PA DE BZHIN DU, DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED MOD KYI STE KYANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD CES DRANG DON NYID DU BSTAN PA NI, ‘JIG RTEN GYI RIM GYIS DE KHO NA NYID KHONG DU CHUD PA’I THABS YIN NO,,

As such, the Conqueror—the Buddha—did give teachings using the expressions “me” and “mine.”  It’s a similar case with the way in which things admittedly have no manner of existing though some nature of their own, and yet only in a figurative sense it was stated that things did exist through just such a nature.  It was only meant as a stratagem for getting those of the world to begin to grasp, very gradually, the way things really are.


[2032]
BSDU NA NGA ZHES PA DANG NGA YI’O ZHES GSUNG PA LTAR NA, DE DANG DE’I RTOG PA YOD PA LTAR SNANG NA’ANG, RTOG PA MED PA NGES DON YIN PA 

To sum then, it’s similar to when statements were made about “me” or “mine”—and the idea we had about them felt as though they referred to something real.  But the actual case was that these ideas never applied to anything real at all.


[2033]
BZHIN DU CHOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR STON PA DE SANGS RGYAS KYI DGONGS PA LTAR SNANG YANG CHOS RNAMS DE LTAR MED PA DE NGES PA’I DON NO ZHES PA’O,,

In the same way, it would appear that Lord Buddha’s intention was to indicate that things existed through some nature of their own; but what he really meant to say was that things didn’t exist that way at all.


[2034]
THA SNYAD KYI RNAM GZHAG ‘JIG RTEN DANG MTHUN PAR ‘JUG TSUL YANG SHAR GYI RI BO’I SDE PA DANG MTHUN PA’I TSIGS SU BCAD PA LAS

This idea, of applying terms in a way which fits the way in which the world uses them, is described for example at length in the following verses, which are written in keeping with the position of those who belong to East Mountain Group:


	[2035]
,GAL TE ‘JIG RTEN RNAM ‘DREN RNAMS,
,’JIG RTEN MTHUN PAR MI ‘JUG NA,
,SANGS RGYAS CHOS NYID [f. 151b] GANG YIN DANG,
,SANGS RGYAS SUS KYANG SHES MI ‘GYUR,

If that Ultimate Guide of the World
Were not to try to fit the world,

It would be a sign that none of the Buddhas
Really understood the teachings
That the Buddhas themselves have taught.


	[2036]
,PHUNG PO DAG DANG KHAMS RNAMS DANG,
,SKYE MCHED RANG BZHIN GCIG BZHED LA,
,KHAMS GSUM PO DAG STON MDZAD PA,
,’DI NI ‘JIG RTEN MTHUN ‘JUG YIN,

They teach the position
That the parts to the person,

And the categories and
The doors of sense
All have a single nature;

And when they undertake
To teach the three realms,

They do it in keeping
With the way of the world.


	[2037]
,MING MED PA YI CHOS KYI RNAMS,
,BSAM PA MED PAS MING DAG GIS,
,SEMS CAN RNAMS LA YONGS BRJOD PA,
,’DI NI ‘JIG RTEN MTHUN ‘JUG YIN,

The nature of all things
Devoid of names, as they are,
Is beyond all thought;

And so using names
To describe them to
The people of the world

Is only in keeping
With the way of the world.


	[2038]
,DNGOS MED NYE BAR STON MDZAD CING,
,SANGS RGYAS RANG BZHIN LA BZHUGS PAS,
,DNGOS MED ‘GA’ YANG ‘DIR MED PA,
,’DI NI ‘JIG RTEN MTHUN ‘JUG YIN,

They undertake to teach
Things that have no reality,
And the Buddhas reside
In a nature to things;

But there is nothing here
With no reality;
It is only in keeping
With the way of the world.


	[2039]
,DON DANG DON MED MI GZIGS LA,
,’GOG PA DANG NI DAM PA’I DON,
,SMRA BA RNAMS KYI MCHOG GSUNG BA,
,’DI NI ‘JIG RTEN MTHUN ‘JUG YIN,

They see neither that
Which is actually there,
Nor that which is not.

Everything that the highest
Of all the teachers there is
Ever said about stopping
And the highest thing of all

Is only in keeping
With the way of the world.


	[2040]
,ZHIG PA MED CING SKYE MED LA,
,CHOS KYI DBYINGS DANG MNYAM GYUR KYANG,
,SREG PA’I BSKAL PA STON MDZAD PA,
,’DI NI ‘JIG RTEN MTHUN ‘JUG YIN,

The fact that nothing stops
And nothing starts
Is all in keeping with
The empty realm of things;

And yet they give teachings
About the eon of fire—
Only in keeping
With the way of the world.


	[2041]
,DUS GSUM DAG TU SEMS CAN GYI,
,RANG BZHIN DMIGS PA MA YIN LA,
,SEMS CAN KHAMS KYANG STON MDZAD PA,
,’DI NI ‘JIG RTEN MTHUN ‘JUG YIN,
ZHES RGYA CHER GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

No nature of a living being
Ever existed
In the past, or present, or future;

And yet they undertake
To teach about
Some quality of beings—

It is all only in keeping
With the way of the world.


[2042]
DE RNAMS KYI SHLO KA THA MAS SEMS CAN RANG BZHIN MED PA’I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED DANG, LHAG MA RNAMS KYIS DNGOS PO DANG DNGOS MED KYI CHOS RANG BZHIN MED PA’I CHOS KYI BDAG MED BSTAN LA,

The last of the verses we’ve given here is referring to the fact that the person has no nature of being itself: the fact that beings have no nature of their own.   The rest of the verses are saying that neither entities which perform a function, nor those which do not, have any nature of their own; that is, they are referring to the fact that things have no nature of their own.


[2043]
SHAR RI’I SDE PA NI DGE ‘DUN PHAL CHEN PA LAS RIM GYIS GYES PA YIN PAR RTOG GE ‘BAR BA LAS BSHAD PAS NA, NYAN THOS KYI SDE SNOD DU CHOS RANG BZHIN MED PA SHIN TU GSAL BAR STON PA CIG YOD PAR SNANG NGO,,

Now the Blaze of Reasoning explains that the East Mountain Group, over time, split off from the Majority Group; as such, it seems to me that there actually is a party in the listener section of the teachings where they teach, quite explicitly, the lack of a self-nature to things.



Mind Only on the sixth level

[2044]
[f. 152a] GNYIS PA SEMS TZAM PA’I LUGS BYE BRAG TU DGAG PA LA GSUM, PHYI ROL MED PA’I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG ,GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I SGRUB BYED TSAD MA DGAG ,SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA’I TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI DON ‘GOG PA MIN PAR BSTAN PA’O,,

This brings us, at last, to the second section in showing how we disprove the position that things can grow from something other than themselves; that is, a more specific denial of this point by the Mind Only school.  Here we have three parts: a denial that the understanding that there are no outer objects could ever exist through some nature of its own; denying the accurate perception which is supposed to prove that dominated things exist through some nature of their own; and a demonstration that the word “only” in the expression “Mind Only” is not meant to deny outer objects.


[2045]
DANG PO LA GNYIS, GZHAN LUGS BRJOD PA DANG, LUGS DE DGAG PA’O,,

The first of these parts has two points of its own: describing the position that others take, and then denying that position.


	[2046]
[VI.45]
Prajñā vihārī sa hi bodhisattvo
vijñāna mātra pratividdha tattvaḥ,
Grāhyaṃ vinā grāhakatām apaśyan
vijñāna mātraṃ tribhavaṃ paraiti.

,GZUNG BA MED PAR ‘DZIN PA MA MTHONG ZHING,
,SRID GSUM RNAM SHES TZAM DU RAB RTOGS PAS,
,SHES RAB LA GNAS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ DES,
,RNAM SHES TZAM DU DE NYID RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR,

	They see there are no
	Objects of perception;

	And they see none
	Which act to hold
	To these—

		They come to a deep
		Realization that all three
		Realms of existence
		Are only consciousness itself.

		A bodhisattva who
		Is staying in wisdom
		Comes to a realization

		Of that real nature of things:
		That they are only consciousness.
		

[2047]
DANG PO NI, RNAM PAR SHES PA SMRA BA DBU MA PA’I LUGS JI SKAD BSTAN PA MI BZOD CING, RGYAL BA’I DGONGS PA MIN PAS, RANG GI RNAM RTOG GIS SBYAR BA’I LUGS BRJOD PA’I SGO NAS DON ‘JOG PAR BYED PA RNAMS KYIS, RANG GI GZHUNG LAS JI SKAD DU BSHAD PA’I LUGS GSAL BAR BYA BA’I PHYIR PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRAS PA,

Here is the first.  Those who assert that everything is consciousness cannot bear the position that those of the Middle Way describe, and say that it is not what the Victors really mean.  Rather, these people seek to establish how things actually are by expressing a position which is just a creation of their own imagination.  And so in an attempt to clarify the system presented in their own classical texts, they begin with the following opening statement.


[2048]
SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA LHAG PA LA GNAS PA STE BZHUGS NAS DE NYID SGOM PAR BYED PA’I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ SA DRUG PA BA DES, RIGS PA GANG GIS DE KHO NA NYID PHYIN CI MA LOG PA DANG, GZUNG ‘DZIN RDZAS THA DAD DU LHAG PAR SGRO MA BTAGS PAR RTOGS PA DANG MTHONG BA DANG, KHONG DU CHUD PA NI DE NYID RTOGS PA STE, RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM DU DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR ZHES RNAM PAR SBYAR RO,,

Let’s consider first then a bodhisattva who is at the sixth bodhisattva level, who is staying in—that is, who has entered—a very special form of the perfection of wisdom, and is undertaking to meditate upon the way things really are.  There is a reasoning that they employ to come to an unmistaken realization of suchness, and to overcome every tendency to exaggerate things wildly by holding that objects of awareness—and the forms of awareness which hold to them—could ever be such that to be one was not to be the other.  To see these truths, and to truly embody them, they come to a realization of that real nature of things, that they are only consciousness.  


[2049]
DE YANG PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS MED PAS SEMS DANG SEMS BYUNG RNAMS KYANG PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS TE DON MED PAR RTEN ‘BYUNG GI DNGOS PO TZAM DU RTOGS PA’I PHYIR, RNAM SHES TZAM DU DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA ZHES BYA’O,,

And so they would say that we must come to realize that—since there is no outer physical form—mind and mental functions in turn have no objects, no physical form on the outside.  That is, we must realize that they are nothing more than creations of dependence.  And so it is that they speak of “realizing the way things really are, as being nothing more than awareness.”


[2050]
YANG JI LTAR BYANG SEMS ‘DIS DE KHO NA NYID DE LTAR RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR ZHE NA,

And how is it, then, that this bodhisattva comes to perceive the real nature of things as being this way?


[2051]
GANG GI PHYIR BYANG SEMS [f. 152b] ‘DIS NANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS GZUGS SOGS ‘BYUNG BAR ‘CHAD PAR ‘GYUR BA’I RIGS PAS SEMS LA RANG LAS RDZAS GZHAN GYI GZUNG BA MED PAR DE LAS DON GZHAN PA’I DE ‘DZIN PAR BYED PA MA MTHONG ZHING, SRID PA KHAMS GSUM PO NI RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM MO ZHES RAB TU RTOGS PAS TE NAS,

The bodhisattva utilizes reasoning—which we are about to explain—to understand how physical form and the like come into being through the ripening of deep seeds inside of themselves; which is to say, this logic allows them to understand how there are no objects of perception which are such that to be them is not to be the mind itself.  They see no entities which act to hold to these objects and are separate from them.  And so—which is to say, first—they come to a deep realization that all three realms of existence are only consciousness itself.


[2052]
GNYIS STONG GI DE KHO NA NYID LA YUN RING POR GOMS PAR BYED LA, DE GOMS PA LAS KYANG SGRAS DE KHO NA NYID DU BRJOD DU MED PA’I DNGOS PO STE GNYIS STONG GI NGO PO {%BO} TZAM ZHIG RANG RIG PAS MNGON SUM DU MTHONG STE, DE’I PHYIR SNGON DU GOMS PA’I RIM PA ‘DIS SA DRUG PA BAS RNAM SHES TZAM DU DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And then they undertake to accustom themselves, for a long period of time, to suchness in the form of things being empty of this particular duality.  With that, they use apperception to see, directly, how things are nothing more than this essential nature of being devoid of that duality; that is, they use the familiarity they have developed to see that nature of things which cannot be described, precisely, in words.  And so a bodhisattva at the sixth bodhisattva level—one who has up to this point gone through the stages of accustoming themselves to these concepts—is able to realize the true nature of things: that they are nothing but awareness itself.


	[2053]
[VI.46]
Yathā taraṅgā mahato’mburāśeḥ
samīraṇa preraṇayodbhavanti,
Tathālayākhyād api sarva bījād
vijñāna mātraṃ bhavati svaśakteḥ.

,JI LTAR RLUNG GIS [f. 206b] BSKUL BAS RGYA MTSO NI,
,CHE LAS CHU RLABS ‘BYUNG BA DE BZHIN DU,
,KUN GYI SA BON KUN GZHI ZHES BYA LAS,
,RANG GI NUS PAS RNAM SHES TZAM ZHIG ‘BYUNG,

	It’s like the great ocean,
	Instigated by the winds [f. 206b];

	And from there
	The waves occur.

	Just so do we have
	What we call
	“The all-foundation”

	For the deep seeds
	Of everything;

	And from that arise
	What is nothing more
	Than consciousness,

	Through energies
	Concordant with them.


[2054]
GAL TE ‘DI DAG PHYI ROL MED PA’I RNAM PAR RIG PA TZAM YIN NA, ‘O NA ‘DIR PHYI ROL MED PAR DE’I RNAM PA CAN GYI SEMS TZAM JI LTAR SKYE BAR ‘GYUR ZHE NA,

One might return then with the following question: “Suppose then it is the case that things are nothing more than awareness, and there are no outer objects.  How is it though that the mind alone can grow, in these particular forms?”


[2055]
SMRAS PA JI LTAR TE DPER NA RLABS KYI RTEN DU GYUR PA’I RGYA MTSO CHEN PO NI, RLUNG GIS BSKUL BA STE KUN NAS BSKYOD PA LAS, SNGAR GNYID LOG PA LTA BU’I MI G-YO BAR GNAS PA LAS CHU’I RLABS RNAMS ‘GREN PA’I SGO NAS BDAG GI LUS RNYED PA LTAR, YONGS SU RGYUG PAR RTOGS PA

Here then is our answer.  It’s like, for example, the great ocean, which acts as a basis for the formation of waves.  This ocean is instigated by the winds—it is stirred up by them, completely—and from there it’s like a person who up to this time has been asleep, and is then stirred.  Which is to say, the waves are led forth; the man rediscovers his body; and he perceives himself running here and there throughout the day.


[2056]
DE BZHIN DU PHYI NANG GI DNGOS PO KUN GYI SA BON KUN GZHI RNAM SHES ZHES BYA BA LAS, CHAGS SOGS DANG DAD SOGS ‘GAG BZHIN PAS RANG DANG RJES SU MTHUN PA’I NUS PA KUN GZHI LA BZHAG PA’I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS MA DAG PA’I GZHAN DBANG RNAM SHES TZAM ZHIG ‘BYUNG BA

Just so do we have what we call “foundation consciousness”: the all-foundation for the deep seeds of every inner & outer entity.  From it come forth things like attachment & such; and faith & the like.  As they come to a stop, they leave deep seeds deposited in the foundation consciousness: energies concordant with their various natures.  As these seeds ripen, things which are nothing more than consciousness arise from that: impure forms of dominated entitites.


[2057]
DE NYID LA, BYIS PA RNAMS GZUNG BA DANG ‘DZIN PA PHYI NANG DU RGYANGS CHAD PAR ‘DZIN PA’I TSUL [f. 153a] GYIS RTOG PAR BYED KYI RNAM SHES LAS RDZAS THA DAD PA’I GZUNG BA NI CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MIN NO,,

Infants look upon what is nothing more than this, grasping to objects and subjects, imagining that they are inner & outer entities existing from a distance.  But in actual fact there is not the slightest trace of any object there which is not such that to be it is to be the consciousness itself.


[2058]
‘DI NI DPER NA DBANG PHYUG LA SOGS PA RGYUR SMRA PA RNAMS,
,BA NI BA SGRA RNAMS KYI RGYU,
,CHU SHEL CHU RNAMS KYI BZHIN DANG,
,BLAG SHA YAL GA RNAMS KYI LTAR,
,DE NI LUS CAN KUN GYI RGYU,

To this point, we can take for example statements by those who say that the Lord of Power or such are the cause behind all the things there are:

	Cows are the cause
	Behind the mooing of cows;

	And just so water crystal
	Behind all the kinds of water.

	Trees are behind
	The branches of trees;

	Just so, he is the cause
	Behind every living being.


[2059]
ZHES DBANG PHYUG LA SOGS PA ‘GRO BA’I BYED PA POR SMRA BA BZHIN DU, KUN GZHI RNAM SHES SMRA BA RNAMS KYANG RNAM SHES DMIGS PA’I DNGOS PO MTHA’ DAG GI RTEN NYID KYIS SA BON THAMS CAD PA SMRA BAR BYED DO,,

That is, it’s being asserted that the Lord of Power—or someone like him—was the creator of living beings.  Just so, those who profess a foundation consciousness say that consciousness is the one & only basis of all the entities in existence.  As such, they say that it is the combination of all the deep seeds there are.


[2060]
GANG DBANG PHYUG RTAG LA KUN GZHI RNAM SHES MI RTAG GO ZHES BYA BA ‘DI NI KHYAD PAR RO,,

There is a difference here though, where people say that the Lord of Power is never-changing, while foundation consciousness is ever-changing.


[2061]
DE’I PHYIR TSE RABS GZHAN MANG POR MU STEGS KYI LTA BA GOMS PA RNAMS NI KUN GZHI BSHAD PAS ‘DUL BA YIN NO,,

Thus it is that those who have accustomed themselves to the viewpoints of the River Schools over a long string of many previous lifetimes can be tamed with the description of a foundation consciousness.


[2062]
‘O NA ‘GREL PAR SEMS TZAM PA’I ‘DOD PA BRJOD PA NA, PHYI ROL MED CES PA MANG DU GSUNGS SHING, RNAM PAR SHES PA LAS THA DAD PAR GYUR PA’I GZUNG BA NI CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MIN ZHES,

The following thought may occur to some:

When, in the autocommentary, they describe the beliefs of the Mind Only school, we see the expression “there are no outer objects” repeated frequently.  Or people say, “There is not the slightest object, anywhere, which is separate from consciousness.”


[2063]
GZUGS SOGS KYI GZUNG BA MED PA LA RNAM SHES LAS THA DAD PA’I ZHES KHYAD PAR SMOS PA DANG, DBANG PO GZUGS CAN MIG CES BYA BAR RTOGS ZHES PA’I

That is, when they say that there are no objects of perception, such as form or the rest, they add the qualification “which are things separate from consciousness.”  Or they say things like “we realize that it’s the physical sense power of the eye.”


[2064]
‘GREL PA LAS, RNAM PAR SHES PA LAS THA DAD PA’I MIG GI DBANG PO NI YOD PA MA YIN NO, ZHES DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR SNGAR LTAR SBYAR BA BZHIN 

And then the autocommentary at this point applies a qualification, such as we noted before, to what we deny here: “There is no such thing as a power of the eye which is separate from consciousness.”


[2065]
SEMS TZAM GYI SKABS SU ‘DOD RGYU YIN NAM, ‘ON TE GZUGS SOGS LNGA DANG DBANG PO GZUGS CAN LNGA MED CES KHYAD PAR MA SBYAR BAR KHAS BLANG RGYU YIN SNYAM NA,

And so our question is, are these kinds of statements reflecting ideas that would be accepted in the context of the Mind Only school?  Or are we to accept these ideas without qualifications such as “devoid of form and the rest of the five” or “devoid of the five physical powers”?


[2066]
‘GREL PA [f. 153b] ‘DIR KHYAD PAR SBYAR MA SBYAR GNYIS KA ‘DUG KYANG, SKYE BA ‘GOG PA LA DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA MANG DU BYUNG NA, MA BYUNG BA’I SKABS THAMS CAD DU YANG DE ‘KHYER BA BZHIN DU, ‘DIR YANG DE LTAR BYA STE, ‘DIR PHYOGS SNGA MA BRJOD PA’I GZHUNG THEG BSDUS SU,

In the autocommentary at this point we see both kinds of references: where they make qualifications of this kind, or where they do not.  In the end though it’s like cases where we deny that things can grow: there are many situations where qualifications are added to what we deny; and where such qualifications are not made, we are expected to assume them nonetheless.  We should do the same here; as we see the previous position described in the classic Summary of the Greater Way—


[2067]
CI’I PHYIR LEN PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA ZHES BYA ZHE NA, DBANG PO GZUGS CAN THAMS CAD KYI RGYU YIN PA DANG, LUS THAMS CAD NYE BAR LEN PA’I GNAS SU GYUR PA’I PHYIR TE, ‘DI LTAR TSE JI SRID PAR RJES SU ‘JUG GI BAR DU DES DBANG PO GZUGS CAN LNGA PO DAG MA ZHIG PAR NYE BAR BZUNG BA DANG, ZHES DANG,

And why do we call it “the consciousness taken”?  The point is that it is the cause of all the powers that have form, and it acts as something taken on with all the bodies there are.  That is, it continues on for as long as the person continues to live; and takes on the five physical sense powers until such time as they come to an end.


[2068]
THUN MONG NI SNOD KYI ‘JIG RTEN GYI SA BON GANG YIN PA’O, ,THUN MONG MA YIN PA DE NI SO SO RANG GI SKYE MCHED KYI SA BON GANG YIN PA’O, ,THUN MONG GANG YIN PA DE NI TSOR BA MED PA ‘BYUNG BA’I SA BON NO, 

It is that thing which is the seed for the vessel of the world, that all of us share.  It is that thing which is the seed for those things which are not shared: for the doors of sense of different individuals.  It is the seed for those things which occur that are shared, but which do not exhibit sensation.


[2069]
ZHES KUN GZHI’I STENG GI SNOD KYI ‘JIG RTEN GYI SA BON TSOR BA MED PA’I DNGOS PO’I SA BON DU GSUNGS PA DANG, BSDU BA LAS KYANG DE BZHIN DU GSUNGS SHING,

What this is talking about is seeds for the vessel of the greater world in general; these are being referred to as “seeds for things without sensation.”  The same sorts of statements are found in The Summary.


[2070]
RTEN ‘BREL MDO ‘GREL DU, KUN GZHI RNAMS KYI RKYEN GYIS MING GZUGS ‘GRUB PAR BSHAD PA’I MING PHUNG PO LHAG MA BZHI DANG, GZUGS ‘BYUNG BA ‘BYUNG ‘GYUR GYI GZUGS LA ‘CHAD CING, DE ‘DRA DE GZUGS MED NA MED KYANG KHAMS GZHAN GNYIS NA YOD PAR BSHAD PA SOGS SEMS TZAM GYI LUGS LA GZUGS KHAS LEN PA MTHA’ YAS PA CIG SNANG NGO,,

The commentary to the Sutra on Interdependence speaks of how the factor of foundation consciousness brings about the link of name & form; this latter is explaned as referring to “name” in the sense of the remaining four parts to the person, and to “form” in the sense of form composed either of the elements themselves, or the products of the elements.  This kind of thing is explained as something that does not occur in the formless realm, but which does exist in the other two realms.  It would appear that—with these and other such ideas—there are almost an infinite number of special positions, in the Mind Only school, relating to form.


[2071]
DE LTA MA YIN NA SEMS TZAM GYI SKABS SU GZUGS PHUNG GI STENG NAS, DE LTAR GZUGS SGRA SOGS THA [f. 154a] SNYAD MDZAD PA THAMS CAD LA, GSAR DU MA BCOS PA THA SNYAD BTAGS PA DE NYID KYIS THA SNYAD BYED DU MI RUNG BA KHO NAR ‘GYUR BAR SNANG LA, DE ‘DRA BA’I THA SNYAD BYAR MI RUNG BAR MTHONG YANG DA DUNG GRUB MTHA’ ‘DI LEGS SO ZHES PA NI ‘PHAGS YUL GYI SANGS RGYAS PA SU LA YANG MI SNANG NGO,,

If it were not this way, it would appear that in the context of the Mind Only school we would have the following problem.  That is—in every case where we used the terms “visible form” or “sound”—it would always be inappropriate to apply the terms in this specific way of their not being created fresh.  We can see that it would be inappropriate to apply terms in this way; and yet to continue to insist then that “This is a really great system” is something that we would never see any follower of Buddhism in the Land of the Realized Ones do.


[2072]
SHES BYA NANG GIR SMRA BA ZHES PA’I MING DON KYANG SHES BYA NI GZUGS SGRA SOGS YIN LA, DE PHYI ROL TU MI ‘DOD KYI NANG SHES PA’I DNGOS POR SMRA BA LA ZER BA YIN NO,,

There is a name that is used here: “those who say knowable things are inner.”  The expression “knowable things” in this case refers to objects like visible form and sounds.  And the name is meant to apply to those who deny that these things could be outside of us; who say that, rather, they are entities on the inside, consisting of mind.


[2073]
GAL TE SEMS TZAM PAS GZUGS SGRA SOGS KHAS LEN NA, DE PHYI ROL YIN PA ‘GOG PA MING TZAM LA RTZOD PAR ‘GYUR TE, PHYI ROL TU SNANG BA’I GZUGS SOGS ‘DI NYID LA PHYI ROL TU ‘JOG PA’I PHYIR RO ZHE NA,

One may come then with the following question:

Since those of the Mind Only school accept things like visible form and sound, then if they go and deny that these are outside objects, it’s all just arguing about names.  The fact is that when physical form appears to be on the outside, then that is exactly what allows us to say that it is on the outside.


[2074]
‘DI DANG DBU MA PAS GZUGS SOGS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA BKAG NAS GZUGS SOGS ‘JOG PA LA, RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PAR SNANG BA’I GZUGS SOGS ‘DI NYID RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ‘JOG PA’I PHYIR, DE YOD MED LA RTZOD PA MED LA RTZOD PA’O ZHES PA DANG ‘DRA STE,

This argument would be similar to talking about those who belong to the Middle Way school in the following way:

These thinkers deny that form and the rest could ever exist by definition; but when they do posit the existence of form and the like, they are talking about form and such which appear to exist by definition—and so they must be saying that these things exist in fact by definition.  And so when they debate about whether these things exist this way or not, they are debating, literally, about nothing.


[2075]
GRUB MTHA’ GNYIS KA’I DKA’ GNAS CHEN POR SNANG BAS, DBU MA’I TSUL DKA’ BAR MA ZAD SEMS TZAM PA’I LUGS ‘DI LA YANG, PHYI ROL BKAG NA GZUGS SOGS KYANG MED PAR ‘GRO ZHING, GZUGS SOGS BZHAG NA PHYI ROL YANG BZHAG DGOS PAR MTHONG BAR ‘DUG PA’I PHYIR RO,,

This would appear to be a point of great difficulty in both of these schools of thought; as such, it’s not just that the system of the Middle Way is something difficult—there is also this point in the tradition of the Mind Only.  That is, if we deny the existence of outer objects, then form and the rest would also have to be things that did not exist; whereas if we do posit things such as form and so on, we can see that we would have to posit them as things with an outside existence.


[2076]
‘DI DAG DKA’ MOD KYANG MANGS BAS ‘JIGS NAS MA BRIS SO,,

And so yes, I admit that these are quite difficult points; but I shall not write further on them here, for I fear that my text would go on much too long.


	[2077]
[VI.47]
Saṃvidyate’taḥ paratantra rūpaṃ
 prajñapti sad vastu nibandhanaṃ yat,
Bāhyaṃ vinā grāhyam udeti sac ca
sarva prapañcāviṣaya svarūpam.

[VI.47a]
,DE PHYIR GZHAN GYI DBANG GI NGO BO GANG,
,DNGOS PO BTAGS PAR YOD PA’I RGYUR ‘GYUR ZHING,

	Therefore an essential nature
	To dominated things
	
	Is the cause for things
	Which exist only as
	They are given these names.


[2078]
GANG GI PHYIR GSUNG RAB KYI RNAM PAR BZHAG [f. 154b] PA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA ‘DI YIN PAR GRAGS PA DE’I PHYIR GZHAN GYI DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I NGO BO GANG YIN PA ‘DI NI GDON MI ZA BAR KHAS BLANG BAR BYA STE, GANG GI PHYIR GZUNG ‘DZIN GYI DNGOS PO BTAGS PAR YOD PA STE RDZAS THA DAD DU YOD PAR ‘DZIN PA SOGS KYI RTOG PA’I DRA BA MA LUS PA’I RGYU STE GZHIR ‘GYUR BAR ‘DOD PA’I PHYIR RO,,

The presentation of the teachings we have made then is known to be as we have described it; and therefore the idea that an essential nature to dominated things which exists through some quality of its own is something that—beyond any shadow of a doubt—we must accept.  And why is this the case?  Because we accept the idea that things like objects of perception and the corresponding perceiving subjects exist only as things that are given these names; and that to hold them as being such that to be one is not automatically to be the other is the cause—which is to say, the foundation—of this entire trap of conceptual thought.


[2079]
THAG PA’I RGYU MTSAN CAN GYI SBRUL DU ‘KHRUL BA NI THAG PA MED PA’I GZHIR MI SKYE LA, BUM PA LA SOGS PA’I RGYU MTSAN CAN GYI ‘KHRUL PA NI, SA LA SOGS PA MED PA’I NAM MKHA’I PHYOGS SU SKYE BAR MI ‘GYUR BA BZHIN DU, PHYI ROL GYI DON MED NA SNGON PO LA SOGS PA PHYI ROL TU ‘KHRUL BA’I RTOG PA ‘KHRUL GZHI JI ‘DRA BA ZHIG GI RGYU CAN DU ‘GYUR,

Mistaking a rope as a snake due to the proximity of the rope is not something that ever occurs in a location where there is no rope.  And a perceptual error founded in a water pitcher or the like is not something that would ever arise in the middle of the sky, where there are no elements of earth or the like.  The case here is just the same; that is, if there are no outer objects, then what would be the cause behind a perception which mistakenly took blue or the like as existing on the outside?  How could the circumstances that allowed the error be present?


[2080]
DE’I  PHYIR GDON MI ZA BAR PHYI ROL TU ‘KHRUL BA’I RTOG PA’I RGYU GZUNG ‘DZIN RDZAS THA DAD PA GNYIS SU SNANG BA’I MA DAG GZHAN DBANG KHAS BLANG DGOS TE, SNANG GZHI DE NYID KUN BYANG GI ‘CHING GROL GNYIS KA’I RGYU YIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

As such, we must—beyond the slightest doubt—accept the concept of an impure form of dominated entities, where the objects held and the perceptions holding them do appear to be such that to be one is not to be the other; that is, there must be some basis for the mistaken perception that outer objects exist.  We can even say that the very scenario which appears to us is the exact cause behind the fetters and the freedom, of vast negativity and perfect enlightenment.


[2081]
DBU SEMS GANG GI LUGS KYIS KYANG DE LTA SEMS CAN RNAMS LA SNANG ZHING, SNANG BA LTAR DU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA’I ZHE NA {%ZHEN} GZHI DE, ZHEN YUL DES STONG PAR BSTAN PA CIG YOD NA, STONG NYID DE RTOGS PA LAM DU ‘GRO BA YIN GYI,

It doesn’t matter which system we’re talking about—that of the Middle Way, or that of the Mind Only.  In either case, there is a basis behind our wrong belief: something that appears to living beings to exist in a certain way, and which they subsequently believe to exist in truth, as it appears to.  If there is something that we can point to as being empty of the object that people believe they see, then—and only then—the realization of that sheer absence or emptiness can function as a path.


[2082]
SEMS CAN RANG DGA’ BA RNAMS KYIS BDEN PAR ZHEN PA’I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG BA’I STONG NYID RTOGS PA LAM DU MI BYED PAR STONG PA GZHAN CIG BDEN PAR SGRUB PA NI, THOG MA MED PA NAS ZHUGS PA’I BDEN ZHEN PHRA RAGS GANG GI YANG GNYEN POR MI ‘GRO BAS [f. 155a] NGAL BA ‘BRAS MED DO,,

And suppose we fail to make a path out of coming to a realization of emptiness—an emptiness where we have overthrown that object of belief: the belief of just normal people of the world that things exist in reality.  That is, suppose we take some other kind of emptiness to exist, really.  This could never serve as an antidote for either one of the forms—more subtle, or more coarse—of the belief in something real which has resided in the hearts of beings for time with no beginning.  And as such, the whole exercise would be one in futility.


[2083]
DE LTAR NA GNYIS SU SNANG BA’I GZHAN DBANG GANG LA GZUNG ‘DZIN RDZAS THA DAD PA SNANG BA BZHIN DU, YOD PAR ‘DZIN PA’I ZHEN YUL GYI KUN BRTAGS GANG MED PA DE NI, GZHI DE DGAG BYA DES STONG PAR YANG DAG PAR RJES SU MTHONG LA,

There is then the appearance of duality: that what our perceptions are holding, and the perceptions themselves, are not such that to be one is to be the other.  Just so, there is the fact of the absence of that imaginary thing whose existence we crave for, and hold on to.  And so there comes a day when we are able to see, perfectly, how the vista we are considering is empty of this thing which was never there.


[2084]
STONG GZHI DANG STONG PA GANG ZHIG ‘DIR LHAG MAR LUS PAR GYUR PA DE, ‘DI NA BDEN PAR YOD PA YIN NO, ZHES YANG DAG PA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RAB TU SHES PAS ‘DI NI STONG PA NYID KYI DON KYANG LEGS PAR GZUNG BAR ‘GYUR RO,,

If there is anything left over after you consider what has the emptiness, and the emptiness itself, then—as they say—“here is what exists in truth.”  That is, when we really understand the way things are, perfectly, then we are also grasping, with excellence, what is really meant when we say “emptiness.”


[2085]
‘DIR PHYOGS SNGAR MDZAD PA NI BYANG SA DANG DBUS MTHA’I ‘GREL PA LAS, GANG LA GANG MED PA ZHES SOGS KYI DON SNGAR LTAR BSHAD PA DE YIN LA, RGYUD BLA MA’I ‘GREL PAR GANG ZHIG GANG NA MED PA DE NI ZHES SOGS KYI DON BKRAL BA NI, SNGA MA GNYIS DANG GTAN MI ‘DRA BAR DBU MA’I ‘GREL TSUL DU YOD DE MANGS PAS ‘JIGS NAS MA BRIS SO,,

What I have presented here as the initial position represents what we described earlier, as reflected in the explanation of the wording that we see in both The Levels of the Bodhisattva and in the commentary to Distinguishing Between the Middle & the Extremes: “with what it is that what is missing.”  The way though in which the commentary to The Higher Line reads the phrase “where it is that something is missing” is completely different from that found in these other two.  Which is to say, there are a great number of different ways that the Middle Way explains these things.  Out of a concern though that I would go on too long, I will refrain from speaking more on that point here.


	[2086]
[VI.47b]
,PHYI ROL GZUNG BA MED PAR ‘BYUNG ‘GYUR LA,
,YOD DANG SPROS KUN YUL MIN RANG BZHIN YOD,

	They occur in a lack
	Of outer objects
	Which are grasped;
	
	And they exist,
	And have a nature,

	Never objects of
Any elaboration.


[2087]
GZHAN DBANG DE NI PHYI ROL GYI GZUNG BA MED PAR RANG GI BAG CHAGS KHO NA LAS ‘BYUNG BAR ‘GYUR LA, RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA DANG ‘DI’I LUGS KYI DON DAM PAR SGRA RTOG GI SPROS PA KUN TE THAMS CAD KYI YUL MIN PA’I RANG BZHIN CAN DU YOD DE, PHYI NANG GI MNGON PAR BRJOD PA NI DNGOS SU MA BRTAGS PA’I RNAM PA ‘DZIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Dominated entities lack any outer objects which are grasped; they are things that occur only from their deep seeds.  And they exist through their own nature and—as being ultimate, in this system—they have a nature where they can never be objects of any, of all, elaboration of word & thought.  And so they retain an aspect where they are not direct formulations of outer or inner expression.


[2088]
MDOR NA GZHAN DBANG LA KHYAD PAR GSUM YOD DE, PHYI ROL MED PAR ‘BYUNG BA DANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA DANG, DON DAM PAR SPROS PA YIN NO COG GI YUL MA YIN PA’O,,

To put it briefly, dominated entitities have three different distinct characteristics: they occur without existing on the outside; the exist through a nature of their own; and they exist ultimately, without ever being any of the many different kinds of elaboration there could be.


[2089]
BRTAG PAR YOD PA’I RGYU NI RANG BZHIN GYIS [f. 155b] YOD PA’I DNGOS PO’I KHONGS SU ‘DU BAS DE NI KHYAD PAR GSUM PO LAS THA MI DAD DO,,

Being a cause that exists as a formulation is something that is included into being an entity which exists through its own nature; as such, we don’t list it separately from the three characteristics just mentioned.


[2090]
GZHAN DBANG YOD CES PA NI YOD TZAM MIN GYI YOD PA KHYAD PAR BA YIN TE, SLOB DPON BLO BRTAN GYIS, YANG DAG MA YIN KUN RTOG YOD, CES BYA BA GSUNGS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS ZHES BYA BA TSIG GI LHAG MA’O, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR YIN PAS, KHYAD PAR ‘DI NGES PA ‘OG TU GAL CHE’O,,

When we say that dominated entities exist, we are not just talking about simple existence; rather, this is a special form of existence.  This then is why Master Sthiramati says,

As they say, “It is not pure; it is imaginary”—and there are some additional words to be added here, “through a nature of its own.”

As such, distinguishing this particular feature will be crucial as we go on below.



Denying the dream

[2091]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DGAG PA RGYAS PAR BRJOD PA DANG, DE LTAR BKAG PA’I MJUG BSDU BA’O,,

Here secondly we present a more specific denial of the explanation of this point by the Mind Only school.  This we will do in two parts: an expanded description of our denial; and then a summary of just such a denial.


[2092]
DANG PO LA GSUM, PHYI ROL MED PA’I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I DPE DGAG ,BAG CHAGS KYI NUS PA LAS DON GYIS STONG PA’I SHES PA SKYE BA’I DON DGAG ,DE LTAR BKAG PA DANG MI SDUG PA SGOM PA GNYIS MI ‘GAL BAR BSTAN PA’O,,

The expanded description has three sections of its own: denying a metaphor which is meant to show that awareness where there are no outer objects could exist through some nature of its own; denying the referent of the metaphor in a case where awareness arises from the power of a deep seed, and is empty of the referent; and finally a demonstration that there is no contradiction between this particular denial, and the meditation on the repulsive.


[2093]
DANG PO LA GNYIS, RMI LAM GYI DPE DGAG PA, SKRA SHAD MTHONG BA’I DPE DGAG PA’O,,

The first section comes in two steps of its own: denying the metaphor of a dream; and denying the metaphor of seeing a strand of hair.


[2094]
DANG PO LA GSUM, RMI LAM GYI DPES SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MI ‘GRUB PA, RMI LAM GYI DPES SAD DUS SU PHYI ROL MED PA MI ‘GRUB PA, RMI LAM GYI DPES DNGOS PO THAMS CAD BRDZUN PAR ‘GRUB PA’O,,

And then finally the first of these steps has three points: how it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish that awareness exists through some nature of its own; how it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish the idea that, when we awake, there are no outer objects; and finally establishing—through the metaphor of a dream—that all entities are deceptive.


	[2095]
[VI.48]
Vinaiva bāhyaṃ kva yathāsti cittaṃ
svapne yathā ced idam eva cintyam,
Svapne’pi me naiva hi cittam asti
yadā tadā nāsti nidarśanaṃ te.

,PHYI ROL MED SEMS DPE NI GANG DU YOD,
,RMI LAM JI BZHIN ZHE NA DE BSAM BYA,
,GANG TSE NGA LA RMI LAM NA YANG SEMS,
,YOD MIN DE TSE KHYOD KYI DPE YOD MIN,

		Where then is
		The metaphor for
		A mind where there
		Are no outer objects?

		Suppose you say
		It is the same
		As a dream—
		We need to consider this.

		Suppose that—
		Even just in a dream—
		There’s a mind;

		In ours there is
		No such existence:
		You would have no
		Metaphor that existed.


[2096]
DANG PO NI, SEMS TZAM PA KHYED PHYI ROL MED LA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA’I SEMS YOD PAR ‘DOD NA, DPER NA ‘DI BZHIN ZHES ‘DI’I DPE NI GANG DU YOD CES ‘DI NYID DPYAD PAR BYA’O,,

Here is the first.  Suppose that you proponents of the Mind Only school assert that there are no outer objects; but that there does exist a mind which exists by definition.  In that case, we need to examine this point more closely; we want you to tell us, “It’s like this particular metaphor.”  Where then is the metaphor you think there might be for this?


[2097]
SEMS TZAM PAS SMRAS PA, DPER NA KHANG MIG SHIN TU CHUNG NGU’I NANG DU NYAL ZHING, GNYID KYIS LOG PAS GLANG PO CHE MYOS PA’I KHYU RMIS PA’I GLANG PO CHE NI, KHANG MIG DER JI [f. 156a] LTAR YANG YOD PA MIN TE,

To this, those of the Mind Only school reply—

As a metaphor, we can point to a person who is sleeping in a very small room.  They fall into a deep sleep, and dream about an entire herd of crazed elephants.  The fact is that an elephant like this could never be present in that particular room.


[2098]
DE’I PHYIR RMI LAM JI LTA BA BZHIN DU PHYI ROL GYI YUL MED BZHIN DU, RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA ‘DI NGES PAR KHAS BLANG BAR BYA’O ZHE NA, ‘DI YANG SNYING PO MED PA NYID DU BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA, DPE DE NYID ‘DIR BSAM PA STE DPYAD PAR BYA’O,,

Suppose then you say that the case here is just the same as a dream, where no outer objects exist; and so we must definitely accept the idea that awareness exists through some nature of its own.  Since this is something described to indicate how nothing has any essence of its own, we need to consider this very metaphor here, in our case—we need to examine it.


[2099]
YANG DPYAD PAR BYA BA DE CI ZHIG CE NA, GANG GI TSE RMI LAM NA YANG BA LANG MYOS PA’I KHYU’I RNAM PA CAN GYI SEMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DE NI, YUL GLANG PO CHE MED PA LTAR NGA’I LUGS LA YOD PA MIN TE, MA SKYES PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And how should this examination proceed?  Suppose that—even just in a dream—we have a state of mind that exists by definition, and which is holding the image of a herd of crazed elephants.  Here in our system too there is no such existence; it never started, just as the object mentioned—the elephants—never existed.


[2100]
RNAM SHES RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED NA, DE’I TSE GNYIS KA LA GRUB PA’I KHYED KYI DPE YOD PA MIN PAS, PHYI ROL MED PAR RNAM PAR SHES PA YOD PA MIN NO,,

But suppose that there is no such thing as a consciousness which could exist by definition.  In that case, you would have no metaphor that existed here which was valid for both parties.  And as such, there could be no awareness that existed without outer objects.


[2101]
‘DIR RMI LAM NA SNANG BA’I GLANG PO CHE MED PA BZHIN DU YUL CAN SHES PA YANG MED PAR STON PA NI MIN GYI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I SHES PA MED PAR STON PA LA NGES PAR ‘DOD DGOS TE,

This is not a demonstration that—just as an elephant which appears in a dream cannot be something which exists—an awareness which holds an object cannot exist either.  Rather, we have to agree that it is indicating how there exists no awareness which could exist through some nature of its own.


[2102]
SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR SEMS TZAM PAS PHYI ROL MED PA’I GZHAN DBANG KHAS BLANGS PA NI, GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YIN PA’I PHYIR DANG,

And so let’s consider this assertion by the Mind Only that—as we described it earlier—there do exist dominated entitites where there are no outer objects.  It goes back to the idea that dominated entities exist through some nature of their own.  


[2103]
DGAG PA ‘DI RNAMS KYIS DON BSDUR, MDOR NA JI LTAR SHES BYA MED DE BZHIN, ,BLO YANG MED, CES PA’I ‘GREL PAR SHES BYA’I RNAM PA CAN GYI BLO YANG RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS MA SKYES PAR RIG PAR BYA’O, ZHES GSAL BAR GSUNGS SHING,

And so to summarize these various denials, we can quote a clear reference in the autocommentary to the lines that say, “To put it briefly, there are no knowable things; and no mind either.”  This reference says—

You should understand that a state of mind holding the image of existing things does not arise by its very own self either.


[2104]
GZHAN YANG RTZA ‘GREL GNYIS SU ‘DI ‘DRA’I RIGS ‘GOG PA’I TSE, DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA DU MA ZHIG YOD PA’I PHYIR [f. 156b] DANG, SLAR YANG DE LAS BDAG NYID CHEN POS SEMS, ,MA RIG LAS LAS SKYES PAR CI PHYIR GSUNGS, ZHES MA RIG PAS ‘DU BYED ‘DU BYED KYIS RNAM SHES SKYED PAR GSUNGS PA RANG GI’ANG LUGS YIN PA’I PHYIR NA, RNAM SHES MED PA ‘DI’I LUGS SU SMRA BA LA NI RTOG LDAN LA DOGS PA’I GNAS MED DO,,

Our reasoning above is further supported by the fact that—when, in both the root text and the autocommentary the Master denies this type of reasoning—there are many examples where qualifications are placed upon the object that we deny with emptiness.  And we do see as well that part in the root text which says—

…And then how
Could it be in it
For the Great Being
To state that the mind

Was born from
Dark ignorance
And karma?

That is, the statement that misunderstanding triggers fresh karma, and then fresh karma in turn triggers consciousness, also represents our own system.  As such, nobody with good understanding would entertain the suspicion that people in the school we’re discussing here would assert that there was no consciousness.


[2105]
DE’I PHYIR SHES BYA DANG SHES PA LA YOD MED MGO MTSUNGS MDZAD PA THAMS CAD NI DGAG BYA’I KHYAD PAR GYI STENG NAS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

As such, you should understand that all the cases in which knowable things and the mind that knows them are stated to be equivalent—in either existing or not existing—are made with reference to distinctions in what we deny when we speak of emptiness.


[2106]
CI STE RMI LAM NA RNAM PAR SHES PA ‘KHRUL PA MED NA, DE’I SAD PAS RMI LAM GYI DUS GYI NYAMS SU MYONG BA PHYIS DRAN PAR MI ‘GYUR RO SNYAM NA,

At this point, the following thought might then occur to one:

If there exists no mistaken awareness within a dream, then when we wake from the dream we shouldn’t be able to remember—later on—what we experienced during the dream.


[2107]
‘DI NI SHES PA RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED NA, SHES PA YE MED PAR BSAMS PA’I RTZOD PA’O,,

This is an argument based on thinking that—if awareness is not something that exists through some essential nature of its own—then it cannot exist at all.


	[2108]
[VI.49]
Svapnasya bodhe smaraṇān mano’sti
yadyastu bāhyo viṣayo’pi tadvat,
Yathā mayā dṛṣṭam iti smṛtis te
bāhye ‘pi tadvat smṛti sambhavo’sti.

,GAL TE SAD TSE RMI LAM DRAN LAS YID,
,YOD NA PHYI ROL YUL YANG DE BZHIN ‘GYUR,
,JI LTAR KHYOD KYI NGAS MTHONG SNYAM DRAN PA,
,DE ‘DRA PHYI ROL LA YANG YOD PA YIN,

	Suppose that,
	When we wake,
	We remember the dream;
	And our mind existed.

	From that then
	Outside objects
	Would be just so.

	It follows from this—
	The memory where
	You think to yourself,
	“I saw something”;

	And moreover
	Such things existed
	As outside.


[2109]
DE LTAR RTZOD PA ‘DI YANG MI RUNG STE, GAL TE GNYID SAD PA’I TSE RMI LAM GYI NYAMS SU MYONG BA DRAN PA LAS, RMI LAM GYI YID RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD NA, RMI LAM GYI GLANG PO CHE LA SOGS PA PHYI ROL TU SNANG BA’I YUL YANG YID DE BZHIN DU YOD PAR ‘GYUR TE,

And making this kind of argument is, further, incorrect, for the following reason.  Suppose that—when we have woken from a dream—we remember what we experienced in the dream.  And then suppose further that our mind in the dream existed through some nature of its own.  In that case, from our remembering then, things like the elephant in the dream would also become just as that state of mind dictated: they would exist as objects appearing in the outside world.


[2110]
CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA, JI LTAR KHYOD KYI SAD PA’I TSE NGAS RMI LAM GYI DUS SU MTHONG SNYAM PA’I YUL CAN GYI DRAN PA YOD PA LAS YID YOD PA DE BZHIN DU, RMI LAM GYI TSE YUL ‘DI MTHONG SNYAM PA’I YUL MYONG DE ‘DRA BA PHYI ROL TE YUL LA YANG DRAN PA YOD PAS, YUL YANG YOD PA’AM YANG NA RNAM SHES KYANG YOD PA MIN NO ZHES KHAS BLANG BAR BYA’O,,

And why would that be the case?  It follows from this.  The fact is that there is a state of mind that comes from the presence of the memory that holds to a certain object; that is, when you wake from the dream, you think to yourself, “During the dream, I saw certain things.”  Following that, we can say that during the dream itself there were certain objects about which you thought, “I am seeing this”; that is, you have an experience of these objects, and you moreover recall such things as being outside objects.  And so we would have to say that those objects did exist; otherwise, there would be no such consciousness of them.  All this is something that you would have to accept.


[2111]
‘O NA RMI LAM GYI YUL DANG YUL CAN DRAN PA RANG LUGS LA YANG YOD PAS, DE GNYIS YOD MED JI LTAR BYA ZHE NA,

“Well then,” one may ask, “remembering both the subject and the object in a dream is something that can also be found in your own system.  So do you say that those two exist, or do not exist?”


[2112]
‘DIR ‘GREL PAR RMI [f. 157a] LAM GYI MYONG BA DRAN PA DANG, RMI LAM GYI YUL NYAMS SU MYONG BA DRAN PA GNYIS BSHAD PAS, RMI LAM GYI SKABS SU GLANG PO CHE LA SOGS PA SNANG BA NA, DPER NA BYAD BZHIN GYI GZUGS BRNYAN MTHONG BA NA DE SNANG BA’I MIG SHES KYIS BYAD BZHIN MYONG BA MIN KYANG, GZUGS BRNYAN LA LTOS PA’I YUL MYONG YOD PA BZHIN DU, RMI LAM GYI TSE YANG GLANG PO CHE MYONG BA’I YUL MYONG MED KYANG, DER SNANG BA’I YUL MYONG YOD PAS YUL DRAN ZER YANG YUL DE MYONG BA DRAN PA’O,,

On this point, the autocommentary describes two different types of remembering: one, a memory of the experience of the dream; and two, a memory of experiencing objects within the dream.  And so suppose that an elephant or the like appears during a dream.  It’s like for example when we see a reflection of an object in a mirror.  It’s not that the visual consciousness which assumes that form is experiencing the object standing in front of the mirror; rather, it is having an experience of an object due to the reflection.  The case with a dream is similar; even though at this point there is no experience of a elephant as the object, there has been an experience of an object appearing as an elephant.  As such, when we say “I remember a certain object,” we are actually remembering the experience of that object.


[2113]
DMIGS MYONG SO SOR ‘BYED PA NI SKABS ‘GA’ ZHIG MA GTOGS PA ‘DI ‘DRA BA MANG PO ZHIG LA MI DGOS SO,,

This idea of distinguishing between an object and an experience is something that we need to do only in a few specific cases; it’s not as though you would need to call on it frequently.


[2114]
DE LTAR NA PHYI ROL GYIS STONG PA’I GZHAN DBANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI ‘JOG PAR MI NUS TE, DNGOS KYI DPE YANG MI SRID LA SKYE BA SNGA PHYI YOD PAR SGRUB PA LTA BU LA DNGOS KYI DPE MED KYANG, SBYOR BA’I ‘GOD TSUL GZHAN GYIS SGRUB PA LTA BU’I DPE YANG ‘DI LA MED PAS, SEMS TZAM PA ‘GOG PA NI RIGS PA SHIN TU STOBS CHE BAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

And so thus we can say that there is no way one could establish the existence of dominated entitites that exist by definition and are devoid of objects existing on the outside.  There is no outright example of this possibility; and whereas—in the case of proving the existence of past & future lives, there is no outright example either, but we can establish it by other means, such as by positing a logical proof based on a metaphor—there is nothing like that here in this case.  As such, you should understand that the denial of the Mind Only position is an extremely powerful expression of logic.



The failure of the dream

[2115]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second point from above: how it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish the idea that, when we awake, there are no outer objects.


	[2116]
[VI.50]
Cakṣur dhiyaḥ sambhava eva middhe
nāstyasti vai mānasam eva cetaḥ,
Tad ākṛtau bāhyatayā niveśaḥ
svapne yathehāpi tathā mataṃ cet.

,GAL TE GNYID NANG MIG BLO MI SRID PAS,
,YOD MIN YID KYI SHES PA KHO NA YOD,
,DE YI RNAM PA PHYI ROL NYID DU ZHEN,
,RMI LAM JI LTA DE BZHIN ‘DIR ‘DOD NA,

		If, in our sleep,
		The mind of vision
		Is impossible,

		Then those are not
		Something; rather,
		All that is present is
		The awareness of our thoughts.

		We are attached to
		An aspect of it;
		The outside world itself.

		Suppose you accept that
		It’s just the same here
		As the way in a dream.


[2117]
GAL TE GLANG PO CHE LA SOGS PA’I GZUGS RMI LAM NA YOD NA, DE ‘DZIN PA’I MIG SHES KYANG RMI LAM NA YOD PAR ‘GYUR NA DE NI MI RIGS TE, GNYID LOG PA NA GNYID KYIS DKRUGS PA LA MIG GI BLO STE SHES PA MI SRID PAS, GLANG PO CHE LA SOGS PA’I GZUGS MIG GI SKYE MCHED KYIS GZUNG BAR BYA BA YOD PA MIN LA, YID KYI SHES PA KHO NA YOD DO,,

It’s not logical to say that—if the form of an elephant or something similar were to exist in a dream—then there must also be a visual consciousness present in the dream.  In our sleep, our minds are disturbed by the sleep; and so it is impossible for there to be “the mind of vision”; which is to say, visual consciousness.  As such, the fact is that the visual form of the elephant or whatever it may be is not something which is held by the sense door of the eyes.  Rather, all that is present is the awareness of our thoughts.


[2118]
DE’I PHYIR PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED MED PA KHO NA YIN ZHING, YID KYI RNAM [f. 157b] PAR SHES PA LA PHYI ROL DE’I RNAM PA SNANG BA TZAM LA PHYI ROL NYID DU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA NI BZLOG TU MED PAR ‘BYUNG NGO,,

As such, an outer door of visible form can only be something which does not exist.  And what’s happening is that we are strongly attached to thinking that the awareness of the thought is an aspect of the outer world—that something which is nothing more than the appearance of being outside is the outside world itself.  This attachment occurs in a very compelling way that is difficult to reverse.


[2119]
RMI LAM DU PHYI ROL MED PAR RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM ‘BYUNG BA JI LTA BA DE BZHIN DU, SAD PA’I SKABS ‘DIR ‘DOD DO ZHE NA,

So suppose then that you say that things are just the way that they happen in a dream; and there is only consciousness going on, without any outer objects.  Suppose you say you accept that things here—referring to the hours of our waking life—are just the same.


[2120]
‘DI NI SNGAR GYI DPE DE MA GRUB TU CHUG KYANG RMI LAM GYI DPES SAD PA’I SKABS SU PHYI ROL MED PA’I RNAM SHES ‘GRUB BO SNYAM PA’O,,

It would appear that—in these lines—it is being allowed that the previous metaphor was not successful, but at the same time there is an assertion that the metaphor of a dream works to establish the fact that, when we awake, there is present a consciousness which has no outer objects.


[2121]
DE NI MA YIN TE RMI LAM DU YID KYI RNAM SHES ‘BYUNG BA MI SRID PA’I PHYIR RO, ZHES GSUNGS PA NI, RMI LAM DU GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED MED DU CHUG KYANG, DA {%DE} MED PA’I YID KYI RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RMI LAM NA’ANG MI SRID PAS, PHYI ROL MED PA DANG YID SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA GNYIS TSOGS PA DE DPER MI RUNG ZHES PA’O,,

And then we have a statement that this is not the way it is; that it’s impossible for consciousness of the thoughts to occur within a dream.  What this is saying is that—even if we accede the point that there is no door of sense of visible form in a dream—it is further the case that in a dream it is impossible for there to exist a consciousness of the thoughts which indeed has no such door, and which exists through some nature of its own.  As such, it’s being said, it is inappropriate to offer this metaphor to illustrate the combination of there being no outer objects, and the awareness of our thoughts existing through some nature of its own.


	[2122]
[VI.51]
Bāhyo yathā te viṣayo na jātaḥ
svapne tathā naiva mano’pi jātam,
Cakṣuś ca cakṣur viṣayaś ca taj jaṃ
cittaṃ ca sarvaṃ trayam apyalīkam.


,JI LTAR KHYOD KYI PHYI YUL RMI LAM DU,
,MA SKYES DE BZHIN YID KYANG SKYES MA YIN,
,MIG DANG MIG GI YUL DANG DES SKYED SEMS,
,GSUM PO THAMS CAD KYANG NI BRDZUN PA YIN,

		Just the way you say
		Outside objects never start
		In a dream,

		The thought too,
		In the same manner,
		Never starts.

		The eye and
		The object of the eye,
		And the state of mind
		Triggered by them—

		All three—
Are also deceptive.		


[2123]
‘DI LTAR JI LTAR KHYOD KYI LTAR NA PHYI ROL GYI YUL TE DON RMI LAM DU MA SKYES PA DE BZHIN DU, YID KYI RNAM SHES KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYES PA MA YIN NO,,

It’s just the way that you say it is: objects that are on the outside are similar to things in a dream—they never start.  In the same manner, consciousness of the thought too never starts through any nature of its own.


[2124]
DE’I PHYIR JI LTAR SAD PA’I TSE GZUGS MTHONG BA NA, MIG DANG GZUGS DANG YID GSUM PO ‘DUS PA DE BZHIN DU, RMI LAM DU YANG YUL YONGS SU GCOD PA NA GSUM ‘DUS PAR BLOS DMIGS PA YIN NO,,

And so we can point to how we see forms when we are awake; the three of the eye, visual form, and the thought come together.  In a dream, the perception is accomplished by the mind, as the three assemble even in the exclusion of the object.


[2125]
JI LTAR RMI LAM DER MIG DANG MIG GI YUL GZUGS GNYIS MED PA DE BZHIN DU, DE GNYIS KYIS BSKYED PA’I SEMS MIG GI RNAM SHES KYANG YOD PA YANG MA YIN PAS, RMI LAM GYI MIG GZUGS YID GSUM PO THAMS CAD KYANG NI BRDZUN PA YIN NO,,

In a dream, these two are absent: the eye and the form which serves as the object of the eye.  Just so, the state of mind which is triggered by these two—the visual awareness—is something that is missing.  As such, all three of these, in a dream, are also deceptive: the eye, the form, and the thought.


	[2126]
[VI.52]
Śrotrādiśeṣaṃ trayam apy ajātaṃ
svapne yathehāpi tathā prabodhe,
Mṛṣā padārthā na tad asti cittaṃ
na gocaraḥ santi ca nendriyāṇi.

	[VI.52a]
,RNA SOGS LHAG MA GSUM PO’ANG SKYE BA MED,

	The extra three
	For the ear and so on
	Also have no growing.
	

[2127]
GSUM PO DE BZHIN DU RNA BA SOGS MIG GI GSUM GYI LHAG MA GSUM PO’ANG RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED [f. 158a] DO,,

In the same way as these three, the ear sense power and so on—the extra three on top of the three for the eye—are also things that have no growing through any nature of their own.


[2128]
‘DIR SOGS PA’I SGRAS NI SGRA DANG RNA BA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA NAS YID DANG CHOS KYI KHAMS DANG YID KYI RNAM PAR SHES PA’I BAR BSDU’O, ZHES GSUNGS PA’I RNA BA’I DBANG PO NAS LUS DBANG GI BAR BZHI DANG, SGRA’I NAS REG BYA’I SKYE MCHED KYI BAR BZHI DANG, RNA BA’I RNAM SHES SOGS BZHI NI

Here, “the phrase ‘and so on’ is meant to include everything from sound and the consciousness of the ear up to the thought, and the category of things, and the consciousness of the thought.”  What this is referring to is the four from the sense power of the ear, up to that of the body; plus the four from the door of sense of sound up to that of tangible objects; plus the four of the consciousness of the ear, and so on.


[2129]
SNGAR MIG GI GSUM LA BSHAD PA BZHIN DU, RMI LAM NA DE DAG MED KYANG DE DAG GI RNAM PAR SNANG BAS BRDZUN PA DANG, YID KYI GSUM NI RMI LAM NA YOD KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS MED BZHIN DU DER SNANG BAS BRDZUN PA’O,,

And then the point is that we consider them just as we explained the three connected to the eye: that is—even though, in a dream, none of these exists—they do appear there, and thus are deceptive.  And even though the three relating to the thought may be present in a dream, they do not exist through any nature of their own.  But since they do appear to exist in this way, we consider them deceptive.


[2130]
DE’I PHYIR RMI LAM NA DBANG SHES YOD PA SLOB DPON ‘DI’I LUGS SU BYAS NAS DE LA DGAG PA BYED PA NI, BLO GROS KYI ‘JUG PA SHIN TU RTZING BAS, PHYOGS SNGA’I NAM MA LANGS PA LA DGAG PA’I NYI MA SHAR BA YIN ZHES GRAGS PA BZHIN YIN PAS, RGYANG RING DU DOR BAR BYA STE

As such, there have been people who took the idea that awareness of the senses exists in a dream as being the position of this master; and then undertook to deny it.  This reflects a very coarse engagement of the intellect—something which resembles that saying about how “The sun of blocking another position rose in the sky, without the daybreak of the original position ever having broken.”  As such, we should discard it, to a great distance!


[2131]
BOD KYI MKHAS PAR RLOM PA ‘GA’ ZHIG LA, ‘DI ‘DRA BA’I GRUB MTHA’ LA MKHAS PA’I DBANG PO SEMS DPA’ CHEN PO YIN, NGO SHES PA RNAMS KYI LUGS RAGS PA’ANG MA GO BAR, DE RNAMS BSOD NAMS MA YIN PA RGYUN LDAN DU GSOG PA’I ZHING DU GZUNG NAS, SEMS CAN DU MA ZHIG BSOD NAMS MA YIN PA LA SBYOR BAR SNANG BAS BAG YOD PAR BYOS SHIG

And I address this comment to a number of Tibetans who imagine themselves to be great masters: Those who are lords among masters within schools of thought like this are themselves great bodhisattvas; and you have failed to achieve an understanding of even the roughest outline of their system, for those who really recognize who they are.  It would appear though that you are taking these lords to be like a garden for harvesting steady flows of negative karma, and are guiding many innocent others to wrongful deeds.  And so I ask you, please: Be careful!


[2132]
,’DIR SEMS TZAM PAS GAL TE GNYID NANG ZHES SOGS KYIS BSHAD PA BZHIN DU RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, SLOB DPON LEGS LDAN GYIS KYANG DPE MA GRUB PA’I LAN MDZAD PA NA, CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED DU GTOGS PA’I GZUGS YID KYI SHES PAS GZUNG BAR BYA BA CIG ,RMI LAM [f. 158b] NA YOD PAS RNAM PAR SHES PA NI YUL MED PAR ‘GAR YANG YOD PA MA YIN NO ZHES SMRA’O,,

When those of the Mind Only put forth their own system as expressed in the lines that include “If, in our sleep,” Master Bhavaviveka also responds to it saying that the metaphor doesn’t work out; that there is something grasped by the awareness of the thought which is subsumed by the door of sense of all things, and this is present in the dream.  As such, as it says, “It is not at all the case that the consciousness here is one for which there is no object.”


[2133]
‘DI LA DE YANG RIGS PA MA YIN TE, RMI LAM NA RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU GSUM PO MI SRID PA’I PHYIR RO, ,CI STE GZHAN GYI GZHUNG LUGS BSAL BAR BYA BA’I PHYIR DE LTAR KHAS LEN NA NI, DE’I TSE RMI LAM GYI DPE DON MED PA NYID DU ‘GYUR TE, DE BRDZUN PA MA YIN PA’I DON CAN YIN PA NYID KYIS DPE LAS BYUNG BA DNGOS KYI DON BRDZUN PA’I DON {Teng: CAN} NYID DU BSTAN PA MI SRID PA’I PHYIR RO,

To this one might say that this idea too is incorrect:

It’s all because, in a dream, all three are impossible, in every respect.  And in the case that you accept it as being that way because you seek to clarify what the position of the major works of other schools is, then the whole referent of the dream would be obviated.  That is, the very fact that you were interpreting the metaphor as referring to something that is not in fact false means that it would hardly be possible then to take the main point of the metaphor as referring to something which was deceptive.


[2134]
ZHES GSUNGS PA’I DON NI YUL DBANG RNAM SHES GSUM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI RMI LAM NA YANG RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MI SRID PA’I PHYIR, CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED KYI GZUGS SHES PA LAS DON GZHAN RMI LAM NA YOD PA MI RIGS ZHES BSHAD RGYU YIN LA,

What this is saying is that—if the three of the object, the power, and the consciousness existed through some nature of their own—then even in a dream they would be, in every respect, an impossibility.  And that means that we would have to say that it is wrong to posit form of the door of sense of all things which could exist in a dream as something discrete from awareness itself.


[2135]
DE’I TSE GZUGS DE RANG GIS KYANG BZHED DGOS LA, DE RMI LAM NA YANG YOD PA MI ‘GAL BAS, GZUGS DE LEGS LDAN GYIS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ZHAL GYIS BZHES BAR GSAL BAS DE MED PA’I RGYU MTSAN DU BYA’O,,

In such a case, one would also have to accept this particular form.  And since there would be no contradiction for it to exist, even in a dream, then it is clear that Bhavaviveka would have to agree that it existed through some nature of its own.  And then we could use that as a reason for saying that it didn’t exist.


[2136]
CI STE SEMS TZAM PA’I LUGS PHYI’I SKYE MCHED DU GTOGS PA’I GZUGS DON GZHAN MED PA LA, RMI LAM DPER ‘JOG PA DES SEL NUS PAS, DE BSAL BA’I PHYIR GZUGS DE RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PAR KHAS LEN NA NI, DE’I TSE DBU MA PAS BDEN MED SGRUB PA LA RMI LAM GYI DPE BKOD PA DON MED DO,,

And it being the case that in the Mind Only system there could exist no other aspect of form which was taken in by the outer doors of sense, the form that we posit in the metaphor of the dream would be able to remove this problem.  If to clarify this point we accept the idea that the form would exist by definition, then it would serve no purpose for those of the Middle Way school to offer the metaphor of a dream in establishing that nothing exists in reality.


[2137]
RMI LAM DE BRDZUN PA MA YIN PA’I DON CAN TE, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NYID KYIS DPE LAS BYUNG BA STE, DES MTSON PA’I DNGOS KYI DON BRDZUN PA NYID DU GRUB PA MI SRID PA’I PHYIR TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA BKAG [f. 159a] BAR DU, BDEN MED SGRUB PA’I RTAGS CHOS DPE DE LA RJES SU ‘GRO BA MED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

A dream then would carry the connotation of something that was not false.  If because of the very fact that it existed by definition, a point were derived from the metaphor, then it would be impossible for the direct referent represented by the metaphor to be established as something that was, in fact, deceptive.  And that’s because—until such point as we have succeeded in denying that something could exist through some nature of its own—there would be no way that the reason and the quality to be proven in a syllogism to prove that things were not real would ever match the metaphor.


[2138]
DES NA SNGAR RANG GI LUGS KYIS RMI LAM NA GANG SNANG THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA’I LAN BTAB PA CHES LEGS SO,,

As such, it is excellent in the extreme for those who belong to our own system to offer the reply that not a single object which appears in a dream could ever exist through some nature of its own.


[2139]
‘O NA RANG LUGS KYIS RMI LAM GYI GZUGS GSAL BAR SNANG BA RNAMS CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED PA’I GZUGS SU ‘DOD DAM MI ‘DOD CE NA,

Suppose someone comes with the following question: “Well then, do you agree that forms which appear clearly in a dream belong to the door of sense of all things, or not?”


[2140]
RMI LAM NA DBANG SHES MED PAS YUL LNGAR SNANG BA RNAMS NI YID SHES KHO NA LA SNANG BAS NA, DE LA GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED SOGS LNGA BZHAG TU MED KYANG, YID TZAM GYI NGOR KENG RUS GSAL BAR SNANG BA LTA BU CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED DU ‘JOG PA DANG ‘DRA BAS, CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED KYI GZUGS YIN LA, DE YANG DE’I GZUGS LNGA LAS KUN BRTAGS PA’I GZUGS YIN NO,,

No awareness of a sense power can appear in a dream; as such, things that appear then as though they were one of the five sense objects can appear only to the consciousness of the thoughts.  Thus then it’s similar to the case where—even though it’s true that it cannot be said to constitute the five of the door of sense of visible form or the rest—something like the vivid appearance of a skeleton to nothing more than the thought can be established as constituting the door of sense of all things.  And that can be referred to as “nominal” form, following the model of the five types of form it would have.


[2141]
‘DIS NI ‘DI ‘DRA BA MANG PO ZHIG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

You can use this description to explain many other similar cases.



Using dreams for the deceptive

[2142]
GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to our third point from above: establishing—through the metaphor of a dream—that all entities are deceptive.


	[2143]
	[VI.52b]
,RMI LAM JI LTA DE BZHIN SAD ‘DIR YANG,
,DNGOS RNAMS BRDZUN YIN SEMS DE YOD MA YIN,
,SPYOD YUL MED CING DBANG PO RNAMS KYANG MED,

	Just as in a dream,
	Here in waking too
	Entities are deceptive.

	As such, this mind
	Is nothing that exists.

	None of the objects
	Of activity
	Have any existence;

	And neither do
	The powers exist.


[2144]
GANG GI PHYIR RMI LAM NA YUL DBANG RNAM SHES SU SNANG BA GSUM CHAR YANG MI BDEN PA DE’I PHYIR, RMI LAM BDEN MED DU RAB TU GRUB PA’I SGO NAS CHOS GZHAN BDEN MED DU MA GRUB PA RNAMS BSGRUB PA’I PHYIR, SAD PA’I TSE NA YANG CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN MED PA NYID DU BSGRUBS PAR ‘GYUR RO ZHES BSHAD PA,

In a dream, none of the three that make their appearance are real: neither the object, nor the sense power, nor the awareness.  And for this very reason, we can establish that things which we have yet to establish as being unreal—by demonstrating, perfectly, that a dream has no reality.  And then for this reason we can say that—when we are awake as well—every entity that exists can be established as having absolutely no nature of its own.  To express all this then, we have the following.


[2145]
JI LTAR RMI LAM GYI YUL DANG DBANG PO DANG RNAM PAR SHES PA RNAMS BRDZUN PA DE BZHIN DU, SAD PA’I SKABS ‘DIR YANG DNGOS PO RNAMS BRDZUN PA YIN PAS, SEMS DE RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN LA, DE BZHIN DU DBANG PO’I SPYOD YUL GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS MED CING, [f. 159b] DBANG PO RNAMS KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED DO,,

It’s just as how the object, and the sense power, and the consciousness in a dream are deceptive; just so, here in the time of waking too entities are deceptive.  As such, this mind is nothing that exists through any nature of its own.  And in the very same way, none of the objects of the activity of the powers—form and the rest—have any existence at all; and neither do the powers exist as things that arise through some nature of their own.


[2146]
DE’I PHYIR MDO LAS,
,JI LTAR SGYU MA’I SEMS CAN DMIGS PA LTAR,
,SNANG YANG DE NYID DU NA YANG DAG MIN,
,SGYU MA LTA BU RMI LAM DANG ‘DRA BA,
,DE LTA’I CHOS NI BDE BAR GSHEGS PAS BSTAN,
ZHES DANG,

Thus it is that sutra says,

An illusory creature
Appears to exist
In just the way we see it;
But it is nothing true.

It is like an illusion;
It is like a dream—

And this is how things
Are described by the
One Who Has Gone to Bliss.


	[2147]
,SRID PA’I ‘GRO BA RMI LAM LTA BU STE,
,’DI LA MI SKYE SU YANG ‘CHI BA MED,
,SEMS CAN MI DANG SROG KYANG MI RNYED DE,
,CHOS ‘DI RNAMS NI DBU BA CHU SHING ‘DRA,
ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA YANG LEGS PAR BSHAD PAR ‘GYUR RO ZHES GSUNGS LA,

The following and the rest is, as it says, “also a great explanation”:

	The way that people
	Travel through existence
	Is just like a dream:

	No one is ever born here,
	And no on ever dies.

Beings find no being human,
Nor any life at all;

All of these things
Are like a bubble,
And hollow as bamboo.


[2148]
SU YANG MI SKYE SOGS NI, DE NYID DU NA YANG DAG MIN, ZHES DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR MDZAD PA LTAR SBYAR RO,,

When the line refers to “no one ever being born here” and such, you should apply a qualification to what is denied: “But it is nothing true.”


[2149]
MDO DE DAG GIS RMI LAM GYI DPES CHOS THAMS CAD DE KHO NAR MA GRUB PAR BSHAD PA DE DBU MA LA ‘GRIG GI ,SEMS TZAM LA MI ‘GRIGS PAS LEGS PAR BSHAD PAR ‘GYUR ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

When these sutras use the metaphor of a dream to describe how nothing in the universe exists in & of itself, it is fine with those of the Middle Way school—but it would not be fine with the Mind Only school.  As such, it is “a fine explanation.”


	[2150]
[VI.53]
Yāvan na bodhaṃ labhate’sti tāvat
trayaṃ hi tasyeha yathāprabodhe,
Sati prabodhe trayam apy asatyaṃ
sa moha nidrākṣaya tas tathaiva.

,’DI NA JI LTAR SAD BZHIN JI SRID DU,
,MI SAD DE SRID DE LA GSUM PO YOD,
,SAD PAR GYUR NA GSUM CHAR YOD MIN LTAR,
,GTI MUG GNYID ZAD LAS DE DE BZHIN NO,

		It’s just as here,
		When we’re awake.

		And it’s the same
		For those who have
		Not yet woken;

		For that length of time,
		All three exist to them.

		When they have awakened,
		None of the three
		Exist any more.

		Just so, we can
		Finish the sleep
		Of dark ignorance;
		Such is it.


[2151]
DE’I PHYIR ‘JIG RTEN ‘DI NA JI LTAR MI SHES PA’I GNYID YOD KYANG, DE LAS THA DAD PA’I THA MAL BA’I GNYID DANG BRAL BAS SAD PA ‘GA’ ZHIG LA, RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS MA SKYES KYANG MA RIG PA’I GNYID KYIS RMI LAM RMI BZHIN PAS DMIGS PA’I NGOR, GSUM CHAR YANG YOD PA 

As such, it’s just as there is a sleep of unknowing here in the everyday world.  But there is a normal sleep which is separate from this, and then some number of people are free from this sleep, and thus awake.  And then they dream dreams, which are not things that arise all by themselves, but rather due to the sleep of misunderstanding.  And to the perceptions of these dreams, all three do exist.


[2152]
DE BZHIN DU JI SRID DU GNYID DANG MA BRAL BA MA SAD PA RNAMS LA YANG, DE SRID DU DE LA STE DE’I NGOR YUL DBANG RNAM SHES GSUM PO YANG YOD PA YIN NO,, 

It’s the same for those who have not yet woken; who are still not free of the sleep.  For that length of time, to them (that is, to their perceptions), all three again exist: object, power, and consciousness.


[2153]
GNYID SAD PAR GYUR PA NA, RMI LAM GYI GSUM CHAR YOD PA MIN PA LTAR, GTI MUG GI GNYID ZAD PA STE MA LUS PAR DRUNGS PHYUNG BA LAS, CHOS KYI DBYINGS MNGON SUM DU MDZAD PA’I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS LA NI, GSUM CHAR YANG YOD PA [f. 160a] MA YIN PAS PHYI ROL MED PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA MED DO,,

When they have awakened from the sleep, none of the three of the dream exist any more.  Just so, we can finish the sleep of dark ignorance; which is to say, we can tear out every trace of it.  And then we can become one of those Enlightened Beings who make the Realm of Is their everyday state.  All three are then, again, nothing that exists; and as such, there exists no consciousness where there is a total lack of outer objects.


[2154]
DE YANG JI LTAR GZIGS PA’I NGOR NI GSUM PO MI SNANG LA, JI SNYED PA GZIGS PA’I NGOR NI YUL CAN RANG NYID MA RIG PA’I BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA’I DBANG GIS SNANG BA MED KYANG, GANG ZAG GZHAN GYI SHES PA BSLAD PA’I DBANG GIS SNANG BA RNAMS, DE LA SNANG BA’I SGO NAS SANGS RGYAS LA SNANG NAS MKHYEN PA YIN NO,,

None of the three, moreover, can appear to the perceptions of a person who is seeing the way that all things are.  What appears though to the perceptions of a person who is seeing all the things there are?  They is no appearance of them to a subject state of mind due to any infection of it by deep seeds for misunderstanding.  They can though make their appearance by force of the fact that the awareness of another person’s mind is infected; and what is appearing to them then appears to the Buddha, and thus they know them.



No strand of hair

[2155]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second step from above: denying the metaphor of seeing a strand of hair.


	[2156]
[VI.54]
Keśākṛtiṃ yāṃ timiraprabhāvād
dhiyā yayā vetti sa taimirākṣaḥ,
Dvayaṃ hi tadbodham apekṣya satyaṃ
spaṣṭārtha dṛṣṭer dvayam apyalīkam.

,DBANG PO RAB RIB BCAS PA BLO GANG GIS,
,RAB RIB MTHU LAS SKRA RNAMS GANG MTHONG BA,
,DE BLO LA LTOS GNYIS CHAR BDEN PA STE,
,DON GSAL MTHONG LA GNYIS KA’ANG BRDZUN PA YIN,

	A power which has 
Cataracts, a particular
State of mind,

Sees certain strands
		Due to the influence
		Of the cataracts.

		Relative to this mind,
		Both of them are real.

		To one seeing objects clearly,
		Both are false.


[2157]
‘O NA RAB RIB CAN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN PA’I SKRA SHAD LA SOGS PA DMIGS PA’I PHYIR, PHYI ROL MED KYANG RNAM PAR SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA YIN NO ZHE NA

One might come with the following:

It is indeed the case that—even though there are no outer objects—awareness does exist through a nature of its own; this is due to the fact that a person who has cataracts on their eyes does perceive strands of hair and the like which do not actually exist.


[2158]
DE YANG MI ‘THAD DO, ,CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA, MIG GI DBANG PO RAB RIB DANG BCAS PA LA BLO GANG GIS RAB RIB KYI MTHU LAS SKRA SHAD RNAMS GANG MTHONG BA NA,

This too though is a mistaken idea.  And why is that?  Let’s think of a sense power of the eye which has cataracts; that is, when a particular state of mind sees certain strands of hair due to the influence of cataracts.


[2159]
