And it is only in correspondence with the aspects of objects under consideration that the essential nature of the pair of accurate perceptions which can recognize the existence of the natures of each of these is itself established.


[2461]
DE DAG GI DON NI TSAD MA GNYIS SU NGES PA GZHAL BYA GNYIS SU NGES PA’I DBANG GIS ‘JOG PA’I PHYIR DANG, TSAD MA LA GZHAL BYA’I RNAM PA SHAR BA’I DBANG GIS ‘JAL BYED KYI TSAD MA’I RANG GI NGO BO YOD PAR ‘JOG LA,

The point of these lines is to say that the fact that the number of accurate perceptions is fixed at two is due to the fact that the objects they take under consideration are also fixed at two.  And accurate perceptions as acting to take things under consideration are further fixed as existing with a nature of such perceptions by force of the aspects that make their appearance with them, as they do take objects under consideration.


[2462]
TZAM GYIS ZHES PA NI SEMS TZAM PA DANG MDO SDE PA ‘DOD PA LTAR TSAD MA GZHAL BYA JI ‘DRA PA DE ‘DRA BA’I RNAM PA’I RJE SU BYED PAS GZHAL BYA ‘GRUB LA,

When they utilize the word “only” in the citation above, what they’re saying is that—according to the beliefs of those who belong to the school of Only Mind, and the Sutrists—the aspect that accurate perceptions take on always follows from the objects they take under consideration, and this then leads to the confirmation of these objects.


[2463]
DE NAS TSAD MA ‘GRUB TSUL NI SNGA MA LAS ZUR DU TSAD MA RANG GI NGO BO LA GNYIS SNANG DANG BRAL BA’I ‘DZIN RNAM YAN [f. 179a] GAR BA MYONG BA’I RANG RIG GIS ‘GRUB PA ‘GOG STE, GZHAL BYA ‘GRUB PA TZAM GYIS ‘GRUB PA’I DON NO,,

And so then we can say that this way in which accurate perception is established acts in turn to deny the idea that things could be established by an apperception which undergoes a discrete experience in an aspect of being the perceiver, free of all subject-object duality in its nature—an accurate perception which has a separate experience from the one that came before.


[2464]
‘DI NI ‘PHAGS PA NYID KYIS,
,GAL TE RANG LAS TSAD MA GRUB,
,GZHAL BYA RNAMS LA MA LTOS PAR,
,KHYOD KYI TSAD MA GRUB GYUR ‘DIR,
,GZHAN LA MI LTOS RAB GRUB ‘GYUR,
ZHES GSUNGS PA’I DGONGS PA YIN TE,

This is in fact what he had in mind when The Arya himself stated,

Suppose this state of mind
Were established
As an accurate perception
All on its own,

Without depending
Upon the objects
It takes under consideration.

When you then
Are establishing
What it is that makes
A thing an accurate
Form of perception,

Your proof itself
Is perfectly free
Of relying on
Anything else at all.


[2465]
TSAD MA ‘GRUB PA LA GZHAL BYA GRUB PA TZAM GYIS MI CHOG PAR TSAD MA RANG LAS TSAD MA ‘GRUB PA GZHAN DAG ‘DOD PA LTAR YIN NA, GZHAL BYA LA MA LTOS PAR TSAD MA ‘GRUB PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

Suppose it were as others would have it: suppose that—in order to establish an accurate perception—we could not simply be satisfied by establishing what that perception takes under its consideration.  Suppose, as others would have it, that accurate perception is established through accurate perception itself.  In that case, something would be established as an accurate perception without relying upon that thing which it takes under consideration.


[2466]
DE ‘DOD NA DNGOS PO RNAMS RGYU RKYEN GZHAN LA MA LTOS PAR RAB TU GRUB PAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES BKAG PAS GZHAL BYA GRUB PA TZAM GYIS TSAD MA GRUB PAR SHUGS KYIS BSTAN NO,,

And if one were to accept that, then functional entities could be established without relying on any other causes or conditions.  This is how the denial here is made; as such, what’s being said, by implication, is that accurate perceptions are to be established only by establishing those objects which they take under consideration.


[2467]
DE LTAR NA SNGO ‘DZIN NI GZHAN LUGS LTAR RANG RIG GIS MI ‘GRUB KYI, DBANG PO’I MNGON SUM TSAD MAS ‘GRUB PAR BSTAN TE, DE YOD PA NI SNGO ‘DZIN GYIS GZHAL BYA GRUB PA DE NYID KYIS RTOGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

As such, what’s being presented here is the idea that the perception of a patch of blue is not—as other schools would have it—established through some apperception; but rather, through a direct form of accurate perception.  And the fact that that exists can be grasped from the very fact that the perception of blue confirms its own object of consideration.


[2468]
DE’I PHYIR TSAD MA GANG YIN THAMS CAD RANG GI GZHAL BYA GRUB PA DE NYID KYIS ‘GRUB BO,,

And so the fact is that every accurate perception there is, is itself established through the object that it takes under its consideration.



Rejecting rebuttal about
deductive accurate perception

[2469]
GNYIS PA NI,

And with this we have reached the second part of our first step from above: rejecting rebuttal about a deductive form of accurate perception


[2470]
‘O NA LUGS ‘DIS GZUGS BRNYAN DANG SGRA BRNYAN SOGS KYANG SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GZUGS DANG SGRA’I SKYE MCHED SOGS SU BZHAG PA DANG, 

Well then, this particular system—as we noted before—says that things like reflections in a mirror and echoes belong to doors of sense such as visible form, sound, and the like.


[2471]
TSIG GSAL LAS KYANG, ZLA BA GNYIS LA SOGS PA DAG NI RAB RIB CAN MA YIN PA’I SHES PA LA LTOS NAS MNGON SUM NYID MA YIN LA, RAB RIB CAN LA SOGS PA LA LTOS NAS NI MNGON SUM NYID KHO NA’O,

A Clarification of the Verses says as well,

Things like the moon appearing as two moons are not—relative to the vision of a person who does not have cataracts—direct perception itself.  But relative to a person who does have cataracts, they are quite surely direct perception.


[2472]
ZHES LUGS ‘DIS GZUGS SGRA LA SOGS PA’I YUL LA [f. 179b] MNGON SUM GYI SGRA DNGOS MING DANG, DE DAG ‘DZIN PA’I YUL CAN LA BTAGS MING DU BSTAN PA’I SKABS SU ZLA BA GNYIS SNANG SOGS ‘JIG RTEN PA RANG DGA’ BA LA LTOS TE, GZHAL BYA MNGON SUM PA YIN MIN GYI KHYAD YOD KYANG, RANG GI LUGS LA NI ZLA BA GNYIS SNANG SOGS KYANG GZHAL BYA MNGON SUM PA MNGON GYUR DU BZHED PA YIN NO,,

In this system then the description “direct perception” can be applied to how this relates to objects such as visible form and sound; whereas it applies to the subject states that hold to them as a more metaphoric name.  In such circumstances, there is a distinction of whether the object under consideration is direct or not, relative to things like the moon appearing to be two moons.  According to our own system though we would say that things like the moon appearing to be two moons is a directly perceived object under consideration—and thus direct.


[2473]
DE’I PHYIR DBANG PO’I SHES PA ‘JIG RTEN RANG DGA’ BA LA LTOS PA’I ‘KHRUL MA ‘KHRUL GANG YIN KYANG, RANG GI GZHAL BYA GRUB PAS YUL CAN ‘GRUB BO,,

And so we can say that whether or not a sense perception is mistaken with reference to the normal perceptions of the world, the object that it takes under consideration is established; which means that the subject state of mind is also established.


[2474]
‘ON KYANG RANG RIG KHAS MI LEN PA LA GZHI DUS KYI YID SHES SNANG BA DANG, ZHEN YUL LA ‘KHRUL BA RNAMS YOD PAR MI ‘GRUB STE, DE RNAMS LA RANG GI GZHAL BYA ‘JAL BAS YUL CAN GRUB PA MED PA’I PHYIR RO ZHE NA, 

One may come then with the following question:

But isn’t it the case that—with someone who does not accept the idea of apperception—the consciousness of the thought (assuming one is still in their original state of evolution) and types of perception which are mistaken towards what one thinks that they see, cannot be demonstrated to exist?  Because it is the case that there is no confirmation of the subject states of mind here, as they take under consideration their particular objects of consideration.


[2475]
‘DI LA BSHAD PAR BYA STE LUGS ‘DIS RNAM SHES TSOGS DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I RNAM SHES MI BZHED PAS, DBANG PO GZUGS CAN LA DNGOS SU BRTEN PA’I TSAD MA DANG YID KYI DBANG PO TZAM LA BRTEN PA’I TSAD MA GNYIS LAS NI MED DO,,

Let’s clarify this point then.  This system does not accept the idea of a consciousness which is essentially separate from the collection of six different types of consciousness.  As such, there are only the two types of accurate perception: one which depends directly upon the physical sense organs, and then a second which depends only upon the sense power of the thought.


[2476]
TSAD MA YANG TSIG GSAL LAS, MNGON RJES GNYIS DANG LUNG GI TSAD MA DANG NYER ‘JAL LAM DPES ‘JAL BA’I TSAD MA BZHI BSHAD PA NI RTZOD ZLOG RTZA ‘GREL LA BRTEN PA’O,,

As far as accurate perception, A Clarification of the Verses makes the presentation of four different forms of this perception; these are the two of direct and deductive; accurate perception based upon scriptural authority; and “closely engaging” accurate perception, which we can also call accurate perception that engages in its object through the use of a metaphor.  This presentation into four is based upon the root text and autocommentary to Stopping All Argument.


[2477]
TSAD MA PHYI MA GNYIS NI RJES DPAG TU ‘DU LA BZHI BRGYA PA’I ‘GREL PA LAS KYANG, DNGOS PO THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU SHES PAS GO BAR BYA BA NI MA YIN GYI RJES SU DPAG PAS RTOGS PAR BYA BA YANG YOD DO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

The latter two types of accurate perception can be grouped into the deductive form of this perception; and as the commentary to the 400 Verses puts it, “Not all entities are such that they can be grasped by direct forms of perception; there are also those which must be perceived through the deductive form.”


[2478]
MNGON SUM TSAD MA LA LUGS GZHAN NAS BZHI BSHAD PA’I RANG RIG MNGON SUM [f. 180a] BKAG LA YID KYI MNGON SUM YANG TSAD MA NAS BSHAD PA LTAR MI BZHED DE,

As far as direct forms of accurate perception, apperception as a direct type which appears in the presentation of four types by other systems is denied; and further, direct accurate perception as it is explained in the classics on accurate perception is not accepted either.


[2479]
BZHI BRGYA PA’I ‘GREL PA LAS, CHOS MNGON PA NAS GZUGS SOGS LNGA RE RE ZHING DBANG PO DANG YID SHES KYIS SHES PAR BYA BAR GSUNGS PA’I DON ‘CHAD PA NA, RNAM PAR SHES PA GNYIS KYIS DON GCIG RNAM PAR SHES PA MA YIN TE, GCIG NI YUL GYI RNAM PA DNGOS SU GCOD PAR BYED PA STE GANG DANG POR SKYE BA’O,,

The commentary to The 400 Verses has a section where it is giving an explanation of the part in the works on higher knowledge which refer to each of the five of form and the rest; the sense powers; and what is perceived by the consciousness of the thought.  Here it says that it is not the case that two kinds of consciousness can be aware of a single object—because one of them will directly discern the aspect of the object; and this will be the first to arise.



Rejecting rebuttal on another consciousness

[2480]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second step from above: rejecting rebuttal concerning another consciousness of the thoughts.


[2481]
DNGOS SU BYED PA NYID DU RNAM PAR SHES PA MA YIN TE, DBANG PO’I RNAM PAR SHES PA’I STOBS KYIS DE LTAR RTOG CING SKYE BA NA, DES KYANG DON DE RNAM PAR SHES SO ZHES NYE BAR ‘DOGS SO,

We see the following quotation:

Consciousness is not something that happens through a direct process; it occurs rather through the force of the consciousness of the sense power, which perceives the object in a certain way and arises.  Only then can it perceive the object.


[2482]
ZHES DANG PO DBANG SHES KYIS GZUGS SOGS KYI DON DE DNGOS SU RIG LA, YID SHES KYIS DBANG SHES KYI STOBS KYIS RIG GI DBANG SHES BZHIN DU DNGOS SU MI RIG PAR GSUNGS SHING DRAN PAR YANG GSUNGS SO,,

What this is saying is that first the consciousness of the sense power perceives the object—something like visible form or the like—directly.  The consciousness of the thought then perceives the object, through the force of the consciousness of the sense power.  It does not, however directly perceive the object in the same, direct way as the consciousness of the sense power does.  Which is to say, that is also how it recollects.


[2483]
YANG BZHI BRGYA PA’I ‘GREL PA LAS, TSOR BA LA SOGS PA LTAR NYAMS SU MYONG BA’I RNAM PA YANG MA YIN LA, GZUGS DANG SGRA LA SOGS PA BZHIN DBANG PO’I SGO NAS YONGS SU BCAD PAR BYA BA YANG MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS 

The commentary to the 400 Verses also says,

It does not display an aspect of experience which is similar to that of feeling or the like.  But then again neither is it similar to the case with things like visible form and sound, where the final discernment is made through the sense power.


[2484]
MNGON GYUR DU ‘JAL BA LA DBANG SHES KYIS GZUGS SOGS GCOD PA LTA BU DANG, TSOR BA BDE SDUG LA SOGS PA LTAR NANG DU NYAMS MYONG GIS YONGS SU GCOD PA GNYIS GSUNGS SO,,

What this is saying is that there are two variations of discernment: one as in the case of where the consciousness of the sense power would make its discernment through direct consideration; and the other where something like feelings of pleasure or pain would do it through an internal experience.


[2485]
DE GNYIS KYI PHYI MA NI GZHI DUS NAS KYANG KHAS BLANG DGOS LA, MNGON SUM GYI TSAD MA BZHI LAS MANG BA ‘DIR YANG MA BSHAD PA’I PHYIR DANG, RNAL ‘BYOR MNGON SUM [f. 180b] DANG DBANG PO’I MNGON SUM DANG, RANG RIG MNGON SUM TSAD MAR GZHAG TU MI RUNG BAS, YID KYI MNGON SUM DU BZHAG STE, YID KYI MNGON SUM TSAD MA NI TSAD MA BA DANG MI MTHUN MOD, DE LTA NA’ANG YID KYI MNGON SUM TSAD MA MI ‘DOD PA NI MIN NO,,

This is because; first of all, of these two, one would have to agree that the latter could occur as well during the period of the original condition; while in this case they don’t talk about there being more than four different types of direct, accurate perception.  Moreover, it would be inappropriate to posit the direct perception of a deep practitioner; the direct perception of the sense powers; or direct perception through apperception as being forms of accurate perception; and so we’d have to say that this was a form of direct perception in the thoughts.  And yes we would have to agree that a direct form of accurate perception for the thoughts was at odds with the schools dedicated to the study of accurate perception; but despite this fact, it’s not as though one would never agree to a direct form of accurate perception for the thoughts.


[2486]
DE LTAR NA TSOR BA ZHES PA NI BYED PA PO DANG BYED PA DANG LAS DANG ‘BREL BA’I TSIG YIN PAS GANG ZAG ‘DIS TSOR BA DANG, BYED PA ‘DIS TSOR BA DANG, ‘DI ‘DRA BA ZHIG TSOR BA ZHES PA GSUM DU ‘GYUR RO,,

As such, when we use the expression “feelings,” this is a term which is related to the agent in an action; to the action; and to the act.  That is, there are three variations here: you can say that “the person felt something”; or you can say “this action had a feeling”; or “what was felt was like this.”


[2487]
DE’I GNYIS PA NI TSAD MA STE SEMS BYUNG TSOR BA’O,,

The second variation refers to the accurate perception; that is, the mental function of feelings.


[2488]
GSUM PA NI GZHAL BYA STE BDE BA DANG SDUG BSNGAL DANG BTANG SNYOMS SO,,

The third variation would be a reference to what we had under consideration; that is, pleasure, pain, or a neutral sensation.


[2489]
‘DI YANG YID SHES KYI DBANG DU BYAS KYI DBANG SHES KYI TSOR BA GSUM GYIS GZUGS SGRA SOGS YONGS SU GCOD DE, DE’I ‘GRUB TSUL NI SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN NO,,

Now the three types of feeling for awareness of the senses relative to the consciousness of the thought discern objects such as visual form and sound; how we establish this follows what we described earlier.


[2490]
‘O NA YID SHES KYI TSOR BAS BDE SDUG SOGS MNGON GYUR DU GCOD NA RANG RIG TU MI ‘GYUR RAM SNYAM NA,

In this case then though one may come with the following question: “If it’s the case that feelings of the consciousness of the thought discern pleasure and pain and the like in a direct way, then wouldn’t that constitute apperception?”


[2491]
SKYON MED DE BKAG PA’I RANG RIG NI SHES PA THAMS CAD KHA NANG LTA LA RIG BYA DANG RIG BYED THA DAD PAR SNANG BA NUB PA’I ‘DZIN RNAM YAN GAR BA YIN ZHING,

And yet there’s no problem here.  The apperception that we deny constitutes a state where all the awareness is focused inward; it is a distinct aspect of holding objects where all appearance of the thing known and the thing knowing it as separate entities is suppressed.


[2492]
‘DIR NI NYAMS SU MYONG BA KHYAD PAR CAN TSOR BA’I MTSAN NYID DU MDO SDER GSUNG LA, ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD LAS KYANG BDE BA DANG SDUG BSNGAL NYAMS SU MYONG NGO ZHES BRJOD PA’I PHYIR,

Here in this case, the collection of sutras describes the definition of feeling as an exceptional form of experiencing.  Moreover, even in the parlance of the world they say things like “I had an experience of pleasure, or of pain.”


[2493]
MYONG BYA DANG MYONG BYED THA DAD PA NYID DU SNANG BA’I PHYIR NA PHYOGS SNGA MA’I RANG RIG DANG MI GCIG GO ,DE’I PHYIR BDE BA SOGS NYAMS SU MYONG BAS GRUB PA NYID KYIS TSOR BA GRUB BO,,

And so because the thing experienced and the thing experiencing it appear with certainty as separate from one another, what we’re describing here is not the same as the apperception accepted by the earlier opponent.  As such, we can say that an occurrence of feeling is confirmed by the very fact of there having been an experience of pleasure or the like.


[2494]
YID SHES KYI NGOR KENG RUS [f. 181a] GSAL SNANG SOGS CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED PA’I GZUGS SNANG BA NA, YID SHES LA DE RNAMS KYI RNAM PA SHAR BA’I SGO NAS DES DE RNAMS GRUB PA NA DE ‘DZIN GYI SHES PA ‘GRUB PA NI SNGAR DANG ‘DRA STE, YUL DE RNAMS NI YID KYI SHES PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’O,,

And so let’s say that form which is part of the door of sense of all things makes its appearance, in the form of a vivid image of skeletons for the consciousness of the thought.  The consciousness of the thought here confirms these images by way of their having appeared to this consciousness.  And then establishing that an awareness is perceiving these objects is accomplished in the same way as we described it before.  That is, these objects are essentially separate from the awareness of the thoughts.


[2495]
BDAG ‘DZIN GNYIS LTA BU’I YID SHES KYI SHES PA DE JI LTAR ‘GRUB PA NI, TSIG GSAL LAS, GAL TE MTSAN GZHI’AM RANG GI MTSAN NYID DAM SPYI’I MTSAN NYID KYANG RUNG STE, ‘JIG RTEN NA YOD NA NI THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR BYA BA YIN PA’I PHYIR LKOG TU MA GYUR BA YIN TE, DE’I PHYIR DE’I YUL CAN GYI RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG LHAN CIG TU MNGON SUM NYID DU RNAM PAR BZHAG GO ,ZHES GSUNGS PA ‘DIS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

How is it then that we establish perceptions of the consciousness of the thought for things like the two forms of the tendency to believe in some kind of self-existence?  The answer to this question can be understood from the following description found in A Clarification of the Verses—

It doesn’t matter whether we’re talking about a defining occurrence of something; or the definition of something; or the general characteristics of the thing.  When things are said to exist in the everyday world, then all of them are objects which can be observed directly.  As such, they are not what we would call “recondite.”  And for this reason, they are established exclusively as being direct, part & parcel with the relevant subject state of awareness.


[2496]
DE LA MTSAN GZHI DANG MTSON BYA GNYIS SKAD DOD GCIG PAS LO TZ’A BA KHA CIG GIS MTSAN GZHIR BSGYUR, KHA CIG GIS MTSON BYAR BSGYUR RO,,

The original Sanskrit terms for the expressions “defining occurrence” and “thing being defined” are identical; and so certain of the ancient master translators of Tibet rendered the term as “defining occurrence,” and while others rendered it as “thing being defined.” 


[2497]
DES NA ‘DIS MTSON PAR BYED PA’I MTSAN NYID DANG, ‘DI MTSON PAR BYA BA’I MTSAN GZHI THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR BYA BAR BSHAD PA NI, TSAD MA BZHIR BYAS PA’I MNGON SUM TSAD MA NGOS ‘DZIN PA’I SKABS YIN PA’I PHYIR, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAS MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR STON PA YANG MIN LA,

And so let’s take a look at the definition which acts to define the thing; and the objects of the definition—those defining occurrences.  All of these are described as being things that we observe through direct perception.  And this is done in the context of the direct form of accurate perception, as it is identified within the division of accurate perception into four different types.  As such, we can say further that it is not refering to the way in which omniscience itself perceives objects directly.


[2498]
‘DI NYID KYI MJUG THOGS SU LKOG TU GYUR PA’I YUL CAN RTAGS BSGRUB PAR BYA BA LA MI ‘KHRUL BA LAS SKYES PA’I SHES PA NI RJES SU DPAG PA’O,

And then just below the section in A Clarification of the Verses mentioned above, we have the statement that—

Deduction then we describe as a state of mind where the subject state that holds to an object which is recondite is unmistaken, due to confirmation by a logical reason.


[2499]
ZHES GSUNGS PAS RANG SPYI THAMS CAD MNGON GYUR YIN GYI, LKOG GYUR MIN PAR STON PA’ANG MIN NO,,

As such, we can say that typical expressions of objects in the world and the general archetypes of those same objects are all forms of manifest reality; but this is not to say that they can’t be recondite as well.


[2500]
DES NA RANG [f. 181b] SPYI GNYIS GANG LA DMIGS PA’I SHES PA LA’ANG DE GNYIS KYI SNANG BA ‘BYUNG LA, SNANG BA DE NYID NI SHES PA DE’I YUL MNGON SUM STE DE DANG DE’I YUL CAN GYI RNAM SHES GNYIS KA MNGON SUM DU ‘JOG PA NI, YUL LA MNGON SUM GYI SGRA DNGOS DANG YUL CAN LA BTAGS NAS ‘JUG PAR BZHED PA’O,,

And so we can say that the states of mind that focus upon these two—the typical expressions and the general archetypes—take on an aspect of the same two.  And that aspect itself is the manifest object of those states of mind.  Which means that we can describe both the objects here, and the states of mind holding those objects, as being direct, or manifest.  And what we say is that the word “direct” here is being applied to the object involved directly; and to the subject involved in only a nominal way.


[2501]
SHES PA GANG LA GANG GI RNAM PA SNANG BA’I SNANG BA THAMS CAD SHES PA DE’I YUL MNGON SUM YIN NA, SNANG BA DE SHES PA DE LA MNGON GYUR YIN ZHING, DE YANG DE LA MI SLU BA’I SHES PA YIN NA ‘JIG RTEN NA MI SLU BA’I SHES PA LA TSAD MAR GRAGS PAS TSAD MAR ‘GYUR BA ZHIG ‘ONG NGO,,

Any time the aspect of any object makes its appearance to any state of mind as the direct object of that mental state, we would say that this appearance is—for that state of mind—direct.  And if the state of mind involved is a perception which is not deceived, then we would follow what the everday world says about an undeceived state of mind constituting accurate perception.  Which means that the state of mind here would then become an “accurate” one.


[2502]
DE’I TSE GZHAL BYA SNANG BA DE SHES PA DE’I GRUB PA NA YUL CAN ‘GRUB PA NI SNGAR BZHIN YIN NO,,

At this point then, if the object under consideration—the appearance—is confirmed for that state of mind, then that state is confirmed as the subject; just as we described it earlier on.


[2503]
DE’I PHYIR BDAG ‘DZIN GNYIS LTA BU LA YANG BDAG GNYIS KYI SNANG BA MNGON SUM DU ‘CHAR LA, DE’I TSE GZHAL BYA SNANG BA MNGON GYUR DE YUL CAN DES ‘GRUB PA SOGS SNGAR DANG ‘DRA STE, DES ZHEN YUL LA ‘KHRUL PA GZHAN YANG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

As such, we can say even with things like the two forms of the tendency to grasp to some self-nature of things that the appearance of two “selfs” here is made directly.  And we can also say at that point things like the fact that the object under consideration is making its appearance directly is confirmed by the subject state of mind; just as we did this earlier.  And from this we can also understand moreover that this state of mind is mistaken towards the object that it thinks it sees.


[2504]
DE LTAR SHES PA RNAMS YUL DU SNANG BA’I SNANG YUL MNGON GYUR GRUB PAR ‘DRA LA, BDAG GNYIS DANG BDAG MED GNYIS DANG, GZUGS SOGS RTAG MI RTAG SOGS LA TSAD MAR ‘GRO MI ‘GRO’I KHYAD PAR CHEN PO YOD PAS, BLO LA TSAD MA DANG TSAD MIN GYI RNAM PAR BZHAG PA’ANG ‘GRUB BO,,

As such, it is in a similar way that we establish that the objects which make their appearance, showing themselves as objects to different states of mind, are direct objects.  At the same time, there is a huge difference between whether or not states of mind are accurate perception relative to the two supposed self-natures and the two absences of any self-nature; and between form and the rest, and things being unchanging & changing.  And thus it is that we can set forth the entire presentation of states of mind being accurate perception, or perception which is not accurate.


[2505]
YID SHES SNANG YUL LA TSAD MAR BSHAD PA DE RNAMS KYANG YUL MNGON GYUR DE RNAMS LA YID KYI MNGON SUM TSAD MAR BYA STE, MTHA’ GZHAN KHEGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

In cases as well where we describe instances of consciousness of the thought as being accurate perception towards the objects which appear to them, what we are saying is that these are a direct form of accurate perception of the thought, towards objects which are themselves direct.  And this is because we have eliminated the other possibilities here.


[2506]
RANG RIG MNGON SUM TSAD MAR MI ‘GYUR TE, YUL DE LA GNYIS KYI SNANG BA DANG BCAS [f. 182a] PA’I PHYIR RO,,

It is not the case though that apperception could constitute a direct form of accurate perception; for it is tied up with duality towards its particular object.


[2507]
MNYAM GZHAG GI SHES PA ZAG PA MED PA LA GNYIS SNANG NUB KYANG CHOS NYID DANG DE GNYIS RIG BYA RIG BYED DU ‘GRO BA DANG, SHES PA THAMS CAD KHA NANG LTA LA GNYIS SNANG LOG KYANG RIG BYA RIG BYED DU ‘GRO BA GNYIS RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MI MTSUNGS TE,
	
This duality is suppressed in the case of an unstained form of a state of mind deep inside of balanced meditation; nonetheless, the fact that the true nature of things and this state of mind constitute the object known and the knowing subject is not at all equivalent to a case where all the forms of consciousness are directed inwards, and duality is suppressed in this way, but you still have something known and something else knowing it.


[2508]
PHYI MA LA NI GRUB MTHAS BTAGS PA’I YUL YUL CAN TZAM MA GTOGS PA RTOG PAS YID CI TZAM GTAD KYANG RIG BYA DANG RIG BYED KYI SNANG BA GNYIS MI ‘CHAR LA, SNGA MA LA NI YID GTAD DE BLTAS PA NA YUL CAN SHES PA DANG YUL CHOS NYID KYI RNAM PA THA DAD PA NGES PAR ‘CHAR BA’I PHYIR RO,,

In the latter case, there is nothing more than an object and subject which are imputed by certain schools of thought; that is, no matter how much you direct your thoughts towards them, there will appear to you neither the aspect of something to be known, nor something which knows it.  If though you direct your thoughts towards the former—if you observe it—it is a certainty that a discrete subject state of mind and object of the very nature of things will make their appearance.


[2509]
MNYAM GZHAG RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA’I YE SHES KYIS RANG GI GZHAL BYA CHOS NYID GRUB PA NA, DE’I STOBS KYIS YUL CAN GYI YE SHES ‘GRUB PA LA, 

When the non-conceptual wisdom of deep, balanced meditation acts to confirm the object that it takes under consideration—that is, the very nature of things—then by the power of this happening, the subject state of wisdom is then established.


[2510]
RIG BYA RIG BYED SO SOR SNANG BA’I GNYIS SNANG LOG PA DANG, GZHAN LUGS KYIS SHES PA THAMS CAD KHA NANG LTA LA GNYIS SNANG LOG PA’I ‘DZIN RNAM YAN GAR BA ‘DOD PA DANG MI MTSUNGS PA’I KHYAD PAR NI ‘BRAS BU’I SA’I SKABS SU ‘CHAD PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

Now there are positions where we find a belief in a discrete subject aspect which is the blocking of duality in which what is known and what knows it appear to be separate; or the blocking of duality where, according to the other systems, all of the states of mind are focused inward.  But there is a specific point which is not the same as these, and we will be giving an explanation of that when we reach the section of our text which treats the spiritual levels which are a result of our practice.


[2511]
‘DI ‘DRA BA’I RNAM GZHAG PHRA MO NI RANG GIS GZHAN LA, ‘DI YI YOD PA GANG GIS SHES PAR ‘GYUR, ZHES SOGS KYI GNOD PA BRJOD PA TSUR LA BZLOG PA NA,

And so suppose that our opponent turns the tables and addresses us with the same fault in our argument that we originally addressed to them, considering this subtle presentation with the question, “And what is it that allows you to understand the existence of this thing?”


[2512]
CHEN PO RNAMS KYI LUGS SO SO BA’I RNAM GZHAG PHRA MO MI SHES SHING, RANG GI LUGS NGES DON GYI LUNG GI DON PHRA MO DANG, SHIN TU RTOGS DKA’ BA’I RIGS LAM PHRA MO NAS ‘DREN MI SHES PA RNAMS KYIS,

Which is to say, there are those who have no understanding of the different and subtle presentations made by the great ones; or of the subtle import of citations even in their own system which happen to be literal; or how to draw these truths from extremely subtle logical arguments here which are extremely difficult to grasp.


[2513]
KHO BO’I PHYOGS LA KHAS LEN MED PAS SKYON DU MI ‘GYUR [f. 182b] RO, ZHES BSNYON ‘DINGS PA TZAM LA RE BA RNAMS LA MI DGOS KYANG,

Now it may be the case that there are those who put their hopes in the positions of people who are nothing more than nut cases—those who say “There’s no problem here, because our position is unique in that we take no position at all.”  The points we have made here would be of no use to them.


[2514]
SKYE BO MKHAS PA MDZANGS SHING PHRA BA’I BLO CAN RIGS PA’I GNAD PHRA MOS SKYON YON SO SOR ‘BYED PA’I LAM MA MTHONG BAR YID MI CHES PA RNAMS KYI

And for their part they have had no sight into the path where truly wise individuals—great masters with the capacity to delve into the subtle keys of reasoning—divide out the weaknesses and the strengths of ideas; which is to say, they have no belief in these.


[2515]
DON DU BSAMS NAS, BDAG GIS LUGS DAM PA ‘DI SKYON MED PAR ‘JOG PA’I PHYOGS ‘DI’I SGO TZAM ZHIG BSTAN PA YIN NO,,

I for my part was giving some thought to the opinions of these individuals, and decided then to make the presentation I have offered here, just a brief sketch of ideas which serve to demonstrate how this perfect position is free of any fault at all.


[2516]
‘O NA NGAS SNGON PO MTHONG NGO ZHES DRAN PA’I NGA NI GANG ZAG YIN LA, SNGO ‘DZIN GYI SHES PA DANG DE GNYIS ‘GAL BAS DE LTAR DRAN PA DE SNGO ‘DZIN DRAN PAR JI LTAR ‘GYUR SNYAM NA,

The following thought might then occur to someone—

When we say “I saw that patch of blue” and thus recollect a “me,” that is a person.  And being a person is contradictory to being a state of mind which perceives the color blue.  How is it then that this recollection of having perceived blue can occur?


[2517]
SNGO ‘DZIN GYI MIG SHES DANG SNGON PO MTHONG MKHAN GYI GANG ZAG GNYIS ‘GAL YANG, SHES PA DES SNGON PO MTHONG BA LA BRTEN NAS NGAS MTHONG NGO ZHES ‘JOG PA MI ‘GAL BA

It is true, first of all, that being the visual awareness which holds to a patch of blue, and being a person who is someone that has seen blue, are two mutually exclusive entities.  Nonetheless, it is still no contradiction to say “I saw the blue, by relying upon how that state of mind saw the blue.”


[2518]
BZHIN DU SNGO ‘DZIN GYI SHES PAS SNGON PO MTHONG BA DRAN PA LA BRTEN NAS NGAS SNGAR SNGON PO MTHONG NGO ZHES GANG ZAG DRAN PA DES SNGO ‘DZIN GYI SHES PA DRAN PA YANG CI ZHIG ‘GAL,

How then could you say that there was any contradiction in stating, “I saw some blue before,” based on the fact that you could recollect how the perception of blue saw the blue?  That is, recalling the person enables us to recall the state of mind that was holding to the blue.



Other proofs of illogic

[2519]
GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to our third part from before: a demonstration that apperception is illogical even according to other proofs.


	[2520]
[VI.76]
Tasmāt svasaṃvedanam asti naiva
kenānya tantra grahaṇaṃ tava syāt,
Kartuś ca karma kriyayoś ca naikyaṃ
tenaiva tasya grahaṇaṃ na yuktam.

,DE PHYIR RANG RIG YOD PA MA YIN NA,
,KHYOD KYI GZHAN DBANG GANG GIS ‘DZIN PAR ‘GYUR,
,BYED PO LAS DANG BYA BA GCIG MIN PAS,
,DE NYID KYIS DE ‘DZIN PAR RIGS MA YIN,

		Therefore, apperception
		Is something that
		Doesn’t exist;

		What is it then
		That holds to your
		Dominated entities?

		The agent,
		The object of the action,
		And the act
		Are not one & the same.

		As such,
		It would be inappropriate
		To say that this
		Were doing the holding.


[2521]
GANG GI PHYIR DE LTA YIN PA DE’I PHYIR RANG RIG YOD PA MA YIN NA, SEMS TZAM PA KHYOD KYI GZHAN DBANG SHES PA GANG GIS ‘DZIN PAR ‘GYUR SHING GCOD PA’I BYED PA PO DANG, BCAD PA’I LAS SU BYA BA SHING DANG, SHING GCOD PA’I BYA BA GSUM GCIG MIN PAS SHES PA DE NYID KYIS DE ‘DZIN PAR RIGS PA MA YIN NO,,

For the reason that we have expressed above, we can say that therefore apperception is something that doesn’t exist, and we ask you members of the Mind Only school just what kind of state of mind it is that holds to your dominated entities.  After all, these three—the agent that acts to cut a tree; and the tree which is the object of the action of the cutting; and the act of cutting the tree itself—are not one & the same.  As such, it would be inappropriate to say that this state of mind itself were doing the holding.


[2522]
‘DI’I GNOD PA ‘BAB TSUL NI BDEN GNYIS RANG ‘GREL LAS SHES PA’I BDAG NYID LA NI, RDUL PHRA RAB DAG DANG GNYIS PO MED PA’I DNGOS PO’I NGO BO MI SNANG NGO, ,MI SNANG BA LA NI THA SNYAD MED DO ZHES PA [f. 183a] GSAL TE,

The way in which the problem applies here is clearly expressed in the autocommentary to Distinguishing Between the Two Realities:

It is not the case that smallest particles of matter, or some kind of essential nature to things where they were beyond any duality, could ever make their appearance to an embodiment of perception; and there is no term that can be applied to something that never makes its appearance.


[2523]
SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI SHES PA KHA NANG LTA LA GNYIS SNANG MED PA’I MYONG TZAM KHO RANG GI RIG BYA DANG, KHO RANG DE’I RIG BYED DU ‘JOG PA LA DE LA JI TZAM GTAD KYANG RTOG PA LA YANG RIG BYA DANG RIG BYED GNYIS SU MI SNANG BA DE LA RIG BYA RIG BYED KYI BYA BYED ‘JOG NA, BYED PA PO DANG LAS DANG BYA BA GZHAN YANG GCIG TU HA CANG THAL BA ‘JUG PA YIN NO,,

As we explained before, it doesn’t matter how much we focus our minds towards a state of mind which is free of subject & object duality; which is only an experiencing entity—something which can be said to be both what it itself knows, and also the one doing the knowing.  It will never be the case then this could ever appear to our conception as both what is known and what does the knowing.  And if we were then to posit these were indeed act and actor in the the sense of what is known and what knows, it would be just too much to say that the agent and the act and the action—all separate things—would be one & the same.


[2524]
DES NA SLOB DPON CHEN PO YE SHES SNYING PO NI, SEMS TZAM PA’I RANG RIG DANG NYAN THOS SDE PA’I RDUL CHA MED GNYIS YOD MED JI LTA BA BZHIN MTSUNGS PAR BZHED DE, RDUL CHA MED LA YANG YUL GYI GO SA GNON PA NI DGOS LA, DE’I RNAM PA SHAR BA NA PHYOGS KYI CHA BCAS MIN PA ‘CHAR SA MED DO,,

Thus it is then that the great master Jnanagarbha is here taking the position that these two—the apperception posited by those of the Mind Only, and the partless physical particles accepted by the Listener schools—are equivalent, in either existing or not.  That is, even a particle of matter which had no sides would have to occupy a particular space; and if it were to appear as such, then there is no way that it could ever make this appearance without sides in different directions.


[2525]
DES NA DE GNYIS KYI RIG BYA RIG BYED DANG PHYOGS KYI CHA MED NI GRUB MTHAS BTAGS PA ‘BA’ ZHIG GO ,DES NA DE GNYIS SNANG YANG MA NGES PA YIN PA YANG BKAG STE, BDEN GNYIS RANG ‘GREL LAS, GAL TE SNANG BA BZHIN DU YANG DE NGES PAR MI ZIN SNYAM NA, DES NA CI DE LTA BU LA NI THA SNYAD MED DO, ,SNANG ZHES BYA BA YANG YID CHES PA MED PA’I PHYIR MNA’ CHU BTUNG DGOS SO, ZHES SNANG BA LA YANG SGRUB BYED MNA’ TZAM DU ZAD DO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

As such, we can say that the ideas of these two groups—something we know which is also the knower; and particles with no directions to them—are nothing more than inventions of their respective systems.  And as such, we are in addition denying the idea that the way things appear as subjects & objects could itself be indefinite; as the autocommentary to the Two Realities again puts it,

Suppose you think to yourself, “Even as this makes its appearance, it is not with certainty perceived.”  But the fact is that when something is like that, there can be no term to describe it.  To simply state that something was appearing would have to be just something that you swore was true.

Which is to say, the only proof you could give for the thing indeed making an appearance would be no more than your swearing it were so.


[2526]
LANG KAR GSHEGS PA LAS GSUNGS PA’I RIGS PAS KYANG RANG RIG MI RIGS TE,
,JI LTAR RAL GRIS RANG GI SO,
,GCOD PAR MI BYED SOR MOS NI,
,RANG LA REG PAR MI BYED LTAR,
,RANG RIG SEMS KYANG DE BZHIN NO,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

The logic described in the Journey to Langka also describes how the idea of apperception is illogical—

A knife cannot cut
Its own blade;

The tip of a finger
Cannot touch itself.

A state where the mind
Could know itself
Would be just the same.



Things the same as no one

[2527]
BZHI PA NI,

Which brings us to our fourth part from above: establishing that dominated entities which existed through some nature of their own would be the equivalent of the child of a barren woman.


	[2528]
[VI.77]
Ajñāya mānātmakam apyajātaṃ
bhāvo yadi syāt paratantra rūpaḥ,
Vandhyāsutenāpakṛtaṃ parasya
kiṃ nāma yenāsya na vetti sattvam.

,GAL TE SKYE BA MED CING MA SHES PA’I,
,BDAG CAN GZHAN DBANG NGO BO’I DNGOS YOD NA,
,GANG GIS NA ‘DI YOD PA MI RIGS PA,
,[f. 208a] GZHAN LA MO GSHAM BUS NOD CI ZHIG BSKYAL,

		Suppose that
		There is nothing
		Which can start,

		And that
		There does exist
		An entity which is
		A dominated one
	
		And has a nature
		Such that it is
		Not perceived.

		There is yet
		Another why
		It would be illogical
		To say that such existed [f. 208a]:

		The child of a
		Barren woman
		Has done so much damage.


[2529]
GZHAN DBANG BDAG DANG GZHAN LAS MI SKYE BAR NI SNGAR BSTAN ZIN LA, DE ‘JAL [f. 183b] BA’I RANG RIG KYANG MED PAR DA LTA NYID DU BSTAN PAS,

We have already, previously, demonstrated that dominated entities can grow neither from themselves, nor from something other than themselves.  And we have just shown how apperception is not something which could exist.


[2530]
GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED CING TSAD MAS MA SHES PA’I BDAG NYID CAN GYI GZHAN DBANG RANG GIS NGO BOS GRUB PA’I DNGOS PO YOD NA, RGYU MTSAN GANG GIS NA ‘DI YOD PAR MI RIGS PA GZHAN TE

Suppose then that there is nothing which can start through any nature of its own; but that there does exist an entity which exists through some nature of its own which is a dominated entity and has a nature such that it is not perceived by any accurate perception.  There is yet another reasoning why it would be illogical to say that such a thing existed.


[2531]
SEMS TZAM PA KHYOD LA MO GSHAM GYI BUS GNOD PA CI ZHIG BSKYAL NAS DE YOD PAR MI ‘DOD DE YOD PAR ‘DOD DGOS TE, ‘DI LTAR MO GSHAM GYI BU ZHES BYA BA SPROS PA THAMS CAD LAS ‘DAS SHING ‘PHAGS PA’I YE SHES KYI SPYOD YUL DU GYUR PA, BRJOD DU MED PA’I RANG BZHIN CAN ZHIG YOD DO ZHES ‘DI YANG YOD PA NYID DU ‘DOD PAR GYIS SHIG

And so how can you proponents of the Mind Only school refuse to accept the existence of the child of a barren woman, when this child has done so much damage to you?  You should be saying that they actually do exist.  After all, you are the ones who say that there is a child of this woman who is free of all projections of reality, and who is the object that the wisdom of the realized beings engages in; something which has a nature which is beyond all describing.  And so you should also be saying that this impossible child exists as well!



Failure of the Mind Only

[2532]
,GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second step from before: a demonstration that the Mind Only system fails from the viewpoint of both of the realities.


	[2533]
[VI.78]
Yadānya tantraṃ na samasti kiṃcit
kiṃ sāṃvṛtānāṃ hi nibandhanaṃ syāt,
Dravyasya lobhena parasya naṣṭāḥ 
sarvā vyavasthā api loka siddhāḥ.

,GANG TSE GZHAN DBANG CUNG ZAD YOD MIN NA,
,KUN RDZOB PA YI RGYUR NI GANG ZHIG ‘GYUR,
,GZHAN GYI LTAR NA RDZAS LA CHAGS PA YIS,
,’JIG RTEN GRAGS PA’I RNAM BZHAG KUN KYANG BRLAG

	At such point
That there did not exist
Even the slightest
Dominated entities,

Then how could
Something ever exist
As a deceptive reason?

If it accords to
These other ones,
Attached to thinking
Of that substance,

Then the way that
The everyday world
Posits how things exist
Is completely lost.


[2534]
GANG YANG DNGOS PO BRTAGS {%BTAGS} PAR YOD PA’I RGYUR ‘GYUR ZHING, ZHES SMRAS PA DE YANG GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD NA RIGS PA ZHIG NA,

We see the lines that refer to “anything it is that could be a cause for entities which exist only by imputation.”  These are referring to yet another line of reasoning which would obtain if dominated entities were to exist through some nature of their own.


[2535]
GANG GI TSE GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MIN NA, THA SNYAD KUN RDZOB PA’I ‘KHRUL PA’I RGYU STE GZHI RDZAS SU GRUB PAR NI GANG ZHIG ‘GYUR TE CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO,,

At such point that there did not exist even the slightest dominated entities which existed through some nature of their own, then how could something ever exist as a deceptive, a nominal, reason for error—how could the foundation here exist substantially?  There could exist not the slightest such thing.


[2536]
DES NI GZHAN DBANG DON DAM DU GRUB PAR ‘DOD PAS DON DAM LAS NYAMS PAR BSTAN NO,,

What this is saying is that those who accept the idea that dominated entities could exist in some ultimate way have degenerated from the idea of the ultimate.


[2537]
DE’I PHYIR SEMS TZAM PA ‘DI LA ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD KYI RGYU GANG YIN PA DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS YOD PA MIN PAS, KYE MA KYE HUD GZHAN SEMS TZAM PA’I LTAR NA NGES DON MTHAR THUG PA ‘BYED PA’I SHES RAB KYI RTZAL MED PAS GZHAN DBANG GI RDZAS SHES TZAM LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA’I CHAGS PA YI SGO NAS, GZHAN DBANG GI BUM PA SO MA BTANG BAR,

As such, let’s consider these followers of the Mind Only.  If it is the fact that what we say is that the cause in the parlance of the world is not something that could exist through any essential nature of its own, then oh my gosh!  According to these other ones—the Mind Only (since they possess none of the fluency of wisdom which makes distinctions regarding the ultimate point of what was truly intended)—then dominated entities exist only as a mental substance, and are still real.  These thinkers are attached to thinking of them thus, as real, and in this manner they approach a clay pot of the concept of dominated entities that was never properly fired.


[2538]
TSUL MIN GYI DPYAD PA CHU DANG ‘DRA BA BLUGS [f. 184a] NAS, RANG GI BLO GROS KYI TSUL NGAN PA’I PHYIR TE RGYU MTSAN GYIS, ‘JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA’I RNAM GZHAG ‘JIG RTEN KHO NA LAS GRUB PA ‘DUG CIG SONG ZHIG BYOS SHIG ,CES PA SOGS DANG

And then into this unready vessel they pour the water of their faulty thinking, which demonstrates the awful workings of their level of intelligence—the thinking that forces them to say things like “the way that the everyday world posits how things exist is something that only works for the world.  This is how it is, and this is how we should take it.”


[2539]
DE BZHIN DU PHYI’I GZUGS DANG PHYI’I DMIGS PA LAS SKYES PA’I TSOR BA LA SOGS PA DE DAG KUN KYANG BRLAG PA STE ‘JIG PAR BYED DO,,

And then in this same way they completely lose—they completely demolish—everything such as how feelings arise from outer form: from outer objects of perception.


[2540]
DE’I PHYIR SEMS TZAM PA ‘DI LA RGUD PA ‘BA’ ZHIG SRID PAR ‘GYUR GYI, MNGON PAR MTHO BA STE PHUL DU BYUNG BA’I GO ‘PHANG NI ‘THOB PA MA YIN NO,,

Thus it seems the case that these Mind Only fellows have only brought trouble upon themselves; and they fail to reach the heights; which is to say, that most wonderful state of being.


[2541]
PHYI ROL BKAG NA SONG ZHIG LA SOGS PA YANG MED PAR ‘GYUR BA’I RIGS PAS, DE RNAMS PHYI ROL LA ‘BREL BA’O,,

Even when they try to dispel the ideas of the non-Buddhists, they are presenting reasoning which would never make anyone depart from these, for example, as they would like them to—which is to say, they actually end up aligning themselves somewhat with these very non-Buddhists.


[2542]
‘DIS NI KUN RDZOB KYI BDEN PA LAS NYAMS PAR BSTAN PA’O,,

What we have demonstrated here then is how the Mind Only school has lost the proper concept of deceptive reality.



Following the Arya

[2543]
GSUM PA NI,

With this we have reached our third step from above: a description of how—therefore—it is appropriate to follow the system of Arya Nagarjuna, exclusively.


	[2544]
[VI.79]
Ācārya Nāgārjuna pāda mārgād
bahir gatānāṃ na śivābhyupāyaḥ,
Bhraṣṭā hi te saṃvṛti tattva satyāt
tad bhraṃśataś cāsti na mokṣa siddhiḥ.

,SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB ZHABS KYI LAM LAS NI,
,PHYI ROL GYUR LA ZHI BA’I THABS MED DO,
,DE DAG KUN RDZOB DE NYID BDEN LAS NYAMS,
,DE LAS NYAMS PAS THAR PA ‘GRUB YOD MIN,

		Those who have
		Wandered away
		From the path of
		Our master, Nagarjuna,

		Lack the method
		Needed to attain peace.

		These people have lost
		The true concepts
		Of deceptive reality
		And the reality
		Of suchness.

		Once we have lost this,
		There is no possibility
		That we can achieve freedom.


[2545]
DE’I PHYIR DE LTAR SLOB DPON PHYIN CI LOG STE DRANG BA’I DON LA NGES PA’I DON DU ‘CHAD PA LAS, SANGS RGYAS KYI DGONGS PAR MA SONG BA’I RANG GI RNAM PAR RTOG PAS SBYAR BA’I LUGS KYI LAM KHO NAR ZHUGS PA, 

And so we can say that these masters are mistaken, and that what they are explaining as the literal meaning of scripture is actually the figurative meaning.  They have entered only into a path which does not represent the actual intent of the Buddhas, but rather is a system that they have simply concocted by themselves.


[2546]
SLOB DPON ‘PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB ZHABS KYIS SROL PHYE BA’I LAM LAS NI PHYI ROL TU GYUR PA LA ZHI BA MYANG ‘DAS ‘THOB PA’I THABS KYI GTZO BO MED DO,,

They have wandered away from the path of the system introduced by our master, the Realized One, Nagarjuna; and they lack the primary method which is needed to attain peace—nirvana.


[2547]
CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA, ‘DI LTAR PHYI ROL TU GYUR PA DE DAG NI KUN RDZOB KYI BDEN PA DANG DE NYID DON DAM BDEN PA LAS NGES PAR NYAMS PAR ‘GYUR LA, BDEN GNYIS DE LAS NYAMS PAS KYANG DE MA BTANG GI BAR DU THAR PA ‘GRUB PA YOD PA MIN NO,,

And why is this the case?  People who have wandered away from this particular system have—quite certainly—lost the true concepts of deceptive reality and ultimate reality: suchness.  And once we have lost this teaching on the two realities, then until we have given up those mistaken ideas there is no possibility that we can achieve freedom.


	[2548]
[VI.80]
Upāya bhūtaṃ vyavahārasatyam
upeya bhūtaṃ paramārtha satyam,
Tayor vibhāgaṃ na paraiti yo vai
mithyāvikalpaiḥ sa kumārgayātaḥ

,THA SNYAD BDEN PA THABS SU GYUR PA DANG,
,DON DAM BDEN PA THABS BYUNG GYUR PA STE,
,DE GNYIS RNAM DBYE GANG GIS MI SHES PA,
,DE NI RNAM RTOG LOG PAS LAM NGAN ZHUGS,

		There is nominal reality,
		Which becomes a method,
		And ultimate reality,
		Which comes from the method.

		Any person who fails
		To understand the divisions
		Of these two has entered
		Into a mistaken path,
		Of mistaken ideas.


[2549]
YANG CI’I PHYIR BDEN GNYIS LAS NYAMS PAS THAR PA MI ‘GRUB CE NA,

“And how is it,” one may ask, “that they have lost the concepts of the two realities, and thus cannot reach freedom?”


[2550]
THA SNYAD BDEN PA’I RNAM GZHAG MA LOG PA NI, [f. 184b] DON DAM BDEN PA JI BZHIN DU RTOGS PA’I THABS SU GYUR PA DANG, DON DAM BDEN PA JI BZHIN RTOGS PA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA’I THABS LAS BYUNG BAR GYUR PA STE, BDEN PA DE GNYIS KYI RNAM DBYE GANG GIS MI SHES PA DE NI PHYIN CI LOG GI RNAM PAR RTOG PAS LAM NGAN PAR ZHUGS PA’O,,

When we are free of any tendency to go wrong in how we set forth nominal reality, this then becomes a method to understand ultimate reality in the proper way.  And when we do grasp ultimate reality correctly, this has come from the method that we described before.  That is, any person who fails to understand the divisions of these two realities has entered into a mistaken path, due to their mistaken ideas.


[2551]
‘DIS NI THA SNYAD KYI RNAM GZHAG SKYON MED PA ZHIG MA BYUNG BAR DU DON DAM BDEN PA JI BZHIN DU MI RTOG PAR BSTAN PA’O,,

What these lines are describing is how—until such time as we arrive at a truly unmistaken presentation of the nominal—we will never grasp ultimate reality correctly.


[2552]
DE’I PHYIR KLU SGRUB KYIS SROL PHYE BA’I LUGS KHO NA’I RJES SU ‘BRANG BAR BYA’O,,

As such, we should seek to follow only that system which was introduced to the world by Nagarjuna.


[2553]
TSUL DE NYID MDOS SGRUB PA LA DE KHO NA NYID NGES PAR BSTAN PA’I TING NGE ‘DZIN LAS,
,’JIG RTEN MKHYEN PAS GZHAN LA MA GSAN PAR,
,BDEN PA ‘DI GNYIS NYID KYIS BSTAN PAR MDZAD,
,GANG ZHIG KUN RDZOB DE BZHIN DON DAM STE,
,BDEN PA GSUM PA GANG YANG MA MCHIS SO,

The exact way this works is established in sutra, and described as follows in Concentration which Reveals Suchness—

The Knower of the World,
Without hearing
These things from others,

Undertook to teach
By using these two different
Types of reality.

These were the deceptive
And the ultimate;

And it’s an impossibility
For there to exist
Any kind of third reality.


[2554]
ZHES PAS NI SANGS RGYAS KYIS RANG DBANG DU BDEN GNYIS BSTAN PA DANG SHES BYA THAMS CAD BDEN GNYIS SU GRANGS NGES PAR BSTAN NO,,

What this is saying is that the Buddha has on his own accord given the teaching on the two realities; and that all existing entities are divided among exactly two realities.


[2555]
DE NAS,
,GANG GIS BDE BAR GSHEGS LA ‘GRO BA RNAMS,
,BDE BA’I DON DU DAD PA SKYE ‘GYUR BA,
,RGYAL BAS ‘GRO BA RNAMS KYI DON SLAD DU,
,’JIG RTEN PHAN PHYIR KUN RDZOB DE BSTAN TO,
ZHES PAS NI KUN RDZOB BSTAN PA’I DGOS PA BSTAN NO,,

The same teaching then presents the following lines, in order to describe the goal of teaching deceptive reality:

There is a teaching
That was given
For the comfort
Of living beings,

So that they would
Feel faith for the one
Who had Gone To Bliss.

And so for the sake
Of living beings,
And to help
The entire world,

The Victors undertook
To teach the deceptive.


	[2556]
,SEMS CAN TSOGS KYI ‘GRO DRUG GANG BSTAN PA,
,SEMS CAN DMYAL DANG DUD ‘GRO YI DVAGS DANG,
,LHA MIN RIS DANG MI DANG LHA YI RNAMS,
,MI YI SENG+GES KUN RDZOB BTAGS PA MDZAD,

Lord Buddha described the method of teaching the deceptive as follows:

Here is what
That Lion Among People
Gave the name
Of “the deceptive”—

All those that he taught
As the six types of birth
Among the mass of beings:

The beings of hell;
The animals,
The craving spirits,
The demigods,
The humans,
And the worldly gods.


	[2557]
,RIGS DMA’ DE BZHIN MTHO BA’I RIGS RNAMS [f. 185a] DANG,
,PHYUG PO’I KHYIM DANG DBUL PO’I KHYIM RNAMS DANG,
,BRAN GYI TSOGS DANG DE BZHIN G-YOG GI TSOGS,
,BUD MED TSOGS DANG SKYES PA MA NING DANG,

And so we see
Those of lower class,
And just so those
Of the higher classes.

We see households
Of the wealthy,
And households too
Of the poor.

We see masses of slaves,
And masses of servants,
And masses of women,
And masses of men,
And masses of those
Who are neuters.


	[2558]
,’GRO BA’I KHYAD PAR JI SNYED GANG YANG RUNG,
,MTSUNGS MED KHYOD KYIS ‘JIG RTEN BSTAN MDZAD PA,
,KUN RDZOB BDEN PAR MKHAS PAS THUGS CHUD NAS,
,’JIG RTEN MKHYEN PAS MI LA DE BSTAN TO,
ZHES PAS NI KUN RDZOB BSTAN TSUL GSUNGS SO,,

	And so you,
	O Matchless One,
	Have described all the different
	Types of beings that there may be.

	Those who became wise
	In deceptive reality
	Grasped all that you taught
	About this world;

	And so it was that you,
	Knower of the World,
	Granted instruction
To human kind. 


	[2559]
,’DI LA DGA’ BA’I ‘GRO BA ‘KHOR BA NA {%NI},
,’GRO BA’I CHOS BRGYAD LA NI ‘JUG ‘GYUR TE,
,THOB DANG MA THOB SNYAN DANG MI SNYAN DANG,
,BSTOD DANG SMAD DANG BDE DANG SDUG BSNGAL LO,

And then he continued with—

Beings who delight
In all of this
Come to engage
In the eight attitudes
Of those in the cycle:

Gain and loss,
Fame and ill-repute,
Praise and criticism,
Pleasure and pain.


	[2560]
,THOB PA RNYED NA DE LA CHAGS PA SKYE,
,MA THOB GYUR NA DES KYANG ‘KHRUG PAR ‘GYUR,
,GANG GZHAN MA BSTAN TSUL ‘DIS SHES PAR BYA,
,NAD RNAMS BRGYAD KYIS DE RGYUN GNOD PAR GYUR,

If they happen
To acquire something,
They begin to feel attachment.

If they fail
To gain something,
Then they get upset.

In a case where the rest
Are not shared,
You can understand them
From this way of things.

People are attacked
Incessantly
By these eight great illnesses.


[2561]
ZHES PAS NI KUN RDZOB PA ‘DI LA BDEN PAR ZHEN NAS DGA’ BA NI ‘JIG RTEN GYI CHOS BRGYAD LA ‘JUG CING DES MNAR NAS ‘KHOR BAR ‘KHOR BA DANG CHOS BRGYAD KYI DANG PO GNYIS BSTAN PAS LHAG MA MA BSTAN PA SHES PAR BYA BAR GSUNGS SO,,

What this is saying is that people are attached to believing that these deceptive entities are reality; and this in turn impels them to engage in those eight different attitudes.  This in turn tortures them; and then they are spun around in the wheel of pain.  And once we teach someone the first two of the eight attitudes here, they can go on to understand all of the rest as well, even if we don’t explicitly share those with them.


	[2562]
,KUN RDZOB DE LA DON DAM SU SMRA BA,
,DE DAG NOR PA’I BLO LDAN SHES PAR BYA,
ZHES PAS NI KUN RDZOB PA ‘GRO BA DRUG LA SOGS PA LA DON DAM STE BDEN PAR GRUB PA ZHES SU SMRA BA DE DAG PHYIN CI LOG GI BLO CAN DU SHES PAR BYA BAR GSUNGS PAS RANG SDE DE LTAR ‘DOD PA RNAMS GRUB MTHA’ NOR BAR GSUNGS SO,,

	You should understand
	That those who describe
	The deceptive as being
	The ultimate possess
	A mind that is mistaken.

And what this is saying is that those who profess that the deceptive—a reference to things like the six forms of suffering life—is “ultimate,” meaning something that exists as real, should be understood as having minds which are mistaken.  That is to say, those whose schools of thought accept this kind of idea are being described as mistaken systems.
	

	[2563]
,MI SDUG SDUG DANG SDUG BSNGAL BDE BA DANG,
,[f. 185b] BDAG MED RANG BZHIN BDAG TU SMRA BA DANG,
,MI RTAG CHOS LA RTAG CES SMRA BGYID CING,

They claim that
Was is not attractive
Is attractive;
And that pain
Is happiness.

And they say
That things which
Have no self
Have a nature
Of being a self.

They make the claim
That things which are
Impermanent
Will somehow last.


	[2564]
,DE LTAR DGA’ STE MTSAN MAR GANG GNAS PA,
,DE DAG BDE GSHEGS GSUNG NI THOS GYUR NA,
,’JIGS SHING JI BZHIN MI RTOGS SPONG PAR BGYI,

They delight in these thoughts,
And stay in signs.

When people like this
Hear the speech of those
Who have Gone to Bliss,

They are terrified,
And fail to understand them,
And so discard these words.


	[2565]
,DE DAG BDER GSHEGS GSUNG NI SPANGS GYUR NAS,
,SEMS CAN DMYAL BAR SDUG BSNGAL MI BZAD MYONG,
,DE DAG TSUL MIN BDE BA TSOL BGYID KYANG,
,SDUG BSNGAL BRGYA DAG BYIS PAS MYONG BAR ‘GYUR,

Having rejected
The holy speech of those
Who’ve Gone to Bliss,

People like this
Experience unending pain
In the realms of hell.

They seek thus happiness
In all the wrong ways;
And then these children
Suffer from a thousand pains.


[2566]
ZHES PAS NI PHYIN CI LOG BZHI LA GOMS PA DANG DE ‘THAD PA’I GRUB MTHAS BSLAD PA PHYI ROL PA RNAMS NI, SANGS RGYAS KYI GSUNG THOS NA SPONG ZHING DE’I MTHUS SEMS CAN DMYAL BAR ‘GRO BA DANG, DE DAG GIS THAR PA’I BDE BA TSUL BZHIN MIN PA’I THABS KYIS BTZAL YANG, DE MI RNYED PAR MA ZAD SDUG BSNGAL DU MAS MNAR BAR ‘GYUR BAR BSTAN NO,,

What this is teaching us is that there are non-Buddhists who become very accustomed to the four different reversed ways of thinking mentioned here, and who are infected by schools of thought which believe that they are correct.  When people like this happen to hear the words of the Buddha, they reject them; and by the power of this they pass to the realms of hell.  These kinds of individuals undertake a search for the happiness of freedom through mistaken means; but not only do they fail to find this happiness, they instead come to be tortured by a great many sufferings.


	[2567]
,’JIG RTEN PHAN PA’I BSTAN PA SU ZHIG GIS,
,MA LOG BLO YIS RNAM PAR RTOGS GYUR NA,
,SBRUL GYI PAGS PA RNYING LTAR RAB SPANGS TE,
,SRID PA KUN LAS ‘DAS NAS ZHI BAR ‘GYUR,

This is a teaching
Which brings help
To the entire world;

Those who grasp it
With a mind
Free of error

Pass beyond all
Of this suffering life.

They leave it behind
Like a snake that sheds
Its old skin, and come
To peace.


	[2568]
,CHOS ‘DI THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN DBEN PA STE,
,STONG PA MTSAN MA MED PA DON DAM ZHES,
,GANG GIS THOS NAS DGA’ BA SKYE ‘GYUR BA,
,DE DAG BLA MED BYANG CHUB THOB PAR ‘GYUR,

Each and every one
Of all the things here
Is devoid of any nature
Of its own.

They are empty,
They have no signs;
They are what we call
The ultimate.

Those who hear these words
And feel delight arise
Within their heart

Are the kinds of people
Who will come to reach
That matchless Enlightenment.


	[2569]
,RGYAL BA KHYOD KYIS PHUNG PO DBEN PAR GZIGS,
,KHAMS DANG SKYE MCHED RNAMS KYANG DE BZHIN TE,
,DBANG PO’I GRONG NI MTSAN MAS DBEN PA DAG
,KUN KYANG THUB PA KHYOD KYIS JI BZHIN GZIGS,

O Ones of Victory,
You have seen
That the heaps are void;

And that the elements
And the doors of sense
Are just the same.

The city of the sense powers
Is devoid of any signs;

And all of these too
Are seen just as they are
By you, o Able One.


[2570]
ZHES BSTAN PA GSUNG RAB ZAB MO’I DON PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR [f. 186a] RTOGS NA, ‘KHOR BA LAS GROL BAR BSTAN NAS, RTOGS TSUL DE JI ‘DRA ZHIG SNYAM PA LA,

And then what this is saying is that it has been taught that—if we are able to grasp, unerringly, the meaning of the teachings, that most profound of the highest of spoken words—then we will gain liberation from the cycle of pain.  One might wonder then just how it is that we should accomplish this understanding.


[2571]
CHOS ‘DI THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN DBEN PA SOGS KYI GTAM THOS PA NA DGA’ NAS DE’I DON RTOGS NA BYANG CHUB ‘THOB PAR GSUNGS TE, SNGAR KUN RDZOB BSTAN LA ‘DIS DON DAM PA BSTAN NO,,

It is stated that we will attain enlightenment if we take delight in hearing descriptions of things like how all of these existing entities are devoid of any nature of their own.  And so whereas the previous lines were in explanation of deceptive reality, these are elucidating ultimate reality.


[2572]
KHAMS NI SA’I KHAMS LA SOGS PA’O,,

The Tibetan word kam in the quotation here—[which can refer to categories or to the elements that compose all physical things]—is a reference to the element of earth and so on.


[2573]
SKYE MCHED NI GZUGS SGRA SOGS SO,,

And then when it says “doors of sense,” it’s referring to things like visible form, and sound.


[2574]
DE’I PHYIR KUN RDZOB BTAGS PA TZAM DANG RANG BZHIN MED PA’I DON DAM BDEN PA SHES PAS DBEN PA RNAMS LA THAR PA LTA GA LA YOD, DE’I PHYIR RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM DU SMRA BA DE DAG NI LAM GOL PAR ZHUGS PA KHO NA’O,,

And so if people are devoid of any understanding of the reality where things are only imputed, only deceptive; and of the reality which is ultimate, where things have no nature of their own, how then could they ever attain freedom?  As such, we would have to say that those who profess that everything is nothing more than consciousness have with absolute certainty walked onto a mistaken path.


[2575]
‘DIR THA SNYAD KYI BDEN PA BSTAN PA NI THABS SU GYUR PA STE, TING NGE ‘DZIN GYI RGYAL PO LAS,
,YI GE MED PA’I CHOS LA NI,
,NYAN PA GANG DANG STON PA GANG,
,’GYUR PA MED LA SGRO BTAGS PAS,
,’ON KYANG NYAN ZHING STON PA YIN,

When we refer to a “nominal” reality here, this is what we call “method.”  As the King of Concentration puts it,

	Whatever listening
	Or teaching we may
	Ever accomplish

	With the dharma which
	Itself lacks all letters

	Is only imputed
	Upon things which
	Cannot ever change;

	And yet still
	We can listen,
	And still we can teach.


[2576]
ZHES GSUNGS TE, RKANG PA DANG PO GNYIS KYIS NI DE DAG DON DAM PAR MED PAR BSTAN NO, ,DON DAM PAR YI GE MED PA DE LA LA SGRO BTAGS PA STE RTOG PAS BTAGS NAS NYAN PA DANG ‘CHAD DO ZHES PA’O,,

The first two lines [in the Tibetan here, first five lines in the English] are indicating that these things do not exist in any ultimate way.  And then we impute—which is to say, make up in our mind—some number of those things which are, ultimately speaking, beyond any letters, and thus come up with the acts of listening and of explaining.


[2577]
YI GE’I SKAD DOD AAKshA RA ZHES PA YI GE DANG ‘GYUR PA MED PA GNYIS KA LA ‘JUG KYANG ‘DIR YI GE MED LA ZHES BSGYUR NA BDE’O,,

The original Sanskrit term for “letter” here is akshara, which can connote either “letter” or “immutable.”  The translation here though works better if we read it as “lacking letters.”


[2578]
SGRO BTAGS PA NI MED PA LA YOD PA DANG, MA YIN PA LA YIN ZHES PA LTA BU LA YANG MANG DU BSHAD MOD KYANG, DE KHO NAR MI GZUNG GI SPYIR RTOG PAS BTAGS NAS ‘JOG PA LA YANG BYA’O,,

Now of course we see many explanations of how the term used for “impute” here can refer to saying that something exists when in fact it does not; of saying that something is one way or the other when in fact it is not.  This though is not the only way of taking the term; and it can also be explained as connoting something which is merely a creation of our thoughts.


[2579]
THA SNYAD KYI BDEN PA KHO NA LA GNAS TE [f. 186b] DON DAM PA STON LA, DE LAS KYANG DON DAM PA KHONG DU CHUD PA LAS DON DAM PA MYANG NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA ‘THOB STE,

It is only by residing in nominal reality that we can teach the ultimate; and it is by coming to a grasp of the ultimate that we can achieve the ultimate, in the form of nirvana.


[2580]
RTZA SHE LAS,
,THA SNYAD LA NI MA BRTEN PAR,
,DAM PA’I DON NI BSTAN MI NUS,
,DAM PA’I DON NI MA RTOGS PAR,
,MYA NGAN ‘DAS PA THOB MI ‘GYUR,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

As Wisdom puts it,

Without relying on the nominal,
We could never teach the ultimate.

Without realizing the ultimate,
We could never attain nirvana.



Denying the dominated
is not to deny the world

[2581]
BZHI PA NI,

With this we have reached our fourth step from above: showing that denying dominated entities and denying the verbiage of the world are not equivalent.


[2582]
GAL TE KHYOD KYIS DE SKAD DU KHO BO CAG LA SHIN TU LTOS PA MED PAR SMRA NA, DA NI NGED CAG KYANG KHYED LA BZOD PA MI BYED DE, GAL TE BDAG NYID GZHAN GYI PHYOGS SUN ‘BYIN PA TZAM LA MKHAS PAR MNGON PAR BYED CING, RIGS PA’I ‘THAD PAS MI RIGS PA’I PHYIR GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I NGO BO SEL BAR BYED NA, ‘O NA DA NI BDAG DANG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA SOGS ‘GOG PA’I ‘THAD PA KHO NAS, MI RIGS PA’I PHYIR KHYOD LA GRAGS PA’I KUN RDZOB SEL BAR BYED DO ZHE NA,

And so suppose someone comes now with the following response—

You have said things about us in those words which have nothing to do with the situation.  And so now we can no longer be so patient with you.  So suppose it is the case that a person starts to look like they are a master, just because they can attack the positions that someone else holds.  But you are just trying to disprove the essential nature of dominated entities, something which does exist through a nature of its own, reasoning which is not itself rational.  What we will do now then is just to show that it is correct to deny that things could grow either from themselves or from other things; and with nothing more than that, we will be able to disprove the kind of deceptive reality that you speak about—for in the end it is illogical.


[2583]
GAL TE KHYOD THOG MA MED PA’I DUS NAS DKA’ BA BRGYA PHRAG GIS BSAGS PA’I NOR GYI TSOGS ‘PHROG PA PO LA, MDZA’ BO’I ZOL GYIS DUG BCAS KYI ZAS BYIN NAS SLAR PHROGS PAS

In reply, we can say that you are like a person who has been accumulating wealth through thousands of difficult efforts, for a period of time that has no beginning.  And then someone comes along and steals it.  In response, you pretend to be their friend, and feed them a nice meal laced with poison—which allows you to steal your things back again.


[2584]
DGA’ BA BZHIN DU, KHO BO CAG GIS GZHAN DBANG LA BDEN PAR ‘DZIN PA’I YUL PHROGS PAS PHAN BTAGS PA NA DE’I LAN DU KHO BO CAG LA GNOD PA BYAS PAS KHYOD DGA’ ZHING RANGS PAR ‘GYUR NA ‘GYUR LA RAG STE, KHO BO CAG NI MNGON PAR MTHO ZHING DAG PA NYID DU ‘GYUR RO,,

And because of that you feel quite pleased with yourself.  Now what we have done is to steal away from you the object that you were holding as dominated entities that exist in reality.  By doing so, we were only helping you.  In response, you tried to hurt us, enjoying—delighting in—the process.  But all that you have accomplished is to assure that we will reach to the higher births, and to absolute purity.


	[2585]
[VI.81]
Na saṃvṛtiś cāpi mayābhyupetā
yathā tvayeṣṭaṃ paratantra rūpam,
Lokānurodhāt tvasatītyam īṣāṃ
satīti kāryārtham ahaṃ bravīmi.

,JI LTAR KHYOD KYIS GZHAN DBANG DNGOS ‘DOD LTAR,
,KUN RDZOB KYANG NI BDAG GIS KHAS MA BLANGS,
,’BRAS PHYIR ‘DI DAG MED KYANG YOD DO ZHES,
,’JIG RTEN NGOR BYAS BDAG NI SMRA BAR BYED,

	You say that
	Dominated entities
	Are real;

	And then when
	You agree to it,
	
	A deceptive reality
	Is not something
	We can accept.

		It is meant
		For a particular effect—

		That all these things
		Are not things
		Which exist.

		Nonetheless,
		What we say is
		That they exist,

		To the appearances
		Of the world.


[2586]
‘DI LTAR JI LTAR SEMS TZAM PA KHYOD KYIS GZHAN DBANG DNGOS POR TE NGO BOS GRUB PA, SUM CU PA LAS, DE MA MTHONG BAR DE MI MTHONG ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR ‘PHAGS PA’I YE SHES KYIS THUGS SU CHUD PAR BYAS [f. 187a] PA ZHIG GI RANG DBANG DU BYAS NAS, RANG LUGS KYIS YOD DO ZHES ‘DOD PA DE LTAR KUN RDZOB KYANG NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BDAG GIS KHAS MA BLANGS SO,,

And here’s how that happens.  You followers of the Mind Only say that dominated entities are real things; which is to say, that they exist through some essential nature of their own.  As the Thirty Verses puts it, “It’s something you fail to see, being something that cannot be seen.”  That is, you are saying that there is something which is comprehended by the wisdom of a realized being which has some independent nature of its own.  And then when you say that your own system says that something does exist, and you agree to it, you are talking about a deceptive reality which could exist through some nature of its own.  This is not something though which we can accept.


[2587]
‘O NA CI ZHE NA, PHUNG PO LA SOGS PA ‘DI DAG RANG BZHIN GYIS MED KYANG, ‘JIG RTEN KHO NA LAS GRAGS PAR ‘GYUR BAS YOD DO ZHES ‘JIG RTEN GYI NGO KHO NAR BYAS NAS BDAG GIS NI SMRA BAR BYED DO,,

And what then is our own position?  We say that all these things—the heaps and the rest—are not things which exist through some nature of their own.  Nonetheless, they are things which are spoken of—if only in the everyday world.  And so what we say is that they do exist, but only to the appearances of normal people in the world.


[2588]
‘DIR KUN RDZOB PA’I PHUNG SOGS ‘JIG RTEN THA SNYAD KYI NGOR ‘JOG PA LA TSUL GNYIS TE, DBU MA PA RANG GIS KUN RDZOB TU ‘JOG PA NI THA SNYAD PA’I TSAD MA’I NGOR KHAS LEN GYI RIGS NGOR MI ‘JOG GO

Now there are two different manners in which deceptive objects such as the heaps can be established in a nominal way: to the perceptions of the world.  Those of the Middle Way school would say that they accept things which are established as existing in a deceptive way as they appear to nominal perceptions which are accurate; they would not though say that they are established relative to perceptions resulting from logic.


[2589]
,SKABS ‘GAR DGOS PA’I DBANG GIS PHUNG SOGS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR ‘JOG PA NI, RANG LUGS LA MI ‘DOD KYI GZHAN NGO KHO NAR KHAS LEN PAS DE GNYIS ‘GOG PA MI MTSUNGS SO,,

There are a few specific occasions upon which the heaps and so forth are—by necessity—established as things which exist through some nature of their own.  This is not to say that these things are accepted within our own system, but rather accepted only relative to the belief of others.  As such, the ways in which we deny the two are not equivalent.


[2590]
GZHAN NGOR DE LTAR KHAS LEN PA NI ‘BRAS BU STE DGOS PA’I PHYIR YIN LA, DE YANG GDUL BYA DE GRUB MTHA’ NGAN PA GZHAN LAS LDOG PA DANG, RIM GYIS DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA’I THABS YIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Accepting these things in the eyes of those others is something meant for a certain effect; which is to say, to satisfy a certain need.  In fact it is meant as a means of turning disciples away from these other, defective systems of thought and bringing them, gradually, to the means of realizing suchness.


[2591]
DES NA GZHUNG DES RNAM GZHAG THAMS CAD GZHAN NGOR BYED KYI, RANG LUGS LA MI BYED PA’I DON GTAN MIN PA NI, ‘DI’I SHES BYED KYI LUNG DRANGS PA NYID KYIS SHES SO,,

As such, we can say that everything such classics present is only intended for the perceptions of the other side.  It is not at all that we would present points that don’t at all represent our own system.  This is something that can be understood by the very supporting citations we quote.


[2592]
LUNG NI SDOM PA GSUM BSTAN PA LAS, ‘JIG RTEN NGA DANG LHAN CIG RTZOD KYI, NGA NI ‘JIG RTEN DANG MI RTZOD DE, GANG ‘JIG RTEN NA YOD PAR ‘DOD PA DE NI NGAS KYANG YOD PAR BZHED DO, ,GANG ‘JIG RTEN NA MED PAR ‘DOD PA DE NI NGA YANG MED PAR BZHED DO, ZHES [f. 187b] GSUNGS PA’O,,

And what are such citations?  As A Presentation of the Three Vows puts it,

The world may dispute with me, but I have no dispute with the world.  Whatever the world says exists, I also agree exists.  Whatever the world says does not exist, I also agree does not.


[2593]
‘DI NI STONG NYID BDUN CU PA LAS,
,GNAS PA’AM SKYE ‘JIG YOD MED DAM,
,DMAN PA’AM MNYAM PA’AM KHYAD PAR CAN,
,SANGS RGYAS ‘JIG RTEN BSNYAD DBANG GIS,
,GSUNGS KYIS YANG DAG DBANG GIS MIN,

The Seventy Verses on Emptiness puts it this way—

	Whether it’s staying,
	Or starting or stopping;

	Whether it’s existing
	Or not existing;

	Whether it’s lower,
	Or equal, or exceptional,

	All are spoken of
	By the Buddhas using
	The wording of the world—

	Never is it independently.


[2594]
ZHES YOD MED LA SOGS PAR ‘JOG PA THAMS CAD ‘JIG RTEN NA JI LTAR GRAGS PA’I THA SNYAD KYI DBANG GIS ‘JOG PAR GSUNGS PA’I DON NO,,

What these lines are saying is that the Buddhas speak in terms of the language that is common in the everyday world, whenever they are describing whether something exists or not, or anything else of the like.


	[2595]
[VI.82]
Skandhān samutsṛjya śiva praveśe
yathārhatāṃ nāsti tathaiva na syāt,
Lokasya cet tadvad imāṃ satīti
brūyām ahaṃ naiva hi lokato’pi.

,JI LTAR PHUNG PO SPANGS NAS ZHIR ZHUGS PA,
,DGRA BCOM RNAMS LA YOD PA MIN DE LTAR,
,’JIG RTEN LA YANG MED NA DE BZHIN ‘DI,
,’JIG RTEN LAS KYANG YOD CES BDAG MI SMRA,

	None exists
	For those who reside
	In peace, where
	
	Enemy destroyers
	Have eliminated
	The heaps.

	Suppose that,
	In a similar way,

	There were none
	In the general
	World as well.

	I do not say that
	It would be similar;	

	That there could exist
	One like this
	For the world.


[2596]
JI STE KUN RDZOB ‘DI JI LTAR DGRA BCOM PA PHUNG PO SPANGS NAS LHAG MED KYI ZHI BA’I DBYINGS SU ZHUGS PA RNAMS LA, KUN RDZOB THAMS CAD YOD PA MIN PA DE LTAR DU GAL TE ‘JIG RTEN LA YANG KUN RDZOB ‘DI MED NA, LHAG MED PA DE BZHIN DU KUN RDZOB PA ‘DI ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD KYI NGO LA LTOS NAS KYANG YOD CES BDAG MI SMRA’O,,

None of all the deceptive objects there may be in the world exists, for those who reside in the realm of peace with nothing left, where these enemy destroyers have eliminated the heaps.  And so suppose that, in a similar way, in the general world as well there were no deceptive reality.  I do not say that it would be similar to that case where nothing remains; that is, I do not say that there could then exist any deceptive reality like this which presented itself to the nominal perceptions of the world.


[2597]
DE’I PHYIR GZHAN ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD LA RAG LAS PA NYID KYI SGO NAS BDAG GIS KUN RDZOB KHAS BLANGS KYI, ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD LA MA LTOS PAR RANG DBANG DU KHAS BLANGS PA NI MIN NO,,

What this is saying then is that “I accept deceptive reality precisely through the common parlance of these others: of those of the world.  It is not though the case that I would accept it independently, without relying upon the expressions of the world.”


	[2598]
[VI.83]
Niṣidhyatāṃ lokata eva caiṣā
na lokabādhā bhavato yadi syāt,
Loko bhavāṃś ceha vivādam etu
paścād balīyāṃsam ahaṃ śrayiṣye.

,GAL TE KHYOD LA ‘JIG RTEN MI GNOD NA,
,’JIG RTEN NYID LTOS ‘DI NI DGAG PAR GYIS,
,KHYOD DANG ‘JIG RTEN ‘DIR NI RTZOD KYIS {%GYIS} DANG,
,PHYI NAS STOBS LDAN BDAG GIS BRTEN PAR BYA,

		If the world
		Is not something
		That could call your
		Ideas into question,

		Then you can
		Go ahead and deny it
		Relative to
		The world itself.

		You and the world
Can go ahead
And argue with
Each other on this.

Once you are done,
I will put my support
Behind the stronger.


[2598]
THOG MAR ‘JIG RTEN KHO NAS KHAS BLANGS PA YIN TE, DE’I PHYIR GANG GIS KHAS BLANGS PA DE KHO NA LA LTOS NAS SEL BAR NUS PAS NA BSAL BAR ‘OS PA YIN TE, GZHAN DBU MA PA LA LTOS NAS NI MA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA

What this is saying is that, to start off, things are accepted only by the world.  As such, when we are denying a certain idea we can only do so dependent upon what someone has accepted as the case; this then becomes something worthy of denial.  It is not though that we are taking some kind of position relative to what those of the Middle Way are asserting.


[2599]
KHO BO CAG NI KUN RDZOB ‘KHRUL PA’I SNANG BA RANG RGYUD LA BZLOG PA’I PHYIR SHIN TU TSEGS CHE BAS LAM SGOM PA LA GNAS PAR ‘GYUR GYI, GAL TE KHYOD LA ‘JIG RTEN GYIS MI GNOD NA, KHYOD KYIS ‘JIG RTEN NYID LA LTOS NAS KUN RDZOB ‘DI NI DGAG PAR GYIS SHIG ,DE KHYOD KYI [f. 188a] RIGS PAS ‘GOG NUS NA NGAS KYANG KHYOD LA STONGS GDAB PA STE GROGS BYA’O,,

We for our part have kept up our practice of the path with incredibly great effort, in order to put a stop to the mistaken appearance of deceptive reality within our own minds.  If what the world says is not something that could call your ideas into question, then you can go ahead and deny this deceptive reality relative to the world itself.  If you find that this is something that you can deny with your particular reasoning, then I will gladly “join hands with you”—meaning, I will accompany you.


[2600]
‘JIG RTEN GYIS NI GNOD PA YANG YIN TE, DE’I PHYIR KHO BO CAG KHYOD KYI GROGS MI BYED PAR BTANG SNYOMS SU GNAS PAR BYA’O,,

The fact though is that the world as well contradicts your ideas; and so actually I will refuse to accompany you—I will leave you as you are.


[2601]
KHYOD DANG ‘JIG RTEN PA GNYIS ‘DIR NI RTZOD PA GYIS SHIG DANG, BRTZAD PA’I PHYI NAS GANG STOBS DANG LDAN PA DE LA BDAG GIS BRTEN PAR BYA’O,,

And so both you and the world can go ahead and argue with each other on this.  Once you are both done fighting, I will put my support behind whichever of you has proved to be the stronger.


[2602]
DE LA KHYOD RGYAL NA NI KHO BO CAG DE ‘DOD PAS KHYOD LA BRTEN PAR BYA’O,,

Which is to say, if you manage to emerge victorious, then all of us will give you our support.


[2603]
‘ON TE KHYOD ‘JIG RTEN GYIS PHAM PAR BYAS NA NI, SHIN TU STOBS DANG LDAN PA’I ‘JIG RTEN LA BRTEN PAR BYA’O,,

If however it turns out though that the world defeats you, we will put our support behind the world, which has proven to be so extremely strong.


[2604]
DE LTAR NA PHYI ROL MED PA LA THA SNYAD PA’I TSAD MAS GNOD PAS PHYI ROL MED PAR SGRUB MI NUS SO,,

As such, nominal forms of accurate perception draw into question the idea that there exist no outer objects; as such, you are unable to prove the idea that no such objects exist.


[2605]
‘O NA SEMS TZAM PAS RDUL CHA MED MED PAS DE BSAGS PA’I PHYI DON ‘GOG PA’I RIGS PAS, PHYOGS KYI CHA MED KYI PHYI DON MI KHEGS SO SNYAM NA, 

Now the following thought might occur to you—

Well, but it’s not the case that followers of the Mind Only are denying outer objects that have no sides to them, by using reasoning that denies that there are any outer objects that are composed of partless particles.


[2606]
DE DAG TSAD MAS MA KHEGS PAR MA SMRA’I DE KHEGS KYANG PHYI ROL GYI DON MED MI DGOS SO,,

Even if they were not to assert that those could not be denied by an accurate perception, it would not have to be the case that there were no outer objects.


[2607]
‘DIS NI SHES PA DUS KYI CHA MED DANG DE ‘THUD PA’I RGYUN KHEGS KYANG SHES PA MI KHEGS PA YANG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

You can also use this to understand how—even if we deny partless instants of time for the stream of consciousness, and thus deny any stream composed of such snippets of consciousness tied together—we are not thereby denying consciousness in general.


[2608]
GZHAN GYI LUGS KYIS NI PHYI ROL CHA MED KHEGS NA SNANG BA LA MA ‘KHRUL BA’I DBANG SHES KHEGS, DBANG SHES ‘KHRUL PAS DON ‘JOG MI NUS PAS PHYI DON KHEGS SO SNYAM DU BSAMS SO,,

According to the other side here, you deny an awareness of the senses which is unmistaken towards what appears to it, when you deny that outside objects have no sides to them.  A sense awareness which is mistaken is not capable of establishing its object; and so one would think that outer objects had been denied.


[2609]
‘DIR NI DBANG SHES ‘KHRUL PAS GZHAL BYA BDEN PA ‘JOG MI NUS KYANG, GZHAL BYA BRDZUN PA ‘JOG PA LA DE GROGS SU SONG NGO SNYAM DU DGONGS SO,,

Here we can say that a sense awareness which is mistaken cannot establish reality as the object under its consideration.  And the thinking here is that—when we seek to establish an object of consideration which is deceptive—it would have to serve in an assisting role.


[2610]
‘DI NYID ‘PHAGS PA LHA YANG BZHED DE BRGYA PA LAS,
,GCIG YOD [f. 188b] GCIG MED CES BYA BA,
,DE NYID MIN ‘JIG RTEN PA’ANG MIN,
,ZHES DON SHES YOD MED ‘BYED PA BDEN GNYIS GANG GI YANG RNAM GZHAG MIN PAR GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

This very point is something that Master Aryadeva also agrees to; as the 400 Verses puts it,

Saying that one is there,
Or that one is not there,

Is not with that particular one;
Nor with that of the world.


[2611]
DE’I PHYIR DE LTAR ‘BYED PA KLU’I ZHABS KYI BZHED PA YANG MA YIN NO,,

We can say thus that making the distinction in this way is not the position of the great Nagarjuna either.



“Only” is not meant
to deny outer objects

[2612]
GSUM PA LA GSUM, SA BCU PA LAS, SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA’I DGONGS PA BSHAD PA, PHYI ROL DANG NANG GI SEMS GNYIS YOD MED MTSUNGS PAR BSTAN PA, LANG KAR GSHEGS PA LAS, SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA’I DGONGS PA BSHAD PA’O,,

Which brings us to our third part from above: a demonstration that the word “only” in the expression “Mind Only” is not meant to deny outer objects.  We proceed in three steps: an explanation of how the intent of the term “mind only” is described in The Ten Levels; a demonstration that outside objects, and the inner mind, are equivalent in either existing or not existing; and finally an explanation of how the intent of “mind only” is described in A Journey to Langka.


[2613]
DANG PO LA GSUM, TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI ROL MI ‘GOG PA SA BCU PA’I LUNG GIS BSGRUB PA, DON DE NYID MDO GZHAN GYIS KYANG BSGRUB PA, TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BO NYID DU BSGRUB PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,
