We’ll cover the first of these three in another three of its own: showing how a citation from The Ten Levels supports the idea that the word “only” is not meant to deny outer objects; demonstrating how this very same point is made in other sutras as well; and establishing that the intent of the word “only” is to say only that the mind is the primary thing.  Here is the first of these.


[2614]
GAL TE DE KHO NA NYID LA DPYOD PA’I ‘THAD PA STE RIGS PAS GRUB PA DANG BRAL YANG, ‘JIG RTEN PA’I GNOD PAS ‘JIGS NAS KHYOD KYIS KUN RDZOB KHAS BLANGS NA NI, LUNG GI GNOD PAS ‘JIGS PAS SEMS TZAM DU YANG KHAS BLANG DGOS TE, SA BCU PA LAS, DE ‘DI SNYAM DU SEMS TE, ‘DI LTAR KHAMS GSUM PO ‘DI NI SEMS TZAM STE, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O ZHE NA,

And so suppose you come and say the following—

I was bereft of the correctness of learning to examine suchness; which is to say, I felt I was without any solid proof for it.  Fearing then that the ideas of the world would harm my position, I accepted the idea of a deceptive reality.  And when I did that, I feared further that I would be disproven by scripture; and so I found myself having to accept the ideas of the Mind Only.  Here I found support from The Ten Levels, where it says: “And then one comes to the following thoughts, saying to oneself, ‘All three of the realms of existence are only the mind.”


[2615]
BRJOD PA RGYAL BA’I GSUNG GI NOR BU AANDA RNYIL LAS SBYAR BA’I MDO SDE’I SA GZHI BSTAR BA LA, AANDA RNYIL YIN PA DE MA SHES PAR RNAM PAR SHES PA DNGOS POR SMRA BA’I CHU’I RNAM PAR YONGS SU ‘GYUR BAR ‘KHRUL BA KHYOD NI,

And yet these statements, the jewel of the speech of the Victorious Ones, are like a vast ground of the sutras, made out of pure sapphire and glistening in light.  You on your side fail to recognize it as the sapphire, and so you have bathed it in the chemical of the Functionalists, saying that things are consciousness, and mistaking what comes out of the transformation wrought by the chemical wash.


[2616]
RNAM PAR SHES PA DNGOS POR SMRA BA’I CHU TZAM ZHIG BCU BAR ‘DOD PAS, RANG GI BLO GROS KYI BUM PA SO MA BTANG BA BSHAL ZHING BSNYUGS NAS DUM BU RNAM PA BRGYAR KLOG PA [f. 189a] NA, DE’I RANG BZHIN SHES PA RNAMS KYI BZHAD GAD DU BYA BA NYID DU ‘GYUR BAR BYED PA YIN NO,,

And so you hope to whitewash everything with this liquid chemical of consciousness according to the Functionalists.  To do so, you take the vessel of your wisdom—a vessel which remains unfired clay—and pour the liquid into the brim and end up with the pot breaking into a hundred shards.  And all you’ve managed to do is to become a laughing stock for those who really understand the nature of these things.


[2617]
MDO’I DGONGS PA ‘DI NI JI LTAR KHYOD KYI BLO LA SNANG BA DE LTAR MA YIN NO,,

The fact is that the true intent of the sutra is not at all the way that it appeared to be, in your minds.


	[2618]
[VI.84]
Vijñāna mātraṃ tribhavaṃ paraiti
yad bodhisattvo ‘bhimukho ‘bhimukhyām,
Nityātma kartṛ pratiṣedha bodhāt
prapadyate kartṛ sa citta mātram.

,MNGON GYUR MNGON PHYOGS BYANG CHUB
SEMS DPA’ YIS,
,SRID GSUM RNAM SHES TZAM DU GANG RTOGS PA,
,RTAG BDAG BYED PO BKAG PA RTOGS PHYIR DES,
,BYED PA PO NI SEMS TZAM YIN PAR RTOGS,

		A bodhisattva
		Headed towards
		The manifestation

		Comes to the realization
		That these three
		Worlds of pain
		Are nothing but the mind.

		What this means
		For them is that
		They have blocked
		
The idea of an
		Unchanging self
		As the creator,

		And come to
		The realization.


[2619]
YANG ‘DIR MDO’I DON CI YIN ZHE NA,

“Well then,” you may ask.  “Just what then is the real meaning of this sutra?”


[2620]
DE’I PHYIR BSHAD PA, SA DRUG PA MNGON DU GYUR PA CHOS DBYINGS LA MNGON DU PHYOGS PA’I BYANG CHUB THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES LA SEMS PA DE LA YOD PAS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ YIS,

It’s to answer that question that we see this explanation.  Let’s consider a bodhisattva—which is to say, a person who is of the type that has an intention to reach the state of enlightenment, or the knowledge of all things—and who is headed towards the realm of all things with the manifestation of the sixth level.


[2621]
SRID PA KHAMS GSUM RNAM SHES SEMS TZAM DU RTOGS PAR GSUNGS PA GANG YIN PA DES NI, BDAG RTAG PA BYED PA PO BKAG NAS, KUN RDZOB SEMS TZAM ZHIG KHO NA BYED PA PO YIN PAR RTOGS PA’I PHYIR,

It certainly is the case that it was stated that this person has come to the realization that this world of pain—the three realms of suffering—are nothing but the mind.  But what this means for them is that they have blocked the idea of an unchanging self as the creator; and have come to the realization that it is the mind only which is the sole creator of deceptive reality.


[2622]
‘JIG RTEN GYI BYED PA PO NI BYANG SEMS DES SEMS TZAM ZHIG YIN PAR RTOGS TE,

As such, this kind of bodhisattva has come to the realization that the creator of the world was the mind alone.


[2623]
SA BCU PA LAS, LUGS SU BYUNG BA’I RNAM PAR RTEN CING ‘BREL PAR ‘BYUNG BA LA RAB TU RTOG GO ,DE LTAR NA SDUG BSNGAL GYI PHUNG PO SDUG BSNGAL GYI LJON PA BYED PA PO DANG, TSOR BA PO MED PA ‘BA’ ZHIG PO ‘DI MNGON PAR ‘GRUB PAR ‘GYUR RO SNYAM MO,,

The way that The Ten Levels puts it, in great detail, is as follows:

They have a great understanding of all it is that occurs in dependence and relationship, in the forward order of this progression.  And so they think to themselves, “The great tree of this heap of suffering, of pain, had no maker; and there is no one to feel it either.  This is all there is; this is how this came to be.”


[2624]
DE ‘DI SNYAM DU SEMS TE, BYED PA PO LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PAS LAS RNAMS YOD PAR GYUR TO,,

And then this thought occurs to them: “All these kinds of karma came about through the strong belief in some creator.”


[2625]
GANG NA BYED PA PO MED PA DE NA DON DAM PAR LAS KYANG MI DMIGS SNYAM MO,,

“And where there is no creator, then neither is there—in an ultimate sense—any karma.”


[2626]
DE ‘DI SNYAM DU SEMS TE, KHAMS GSUM PA ‘DI NI SEMS TZAM STE, SRID PA’I LAN LAG BCU GNYIS PO GANG DAG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS RAB TU PHYE STE BKA’ STZAL PA DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PA DAG GO ZHES RGYA CHER GSUNGS SO,,

And they think to themselves, “All three of these realms of existence are only the mind.  And all of the twelve links of suffering existence which the One Thus Gone enumerated in his holy speech—each and every one of them—is something that relies upon the one mind.”


[2627]
MDO DES NI BYED PA PO DANG TSOR BA PO [f. 189b] MED PA’I ‘BA’ ZHIG PA ‘GRUB PA DANG, SEMS TZAM GYI DON BSHAD PA NA YAN LAG BCU GNYIS SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PAS,

These lines of the sutra are establishing a singularity where there is no agent, and no one who has feelings.  And when it gets into explaining the meaning of “mind only,” it states that the twelve links of dependence depend upon the one thing, mind.


[2628]
MDO ‘DI’I TZAM GYI SGRAS DON MI ‘GOG PA DANG, SEMS LAS GZHAN PA’I BYED PA PO ‘GOG PA YIN NO,,

When this sutra uses the word “only” then, it is not meant to deny certain objects.  Rather, it is denying any creator other than the mind.


[2629]
‘DI’I PHYOGS SNGA MA NI THEG BSDUS LAS, DE LA LUNG NI BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS SA BCU PA LAS, ‘DI LTA STE, KHAMS GSUM PO ‘DI NI SEMS TZAM MO ZHES PA DANG, ZHES RNAM RIG TZAM DU DPOG PA LA LUNG RIGS GNYIS GSUNGS PA’I LUNG DE LA MDZAD CING,

The opponent here is utilizing a line from A Compendium of the Greater Way, where it says: “As far as scriptural authority for this, The Ten Levels says, ‘This is how it is: these three realms of existence are only the mind’.”  That is, they are using this as the scriptural source for both scripture & reasoning for concluding that everything is only mental.


[2630]
NYI SHU PA’I RANG ‘GREL LAS KYANG, LUNG DE DRANGS SHING SEMS ZHES PA MTSUNGS LDAN DANG BCAS PA LA DGONGS SHING, TZAM SMOS PAS DON ‘GOG PAR BSHAD DO,,

The autocommentary to The Twenty Verses cites the same lines of the sutra, and says that the word “mind” here is intended to include those items which share a mental link with main mind.  And then it states that the term “only” here is meant to deny the object.


[2631]
‘DI SNGAR LTAR ‘GOG PA NI SNGON DU LEGS LDAN GYIS MDZAD LA, DE NAS ZLA BAS KYANG MDZAD DO,,

Making the denial as we described it before was done previously by Master Bhavaviveka; and then afterwards Master Chandrakirti did the same.



How others sutras
make the same point

[2632]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second step from above: demonstrating how this very same point is made in other sutras as well.


	[2633]
[VI.85]
Uktaṃ cāto dhīmatāṃ dhī vivṛddhyai
sarva jñenottuṅgatīrthyādribhedi,
Sūtre tasminn ārya Laṃkāvatāre
sandhyucchittau vāṅmayaṃ vajram etat.

,DE PHYIR BLO LDAN BLO NI ‘PHEL BYA’I PHYIR,
,LANG KAR GSHEGS MDO DE LAS KUN MKHYEN GYIS,
,MU STEGS SPO MTHON RI ‘JOMS NGAG RANG BZHIN,
,RDO RJE ‘DI NI DGONGS PA BCAD PHYIR GSUNGS,

		Thus it is
		The Journey to Langka
		Speaks of the diamond weapon

		Consisting of speech
		Used by the Omniscient One
		To smash down
		The lofty summit
		
		Of the mountain
		Of the River Schools.

		This is the one
		Described in order
		To carve out
		The real intent.		


[2634]
SEMS TZAM GYI TZAM GYI SGRAS BYED PA PO GZHAN ‘GOG PA SA BCU PA’I DON DU BSHAD NAS, DON ‘DI NYID MDO GZHAN GYIS KYANG BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

Now that we have explained how the point of The Ten Levels here is to indicate how the word “only” in the expression “mind only” is meant to deny any other creator, we will show how this very same point is indicated by other sutras as well.


[2635]
TZAM GYI SGRAS BYED PA PO GZHAN ‘GOG PA SA BCU PA’I DON YIN PA DE’I PHYIR, DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS NUS PA’I BLO LDAN GYI BLO NI ‘PHEL BAR BYA BA’I PHYIR, LANG KAR GSHEGS PA’I MDO DE LAS KUN MKHYEN GYIS MU STEGS PA’I RGYUD KYI BDAG DANG GTZO BO SOGS ‘JIG RTEN GYI BYED PA POR ‘DOD PA’I LTA BA NGAN PA’I RI BO SPO MTHON PO ‘JOMS PA’I NGAG GI RANG BZHIN GYI RDO RJE

And so we could put it this way.  The actual meaning of those lines from The Ten Levels is to say that the word “only” is intended to deny that there is any other creator.  Thus it is the Journey to Langka—in order to augment the understanding of those intelligent ones who are capable of grasping suchness—speaks of the diamond weapon (consisting of speech itself) used by the Omniscient One to smash down the lofty summit of the mountain of terrible viewpoints, in the minds of those of the River Schools, where one holds that a Divine Self or Supreme Being or something of the like was the one who created the world.


[2636]
‘OG NAS ‘BYUNG BA ‘DI NI, MDO GZHAN DU SEMS TZAM ZHES GSUNGS PA’I DGONGS PA [f. 190a] GCAD PA’I PHYIR DU STON PAS GSUNGS SO,,

This diamond is the one that we find in the reference following; it was described by the Teacher in order to carve out the real intent of the term “mind only” as mentioned in other sutras.


[2637]
RDO RJE NI,
,GANG ZAG RGYUN DANG PHUNG PO DANG,
,DE BZHIN RKYEN DANG RDUL DAG DANG,
,GTZO BO DBANG PHYUG BYED PO RNAMS,
,SEMS TZAM DU NI NGAS BSHAD DO,
ZHES LANG GSHEGS LAS GSUNGS TE,

And so here is the “diamond” mentioned in the Journey to Langka:

	All these things—
	The person, the stream,
	The heaps, and so too
	The factors, the particles,
	The Supreme Being,
	The Lord of Power,
	And the Creator—

	Are all of them, I say,
	Only the mind itself.


[2638]
GANG ZAG NAS DBANG PHYUG BYED PA POR SMRA BA RNAMS KYI BYED PA PO NI, DE RNAMS MIN GYI SEMS TZAM ZHIG BYED PA POR NGA SMRA’O, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

What this is saying is that all the creators mentioned in these lines from the word “the person” up to “the Lord of Power and the Creator” are in fact not creators; and “What I say is that the real creator is the mind only.”


	[2639]
[VI.86]
Tasmin tasmin varṇitāḥ śāstra ete
tīrthyair yuktyā pudgalādyā yathāsvam,
Kartṛ tvenāpaśyatā tān jinena
lokasyoktaṃ citta mātraṃ tu kartṛ.

,JI BZHIN RANG GI BSTAN BCOS DE DE LAS,
,MU STEGS RNAMS KYIS GANG ZAG SOGS DE DAG,
,SMRAS PA DE DAG BYED POR MA GZIGS NAS,
,RGYAL BAS SEMS TZAM ‘JIG RTEN BYED POR GSUNGS,

		Look at the way
		The River Schools—

		In this or that
		Of the commentaries
		Of theirs—

		Speak of the person
		And such and such.

		The Victors though
		Do not see these
		As creators,

		And so have stated
		That it is only the mind
		Which is the creator.		


[2640]
MDO ‘DI’I DON DGROL BA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA, JI BZHIN TE JI LTAR RANG RANG GI BSTAN BCOS KYI GRUB PA’I MTHA’ DE DANG DE LAS, MU STEGS RNAMS KYIS GANG ZAG DANG SOGS PAS RGYUN DANG PHUNG PO SOGS BYED PA POR SMRAS PA DE DAG BYED PA POR MA GZIGS NAS, RGYAL BAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG ‘JIG RTEN GYI BYED PA POR GSUNGS SO,,

And so the following is stated, to unravel the intent of these lines from sutra.  Look at the way—the manner—in which the River Schools, in this or that of the commentaries of their respective systems, speak of the person “and such”—which is meant to include a flow or the heaps or such as the creator.  The Victors though do not see these as being creators, and so have stated that it is only the mind which is the creator of the world.


[2641]
RTZA BAR MU STEGS RNAMS KYIS ZHES PA NI PHAL CHE BA LA BSAMS PA STE, CHOS ‘DI PA SANGS RGYAS PA DAG GIS KYANG GANG ZAG DANG, RGYUN LA SOGS PA BYED PA POR BTAGS PA KHO NA’O,,

When the root text here mentions “non-Buddhists,” it is meant only to refer to the majority of the cases.  And that’s because those who belong to these teachings here—the Buddhists themselves—also include those who in sheer imagination impute creatorship upon things like the person, or the flow.


[2642]
YANG NA GANG ZAG SOGS BYED PA POR RTOG PA DE DAG KYANG CHOS ‘DI PA SANGS RGYAS PA MA YIN TE, MU STEGS LTAR SANGS RGYAS KYI BSTAN PA’I DON PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR MA RTOGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

We can also say that those who imagine that the person and so forth could be the creator here could never be those of “this” school—referring to the Buddhists.  And that’s because, like those of the River Schools, they would have to fail to grasp the meaning of the teachings of the Buddha in an unmistaken way.


[2643]
DE’I PHYIR MU STEGS ZHES PA NI KHYAB PAR BYED PA’I TSIG GO

As such, we would then say that the term “follower of the River School” was comprehensive.


[2644]
,RIN CHEN ‘PHRENG BA LAS KYANG,
,GANG ZAG PHUNG POR SMRA BA YI,
,’JIG RTEN GRANGS CAN ‘UG PHRUG DANG,
,GOS MED BCAS LA GAL TE ZHIG
,YOD MED ‘DAS PA SMRA NA DRIS,

We further see the following lines in the String of Precious Jewels—

Suppose we ask
Those who say
That the person
Is the heaps—

The worldly ones,
The Numerists,
The Children of the Owl,
And those Unclothed—

Whether or not
There could be something
That was beyond existing,
Or not existing.


	[2645]
,DE PHYIR SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS NI,
,BSTAN PA ‘CHI MED YOD MED LAS,
,’DAS [f. 190b] PA ZAB MO ZHES BSTAN PA,
,CHOS KYI KHUD PA YIN ZHES GYIS,

This then is why
We say that it was
The true treasure
Of all teachings

When the Buddhas declared
The deathless and profound
Instruction which states

That everything is beyond
Either existing or not existing.


[2646]
ZHES GANG ZAG DANG PHUNG PO RDZAS SU YOD PAR SMRA BA SOGS LA YOD MED GNYIS KYI MTHA’ DANG BRAL BA SMRA BAR SNANG NA DRIS SHIG DANG, DE’I DON BSHAD RGYU MI ‘ONG NGO,,

What this is saying is that someone could make their appearance to people like those who say that the person and the parts of the person exist in a substantial way, and make the statement that these things are free of the two extremes of existing or not existing, and these people wouldn’t be able to give any explanation of what this means at all.


[2647]
DE’I PHYIR BSTAN PA’I DON YOD MED GNYIS KYI MTHA’ DANG BRAL BA NI, DAM PA’I CHOS KYI KHUD PA STE KHYAD PAR GYI CHOS GZHAN LA MED PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG CES GSUNGS SO,,

As such, it’s saying, the meaning of the teaching—that things are free of either extreme, of existing or not existing—is the true treasure of all the teachings.  Which is to say, you should realize that it can be found in no other teaching there is, no matter how special it may be.


[2648]
‘KHOR BA ‘DI NI THOG MA MED PAS ‘DIR SNGAR NGAN RTOG CI ZHIG MA BYUNG PHYIS KYANG CI ZHIG MI ‘BYUNG ZHING, ‘DI LTAR DA LTA NYID DU YANG SPONG BA DKAR PO LA SOGS PA DAG LA PHUNG PO LA SOGS PA RDZAS SU YOD PA BYED PA PO NYID DU STON PA SNANG NGO,,

“This cycle of suffering has no starting point; as such, there is no unsavory idea that has not occurred at some point in time before now; and there is none that will not occur after this, either.  And so even in the present days themselves we see groups like the White Renunciates, who teach that the heaps exist in a substantial way, and that they are the creator of things.”


[2649]
‘DI LA DPE KHA CIG LAS SPONG DKAR PO LA SOGS PA ZHES KYANG ‘BYUNG ZHING, ‘GREL BSHAD KYI ‘GYUR LAS DGE SLONG SKYA BA SING LA SOGS PA ZHES ‘BYUNG LA, DE’I DON GCER BU PA’I DGE SLONG RNAMS LA ‘CHAD DO,,

In some manuscripts, we also see the wording here as “things like the white renunciation”; while there is a translation of the commentary that says it as “the monk named Kyawa Sing” or things of the like.  The meaning of this term is explained as referring to the equivalent of a monk among the Jains.


[2650]
SPONG BA PA NI BSAM GTAN PA’I MING YIN PAS BSAM GTAN PA DKAR PO ZHES PA’I RANG SDE PHUNG PO RDZAS YOD BYED PA POR SMRA BA ZHIG GO

“Renunciate” is another name for a person who meditates frequently; as such, we could say it here as “The White Meditator.”  The point is that it is a group which says the heaps to a person exist substantially, and that they are the creator.



“Only” means “primary”

[2651]
,GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to our third part from above: establishing that the intent of the word “only” is to say only that the mind is the primary thing.


[2652]
DE LTAR NA RE ZHIG BYED PA PO SEMS LAS GZHAN PA BKAG PAS, TZAM GYI SGRA’I DON BYAS ZIN PA’I PHYIR TZAM GYI SGRAS SHES BYA PHYI ROL GYI DON ‘GOG MI NUS PAR BRJOD NAS, BSHAD TSUL DE LAS RNAM PA GZHAN SEMS GTZO BOR GYUR PAR BSHAD PA LAS KYANG PHYI ROL ‘GOG PA MI SRID PAR BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

And so to this point we have expressed how we deny that the creator could be anything other than the mind; and also finished our treatment of what the term “only” refers to, showing how—as such—this term is unable to deny entities that could ever be outside objects.  Now then we will diverge from that explanation to another, which shows that even if we take the meaning of this term to say that the mind is the main thing, it is still not possible for that to be used to say that there are no outside objects.


	[2653]
[VI.87]
Buddho yadvad buddha tattvo niruktas
tadval lokaś citta mātra pradhānaḥ,
Uktaḥ sūtre cittamātraṃ niṣedho
no rūpasyetīha sūtrārtha evam.

,DE NYID RGYAS LA SANGS RGYAS BSNYAD JI BZHIN,
,DE BZHIN SEMS TZAM GTZOR GYUR ‘JIG RTEN LA,
,MDO LAS SEMS TZAM ZHES [208b] GSUNGS GZUGS NI ‘DIR,
,’GOG PA DE LTAR MDO YI DON MA YIN,

	We refer to those
	Who have expanded
	Their mind
	Into suchness
	As “Buddhas.”

	In the same way,
	It is “mind only”
	In the sense of 
	The main thing.

	This is from
	References in sutra
	Which say that

	“For the world,
	There is only mind [f. 208b].”

	Here it is not the
	Meaning of sutra to be
	Some kind of denial
	Of outer form.


[2654]
JI LTAR DE KHO NA NYID LA BLO RGYAS PA LA SANGS RGYAS ZHES BSHAD PA NA, TSIG SNGA MA SANGS ZHES PA MI MNGON [f. 191a] PAR BYAS NAS TE MI MNGON KYANG, SANGS RGYAS ZHES BSNYAD PA YOD PA JI LTA BA

Now the name “Buddha” is explained as referring to someone who has expanded their mind into suchness; with this explanation though, it is still not obvious how the former of the syllables applies.  Even though it is not evident in this way, we still refer to these beings as “Buddhas”.


[2655]
DE BZHIN DU, GZUGS DANG SEMS GNYIS KYI NANG NAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG GTZO BOR GYUR PA LA TSIG PHYI MA GTZO BOR GYUR PA MI MNGON PAR BYAS NAS, MDO LAS ‘JIG RTEN LA STE KHAMS GSUM NI SEMS TZAM MO ZHES GSUNGS PAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

In the same way, we can say—among the two options of form or mind—something is “mind only” in the sense of mind being the main thing.  Now in the second syllable of this term, it may not be obvious that the reference is to being primary; but it can be understood from references in sutra which say that “for the world”—for the three realms of existence—“there is only the mind.”


[2656]
DE’I PHYIR SEMS TZAM MO ZHES PA ‘DIR NI STE ‘DIS NI, GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS KHAMS GSUM ‘GRUB PA LA GTZO BO YIN PA SEL BAR BYED KYI, SEMS TZAM ZHIG KHO NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YIN GYI PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NI MED DO ZHES ‘GOG PA DE LTAR ‘CHAD PA NI MDO YI DON MA YIN NO,,

And so let’s look at the term here in the expression “mind only.”  It serves, first of all, to preclude the possibility that—in the formation of the three realms—physical matter is the main thing.  But it is not the meaning of sutra here when people explain it as some kind of denial; that is, as saying that it is just—that is, only—the mind which exists through its own nature, and there is then no outer form.


[2657]
SA BCU PA’I MDO’I DON ‘DI NI KHO BO CAG GIS JI SKAD DU BSHAD PA DE BZHIN DU GDON MI ZA BAR ‘DOD PAR BYA’O,,

As for the meaning of the sutra on The Ten Levels, it should most certainly be accepted just as we for our part have explained it here.


	[2658]
[VI.88]
Rūpam eva yadi tatra niṣiddhaṃ
citta mātram idam ityavagamya,
Moha karmajam uvāca kim arthaṃ
cittam atra punar eva mahatma.

,GAL TE ‘DI DAG SEMS TZAM ZHES MKHYEN NAS,
,DE LAS GZUGS NYID DGAG PAR MDZAD NA NI,
,SLAR YANG DE LAS BDAG NYID CHEN POS SEMS,
,GTI MUG LAS LAS SKYES PAR CI PHYIR GSUNGS,

		Suppose all these
		Were referred to
		As “only the mind,”

		And the Buddha
		Knew this, and so
		Meant in this
To deny “form itself.”

And then how
Could it be in it
For the Great Being
To state that the mind

Was born from
Dark ignorance
And karma?


[2659]
KHYOD KYI LUGS LTAR NA GAL TE KHAMS GSUM PO ‘DI DAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I SEMS TZAM MO ZHES MKHYEN NAS, SA BCU PA DE LAS PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NYID DGAG PAR MDZAD NA NI,

Suppose then it were the way that your system would have it.  That is, suppose all these three realms of existence were referred to as “only the mind,” as something which existed through its own nature.  And suppose the Buddha knew this, and so meant—in this Ten Levels—to deny “form itself,” in the sense of outer form.


[2660]
SLAR YANG SA BCU PA DE LAS BDAG NYID CHEN PO SANGS RGYAS KYIS SEMS TE RNAM SHES DE MA RIG PA’I RKYEN GYIS ‘DU BYED, ‘DU BYED KYI RKYEN GYIS RNAM SHES ZHES GTI MUG MA RIG PA DANG, ‘DU BYED LAS GNYIS LAS SKYES PAR CI’I PHYIR GSUNGS PA RIGS TE MI RIGS SO,,

And then how could it be correct for The Ten Levels to go further, and in it for the Great Being—the Buddha—to state that the mind, which is to say consciousness, triggered (through the factor of misunderstanding) fresh karma; and that then the factor of fresh karma triggered consciousness?  That is, how could it be correct for him to have stated that these things were born from the two of misunderstanding—dark ignorance—and the fresh type of karma?  It could not have then been correct!


[2661]
SA BCU PA’I MDO DE NYID LAS RNAM SHES MA RIG PA DANG ‘DU BYED KYI ‘BRAS BUR GSUNGS KYI, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR NI MA GSUNGS [f. 191b] SO,,

That is, this same Ten Levels does state that consciousness is a result of misunderstanding and fresh karma; but it doesn’t say anything about things existing by definition.


[2662]
RTEN ‘BYUNG DU YANG GSUNGS LA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR YANG GSUNGS NA NI GSUNG BA PO ‘KHRUL ZAD LA DE GNYIS KA RANG LUGS SU BZHED PA MI SRID PAS, GDUL BYA GZHAN BKRI PA’I PHYIR GZHAN NGOR ZHAL GYIS BZHES PAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

That is, it would be nothing less than a gross error for the person making these statements to say that things were arising out of dependence, and at the same time to say that they existed by definition.  Which is to say, it would be impossible to say that your own system was that you accepted both concepts.  As such, you should understand that that they were accepted only in front of certain disciples, in order lead them—in time—to something higher.


[2663]
GNYIS KA RANG LUGS SU MI RUNG BA NI GAL TE RNAM PAR SHES PA RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS GRUB PAR GYUR NA NI, RNAM SHES DE MA RIG PA’AM ‘DU BYED LA MI LTOS PAR ‘GYUR BA ZHIG NA, LTOS PA YANG YIN TE, DE’I PHYIR RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI MED DO,,

And just how is it that both could never represent our own system?  Say for example that consciousness were something that could exist in & of itself.  In that case, consciousness would come to a stop, but without relying on misunderstanding, or on fresh karma; which means that it did depend on something.  And that would mean that it couldn’t be something that existed in & of itself.


[2664]
DE’I PHYIR RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU RNAM PAR SHES PA NI RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN PA KHO NA STE, RAB RIB CAN GYIS DMIGS PA’I SKRA SHAD LA SOGS PA LTAR, PHYIN CI LOG GI RKYEN YOD NA YOD PA’I PHYIR LA, DE KHO NA LTAR PHYIN CI LOG GI RKYEN MED NA MED PA’I PHYIR RO SNYAM DU BSAMS SO,,

And thus we can say that consciousness could never be something—no matter which way you look at it—that could exist through some nature of its own.  Such a thing would be similar to the strand of hair that those who have cataracts think they see—something like that.  If you say that something exists only because it has an erroneous factor, then for the very same reason we’d have to say that if something lacked an erroneous factor, then it couldn’t exist at all.  At least, that’s the way it seems to me.


[2665]
PHYIN CI LOG MA RIG PA’I RKYEN YOD NA RNAM SHES YOD PA NI, RTEN ‘BREL LUGS ‘BYUNG GIS BSTAN LA, MA RIG PA MED NA RNAM SHES LDOG PA NI LUGS LDOG GIS BSTAN PA’I 

The fact that—if the factor of misunderstanding, a mistaken state of mind, is present—then consciousness will be present, is a point which is conveyed in the presentation of interdependence in its forward order.  And then the fact that—if misunderstanding is absent, then consciousness will come to a stop—is conveyed through interdependence in its reverse order.


[2666]
MTHAR, DE LTAR ‘DU BYED DU GYUR PA NYES PA MANG PO’I SKYON CHAGS SHING NGO BO NYID MED PA DANG, MA SKYES PA MA ‘GAGS PAR SO SOR RTOG PA NA ZHES RGYAS PAR GSUNGS TE,

And then at the end of this process we have an extensive description of how—if the link of fresh karma then comes up—many problems will arise; and then we have individual ideas about the lack of an essence to things, and how things neither start nor stop.


[2667]
DE LTAR NA SEMS DANG BCAS PA SU ZHIG DE NYID LAS GSUNGS PA’I LUNG MTHONG NAS RNAM SHES RDZAS SU YOD PAR RTOG PAR BYED DE MI BYED DO,,

And so where could you ever find anyone with a brain that could lay their eyes on these sources and still imagine that consciousness could exist substantially?  Don’t do that!


[2668]
DE LTAR BYED PA NI NANG GI BDEN ‘DZIN GYI GRUB MTHAS BYAS PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

When people do act this way, it is caused by beliefs of a school of an inner tendency to hold to things as real.


[2669]
RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG,
,’JIG RTEN MA RIG RKYEN CAN DU,
,GANG PHYIR RDZOGS PA’I SANGS [f. 192a] RGYAS GSUNG,
,DE YI PHYIR NA ‘JIG RTEN ‘DI,
,RNAM RTOG YIN ZHES CIS MI ‘THAD,

The Sixty Verses on Reasoning also says it like this—

The total Buddhas stated
That the world is rooted
In misunderstanding.

Why then would it ever be
Incorrect to say
That this entire world
Is our imagination?


	[2670]
,MA RIG ‘GAGS PAR GYUR NA NI,
,GANG ZHIG ‘GAG PAR ‘GYUR BA DE,
,MI SHES PA LAS KUN BRTAGS PAR,
,JI LTA BUR NA GSAL MI GYUR,

When misunderstanding
Comes to a stop,
Why wouldn’t those elements
Come to a stop,

Since all the mistaken
Imaginations of failing
To understand things
Were brought to light?


[2671]
ZHES GSUNGS TE, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PAR ‘GYUR LA, DE’I TSE ‘KHRUL PA LOG PA NA GSAL DU ‘GRO DGOS KYI, LDOG PAR MI ‘GYUR RO, ZHES PA’I DON NO,,

The point here is that—if things could exist through some essential nature of their own—then they would exist by the very nature of things.  In that case, if we were able to correct our error, the truth would have to be brought to light.  But in the opposite case, it would not.


	[2672]
[VI.89]
Sattva lokam atha bhājana lokaṃ
cittam eva racayatyaticitram,
Karmajaṃ hi jagad uktam aśeṣaṃ
karma cittam avadhūya ca nāsti,

,SEMS NYID KYIS NI SEMS CAN ‘JIG RTEN DANG,
,SNOD KYI ‘JIG RTEN SHIN TU SNA TSOGS ‘GOD,
,’GRO BA MA LUS LAS LAS SKYES PAR GSUNGS,
,SEMS SPANGS NAS NI LAS KYANG YOD MA YIN,

	This one thing,
	The mind,

	Has set forth
		The world
		Of living beings,

		And the vessel
		Of the outer world,
		With all its
		Endless variation.

		It was stated that
All the beings there are
Have been created by karma;

If we were to eliminate
The mind, then there
Would no longer be
Any karma either.	


[2673]
SEMS GTZO BO YIN PA DE NYID BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA DE LA SEMS CAN GYI ‘JIG RTEN NI RANG GI SEMS KYIS BSAGS PA’I LAS DANG NYON MONGS PAS BDAG GI DNGOS PO RNYED PA YIN LA,

The goal here then is to explain this one thing: that the mind is the principal point.  To do so, we show how the world of living beings is brought into being as something for them through the karma and the negativities that they have accumulated with their own minds.


[2674]
SNOD KYI ‘JIG RTEN SHIN TU SNA TSOGS PA NI SEMS CAN DE DAG KHO NA’I SEMS NYID KYIS BSAGS PA’I THUN MONG BA’I LAS KYIS ‘GOD PA STE SKYED DE, RLUNG GI DKYIL ‘KHOR NAS ‘OG MIN GYI SNOD KYI MTHAR THUG PA’O,,

And the vessel of the outer world, with all its endless variation, is something that has been “set forth”—which is to say, created—only by all these living beings, through the communal karma they have accumulated with nothing other than their own minds.  And this refers to the entire universe, up to its very ends—starting from the disk of wind that serves as the foundation of the universe, up to the highest of its levels, known as “Below None.”


[2675]
DE LA RMA BYA LA SOGS PA’I MDONGS LA SOGS PA SNA TSOGS PA NI, SEMS CAN DE RNAMS KHO NA’I LAS THUN MONG MA YIN PAS SKYED PA’O,,

And so things like the extraordinary variety of colors found in things such as the feathers of the peacock are all objects which were created by the unique karma only of living beings themselves.


[2676]
PAD+MA LA SOGS PA’I ‘DAB MA DANG KHA DOG SNA TSOGS PA NI, SEMS CAN GYI THUN MONG GI LAS KYIS BSKYED PA’O,,

The petals and multifarious hues of things like the lotus too are produced from the shared karma of living beings.


[2677]
DE BZHIN DU GZHAN LA’ANG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

And you can understand everything else there is, as being similar.


[2678]
JI SKAD DU,
,SEMS CAN LAS KYI DBANG GIS RI,
,NAG PO’I DUS SU SKYES TE DPER,
,SEMS DMYAL MTHO RIS ‘JIG RTEN DU,
,MTSON DANG RIN CHEN SHING BZHIN NO,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

In the days of darkness,
The mountains rose up
Due to the power
Of the karma of beings.

It was just the same
As how weapons
And trees made of jewel
Appear in the realms
Of hell and the higher births.


[2679]
‘JIG RTEN GNYIS THUN MONG GI LAS YIN MIN GNYIS KYIS BSKYED PA NI, SEMS TZAM [f. 192b] GYI GZHUNG DU YANG BSHAD PAS SEMS TZAM GYI LUGS LA’ANG SNOD KYI ‘JIG RTEN MED PA MIN NO,,

The idea of two different worlds created by karma of beings which is either shared or not is something that we also observe in the great books of the Mind Only school; as such, we can say that it is not the case that in the Mind Only system there is no vessel of the outer world.


[2680]
DE LTAR NA ‘GRO BA MA LUS PA LAS LAS SKYES PAR GSUNGS SHING, SEMS SPANGS NAS NI LAS KYANG YOD PA MA YIN TE SEMS DANG BCAS PA KHO NAS LAS GSOG PA’I PHYIR NA LAS KYANG SEMS LA BRTEN PA’O,,

Thus it is then that it was stated that all the beings there are have been created by karma; and that—if we were to eliminate the mind—then there would no longer be any karma either.  That is, it being the case that karma is collected only by those who possess a mind, we can say that karma too is something that depends upon the mind.


[2681]
DE LTAR NA SA BCU PAR BYED PA PO DANG TSOR BA PO MED PA ZHES GSUNGS PA LA BRTEN NAS, TZAM GYI SGRAS BYED PA PO GZHAN ‘GOG PAR BSTAN LA, 

We can say then that—based on the statement in The Ten Levels that there is no creator, and no one who has feelings—the term “only” is meant to deny any other creator of things.


[2682]
YAN LAG BCU GNYIS PO THAMS CAD KYANG SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LA BRTEN NAS, TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BOR GYUR PAR BSTAN TE, BSHAD PA SNGA MA DGAG PHYOGS DANG PHYI MA SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN NO,,

And so we see statements that all of the twelve links of dependence rely on but one thing, the mind.  Relying on these statements, we can say then that the word “only” is meant to indicate that it is the mind which is primary.  The former of the two statements is made from the negative side of things; while the latter is meant from the positive side of things.


[2683]
DE’I PHYIR ‘GRO BA RAB TU ‘JUG PA LA SEMS NYID GTZO BO’I RGYU YIN GYI, SEMS LAS GZHAN PA NI GTZO BO’I RGYU MIN PAS, MDO LAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG GTZO BOR BZHAG GI GZUGS NI MA YIN NO,,

And so for the concerns of living beings, the mind is the principal cause; but things which are other than the mind are not the main cause of things; as such, what sutra is saying is that it is “only the mind” which is the main thing, and not physical matter.


	[2684]
[VI.90]
Rūpam asti khalu yadyapi tasya
kartṛtā tu na hi cittavad asti,
Tena kartur itarasya hi cittād
vāraṇaṃ na khalu rūpa niṣedhaḥ.

,GAL TE GZUGS YOD MOD KYI DE LA NI,
,SEMS BZHIN BYED PA PO NYID YOD MA YIN,
,DES NA SEMS LAS GZHAN PA’I BYED PA PO,
,BZLOG GI GZUGS NI BKAG PA MA YIN NO,

		We would
		Have to admit
		That physical matter
		Does exist;

		It is not the case
		That with this
		You find the
		One creator,

		As in the case
		Of the mind.
		
		As such, we reject
		Any creator other than
		The mind itself;

		But that is not denying
		Outer form itself.


[2685]
GAL TE GZUGS YOD PAR ‘DOD MOD KYI STE KYANG GZUGS DE LA NI SEMS BZHIN DU ‘GRO BA’I BYED PA PO NYID NI YOD PA MA YIN NO,,

Now we would have to admit that physical matter is indeed something which does exist; but it is not the case that with this matter you find the one creator of beings, as you do in the case of the mind.


[2686]
DES NA SEMS LAS GZHAN PA’I BYED PA PO BZLOG PA STE BKAG GI ,PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NI BKAG PA MA YIN NO,,

As such, we reject—which is to say, we deny—any creator other than the mind itself.  But we are not thereby denying outer form itself.


[2687]
‘DI NA GRANGS CAN SOGS KHA CIG NI GTZO BO LA SOGS PA BYED PA PO DANG, SANGS RGYAS PA KHA CIG GIS NI SEMS BYED PA POR ‘DOD LA, GZUGS BYED PA PO MIN PA LA NI RTZOD PA MED DO,,

In a sense then there is no argument on this point, at least insofar as these different schools are denying that physical matter is the creator of things.  That is, the Numerists and systems like that say that the Supreme Being or the like is the creator; while some number of the Buddhists say that this creator was the mind.


[2688]
DE’I PHYIR GTZO BO LA SOGS PA GZHAN GYIS BYED PA POR DOGS PA STE BRTAGS PAR BYAS PA, BYED PA PO DE’I MTSAN NYID MED PA GTZO [f. 193a] BO LA SOGS PA KHO NA BSAL BAR BYA BA’I PHYIR, THA SNYAD DU BYED PA PO NYID DU NUS PAR MTHONG BAS,

And so let’s look at the Supreme Being or the like, that others impute or imagine is the creator of things.  The goal then became only to refute the idea of a Supreme Being or the like, as lacking the necessary qualities of a creator.  People were looking for something that, in a nominal sense, had the capacity to be a real creator.


[2689]
SEMS TZAM ZHIG BYED PA POR BRJOD PA NA GTZO BO LA SOGS PA BYED PA PO YIN PA BSAL NAS, GTZO BO LA SOGS PA YUL BTON PA’I RTZOD PA’I GNAS KYI YUL GNON NO ZHES BYA BAR RIGS TE,

And so by saying that it was only the mind that was the creator, they could eliminate the possibility that a Supreme Being or something of the like could be the creator.  And so it would be accurate to say now that we had “singled out” a Supreme Being or the like, in the sense of singling them out as the new object of our argument.


[2690]
YUL GCIG LA DBANG BYED PAR ‘DOD PA’I RGYAL PO GNYIS KYI NANG NAS ‘GRAN ZLA GCIG BTON NAS, BTON PA RANG GI YUL ‘THOB CING GNYIS KA LA NYE BAR MKHO BA’I PHYIR SKYE BO PHAL PA LA GNOD PA MED PA LTAR

Suppose for example that there are two kings who would both like to be the one in charge of a single country.  If then you remove one of the two contenders and go to that one and make sure that they get their own separate land as well, then it does no harm to the general populace that is—after all—necessary for both parties.


[2691]
DE BZHIN DU ‘DIR YANG GNYIS KA LA NYE BAR MKHO BA’I PHYIR, GZUGS LA GNOD PA MED PAS GZUGS YOD PA KHO NA YIN NO ZHES BYA BAR NGES PAR BYA’O,,

Here the case is the same; after all, the concept of physical matter is something which is helpful to both parties.  And so we would certainly have to avoid challenging the concept of form in general, in a sense saying “form only”—but with the connotation that “form is only something which exists.”



Outer & inner are equivalent

[2692]
GNYIS PA NI,

With this we have reached our second part from above: a demonstration that outside objects, and the inner mind, are equivalent in either existing or not existing.


	[2693]
[VI.91]
Pañcāpyete santi loka prasiddhāḥ
skandhās tattve laukike’vasthitasya,
Tattva jñānasyodaye vāñchite vai
pañcāpyete yogināṃ naivajātāḥ.

,’JIG RTEN PA YI DE NYID LA GNAS LA,
,PHUNG PO ‘JIG RTEN GRAGS TE LNGA CHAR YOD,
,DE NYID YE SHES ‘CHAR BAR ‘DOD PA NA,
,RNAL ‘BYOR PA LA DE LNGA ‘BYUNG MI ‘GYUR,

		All five do exist,
Just as they are
Spoken of in
		The everyday world:

		That part
		Can be found
		In the way things are,
		According to the world.

		In a case where
		We accept that
		There can appear
		That wisdom
		Of suchness,

		These five
		Do not occur
		For a deep practitioner.


[2694]
DE PHYIR DE LTAR SNGAR JI SKAD BSTAN PA’I TSUL GYIS ‘JIG RTEN PA YI DE NYID DE RNAM GZHAG LA GNAS PA LA PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS KYI PHUNG PO LA SOGS PA RNAMS ‘JIG RTEN LA GRAGS TE PHUNG PO LNGA CHAR YOD LA, 

And so as such, we have demonstrated that all five parts to a person, just as they are spoken of in the everyday world, do exist.  Which is to say that—in the way in which we described it before—there does exist that part of outside form which can be found in the presentation of the way things are, according to the world at large.


[2695]
DE KHO NA NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA’I YE SHES ‘CHAR BAR ‘DOD PA NA RNAL ‘BYOR PA MNYAM PAR GZHAG PA LA DE’I NGOR PHUNG PO DE LNGA ‘BYUNG BAR MI ‘GYUR RO,,

In a case where we accept that there can appear to a person that wisdom which perceives suchness directly, then we can say that these five parts to a person do not occur in the perceptions of this balanced meditation of a deep practitioner.


	[2696]
[VI.92]
	Rūpābhāve mā grahīś cittasattāṃ
rūpābhāvaṃ cittasattve ca mā gāḥ,
Prajñānītau sūtra ete samānaṃ
Buddhaiḥ kṣiptā varṇitāś cābhidharme.


[VI.92a]
,GZUGS MED NA NI SEMS YOD MA ‘DZIN ZHIG
,SEMS YOD ‘DI NA’ANG GZUGS MED MA ‘DZIN ZHIG

		If there exists
		No form,
		Then you shouldn’t
		Hold that mind
		Exists either.

		And if
		Mind exists,
		You shouldn’t
Be holding that
There exists no form.


[2697]
GANG GI PHYIR DE LTA YIN PA DE’I PHYIR PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS MED PAR ‘DOD NA NI SEMS YOD PAR MA ‘DZIN CIG ,NANG GI SEMS YOD PAR ‘DOD PA NYID YIN NA’ANG PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS MED PAR MA ‘DZIN CIG

For the reason that this is the way that things are, if you are going to hold that there exists no outer form, then you shouldn’t hold to the idea that mind exists either.  And if you want to be someone who keeps holding to this belief that the inner mind exists, then you shouldn’t be holding to the idea that there exists no outer form.


[2698]
,GANG GI TSE BTAGS DON ‘TSOL BA’I ‘THAD PAS DPYAD PA NA PHYI’I GZUGS MED PAR RTOG NA NI DE’I TSE PHYI NANG GNYIS KA’I YOD PA ‘THAD PAS LAS ‘GRUB PA [f. 193b] DANG BRAL BA’I PHYIR NANG GI SEMS MED PAR YANG RTOGS PAR BYA DGOS LA,

And suppose you use reasoning to go looking for the the thing that is given the name, and thus come to the idea that there is no outer form.  At that point, you would fail to be able to establish karma, through reasoning which establishes both the existence of the outer and the inner.  And at that juncture, you would have to come to a realization that there was no mind, on the inside.


[2699]
YANG GANG GI TSE SEMS YOD PA NYID DU RTOG NA NI DE’I TSE GZUGS KYANG RTOGS PAR BYA DGOS TE GNYIS KA YANG ‘JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Or we could say that if you think that the mind truly is something that exists, then you would also have to come to the realization that form exists as well.  After all, both of them are accepted by the world at large.


[2700]
‘DIR SEMS TZAM PAS GZUGS DANG SEMS GNYIS LA YOD MED KYI KHYAD PAR ‘DOD PAR BSHAD PA’I GZUGS MED PA NI PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS MED PA YIN TE, PHYI GZUNG MED PAR RANG GI SA BON LAS, ,SNGO SOGS SNANG NYID ‘BYUNG BAR, ZHES GSUNGS SHING

So here we have those of the Mind Only saying that they believe that there is a difference between the two of form and the mind, where one exists but the other does not.  And when they say that form does not exist, what they’re saying is that it’s outer form that does not exist.  As the text says,

		The appearance
		Of blue and the like,
		Comes from
		Seeds for it
		In the absence
		Of outer objects.


[2701]
DE’I ‘GREL PA LAS KYANG, SNGON PO LA SOGS PA’I PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS MED PAR ZHES GZUGS MED PA’I DGAG BYA LA PHYI ROL GYI KHYAD PAR SMOS SHING,

We also see the autocommentary on this specifically mentioning the qualification of “outer” to the thing that we deny when we say “there exists no form”: “none of the outer form of blue and the rest exists.”


[2702]
YANG ‘GREL PA LAS, TZAM GYI SGRAS SHES BYA ‘GOG PAR MI NUS PAR BRJOD NAS RNAM PA GZHAN DU BSHAD PA LAS KYANG PHYI ROL ‘GOG PA MI SRID PAR BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA ZHES GZUGS ‘GOG PA MDO’I DON MIN PAR GSUNGS PA’I GZUGS ‘GOG PA PHYI ROL ‘GOG PA LA BSHAD PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And for the same reason we also see in the autocommentary:

Having described how the term “only” would not be able to deny existing entities, there may be other ways of explaining it; and the clarification is meant to indicate that it is not possible to deny outer objects.

What this is saying is that denying form is not the intent of the sutra; but rather that the denial of form here is a a denial of that which is outside.


[2703]
DE LTA MA YIN PAR TSIG ZIN TZAM LA BYED NA TZAM GYI SGRAS SHES BYA ‘GOG MI NUS PA BRJOD NAS, ZHES GSUNGS PAS SEMS TZAM PAS TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS KYI SHES BYA BKAG PAR ‘DOD DO ZHES KYANG BRJOD PAR BYA’O,,

If this were not the way it is, and we were to take the “only” in its literal sense, then what this is saying is that the “only” could not be able to deny an existing entity.  As such, we would also have to say that Mind Only believed that the term “only” was meant to deny the existing entity of the mind itself.


[2704]
GAL TE SEMS TZAM PAS GZUGS CAN KHAS MI LEN NA SEMS TZAM PAS KUN GZHI SGRUB PA’I RIGS PA STON PA NA, THEG BSDUS LAS, NYING MTSAMS SBYOR BA SBREL {%SPREL} ZIN PA RNAMS KYI DBANG PO GZUGS CAN ‘DZIN PAR BYED PA YANG DE LAS GZHAN RNAM PAR SMIN PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA MED PAR {%this med-pa not in Teng!} MI [f. 194a] ‘THAD DE ZHES DANG,

And suppose you say that the Mind Only did not accept things with form.  In such a case, it would be a sheer contradiction for A Compendium of the Greater Way to make certain statements that it does, in its presentation of the reasoning that the Mind Only uses for for establishing foundation consciousness.  One of these is—

It would be incorrect to say that those who have already made the connection of the crossing between death & birth—and who were thus holding to sense powers consisting of form—possessed none of the consciousness that was other than these and which had then ripened.


[2705]
RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG MING DANG GZUGS MDUNG KHYIM LTAR GCIG LA GCIG BRTEN PA’I TSUL GYIS ‘JUG PA GANG YIN PA DE YANG RNAM PAR SMIN PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA MED NA MI RUNG NGO, ZHES GSUNGS PA RNAMS ‘GAL BA KHO NAR ‘GYUR TE

Another of these references says that—in a case where consciousness and name & form engage in dependence one upon the other, like spears leaned point-up against each other in a tripod—then “it would be incorrect to say that there was no consciousness that had ripened here.”


[2706]
GZUGS CAN GYI CHOS KHAS BLANGS NA PHYI ROL KHAS LEN DGOS PAR ‘DOD PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Which is to say, if you accept the idea of entities which have form, then you would have to accept the idea of things on the outside.


[2707]
DES NA RNAM PAR SHES PA’I RKYEN GYIS MING GZUGS SKYE BA SOGS KHAS LEN KYANG PHYI ROL KHAS LEN MI DGOS PAR ‘DOD PA LA BZLOG NAS SMRA BAR MI BYA STE, SEMS TZAM GYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA’I RNAM GZHAG STON PA NA DE LTAR BSHAD PA SHIN TU MANG NGO,,

As such, I would encourage people not to say it all backwards here: don’t go around claiming that you can accept for example that name & form arise through the factor of consciousness, but that this doesn’t necessitate accepting things on the outside.  We see a massive number of people offering this type of explanation when they make presentations of the unique beliefs of the Mind Only.


	[2708]
[VI.92b]
,DE DAG SHES RAB TSUL MDOR SANGS RGYAS KYIS,
,MTSUNGS PAR SPANGS SHING MNGON PA’I CHOS LAS GSUNGS,

		In sutras
		On the ways
		Of wisdom,

		The Buddha
		Treated them
		As equivalent,
		In rejecting.

		He also stated this
		In the teachings
		Of higher knowledge.


[2709]
LUNG LAS KYANG PHYI ROL GYI DON DANG NANG GI SHES PA YOD MED MTSUNGS PA DE LTAR RTOGS PAR BYA STE, ‘DI LTAR GZUGS LA SOGS PA’I PHUNG PO LNGA PO DE DAG NI SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’I TSUL GYI MDOR NI SANGS RGYAS KYIS LNGA CHAR YANG MTSUNGS PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA SPANGS SHING STE BKAG PA YIN TE,

We can also understand, from scripture, how outside objects and inside awareness must be equivalent, in either existing or not existing.  We can look thus at physical form and the rest of the five parts to the person as these are presented in sutras on the ways of the perfection of wisdom.  Here, the Buddha treated all five as equivalent, in rejecting—that is, denying—that they could exist through any nature of their own.


[2710]
RAB ‘BYOR GZUGS NI RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG NGO ZHES BYA BA NAS RNAM PAR SHES PA NI RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG NGO ZHES GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And that’s because he made statements ranging from “O Subhuti, form is empty of any nature of its own” up to “awareness is empty of any nature of its own.”


[2711]
CHOS MNGON PA LAS NI LNGA CHAR YANG RANG DANG SPYI’I MTSAN NYID LA SOGS PA’I SGO NAS MTSUNGS PAR GSUNGS SO,,

In the teachings of higher knowledge as well, it is stated that all five are equivalent in features such as both their unique and general defining characteristics.


	[2712]
[VI.93]
Bhitvāpyetāṃ satyayor ānupūrvīṃ
na dravyaṃ te yāti siddhiṃ niṣiddham,
Tasmād evaṃ prakramād viddhi bhāvān
loke jātāṃs tattva taś cādyajātān.

,BDEN GNYIS RIM PA ‘DI DAG BSHIG NAS KYANG,
,KHYOD KYI RDZAS NI BKAG PAS ‘GRUB MI ‘GYUR,
,DE PHYIR DE LTA’I RIM PAS DNGOS GDOD NAS,
,DE NYID MA SKYES ‘JIG RTEN SKYES RIG BYA,

		Even though
These stages
		Of the two realities
		Are destroyed,

		That doesn’t mean
		That your idea
		Of the substantial
		Is established;
		For it was disproved.

		Thus it is that,
		Because of stages
		Like that,
		
		Entities have
		Never arisen,
		For all the time
		There ever was.

		It is reasonable
		To say,
		In the world,
		That they have arisen.


[2713]
DE’I PHYIR PHA ROL GYIS NI SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR PHYI ROL DANG SEMS GNYIS DON DAM PAR MED MNYAM DANG, KUN RDZOB TU YOD MNYAM DU LUNG DANG RIGS PAS GRUB PA’I BDEN GNYIS KYI RIM PA ‘DI DAG BSHIG [f. 194b] PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

As such, the explanation of the other side about these stages of the two realities is destroyed: where it is established by both scripture & reasoning that the two of outside things and the mind are equivalent in not existing in an ultimate way, and equivalent as well in existing in a deceptive way.


[2714]
DE LTAR BSHIG NAS KYANG SEMS TZAM PA KHYOD KYI GZHAN DBANG RDZAS SU GRUB PA NI ‘GRUB PAR MI ‘GYUR RO,,

And even though these things are thus destroyed, that doesn’t mean that your Mind Only idea of dominated entities that exist substantially is established.


[2715]
CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA, GANG GI PHYIR SNGAR GZHAN DBANG RDZAS SU GRUB PA LAN DU MAR BKAG PA DE’I PHYIR, KHYOD KYI NGAL BA DON MED PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And why is that?  Because all your efforts to exhaust yourself here are simply pointless, given that we have earlier on disproved—many times over—your idea that dominated entities could exist substantially.


[2716]
BDEN GNYIS KYI RIM PA MI ‘JIG PA LA DON DAM PAR MED CING THA SNYAD DU YOD PAR ‘DOD DGOS PA DE’I PHYIR, SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTA BU’I RIM PAS DNGOS PO RNAMS GDOD MA NAS DE KHO NA NYID DU MA SKYES SHING, ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU SKYES PAR RIG PAR BYA’O ZHES GSUNGS TE,

To keep the stages of the two realities from being destroyed, you would have to agree to the idea that they do not exist in any ultimate way, but do exist nominally.  Thus it is that it was stated that—because of the stages that we have previously explained as being like that, we would have to say that entities have never arisen, for all the time there ever was, through some inherent nature of their own; and that it is still reasonable to say, in the normal parlance of the world, that they have arisen.


[2717]
‘DIS NI DNGOS PO RNAMS MA SKYES PA DON DAM DANG, SKYES PA THA SNYAD DU KHAS BLANG BAR STON PAS DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR NGES PAR SBYAR BAR BYA’O,,

What all this is demonstrating is that we accept that the way in which things do not arise is the ultimate; and that their arising is nominal.  As such, we definitely have to differentiate what we deny, by applying certain distinctions.



“Mind only” in
A Journey to Langka

[2718]
GSUM PA LA GNYIS, PHYI ROL MED PA’I SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA DRANG DON DU BSTAN PA, MDO’I DRANG NGES KYI DON RTOGS PA’I THABS BSTAN PA’O,,

Which brings us to our third step from above: an explanation of how the intent of “mind only” is described in A Journey to Langka.  We proceed in two sections here: a demonstration that the statement that things were mind only, without anything on the outside, was meant figuratively; and then showing the way in which we can understand which points in sutra are meant figuratively, and which meant literally.


[2719]
DANG PO LA GNYIS, DRANG DON DU LUNG GIS BSTAN PA, RIGS PAS BSTAN PA’O,,

We cover the first section in two stages: showing how scripture takes this statement as figurative; and then showing how logic does the same.


[2720]
DANG PO LA GNYIS, DNGOS KYI DON DANG, DE ‘DRA BA’I MDO GZHAN YANG DRANG DON DU BSTAN PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

The first of these stages has two points of its own: the actual point to be made; and then showing how other such sutras should be taken figuratively as well.  We begin now with the first.


[2721]
GAL TE YANG SA BCU PA’I MDO’I DON DE LTAR BSHAD MOD KYI, DE LTA NA YANG LUNG GZHAN LANG KAR GSHEGS PA LAS,
,PHYI ROL SNANG BA YOD MED DE,
,SEMS NI SNA TSOGS RNAMS SU SNANG,
,LUS DANG LONGS SPYOD GNAS ‘DRA BA,
,SEMS TZAM DU NI NGAS BSHAD DO,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

One may come then saying the following:

Admittedly, the meaning of The Ten Levels may be explained that way; but then again we also have the following lines, from A Journey to Langka—

		The appearance
		That things exist
		On the outside
		Is actually nothing;

		It is only the mind
		Appearing in a
		Variety of ways.

		Things like your body,
		And all that you use,
		And the place where you live—

		What I say is that
		All of them
		Are there only
		In the mind.


[2722]
DE LA LUS NI MIG LA SOGS PA’I SKYE MCHED GZUGS CAN RNAMS SO,,

The word “body” here is a reference to the eye, and the rest of the physical doors of sense.


[2723]
LONGS SPYOD NI GZUGS SGRA SOGS [f. 195a] YUL LNGA’O,,

And when it says “all that you use,” it’s referring to the five objects of the senses: visible form, sound, and the rest.


[2724]
GNAS NI SNOD KYI ‘JIG RTEN NO,,

“Place where you live” then is a reference to the outer vessel of the world.


[2725]
SEMS LAS LOGS SHIG NA PHYI ROL YOD PA MA YIN PA’I PHYIR, RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM ZHIG KHO NA LUS DANG LONGS SPYOD DANG GNAS SU SNANG BA SKYE BA NA YUL GYI DNGOS POR GNAS PA LUS LA SOGS PA RNAM PAR SHES PA LAS THA DAD PAR PHYI ROL LTA BUR MNGON PA YIN NO,,

The point is that there does not exist anything on the outside: something discrete from the mind.  And so when there arises the appearance that what is actually nothing more than consciousness seems to be our body, and the things we make use of, and the place where we live, those entities which are serving as the object of our awareness do appear as if they were a body and such on the outside, separate from our consciousness.


[2726]
DE’I PHYIR KHAMS GSUM PA NI SEMS TZAM YIN NO ZHE NA,

As such, these three realms of the universe are only mind.


	[2727]
[VI.94]
Yatrāpyuktaṃ nāsti dṛśyaṃ bahir vai
cittaṃ citraṃ dṛśyate ceti sūtre,
Rūpe’tyantaṃ ye prasaktā badhāna
rūpaṃ tebhyas tac ca neyārtham ehi.

,MDO SDE GANG LAS PHYI ROL SNANG YOD MIN,
,SEMS NI SNA TSOGS SNANG NGO ZHES GSUNGS PA,
,GZUGS LA SHIN TU CHAGS GANG DE DAG LA,
,GZUGS BZLOG PA STE DE YANG DRANG DON NYID,

There is that sutra
Which states that
The appearance
Of the outside
Is nothing that exists.

What this is saying
Is that the mind
Appears in a
Variety of ways.

There are those
With an extreme
Attraction to forms;

And so they put
A stop to forms
For these individuals—

And those were only intended
As something metaphorical.


[2728]
MDO ‘DI YANG DGONGS PA CAN NYID DU BRJOD PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,
,MDO SDE GANG LAS PHYI ROL SNANG YOD MIN,
,SEMS NI SNA TSOGS SNANG NGO ZHES GSUNGS PA,

In reply then we see the following lines of the root text, which are meant to say that this sutra too was only meant metaphorically—

There is that sutra
Which states that
The appearance
Of the outside
Is nothing that exists.

What this is saying
Is that the mind
Appears in a
Variety of ways.


[2729]
,DE’I DGONGS PA NI ‘DI YIN TE, GANG DAG GZUGS LA SHIN TU CHAGS PA’I RKYEN CAN GYI RDZAS SU CHAGS PA DANG, KHONG KHRO BA DANG NGA RGYAL LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYIS ‘JUG PA RANG DBANG MED PAR BYAS PAR ‘GYUR ZHING,

What is intended here is the following.  There are those individuals for whom certain emotions engage, beyond their control.  These are—for example—a desire for physical things triggered by an extreme attraction to forms; or else getting angry, or feeling pride.


[2730]
DE LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PAS DE DAG SDIG PA CHEN PO DANG SBYOR LA BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS BSAGS PA LAS NYAMS PAR ‘GYUR BA

And then because of their strong craving, people like this undertake major negative actions; which means that they begin to fail in their intended accumulation of merit and wisdom.


[2731]
DE DAG LA BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS GZUGS KYI RKYEN CAN GYI NYON MONGS PA BZLOG PA’I PHYIR, CHAGS PA CAN DAG LA PHYI ROL GYI YUL LA CHAGS PA ‘JOMS PA’I KENG RUS LTAR, 

The Conquerors then undertake to help these individuals put a stop to the negative emotions they feel—those emotions that find their causes in form.  And so then they teach them something like the visualization of skeletons, which smashes the attraction to outer objects that these people with craving feel so strongly.


[2732]
DE LTA BUR GYUR PA MA YIN YANG DE LTA BU NYID DU SEMS TZAM NYID BSTAN PA YIN NO ZHES BYA BAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

The things that they are taught to visualize are not actual skeletons; but what the sutra is indicating is that they are only a mental form of those very things.  This is how we should understand its lines.


[2733]
YANG LUNG ‘DI DRANG BA’I DON NYID YIN GYI NGES DON NI MA YIN NO ZHES BYA BA DE LTAR GANG LAS NGES SHE NA,

And one may then inquire—

Are there any other means that we can employ to understand that this particular citation was only intended as something metaphorical, and is therefore not something that was literal?


	[2734]
[VI.95]
Neyārthatvaṃ cādideśāsya śāstā
yuktā yuktyā cāpi neyārthatāsya,
Sūtrasyānyasyāpi caivaṃ vidhasya
neyārthatvaṃ dyotayatyāgamo’yam.

[VI.95a]
,’DI NI STON PAS DRANG DON NYID GSUNGS SHING,
,’DI NI DRANG DON NYID DU RIGS PAS ‘THAD,

	This statement was made
	By the Teacher only
	As something to be
	Taken figuratively;

	It can also be established
	That it was only meant
	As metaphorical,
	And nothing more—
	
	Through logical reasoning.


[2735]
PHYI ROL MED PAR SEMS TZAM MO ZHES GSUNGS PA ‘DI NI, STON PAS DRANG DON NYID DU GSUNGS PAS LUNG LAS DRANG DON DU ‘GRUB LA, MDO [f. 195b] ‘DI NI DRANG DON NYID DU RIGS PAS KYANG ‘THAD PA STE ‘GRUB BO,,

Let’s consider then this statement that things are only the mind—and that there are no outer things.  It was indeed made by the Teacher only as something that was meant to be taken figuratively; and we have shown that it can be established as such, from scripture itself.  So too though it can also be established—shown that it was only meant as metaphorical, and nothing more—through logical reasoning as well.


[2736]
DE LTAR PHYI ROL SNANG BA YOD MED DO, ZHES PA RNAMS KYIS SEMS TZAM DU BSTAN PA’I TZAM GYI SGRAS NI SA BCU PA’I MDO LAS BSHAD PA LTAR PHYI ROL MI ‘GOG BYED PA PO GZHAN ‘GOG CES SLOB DPON ‘DIS MI ‘CHAD KYI, DE LA NI TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI ROL ‘GOG KYANG MDO DE DRANG DON NO ZHES ‘GREL LO,,

And so let’s look at this word “only” in the expression “mind only” as it appears in the citation here about “The appearance that things exist on the outside is actually nothing.”  It is not the case that our particular master here explains this reference as he did the sutra of The Ten Levels: as denying a creator, rather than denying things on the outside.  The way he comments on this is by saying that the word “only” does indeed deny outside things, but that this sutra reference is—rather—something that was only meant in a figurative way.


[2737]
SLOB DPON CHEN PO LEGS LDAN GYIS NI MDO DES KYANG SEMS LUS DANG, LONGS SPYOD DANG GNAS DANG ‘DRA BA STE DE’I RNAM PA GRIB MA LTA BUS KHA BSGYUR BAR SKYE BA LA ‘CHAD CING PHYI ROL YOD MIN GYIS KYANG BLOS RNAM MED DU MTHONG BA ‘GOG PAR BZHED PAS TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI ROL ‘GOG PA MIN PAR ‘CHAD DO,,

The great master Bhavaviveka interprets the sutra in a way where the term “only” is not meant to deny outer objects.  Rather, he says that the sutra is saying that the mind colors the formation of our body, our possessions, and our environment in the same way that a shadow might.  Saying that things don’t exist on the outside then is meant, according to him, to deny that the mind could perceive things that have no existence at all.



Other sutras on “mind only”
are also figurative

[2738]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second point from above: showing how other such sutras should be taken figuratively as well.


	[2739]
	[VI.95b]
,RNAM PA DE LTA’I MDO SDE GZHAN YANG NI,
,DRANG DON NYID DU LUNG ‘DIS GSAL BAR BYED,

	There are
Citations from
	The body of sutras
	Like those;

	But there are
	Even more citations

	Which these quotations
	Explain to be taken
	Metaphorically.


[2740]
PHYI ROL SNANG BA YOD MED DE, ZHES SOGS KYIS PHYI ROL MED PAR SEMS TZAM ZHIG YOD PAR BSTAN PA DRANG DON YIN PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, SNGAR BSHAD PA RNAM PA DE LTA BU’I MDO SDE SEMS TZAM PA RNAMS KYIS NGES DON DU KHAS BLANGS PA LAS, GZHAN YANG NI DRANG DON NYID DU ‘CHAD ‘GYUR GYI LUNG ‘DIS GSAL BAR BYED DO,,

It’s not only the case that statements which teach about “mind only”—such as “The appearance that things exist on the outside is actually nothing”—are the only ones that should be taken metaphorically.  That is, followers of the Mind Only do take citations from the body of sutras that are like those that we’ve already mentioned here, and accept that they are to be taken literally.  But there are even more citations than these lines which these quotations to come below explain should be taken metaphorically.


[2741]
RNAM PA DE LTA BU’I MDO SDE DE YANG GANG YIN ZHE NA,

“What then,” you may ask, “are these further citations from sutra?”


[2742]
DGONGS PA NGES ‘GREL LAS NGO BO NYID GSUM BSTAN PA LAS, KUN BRTAGS PA MED PA DANG, GZHAN GYI DBANG YOD PA DANG,

Well, the autocommentary points first to the sections in What I Really Meant which describe the three different natures of things, and say that fabrications don’t exist at all; and that dominated entities do exist.


[2743]
DE BZHIN DU,
,LEN PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA ZAB CING PHRA,
,SA BON THAMS CAD CHU YI RGYUN LTA ‘BAB,
,BDAG TU RTOG PAR GYUR NA MI RUNG ZHES,
,BYIS PA RNAMS LA NGAS NI DE MA BSTAN,
ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA STE, ZHES ‘GREL PAR GSUNGS SO,,

And then it references the following verse from the sutra—

The consciousness
Which takes it on
Is deep, and subtle;

All of these seeds
Flow down like
A stream of water.

I never came
To the infants
And told them,

You should never think
That anything is itself.


[2744]
DE LA MDO DER KUN BRTAGS RANG GI [f. 196a] MTSAN NYID KYIS MED PA DANG, GZHAN DBANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS YOD PA’I YOD MED KYI KHYAD PAR PHYI’O {%PHYE’O? scan says PHYI’O},,

That is, here in this sutra there is a distinction made between existing and not existing in the sense of fabrications not existing by definition; and dominated entities existing by definition.


[2745]
BDAG GNYIS SU KUN BRTAGS PA LTA BU DANG, CHOS RNAMS LA NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR DU BTAGS PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI, DE’I LUGS KYIS SHES BYA LA MI SRID KYANG NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR DU BTAGS PA’I KUN BRTAGS DU MA ZHIG NI GZHI GRUB PA YIN NO,,

And so first we have fabricated things such as that into the two realities; and where entities are labelled into the essence and the features, as things that exist by definition.  Even though—in this system—these things are impossible with reference to existing objects, many examples of fabricated things labelled as essence and features do indeed exist.


[2746]
MDO DER GZHAN DBANG DANG YONGS GRUB GNYIS KA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR GSUNGS KYANG, ‘GREL PAR GZHAN DBANG TZAM LAS MA GSUNGS PA NI DBU SEMS BDEN PAR YOD MED RTZOD PA’I GZHI’I GTZO BO NI GZHAN DBANG YIN TE KUN BRTAGS ‘DOGS PA’I GZHI YANG GZHAN DBANG YIN LA, YONGS GRUB KYANG GZHAN DBANG LA BRTEN NAS GZHAG DGOS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

In the sutra, both dominated entities and totality are said to exist by definition; but in the commentary we only see mention here of the dominated ones.  This is because the main point of contention between the Middle Way and the Mind Only schools—as far as the question of whether they exist in truth or not—is the dominated entities.  That is, the basis upon which we label things as fabrications consists of these entities; and we must also posit totality itself on the basis of of these same dominated entities.


[2747]
DE LTAR PHYE BA YANG LUGS ‘DIS DRANG DON DU ‘CHAD DO,,

This system adds that even that kind of division itself is a point that we should take metaphorically.


[2748]
YANG MDO DER LEN PA’I RNAM PAR SHES PA ZHES SOGS KYIS RNAM SHES TSOGS BRGYAD DU GSUNGS PA’I ‘JUG SHES DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I KUN GZHI RNAM SHES GSUNGS PA YANG ‘DIR DRANG DON DU ‘CHAD DO, KUN GZHI RNAM SHES MED NA NI NYON YID KYANG GZHAG TU MED PA YIN NO,,

The same sutra, when it mentions things like “the consciousness which takes it on,” is referring to the collection of eight types of consciousness—which includes a foundation consciousness which is essentially distinct from the six sense consciousnesses.  This too is explained here as being a point to be taken figuratively.  And if no foundation consciousness exists, then negative consciousness is also something that can no longer be posited.


[2749]
LA SOGS PA’I SGRAS BSDUS PA LA MDO DER PHYI ROL BKAG PA DANG, MTHAR THUG THEG PA GSUM DU BSHAD PA GNYIS TE, ‘DIR DRANG DON DU ‘GREL DGOS PA BZHI YOD DO,,

When the autocommentary just quoted mentions “the autocommentary points first,” it’s implying other parts; these are where, in the sutra, places where things on the outside are denied, and the description of how there are, ultimately speaking, three different ways.


[2750]
‘DI RNAMS LA GO BA MTHA’ CHOD PAR MA CHAGS NA SPYIR DBU SEMS DANG KHYAD PAR DU LUGS ‘DI’I GNAD THUN MONG MA YIN PA RNAMS MI SHES PAR MTHONG NAS DRANG [f. 196b] NGES RNAM PAR ‘BYED PAR ZHIB TU BSHAD DO,,

I have come to the realization that if a person fails to develop a definitive understanding of these points, then more generally they will never come to an understanding of the schools of the Middle Way and the Mind Only—most especially the unique, crucial points of this particular way of things.  As such, I have explained covered all these ideas in great detail in my presentation on distinguishing the literal & the figurative.


[2751]
DGONGS ‘GREL LAS TSIG GANG GIS PHYI ROL MED PAR BSTAN PA NI, THEG BSDUS LAS, BCOM LDAN ‘DAS TING NGE ‘DZIN GYI SPYOD YUL GYI GZUGS BRNYAN DE CI SEMS DE LAS THA DAD PA ZHES BGYI’AM THA DAD PA MA LAGS PA ZHES BGYI, BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS BKA’ STZAL PA, BYAMS PA THA DAD PA MA YIN ZHES BYA’O,,

What exactly is the wording in What I Really Meant which presents the idea that there is nothing on the outside?  The Compendium of the Greater Way cites it this way:

He asked, “O Conqueror, what about this reflection in a mirror which is the object of the activity of concentration?  Are you saying that it is the case that the reflection is something distinct from the mind; or are you saying that it is not?”

And then the Conqueror made the following declaration: “O Loving One, it is not distinct.”


[2752]
DE CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA, RNAM PAR SHES PA NI DMIGS PA RNAM PAR RIG PA TZAM GYIS RAB TU PHYE BA CAN YIN NO ZHES NGES {%NGAS Teng} BSHAD DO, ZHES SOGS DRANGS PA RNAMS YIN NO,,

“And why is that?  Because what I say is that consciousness is something that is distinguished only by being aware of an object of perception.”


[2753]
LUGS ‘DIS NI SNGAR BSHAD PA’I DON TSAN BZHI GA DRANG DON DU ‘GREL GYI, DE DAG GI GSEB NAS KHA CIG DRANG DON DANG, KHA CIG NGES DON DU ‘GREL BA LTAR NI MI MDZAD DO,,

In this system, all four of the points covered earlier are interpreted as being metaphoric; it is not the case that they take some points out of the middle of the four together and say that this particular one is metaphoric, but this particular one is literal.


[2754]
‘DI LA YANG MTHAR THUG THEG PA GSUM DU BSHAD PA NI ‘PHAGS PA NYID KYIS MDO KUN LAS BTUS PA LAS MTHAR THUG THEG PA GCIG TU SGRUB PA LAS GO NUS PAR DGONGS NAS ‘JUG ‘GREL DU MA SMOS SO,,

Along the same lines, the explanation that—ultimately—there are three ways is something that can be understood from the substantiation in A Compendium of All the Sutras of that ultimately there is only on way.  This is why we don’t see it stated in the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way.


[2755]
LHAG MA GSUM GYI PHYI ROL MED PAR SEMS TZAM ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BSTAN PA DRANG DON DU LUNG GIS GSAL BAR BYED PA NI, LANG KAR GSHEGS PA LAS,
,JI LTAR NAD PA NAD PA LA,
,SMAN PA SMAN RNAMS GTONG BA LTAR,
,SANGS RGYAS DE BZHIN SEMS CAN LA,
,SEMS TZAM DU YANG RAB TU GSUNGS,
ZHES PA ‘DI YIN TE

Things not existing on the outside, and being the mind only, and existing through some nature of their own—according the remaining three points—are ideas that are clarified in citations from scripture as being metaphoric.  Here for example is what the Journey to Langka says:

Doctors deliver medicines
To those who are ill
According to the disease;

In the same way,
The Buddhas keep telling
Beings that it is all
Only the mind.


[2756]
NAD PA SO SO LA SMAN STER BA NI SMAN PA’I RANG DBANG GIS MA YIN GYI, NAD PA’I NAD KYI TSUL DANG BSTUN DGOS PA BZHIN DU SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA YANG STON PA’I RANG LUGS KYI DBANG GIS [f. 197a] MIN GYI, GDUL BYA’I BSAM PA’I DBANG GIS YIN PAR GSUNGS PAS LUNG SNGA MA DRANG DON DU SHES SO,,

When a doctor prescribes medicine for different patients, it is not something that they do just on their own; rather, they have to prescribe according to the way in which the sick person is sick.  What these lines are saying is that—in the same way—describing things as mind only is not something that the Teacher did because this was his own system of thinking; rather, he acted as demanded by the way that his disciples were thinking.  As such, that earlier scriptural citation can be understood as metaphorical.


[2757]
JI LTAR NAD PA ZHES SOGS KYI MJUG TU ‘GREL PA LAS, DE BZHIN DU BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYI {Tengy: %KYIS} MDO BRJOD PA LAS ZHES PA NAS, MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR ‘TSANG RGYA BA JI LTAR ‘GYUR ZHES TE, ZHES PA’I BAR LANG GSHEGS LAS GSUNGS PA RNAMS DRANGS PA NI RNAM RIG PAS KUN GZHI NGES DON DU KHAS BLANGS PA DRANG DON DU STON PA’I LUNG NGO,,

Just after the part about the patients and so on, the autocommentary continues with the wording that goes from “In the same way, when the Conqueror expressed these things in sutra…” up to “…how could one then attain perfect & total enlightenment?”  What this section is saying is that the citations that the Mentalists assert to be an acceptance of the concept of a foundation consciousness were actually scripture that was intended to express something to be taken metaphorically.


[2758]
‘DIR ‘GREL BSHAD LAS DE BZHIN DU ZHES PAS RTAG BRTAN GYI SNYING PO GSUNGS PA DRANG DON YIN PA DE BZHIN DU SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA YANG DRANG DON DU STON PA YIN ZER BA NI LOG PAR SMRA BA YIN TE, ‘GREL PA LAS SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA DRANG DON YIN PA DE BZHIN DU ZHES PA’I DON DU GSAL BAR BSHAD PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Some people claim that when the autocommentary states “in the same way” at this point, what it means to say is that statements that things are mind only were taught metaphorically, in the same way that Lord Buddha talked about “a heart that was unchanging and firm.”  This position though is completely mistaken, since that point is very clearly made in the autocommentary when it says that a case is similar to how “statements about things being mind only” were meant only metaphorically.


[2759]
DES JI LTAR NAD PA ZHES SOGS KYIS SEMS TZAM DU SMRA BA DRANG DON DU BSHAD PA BZHIN DU RTAG BRTAN GYI SNYING PO DRANG DON DU GSUNGS PAS KYANG DGONGS ‘GREL SOGS LAS KUN GZHI RNAM SHES GSUNGS PA SGRA JI BZHIN PA MIN PAR SGRUB PA YIN NO,,

That is, this part in the autocommentary is expressing the point that the statement “in the same way with people that are ill” can be used to show that—just as statements that things are mind only are explained as being metaphors—statements about a heart which is unchanging & firm are metaphoric.  And then it is for this reason that we can establish that statements in sources such as What I Really Meant about a foundation consciousness were never meant to be taken literally.


[2760]
DE LA NI THOG MAR SNYING PO BSTAN PA SGRA JI BZHIN PA MIN PAR SHES DGOS PAS, LANG GSHEGS LAS, MDO SDE {%SDE DE Kang} NI SEMS CAN GYI BSAM PA BZHIN BSTAN PA DON ‘KHRUL BA YIN TE, DE KHO NA’I GTAM MIN NO,,

For all this, we need to grasp first how those statements about a heart were not meant literally.  And so we go back to A Journey to Langka, where it says—

These words from scripture were taught only to fit the thinking of living beings; in actuality though they are mistaken, and were never meant to be taken as statements of the way things really are.


[2761]
DPER NA SMIG CHU NI CHUR MED PAS CHUR ZHEN PA’I RI DVAGS SLU BA BZHIN DU BSTAN PA’I CHOS KYANG BYIS PA MGU BAR BYED KYI, ‘PHAGS PA’I YE SHES RNAM PAR DGOD PA’I GTAM NI MIN NO,,

There is, for example, no water in a mirage; but still a wild animal who sees it will hold strongly to the idea that it is water.  Just so, there may be a teaching which was granted that pleases the infants, but which is talk that would never delight the wisdom of a realized being. 


[2762]
DES NA KHYOD KYIS DON GYI RJES SU ‘BRANG BAR BYA’I BRJOD PA LA CHAGS PAR MI BYA’O ZHES [f. 197b] BKA’ STZAL PA DANG, BLO GROS CHEN POS MDO SDE LAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA’I SNYING PO GSUNGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS ‘OD GSAL BA THOG MA MED PA NAS RNAM PAR DAG PA MTSAN SO GNYIS DANG LDAN PA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI LUS KYI NANG NA YOD PAR BRJOD DE,

Thus it was that you told us that we should follow after the meaning, and never be attached to the words.  And the ones of great wisdom have said that what was taught in the collection of sutras—what was described as the very heart of Those Gone Thus—is something possessed with the 32 marks of a total purity which has been possessed from time with no beginning, and is pure light in its very nature.  And they have stated that this is present within the bodies of every living being that there is.


[2763]
NOR BU RIN PO CHE GOS DRI MA CAN GYIS DKRIS PA BZHIN DU PHUNG KHAMS SKYE MCHED KYI GOS KYIS DKRIS SHING DRI MA CAN DU GYUR PA RTAG BRTAN THER ZUG TU BRJOD NA SNYING POR SMRA BA ‘DI MU STEGS KYI BDAG SMRA BA DANG JI LTAR MI ‘DRA BA LAGS ZHES ZHUS SO,,

But then there are those who come and ask how this kind of description by those who assert some very heart of things is in any way different from that of the River Schools, who say that everything has a self-nature.  Because what you are describing is something like a precious jewel that has laid wrapped up in a filthy cloth for some time—wrapped in the cloth of the heaps and categories and doors of sense—and thus taken on some kind of stench.  And then at the same time you are saying that it is unchanging, and stable, and solid.


[2764]
DE’I LAN DU DE LTAR BSTAN PA DE SGRA JI BZHIN PA MIN PAS MU STEGS KYI BDAG DANG MI ‘DRA ZHES ‘CHAD PA NA, GANG LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS PA’I DGONGS GZHI NI STONG NYID DANG MTSAN MED DANG SMON MED NI CHOS KYI BDAG MED PA’O,,

In response we can say that teaching things as being like this was not something that was meant literally, and is therefore not at all the same as the self posited by the River Schools.  That is, what this description was meant to refer to—what was really meant—was the lack of any self-nature to things, in the form of emptiness; a lack of signs; and something beyond aspiration.


[2765]
DE LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS PA’I DGOS PA NI BYIS PA RNAMS BDAG MED PAS ‘JIGS PA SPANG BA DANG, MU STEGS BYED BDAG TU SMRA BA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS DANG, SNGON DE’I LTA BA LA GOMS PAR BYAS PA RNAMS DE KHO NA NYID LA RIM GYIS DRANG BA’I PHYIR DU

Why were these points then spoken of in terms of allusion?  First of all, the Buddha wished to prevent any trepidation that the infants might feel towards the concept that things are not themselves.  And he wanted to take those of the River Schools who were so attached to their profession of a self, and those who had, earlier, already accustomed themselves strongly to those ideas, and draw them out, gradually, to the idea of suchness.


[2766]
RTAG BRTAN THER ZUG GI SNYING PO YOD PAR BSTAN PAS ‘DI LA DA LTAR DANG MA ‘ONGS PA’I BYANG SEMS KYIS BDAG TU ZHEN PAR MI BYA BAR GSUNGS TE SGRAS ZIN LTAR GZUNG NA MU STEGS KYI BDAG LA ZHEN PA DANG ‘DRA BAS SGRA JI BZHIN PAR ZHEN PAR MI BYA BA’I DON NO,,

And so when we teach that there is a heart nature which is unchanging, stable, and solid, what we are really saying is that present and future bodhisattvas are not to feel any attachment to any self-nature here.  If we do take the description of the heart as being something meant literally, then it would indeed end up similar to the attachment that the River Schools have towards some kind of self-nature.  And so the point is that we need to avoid doing this.


[2767]
SGRA JI BZHIN PA DNGOS LA GNOD BYED NI SGRAS ZIN BZHIN KHAS LEN NA MU STEGS KYI BDAG DANG KHYAD PAR MED PAR ‘GYUR BA’O,,

When we say that taking something as literal hurts what is actual, what we mean is that—if we take these kinds of statements as literal—then what we end up with is something no different than the self-nature that the River Schools hold to.


[2768]
‘DI DAG GI DON RGYAS PAR GZHAN DU BSHAD ZIN PAS ‘DIR MA SPROS SO,,

I have already gone into great detail on these points elsewhere; so I will not expand upon them further here.


[2769]
‘GREL [f. 198a] PAR YANG DE NYID LAS, BLO GROS CHEN PO STONG PA NYID DANG MI SKYE BA DANG MI GNYIS PA DANG RANG BZHIN MED PA’I MTSAN NYID SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYI MDO SDE’I NANG DU CHUD PA ‘DI ZHES BSTAN TO ZHES DRANGS PA’I

In the autocommentary at this point we see the following words quoted—

In the same source we see, “O you of great wisdom, these ideas of emptiness itself; and of nothing starting; and of that which is beyond all two; and a quality of having no nature at all, were taught by all the Buddhas, and inserted into all of their sutras.”


[2770]
‘OG TU, DE’I PHYIR DE LTAR NA RNAM PA DE LTA BU’I MDO SDE RNAM PAR SHES PAR SMRA BA RNAMS KYIS NGES PA’I DON NYID DU KHAS BLANGS PA THAMS CAD DRANG PA’I DON NYID DU YIN PAR LUNG ‘DIS MNGON PAR GSAL BAR BYAS NAS ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

And then just below that, we see it stated:

As such, we can then say that all such sutras that the Consciousness School assert to be something we should take literally are clearly shown, by this citation, to be exclusively statements that we should take as being figurative.


[2771]
RNAM PA DE LTA BU’I MDO SDE NI DRANGS MA THAG PA’I LANG GSHEGS KYI LUNG TSAN PA GNYIS MIN TE, DE GNYIS KA RNAM RIG PAS NGES DON DU KHAS MA BLANGS PA’I PHYIR DANG, SNGAR ‘GREL PAR DGONGS ‘GREL LA GSAL POR BSHAD PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Now the references from sutra referred to in these lines are not the two selections that we have just cited from the Journey to Langka, because neither of those would be accepted by the Mentalists as being intended literally; and the autocommentary has clearly referenced these, earlier, as referring to What I Really Meant.


[2772]
LUNG ‘DIS ZHES PA ‘GREL BSHAD LAS SA BCU PA’I MDO’I RTEN ‘BREL LA RTOG PA’I SKABS SU BYED PA PO BKAG PA LA ‘CHAD PA NI SHIN TU MI RIGS TE, BYED PA PO GZHAN BKAG PA NI SA BCU PA LAS SEMS TZAM MO ZHES GSUNGS PA’I TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI ROL MI ‘GOG PA’I SHES BYED DU GSUNGS KYI, PHYI ROL BKAG PA DRANG DON DU STON PA’I SHES BYED MIN NO,,

Some people have explained the words here, “by this citation,” as referring to the section in the sutra on The Ten Levels where it examines dependence, and denies any agent.  This idea though is mistaken in the extreme.  When it is denying any other agent, the word “only” in the mention of “mind only” in The Ten Levels is stated as evidence that we are not denying things on the outside; it is not something meant as evidence in demonstrating that the denial of things on the outside was intended to be taken as figurative.


[2773]
DES NA RTZA BAR DRANG DON NYID DU LUNG ‘DIS GSAL BAR BYED CES PA’I LUNG LA GSUM LAS PHYI ROL BKAG PA’I SEMS TZAM DRANG DON DU STON PA NI JI LTAR NAD PA ZHES PA BZHI’O,,

As such, let us look at the line in the root text where it mentions “even more citations which these quotations explain to be taken metaphorically.”  There are three examples of the “citations”; one which shows us that “mind only” as a denial of things on the outside was meant metaphorically is the four lines [in the Tibetan; seven in the English] above which include “those who are ill.”


[2774]
KUN GZHI DRANG DON DU STON PA NI RTAG BRTAN GYI SNYING PO DRANG DON DU STON PA’I LUNG NGO,,

A case where foundation consciousness is shown to be meant metaphorically is the citation above that talked about an unchanging and stable heart of things being meant metaphorically.


[2775]
RTAG BRTAN GYI SNYING PO YOD PAR BSTAN PA DRANG DON YIN PAS KUN GZHI DRANG DON DU JI LTAR ‘GRUB CE NA,

“How is it,” one may ask then, “that foundation consciousness is proven to be meant in a figurative way, just because that teaching about the existence of a heart to things which is unchanging and stable was intended figuratively?”


[2776]
RGYAN STUG PO [f. 198b] BKOD PA LAS,
