,’JIG RTEN GZHAN GTOGS YOD PA NYID DU
RTOGS PA’I DUS SU BDAG
,SHES BYA’I RANG BZHIN DAM PA’I DON NI 
LTA BAR RTOGS BYA STE,
,BDAG GI LTA BA’I RNAM PA’I RTEN MTSUNGS
LUS DANG LDAN NYID PHYIR,
,GANG GI TSE NA BDAG MED RTOGS PAR
KHAS LEN DE TSE BZHIN,
ZHES BRJOD PAR NUS PA YANG YIN NO,,

We are also able to make the following pronouncement:

When I am able
To realize that what
Is contained in the other world
Is certainly something which exists,

Then I realize
That ultimate object:
The nature of every existing thing.

I possess indeed that body
Which is a likeness of
The type of view I have reached;

For this reflects the point
In time when I accepted
That I had realized
That there is no self-nature. 


[2888]
DE BZHIN DU,
,’DI NA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA YOD CES
RTOGS PA’I DUS SU BDAG
,SHES BYA’I RANG BZHIN DAM PA’I DON NI
LTA BAR RTOGS BYA STE,
,GTAN TSIGS DANG DPE DAG NI DE GNYIS KHO NA’O,,

And the autocommentary continues with:

In the same way, we have here nothing less than the pair of a proof and representative example—

	At that point in time when
	I come to the realization
	That there truly does exist
	The state of knowing all things,

	Then I have realized
	The nature of all things;
	I have seen that ultimate object.
	

[2889]
DE BZHIN DU DNGOS PO THAMS CAD ZHES PA LA YANG SBYAR BAR BYA’O,,

We can also apply this to the expression “every object there is.”


[2890]
DE’I PHYIR TSUL ‘DIS NI,
,DE NYID DE LAS ‘BYUNG MIN GZHAN DAG
LAS LTA GA LA ZHIG
,GNYIS KA LAS KYANG MA YIN RGYU MED
PAR NI GA LA YOD,
CES GANG DAM BCAS BAR {%PAR} GYUR PA BZHI PO RAB TU BSGRUBS PA YIN NO, ZHES [f. 205b] GSUNGS PAS GZHAN LUGS BKAG PA YIN GYI RANG LUGS MA BSGRUBS SO ZHES SMRA BAR MI BYA’O,,

The autocommentary concludes here with—

And so we see it stated that (the four points) which we assert are perfectly established:

	That never came
	From that thing itself;

	And so how
	Could it ever have come
	From other things?

	Neither did it come
	From both;

	And how could it
	Ever have come
	Without a cause at all?

Thus we would have to ask you not to make the claim here that the position of the other side has been denied, but that our own position has not been substantiated.



Where the four take us

[2891]
GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to our third general topic from before: the point we arrive at, by denying that things could start in any of these four different ways.


[2892]
‘DIR SMRAS PA, DNGOS PO RNAMS BDAG DANG GZHAN DANG GNYIS KA DANG RGYU MED LAS MI SKYE NA, ‘O NA JI LTAR SKYE ZHE NA

And so here’s the question.  Suppose someone comes along and asks the following question—

If it’s the case that things arise neither from themselves, from something other than themselves, from both, or without any cause at all, then how is it that they do arise?


[2893]
BSHAD PA, GAL TE DNGOS PO RNAMS LA RANG BZHIN ‘GA’ ZHIG YOD NA NI, SKYE BA’I RNAM PAR RTOG PA GZHAN MI SRID PA’I PHYIR, THE TSOM MED PAR DE BDAG GAM GZHAN NAM GNYIS KA’AM RGYU MED PA ZHIG LAS SKYE BA’AM DMIGS PAR ‘GYUR BA ZHIG GO

And then here is the answer.  If entities had any kind of nature at all to them, then any other idea about how they could ever arise would be impossible—which means that beyond any shadow of a doubt they would have to arise or come to exist through themselves, or something other, or from both, or without any cause at all.


[2894]
,GANG DAG DBANG PHYUG LA SOGS PA DAG LAS DNGOS PO RNAMS SKYE BAR MNGON PAR ‘DOD PA DE DAG GI LTAR NA YANG, DBANG PHYUG LA SOGS PA DE DAG BDAG TU GYUR PA’AM, GZHAN DU GYUR PA’AM, GNYIS KAR GYUR PA ZHIG TU ‘GYUR BAS DBANG PHYUG LA SOGS PA RGYUR SMRA BA DAG KYANG BSHAD ZIN PA’I SKYON LAS MI ‘DA’ STE, DE’I PHYIR SKYED PAR BYED PA’I RGYU’I RNAM PAR RTOG PA GZHAN LNGA PA YOD PA MA YIN NO,,

And it doesn’t really matter how those who believe that things have arisen through some all-powerful being or the like say it happened; because their beliefs would be subject to the same old problems that we have spent all this time describing.  That is, the all-powerful being or whatever else it was would themselves have to represent the result itself, or something other than it, or both.  As such, there would be no fifth possibility one could imagine for the cause that inspired all these things to arise.


[2895]
DE’I PHYIR GZHAN MED PA’I PHYIR LA, RNAM PAR RTOG PA BZHIS SKYE BAR BTAGS PA BKAG PA’I PHYIR DNGOS PO RNAMS KYI RANG BZHIN SKYE BA MED DO ZHES BSTAN PA’I PHYIR,

As such, there really are no other options; and so to deny some kind of arising that a person might imagine happening through those four options mentioned, the following lines of the root text are meant to demonstrate that there is no arising to things that could occur through some nature of its own.


	[2896]
[VI.104]
Bhāvāḥ svabhāva rahitāḥ svaparobhayasmāj
janmāsti hetum anapekṣya ca naiva yasmād,
Mohas tu yena bahalo ghana vṛnda tulyo
lokasya tena viṣayāḥ khalu bhānti mithyā.

[VI.104a]
,GANG GI PHYIR NA BDAG DANG GZHAN DANG
GNYIS KA LAS SKYE DANG,
,RGYU LA MA LTOS YOD PA MIN PAS
DNGOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN BRAL,

		For the reason
		That there can exist
		No arising of a thing
		Which could occur
		From itself,

		Or from something other,
		Or from both,
		Or without relying
		Upon any cause at all,

		Entities are devoid
		Of some nature
		Of their own.


[2897]
RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA BDAG DANG GZHAN DANG GNYIS KA LAS SKYE BA DANG, RGYU LAM {%LA MA} LTOS PAR SKYE BA YOD PA MIN PAS DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG BRAL LO, ZHES SMOS SO,,

For the reason that there can exist no arising of a thing which could occur from itself, or from something other than itself, or from both, or without relying upon any cause at all, we can say that entities are devoid of existing through some nature of their own.


[2898]
‘DIS NI MTHA’ BZHI’I SKYE BA THAL ‘GYUR GYIS BKAG KYANG, MTHAR RTAGS GANG LA BRTEN NAS RJES DPAG SKYE TSUL STON TE, DE YANG MTHA’ BZHI LAS SKYE BA MED PA NI GTAN TSIGS SO,,

What we have just done here is to deny that things could arise through any of four different extreme possibilities; but in the end we will need to show a logical reasoning which is something that we can rely upon to inspire a deductive form of accurate perception for this point.  And that then is the reasoning which demonstrates that things cannot arise through any one of four extreme possibilities.


[2899]
DNGOS PO RNAMS ZHES PA NI CHOS CAN NO, ,RANG BZHIN GYIS [f. 206a] GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA NI DAM BCA’O,,

The subject under consideration here is provided by the phrase, “all entities.”  And the assertion is provided by saying “they are devoid of existing through any nature of their own.”



Refuting debate
about the denial

[2900]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DNGOS KYI DON DANG, DE’I DON BSDUS TE BSTAN PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us to our second point from before: refuting debate about this denial.  We proceed in two sections: the actual point, and a summary presentation.  Here is the first.


[2901]
GAL TE DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PA ZHIG YIN NA, ‘O NA MA SKYES PA SNGON PO LA SOGS PA RNAMS JI LTAR GZUNG ZHE NA,

One may begin with the following question:

Suppose it is the case that there is no such thing as objects arising through any nature of their own.  If then things like blue have never arisen, how is it that we can perceive them?


[2902]
SNGON PO LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI RANG BZHIN JI LTAR YANG MA RIG PAS BSLAD PA ‘GA’ ZHIG GI SNANG BA’I YUL NYID DU ‘GYUR BA MIN PAS, DE LTAR GYI MIG LA SOGS PA’I SHES PAS, SNGO SOGS KYI RANG BZHIN NI BZUNG BA MA YIN NO,,

It is not the case that blue and the rest—regardless of what their nature may be—could ever act as that particular object which makes its appearance to some number of states of mind infected by ignorance.  As such, the nature of blue and the like is not something which can be perceived by the awareness of an eye or the like such as these.


[2903]
‘O NA GANG ZHIG YANG DANG YANG DU YUL GYI NGO BO NYID DU MDUN DU SNANG BAR MTHONG BA DE, CI ZHIG TU ‘GYUR BAR ‘OS SHE NA,

Which would lead one then to the following question:

Well then, but it does happen that there is something which makes its appearance before us, over and over, as the very essence of an object of perception; and we observe it.  How then would that ever be something that could happen?


[2904]
‘DI NI PHYIN CI LOG GI DBANG GIS SNANG BAS NA RANG BZHIN MA YIN TE, MA RIG PAS BSLAD PA’I DBANG KHO NAS BDAG NYID DER DMIGS PA’I PHYIR RO, ZHES BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

This is something that appears only through the power of some mistaken perception; it is not though the nature of a thing.  It is only something that we perceive as some kind of entity by force of our mind’s being infected by misunderstanding.  In order to convey this point, the root text says the following—


	[2905]
[VI.104b]
,GANG GIS SPRIN TSOGS DANG MTSUNGS GTI MUG
STUG PO ‘JIG RTEN LA,
,YOD PA DES NA YUL RNAMS LOG PA
DAG TU SNANG BAR ‘GYUR,

		The fact is that
		The everyday world
		Exists in a dense
		Lack of understanding

		Which is just the same
		As a huge gathering
		Of rain clouds.

		And for that reason, they have
		A mistaken impression
		Of the objects around them;

		This is how things make
		Their appearance to them.


[2906]
GANG GIS TE GANG GI PHYIR CHAR SPRIN NAG PO’I TSOGS DANG MTSUNGS PA’I GTI MUG STUG PO STE ‘THUG PO SNGON PO LA SOGS PA’I RANG BZHIN MTHONG BA G-YOGS NAS GNAS PA ‘JIG RTEN SEMS CAN LA YOD PA

The fact is—the point is—that beings of the everyday world exist in a state where they are smothered by seeing a nature in things like blue and the rest: they are surrounded by a dense, a very thick, lack of understanding which is just the same as a huge gathering of dark rain clouds.


[2907]
DES NA, BYIS PA RNAMS LA SNGON PO LA SOGS PA’I RANG BZHIN MTHONG BA YOD PA MIN TE, YUL RNAMS LA RANG GI NGO BO PHYIN CI LOG PA DAG TU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA’I GNAS SU GYUR PA ‘DI NI, BYIS PA ‘DI BDEN PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS LA SNANG BAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And for that reason, infants do not experience any sight towards the nature of things like blue and the rest; they live in a state where they have a craving for—they have a completely mistaken impression of—the real nature of the objects around them.  This then is how things make their appearance to these infants, who crave some true existence to things.


[2908]
GAL TE GTI MUG GIS BKAB PA’I PHYIR DE KHO NA NYID MI MTHONG DU CHUG KYANG, PHYIN CI LOG TU MTHONG BA CI LAM {%LA MA} YIN ZHE NA,

One may next ask the following question:

Suppose ones eyes are blocked by dark ignorance; even if, then, we were induced to try to see suchness, wouldn’t we necessarily see it in a mistaken way?


[2909]
RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA MIN BZHIN DU DER SNANG BA NI, GTI MUG GI [f. 206b] DBANG GIS YIN NO ZHES PHYI’I DPE’I SGO NAS BSTAN PA’I PHYIR,

The answer is that what comes next in the root text is meant to present a follow-up metaphor to indicate how the fact that things appear to exist through some essential nature of their own—even though they have no such nature—is due to dark ignorance.


	[2910]
[VI.105]
Kaścid yathaiva vitathaṃ timira prabhāvāt
keśa dvicandra śikhicandraka makṣikādi,
Gṛhṇāti tadvad abudhaḥ khalu moha doṣād
buddhyā vicitram avagacchati saṃskṛtaṃ hi.

,JI LTAR RAB RIB MTHU YIS ‘GA’ ZHIG
SKRA SHAD ZLA GNYIS DANG,
,RMA BYA’I MDONGS DANG SBRANG MA LA SOGS
LOG PAR ‘DZIN BYED PA,
,DE BZHIN DU NI GTI [209b] MUG SKYON GYI
DBANG GIS MI MKHAS PAS,
,’DUS BYAS LTA ZHIG SNA TSOGS BLO GROS
KYIS NI RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR,

It’s possible
For some people,
By force of a cataract,

To be made to hold,
Mistakenly,

A strand of hair,
One moon as two,
The pattern
Of a peacock’s feathers,

A random fly, or
Something of the like [f. 209b].

The same sort of thing
Happens with those
Who are not wise,

Due to the problem
Of their dark ignorance.

They perceive
Various objects
Like produced things
With their intellect.


[2911]
JI LTAR DBANG PO RAB RIB KYIS BSLAD PA’I MTHU YIS RAB RIB CAN ‘GA’ ZHIG GIS SKRA SHAD DANG ZLA BA GNYIS DANG RMA BYA’I MDONGS DANG SBRANG MA LA SOGS PA LOG PAR TE MED KYANG YOD PA LTAR ‘DZIN PA STE MTHONG BAR BYED PA

It’s possible for ones sense powers to be skewed by force of the effects of a cataract; so that some people with cataracts may mistakenly see a strand of hair that’s not actually there; or one moon that appears as two; or a spot of color like the pattern on a peacock’s feathers; a random fly; or something of the like.  When we say “mistakenly” here, what we mean is that—even though none of these things is actually there—our condition makes us hold to or see them as existing.


[2912]
DE BZHIN DU, GTI MUG GI SKYON GYI DBANG GIS MI MKHAS PA SO SKYES SNGON PO SOGS KYI ‘DUS BYAS LTA ZHIG SNA TSOGS PA BLO GROS KYIS TE DE DAG GI SHES PAS RTOGS PAR TE MTHONG BAR ‘GYUR RO,,

The same sort of thing happens with those who are not wise—that is, with common beings—due to the problem of their dark ignorance.  That is, they perceive—they see—various objects like produced things (blue and such) with their intellect; with their particular mental state.


[2913]
‘DI NI RTEN ‘BREL GYI MDO LAS, MA RIG PA’I RKYEN GYIS ‘DU BYED RNAMS ZHES BYA BA DANG,

This point is expressed in the Sutra on Interdependence, where it mentions “examples of fresh karma, due to the factor of misunderstanding.”


[2914]
DE BZHIN DU MA RIG PA DANG RJES SU ‘BREL BA’I GANG ZAG ‘DI NI, BSOD NAMS MNGON PAR ‘DU BYA BA DANG, BSOD NAMS MA YIN PA MNGON PAR ‘DU BYA BA DANG, MI G-YO BA MNGON PAR ‘DU BYA BA YANG MNGON PAR ‘DU BYED DO, ZHES BYA BA DANG,

We also read:

And in the same way, we see statements that an individual who is linked with misunderstanding will bring together an expression of merit; and they will bring together an expression of non-merit; and they will bring together an expression of unshifting karma.


[2915]
DE BZHIN DU MA RIG PA ‘GAGS PAS ‘DU BYED ‘GAG CES BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS GSUNGS PA YIN NO,,

In the same way, the Conqueror has stated that “When we put a stop to misunderstanding, we put a stop to fresh karma.”


	[2916]
[VI.106]
Mohaṃ pratītya yadi karma vinā na mohād
bhūtaṃ tad ityabudha eva pareti nūnam,
Sad buddhi bhāskara vihīna ghanāndhakāro
vidvāṃs tu śūnyam avagacchati mucyate ca.

,GAL TE GTI MUG BRTEN NAS LAS ‘BYUNG
GTI MUG MED PAR DE,
,MI ‘BYUNG ZHES BYAR MI MKHAS KHO NAS
RTOGS PAR GOR MA CHAG,
,BLO BZANG NYI MAS MUN PA STUG PO
RNAM PAR BSAL BA YI,
,MKHAS PA DAG NI STONG NYID KHONG DU
CHUD CING GROL BAR ‘GYUR,

		This description
		Is without doubt
		A reference to the fact

		That it is only those
		Who are not wise
		Who understand all this

		As saying that karma
		Occurs dependent upon
		Dark ignorance;

		And without
		This dark ignorance, then
		That would not occur.

		The wise grasp
		That these are
		Perfectly empty,

		Using the bright sun
		Of their fine minds
		To dispel—completely—
		That thick fog;
		And they are liberated.


[2917]
DE’I PHYIR TSUL ‘DIS GAL TE GTI MUG MA RIG PA LA BRTEN NAS ‘DU BYED KYI LAS ‘BYUNG LA, GTI MUG MED PAR LAS DE MI ‘BYUNG ZHES BYA BAR GSUNGS PA NI, MI MKHAS PA KHO NAS RTOGS PAR TE DE’I DBANG DU BYAS BAR GOR MA CHAG GO

As such, this description is without a doubt a reference to the fact that it is only those who are not wise who understand all this as saying that karma of the fresh type occurs dependent upon dark ignorance, or misunderstanding; and that without this dark ignorance, then that karma would not occur.


[2918]
,MKHAS PA DAG NI MA RIG PA’I RKYEN GYIS ‘DU BYED DO ZHES GSUNGS PA MTHONG BA NA, ‘DU BYED RNAMS RANG BZHIN MED PA’I STONG NYID KHONG DU CHUD PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU

The wise, on the other hand, gain a different understanding when they see these statements that “fresh karma comes about through the factor of misunderstanding.”  That is, they grasp them as saying, and only saying, that these examples of fresh karma are perfectly empty of any nature of their own.


[2919]
MA ZAD KYI, RTEN ‘BYUNG GI DE NYID RTOGS PA’I BLO BZANG PO’I NYI MAS, MUN PA STUG PO DANG ‘DRA BA’I MA RIG PA RNAM PAR BSAL BA STE SPONG ZHING,

Not only that, but they use the bright sun of their fine minds to delve the suchness of interdependence itself, and thus dispel—completely—that misunderstanding which is so similar to a thick fog.  Which is to say, they eliminate this darkness within themselves.


[2920]
LAS ‘DU [f. 207a] BYED DAG KYANG NYE BAR MI LEN TE, LAS DE NYE BAR LEN PA’I RGYU MA RIG PA SPANGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

This also means then that they never take on any fresh karma; for they have abandoned the misunderstanding that would allow them to take this on.


[2921]
DE’I PHYIR ‘KHOR BA LAS NGES PAR GROL BAR ‘GYUR TE, SDUD PA LAS,
,BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ GANG ZHIG RTEN CING
‘BREL ‘BYUNG LA,
,SKYE MED ZAD PA MED PAR SHES RAB
‘DIS SHES TE,
,NYI MA SPRIN MED ‘OD ZER ‘PHRO BAS
MUN BSAL LTAR,
,MA RIG THIBS PO BCOM NAS RANG ‘BYUNG
THOB PAR ‘GYUR,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

And because of this, they are quite certainly liberated from the cycle of pain.  As the Brief Presentation of the Perfection of Wisdom puts it,

Think of a bodhisattva
	Who uses their wisdom

	To grasp how things
	That occur in interdependence

	Never grow, and
	Never come to an end.

	They are like the sun
	Freed from clouds,
	Whose rays of light
	Banish the darkness;

	They destroy the overcast
	Of misunderstanding,
	And achieve the state
	Of the self-made ones.


	[2922]
[VI.107]
Na tattvataś cet khalu santi bhāvās
teṣām asattvaṃ vyavahārato’pi,
Syād eva vandhyātana yasya yadvat
svabhāvataḥ sattvam ato’sti teṣām.

,GAL TE DNGOS RNAMS DE NYID DU MED NA,
,THA SNYAD DU YANG MO GSHAM BU JI BZHIN,
,DE DAG MED PA NYID ‘GYUR DE YI PHYIR,
,DE DAG RANG BZHIN GYIS NI YOD PA NYID,

		If it’s the case
	That all these things
	Have nothing
	In & of themselves,

	Then they are like
	The child of
	A barren woman,
	
	And the same
	In a nominal sense:
	They really do
	Possess none.

	And then
	For that reason,
	They could exist
	Only by nature.


[2923]
GAL TE DE LTAR GZUGS SOGS KYI DNGOS PO RNAMS DE NYID DU STE DON DAM PAR RANG BZHIN ‘GA’ YANG MED NA, MO GSHAM GYI BU JI LTA BA BZHIN DU, 

Now suppose the following thought occurs to someone—

And so if it’s the case that all these things such as physical form and the like have no nature of their own at all—at least in & of themselves, or ultimately speaking—then in a sense they are like the child of a barren woman.


[2924]
THA SNYAD DU YANG SNGO SOGS DE DAG GI RANG BZHIN TE NGO BO MED PA NYID DU ‘GYUR NA, GZUGS SOGS KYI NGO BO NI KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA YANG YIN PA DE YI PHYIR, DE DAG GI YOD PA NI RANG BZHIN GYIS TE DON DAM PAR YOD PA NYID DE KHO NA’O SNYAM NA,

But if it’s the same in a nominal sense—which is to say, if these things like blue and the rest really do possess no nature or essence—then the essential nature of form and the rest must be that they exist deceptively.  And then for that reason, it would seem to me that all the same they could exist only in some kind of real way—that their existence would be something that existed by nature.


	[2925]
[VI.108]
Keśādayas te na hi nāma jātā
ye taimirāder viṣayaṃ prayānti,
Ta eva tāvat khalu codanīyāḥ
paścād avidyātimirānujātāḥ.

,GANG DAG RAB RIB CAN SOGS YUL ‘GYUR BA,
,SKRA SHAD LA SOGS DE DAG MA SKYES PAS,
,RE ZHIG DE DAG NYID LA BRTZAD BYA STE,
,PHYI NAS MA RIG RAB RIB RJES ‘BREL LA’O,

	Strands of hair
	Or the like act
	As objects

	For a person
	Who possesses
	Cataracts or such;

	And these
	Have never started.

	So let’s assume first
	That we seek out
	The way that
	Things really are.

	After that,
	There’s the connection
	To the cataracts
	Of misunderstanding.


[2926]
‘DI LA BRJOD PAR BYA STE, GANG DAG RAB RIB CAN LA SOGS PA’I BLO’I YUL DU ‘GYUR BA’I SKRA SHAD LA SOGS PA DE DAG MA SKYES PAS NA, MA SKYES PAR MO GSHAM GYI BU DANG MTSUNGS PA LA,

To this thought we reply as follows.  The mind of a person who possesses cataracts or such sees strands of hair or the like that act as its objects.  And if these objects have never started, then in their not starting they are totally equivalent to the child of a barren woman.


[2927]
CI’I PHYIR KHYED CAG GIS YOD PA MIN PA’I YUL SKRA SHAD SOGS MTHONG LA, MO GSHAM GYI BU MI MTHONG BA CI YIN ZHES,

And then we would have to ask you a question: Why is it that you would see things like that strand of hair that didn’t exist; but not see this child of a barren woman?


[2928]
RE ZHIG SNGON LA RAB RIB LA SOGS PAS MIG NYAMS PA DE DAG NYID DE KHO NA LA BRTZAD PAR BYA STE, DE’I PHYI NAS TE RJES SU NI CI’I PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PAR MTSUNGS PA LA,

So let’s assume first that—prior to anything—the eye as been degraded because of a cataract or something of the like.  And then we use these same eyes to seek out the way things really are.  Why then, after that—subsequent to that—wouldn’t things be just the same, in the sense of not arising through some nature of their own?


[2929]
KHYOD GZUGS SOGS MTHONG LA MO GSHAM GYI BU MI MTHONG BA CI YIN ZHES, MA RIG PA’I RAB RIB RJES SU ‘BREL BA STE DES BLO MIG BSGRIBS PA RNAMS LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR BYA’O,,

And then we would ask you, why is it that you could see forms and the like, but not see the child of a barren woman?  That is, now we are arguing about—now we are examining—the connection to the cataracts of misunderstanding: those things that obscure the eyes of the mind.


[2930]
KHO BO [f. 207b] CAG LA NI ‘DI BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR BYA BA MA YIN TE, ‘DI LTAR KHO BO CAG LA NI RNAL ‘BYOR PA RNAMS KYIS DNGOS PO DAG ‘DI LTAR GZIGS SHING, GZHAN GANG DAG RNAL ‘BYOR BA’I YE SHES THOB PAR ‘DOD PA DE DAG GIS KYANG, CHOS KYI RANG BZHIN DE SKAD BSHAD PA LA LHAG PAR MOS PAR BYA’O ZHES

As for our part, it’s not as if we are arguing about or examining these things.  As far as we’re concerned, those deep practitioners are checking into entities in this way; and other people who hope to attain the wisdom of these deep ones (as the scriptures tell us) need to follow a simple aspiration to reach this nature of things as it has been described to us.


[2931]
LUNG JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RNAL ‘BYOR PA’I YE SHES KYIS THUGS SU CHUD PA’I SGO NAS, DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN MED PAR ‘CHAD PAR ZHUGS PA YIN GYI, RANG GI SHES PA LA LTOS NAS NI MA YIN TE, KHO BO CAG NI MA RIG PA’I RAB RIB KYIS BLO’I MIG BSGRIBS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Which is to say, we need to follow these scriptures and try to grasp the wisdom of these deep practitioners; thus then we engage in the explanations of how things lack any nature of their own.  It is not though the case that we could rely on our own understanding, for we remain people who find the eyes of their mind obstructed by the cataracts of misunderstanding.


[2932]
JI SKAD DU MDO LAS,
,PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN DBEN ZHING STONG PA NYID,
,BYANG CHUB RANG BZHIN STONG ZHING DBEN PA NYID,
,GANG SPYOD DE YANG RANG BZHIN STONG PA STE,
,YE SHES LDAN PAS SHES KYI BYIS PAS MIN,

This entire situation is as we see it described in the sutras:

	The parts to the person
	Are devoid of any nature,
	And simple emptiness.

	Enlightenment itself
	Is empty of any nature,
	And thus that absent void.

	Whatever we try to do
	Is as well empty
	Of any nature of its own.

	These are things
	That are understood
	By those who possess wisdom;
	But not by infants.	


	[2933]
,YE SHES RANG BZHIN STONG PAR RIG ‘GYUR TE,
,SHES BYA’I RANG BZHIN STONG PAR RIG GYUR NAS,
,SHES PA PO DANG ‘DRA BAR RTOGS GYUR NA,
,BYANG CHUB LAM LA DE DAG SPYOD CES BYA,
ZHES GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

	Come to see
	That wisdom itself
	Is empty of any nature;

	See that is empty
	Of any nature
	Of being an existent thing.

	When you realize
That these things
Are similar to the knower,

Then we can say
You are one of those
Who is practicing the path
To enlightenment.


[2934]
DE’I PHYIR ‘DI NI RNAL ‘BYOR PA RNAMS LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PA MA YIN TE, DE DAG GIS NI KUN RDZOB TU YANG CHOS ‘GA’ ZHIG LA NGO BOS GRUB PA’I RANG BZHIN ‘GA’ YANG MA GZIGS LA, DON DAM PAR YANG CI YANG MA GZIGS SO,,

As such, it is not the case that all this is meant to be conjecture or argument with those deep practitioners.  They for their part see no kind of nature in any kind of thing at all, where these could exist through some essential nature of their own, even deceptively.  Neither do they see how these could have any such nature in an ultimate way.


	[2935]
[VI.109]
Svapnaṃ sagandharva puraṃ marīcyāṃ
kam indrajālaṃ pratibimbakādi,
Paśyasyajātān yadi tat kathaṃ te
tulye’py asattvena tu tan na yuktam.

,GAL TE RMI LAM DRI ZA’I GRONG KHYER BCAS,
,SMIG RGYU’I CHU DANG MIG ‘PHRUL GZUGS BRNYAN SOGS,
,SKYE MED MTHONG NA YOD NYID MIN MTSUNGS KYANG,
,KHYOD LA JI LTAR DER ‘GYUR DE MI RIGS,

		Now suppose there is
		A dream, along
With a city of the
Craving spirits.

Or water flowing
From a mirage—
An illusionist at work—
Or a reflection,

Or something
Of the like:
Things that
Never started.

When we come to see,
We can say that
They are equivalent

In not being
Existing entities.

And you should be
Asking, how are
All these things?

It doesn’t make sense!


[2936]
RAB RIB CAN LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PA LTA BAR ZHOG CIG RE ZHIG ‘DI NI KHYOD NYID LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR BYA BA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA,

And then the root text goes on to say, “Not only are we not making conjectures or examinations with those who are afflicted with the cataracts; right now the one that we’re doing the conjecturing and the examining towards is you yourself.”  Here is how that is expressed.


[2937]
GAL TE RMI LAM GYI KHANG KHYIM DANG DRI ZA’I GRONG KHYER DANG BCAS PA MTHONG BA DANG, MIG ‘PHRUL MKHAN GYIS SPRUL PA’I SKYES PA DANG BUD MED SOGS DANG, [f. 208a] SMIG RGYU LA CHU DANG, GZUGS BRNYAN LA BYAD BZHIN DU MTHONG BA DANG,

Now suppose that we see a dream house; along with a city of the craving spirits.  Or we see something like a man or woman who has been emanated by an illusionist.  We see water flowing from a mirage; or we see the reflection of a thing in the mirror as being the thing standing in front of the mirror.


[2938]
SOGS KYIS BRAG CHA DANG SPRUL PA SOGS LA SKYE MED DE YOD PA MIN PA MTHONG BA NA YOD PA NYID MIN PAR MTSUNGS KYANG,

And then the words “or something of the like” here refer to things like the echo of a sound, or else an emanation created by someone—things that never started.  When we come to see that these are not things that have any existence at all, we can say that they are equivalent in not being existing entities.


[2939]
KHYOD LA JI LTAR DE DAG MTHONG BA DER ‘GYUR LA, MO GSHAM GYI BU MTHONG BA DER MI ‘GYUR BA DE MI RIGS SO ZHES JE {%DE? our scan says JE} BDAG NYID LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR GYIS LA, PHYIS KHO BO LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR BYA’O,,

And so first of all you should be conjecturing and examining you yourself, asking “How is it that you can see all these things, and not see the child of a barren woman?  It doesn’t make sense!”  When you’re done with that, then later you can conjecture and examine what we think!


	[2940]
[VI.110]
Ete na tattvena yathaiva jātā
na vāpi vandhyāsutavan na yānti,
Lokasya yad darśana gocaratvaṃ
tasmād anaikāntikam etad uktam.

,DE NYID DU ‘DI JI LTAR SKYE MED KYANG,
,MO GSHAM BU LTAR GANG PHYIR ‘JIG RTEN GYI,
,MTHONG BA’I YUL DU MI ‘GYUR MA YIN PA,
,DE YI PHYIR NA SMRA ‘DI MA NGES PA’O,

		Speaking purely,
		Things never start
		In any way at all.

		And yet this is not
		Something that can be
		An object that is seen

		In the eyes of the
		Everyday world,

		In the way that
		They would regard
		The child of
		A barren woman.

		And since it is not,
		This statement
		Is itself inconclusive.


[2941]
DE’I PHYIR DE KHO NA NYID DU GZUGS SOGS ‘DI JI LTAR YANG SKYE BA MED KYANG, GANG GI PHYIR MO GSHAM GYI BU LTAR ‘JIG RTEN GYI MTHONG BA’I YUL DU MI ‘GYUR BA MA YIN PA DE YI PHYIR, DON DAM DU MED NA THA SNYAD DU YANG MO GSHAM GYI BU BZHIN MI MTHONG BAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES SMRA BA ‘DI NI GTAN TSIGS MA NGES PA STE, ‘KHRUL PA CAN YIN NO,,

Thus we can say that form and the like—when we are speaking about their pure essence—are things that never start in any way at all.  And yet this is not something that can be an object that is seen in the eyes of the everyday world, in the way that they would regard the child of a barren woman.  And since it is not, then this statement where you say that “If something didn’t exist in an ultimate way, then even nominally it should act like the child of a barren woman, and not be something we could see,” is itself reasoning which is inconclusive—which is to say, faulty.


[2942]
BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS KYANG,
,’GRO BA DAG NI RMI ‘DRAR BSHAD,
,DE NYID DU NI RNAM MA BZHAG
,RMI LAM GANG LA DNGOS PO MED,
,LOG PA’I BLO LDAN MNGON PAR ZHEN,

The Conqueror himself has put it this way:

	What I have explained
	Is that all these living beings
	Are something like a dream;

	They cannot be described
	As existing in actual fact.

	Those with a mistaken
	State of mind
	Hold strongly to what

	Is a thing in a dream
	That never existed.


	[2943]
,DRI ZA’I GRONG KHYER JI LTAR SNANG GYUR KYANG,
,GRONG KHYER PHYOGS BCUR YOD MIN GZHAN NA’ANG MED,
,GRONG KHYER MING TZAM ZHIG GIS RAB TU BZHAG
,DE BZHIN BDE BAR GSHEGS PAS ‘GRO ‘DI GZIGS,

The city of the ghosts
Can appear all it wants;

But still it is not
A city that could exist
In any of the ten
Directions of space,
Nor anywhere else.

It exists as a city
Only in name;

And this is how
Those who have
Gone to Bliss

See every living being.


	[2944]
,CHU YI ‘DU SHES CAN GYIS NI,
,MTHONG YANG SMIG RGYU LA CHU MED,
,DE BZHIN YONGS SU RTOG PAS DKRUGS,
,SDUG PA MIN PAR SDUG PAR RTOG

Those who think
They see some water
May indeed
Believe they see it;

But that doesn’t mean
The mirage will be filled
With water.

Those full of delusion
Are confused in just
The very same way,

Seeing what is anything
But beautiful
As being beautiful indeed.


	[2945]
,ME LONG SHIN TU YONGS DAG LA,
,JI LTAR RANG BZHIN MED PA YI,
,GZUGS BRNYAN SNANG BA DE BZHIN DU,
,LJON PA CHOS RNAMS SHES PAR GYIS,

Everything is just the way
That a reflection that has
No real nature

Makes its appearance
In mirror that is perfectly clean;

Now you can look
At things like trees this way.


[2946]
ZHES GSUNGS PA’I LUNG LAS NA GZUGS SOGS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES [f. 208b] PA YIN BZHIN DU, ‘JIG RTEN GYI ‘DZIN PA’I YUL NYID DU ‘GYUR LA, MO GSHAM GYI BU NI MA YIN PAS ‘DI NI KHYOD RANG NYID LAS MA NGES PA’O,,

According to this original citation from scripture, form and the rest arise, but not through any nature of their own.  And then in the same way they serve as the very objects that are held to by the world.  The child of a barren woman though is not like this; therefore this would be uncertain, even according to you.


[2947]
KHO BO CAG LA NI ‘DI BRTZAD DU MED PA NYID DE, ‘DI LTAR KHO BO CAG GIS NI GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS KUN RDZOB TU RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BAR KHAS BLANGS NAS DON DAM PAR ‘GOG PA MA YIN NO,,

For us, this point is something that is—quite certainly—beyond any need to dig further.  That is, we accept that form and the rest arise through a deceptive nature; and so we are not denying them in any ultimate way.



A summary of the refutation

[2948]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to a summary presentation of our refutation of debate about the denial that was made.


	[2949]
[VI.111]
Svenātmanā janma na tattvato’sti
vandhyā sutasyāpi na lokato’pi,
Tathā svabhāvena na lokato’mī
jātā na tattvena ca sarva bhāvāḥ.

,MO GSHAM BU LA RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS,
,SKYE BA DE NYID DU MED ‘JIG RTEN DU’ANG,
,YOD MIN DE BZHIN DNGOS ‘DI KUN NGO BO,
,NYID KYIS ‘JIG RTEN DE NYID DU MA SKYES,

		The child
		Of a barren woman
		Is not something

		Which arises
		All on its own accord;

		It has no existence
		In & of itself.

		Neither is it
Something which exists,
In the everyday world.

Just so,
All these entities
Have never arisen through
		Some essential nature;

		For the world, or from
		The point of view
		Of suchness.
 

[2950]
KHYOD KYI LUGS KYIS GZUGS SOGS RNAMS KUN RDZOB TU RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BAR DMIGS NAS, DON DAM DU ‘GOG PA MIN PA DE CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA,

One may begin here with the following question—

According to your system, form and the like are perceived as arising, deceptively speaking, through a nature of their own; and this is not to be denied, in an ultimate sense.  Why is that?


[2951]
JI LTAR MO GSHAM GYI BU LA RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS SKYE BA DE KHO NA NYID DU MED CING ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU’ANG YOD PA MIN PA

Here is what has been stated.  Think first of how the child of a barren woman is not something which arises all on its own accord: how it has no existence in & of itself.  Neither is it something which exists, in the parlance of the everyday world.


[2952]
DE BZHIN DU, GZUGS SOGS KYI DNGOS PO ‘DI KUN ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DANG, DE KHO NA NYID GNYIS KAR RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS MA SKYES SO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS,

Just so is it the case that all these entities of form and the rest have never arisen through some essential nature of their own—whether we’re talking about this parlance of the world, or from the point of view of suchness.


[2953]
DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS SKYE BAR ‘DZIN PA’I ‘KHRUL NGOR YOD PA LA DBU MA PAS, KUN RDZOB TU YOD PAR GTAN MI ‘DOD LA, NGO BO NYID KYIS SKYE BA ZHES DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR GSAL BAR YANG SBYAR BA RNAMS DRAN PAR BYA’O,,

As such, you should recall how those of the Middle Way talk about the way in which things exist to the perceptions of one who is mistaken; who holds that they could grow through some essential nature of their own.  That is, they would never accept—in the slightest—that these existed in a deceptive manner.  And remember too the way in which they add a qualification to the object they deny: “It does not grow through any essential nature of its own.”


	[2954]
[VI.112]
Dharmān jagādādita eva śāntān
ataḥ prakṛtyā parinirvṛtāṃś ca,
Śāstā viyuktān udayena sarvān
yatas tato nāsti sad eva janma.

,DE PHYIR ‘DI LTAR STON PAS CHOS RNAMS KUN,
,GDOD NAS ZHI ZHING SKYE BRAL RANG BZHIN GYIS,
,YONGS SU MYA NGAN ‘DAS PA GSUNGS GYUR PA,
,DE PHYIR RTAG TU SKYE BA YOD MA YIN,

		For this reason,
		The Teacher has stated
		That all the objects
		That exist consist

		Of peace from
		The very beginning;

		And are devoid
		Of arising;

		And that they have,
		By their very nature,
		Gone entirely to nirvana.

		As such,
		They have never
		Displayed any arising.


[2955]
GANG GI PHYIR DE LTA YIN PA DE’I PHYIR ‘DI LTAR STON PA BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS CHOS RNAMS KUN GDOD MA NAS ZHI ZHING RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA DANG BRAL BA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS YONGS SU MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA’O ZHES GSUNGS PAR GYUR PA DE’I PHYIR DUS RTAG TU RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA YOD PA MA YIN NO,,

For the reason that this is the way things are, the Teacher—the Conqueror—has stated that all the objects that exist consist of peace from the very beginning; and that they are devoid of arising through any nature of their own; and that they have—by their very nature—gone entirely to nirvana.  As such, they are things which have never, for all of time, displayed any arising through some nature of their own.


[2956]
GSUNGS TSUL NI, DKON MCHOG SPRIN LAS,
,CHOS KYI ‘KHOR LO BSKOR BA NA,
,GDOD NAS ZHI ZHING MA SKYES PA,
,RANG BZHIN MYA NGAN ‘DAS PA YI,
,CHOS RNAMS MGON PO [f. 209a] KHYOD KYIS BSTAN,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

And how was it that these things were stated?  We can point to the following words from the Cloud of Jewels:

	When you turned
	The wheel of the Dharma,
	O Protector,

	You taught us that
	All things had a nature
	Of nirvana—

	Peace from
The very beginning,
	And never born at all.


[2957]
CHOS RNAMS KYI DE KHO NA NYID NI YE SHES ZHI BA’I YUL YIN PA’I PHYIR ZHI BA’O, ,DE’I RGYU MTSAN NI RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Since the very nature of all existing entities is the object of peace in the form of wisdom, they are here being referred to as “peace.”  The reason for saying this is that they have never arisen through any nature of their own.


[2958]
DE’I RGYU MTSAN YANG GAL TE ‘GA’ ZHIG LA RANG BZHIN TE NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA YOD NA, DE SKYE BAR ‘GYUR NA RANG BZHIN DE YANG YOD PA MIN PAS CI ZHIG SKYE BAR ‘GYUR, DE’I PHYIR MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA STE RNAM PAR DAG PA’O,,

And this in itself has a reason.  Suppose that there did exist some number of entities that did exist through some nature of their own—through some essential quality.  If they were to grow then, then they could no longer have that nature; what then is it that grew?  As such, these things are described as “nirvana”; which is to say, as being completely pure.


[2959]
GDOD NAS ZHES PA NI CHOS DE DAG RNAL ‘BYOR PA’I YE SHES KYI SKABS KHO NAR MA SKYES PA NI MIN TE,

When it says here “from the very beginning,” the point is that it is not the case that these entities are something that exhibits no growing only with reference to the occasion of the wisdom of a deep practitioner.


[2960]
‘O NA CI ZHE NA, DE’I GONG ROL ‘JIG RTEN PA’I THA SNYAD KYI SKABS SU YANG CHOS DE DAG RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS MA SKYES PA’O ZHES PA ‘DI STON PAR BYED DE, GDOD KYI SGRA NI DANG PO’I SGRA’I RNAM GRANGS SO,,

And how does that work?  What this is meant to indicate is that even before that point—even on the occasion when we are speaking nominally—none of these entities has arisen in and of itself.  That is, the expression “the very beginning” is intended as a synonym for saying “the very start.”


	[2961]
[VI.113]
Ghaṭādayaḥ santi na tattvato’mī
loka prasiddhyā tu yathā bhavanti,
Bhāvā bhaviṣyanti tathaiva sarve
syān naiva vandhyā sutavat prasaṅgaḥ.

,BUM SOGS ‘DI DAG DE NYID DU MED CING,
,’JIG RTEN RAB TU GRAGS PAR YOD CI BZHIN,
,DE BZHIN DNGOS PO THAMS CAD ‘BYUNG [*’GYUR?] BAS NA,
,MO GSHAM BU DANG MTSUNGS PAR THAL MI ‘GYUR,

		Things like
		Pitchers and the like
		Are not such that
		
		They exist
		In their essence;

		They do though
Exist as they are
Spoken of in the
World at large.

All the entities
That exist
Follow this
Very same pattern;

It is not the case
That they would
Have to be

The equivalent
Of the child
Of a barren woman.


[2962]
RANG GI SDE PA RNAMS KYIS NI DON DAM DU MED NA, KUN RDZOB TU YANG MED DO ZHES PA’I BRGAL BA ‘DI BYA BA MA YIN TE, CI’I PHYIR ZHE NA,

One may continue with the following question:

Those of our own group say that it is a mistake to present the argument that “If something doesn’t exist ultimately, then neither can it exist deceptively.”  Why is that?


[2963]
GANG GI PHYIR DE DAG GIS KHAS BLANGS PA BUM SOGS ‘DI DAG DE NYID DU STE DON DAM PAR MED CING ‘JIG RTEN GYI RAB TU GRAGS PA STE THA SNYAD DU YOD PA

This is for the reason that what they accept goes as follows.  First of all, things like pitchers and the like are not such that they exist in their essence; which is to say, in an ultimate sense.  They do though exist as they are spoken of in the world at large; which is to say, they do exist in a nominal sense.


[2964]
JI BZHIN PA DE BZHIN DU, DNGOS PO THAMS CAD KYANG ‘GYUR BAS NA, DON DAM PAR MED NA MO GSHAM GYI BU DANG MTSUNGS PAR THAL BAR MI ‘GYUR RO,,

All the entities that exist also follow this very same pattern.  That is, it is not the case that if a thing has no existence in an ultimate sense, then it would have to be the equivalent of the child of a barren woman.


[2965]
‘DI NI MDZOD LAS,
,GANG LA BCOM DANG BLO YIS GZHAN,
,BSAL NA DE BLO MI ‘JUG PA,
,BUM CHU BZHIN DU KUN RDZOB TU,
,YOD DE DON DAM YOD GZHAN NO,
ZHES BSHAD PA LTAR TE,

The way this works is expressed in the Treasure House of Higher Knowledge as follows—

	Consider any object
	That—when you destroy it,
	Or break it down mentally
	Into its component parts—
	Your mind can no longer
	Engage in it:

	Something, for example,
	Like the water in a pitcher.

	This then is an example
	Of deceptive reality;
	Whereas the ultimate
	Would be something other.
	

[2966]
CHA SHAS SU BCOM PAS DE’I BLO MI ‘JUG PA’I KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA STE DPER NA BUM PA LTA BU’O,,

What this is saying is that any object which exists in a way where—if you broke it down into its component parts—the mind could no longer engage in it, is an example of deceptive reality.  And an example would be something like a clay pitcher.
	

[2967]
DE LA NI GYO MOR BCOM NA BUM PA’I BLO MI ‘JUG PA’O, ,[f. 209b] BLOS CHOS GZHAN BSAL NA DE’I BLO MI ‘JUG PA YANG KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA STE DPER NA CHU LTA BU’O,,

If you take a pitcher and smash it into shards of clay, then the conception of it as a pitcher can no longer engage.  And things that cannot be engaged in when you break them down mentally are also said to exist deceptively; an example would be water.


[2968]
DE LA NI BLOS GZUGS LA SOGS PA’I CHOS GZHAN BSAL NA CHU’I BLO MI ‘JUG GO

That is, when the mind breaks down the form and other components of the water, the conception of it as water can no longer engage.


[2969]
,GANG LA BCOM YANG DE’I BLO ‘JUG LA, BLOS CHOS GZHAN BSAL YANG DE’I BLO ‘JUG PA NI DON DAM PAR YOD PA YIN TE, DPER NA GZUGS LTA BU’O,,

And suppose that you were to break the object down, but the mind could still engage in it.  Any case where the mind breaks the thing down into component parts and can still engage in the object is what they consider to exist ultimately: an example would be form itself.


[2970]
DE LA NI RDUL PHRA RAB TU BCOM YANG RUNG, BLOS RO LA SOGS PA’I CHOS GZHAN BSAL YANG RUNG, GZUGS KYI RANG BZHIN BLO ‘JUG PA NYID DO,,

That is, you could break the thing down into smallest particles; or the mind could break the object down into other entities, such as taste or the like.  But still the mind would invariably engage in the thing as having the nature of form.


[2971]
TSOR BA SOGS LA YANG DE BZHIN DU BLTA BAR BYA’O, ZHES MDZOD ‘GREL DU ‘CHAD DO,,

And the commentary to the Treasure House says that “you should view feelings and the like as being the same.”


[2972]
SDE PA DE DAG GIS NI SPYIR DON DAM DU MED NA KUN RDZOB TU MED DO ZHES SMRA BA MI RIGS SO, ZHES GSUNG PA YIN GYI DE DAG GIS BDEN PA GNYIS SU YOD TSUL BYAS PA DANG, RANG GIS MDZAD PA GNYIS MTHUN PAR STON PA MIN TE, DE DAG GIS KUN RDZOB TU YOD PAR BZHAG PA LA DBU MA PAS BSHAD PA’I DON DAM DU YOD PAR ‘DZIN PA SHA STAG YIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

These groups would, in general, say things like “It would be incorrect to say that if something did not exist ultimately, it could not exist in a deceptive way.”  This is not though indicating that the way that they say there exists a division of realities into two, and the way that we ourselves set forth two, are compatible with each other.  And that’s because every single thing that they would establish as existing in a deceptive way is something that those of the Middle Way would consider to exist in an ultimate way.


[2973]
GAL TE BUM PA LA SOGS PAR GDAGS PA’I RTEN ‘BYUNG BA BZHI DANG, ‘BYUNG ‘GYUR BZHI LA SOGS PA RNAMS RDZAS GRUB TU YOD PA’I PHYIR, BUM PA LA SOGS PAR BTAGS PA NI RGYU ‘AM GZHI DANG BCAS PAR RIGS NA DBU MA PA LTAR NA CHOS THAMS CAD BTAGS PA TZAM KHO NA YIN GYI, BTAGS PA’I RTEN RDZAS SU GRUB PA CI YANG MED PA LA MO GSHAM GYI BU DANG ‘DRA BAR THAL BA LDOG PA MED DO SNYAM NA,

One might then have the following thought—

Let’s consider the four elements, and the four products of the elements, and so on which provide the basis for labeling something as a pitcher or the like.  These exist substantially, and so suppose that it is acceptable to say that when we label a pitcher or something similar, there is an accompanying cause or basis.  According to those of the Middle Way, every object in the universe exists only as something labeled, but there is never any basis for the labeling that could substantially.  As such there is no avoiding the necessary implication that everything would be like the child of a barren woman.


[2974]
DE YANG MI RIGS TE, BTAGS PA’I RTEN RDZAS SU GRUB PAR SGRUB PAR MI NUS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And yet this is incorrect, since there is no way of proving that the basis for the labeling exists in a substantial manner.


[2975]
DPER NA BTAGS PAR YOD PA BYAD BZHIN LA SOGS PA’I TSOGS PA LA BRTEN NAS [f. 210a] GZUGS BRNYAN BRTAGS PA TZAM DMIGS PA DANG, BTAGS PAR YOD PA KA BA SOGS LA BRTEN NAS KHYIM DU BTAGS PA DANG, DE BZHIN DU SHING GI RTEN CAN NAGS BTAGS PA DANG,

We can see, for example, things that exist through labeling: a reflection in a mirror is something that only exists through labeling, based upon the collection of parts involving the original image standing before the mirror, and so on.  And then there are other things that exist through labeling; the idea of a “house,” for example, is imputed on the basis of its supporting pillars and the like.


[2976]
JI LTAR RMI LAM NA MA SKYES PA’I RANG BZHIN CAN GYI SA BON LAS MA SKYES PA’I RANG BZHIN GYI MYU GU SKYE BAR DMIGS PA DE BZHIN DU, DNGOS PO BTAGS PAR YOD PA THAMS CAD KYI GDAGS GZHI YANG DNGOS PO BTAGS PAR YOD PA NYID DU RIGS SO,,

In a dream, we observe a sprout that has a nature of never arising arising from a seed that has a nature of never arising.  Just so, it is logical to say that the bases that we use to label all those entities which exist as creations of lables are themselves invariably entities which exist as creations of labels.



Dependence stops the mistake

[2977]
GSUM PA NI,

Which brings us to our third part from before: an explanation of how the concept that things start in dependence prevents mistaken ideas where we hold to extremes.


	[2978]
[VI.114]
Ahetutaś ceśvara kāraṇādeḥ
svasmāt parasmāt dvayataś ca yasmād,
Utpadyamānā na hi santi bhāvās
tasmāt pratītya prabhavaṃ prayānti.

,GANG PHYIR RGYU MED PA DANG DBANG PHYUG GI
,RGYU LA SOGS DANG BDAG GZHAN GNYIS KA LAS,
,DNGOS RNAMS SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA MA YIN PA,
,DE PHYIR BRTEN NAS RAB TU SKYE BAR ‘GYUR,

	It is indeed the case
	That these entities
	Do not arise without
	Any cause at all;

	Nor from the cause
	Of some supreme
Being, or the like.

And because
These do not arise
From themselves,

From something other,
Or from both,

Their arisal
Most definitely flows
From a dependence.


[2979]
GAL TE KHYOD KYIS BDAG DANG GZHAN DANG GNYIS KA DANG RGYU MED PA LAS SKYE BA BDEN GNYIS KYI PHYOGS GNYIS KAR YANG BKAG NA, MA RIG PA LA SOGS PA LAS ‘DU BYED RNAM PAR SHES PA LA SOGS PA DANG, SA BON LA SOGS PA LAS MYU GU LA SOGS PA KUN RDZOB TU SKYE BA DE JI LTAR NGES PAR BYA ZHE NA,

One may next come with this following question:

You have denied—from the point of view of both of the two realities—that things could arise from themselves; from something other than themselves; from both themselves and from something other; and without any cause at all.  If this is indeed the case, then how is it that we can confirm that things do arise in a deceptive sense—that fresh karma and consciousness and the rest can come from misunderstanding and the like; and sprouts & such from seeds and so on?


[2980]
DE LA BRJOD PAR BYA STE, GANG GI PHYIR NA SNGAR JI SKAD BSHAD PA’I TSUL GYIS, DNGOS PO RNAMS KYI SKYE BA RGYU MED PAR NGO BO NYID LAS ‘BYUNG BA DANG, DBANG PHYUG GI RGYU DANG

We’ll explain our answer here.  It is indeed the case—in the manner that we provided the previous explanation—that the arisal of entities is not something where things have somehow occurred in and of themselves, their birth occurring without any cause at all; nor have they grown from causes such as some supreme being, or the like.


[2981]
LA SOGS PAS DUS DANG, RDUL DANG RANG BZHIN DANG SKYES BU DANG SRED MED KYI BU LA SOGS PA RNAMS LAS KYANG SKYE BA MA YIN ZHING,

The phrase “or the like” here, by the way, covers things coming from the concept of time; or from particulate matter; or from some nature to things; or from some special person; or from the one they call “child beyond desire”; or any such thing.


[2982]
BDAG DANG GZHAN DANG GNYIS KA LAS SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA MIN PA DE’I PHYIR RGYU DANG RKYEN ‘DI LA BRTEN NAS ‘BRAS BU ‘DI RAB TU SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA ZHIG STE, MTHA’ BZHI’I SKYE BA SPANGS PA DE TZAM ZHIG LA ‘JIG RTEN GYI RGYU ‘BRAS KYI THA SNYAD MI BCAD PA’I DON DU RTEN NO,,

And simply because these results do not arise from themselves, from something other than themselves, or from both of these, their arisal most definitely flows from a dependence upon the specific causes and factors.  The point is that the very denial that things could arise through any one of the four extreme options itself relies upon the fact that we are not eliminating the expression, in the everyday world, of how cause & effect works.


[2983]
JI SKAD DU BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS DE LA CHOS KYI BRDA NI ‘DI YIN TE, ‘DI LTA STE ‘DI YOD NA ‘DI ‘BYUNG, ‘DI SKYES PAS ‘DI SKYE STE, GANG ‘DI MA RIG PA’I RKYEN GYIS ‘DU BYED [f. 210b] RNAMS ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA GSUNGS PA DANG,

The expressions that the Conqueror has given to this idea in the classical teachings are things like the following—

This is how it is.  If this is present, then this will occur.  If this has arisen, then this will arise.  What this is is where the factor of misunderstanding leads to fresh karma, and…


[2984]
RIN CHEN ‘PHRENG BA LAS,
,’DI YOD PAS NA ‘DI ‘BYUNG DPER,
,RING PO YOD NA THUNG NGU BZHIN,
,’DI SKYES PAS NA ‘DI SKYE DPER,
,MAR ME ‘BYUNG BAS ‘OD BZHIN NO,
ZHES DANG,

As the String of Precious Jewels puts it,

	If this is present,
	Then that will occur;

	It’s like, for example,
	There is short
	Wherever there is long.

	If this has arisen,
	Then that will arise;

	It’s like where
	Light occurs
	If a lamp does.


[2985]
RTZA SHE LAS KYANG,
,BYED PO LAS LA BRTEN BYAS SHING,
,LAS KYANG BYED PO DE NYID LA,
,BRTEN NAS ‘BYUNG BA MA GTOGS PAR,
,’GRUB PA’I RGYU NI MA MTHONG NGO,

Wisdom says as well—

	An agent is created
	Dependent upon its action.

	An action as well
	Comes about in dependence
	On nothing less
	Than its agent.
	
	Aside from this,
	We can see
	No cause which would
	Establish them.	


	[2986]
,DE BZHIN NYER LEN SHES PAR BYA,
,LAS DANG BYED PO GSAL PHYIR RO,
,LAS DANG BYED PA PO DAG GIS,
,DNGOS PO LHAG MA SHES PAR BYA,

One should understand
	Taking things on
	In just the same way,

	For we have dispelled
	Actions and agents.

Agents and actions
	Can be used
	To understand
	The rest of things.


[2987]
ZHES ‘DI TZAM ZHIG KHO NA GSUNGS KYI MTHA’ BZHI’I SKYE BA MA GSUNGS SO,,

This by the way is all that was stated; the idea of things arising through the four extreme options was not.


[2988]
DE LTAR RGYAL BAS RKYEN NYID ‘DI PA TZAM GYI SKYE BA GSUNGS PA BZHIN DU, ‘PHAGS PAS KYANG DE LTAR MDZAD CING,

And so we can say that—just as the Victors have described an arising to things which occurs through such and such a factor alone—The Realized One has done the same.


[2989]
KHYAD PAR DU BYED PA PO LAS LA BRTEN PA SOGS KYI LTOS ‘BYUNG GI RTEN ‘BREL BZHED PAS, DE MA GTOGS PA ZHES RANG DANG GZHAN LUGS KYI SKYE BA’I KHYAD PAR PHYE ZHING, DE DNGOS PO SRID TSAD LA SBYOR BAR GSUNGS PA DANG,

More particularly, we can say that they accept the idea of dependence in the sense of things occurring through reliance, where the doer depends for example upon the action done.  When the text says “aside from this” here, the point is that our presentation of how things arise is being differentiated from the way in which the other party here describes it; and it’s being stated that this description applies to the entirety of existing entitites.


[2990]
SLOB DPON ‘DIS SPYIR SKYE BA GZHAG DGOS PA DANG, MTHA’ BZHI LAS MI SKYE BA’I PHYIR BRTEN NAS SKYE BAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES ‘BAD PA DU MAS BSGRUBS PA LA,

Our master here must necessarily set forth how it is that things arise; and he is establishing—by expending quite considerable efforts—how it is that they arise through dependence, since they cannot arise through any of the four extreme options.


[2991]
MTHA’ BZHI LAS MI SKYE NA SKYE BA GTAN MED DO ZHES LUGS DE DAG LAS PHYIN CI LOG TU BZLOG NAS SMRA BA NI, NGAN RTOG GI DRI MA ‘THUG POS STONG NYID RTOGS PA’I RGYU MTSAN BLA NA MED PA RTEN ‘BYUNG ZAB MO’I DON, STONG PA NYID KYI DON DU ‘CHAR BA’I LUGS BLA NA MED PA LEGS PAR SLOD PA YIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG

And so it is that this other system is the source of the idea where they say that—if things do not arise through any of the four extreme options—then they cannot arise at all.  As such, you should all understand that these people have taken the thick stench of their mistaken ideas and used them to pollute, perfectly, the idea that the profound presentation of how things occur in dependence—the very trigger for realizing emptiness itself—makes its appearance as the true intent of emptiness.  For this is supreme teaching of all.


[2992]
,DE LTAR RKYEN NYID ‘DI PA TZAM GYI RTEN ‘BREL BSHAD PA NA, RGYU MED LAS SKYE BA LA SOGS PA BZHI [f. 211a] MI SRID PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI,

And so once we have offered our explanation of a dependence that depends on no more than this one factor behind everything, it becomes impossible for things to have arisen through any of these four choices of having had no cause, and the rest.  But it doesn’t end there!


[2993]
RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR SGRO ‘DOGS PA’I RTAG PAR LTA BA DANG, BYA BYED MI ‘THAD PA’I CHAD PAR LTA BA DANG, DUS SNGA MA NA YOD PA DE NYID DUS PHYI MA RNAMS SU ‘ANG YOD PA’I RTOG PA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS SNGA PHYI SO SO BA’I SKAD CIG MA’I MI RTAG PA DANG, DNGOS PO DANG DNGOS POR MED PA GNYIS NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA SOGS PAR RTOG PA’ANG BRTAGS PA’I YUL GZHAN DAG KYANG, MI SRID DO ZHES BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

Because now, with the following lines of the root text, we will describe how other options here that are products of sheer imagination are flatly impossible.  These include ideas like the following—

The view that things could never change, due to overrating these things and holding them to exist through some nature of their own;

The view that things would simply discontinue, due to the belief that the way everything works in the world is something mistaken;

The notion that the very same things which existed at some previous point in time could also exist at a later point in time;

The idea of a changing nature to things consisting of discrete milliseconds of time which exist, through some nature of their own, either earlier or later; or else

The concept of existents and non-existents—both of them—that could through some essential nature of their own.


	[2994]
[VI.115]
Pratītya bhava prabhavena śakyā
na kalpanāḥ kalpayituṃ yad etāḥ,
Tasmāt pratītyodaya yuktir eṣā
kudṛṣṭi jālaṃ sakalaṃ chinatti.

,GANG PHYIR DNGOS PO BRTEN NAS RAB ‘BYUNG BAS,
,RTOG PA ‘DI DAG BRTAG PAR MI NUS PA,
,DE PHYIR RTEN ‘BYUNG RIGS PA ‘DI YIS NI,
,[210a] LTA NGAN DRA BA MTHA’ DAG GCOD PAR BYED,

		The fact is
		That entities will
		Always spring forth
		In dependence.

		Thus these notions
		Cannot stand up
		Under close examination.

		And thus things
		Occur in dependence [f. 210a];

		This logic serves
		To sever all the cables
		Of the vast net
		Of terrible viewpoints.


[2995]
GANG GI PHYIR RGYU ‘DI LA BRTEN NAS ‘BRAS BU ‘DI RAB TU ‘BYUNG NGO ZHES BYA BA’I RIGS PA ‘DI TZAM ZHIG GIS, DNGOS PO KUN RDZOB PA RNAMS KYI BDAG GI DNGOS PO YOD PA ‘THOB KYI GZHAN DU MA YIN PAS,

The fact is that any particular result will always spring forth dependent upon a particular cause.  Thus this is the only logical statement needed to establish the ontological status of selected entities which are deceptive; and it cannot be otherwise.


[2996]
BDAG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA LA SOGS PA’I RTOG PA ‘DI DAG BRTAG PAR MI NUS PA DE’I PHYIR RTEN CING ‘BREL PAR ‘BYUNG BA RKYEN NYID ‘DI PA NYID KYI RIGS PA ‘DI YIS NI, JI SKAD BSHAD PA’I BDAG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA LA SOGS PAR LTA BA’I LTA BA NGAN PA’I DRA BA MTHA’ DAG GCOD PAR BYED PA YIN NO,,

These notions that things could arise from themselves, or from something other than themselves, or anything of the like cannot stand up under close examination.  And thus it comes down to things occurring in dependence and interconnection; this logic of the particular factor involved.  And this is a logic which serves to sever all the cables of the vast net of terrible viewpoints where people view things in ways such as arising either from themselves or from something other than themselves, in the manner that these are described by these thinkers.


[2997]
‘DI LTAR RKYEN NYID ‘DI PA TZAM ZHIG RTEN ‘BREL GYI DON DU ‘JOG PA’I DBU MA PAS NI, DNGOS PO ‘GA’ LA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS MA BLANGS TE,

And thus it is that those of the Middle Way establish the meaning of dependence, as nothing more complicated than talking about this particular factor for things.  They do not agree that any entity that ever exists could come about through some nature of its own.


[2998]
RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS,
,DE DANG DE RTEN GANG ‘BYUNG BA,
,RANG GI NGO BO DER MA SKYES,
,RANG GI NGO BOR GANG MA SKYES,
,DE NI SKYES ZHES JI SKAD BYA,

As the Sixty Verses on the Reasoning behind Emptiness puts it,

Anything which occurs
In dependence
On any particular thing
Cannot have started
In & of itself.

How could you ever say
That something which
Had not yet started,
In & of itself,
Then started?


[2999]
ZHES BRTEN NAS SKYES PA NI RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS MA SKYES PA DANG,

The point being made here is that things which have arisen through dependence cannot have arisen through some essential nature of their own.


[3000]
DE LTA YIN NA MYU GU LA SOGS PA RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS SKYES PAR JI SKAD DU BRJOD PAR BYA ZHES DANG,

And then it’s saying that—if this is the way things are—how could you other people be saying that sprouts or the like arise through just such an essential nature?


[3001]
RTZA SHE LAS KYANG,
,RTEN CING ‘BREL BAR ‘BYUNG [f. 211b] BA GANG,
,DE NI STONG PA NYID DU BSHAD,
,DE NI RGYUR BYAS GDAGS PA STE,
,DE NI DBU MA’I LAM YIN NO,

Wisdom puts it this way:

Anything that occurs
Through dependence & connection
Is something we explain
As emptiness itself.

We speak of this
As being produced
Through causes;

And that is the path
Of the middle way.


[3002]
ZHES RTEN ‘BYUNG YIN PA NYID KYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR GSUNGS SHING,

What this is saying is that the very fact that something has occurred through dependence is enough to say that it is empty of existing through any nature of its own.


[3003]
MDO SDE LAS KYANG,
,GANG ZHIG RKYEN LAS SKYES PA DE MA SKYES,
,DE LA SKYE BA’I RANG BZHIN YOD LA {%MA} YIN,
,RKYEN LA RAG LAS GANG DE STONG PAR BSHAD,
,GANG ZHIG STONG NYID SHES DE BAG YOD YIN,
ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

The sutras also include the following lines:

Anything which has arisen
Through factors
Is something that never arose;

That would not be
Something that had
A nature of arising.

What we say is that
Anything which relies
Upon factors is empty;

Anyone who truly
Understands emptiness
Is a person who is
Truly aware.


[3004]
RKYEN LAS SKYES PA NI GTAN TSIGS SO,,

“Arisen through factors” is in fact the logical reason here.


[3005]
BSGRUB PAR BYA BA MA SKYES ZHES PA’I DON NI RKANG PA GNYIS PAS BSTAN TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES TE ZHES PA’I DON YIN GYI, DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR MA SBYAR BA MIN TE,

What the reason is proving is expressed in the words, “never arose”; and its meaning is expressed in the second line of the verse [in Tibetan, corresponding to the second section in the English translation], where it says “that would not be something that had a nature of arising.”  But it’s not as if there is no distinction in the wording for what it is we’re denying.


[3006]
LANG GSHEGS TSIG GSAL DU DRANGS PA LAS, BLO GROS CHEN PO RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA LA DGONGS NAS, NGAS CHOS THAMS CAD MA SKYES PA’O, ,ZHES BSTAN TE, ZHES SANGS RGYAS NYID KYIS RANG GI DGONGS PA RANG GIS BLANGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And that’s because we see the following reference to A Journey to Langka in A Clarification of the Verses:

Understand, my intelligent ones, that when I say that not one of all the things that exists ever arose, what I mean to say is that none of them has ever arisen through some nature of their own.

Which is to say, the Buddha himself is identifying what his true intent was, when he made certain statements.


[3007]
DE’I PHYIR RIGS PA’I RGYAL PO RTEN ‘BYUNG GI RIGS PA NYID KYIS, RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA ‘GOG PA ‘DI NYID BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS GSUNGS PAS THUGS PHROGS NAS,

And so it was that sages have seen their hearts stolen away by this very description by the Conqueror of how things arising through some nature of their own is to be denied, by employing the king of all reasoning: this logic of dependence we’ve described here.


[3008]
RTZA SHE DANG RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LA SOGS PA GZHUNG DU MAR, ‘PHAGS PAS BCOM LDAN ‘DAS LA RTEN ‘BYUNG GSUNG PA NYID KYI SGO NAS BSTOD PA MDZAD PA LA, BRTEN NAS SKYES PA NYID KYIS MA SKYES SO ZHES PA’I MUN SPRUL GANG CI YANG RUNG BA SHES RAB CAN GYIS SMRA BAR MI BYA’O,,

And so too is it that in many great classics such as Wisdom or The Sixty Verses, the Realized Being himself has sung the praises of the Conqueror for this very fact: that he spoke to us of how things occur in dependence.  And so too is it that those of you with intelligence should never devolve into some kind of total darkness and say things like “things cannot start, since they must start in dependence.”


[3009]
GANG GI TSE DE LTAR DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS MA BLANGS PA DE’I TSE RANG BZHIN MED PA NI BDAG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA LA SOGS PA GANG ZHIG TU ‘BYUNG BAR ‘GYUR,

At the point where we refuse to accept that idea that things could exist through some nature of their own, then the general lack of a self-nature to things begins to refer to the fact that—for example—things might arise from themselves, or from something other than themselves.


[3010]
GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS [f. 212a] GRUB PA ‘GA’ ZHIG YOD NA NI DE’I TSE SKYE BA NGO BO NYID LAS SAM BDAG GZHAN DANG DBANG PHYUG SOGS LAS SKYE BAR ‘GYUR ZHING,

If there did exist some kind of natural existence to things, then the arising of things could be something that happened in and of itself; or from itself or something other than itself; or from some supreme being—or something else of the like.


[3011]
SKYES ZIN PA MI ‘JIG PAR GNAS PAS RTAG PA DANG, ‘JIG PAS CHAD PA LA SOGS PAR RTOG PA ‘BYUNG BA SRID LA, DE LAS GZHAN DU NI MA YIN NO ZHES BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

And then it would be possible for people to entertain notions such as the one which says that things that had already arisen would remain, without ever stopping; and would thus be forever unchanging—or that they had long since been destroyed, and thus discontinued.  Otherwise though it would not be possible for such ideas to come up.  To express all this, we have the next verse of our root text.


	[3012]
[VI.116]
Syuḥ kalpanā vastuni vidyamāne
parīkṣitaṃ vastu yathā ca nāsti,
Vinendhanaṃ nāsti yathaiva vahnis
tadvad vinā vastu bhavanti naitāḥ.

,RTOG RNAMS DNGOS PO YOD NA ‘GYUR BA STE,
,DNGOS PO JI LTAR MED PAR YONGS DPYAD ZIN,
,DNGOS PO MED PAR ‘DI RNAMS MI ‘BYUNG DPER,
,BUD SHING MED PAR ME YOD MIN DE BZHIN,

		We have already examined,
		In depth, these notions
		That things could exist,

		And how things
		Could never be.

		In the absence
		Of things,
		These will never
		Come up;

		It’s like,
		For example,
		The way that

		Fire can never occur
		In the absence
Of firewood.


[3013]
MTHAR ‘DZIN PA’I RTOG PA RNAMS DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR ‘DZIN PA YOD NA ‘BYUNG BAR ‘GYUR BA STE, JI SKAD BSHAD PA’I RIGS PAS DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA JI LTAR YANG MED PAR YONGS SU DPYAD ZIN LA,

Suppose it happens that these notions that hold to the extremes come up, and they begin to hold that things could exist through some nature of their own.  We have already examined in depth—with the logic we covered—how any existence of things through this kind of nature is something that could never be.


[3014]
DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR ‘DZIN PA MED PAR MTHAR ‘DZIN GYI RTOG PA ‘DI RNAMS MI ‘BYUNG STE, DPER NA RGYU BUD SHING MED PAR ‘BRAS BU ME YOD PA MIN PA DE BZHIN NO,,

In the absence though of the habit of holding that things could exist through some nature of their own, these kinds of notions will never come up; it’s like, for example, the way that the result of fire can never occur in the absence of its cause: the firewood.


[3015]
DE LTAR NA DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON GTAN LA PHAB PA GOMS PA LAS, RNAL ‘BYOR PA ‘PHAGS PA’I LAM MNGON SUM DU MDZAD PA’I MNYAM GZHAG GIS SNANG BA’I SPROS PA MA GZIGS PA’I TSUL GYIS DE KHO NA NYID GZIGS PA DE DAG LA CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA’I RTOG PA THOG MA MED PA NAS GOMS PA RNAMS LDOG PAR ‘GYUR TE,

And so it is that when they have accustomed ourselves to establishing just what it is that suchness refers to, the deep practitioner is able to go into a balanced meditation where they can manifest—directly—the path of a realized being.  And then this meditation helps them to see suchness, in the manner of not seeing the various ways that things might appear to one as false elaborations.  Thus then are such people able to put a stop to any habit of the kind that we have possessed for time with no beginning, of a notion where they feel strongly attached to the idea that any object at all could exist in truth.


[3016]
DPER NA MIG SMAN BSKUS PAS SKRA SHAD LA SOGS PAR SNANG BA LOG PA NYID RAB RIB CAN LA ‘BRAS BUR ‘GYUR GYI, SKRA SHAD LA SOGS PA RANG BZHIN GZHAN ZHIG TU SONG BA’I SGO NAS DE’I YUL DU ‘GYUR BA MIN PA BZHIN NO,,

It’s like, for example, when we apply some medicinal drops to our eyes, and this puts a complete stop to the appearance of any strand of hair or the like; this is the kind of result that comes to the person who was afflicted with the cataracts.  It is not the case though that some strand of hair or the like has transformed into having some other sort of nature, and then can no longer serve as the object of our perceptions.



Fruits from the examination

[3017]
BZHI PA NI,

Next comes our fourth part from before: identifying the fruits we derive from having undertaken this logical examination.


	[3018]
[VI.117]
Yā kalpanānāṃ vinivṛttir etat
phalaṃ vicārasya budhā vadanti,
Pṛthagjanāḥ kalpanayaiva baddhā
akalpayan muktim upaiti yogi.

,SO SO’I SKYE BO RNAMS NI RTOG PAS BCINGS,
,MI RTOG RNAL ‘BYOR PA NI GROL ‘GYUR BAS,
,RTOG RNAMS LOG PAR GYUR PA GANG YIN DE,
,RNAM PAR DPYOD PA’I ‘BRAS BUR MKHAS RNAMS GSUNG,

		Common beings
		Are enslaved by notions;

		Deep practitioners
		Do not imagine things,
		And become liberated.

		The wise
Have presented this:

The results of
Correct analysis,
Turning away
From those notions.		


[3019]
GANG GI PHYIR SO SO’I SKYE BO CHOS NYID ‘DI SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR MI SHES PA RNAMS NI GTZO BOR MTHAR ‘DZIN GYI RTOG PAS BCINGS PA DE’I PHYIR CHOS NYID ‘DI [f. 212b] DE LTAR THUGS SU CHUD PAS PHYIN CI LOG TU RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA NA RNAL ‘BYOR PA ‘PHAGS PA RNAMS NI GROL BAR ‘GYUR BAS

Common beings, as we have noted before, fail to understand this way of all things; which is to say, they are for the most part enslaved by notions where they hold to extremes.  As such, deep practitioners—which is to say, realized beings—do not imagine things to exist in any wrong way, for they have gained a complete grasp of that way of things.  And in this way, they become liberated.


[3020]
DE’I PHYIR MTHAR ‘DZIN PA’I RTOG PA RNAMS KYI ‘DZIN STANGS KYI YUL MA LUS PA BKAG PAS RTOG PA LOG PAR GYUR PA GANG YIN PA DE NYID ‘PHAGS PAS DBU MA’I BSTAN BCOS LAS BSHAD PA’I RNAM PAR DPYOD PA’I ‘BRAS BUR RNAM PAR BZHAG GO ZHES MKHAS PA RNAMS GSUNG NGO,,

And so it is that the wise have presented the following description; which is to say, this one thing has been explained, by the Realized One, in his classical commentary to the middle way.  And this is a description of the results of correct analysis: turning away from those notions, and putting this end to all the objects that notions which hold to the extremes grasp onto.


[3021]
BRGYA PA LAS KYANG,
,DNGOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD NA,
,STONG MTHONG YON TAN CI ZHIG YOD,
,RTOG PAS MTHONG BA ‘CHING BA STE,
,DE NYID ‘DIR NI ‘GOG PA YIN,

As the 400 Verses puts it,

	If things did exist
	Through some nature
	Of their own,

	Then what good
	Would it ever be
	To see emptiness?

	Those who see
	With their conceptions
	Are enslaved;

	And that’s exactly
	What we here deny.


[3022]
ZHES CHOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD NA DE NYID GSHIS YIN PAS DE MTHONG BA MDZES KYI, RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PA MTHONG BA LA YON TAN MED DO,,

What this is saying is that—if things did exist through some nature of their own—then that would be the way things are.  And then it would be a beautiful thing to see this; and there would be no great benefit to seeing that things were empty of any self-nature.


[3023]
DE’I PHYIR RTOG PAS MTHONG BA STE, RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR BZUNG BAS ‘CHING BA YIN PAS, DE’I ZHEN YUL DBU MA’I BSTAN BCOS ‘DIR DGAG PAR BYA BA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS LA,

As such then, a person who sees things with these notions in mind is holding that things exist through some nature of their own; and are enslaved by this view.  And the object that they hold to exist is what it is we are denying here in our classical commentary upon the middle way.


[3024]
DE’I ‘GREL PA LAS KYANG RTOG PA NI YANG DAG PA MA YIN PA’I RANG BZHIN GYI DON SGRO ‘DOGS PA STE, ZHES YANG DAG PAR YOD PA MA YIN PA LA YANG DAG TU YOD PAR SGRO ‘DOGS PA LA BSHAD PAS, RTOG PA GANG YIN THAMS CAD LA MI BYED KYI BDEN ‘DZIN GYI RTOG PA DANG MTHAR ‘DZIN GYI RTOG PA LA BYED DO,,

In the commentary to this we further see this notion described as “an overestimation of reality involving a nature which is flawed.”  Which is to say, it is being described as the overestimation of something which does not exist purely as existing purely.  As such this is not a blanket reference to all forms of mistaken notions, but rather referring to the notion where one believes that things exist in truth; or else a notion where one is holding to extreme viewpoints.


[3025]
MTHAR ‘DZIN GYI RTOG PA YANG MTHA’I SGRA DON MANG PO LA ‘JUG KYANG MTHA’ BRAL GYI MTHA’ NI DBU MA SNANG BA LAS, 

Now as far as these “notions where one is holding to extreme viewpoints,” the word “extreme” can in general refer to a lot of different things.  As for the use of “extreme” in the expression “free of extremes,” we can follow the following description from Light on the Middle Way.


[3026]
GAL TE DBU MA LA SEMS KYI RANG GI NGO BO’I BDAG NYID KYI DNGOS PO DON DAM PA CI YANG RUNG BA ZHIG YOD PAR GYUR NA NI, DE’I TSE DE LA YOD PAS RTAG GO ZHE’AM, MI RTAG GO ZHES BYA BAR MNGON PAR [f. 213a] ZHEN PA YANG JI LTAR MTHAR ‘GYUR TE, DNGOS PO’I DE KHO NA NYID JI LTA BA BZHIN GYI RJES SU SONG ZHING TSUL BZHIN YID LA BYED PA NYID NI, LTUNG BA’I GNAS SO ZHES BYA BAR RIGS PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PA BZHIN NO,,

If it were the case that in the middle way there could ever be some kind of ultimately existing entity with some essential nature of its own, then at that point there could exist with that the deluded belief that “this is unchanging,” or “this is changing”; which is to say, there would be a way of holding to an extreme.  That is, if a person has reached a place where they see the suchness of entities just as it really is, and if they are thinking of that in a perfectly correct manner, then it would never be appropriate to say of them, “They are at a place where they could fall.”


[3027]
DE YANG JI LTAR BZUNG BA DE LTAR YOD PA’I YUL DE NI ‘DIR MTHA’ MIN LA, BLO YANG TSUL BZHIN YID BYED YIN PAS MTHAR ‘DZIN MIN NO,,

That is, an object which does exist exactly in the way that we hold it to is something that we would not call an extreme.  And since the corresponding state of mind would be focusing upon its object in a correct way, it could never be described as “holding to an extreme.”


[3028]
DES NA ‘DI’I MTHA’ NI LTUNG BA’I GNAS YIN TE, ‘JIG RTEN NA BRAG G-YANG LA MTHA’ DANG DE LA LHUNG BA LA MTHA’ LA LTUNG ZHES SMRA BA LTAR, GANG DU GZUNG BAS ‘DZIN PA PO PHUNG BAR ‘GYUR BA LA MTHAR LHUNG ZHES BSHAD PA’O,,

As such, when we refer to an “extreme” here, we are talking about a place from which you could take a fall.  In the everyday world, for example, they talk about a cliff on a mountain as being the “extreme limit”; and when a person falls off of a cliff like this people say “they went over the edge.”  Here we are talking about the same thing: we’re referring to a position that—when you hold to it—you are completely lost: you have “fallen off the very edge of the cliff.”


[3029]
DE LA YANG DAG PAR YOD PA THA SNYAD DU YANG MI SRID PAS YANG DAG PAR MED PA THA SNYAD DU YOD PA’I PHYIR, DON DAM PAR MED CES PA MED PA’I MTHAR ‘DZIN DANG,

For something to exist in some absolutely pure sense in the context we’re speaking about here is in fact an impossibility, even nominally speaking; and so we can say that—speaking nominally—things do not exist purely.  To say then that things failed to exist, but in a pure sense, would again to be holding to an extreme.


[3030]
DE LTAR MA YIN ZHES ‘GOG PA MED MTHA’ ‘GOG PA MIN KYANG, DGAG BYA BKAG PA’I MED PA YANG DAG PAR YOD DO ZHES ‘DZIN NA DNGOS PO MED PA’I MTHAR LTUNG BAS DE ‘GOG PA YANG MED MTHA’ ‘GOG PA YIN NO,,

Now making a denial here and saying that this is not the way things are does not constitute a denial of the extreme notion of saying that nothing can exist.  But one would have fallen into the extreme of saying that no entity could exist, if they were to hold that the absence remaining once we have blocked the object that we deny did have some pure existence.  And so we can say that denying that idea does constitute the denial of the notion that things could never exist.


[3031]
LAS ‘BRAS LA SOGS PA’I CHOS RNAMS THA SNYAD DU YOD PA LA TSAD MA SUS KYANG GNOD MI SRID PAR, DE DAG YOD PA MIN PA’AM MED PAR ‘DZIN PA’I YUL YUL CAN NI MED MTHA’ DANG DE’I MTHAR ‘DZIN GYI, SANGS RGYAS LA SKYON MED CES PA LTA BU RNAMS MED MTHA’ DANG DE’I MTHAR ‘DZIN MIN NO,,

The fact that things like karma and its consequences do exist in a nominal sense is something that is impossible to question with any example of accurate perception.  The object and the subject holding to such entities and saying either that they are not existing things, or that they are non-existent, constitute the extreme of not existing at all, and the holding to that extreme.  We could never speak though—of the extreme notion of things not existing, or holding to this extreme—using something like the wording for “flaws do not exist” which we employ when we refer to an Enlightened Being.


[3032]
‘DI NI SKUR ‘DEBS KYI MED MTHA’ YIN LA SNGA MA NI SGRO ‘DOGS KYI MED MTHA’ ‘O,,

This by the way is the extreme notion of things not existing in the form of discounting what is actually there; whereas the earlier case represents the same extreme notion in the form of an overestimation of things.


[3033]
DE’I PHYIR SNGAR BSHAD PA’I BKAG PA LAS MA GTOGS PA’I CHOS RNAMS NI, DON DAM PAR RAM RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS YOD PAR ‘DZIN PA’I YUL YUL CAN NI [f. 213b] YOD MTHA’ DANG DE’I MTHAR ‘DZIN YIN GYI, SANGS RGYAS LA MKHYEN BRTZE YOD CES PA LTA BU RNAMS YOD MTHA’ DANG DE’I MTHAR ‘DZIN MIN NO,,

As such, let us consider those objects that would be excepted from the denial that we have earlier expressed here.  The object involved, and the subject involved, when we hold that these things could exist ultimately, or by definition, are what we are referring to when we speak of the extreme notion that things do exist, or to holding to this particular extreme.  It is not though that saying things like “an Enlightened Being does possess knowledge & love” would represent this extreme notion that things exist, or cleaving to that extreme.


[3034]
GZHUNG GI SKABS ‘GA’ ZHIG TU DON DAM PAR YOD PA THAMS CAD YOD MTHAR BSHAD PA YANG YOD DO,,

We do also see, in selected passages of the text, the totality of things that exist ultimately refered to as “the extreme of existence.”


	[3035]
[VI.118]
Na vādalobhād vihito vicāras
tattvaṃ tu śāstre kathitaṃ vimuktyai,
Vyākhyāyamāne yadi nāma tattve
bhidāṃ gatānyanyamatānyadoṣaḥ.

,BSTAN BCOS LAS DPYAD RTZOD LA CHAGS PA’I PHYIR,

		In the classical commentary
		Were not made

		Out of a love for
		Disputation.

		The concept of suchness,
		For the purpose
		Of liberating beings.

		Suppose it is the case
		That, when we undertake
		To present the details
		Of our explanations
		Of suchness,

		The texts of other
		Groups are shattered.
		You cannot fault us
		For that.


[3036]
DE NYID KYI PHYIR ‘PHAGS PAS DBU MA’I BSTAN BCOS LAS, RIGS PA’I RNAM PAR DPYAD PA SHIN TU MANG BAR MDZAD PA NI, RTZOD PA LA CHAGS PA STE GZHAN ZIL GYIS GNON PAR ‘DOD PA’I PHYIR MA MDZAD DO ZHES SHES PAR BYA STE,

For this very reason, one should understand something about how the Realized One employs a vast number of different logical arguments in his classical commentary upon the middle way.  Which is to say, it is not at all that he made them out of a love for disputation—to somehow put down others.


[3037]
RIGS PA’I RNAM PAR DPYAD PA MDZAD PA NA, DBU MA’I BSTAN BCOS LAS DE KHO NA NYID BSTAN PA NI, SEMS CAN GYIS DE KHO NA NYID ‘DI LTA BU PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR RTOGS NAS, THAR PA THOB PAR GYUR NA CI MA RUNG ZHES SKYE BO RNAMS RNAM PAR GROL BAR BYA BA’I PHYIR NI MDZAD PA YIN NO,,

When he does undertake these different forms of logical analyses, and uses them in his commentary on the middle way to teach the concept of suchness, what he’s saying is “How wonderful it would be if living beings could come to realize this kind of suchness, with complete accuracy, and thus attain freedom!”  That is, he follows this methodology of reasoning all for the purpose of liberating living beings.


[3038]
GAL TE KHYOD KYIS DNGOS POR SMRA BA RNAMS KYI RGOL BA JI LTAR BRTAGS PA THAMS CAD BKOD CING BSTAN BCOS LAS BKAG PA MA YIN NAM, DE’I PHYIR BSTAN BCOS KYI ‘JUG PA NI RTZOD PA’I PHYIR YIN PAS, RTOG PA LDOG PA TZAM ZHIG KHO NA ‘BRAS BUR JI LTAR RNAM PAR BZHAG CE NA,

One may then come with the following question—

But isn’t the case that in your commentary you have set forth all the fabricated arguments of your opponents—those who believe that functional things have some self-existence—and then set about denying their correctness?  So isn’t it in fact the case that the very methodology of your commentary is argumentation, and is not the result of that argumentation simply to stop some made-up ideas?  What kind of useful result then could come out of that?


[3039]
RNAM PAR DPYAD PA ‘DI NI RTZOD PA’I PHYIR MDZAD PA MA YIN MOD KYI, ‘ON KYANG DE KHO NA NYID NYE BAR BSTAN PA NA, GZHAN PHYOGS RANG BZHIN GYIS STOBS CHUNG BAS GZHAN GYI GZHUNG LUGS RNAMS BDAG NYID ‘THEN MI ‘DZUGS SHING, 

Our logical explorations, admittedly, were not done with the intention of simple argumentation.  Rather, the fact is that, when we are on the topic of trying to explain suchness, the opponents involved are of relatively low capacity—and therefore prove incapable, themselves, of bringing out the main points of the opposing schools involved.


[3040]
SNANG BA NYE BA NA MUN PA LTAR RANG NYID ‘JIG PAR ‘GYUR BA DES NA KHO BO CAG LA SKYON MED PA NYID DO ZHES BSHAD PA,

Which is to say, when dawn is close to breaking, the darkness rushes to destroy itself; as such, you cannot fault us.  To express these thoughts, we see the next lines of our root text here.


[3041]
GAL TE DE KHO NA NYID RNAM PAR BSHAD PA NA GZHAN GYI GZHUNG GIS BTAGS PA RNAMS ‘JIG PAR ‘GYUR NA KHO BO CAG LA NYES PA MED DE,

Suppose then that it is the case that—when we undertake to present the details of our explanations of suchness—the fabricated arguments found in the texts of other groups are shattered.  But you cannot fault us for that.


[3042]
BRGYA [f. 214a] BA LAS,
