Here the wagon—the thing itself—is a composite which relies upon its component pieces of the wheels and the rest.  We could also say that this same thing is a whole which relies upon the parts of the wheels and the rest.


[3508]
SHING RTA DE NYID ‘PHANG LO LA SOGS PA NYE BAR BLANG BAR BYA BA NYE BAR LEN PA’I BYA BA LA LTOS NAS NI, BYED PA PO ZHES ‘GRO BA LA BSNYAD PA DANG, RANG GI NYE BAR LEN PA GZUGS LA SOGS PA’I GDAGS GZHI LA LTOS NAS NI, SKYE BO RNAMS LA LEN PA PO NYID DU YANG ‘GRUB BO,,

We can also say that this same wagon is an incorporation of the the wheels and the rest.  And then since it relies upon what it has incorporated, we can call it an “agent.”  Living beings are designated in the same way; that is, dependent upon what it is they incorporate—their form and the rest—we can also say that people are thus established as nothing other than the ones that do this kind of taking on or incorporating.


[3509]
GANG ‘GA’ ZHIG GSUNG RAB KYI DON PHYIN CI LOG TU RTOGS PAS YAN LAG TSOGS PA TZAM ZHIG YOD KYI, TSOGS PA TZAM DE MIN PA’I YAN LAG CAN NI RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MED DE, TSOGS PA DE LAS NGO BO THA DAD PAR MA DMIGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Now there are some who understand the meaning of the scriptures in a completely mistaken way, and thus would say that there does exist the simple collection; but that there is in no manner at all of some whole of the component parts which is not the simple collection.  And this, they would say, is because there does not exist any such a whole which can be observed which is essentially separate from the collection.


[3510]
DE BZHIN DU SBYAR TE CHA SHAS DANG LAS DANG NYE BAR LEN PA TSOGS PA TZAM ZHIG YOD KYI, DE MIN PA’I CHA SHAS CAN DANG BYED PA PO DANG, NYE BAR LEN PA PO NI RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MED DE, DE RNAMS LAS [f. 238b] NGO BO THA DAD PAR MA DMIGS PA’I PHYIR,

Continuing on in the same vein, they would say that there do exist the pieces; and the action; and the incorporating and the simple collection; but they would say that there is in no wise a whole of the pieces which is not them; or such an agent, or one who does the incorporating.  This is due to the fact that none of these could ever be observed in a way which was essentially different from those things.


[3511]
ZHES DE LTA BUR RNAM PAR GNAS PA’I ‘JIG RTEN GYI KUN RDZOB PHYIN CI LOG TU SMRA BA DE’I LTAR NA, BSHAD MA THAG PA’I YAN LAG CAN MED PA’I GTAN TSIGS DE NYID KYIS, YAN LAG LA SOGS PA TZAM YANG MED PAR ‘GYUR BAS ‘JIG RTEN NA GRAGS PA’I KUN RDZOB SHING RTA LA SOGS PA MA BRLAG PA STE ‘JIG PAR MA BYED CIG CES ‘DI NI BZLOG PAR BYA BA KHO NA’O,,

Thus it is that that they describe, mistakenly, a deceptive nature of the world which exists in this way.  According to the logical statement just described—where it is said that no whole of the composite parts exists—even just those parts and so on could no longer exist.  And then the expression about the deceptive in the common parlance of the world—where someone says “don’t ruin that wagon” or the like, asking that we refrain from destroying it—would only be something that was refused.


[3512]
‘DIR RANG GI SDE PA GONG ‘OG GZHAN RNAMS YAN LAG TSOGS PA LA SOGS PA YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PAR ‘DOD PA NI, DE RNAMS YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PAR MA BZHAG NA DE RNAMS LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA YANG MED PAR MTHONG NAS BYA BA BYED NUS KYI YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA ‘JOG MA SHES PAS

Now others of the higher & lower schools of our own group take the position that the collection of the component parts and the like are the whole of the parts and such.  If they do not posit thus the whole of the parts and so on, then they see that there is no such whole of the parts or the like that could exist as essentially different from these.  Thus then they cannot understand how to establish a whole of the component parts, or anything of the like, that would have the capacity to perform the relevant functions.


[3513]
DE LTAR ‘DOD DE, DE DAG GIS YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA’I BTAGS DON BTZAL NAS MA RNYED NA, DE RNAMS ‘JOG MI SHES PA YIN NO,,

And thus then too do they take their position.  If these thinkers go looking for what was given the label in things like the whole of the component parts and don’t find anything, then they don’t see how these things could be established what they are.
 

[3514]
DE’I PHYIR SHING RTA SOGS MING DU BTAGS PA TZAM DU MI ‘DOD PAS SHING RTA LA SOGS PA RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ‘DOD PA YIN PAS,

As such—given that they cannot accept that things like a wagon and so forth are simply labeled what they are—they have to take the position that wagons and the like exist by definition.


[3515]
DE LA GSUNG RAB KYI DON PHYIN CI LOG TU RTOGS PA ZHES ‘GREL PAR GSUNGS TE, LUGS DAM PA ‘DIS NI YAN LAG TSOGS TZAM DANG, DE’I YA GYAL SOGS GANG YANG YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA’I MTSAN GZHIR MA BZUNG YANG, YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA MING DU BTAGS PA TZAM LA BYA BYED LEGS PAR ‘JOG NUS PA

And then what the autocommentary says is that these kinds of people have completely misunderstood the meaning of the scriptures.  That is, in this highest system suppose even that we refuse to consider the simple collection of the component parts, or any form of its separate constituents or the like, as the typical example of the whole of the component parts, and such.  But at the same time we interpret the meaning of scripture as saying that—even in a case where we do nothing more than apply a name to the whole of the component parts or the like—we are still perfectly able to establish with ease the entire manner in which things work in the world.


[3516]
GSUNG RAB KYI DON DU ‘GREL PA, THUB PA’I DGONGS PA THUN MONG MA YIN PA YIN PAS, RNAM DPYOD CAN GYIS DGONGS PA ‘GREL LUGS ‘DI LA SBYANG BAR BYA’O,,

Taking this as the meaning of scripture represents the perfectly unique intent of the Able Ones; as such, those of you possessed of discernment should verse yourselves in this manner of explaining their true thought.



The actual point about
eliminating extremes

[3517]
DRUG PA LA LNGA, DNGOS [f. 239a] KYI DON, DE LA RTZOD PA SPONG BA, SHING RTA DANG BDAG GI THA SNYAD RNAMS DPE DON DU SBYAR BA, BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA’I BDAG KHAS LEN PA’I YON TAN GZHAN BSTAN PA, MKHAS RMONGS KYI ‘CHING GROL GYI GZHI’I BDAG NGOS GZUNG BA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us then to our sixth point from above, which is a demonstration of how setting things forth in this manner has the advantage of making it easy to eliminate the notion where we hold to things in some extreme way.  We cover this topic in five different sections: (1) the actual point being made; (2) refuting argument on the point; (3) explaining the terms of a wagon and the self with reference to a metaphor and its referent; (4) demonstrating further advantages to accepting the position of a self which is labeled in dependence; and (5) an identification of the self, which is the foundation for the bondage & liberation of the ignorant & masters.


[3518]
GANG GI PHYIR ‘JIG RTEN GYI KUN RDZOB ‘DI SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR BTAGS DON ‘TSOL BA’I TSUL GYIS RNAM PA BDUN DU DPYAD PA NA,

Let’s examine this question of explaining, as we mentioned before, the deceptive reality of the everyday world in terms of seeking what it is we have given a label, in an examination of seven different steps.


[3519]
YOD PA RNYED PAR MI ‘GYUR ZHING, MA BRTAGS PA GRAGS PAS YOD PA DE NYID KYI PHYIR, RNAL ‘BYOR PAS SNGAR BSHAD PA’I RIM PA ‘DI NYID KYIS BDAG DANG SHING RTA ‘DI LA SNGAR LTAR RNAM PAR DPYOD PA NA, CHES MYUR BA KHO NAR DE KHO NA NYID KYI GTING DPOGS PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

In this case we will not find anything existing there; but the fact remains that it exists by convention, in an unexamined manner.  And suppose that a deep practitioner uses these very same steps that we have explained earlier, to undertake a thorough examination (also as we described it before) of this self, and this wagon.  It is only with extreme speed then that they will manage to plumb the depths of suchness.


[3520]
DE JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA, SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA ZHIG YIN NA RNAM PA BDUN GYIS BTZAL BA NA NGES PAR BDUN PO GANG RUNG ZHIG TU RNYED DGOS PA LA, RNAL ‘BYOR PAS SHING RTA ‘DI’I YOD PA NYID MI RNYED DO,,

“Just what does that look like?” you may inquire.  Suppose that a wagon were something that existed through some nature of its own.  In that case, if we did our search in those seven different aspects, we would without doubt have to locate the wagon in some one of the seven options.  The fact is though is that the deep practitioner does not arrive at any pure existence of this wagon.


	[3521]
[VI.160]
Yaḥ saptadhā nāsti kathaṃ tu sa syād
ityasya sattāṃ labhate na yogi,
Tattvāvatāro’pi sukhena vāta
itīṣyatām evam ihāsya siddhiḥ.

,RNAM BDUN GYIS MED GANG DE JI LTA BUR,
,YOD CES RNAL ‘BYOR PAS ‘DI’I YOD MI RNYED,
,DES DE NYID LA’ANG BDE BLAG ‘JUG ‘GYUR BAS,
,’DIR DE’I GRUB PA DE BZHIN ‘DOD PAR BYA,

		Not finding anything
		Using seven different
		Options means that
	
		The way things
		Really are is something
		Which is devoid
		Of existing.

		In this, the
Deep practitioner
Also engages with ease
In suchness.

As such,
Here we are
Also to accept
This, in the
Same manner.


[3522]
DE’I TSE RNAM PA BDUN GYIS BTZAL BA NA MI RNYED PA GANG DE JI LTA BUR NA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD CES TE MED DO,,

This not finding anything when we do our search using the seven different options means that the way things really are is something which is devoid of existing through any nature of its own.


[3523]
DE’I PHYIR SHING RTA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA ZHES BYA BA NI, MA RIG PA’I LING TOG GIS BLO’I MIG NYAMS PAR BYAS PA KHO NAS BRTAGS PA YIN GYI,

As such, we can say that the very expression that “a wagon is something which exists through some essential nature of its own” is only something imputed by an individual who has seen the eyes of their intellect degraded by the cataract of misunderstanding.


[3524]
RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI YOD PA MA YIN NO SNYAM PA DE LTAR RNAL ‘BYOR PA LA NGES PA SKYE BAR ‘GYUR ZHING, TSUL DES DE KHO NA NYID LA YANG RNAL ‘BYOR PA BDE BLAG TU ‘JUG PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

The deep pracititioner though is someone who gives birth to a certain certainty, as they think to themselves that there is no such thing as something existing through some nature of its own.  And in this manner, as well, the deep practitioner engages with ease in suchness.


[3525]
‘ANG GI SGRAS NI KUN RDZOB KYI RNAM GZHAG NYAMS PAR YANG MI ‘GYUR BA BSDU’O,,

The phrase “as well” in the root text here is meant to embrace the additional point that neither is it the case that in this case the practitioner will lose a correct understanding of deceptive reality.


[3526]
DE BAS NA DBU MA PA’I SKABS ‘DIR SHING RTA DE’I GRUB PA’I TSUL NI MA BRTAGS PAR [f. 239b] GRUB PA DE BZHIN DU ‘DOD PAR BYA’O,,

As such, then, here in the context of a follower of the Middle Way, we are also to accept—in the same manner—a way in which this wagon can exist without being examined.


[3527]
DBU MA PA’I LUGS LA MKHAS PA DAG GIS SNGAR BSHAD PA’I PHYOGS ‘DI NI SKYON MED CING PHAN YON DANG BCAS PA’O SNYAM DU BSAMS TE NGES PAR KHAS BLANG BAR BYA’O ZHES GSUNGS PAS,

Those who are masters of the system of the Middle Way then should think to themselves, as we see it said here, “The position that has previously been explained here is without fault; and possesses as well great benefit—it is quite certainly something that should be accepted.”


[3528]
‘DI’I LUGS SKYON MED PA RANG GI LUGS LA KHAS BLANG BAR BYA’I, ‘DI LA LUGS YOD PA MIN NO ZHES GNOD BKUR BAR MI BYA’O,,

The faultless system expressed here then is something that we should accept as being our own position.  One should never though do damage to this same approach by denigrating it with the statement that “Here in this system, we have no system at all.”



Refuting argument
on eliminating extremes

[3529]
GNYIS PA NI,

And so now we have reached our second section from above: refuting argument on the point of eliminating the extremes.


[3530]
‘DIR SMRAS PA, RNAL ‘BYOR PAS SNGAR LTAR DPYAD PA NA SHING RTA MA DMIGS PA LA RAG MOD, DE’I YAN LAG TSOGS PA TZAM ZHIG DMIGS PA NI RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD DO ZHE NA,

Here then someone comes with the following statement:

Your position here is one given with reference to a deep practitioner who has made an examination as described earlier, and failed to perceive then a wagon; they do though observe a collection of the component parts to this thing, and that does exist through some nature of its own.


	[3531]
[VI.161]
Sattvaṃ rathasyāsti na cet tadānīṃ
vināṅgināṅgānyapi santi nāsya,
Dagdhe rathe’ṅgāni yathā na santi
dhī vahni dagdhe’ṅgini tadvad aṅgam.

,SHING RTA YOD NYID MIN NA DE YI TSE,
,YAN LAG CAN MED DE’I YAN LAG KYANG MED,
,SHING RTA TSIG NA YAN LAG MED DPE BZHIN,
,BLO MES YAN LAG CAN BSREGS YAN LAG GO ,

		If it’s the case
		That a wagon
		Cannot exist
		In itself, then

		At that point
		The whole of the
		Component parts
		Cannot exist;

		Those component
		Parts too cannot exist.

		Suppose the wagon
		Is burned up;
		The component parts
		Are gone—

		We follow now
		This metaphor.

		The fire of the mind
		Burns up the whole
		Of the component parts;

		And those
		Component parts.


[3532]
SNAM BU TSIG PA’I THAL BA LA SNAL MA TSOL BA KHYOD NI BZHAD GAD DU BYA BA ZHIG STE, SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA NYID MIN NA, DE’I TSE YAN LAG CAN NGO BO NYID KYIS MED PAS, DE’I YAN LAG DAG KYANG NGO BO NYID KYIS MED DO,,

Your attempt here to find a surviving thread within the ashes of a burnt bolt of cloth is a real joke.  If it’s the case that a wagon cannot exist in itself—through some nature of its own—then at that point the whole of the component parts cannot exist through some essence of its own.  Thus then it’s the case that those component parts too cannot be things that exist through some essence of their own.


[3533]
GAL TE SHING RTA SO SOR ZHIG PA NA DE’I ‘PHANG LO LA SOGS PA TSOGS PA DMIGS PA NYID MA YIN NAM, DE’I PHYIR YAN LAG CAN MED PAR YAN LAG DAG KYANG MED DO ZHES CI STE BRJOD CE NA,

One may come then with the following question—

Suppose you take a wagon and break it apart.  Isn’t it the case then that the collection of the parts—the wheels and so forth—is still something you can observe?  Why then do you say if the whole of the parts is gone, the parts too must be gone?


[3534]
DE NI DE LTAR MA YIN TE SO SOR GYES PA’I YAN LAG SHING RTA’I YAN LAG TU ‘DZIN PA NI, SNGAR DE RNAMS SHING RTA DANG ‘BREL BAR RIG PA KHO NAS, ‘PHANG LO LA SOGS PA ‘DI DAG NI SHING RTA’I YAN LAG YIN NO SNYAM DU RTOGS KYI,

But that isn’t exactly the way things are.  When you grasp to the disassembled, separate parts as being the parts to a wagon, it is something that only happens because you know that previously they were connected to the wagon.  That’s the only way that you can come to this conclusion, thinking to yourself, “Oh, these things—the wheels and the rest—are parts of a wagon.”


[3535]
SNGAR DE LTAR MI SHES PA GZHAN GYIS NI MA YIN TE, GANG ZAG DE NI ‘PHANG LO SOGS KYI RANG GI CHA SHAS LA LTOS NAS, ‘PHANG LO LA SOGS PA KHO NA YAN LAG CAN NYID DU RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

This though is not something that someone else can do, who didn’t know that fact earlier.  That is, this other kind of person is depending upon the parts to the wheels and so on, and understanding no more than the wheels and the rest as wholes of parts.


[3536]
GANG ZAG DE’I NGOR ‘PHANG LO LA SOGS PA SHING RTA DANG ‘BREL BA YANG RGYANG RING DU SPANGS PA KHO NA YIN PAS, DE’I TSE DE DAG NI SHING RTA’I YAN LAG TU [f. 240a] MI RTOGS SO,,

In the perceptions of this person, the wheels and the rest may be related to a wagon; but this concept can only be quite removed, and far off.  As such, they do not at that moment understand these things as the component parts of a wagon.


[3537]
GZHAN YANG SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB NA DE’I YAN LAG KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN PA’I DON ‘DI NI, DPE ‘DI LAS SHES PAR BYA STE,

Moreover, the point that if a wagon is not something that could exist through some nature of its own, then its component parts cannot either be things that exist through some nature of their own is something that we can understand from this metaphor.


[3538]
DPER NA SHING RTA YAN LAG CAN MES TSIG NA YAN LAG RNAMS KYANG MED PA STE MES ‘TSIG PAR ‘GYUR BA’I DPE DE BZHIN DU,

Suppose for example that the whole of the component parts—the wagon—is burned up in a fire.  Then the component parts themselves are also gone—they are consumed by the fire.  We follow now this metaphor.


[3539]
RNAM PAR DPYOD PA’I GTZUB SHING GTZUBS PA LAS BYUNG BA’I MI DMIGS PA RTOGS PA’I BLO SHES RAB KYI MES,

And so consider then the fire of the mind, the wisdom, with which we grasp the way in which things are not even there: consider this fire, which springs from the heat of the friction of the fire sticks of true analysis.


[3540]
YAN LAG CAN SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA LUS PA MED PAR BSREGS PA NA, SHES RAB KYI ME’I BUD SHING DU GYUR PA’I YAN LAG DAG GIS KYANG BDAG NYID ZUG TSUGS PAR TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SDAD PAR BYED MI NUS TE, SHES RAB KYI MES NGES PAR BSREGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

This fire burns up, without a single thing left over, that idea that the whole of the component parts—the wagon—could exist through any nature of its own.  And those types of component parts themselves—which provide the firewood for the fire of wisdom—cannot stand on their own; that is, nothing can make them capable of staying there through some nature of their own.  Which is to say, they are with certainty burned up completely in these flames of wisdom.



The wagon & the self

[3541]
GSUM PA NI,

Which brings us to our third section from above: explaining the terms of a wagon and the self with reference to a metaphor and its referent.


	[3542]
[VI.162]
Ātmāpyupādātṛtayā tatheṣṭaḥ
skandhān upādāya jagat pratītyā,
Dhātūṃs tathā cāyatanāni ṣaḍḍhā
karmāpyupādānam asau ca kartā.

,DE BZHIN ‘JIG RTEN GRAGS PAS PHUNG PO DANG,
,KHAMS DANG DE BZHIN SKYE MCHED DRUG BRTEN NAS,
,BDAG KYANG NYE BAR LEN PA NYID DU ‘DOD,
,NYER LEN LAS YIN ‘DI NI BYED PO’ANG YIN,

	We are asserting
	That similarly,
	In the convention of
	The everyday world,
	
	The self as well
	Depends upon the
	Parts to the person;
	The realms; and
	Just so the six
	Doors of sense—

	And thus
Becomes a perfect
	Incorporator of them.
	
	What is incorporated
	Is the act, while this
	Is the agent.


[3543]
JI LTAR KUN RDZOB KYI BDEN PA MI GCAD PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR DANG, RNAL ‘BYOR PA RNAMS DE KHO NA NYID LA BDE BLAG TU ‘JUG PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR, SHING RTA RNAM PAR DPYAD PA’I TSUL LA BSAMS TE BRTEN NAS GDAGS PA RNAM PAR BZHAG PA

Think then of how we are taking care not to exclude the concept of deceptive reality, and how easily here deep practitioners can engage with perfect ease in the concept of suchness.  That is, by giving thought to this manner of examining a wagon, we are able to establish how things are labeled in dependence.


[3544]
DE BZHIN DU, ‘JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA’I SGO NAS NYE BAR LEN PA PHUNG PO LNGA DANG, KHAMS DRUG DANG, DE BZHIN DU SKYE MCHED DRUG LA BRTEN NAS BDAG KYANG SHING RTA LTAR NYE BAR LEN PA PO NYID DU ‘DOD DE, DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS BDAG TU BTAGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And what we assert is similar to this.  We are following the convention of the everyday world, with regard to the five parts to the person; the six outer realms; and just so the six doors of sense.  We are asserting that the self as well depends upon these things—like a wagon—and thus becomes a perfect incorporator of them.  Which is to say, we label something the “self” dependent upon these things.


[3545]
DE BZHIN DU NYE BAR LEN PA PHUNG PO NI LAS YIN LA, BDAG ‘DI NI BYED PA PO’ANG YIN NO ZHES RNAM PAR BZHAG GO

In the same way, we can also describe what is incorporated—the parts to the person—as being in a sense the act, while this self is the agent.



Further advantages
to a dependent self

[3546]
,BZHI PA NI,

Which brings us to our fourth point from before: demonstrating further advantages to accepting the position of a self which is labeled in dependence.


	[3547]
[VI.163]
Nānityatā cāsya na nityatā ca
na jāyate naśyati naiva cāyam,
Na śāsvatatvādi ca vidyate’sya
tattvaṃ na cānyatvam avastu sattvāt.

,DNGOS YOD MIN PHYIR ‘DI NI BRTAN MIN ZHING,
,MI BRTAN NYID MIN ‘DI NI SKYE ‘JIG MIN,
,’DI LA RTAG PA NYID LA SOGS PA YANG,
,YOD MIN DE NYID DANG NI GZHAN NYID MIN,

	Because that entity
	Is not something
	That exists,

	This could not be
	Something perfectly
	Solid, or not solid;

	This neither
	Starts nor stops;

	Nor could this exist as
	Perfectly unchanging,
	Or so forth—

	It does not exist
	As that itself,
	Or something
	Essentially different.


[3548]
BDAG BRTEN NAS GDAGS PA LA ‘JOG PA NA, BRTAN PA DANG MI BRTAN PA LA SOGS PA’I MTHAR ‘DZIN GYI RTOG PA’I RTEN MIN PAS MI RTAG PA LA SOGS [f. 240b] PAR NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ‘DZIN PA’I RTOG PA BZLOG PAR SLA BAR ‘GYUR RO ZHES BSHAD PA,

Our next section here is presented in order to make the following point.  Suppose we can establish that the self is something which is labeled in dependence.  In this case, it would no longer serve as a foundation for the kind of thinking where we hold to the extremes of believing that things are either solid, or not solid.  It then becomes relatively easy to stop the idea where we hold that things like impermanence could exist through some essence of their own.


[3549]
PHUNG PO DAG LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA’I BDAG ‘DI NI BRTAN PA DANG MI BRTAN PA NYID DU RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN NO,,

And so we can say that this kind of self which was labeled on the basis of the parts to the person could not be something that existed through some nature of its own—as being perfectly solid, or not solid.


[3550]
GAL TE BDAG MI BRTAN PAR NGO BO NYID KYIS YOD NA NI, BDAG DANG NYE BAR LEN PA GNYIS NGO BO THA DAD PA MI RUNG BAS NYE BAR LEN PA NYID BDAG TU ‘GYUR LA,

Now if the self existed in & of itself in a way which was not solid, it would be inappropriate to say that these two—the self and what it incorporated—were essentially separate from each other.  And in that case then, what was incorporated would itself become the self.


[3551]
DE LTA NA BDAG SKAD CIG SO SO LA NGO BO NYID KYIS SKYE ‘JIG SO SOR BYED PAS SNGA PHYI ‘BREL MED DU ‘GYUR BA DANG, NYE BAR BLANG BAR BYA BA RNAMS DE’I NYE BAR LEN PA POR ‘GYUR BA’I PHYIR MI RIGS SO,,

And in that case then the self would act to arise and to stop, individually, through some essence of its own, in every individual moment in time.  And this means then that what comes earlier and what comes later would share no connection; and all the items that were incorporated would become what incorporated them—which doesn’t make any sense at all.


[3552]
DE BZHIN DU BRTAN PA STE RTAG PAR YANG MI ‘THAD DE, DE RTAG NA SNGON GYI TSE RABS SU BYUNG BA’I DUS KYI BDAG DE NYID ‘DIR BYUNG BA’I BDAG YIN PA DANG, TSE SNGA MA DANG ‘DI’I BDAG GNYIS KYI NYE BAR LEN PA’I PHUNG PO NGO BO THA DAD PA YIN PAS, BDAG GCIG TU MI RUNG STE NYE BAR LEN PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I BDAG MED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

It would by the same token also be incorrect to say that this self were solid—which is to say, unchanging.  If it were unchanging, then the very same self that had occurred at the point of the earlier string of lifetimes would be the self that had occurred here.  And since the parts to the person taken on for the two selves—that of the previous life, and that of this one—would be essentially separate, then it would be wrong to say that they were essentially one & the same.  That is, there could be no self that was essentially separate from what it incorporated.


[3553]
RTZA SHER, GAL TE PHUNG PO BDAG YIN NA, ,SKYE DANG ‘JIG PA CAN DU ‘GYUR, ZHES GSUNGS PA

Now Wisdom has those lines that say,

If the self
	Were the parts
	To the person,

	Then it would be
	Something that
Went through starting
And stopping too.


[3554]
‘DI LAS NA ‘DI NI SKYE ‘JIG MIN ZHES PA’I KHYAD PAR GNYIS BKOD PA SLOB DPON GYI BZHED PA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS TE, SKYE ‘JIG NI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA’O,,

Here we see “it is the Master’s position that we mention both characteristics, that ‘this neither starts nor stops.’”  This is referring to a starting & stopping that would exist through some essence of its own. 


[3555]
BDAG ‘DI LA RTAG PA NYID LA SOGS PA’I BZHI TSAN YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN TE, RTZA SHE LAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA BRTAG PA’I THABS KYIS YONGS SU RTOG PAR MDZAD PA NA, RTAG DANG MI RTAG LA SOGS BZHI, ,ZHI BA ‘DI LA GA LA YOD, CES BYA BA LA SOGS PA LTA BU’O,,

Nor could this self be something that displayed any of the set of four different possibilities—being perfectly unchanging, or so forth—where these existed through some nature of their own.  This is similar to where Wisdom examines the question by means of examining the Ones Gone Thus; and expresses it with lines such as:
	
How could you ever say
	That this state of peace

	Involved any of the four
	Of being unchanging,
	Or changing, or the rest?


[3556]
BDAG ‘DI NI DE NYID DE NGO BO GCIG PA DANG [f. 241a] GZHAN NYID DU RANG BZHIN GYIS MED DO,,

That is, this self does not exist as that itself—meaning, the one thing, essentially one, or something essentially different; at least through any nature of its own.


[3557]
DE RNAMS KYI RGYU MTSAN NI BDAG CES BYA BA’I DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD PA MIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And that’s all because—the reason for saying these things is—that entity which we refer to as the “self” is not something that exists through any nature of its own.


[3558]
JI SKAD DU MDO LAS,
,MI ZAD PA YI CHOS BZHI NI,
,’JIG RTEN MGON GYIS BSTAN PA STE,
,SEMS CAN NAM MKHA’ BYANG CHUB SEMS,
,DE BZHIN SANGS RGYAS CHOS RNAMS SO,,

Sutra puts it this way:

	The Savior of the World
	Taught that four different things
	Would never wear out:

	Living beings;
	The sky; the Wish
	For enlightenment;
	And the teachings
	Of the Buddhas.
 	

	[3559]
,GAL TE DE DAG RDZAS YOD NA,
,DE DAG YONGS SU ZAD ‘GYUR GRANG,
,MED PA DE DAG MI ZAD DE,
,DE PHYIR DE DAG ZAD MED GSUNGS,
ZHES SO,,

	If these things
	Existed substantially,

	Then we would have to
	Consider them things
	That could wear out.

	But things that cannot
	Exist cannot wear out;

	Thus it is it was spoken
	That this they could never do.
	

[3560]
SEMS CAN RDZAS SU MED PAS MI ZAD PAR GSUNGS PA NI ‘DIR KHUNGS SO,,

This by the way is the source for statements that living beings can never wear out, because they do not exist substantially.



Self: foundation
for bondage & liberation

[3561]
LNGA PA NI,

And now we have reached our fifth and final point from above: an identification of the self, which is the foundation for the bondage & liberation of the ignorant & masters.


[3562]
GANG ZHIG BTAGS DON RNAM PA BDUN GYIS BTZAL BA NA, RTAG PA DANG MI RTAG PA NYID DU MI SRID CING, BDAG GANG ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NYID MA MTHONG ZHING,

Now there are those who fail to seek—in those seven different ways—what it is that receives the label; and thus cannot come to see that it is simply not possible for it to be unchanging or changing—and cannot recognize that there is absolutely no self anywhere that could exist through some nature of its own.


[3563]
MA RIG PA’I DBANG GIS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA NYID DU ZHEN NAS, ‘JIG LTAS BDAG ‘DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS ‘KHOR BAR ‘GYUR LA,

Due to misunderstanding then they are strongly attracted to the idea that things must exist through some nature of their own.  And due to this, they hold strongly—through that view of destruction—to the idea that this self could exist through some nature of its own.  And because of this, they must make their circle.


[3564]
BDAG GANG ZHIG YONGS SU TSOL BA NA, MU STEGS PA BDAG ‘TSOL BA DE’I RIGS PAS PHUNG PO NYID BDAG TU MI ‘THAD PAR MTHONG BAS, BDAG DE’I RANG GI NGO BO LA PHYIN CI LOG TU GYUR PA THAMS CAD PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PAR ZHEN CING,

When people undertake some exhaustive examination to find the self, they see that the logic which is used by the River Schools in their search for the self is insufficient for proving that the parts to the person themselves could be the self.  As such, all of those here who are completely mistaken about the essential nature of that self feel a strong attraction to the idea that the self must be something essentially separate from these parts to the person.


[3565]
RANG GI SDE PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I BDAG MED DO SNYAM ZHING ‘KHRUL BAS, PHUNG PO TZAM NYID BDAG TU KHAS BLANGS TE, DE GNYIS GANG RUNG ZHIG TU KHAS BLANG DGOS SNYAM DU BSAMS PA’O,,

There are those in our own group as well who think to themselves that there must be no self that is essentially separate from the parts to the person.  In their mistake then they agree to the idea that the it is the simple parts to the person which constitute the self.  That is, their thinking here is that—the way they see it—they would have to accept one or another of the two options.


	[3566]
[VI.164]
Ayaṃ sa ātmā jagatāṃ pravṛttā
yasmin ahaṃkāra matiḥ sadaiva,
Yat tasya tasmin mamakāra buddhir
udeti mohād avicāra buddhyā.

,GANG PHYIR RTAG TU ‘GRO RNAMS NGAR ‘DZIN BLO,
,RAB TU ‘BYUNG ZHING DE YI GANG YIN DER,
,NGA YIR ‘DZIN BLO ‘BYUNG BA’I BDAG DE NI,
,MA BRTAGS GRAGS PAR GTI MUG LAS YIN NO,

		It is indeed the case
		That a state of mind
		Is forever arising with

		All those living beings
		Which holds to “me.”

		Everything there
		Is that which is of it:

		Everything that makes up
		That self towards which
		There arises the state
		Of mind that
Holds to “me.”

It is something
That stems from
That dark state
Of ignorance

Towards one
Which is unexamined,
In the parlance
Of the world.		


[3567]
GSUNG RAB KYI DON PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR ‘CHAD PA RNAMS NI,

Here though is what would be said by those who are capable of explaining the meaning of scripture in a completely unmistaken way.


[3568]
SNGA MA DE GNYIS GANG DU YANG YOD PA MA YIN NO SNYAM DU RIG NAS LAN BRGYAR [f. 241b] GROL BAR ‘GYUR BA DE NI BDAG YIN ZHING,

First of all, they would understand; they would have the thought that neither of those two options presented earlier was the way things are.  They would repeat—a thousand times—that it is the self which achieves liberation.


[3569]
‘GRO BA MI DANG YI DVAGS DANG DUD ‘GRO LA SOGS PAR GNAS PA MTHA’ DAG RNAMS LA, RTAG TU DMIGS PA’I GZHI GANG ZHIG LA DMIGS NAS NGAR ‘DZIN PA’I BLO RAB TU ‘BYUNG ZHING,

And they would say that this self is the foundation that all those living beings—they who live among the humans, the craving spirits, the animals, and every other form of life—are forever looking upon; and that towards which, when they look upon it, a state of mind is forever arising which holds that to be “me.”


[3570]
GANG DU BDAG ‘DI DBANG BYED PA NYID DAM, BDAG DE DANG ‘BREL BA ‘GA’ ZHIG TU ‘GYUR BA BDAG ‘DI GDAGS PA’I RTEN MIG LA SOGS PA NANG GI BDAG NYID CAN DANG, PHYI ROL GANG YIN PA

And then also let us consider what pertains to this self; that number of things which are related to the self.  That is, let’s consider that basis which is labeled this “self”: those entitites which are inner (the eye and so on); and those which are outer.


[3571]
BDAG DE YI BDAG GI BA GANG YIN PA DER, NGA YI BAR ‘DZIN PA’I BLO ‘BYUNG BA’I BDAG DE NI, MA BRTAGS PA’I GRAGS PA’I NGOR GTI MUG STE MI SHES PA LAS GRUB PA YIN GYI RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA NI MA YIN NO,,

In short then, let us consider everything there is which is of it, the self: which belongs to the self.  This is everything that makes up that self towards which there arises the state of mind that holds to “me.”  And it is something that stems from misunderstanding: from that dark state of ignorance focused towards a self that is unexamined, and accepted on face value, in the parlance of the world.  It is not though something that could exist through some essence of its own.


[3572]
GANG GI PHYIR BDAG ‘DI RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN MOD KYI, ‘ON KYANG GTI MUG STE MI SHES PA LAS YOD PAR THA SNYAD ‘DOGS PA’I PHYIR, RNAL ‘BYOR PAS DE ‘DRA BA’I BDAG RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MA DMIGS LA,

“It is indeed the case”; that is, it is admittedly true that this self is not something that could exist through some nature of its own.  The appellation “it exists” though is applied to it, through our ignorance: our failure to understand.  As such, no deep practitioner could ever perceive this type of self, in any way at all.


[3573]
DE MA DMIGS NA’ANG MIG LA SOGS PA BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DE’I NYE BAR LEN PA RNAMS DMIGS PAR MI ‘GYUR TE, ‘DI LTAR RNAL ‘BYOR PAS NI BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA’I GZHI’I DNGOS PO ‘GA’ LA YANG RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA DMIGS PA MED DE, DE’I PHYIR ‘KHOR BA LAS GROL BAR ‘GYUR TE,

And even though they never perceive such a thing, neither do they perceive anything it is that this self-existent self could incorporate.  Thus it is that there is nothing at all that the deep practitioner perceives as existing through some essence of its own, when we are talking about that base entity for the self, and what belongs to the self.  And because of that not seeing, this practitioner comes to be free of the cycle of pain.


[3574]
RTZA SHE LAS,
,NANG DANG PHYI ROL NYID DAG LA,
,BDAG DANG BDAG GI SNYAM ZAD NA,
,NYE BAR LEN PA ‘GAG ‘GYUR ZHING,
,DE ZAD PAS NA SKYE BA ZAD,
CES GSUNGS SO,,

As Wisdom puts it,

	The idea of self
	And something belonging
	To the self
	Is finished,

	Towards both
	What could be inside,
	And what could be out.

	Taking them on then
	Is blocked;

	And when that is done,
	We are done
	With being born.



Denying any nature
to what belongs to the self

[3575]
GNYIS PA NI,

With this we have reached our second point from above: denying that what belongs to the self could exist through any nature of its own.


	[3576]
[VI.165]
Akartṛkaṃ karma ca nāsti yasmād
ātmānam ātmīyam ato vinā’sat,
Ātmānam ātmīyam ataḥ sa śūnyaṃ
paśyan vimuktiṃ samupaiti yogi.

,GANG PHYIR BYED PO MED CAN LAS MED PA,
,DE PHYIR BDAG GI BDAG MED PAR YOD MIN,
,DE PHYIR BDAG DANG BDAG GI STONG LTA ZHING,
,RNAL ‘BYOR PA DE RNAM PAR GROL BAR ‘GYUR,

		An agent
		Has no existence,
		
		And what they
		Act towards
		Has no existence
		Either.

		As such,
		Something belonging
		To the self

		Is not something
		That could ever exist
		With a self
		That could not
		Itself exist.

		As such,
		That deep practitioner
		Who sees that
		Both the self
		
		And what belongs
		To the self 
		Are empty
		Is completely liberated.


[3577]
YANG JI LTAR BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS MED NA BDAG GI BA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS MED CE NA,

One might begin with the following question:

Given that the self cannot exist through any nature of its own, is it also true that what belongs to the self cannot exist through any such nature?


[3578]
JI LTAR BYED PA PO RDZA MKHAN MED PA CAN GYI LAS SU BYA BA RDZA BUM MED PA DE’I [f. 242a] PHYIR BDAG GI BA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI, BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR YOD PA MIN NO,,

It’s just the way in which an agent—say, the potter—is something that has no existence; and what they act towards—the clay pot itself—has no existence either.  As such, let’s consider something belonging to the self that could exist through some nature of its own.  This is not something that could ever exist, with a self that could not itself exist through any nature of its own.


[3579]
DE’I PHYIR BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR LTA ZHING, DE’I DON GOMS PAR BYED PA NA RNAL ‘BYOR PA DE ‘KHOR BA LAS RNAM PAR GROL BAR ‘GYUR RO,,

As such, let’s consider that deep practitioner who sees that both the self and what belongs to the self are empty of existing through any nature of their own; and who then undertakes to accustom themselves to this fact.  This then is a person who is completely liberated from the cycle of suffering.


[3580]
GZUGS LA SOGS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA DMIGS PA NA, GZUGS LA SOGS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR RTOG PA’I CHAGS SOGS KYI NYON MONGS RNAMS ZAD PAR ‘GYUR BAS,

Suppose that we no longer look at form and the rest as being things that could exist through some nature of their own.  In that case, negative thoughts such as attachment and the rest—thoughts where we imagine that form and such could indeed exist through some nature of their own—will come to a stop.


[3581]
NYAN RANG RNAMS YANG SRID LEN PA MED PAR MYA NGAN LAS ‘DA’ LA, BYANG SEMS NI DE ‘DRA BA’I BDAG MED PA MTHONG DU ZIN KYANG, SNYING RJE’I GZHAN GYI DBANG GIS BYANG CHUB KYI BAR DU SRID PA’I RGYUN GYI SKYE BA ‘DZIN PAR BYED DO,,

Bodhisattvas have long since seen that kind of lack of a self-nature which the listeners and self-made buddhas use to reach the nirvana where they no longer have to take a rebirth.  But since they live at the mercy of thoughts of compassion, these bodhisattvas will still work to take a birth in the flow of lifetimes, until such time as they reach enlightenment.


[3582]
DE LTAR THEG PA CHE CHUNG GNYIS KA’I LAM GYI GNAD DAM PA YIN PA’I PHYIR MKHAS PAS JI SKAD BSHAD PA’I BDAG MED PA YONGS SU BTZAL BAR BYA’O,,

This is a high and holy, crucial point of the paths of both the greater and the lesser way.  As such, wise ones among you should do their utmost to seek out the absence of a self, as we have explained it here.



How the examination follows
for common entities

[3583]
GSUM PA LA GSUM, BUM SNAM SOGS KYI DNGOS PO LA BSGRE BA, RGYU DANG ‘BRAS BU’I DNGOS PO LA BSGRE BA, DE LA GZHAN GYI RTZOD PA SPANG BA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

Which brings us to our third point from before: the way in which we can apply our examination of the self, and of a wagon, to other entities as well.  This we cover in three different sections: showing how this examination follows for entities such as water pitchers, bolts of cloth, and the like; showing how it follows for the entitites of cause & effect; and then finally refuting any other argument on these points.  Here is the first of these.


	[3584]
[VI.166]
Ghaṭa paṭa kaṭa senāḥ kānanaṃ paṅkti vṛkṣā
gṛha śakaṭa maṭhādyā ye ca kecit padārthāḥ,
Vyavaharati jano’yaṃ yais tathā tān pratīhi
vivadati sa Munīndro yan na lokena sārddham.

,BUM PA SNAM BU RE LDE DMAG DANG
NAGS TSAL PHRENG BA LJON SHING DANG,
,[212b] KHANG KHYIM SHING RTA PHRAN DANG ‘GRON GNAS
LA SOGS DNGOS RNAMS GANG DAG DANG,
,DE BZHIN GANG DAG SGO NAS SKYE ‘DIS
BSNYAD PA DE RNAMS RTOGS BYA STE,
,GANG PHYIR THUB DBANG DE NI ‘JIG RTEN
LHAN CIG RTZOD MI MDZAD PHYIR RO,

Let’s consider
Things like
Water pitchers
And bolts of cloth
And rolls of felt;

As well as
Armies and forests,
And strings of
Beads, and trees [f. 212b].

Or houses and carts,
And meeting places,
And guest houses,
And all such entities;

And in the same vein,
		We should understand
		These things as well:

All those things which
These same people
Would ascribe.

And why is
This the case?
It’s because this
Lord of the Able Ones

Has no argument
With the world.


[VI.167]
Avayava guṇa rāgā lakṣaṇānīndhanādyā
avayaviguṇiraktā lakṣyam agnyādayo’rthāḥ,
Vihita ratha vicārāt saptadhā santi naite
sati tu tad itarasmin santi loka prasiddhyā.

,YAN LAG YON TAN ‘DOD CHAGS MTSAN NYID
DANG NI BUD SHING LA SOGS DANG,
,YON TAN CAN YAN LAG CAN CHAGS DANG
MTSAN GZHI ME LA SOGS DON DAG,
,DE RNAMS SHING RTA’I RNAM DPYAD BYAS PAS
RNAM BDUN YOD PA MA YIN ZHING,
,DE LAS GZHAN DU GYUR PAR ‘JIG RTEN
GRAGS PA’I SGO NAS YOD PA YIN,

		There are
Component parts,
		Qualities,
		Wanting itself,
		Defining characteristics,
		Firewood, and so on;

		And then there are
		The combination
		Of the qualities,
		The whole of
		The component parts,
		The one with the wanting,
		The thing which is defined,
		Fire, and so on.

		We can use the same
		Examination on them
		As we did on the wagon;

		Using the seven options,
		We cannot find
		Anything that exists.

		And if we proceed
		In a different manner,
		They are all things
		That do exist, if only
		In the parlance of
		The everyday world.


[3585]
JI LTAR BDAG DANG DE’I NYE BAR LEN PA’I GDAGS PA RNAMS SHING RTA’I DPYAD PA DANG MTSUNGS PA DE BZHIN DU, DNGOS PO GZHAN RNAMS KYI DPYAD PA YANG YIN NO ZHES BSTAN PA’I PHYIR,

This next section is meant to present the following idea.  When we talk about the ascribed entitites of the self and what it incorporates, things work the same as in the case where we examine a wagon.  We undertake the examination of other entities in just this same manner.


[3586]
GANG DAG BUM PA DANG SNAM BU DANG RE LDE DANG, DMAG DANG NAGS TSAL DANG, ‘PHRENG BA DANG LJON SHING DANG, KHANG KHYIM DANG SHING RTA PHRAN DANG, ‘GRON GNAS LA SOGS PA’I DNGOS PO DE RNAMS SHING RTA’I RNAM [f. 242b] PAR DPYAD PAS,

And so let’s consider here things like water pitchers and bolts of cloth and rolls of felt.  And let’s take as well armies and forests.  Let’s consider strings of beads, and trees.  Let’s think on houses, and carts, and meeting places, and guesthouses, and all such entities.  We can use the same examination on them as we did on the wagon.


[3587]
RANG RANG GI BTAGS DON RNAM PA BDUN DU BTZAL BA NA YOD PA MA YIN ZHING, BTZAL BA DE LAS GZHAN DU GYUR PAR TE MA DPYAD PAR ‘JIG RTEN NA GRAGS PA’I SGO NAS YOD PA YIN NO,,

If we search out what it is that got the name in each of these cases, using the seven different options, we cannot find anything that exists.  And if we proceed with our search in a different manner—meaning, if we leave off that kind of examination—then they are all simply things that do exist, if only in the parlance of the everyday world.


[3588]
SHING RTA PHRAN LA BOD KYI BLA MA KHA CIG ,SHA KA KRA NI ‘KHOR LO CAN TE SHING RTA’I PHRAN JA SIG GSUM TZAM ‘GEL BA STE, DE YANG ‘KHOR LO DANG BAR YANG YOD PA’I KHANG PA GCIG YIN ZER RO,,

As for certain wording in the Tibetan translation of the verse here—shing ta tren—some teachers in Tibet have claimed that the Sanskrit term shakakra means “a vehicle with wheels,” referring to a supporting structure consisting of the three of wood and case and straps.  They would say then that it refers to both to the cart and to a small cabin in the middle of the coach.


[3589]
DE BZHIN TE DE LTA BU’I RIGS CAN GYI DNGOS PO GZHAN GANG DAG GI SGO NAS SKYE BO ‘DIS BSNYAD PA STE THA SNYAD BTAGS PA DE RNAMS KYANG, MI BRTAGS PA’I GRAGS PA KHO NAR YOD PAR RTOGS PAR BYA STE,

And so in the same vein we can consider other entities of this same general category: all those things which these same people would ascribe—or give a label—in a similar manner.  We should understand that all of these things as well exist only in an unexamined way, according to the general parlance.


[3590]
RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA THUB PA’I DBANG PO DE NI ‘JIG RTEN DANG LHAN CIG ‘JIG RTEN LA MI MTHUN PA’I RTZOD PA MI MDZAD PAR GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR TE,

And why—for what reason—is this the case?  It’s because this very Lord of the Able Ones has made the statement that “I have no argument with the world”; which is to say, nothing against the way of the world at large.


[3591]
DKON BRTZEGS KYI SDOM PA GSUM BSTAN PA LAS, ‘JIG RTEN NGA DANG LHAN CIG RTZOD KYI, NGA NI ‘JIG RTEN DANG MI RTZOD DO,

And in fact we do see the statement, in the presentation of the three sets of vows in the Pile of Jewels, that—

	The world may argue with me,
	But I have no argument with the world.


[3592]
ZHES ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD GNOD MED KYIS YOD PAR BZHAG PA RNAMS, THUB PAS KYANG ZHAL GYIS BZHES PAR GSUNGS PAS NA, ‘JIG RTEN GYI GRAGS PA LA GNOD PAR MI BYA’O,,

What this is saying is that those things which are established as existing by the world at large, through the unmistaken naming of objects, are also fully accepted by the Able Ones.  As such, their positions do not draw into question what the world in general says of things.


[3593]
GANG YANG ‘JIG RTEN PA RNAMS DNGOS PO GANG DAG GIS JI LTAR THA SNYAD ‘DOGS ZHE NA,

One might then ask just how it is that those of the world do their labeling of things.


[3594]
DE BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA, JI LTAR BUM PA YAN LAG CAN DANG GYO MO LA SOGS PA DE’I YAN LAG DANG, BUM PA YON TAN CAN YIN LA, ME RIS SNGO BSANGS LA SOGS PA DE’I YON TAN DANG,

The next section here is meant to explain this point.  A water pitcher for example constitutes the whole of its component parts; and the shards of clay and such constitute those parts.  A water pitcher is also the combination of its qualities, and things like the greenish blue hue of the glaze on the pitcher are its qualities.


[3595]
YID DU ‘ONG BA’I YUL LA CHAGS PA’I SEMS CAN NAM GANG ZAG ‘DOD CHAGS KYI RTEN NI CHAGS PA DANG, ZAG BCAS KYI YUL [f. 243a] YID DU ‘ONG BA LA DMIGS NAS LHAG PAR SRED PA NI ‘DOD CHAGS DANG,

A living being, or person, who is attached to an attractive object—the one who serves as the basis of the desire—is the one with wanting; while the wanting itself is that craving that comes when they focus upon an impure but attractive object.


[3596]
BUM PA NI MTSAN GZHI DANG, LTO BA LDIR BA DANG MCHU ‘PHYANG BA MGRIN PA RING BA LA SOGS PA DAG DE’I MTSAN NYID DANG,

A water pitcher is the thing which is defined; while the rounded belly, the protruding spout, and the lengthened neck of the pitcher and such are its defining characteristics.


[3597]
ME NI SREG PAR BYED PA DANG, BUD SHING NI BSREG PAR BYA BA LA SOGS PA NI,

Fire is the thing that acts to burn; while firewood is the thing that is burned; and so on.


[3598]
YAN LAG LA BRTEN NAS YAN LAG CAN DANG, YAN LAG CAN LA BRTEN NAS YAN LAG TU ‘DOGS TE, DE BZHIN DU MED {%ME} DANG BUD SHING GI BAR DU PHAN TSUN BRTEN NAS ‘DOGS PA’I BAR DU’O,,

The whole of the component parts is always labeled upon its component parts; and the component parts are labeled upon the whole of the component parts.  And everything on up to the fire and firewood is labelled in mutual dependence.


[3599]
‘DI RNAMS KYI BTAGS DON RNAM PA BDUN DU BTZAL BA NA MED KYANG YOD PAR ‘JOG NUS PA NI, ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD KYIS YIN GYI, DE KHO NA NYID LA DPYOD PA’I RIGS PA’I DPYAD RA MI GZHUG GO

When we look in those seven different ways for what was given the label, we cannot find it—and yet we are able to establish that the thing exists.  This is all due to the verbiage of the everyday world; but none of it stands up under the logic we use to investigate suchness.



How the examination follows
for cause & effect

[3600]
,GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second part from above: showing how this examination follows for entitites of cause & effect.


	[3601]
[VI.168]
Janayati yadi hetur janyam evaṃ sa hetur
na janayati phalaṃ cet tad vinā hetukaḥ syāt,
Phalam api sati hetau jāyate yena tasmāt
kathaya bhavatu pūrvaṃ kiṃ kuto yad yataḥ syāt.

,GAL TE RGYU YIS BSKYED PAR BYA SKYED
DE LTA NA DE RGYU YIN ZHING,
,GAL TE ‘BRAS BU MI SKYED NA NI
DE MED RGYU MED CAN DU ‘GYUR,
,’BRAS BU YANG NI RGYU YOD GYUR NA
SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA DE YI PHYIR,
,GANG LAS GANG ZHIG ‘GYUR BA GANG ZHIG
LAS SNGAR GANG ZHIG ‘GYUR BA SMROS,

		Suppose a cause
		Were to give rise
		To what it acts
		To instigate.

		In this case,
		The cause
		Would be that.

		If it did not act
		To trigger a result,
		Then with
		Nothing such,
		
		It would be one
		Which had no cause.

		The result as well—
		If there is a cause—
		Will grow.

		Thus then
		Whatever could
		Either one
		Occur from?

		Please describe
		To us which of these
		Is earlier, and which
		Could occur.


[3602]
YAN LAG LA SOGS PA RNAMS PHAN TSUN LTOS PA’I GRUB PA YIN PA ‘BA’ ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, RGYU DANG ‘BRAS BU GNYIS KYANG PHAN TSUN LTOS NAS GRUB PA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA,

This next section is meant to explain how not only is it the case that the component parts of things exist in reliance upon each other; but that causes and effects as well exist in this kind of mutual reliance as well.


[3603]
GANG GI PHYIR NA GAL TE RGYU YIS BSKYED PAR BYA BA ‘BRAS BU SKYED PA DE LTA NA SKYED BYED DE RGYU YIN ZHING, GAL TE ‘BRAS BU MI SKYED NA NI SKYED PA DE MED PAS, ‘BRAS BU DE RGYU MED PA CAN DU ‘GYUR RO,,

Here is the reasoning at this point.  Suppose a cause were to give rise to the result that it acts to instigate.  In this case the cause would be that particular trigger here.  If it did not act to trigger a result, then since there was no such trigger the result would come to be one which had no cause.


[3604]
‘BRAS BU YANG NI RGYU YOD PAR GYUR NA, DE LAS SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA DE YI PHYIR RGYU ‘BRAS GNYIS KYANG PHAN TSUN LTOS NAS YOD PA YIN GYI, RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN NO,,

The result as well, from its side, is such that—if there is a cause—then it will grow from that cause.  Thus then the pair of causes & results are things that exist in a mutual dependence—but cannot be said to exist through some nature of their own.


[3605]
CI STE RGYU ‘BRAS RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PAR SEMS NA,

And suppose now that you think to yourself that causes & effects could exist through some essential nature of their own.


[3606]
KYE RGYU’AM ‘BRAS BU GANG LA BRTEN NAS DE GNYIS GANG ZHIG TU ‘GYUR BA GANG ZHIG STE DE GNYIS LAS SNGAR RGYU GANG ZHIG GAM ‘BRAS BU GANG ZHIG ‘GYUR BA DE SMROS SHIG

Goodness!  Whatever cause or effect then could either one of these two rely upon to occur?  Please describe to us which of these two could occur earlier as some cause; and which of them could occur as a result.


[3607]
[f. 243b] DE LTA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA LA RGYU SNGA BA MI RIGS TE, RGYU’I DUS SU RGYU’I LTOS SA ‘BRAS BU DE GRUB DGOS PAS SO,,

If things were like that, and they existed through some nature of their own, then it would be illogical to say that the cause had come earlier—since there would have had to exist a result in the same time period as the cause, for the cause to rely upon.


[3608]
‘BRAS BU SNGA BA YANG MI RIGS TE RGYU MED DU ‘GYUR BAS SO,,

But neither could you say that the result were there before; since then it could have no cause.


[3609]
DE’I PHYIR RGYU DANG ‘BRAS BUR GDAGS PA YANG SHING RTA LTAR PHAN TSUN BRTEN NAS GRUB PAR RIG PAR BYA’I RANG BZHIN LAS GYUR PA NI MA YIN NO,,

As such then we should understand the labelling of causes and effects as being something that occurs in a mutual dependence, as we saw with the wagon.  It is not though something that could occur through any nature of its own.


	[3610]
[VI.169]
Janayati yadi hetuḥ prāpya kāryaṃ tadā te
na janaka phala bhedaḥ syāt tayor aikya śakteḥ,
Pṛthag ayam aviśiṣṭo’hetubhiḥ syāc ca hetur
dvayam idam avadhūyānyāsatī kalpanā ca.

,GAL TE KHYOD KYI RGYU YIS PHRAD NAS
‘BRAS SKYED BYED NA DE YI TSE,
,DE DAG NUS PA GCIG PAS SKYED BYED
‘BRAS BU THA DAD MED ‘GYUR ZHING,
,SO SOR NA NI RGYU ‘DI RGYU MIN
RNAMS DANG KHYAD PAR MED ‘GYUR LA,
,GNYIS PO ‘DI DAG SPANGS NAS RTOG PA
GZHAN YANG YOD PAR ‘GYUR MA YIN,

		Let’s suppose
		You respond that
		The cause acts to
		Trigger the result
		
		Through making contact
		With that result.

		In this case then
		These two would
		Constitute a 
Single force.

If so, the trigger
And the result
Would become
Inseparable.

And suppose
They are
Completely separate.

There wouldn’t be
Anything about the cause
That distinguished it
From things that
Weren’t the cause.

They have given up
These two; and there
Is further no different
Idea which could exist.


[3611]
GZHAN YANG GAL TE RGYU YIS ‘BRAS BU RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYED PAR BYED NA, ‘BRAS BU DANG PHRAD NAS SAM MA PHRAD PAR SKYED PAR BYED,

And suppose, further, that it were indeed the case that a cause could trigger a result through some nature of its own.  Would you say that it triggers the result through making contact with it, or without making contact with it?


[3612]
DE LA GAL TE KHYOD KYI LTAR NA RGYU YIS ‘BRAS BU DANG PHRAD NAS ‘BRAS BU SKYED PAR BYED NA, DE YI TSE RGYU ‘BRAS DE DAG NUS PA GCIG TU ‘GYUR TE, KLUNG DANG RGYA MTSO’I CHU PHRAD PA BZHIN NO,,

Let’s suppose you respond that on this point, the cause acts to trigger the result through making contact with that result.  In this case then these two—the cause and the effect—would constitute a single force; similar to what we see when the waters of a river and the ocean meet with each other.


[3613]
GCIG TU SONG NA ‘DI NI RGYU DANG ‘BRAS BU’O ZHES DBYE BAR MI NUS TE, SKYED BYED DANG ‘BRAS BU THA DAD MED PAR ‘GYUR BA’I PHYIR GANG GIS GANG ZHIG SKYED PAR GYUR,

But if indeed they became one, then we would be unable to distinguish one from the other, saying “This is it the cause, and that is the result.”  That is, the trigger and the result would become inseparable; and then which would you say is triggering the other?


[3614]
CI STE SO SOR TE MA PHRAD PAR SKYED NA NI, ‘BRAS BU’I RGYUR ‘DOD PA ‘DI, DE’I RGYU MIN PA RNAMS DANG SKYED MI SKYED KHYAD PAR MED PAR ‘GYUR TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I SO SO BA RNAMS ‘BREL MED DON GZHAN DU ‘GYUR BA’I PHYIR RO,,

And suppose that the the triggering is done without any contact between them at all; they are completely separate.  In that case there wouldn’t be anything about the thing that you asserted was the cause of the result that distinguished it from things that weren’t the cause, as far as what did the triggering and what didn’t do the triggering.  And that’s because things that exist through some nature of their own, and which are separate from one another, are different entitites which share no connection at all.


[3615]
RGYU ‘BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SMRA BA LA BSKYED BYA SKYED BYED LA PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI RTOG PA GNYIS PO ‘DI DAG SPANGS NAS TE DE MA GTOGS PA’I RTOG PA GSUM PA GZHAN YANG YOD PAR ‘GYUR BA MA YIN PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I RGYUS ‘BRAS BU MI SKYED PA KHO NA’O,,

Those who assert that causes and effects can exist through some nature of their own have given up these two ideas: that these—what is triggered and what does the triggering—could either make contact with each other, or never make contact with each other.  And yet there is further no different, third idea—one other than those two—which could exist.  Thus it can only be the case that a cause which existed through some nature of its own could never trigger a result.


	[3616]
[VI.170]
Phalam atha tava hetur no karotītyato’sat
phalam iti phalahīno’hetuko san na hetuḥ,
Dvayam idam api māyā saṃnibhaṃ yena tasmād
bhavati na mama doṣo laukikāḥ santi cārthāḥ.

,CI STE KHYOD KYI RGYU YIS ‘BRAS BU
SKYED PAR MI BYED DE PHYIR ‘BRAS,
,ZHES BYA YOD MIN ‘BRAS BRAL RGYU NI
RGYU MED CAN ‘GYUR YOD PA’ANG MIN,
,GANG PHYIR ‘DI DAG GNYIS CHAR YANG NI
SGYU MA DANG ‘DRA DE YI PHYIR,
,BDAG LA SKYON DU MI ‘GYUR ‘JIG RTEN
PA YI DNGOS PO RNAMS KYANG YOD,

		As such, this cause
		Of yours could never
		Act to trigger a result.

		And as such,
		There is no such thing
		As something that
You could refer to
		As a “result.”

		Devoid of a result,
		The cause would be
		Without any reason;

		And that is also
Something that
Could never be.

And suppose
It were the case;
These two would also be
Similar to an illusion.

As such,
The problem
That has been raised

		Does not apply
		To me.

		These things
		Of the world
		Do, further, exist.


[3617]
DE’I PHYIR CI STE KHYOD KYI LTAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I RGYU YIS ‘BRAS BU SKYED PAR MI BYED PA DE’I PHYIR ‘BRAS BU ZHES BYA BA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN LA,

As such, given that, this cause which according to you exists through some nature of its own could never act to trigger a result.  And as such, we would have to say that there is no such thing as something you could refer to as a “result” which existed through some nature of its own.


[3618]
RGYU RGYU NYID DU ‘JOG PA’I RGYU [f. 244a] MTSAN NI, ‘BRAS BU ‘BYUNG BA YIN NA GAL TE ‘BRAS BU DANG BRAL BA STE MED PAR YANG RGYU RGYU NYID DU ‘JOG NUS NA NI, DE’I TSE RGYU NI RGYUR ‘JOG PA’I RGYU MTSAN MED PA CAN DU ‘GYUR NA,

The very reason that we can say that any cause is a particular cause is that a result is produced.  And suppose that it were possible to say that a cause was a particular cause devoid of—in the absence of—a result.  In that case, the cause would be established as a cause without any reason for it to be established as such.


[3619]
‘DI NI YOD PA’ANG MIN TE, DE’I PHYIR RGYU ‘BRAS GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN NO,,

That is also something that could never be; as such, these two—causes & effects—are not things that could ever exist through some nature of their own.


[3620]
‘O NA KHYOD KYI LTAR NA JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA,

One may then respond with the following question:

Well then, according to your view, how does all of this really work?


[3621]
RGOL BA GANG GI LTAR NA BSKYED BYA SKYED BYED GNYIS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ‘DOD PA DE LA, RGYUS ‘BRAS BU DANG PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI BRTAG PA BYAS NAS PHYOGS GNYIS KA LA SKYON DU ‘GYUR BA YIN GYI,

So suppose we have some debater here who asserts that these two—what is triggered, and what does the triggering—could exist by definition.  When we proceed from here and examine whether the cause ever makes contact with the result or not, we get problems on both sides.


[3622]
GANG GI PHYIR GANG GI LTAR NA DNGOS PO RNAMS LOG PAR KUN BRTAGS PA’I DBANG GIS BSKYED CING THA SNYAD TZAM GYI RTOG PAS BZHAG PA’I PHYIR, RGYU ‘BRAS ‘DI DAG GNYIS CAR YANG NI SGYU MA DANG ‘DRA BAR RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA YIN ZHING,

And suppose it were the case—suppose it could be—that entities could be triggered in some wrong way, in a way which were only ascribed.  Suppose that they could be established only in terms, through concepts.  In that case, these two—cause & effect—would also both be similar to an illusion; which is to say, things that had never grown through any nature of their own. 


[3623]
RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED KYANG RAB RIB CAN GYIS DMIGS PA’I SGRA {%SKRA} SHAD LA SOGS PA LTAR, THA SNYAD PA’I RNAM PAR RTOG PA TZAM GYIS ‘JOG PA’I YUL DU ‘GYUR BA LA NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I RGYU ‘BRAS KHAS LEN PA LA BKOD PA’I SKYON MTSUNGS PA BSAM DU MED PA NYID DO,,

And so let’s consider an object which is established only through concepts involving terms—something which is like the strand of hair that someone with cataracts perceives, even though it cannot exist through any nature of its own.  It is not at all the case that we are thinking to posit here a problem which would be equivalent, for a person who accepted the idea that cause & effect could exist through some nature of its own.


[3624]
DE YI PHYIR BDAG LA JI SKAD BSHAD PA’I PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI SKYON DU MI ‘GYUR ZHING, ‘JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA YI DNGOS PO MA BRTAGS PAR GRUB PA RGYU ‘BRAS DANG SHING RTA LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYANG YOD PAS THAMS CAD ‘GRUB BO,,

As such, the problem that has been raised—about these things making contact or not making contact—does not apply to me.  All these things that are spoken of in the vernacular of the world, existing without being examined—cause & effect, and wagons, and all the like—do, further, exist.  As such, everything is right there.


[3625]
‘DIR ‘GREL PAS DGAG BYA’I KHYAD PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS DANG RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA SOGS KYI RGYU ‘BRAS LA GNOD PA BRJOD PA, RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PA SGYU MA LTAR SMRA BA LA TSUR LA BZLOG NA MI ‘JUG CES SMRA DGOS PA YIN [f. 244b] GYI,

At this point in the autocommentary, problems are raised with cause & effect which are specified by applying a distinction of something being denied: “those that exist through some nature of their own,” or “those that exist through some essential nature.”  That is, we need to mention phrases like “which do not exist through any nature of their own,” or “which resemble an illusion,” so that the same arguments cannot be turned back upon us.


[3626]
RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG YOD PA GNYIS KYI KHYAD PAR MA PHYED PA’I LAN LTAR SNANG ‘BA’ ZHIG ‘DEBS PA MI BYA’O,,

We should not here though fail to apply the distinction between existing through some nature of its own and existing in general; if we did make such replies, then they would only be mistaken ones.



An argument that
the problems are just the same

[3627]
GSUM PA LA GNYIS, RGYU ‘BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA ‘GOG PA LA SKYON MTSUNGS PA’I RTZOD PA, RANG LA SKYON MI MTSUNGS PA’I LAN BSTAN PA’O,,

This brings us to our third point from above—refuting any other argument on these points.  This we will cover in two parts: argument that the problems are just the same with the denial that cause & effect could exist through any nature of its own; and presenting a response which shows that the problems are not the same with our position.


[3628]
DANG PO NI, ‘DIR RGYU ‘BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA’I LAN DU, KHA CIG ‘DI SKAD DU RGYUS ‘BRAS BU SKYED PA LA PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI BRTAG PA BYED PA NI KHYED LA YANG MTSUNGS SO,,

Someone comes now to respond to our denial that cause & effect could exist through some nature of its own.  This person would say, “This approach of examining whether or not the cause makes contact with the result when it triggers that result applies to you, just the same.”


	[3629]
[VI.171]
Dūṣyaṃ vidūṣayati dūṣaṇam āpya caitad
aprāpya ceti nanu caiṣa tavāpi doṣaḥ,
Svaṃ pakṣam eva vinihaṃsi vadan yadaivaṃ
dūṣyaṃ tadāsi na hi dūṣayituṃ samarthaḥ.

,SUN ‘BYIN ‘DIS SUN DBYUNG BYA PHRAD NAS
‘BYIN NAM MA PHRAD PAR,
,YIN ZHES NYES PA ‘DIR NI KHYOD LA’ANG
‘GYUR BA MA YIN NAM,
,GANG TSE DE SKAD SMRA ZHING RANG PHYOGS
KHO NA RNAM ‘JOMS PA,
,DE TSE KHYOD KYIS SUN DBYUNG SUN NI
‘BYIN PAR NUS MA YIN,

		When you attack
		My position,

		Is it through
		Making contact
		With what it attacks,

		Or without 
		Making contact?

		Doesn’t the problem
		Stated also apply
		To you yourself?

		Let’s consider a case
		Of expressing just such, 
		Which ends up destroying
		Only their own position.

		In this situation,
		It is not the case
		That your attack is
		Anything with the ability

		To do any successful
		Attacking at all.


[3630]
JI LTAR ZHE NA, KHYOD KYI SUN ‘BYIN PA ‘DIS SUN DBYUNG BYA PHRAD NAS SUN ‘BYIN NAM, MA PHRAD PAR SUN ‘BYIN PA YIN ZHES PA’I NYES PA ‘DI NI KHYOD LA’ANG ‘GYUR BA MA YIN NAM STE YIN TE,

And how is that?  Let me ask you a question.  When you attack my position, does your attack attack my position through making contact with what it attacks, or does it attack my position without making contact with what it attacks?  Doesn’t the problem that you have stated also apply to you yourself?  Of course it does!


[3631]
‘DI LTAR GAL TE PHRAD NAS SUN ‘BYIN NA GCIG TU ‘GYUR BAS GANG GIS GANG SUN ‘BYIN,

Suppose you reply that your attack attacks my position by making contact with it.  In that case, the two would have to be the same thing.  And in that case, what would be attacking what?


[3632]
‘ON TE MA PHRAD PAR SUN ‘BYIN NA NI, MA PHRAD PAR MTSUNGS PA THAMS CAD KYIS SUN ‘BYIN PAR ‘GYUR BAS MI RIGS LA, BRTAG PA GNYIS PO ‘DI LAS GZHAN PA’I BRTAG PA GSUM PA YANG MED DO,,

And suppose your attack attacks my position without making any contact with it.  In that case, it would attack every other position in the universe that was also the same, in not making contact with it—and so it just doesn’t make sense.  And furthermore there is no third way of examining the question, beyond these two ways.


[3633]
DE LTAR BYAS NA KHYOD KYI SUN ‘BYIN PA LA SUN DBYUNG BYA SUN ‘BYIN PA’I NUS PA MED PAS, KHYOD KYI SUN ‘BYIN NYID SUN PHYUNG BA YIN PAS SHUGS KYIS NA RGYU ‘BRAS KYI DNGOS PO YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NYID DO ZHES BRTAN PA’I {%both editions say brtan pa’i here} PHYIR SMRAS PA,

As such, we can say that your attack has no power to attack any idea at all to be attacked.  And that means that your attack is itself attacked.  And as such, the implication is that entities of cause & effect are indeed quite precisely things that exist through some nature of their own; we can say it then ever more firmly.


[3634]
GANG GI TSE SUN ‘BYIN LTAR SNANG DE SKAD SMRA ZHING RANG GI PHYOGS KHO NA RNAM PAR ‘JOMS PA DE’I TSE KHYOD KYIS GZHAN GYI LUGS SUN DBYUNG BAR BYA BA SUN NI ‘BYIN PAR NUS PA MA YIN NO,,

And so let’s consider a case when someone is expressing just such a faulty attack, which ends up destroying only their own position.  In this situation, it is not the case that your attack of your opponent’s position is anything with the ability to do any successful attacking at all.


	[3635]
[VI.172]
Jātyantaraiḥ svavacane’pi samaprasaṅgair
nyāyaṃ vinā’pavadase sakalān padārthān,
Yasmāt tato na khalu sajjana saṃmato’si
vaitaṇḍiko’si ca yato’sti na te svapakṣaḥ.

,GANG PHYIR RANG GI TSIG LA’ANG THAL BA
MTSUNGS PA’I LTAG CHOD KYIS,
,RIGS PA MED PAR DNGOS MTHA’ DAG LA
SKUR ‘DEBS DE YI PHYIR,
,KHYOD NI SKYE BO DAM PAS BZHED MI
‘GYUR ZHING GANG GI PHYIR,
,KHYOD LA RANG PHYOGS MED PAS SUN CI
PHYIN DU RGOL BA’ANG YIN,

		What’s the case here
		Is of a statement
		Of necessary consequence
		
		Whose resulting implication
		Applies equally as well.

		This failure of reasoning
		Represents a dismissal
		Of all the entities
		That exist;

		As such,
		Your position
		Could not represent
		The stance of
		The holy ones.

		The fact is that,
		For you,
		Suppose one
		Has no position
		Of their own;

		What then are
		They debating for?


[3636]
GZHAN YANG GANG GI PHYIR NA RGOL BA RANG GI TSIG LA’ANG PHYIR RGOL GZHAN LA ‘PHANGS PA’I THAL BA MTSUNGS PA’I LTAG CHOD KYIS TE [f. 245a] SUN ‘BYIN LTAR SNANG GIS,

Moreover, what’s actually the case here is that one debater is attempting to attack their opponent by using a statement of necessary consequence whose resulting implication—meant to apply to the opponent—applies equally as well to their own expression.  And this makes the attack itself a faulty one.


[3637]
RIGS PA MED PAR DNGOS PO MTHA’ DAG LA SKUR PA ‘DEBS PA DE’I PHYIR KHYOD NI SKYE BO DAM PAS BZHED PA STE ‘DOD PAR MI ‘GYUR RO,,

This failure of reasoning represents a dismissal of all the entities that exist; as such, your position could not represent the stance—or the accepted thinking—of the holy ones.


[3638]
JI LTAR ZHE NA, MA PHRAD PAR SKYED NA MA PHRAD PAR MTSUNGS PA THAMS CAD KYIS SKYED DGOS PA LA, DE DAG GIS SKYED PA MA YIN NO ZHES BYA BA ‘DI LA RIGS PA CI ZHIG YOD,

And how would that be the case?  If something were to trigger another thing without making contact with it, then it would necessarily trigger everything else in the universe that was equivalent, in not making contact with it.  That is, what logic could you ever show to say that things like this didn’t trigger those others?


[3639]
‘DI LTAR KHAB LONG GIS MA PHRAD PA NYID DU RUNG BA’I YUL NA GNAS PA’I LCAGS ‘DREN PAR BYED KYI MA PHRAD PA THAMS CAD NI MI ‘DREN LA, MIG GIS KYANG MA PHRAD PA KHO NAR RUNG BA’I YUL NA GNAS PA’I GZUGS MTHONG GIS, MA PHRAD PA THAMS CAD MI MTHONG BA

Think of a magnet.  It acts to attract iron filings located at an appropriate distance—even though it makes no contact with them; but we cannot go further and say that it attracts everything there is that it makes no contact with.  The eye also sees, exclusively, those forms that it makes no contact with, assuming they are in the appropriate locale.  It does not though see everything there is that it doesn’t make contact with.


[3640]
DE BZHIN DU, RGYUS KYANG MA PHRAD PAR SKYED DU ZIN KYANG MA PHRAD PA THAMS CAD SKYED PAR MI ‘GYUR GYI, ‘BRAS BU RUNG BA KHO NA SKYED PAR BYED DO,,

Just so, even though it is the case that a cause can—without making contact—trigger something, it’s not the case that it would trigger everything there is that it didn’t make contact with.  That is, causes only act to trigger those things that are appropriate to be their results.


[3641]
GZHAN YANG GANG GI PHYIR KHYOD NI SUN CI PHYIN DU RGOL BA NYID DU YANG ‘GYUR TE, RANG GI PHYOGS BZHAG PA DANG BRAL ZHING GZHAN PHYOGS SEL BA TZAM LA ZHUGS PA’I RGOL BA NI SUN CI PHYIN DU RGOL BA PA ZHES BYA NA, KHYOD KYANG DE LTAR GNAS PA’I PHYIR RO ZHE NA,

And moreover, the fact is that there is further perfect debate which we can express to your attack.  Suppose that a debater has no position of their own which they have chosen to take, and they confine themselves only to attempting to overthrow some other’s position.  What then are they debating for; why are they making their attack?  And we would say that you are in the very same situation here.

This then is the position that the other party takes.



How we accept,
nominally, the attack

[3642]
GNYIS PA LA BZHI, RANG GI PHYOGS LA SUN ‘BYIN DANG SGRUB PA ‘THAD TSUL, GZHAN GYI THAL BA MI MTSUNGS PA’I RGYU MTSAN GSAL BAR BSHAD PA, RANG BZHIN MED PA BSGRUB NUS PA BZHIN DU GZHAN GYIS BZLOG STE BSGRUB MI NUS PA, ‘DIR MA BSHAD PA’I SUN ‘BYIN LHAG MA SHES PAR BYED TSUL LO,,

This brings us to the second section from above, which is presenting a response which shows that the problems are not the same with our own position.  Here we proceed in four parts: (1) demonstrating how the attack and the proof utilized in our own position are correct; (2) a clear explanation of the reason why our position is not equivalent to the statement of a necessary implication for the other party; (3) a demonstration of how—so long as we are able to establish that things have no nature of their own—the other party will be unable to prove any denial of our position; and (4) showing how we can understand additional attacks that have not been explained here so far.


[3643]
DANG PO LA GNYIS, THA SNYAD DU GZHAN PHYOGS SUN ‘BYIN PA KHAS LEN TSUL DANG, RANG GI PHYOGS SGRUB PA KHAS LEN TSUL LO, ,DANG PO NI,

The first of these has two topics of its own: how it is that we accept, nominally, the attack of the opposing position; and how it is that we accept the proof of our own position.  Here is the first.


	[3644]
[VI.173]
Aprāpya dūṣayati dūṣaṇam eva yasya
prāpyātha dūṣyam iti vā niyamena pakṣaḥ,
Syāt tasya doṣa udito’yam ayaṃ tu pakṣo
nāstīti naiṣa mama sambhavati prasaṅgaḥ.

,SUN ‘BYIN PAS SUN DBYUNG BYA MA PHRAD
SUN NI ‘BYIN BYED DAM,
,’ON TE [213a] PHRAD NAS YIN ZHES SMRAS ZIN
NYES PA ‘DIR GANG LA,
,NGES PAR PHYOGS YOD DE LA ‘GYUR GYI
BDAG LA PHYOGS ‘DI NI,
,YOD PA MIN PAS THAL BAR ‘GYUR BA
‘DI NI SRID MA YIN,

		First there is
		The problem that
		Has already been raised,

		Of whether the attack
		Serves to attack the idea
		Which is attacked

		Without making contact
		With it, or by making
		Contact with it [f. 213a].

		Here it arises
		With that person who
		Surely has a position;

		We though
		Do not take
		Any such position;

		As such,
		This statement of
		A necessary consequence

		Is not something
		Which is even possible.	


[3645]
‘DI LA BRJOD PAR [f. 245b] BYA STE, SUN ‘BYIN PAS SUN DBYUNG BYA MA PHRAD PAR SUN NI ‘BYIN PAR BYED DAM, ‘ON TE PHRAD NAS SUN ‘BYIN PAR BYED PA YIN ZHES SNGAR SMRAS ZIN PA’I NYES PA NI,

And so here we will describe the point.  Let’s consider first the problem that has already been raised, where we ask the question of whether the attack serves to attack the idea which is attacked without making contact with it, or whether it serves to attack this idea by making contact with it.


[3646]
‘DIR RGOL BA GANG LA PHYOGS YOD PA STE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I DON DAM ‘CHA’ BA DE LA SKYON DU ‘GYUR GYI, 

Here a problem arises with that person who has a position; which is to say, with a person who is asserting that there is an object which could exist through some nature of its own.


[3647]
BDAG LA RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PA’I DON DAM ‘CHA’ BA’I PHYOGS ‘DI NI YOD PA MIN PAS, PHRAD MA PHRAD GNYIS KA LA SKYON BSTAN PA’I THAL BAR ‘GYUR BA ‘DI NI, BDAG LA SRID PA MA YIN TE, NGED KYI LTAR NA SUN ‘BYUNG BYA DANG SUN ‘BYIN PA GNYIS KA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PAR KHAS LEN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

We though do not take any such position wherein we assert that there is any object which could exist through some nature of its own.  As such, this statement of a necessary consequence presenting the problems of both making contact or not making contact is not something which is even possible for us.  And that’s because—according to us—one should accept the idea that neither the idea which is attacked nor the attacking itself is something that could exist through some nature of its own.


[3648]
‘GREL PAR SNGAR GZHAN GYI PHYOGS LA RGYUS ‘BRAS BU SKYED PA LA PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI BRTAG PA BYAS PA’I SKYON RANG LA MI MTSUNGS PA’I RGYU MTSAN DU,

The autocommentary gives a particular reason why the problems that arose earlier, as we investigated whether the other side asserted that—when a cause triggers a result—it did so through making contact with that result, or not, do not apply to ourselves.


[3649]
PHA ROL POS RGYU ‘BRAS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR KHAS BLANGS LA, RANG GIS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA’I SGYU MA BZHIN DU KHAS BLANGS PA BKOD DO,,

And that is that when our opponent has accepted cause & effect that could exist by definition, we present to them our position, that these are things that cannot exist by themselves, through some kind of self-nature; but are, rather, similar to an illusion.


[3650]
SKABS ‘DIR YANG GZHAN LA ‘PHANGS PA’I SKYON RANG LA MI ‘ONG BA’I RGYU MTSAN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA’I PHYIR RO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS RANG LA MI MTSUNGS PA’I RGYU MTSAN NI, PHYOGS GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS MI LEN PA YIN PAR GDON MI ZA BAR ‘DOD PAR BYA’O,,

What’s being said here is “the reason that the problems which are implied by the positions of the others do not apply to ourselves is that these things do not exist through any nature of their own.”  That is, we would beyond any doubt have to say that the reason why these issues do not apply to ourselves in an equivalent way is that we would never accept the idea that either possibility existed through any nature of its own.


[3651]
DE’I PHYIR RTZOD ZLOG LAS,
,GAL TE NGAS DAM BCAS ‘GA’ YOD,
,DES NA NGA LA SKYON DE YOD,
,NGA LA DAM BCA’ MED PAS NA,
,NGA LA SKYON MED KHO NA YIN, 
ZHES SOGS KYIS DAM BCA’ DANG PHYOGS MED PAR GSUNGS PA THAMS CAD KYI DON YANG SNGAR [f. 246a] BZHIN SHES PAR BYA’O,,

This then is why we see, in Stopping All Argument, the following lines—

If I had
Any position at all,
Then I would have
Those problems.

But since I don’t
Have any position,
I am completely faultless.

And as always, we need to understand as we described it earlier on the meaning of all these kinds of statements that we have no position, or stance that we take.


[3652]
JI SKAD DU RGYAL BA’I YUM LAS, TSE DANG LDAN PA RAB ‘BYOR, CI SKYES PA’I CHOS KYIS MA SKYES PA’I THOB PA ‘THOB PAR ‘GYUR RAM, ‘ON TE MA SKYES PA’I CHOS KYIS MA SKYES PA’I THOB PA ‘THOB PAR ‘GYUR,

The Mother of the Victorious Ones puts it this way—

O junior monk, Subhuti.  Is it the case that things which have started attain the attainment of not having started?  Or is it that things which have not started attain the attainment of not having started?


[3653]
RAB ‘BYOR GYIS SMRAS PA, TSE DANG LDAN PA SH’A RI’I BU KHO BO NI SKYES PA’I CHOS KYIS MA SKYES PA’I THOB PA ‘THOB PAR MI ‘DOD LA, MA SKYES PAS KYANG MA SKYES PA’I THOB PA ‘THOB PAR MI ‘DOD DO,,

	And then Subhuti replied,

O junior monk Shariputra; it is not that I agree to the idea that things which have started have attained the attainment of not having started.  And neither is it the case that I agree that things which have not started have attained the attainment of not having started.


[3654]
SH’A RI’I BUS SMRAS PA, TSE DANG LDAN PA RAB ‘BYOR YANG CI THOB PA MED CING MNGON PAR RTOGS PA MED DAM,

Shariputra said then,

O junior monk Subhuti, would you further say that there is no attaining anything, and that there is no state of realization?


[3655]
RAB ‘BYOR GYIS SMRAS PA, TSE DANG LDAN PA SH’A RI’I BU THOB PA YANG YOD MNGON PAR RTOGS PA YANG YOD MOD KYI, GNYIS KYI TSUL GYIS NI MA YIN NO,,

	And Subhuti replied,

O junior monk Shariputra, it certainly is the case that there is attainment, and that there is realization.  It’s just that they don’t exist in the way of duality.


[3656]
TSE DANG LDAN PA SH’A RI’I BU THOB PA DANG MNGON PAR RTOGS PA NI ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU YIN LA, RGYUN DU ZHUGS PA DANG, LAN CIG PHYIR ‘ONG BA DANG, PHYIR MI ‘ONG BA DANG, DGRA BCOM PA DANG, RANG SANGS RGYAS DANG, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ YANG ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU YIN GYI,

O junior monk Shariputra, attainment and realization are things that exist in the vernacular of the world.  We can also say that entering the stream; and returning but once; and never returning; and the state of an enemy destroyer; and that of a self-made buddha, and the bodhisattva are all things that exist in the vernacular of the world.


[3657]
DON DAM PAR NI THOB PA MED CING MNGON PAR RTOGS PA MED DO ZHES RGYA CHER GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

In an ultimate sense though, there is no attainment, and there is no realization.

We see a great many such statements in scripture.


[3658]
DE LA MA SKYES PA’I THOB PA ‘THOB PAR MI ‘DOD DO ZHES PA YAN CHAD KYIS, THOB BYA THOB BYED GNYIS KYI BTAGS DON BTZAL BA NA THOB PA MED PAR ‘GYUR BAS, DE LTAR DPYAD PA’I TSE PHYOGS GNYIS KYI SGO NAS THOB BYA ‘THOB PA BKAG CING,

The part here up to “I disagree that there is an attainment of an attainment of not having started,” is meant to express that—when we go looking for what it is that was given the name, for both what we attain and the means by which we attain it, we find that there  is no attainment at all.  As such, when we undertake this kind of examination, we end up denying both what is attained, and the attaining, from both points of view.


[3659]
GNYIS SU DPYAD PA’I THOB BYA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I DNGOS PO MED PA LA MI RIGS PA’I PHYIR, MA BRTAGS PAR ‘JIG RTEN [f. 246b] GYI THA SNYAD DU THOB PAR KHAS BLANGS PA NI, ‘THOB PA YANG YOD CES PA NAS GNYIS KYI TSUL GYIS NI MA YIN NO, ZHES PAS BSTAN TE, THOB PA ZHES PA NI THOB BYA THOB PA DANG MNGON PAR RTOGS PA LA BYA’O,,

Now it would be illogical to say that something attained which we examined in the two different ways could not exist with an entity that existed through some nature of its own.  As such, accepting the idea of an attainment without examination—in the vernacular of the world—is what’s being indicated from the point of saying that there is an attainmnent, up through saying that it is not something that is there in either of the two ways.  That is, when we speak of an “attainment,” we are referring to the attainment of an attainment, and a realization.


[3660]
DE GNYIS DON DAM PAR MED LA THA SNYAD DU KHAS LEN PA DE BZHIN DU, SUN ‘BYIN BYED KYIS SUN DBYUNG BYA DON DAM PAR SUN MI ‘BYIN KYANG THA SNYAD DU SUN ‘BYIN PAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

What we accept then is that neither of these could exist in an ultimate way; but that they exist in a nominal manner.  Just so, we should understand that even though it is not the case that what does the attacking ever succeeds in attacking what is attacked in any ultimate way, it does accomplish the attack in a nominal manner.



How we accept
the proof of
our own position

[3661]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second point from above, which is how it is that we accept the proof of our own position.


	[3662]
[VI.174]
Dṛṣṭā yathā grahaṇakādiṣu te viśeṣā
āditya maṇḍala gatāḥ pratibimbake’pi,
Nāprāpya cāpya ca raviṃ pratibimba jātaṃ

		Let’s consider how you
		Can see a reflection,
		
		And based on that
		You can observe
		Certain features

		That are present in
		The disk of the sun.
		
		When there is an eclipse
		Of that sun or
		Something else of the like,
		
		You can watch it.

		Not right that the sun
		Either does make

		Actual contact 
		With the reflection,
		Or not.

		But something
		Did occur, based on it,
		If only nominally.


[VI.175]
Yadvad vyalīkam api tat svamukhopaśobhā-

Hetoḥ svasādhyagatam ityupapattihīnāt
prajñā mukhoparacanaṃ prati dṛṣṭa śakteḥ.

,MI BDEN BZHIN DU’ANG RANG GI BYAD BZHIN

		It may not be
		The real thing,

		To establish the beauty
		Of the original object

		And we should
Understand that we

Are undertaking
