11) The emptiness that can never be given up


	[3828]
[VI.196]
Avakāro’vakiraṇaṃ choraṇaṃ hi nirucyate,
Na tyāgo’navakāras tu choraṇaṃ yan na kasyacit.

,DOR BA CES BYA ‘THOR BA DANG,
,’BOR BA LA NI NGES PAR BRJOD,
,DOR MED GTONG PA MED PA STE,
,’GA’ YANG DOR MED GANG YIN PA’O,

		The expression “given up”
		Can be used both
		In the sense of
		“Throwing off”
		And “abandoning.”

		“Never given up”
		Means “cannot
		Be sent off”:

A reference to
No kind of thing		
		That could ever 
		Be relinquished.


[3829]
DOR BA ZHES BYA BA NI ‘THOR BA DANG ‘BOR BA LA NI NGES PAR BRJOD LA, DOR BA DE MED PA NI PHAR LA GTONG BA MED PA STE RANG GI NGO BO ‘GA’ DANG DUS ‘GAR YANG DOR DU MED PA STE DOR DU MI RUNG BA THEG CHEN [f. 256b] GANG YIN PA’O,,

Now the expression “given up” can be used both in the sense of “throwing off” and “abandoning.”  And when we say “it is never given up,” what we are saying is that it cannot be sent off, away from us.  Which is to say, there is no kind of essential nature to things, nor any particular time, where and when this could ever be relinquished; and this is a reference to the greater way, which is never something that we should ever give up.


	[3830]
[VI.197]
Tenaivānavakāreṇa yā tasyaiva hi śūnyatā,
Śūnyatānavakārākhyā tasmād eṣā nirucyate.

,DOR BA MED PA DE NYID KYIS,
,DE NYID STONG PA NYID GANG YIN,
,DE DE’I PHYIR NA DOR MED PA,
,STONG PA NYID CES BYA BAR BRJOD,

		It is an essential
		Never being given up;

		The fact of the emptiness
		Of this particular object
		Was then referred to
		As emptiness:

		This is because of
		Its being something
		That we should
		Never relinquish.		


[3831]
DOR BA MED PA NI DOR BA MED PA DE NYID KYI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA DE NYID KYI STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, DOR BA MED PA STONG PA NYID CES BYA BAR BRJOD DE, STONG NYID DE DOR BA MED PA’I RANG BZHIN YIN PA DE’I PHYIR NA’O,,

This quality of never being given up is an essential never being given up which is empty of existing through any nature of its own.  The fact of the emptiness of this particular object was then referred to as “the emptiness of never being given up”; and this is because this particular kind of emptiness has a nature of being something that we should never relinquish.



12) The emptiness of any nature

	[3832]
[VI.198]
Śikṣaiḥ pratyeka buddhaiś ca bodhisatvais Tathāgataiḥ,
Svabhāvaḥ saṃskṛtādīnāṃ yato naiva kṛtas tataḥ.

,’DUS BYAS LA SOGS NGO BO NYID,
,GANG PHYIR SLOB MA RANG SANGS RGYAS,
,RGYAL SRAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS RNAMS KYIS,
,MA MDZAD DE’I PHYIR ‘DUS BYAS LA,

	The essential nature
	Of produced things
	And the like has been
	Named their “very nature.”

	And why is it so?
	The essential nature
	Of produced things
	And such is not something
	That was ever created

	By the students,
	Or self-made Buddhas,
	Or children of the Victors,
	Or Those Who Have Gone
	That Way.  The essential nature


[VI.199]
Svabhāvaḥ saṃskṛtādīnāṃ prakṛtitvena kathyate,
Tayaiva śūnyatā tasyā yā sā prakṛti śūnyatā.

,SOGS PA RNAMS KYI NGO BO NYID,
,RANG BZHIN NYID DU BSNYAD PA STE,
,DE NYID KYIS DE STONG NYID GANG,
,DE NI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID,

		Of produced things
		And the like
Has been named 
Their “very nature.”

This very thing
Is empty of itself;
		
		And this fact then
		Is the emptiness
		Of any nature.


[3833]
‘DUS BYAS LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI NGO BO CHOS NYID NI, RANG BZHIN NYID DU BSNYAD CING BRJOD PA STE,

The essential nature or essence of produced things and the like has been named their “very nature.”


[3834]
RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA ‘DUS BYAS LA, SOGS PA RNAMS KYI NGO BO CHOS NYID NI, SLOB MA NYAN THOS DANG, RANG SANGS RGYAS DANG, RGYAL SRAS BYANG SEMS DANG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS KYIS MA MDZAD CING, DE GSAL BAR BYED PA YIN LA, GDOD MA NAS DE DAG GI GSHIS SU GNAS PA DE’I PHYIR RO,,

And why is it so—what is the reason?  The very nature or essential nature of produced things and such is not something that was ever created or revealed by the “students” (referring to the listeners); or by the self-made buddhas; or by the “children of the Victors” (the bodhisattvas), or by Those Who Have Gone That Way.  And that’s because these have been the very way of all things for time with no beginning.


[3835]
RANG BZHIN DE NYID DE NYID KYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID DO,,

This very thing—this nature of things—is empty of existing in & of itself; which is to say, through some essential nature of its own.  And this fact then is the emptiness of any nature.


[3836]
‘O NA DON ‘DI STONG PA NYID STONG PA NYID KYI SKABS SU YANG BRJOD PA MA YIN NAM ZHE NA,

One may ask, “Wasn’t this point already expressed, when we discussed the emptiness of emptiness?”


[3837]
BDEN MOD ‘ON KYANG SKABS SNGA MAR NI PHYI NANG GI CHOS RNAMS KYI STONG NYID DE, DE KHO NA NYID ‘JAL BA’I RIGS SHES KYIS GRUB PAS BDEN PAR GRUB BAM SNYAM PA BSAL BA’I PHYIR YIN LA,

That is indeed the case, but in that previous instance we were referring to the emptiness of inner and outer entities.  And that was for the purpose of clarifying the question that might have come up, where someone asks, “Wouldn’t it be the case that if something were established by a logical perception which were holding suchness under consideration, wouldn’t that thing then exist in truth?”


[3838]
‘DIR NI SUS KYANG MA BYAS PAR GSHIS SU GRUB PA’I RANG BZHIN YIN NA, BDEN PAR GRUB BAM SNYAM PA BSAL BA’I PHYIR GSUNGS PAS MI ZLOS SO,,

Here though the kind of nature being considered is one in which there has been a natural existence, for all time—one which was never put together, by anyone at all.  And the reason we were mentioning that here was to prevent the possibility that someone might wonder whether this sort of nature might exist in truth.  As such, there is no redundancy here.


[3839]
DOGS PA’I RGYU MTSAN ‘DI GNYIS KA CHOS NYID LA YOD KYANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA ‘GOG NUS PA MI ‘GAL BA ‘DI SHES NA, DON DAM BDEN PA BLO GANG GIS KYANG MI RTOGS PAR ‘DZIN PA’I LOG PAR RTOG PA RNAMS LDOG PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

Both of the reasons why a person might hold some doubts here apply to a real nature of things; but there is no contradiction between them with reference to their ability to deny that things could exist in truth.  Once you realize this point, you can stop the wrong idea which questions whether or not ultimate reality is something that any state of mind could ever realize.



The emptiness of all things

[3840]
BZHI PA LA GSUM, [f. 257a] CHOS THAMS CAD STONG PA NYID DANG, RANG GI MTSAN NYID STONG PA NYID DANG, MI DMIGS PA DANG DNGOS PO MED PA’I NGO BO NYID STONG PA NYID BSHAD PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

Which brings us to our fourth point from above: an explanation of the four starting with the emptiness of all things.  Here we have three sections: an explanation of the emptiness of all things; an explanation of the emptiness of its own quality; and an explanation of both the emptiness of not seeing anything and the emptiness of true nature, beyond all things.



13) The emptiness of all things


	[3841]
[VI.200]
Dhātavo’ṣṭādaśa sparśāḥ ṣaṭ tajjā vedanāś ca ṣaṭ,
Rūpiṇo’rūpiṇo dharmāḥ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtās tathā.

,KHAMS BCO BRGYAD DANG RE {%REG?} DRUG DANG,
,DE LAS BYUNG BA’I TSOR DRUG DANG,
,GZUGS CAN GZUGS CAN MIN DE BZHIN,
,’DUS BYAS ‘DUS MA BYAS CHOS RNAMS,

	There are the eighteen
	Categories of existence;
	The six forms of contact;
	And the six forms of feeling
	That arise from these.

	There is everything
	That possesses form,
	And everything
	Which does not
	Possess such form.

	In the same way,
	We have those entities
	Which are produced things,

	And those which exist
	But which are not produced.


[3842]
CHOS THAMS CAD NI MIG SOGS RTEN DBANG PO’I KHAMS DRUG DANG, MIG GI RNAM SHES SOGS BRTEN PA RNAM SHES KYI KHAMS DRUG DANG, GZUGS LA SOGS PA DMIGS PA YUL GYI KHAMS DRUG STE KHAMS BCO BRGYAD DANG,

When we say “all things,” what are we referring to?  First there are the six categories of the sense powers: the bases of perception represented by the eye and so on.  Then there are the six categories of consciousness, meaning the consciousness of the eye and such.  Next we have the six objects: the objects of perception represented by visual form and the rest.  This then makes a total of eighteen categories of existence.


[3843]
MIG GI ‘DUS TE REG PA NAS YID KYI ‘DUS TE REG PA’I BAR REG PA DRUG DANG, REG PA DE DRUG LAS BYUNG BA’I TSOR BA DRUG DANG,

Along with that, we have the six forms of contact, referring to contact involving the eye up to contact involving the thoughts.  And then there are the six forms of feeling that arise from these six types of contact.


[3844]
GZUGS CAN DANG GZUGS CAN MIN PA NYID DANG, DE BZHIN DU ‘DUS BYAS DANG, ‘DUS MA BYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS SO,,

And then finally we have the divisions into everything that possesses form, and everything in existence which does not possess such form.  In the same way, we have those entitites which are produced things, and finally those entities which exist but which are not produced.


	[3845]
[VI.201]
Śūnyatā sarva dharmāṇāṃ yā teṣāṃ tair viyuktatā,
Rūpaṇāder abhāvo yaḥ sā svalakṣaṇa śūnyatā.

[VI.201a]
,CHOS DE DAG NI THAMS CAD KYI,
,DE DAG GIS DBEN STONG NYID GANG,

		All of these
		Various existing entities
		Possess an emptiness

		Where they are devoid
		Of their own.


[3846]
CHOS DE DAG THAMS CAD NI DE DAG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS DBEN PA’I STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA ‘DI NI, CHOS THAMS CAD KYI STONG PA NYID DO,,

Now all of these various existing entities possess an emptiness where they are devoid of existing through any essential nature of their own.  This then is the emptiness of all things.



The emptiness of its own quality, in brief

[3847]
GNYIS PA LA GSUM, MDOR BSTAN, RGYAS PAR BSHAD, DON BSDU BA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

Which brings us to our third section—an explanation of the emptiness of its own quality.  Here we have three parts: a briefer explanation; a more detailed explanation; and then a concluding summary.



14) The emptiness of its own quality


	[3848]
[VI.201b]
,GZUGS RUNG LA SOGS DNGOS MED GANG,
,DE NI RANG MTSAN STONG PA NYID,

		Those things
		That can be pointed to
		As being form,

		And all the rest
		Which lack being
Things, is the emptiness
Of a thing’s own quality.


[3849]
GZUGS PHUNG GI MTSAN NYID NI GZUGS SU RUNG BA DANG LA SOGS PAS BSDUS PA RNAM MKHYEN GYI BAR GYI KUN BYANG GI CHOS RNAMS KYI RANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID DNGOS PO STE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA GANG YIN PA DE NI RANG GI MTSAN NYID STONG PA NYID DO,,

Here next we consider those things that can be pointed to as being form (which is in fact the definition of “form”), and “all the rest”—which includes all of those entities up to omniscience itself, whether they be on the negative side of things, or the enlightened side of things.  These are all things which lack any quality of being “things” in the sense of possessing, each one, their own quality; which is to say, they have no quality of existing through some essential nature of their own.  This then is the emptiness of a thing’s own quality.



Emptiness of own quality
related to the original condition

[3850]
GNYIS PA LA GSUM, GZHI’I CHOS DANG, LAM GYI CHOS DANG, ‘BRAS BU’I CHOS KYI RANG GI MTSAN NYID DO, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us to our second part, of a more detailed explanation.  We proceed in three sections: the own quality of things related to the time of the original condition; the own quality of things related to the time of the path; and the own quality of things related to the time of the result.


	[3851]
[VI.202]
Rūpaṇālakṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ vedanānubhavātmikā,
Nimittodgrahaṇaṃ saṃjñā saṃskārās tv abhisaṃskṛtiḥ.

,GZUGS NI GZUGS RUNG MTSAN NYID CAN,
,TSOR BA MYONG BA’I BDAG NYID CAN,
,’DU SHES MTSAN MAR ‘DZIN PA STE,
,’DU BYED MNGON PAR ‘DU BYED PA’O,

		What we accept
		Is that the “own quality”
		That form possesses
	
	Is that it can be pointed to
	As being form.

	Feelings consist of
That entity which
Possesses a self-nature
Of experience.

Discrimination
Holds to features;

And other factors
Act to bring together.


[VI.203]
Viṣayaṃ prati vijñaptir vijñānasya svalakṣaṇam,
Duḥkha svalakṣaṇāḥ skandhā dhātvātmāśīviṣaṃ matam.

,YUL LA SO SOR RNAM RIG PA,
,RNAM SHES RANG GI MTSAN NYID DO,
,PHUNG PO SDUG BSNGAL RANG MTSAN NYID,
,KHAMS KYI BDAG NYID SBRUL GDUG ‘DOD,

	The own quality
	For consciousness
	Consists of being

	A state of mind
	Which perceives
	Individual objects.

	The own quality of
	The parts to the person
	Is suffering; and

	The self-nature
Or own quality
Of the categories
Of existence is that
They are poisonous snakes.


[3852]
YANG GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI RANG GI MTSAN NYID CI YIN ZHE NA,

“What then,” one may ask, “is their ‘own quality,’ for things like form and the rest?”


[3853]
GZUGS NI GZUGS SU RUNG BA’I MTSAN NYID CAN TE, DE YANG MDO LAS, DGE SLONG DAG GZUGS [f. 257b] SU YOD CING GZUGS SU RUNG BA DE’I PHYIR GZUGS NYE BAR LEN PA’I PHUNG PO ZHES BYA’O, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

The “own quality” that form, for example, possesses is that it can be pointed to as being form.  As sutra puts it, “O monks, when something exists as form, or can be pointed to as form, then we refer to it as the ‘part to the person taken on which is form’.”


[3854]
RANG GI MTSAN NYID ‘DI RNAMS DON LDOG YIN PA’I NGES PA MED PAR RANG RANG GI RANG BZHIN MTSON PA’I GTZO BO SMOS PA’O,,

Now there is no certainty, with these “own qualities,” that they will constitute the entirety of the opposite of all that the particular thing is not; rather, what we are referring to here is the primary attribute that represents their nature.


[3855]
TSOR BA NI BDE SDUG BTANG SNYOMS KYI MYONG BA’I BDAG NYID CAN NO,,

Feelings consist of that entity which possesses a self-nature of the experience of pleasure, pain, or neutral feeling.


[3856]
‘DU SHES NI PHYI’I MTSAN MA SNGO SER SOGS DANG, NANG GI MTSAN MA BDE SDUG SOGS KYI KHYAD PAR ‘DZIN PA STE, MTSAN MA NI YUL GYI SPU RIS SO,,

Discrimination is a state of mind which holds to outer features such as blue, yellow, or the like; and also to inner features such as pleasure or pain.  And when we say “feature” here, what we are referring to is a quality which allows us to make distinctions between different objects.


[3857]
‘DU BYED NI ‘DUS BYAS MNGON PAR ‘DU BYED PA STE PHUNG PO GZHAN BZHI LAS GZHAN PA’O,,

And then when we say “other factors,” what we are referring to are factors that act to bring together produced things, and are not included into the other four parts to the person.


[3858]
GZUGS SGRA LA SOGS PA’I YUL SO SO LA SO SOR RNAM PAR RIG PA NI, RNAM SHES KYI RANG GI MTSAN NYID DO,,

The “own quality” for consciousness consists of being a state of mind which perceives individual objects: the individual entities of visual form, sound, and all the rest.


[3859]
PHUNG PO’I RANG GI MTSAN NYID SDUG BSNGAL DANG KHAMS RNAMS KYI BDAG NYID DE RANG GI MTSAN NYID NI, SBRUL GDUG PAS GZHAN LA BZUNG NAS GNOD PA SKYED PA DANG ‘DRA BA SEMS CAN RNAMS ‘KHOR BAR ‘DZIN PA’O,,

The “own quality” of the parts to the person is suffering; and the self-nature or “own quality” of the categories of existence is that they are poisonous snakes, meaning that when any other being tries to grasp them, they cause harm to that being.  Which is to say, they keep living beings turning inside this wheel of pain.


	[3860]
[VI.204]
Āyadvāratayoktāni Buddhair āyatanāni ca,
Yaḥ pratītya samutpādaḥ sa sāmagrī svalakṣaṇaḥ.

,SKYE MCHED RNAMS NI SANGS RGYAS KYIS,
,SKYE BA’I SGOR GYUR NYID DU GSUNGS,
,RTEN CING ‘BREL BAR ‘GYUR BA GANG,
,DE NI ‘DU ‘PHROD MTSAN NYID DO,

		The doors of sense
		Were described
		By the Buddhas as
		
		The very doors
		For growing.

		Its own quality for
That thing we refer to as
		A “dependent relationship”

		Is the coming together
		And contact.


[3861]
SKYE MCHED RNAMS NI SANGS RGYAS KYIS SDUG BSNGAL ‘BYUNG ZHING, SKYE BA’I SGOR GYUR PA NYID DU GSUNGS SO,,

The doors of sense were described by the Buddhas as the very doors through which suffering grows, or arises.


[3862]
DE GSUM NI ‘KHOR BA’I PHUNG KHAMS DANG SKYE MCHED LA DGONGS PA’O,,

Thus then these three were intended to refer to the heaps, the categories, and the doors of sense for the circle of suffering.


[3863]
RTEN CING ‘BREL PAR ‘BYUNG BA GANG YIN PA DE’I RANG GI MTSAN NYID NI RGYU RKYEN GYI ‘DU ‘PHROD KYIS RAB TU PHYE BA’O,,

And then that thing which we refer to as the occurrence of things through a dependent relationship is distinguished by the coming together and contact of causes & conditions, as its own quality.



Emptiness of own quality
related to the time of the path

[3864]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second point from above: the own quality of things related to the time of the path.


	[3865]
[VI.205]
Dāna pāramitā tyāgaḥ śīlaṃ cādāhalakṣaṇam,
Akopa lakṣaṇā kṣāntiḥ vīryasya tvanavadyatā.

,GTONG BA SBYIN PA’I PHA ROL PHYIN,
,TSUL KHRIMS GDUNG MED MTSAN NYID BZOD,
,KHRO MED MTSAN NYID BRTZON ‘GRUS KYI,
,KHA NA MA THO MED NYID DO,

		The perfection of giving
		Is giving away.

		The own quality
		For the ethical life
		Is turning away
		From the torment.

		The own quality
		Of patience is
		An absence of anger;

		And for joyful effort
		It is that free
		Of disreputable actions.


[3866]
SBYIN PA’I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’I MTSAN NYID NI, LUS DANG LONGS SPYOD DGE BA’I RTZA BA YONGS SU GTONG BA’I SEMS PA’O,,

The own quality for the perfection of giving is that movement of the mind where we want to give away, entirely, our own body; our possessions; and our roots of virtue.


[3867]
TSUL KHRIMS KYI MTSAN NYID NI NYON MONGS KYI GDUNG BA LAS DE MED PA’I BSIL BA THOB PA’O,,

The own quality for the ethical life is that we attain the cooling sensation of turning away from the torment of the negative emotions, and then having no more of them.


[3868]
BZOD PA’I MTSAN NYID NI KHRO BA MED PA STE DE LA SEMS KYI BSRAN ‘DZUGS NUS PA’O,,

The own quality of patience is an absence of anger; which is to say, the ability to place ones mind into a state of forbearance.


[3869]
BRTZON [f. 258a] ‘GRUS KYI MTSAN NYID NI, KHA NA MA THO BA MED PA’I DGE BA YONGS SU ‘DZIN PA LA SPRO BA NYID DO,,

The own quality of joyful effort is that perfect joy one feels about maintaining ones virtue, free of any disreputable actions.


	[3870]
[VI.206]
Saṃgraha lakṣaṇaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñā cāsaṅga lakṣaṇā,
Ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ vai lakṣaṇaṃ kathitaṃ tvidam.

,BSAM GTAN SDUD PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN,
,SHES RAB CHAGS MED MTSAN NYID DE,
,PHA ROL PHYIN PA DRUG RNAMS KYI,
,MTSAN NYID ‘DI DAG YIN PAR BRJOD,

		Meditation possesses
		Its own quality
		Of gathering together;

		The own quality of wisdom
Is a freedom from craving.

Thus the own qualities
Of the six different perfections
Have been described as
Being these ways.


[3871]
BSAM GTAN GYI MTSAN NYID NI DGE BA’I CHOS THAMS CAD SDUD PA’I PHYIR DU DGE BA’I DMIGS PA LA SEMS RTZE GCIG TU GNAS PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NO,,

The own quality of meditation is that it possesses its own quality of being able to keep ones mind single-pointedly on a virtuous object, in order to gather together each and every virtuous quality.


[3872]
SHES RAB KYI MTSAN NYID NI CHAGS PA MED PA STE, MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PAR BGROD PA’I PHYIR DU, CHOS ‘GA’ LA YANG CHAGS PA STE BDEN ZHEN MED PA STE ‘GOG PAR BYED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

The own quality of wisdom is a freedom from craving; that is, in order to help us to travel to the state of nirvana, it functions to stop us from believing in some real existence—which is itself a craving for any entity at all.


[3873]
DE LTAR NA PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA DRUG PO RNAMS KYI MTSAN NYID NI, SNGAR BSHAD PA ‘DI DAG YIN PAR MDO LAS BRJOD DO,,

Thus it is then that the own qualities of the six different perfections have been described in the sutras, as being the ways that we have now explained.


	[3874]
[VI.207]
Dhyānāni cāpramāṇāni ye cārūpyāś tathā pare,
Akopa lakṣaṇā eta uktāḥ samyak prajānatā.

,BSAM GTAN RNAMS DANG TSAD MED DANG,
,DE BZHIN GZHAN GANG GZUGS MED PA,
,DE DAG YANG DAG [214b] MKHYEN PA YIS,
,MI ‘KHRUG MTSAN NYID CAN DU GSUNGS,

		Then there are the
		Concentration levels
		And the immeasurables;

		And just so, other items:
		Those for the formless realm [f. 214b].

		These are what that
		Being of Perfect Knowledge
		Described as states

		Whose own quality was
		Beyond being disturbed.


[3875]
BSAM GTAN DANG PO LA SOGS PA BSAM GTAN BZHI RNAMS DANG, BYAMS PA TSAD MED LA SOGS PA TSAD MED BZHI DANG,

Let’s consider next the following list.  We start with the four concentration levels of the first concentration level and so on.  And then there are the four immeasurables, of immeasurable love and the rest.


[3876]
DE BZHIN DU SNGA MA GNYIS LAS GZHAN GANG NAM MKHA’ MTHA’ YAS LA SOGS PA GZUGS MED PA’I SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG PA BZHI PO DE DAG ,YANG DAG MKHYEN PA YI SANGS RGYAS KYIS MI ‘KHRUG PA KHRO BA MED PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN DU GSUNGS TE, DE RNAMS NI KHRO BA SPANGS PAS ‘THOB PA’I PHYIR RO,,

Just so we have items that are other than the two just mentioned; for example, those four states of balanced meditation for the formless realm levels of infinite space and the rest.  These are what the Buddha, that Being of Perfect Knowledge, described as states whose own quality was beyond being disturbed—that is, free of all anger.  And that’s because these levels are attained by eliminating, within ourselves, anger.


	[3877]
[VI.208]
Saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyā nairyāṇika svalakṣaṇāḥ,
Śūnyatāyā viviktatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nopalambhanāt.

,BYANG CHUB PHYOGS CHOS SUM CU BDUN,
,NGES PAR ‘BYUNG BYED RANG MTSAN NYID,
,STONG PA NYID KYI MTSAN NYID NI,
,DMIGS PA MED PAS RNAM DBEN NYID,

		The own quality
		Of the 37 elements
		Of enlightenment

		Is those points
		Which produce 
		Our release.

		Its own quality
		For emptiness
		Is that very quality
		
Of being devoid,
		No longer focusing.


[3878]
BYANG CHUB KYI PHYOGS KYI CHOS SUM CU RTZA BDUN GYI RANG GI MTSAN NYID NI, GANG DU NGES PAR ‘BYUNG SA THAR PAR NGES PAR ‘BYUNG BAR BYED PA’O,,

The own quality of the 37 elements of enlightenment is described as those points which produce our release: at which we attain the level of release—that is, freedom.


[3879]
RNAM PAR THAR PA’I SGO STONG PA NYID KYI MTSAN NYID NI BDEN ‘DZIN GYI DMIGS GTAD KYI RTOG PA’I DRI MAS MA SBAGS PA’I PHYIR RNAM PAR DBEN PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NO,,

Its own quality for the door to freedom of emptiness is that very quality of being devoid, in the sense that we are no longer defiled by the stench of misperception: the manner in which holding that things are real focuses upon its objects.


	[3880]
[VI.209]
Śāntatā tvanimittasya duḥkhāmohas tu lakṣaṇam,
Tṛtīyasya vimokṣāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tu vimocanam.

,MTSAN MA MED PA ZHI NYID DE,
,GSUM PA’I MTSAN NYID SDUG BSNGAL DANG,
,GTI MUG MED RNAM THAR RNAMS KYI,
,MTSAN NYID RNAM PAR GROL BYED PA’O,

		That beyond all signs
		Has its own quality
		Of peace;

		Its own quality
		For the third
		Is a freedom from
		Suffering and
		Dark ignorance.

		The own quality
		For the freedoms
		Is that they act
		To liberate us.


[3881]
RNAM PAR THAR PA’I SGO MTSAN MA MED PA NI MTSAN MA MA DMIGS PA’I SGO NAS ZHI BA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NO,,

The door to freedom beyond all signs has its own quality of peace, in the sense of no longer perceiving signs.


[3882]
RNAM PAR THAR PA’I SGO [f. 258b] GSUM PA SMON PA MED PA’I MTSAN NYID NI, ‘DU BYED SDUG BSNGAL GYI BDAG NYID CAN RNAMS LA SDUG BSNGAL DU YANG DAG PAR RJES SU LTA BA DANG, DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA’I SHES RAB KYIS ‘DU BYED KYI YIN LUGS LA LTA BA NA, SRID PA’I PHUN TSOGS LA MI SMON ZHING,

And then here is its own quality for the third of the doors to freedom: the one beyond all aspirations.  Here first we recognize, perfectly, that factors which have a self-nature of suffering are indeed suffering.  And when we use wisdom which realizes the suchness of things to look into how it is that factors exist, we no longer have any aspiration for the good things of the cycle of pain.


[3883]
‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA’I GO ‘PHANG LA YANG BDEN PAR ‘DZIN PA’I SGO NAS SMON PA MED PA’I PHYIR NA, SDUG BSNGAL DANG GTI MUG MED PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NO,,

Moreover, we have no further aspiration for the state of going beyond the world—in the sense of holding this to exist in some real way.  As such, this door displays, as its own nature, a freedom from both suffering and dark ignorance.


[3884]
RNAM PAR THAR PA BRGYAD PO RNAMS KYI MTSAN NYID NI, SNYOMS ‘JUG GI SGRIB PA LAS RNAM PAR GROL BAR BYED PA’O,,

The own quality for the eight freedoms is that they act to liberate us from impediments to balanced meditation.


[3885]
RNAM PAR THAR PA BRGYAD NI NANG LA GZUGS CAN DU ‘DU SHES PA MA BSHIG PAR PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS LA LTA BA DANG, NANG LA ‘DU SHES DE BSHIG NAS PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS LA LTA BA’I RNAM THAR GNYIS NI, SPRUL PA LA GEGS BYED PA’I SGRIB PA’I GNYEN PO’O,,

Within the eight types of freedom, we have the freedom where we look at outer forms without having disassembled our conceiving of things possessed of form on the inside.  And then we have the freedom where we look at outer forms after having disassembled this conception about the inside.  These two types of freedom then act as antidotes for obstacles which block our ability to emanate ourselves.
  

[3886]
‘GREL PA’I DPE MANG PO LA GNYIS PA LA NANG GZUGS SU ‘DU SHES PA ZHES ‘BYUNG BA NI MA DAG PA’O,,

In many manuscripts of the autocommentary, we see for the second the wording “conception of inside form.”  This is a textual corruption.


[3887]
SDUG PA’I RNAM PAR THAR PA BSAM GTAN BZHI PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NI GSUM PA STE, GZUGS SDUG PA SPRUL PA LA DGA’ BA DANG, MI SDUG PA SPRUL PA LA MI DGA’ BA’I KUN NAS NYON MONGS PA’I GNYEN PO’O,,

The third one is the freedom of the attractive, with an own nature of the fourth concentration level.  This is an antidote to the completely negative attitude of enjoying emanating attractive forms, and then not enjoying emanating unattractive forms.


[3888]
MTHONG CHOS BDER GNAS KYI LAM LA GNYIS LAS THAR PA DANG MTHUN PAR GNAS PA’I LAM LA, GZUGS MED KYI SNYOMS ‘JUG BZHI’I RNAM PAR THAR PA DANG, ZHI BAR GNAS PA’I LAM LA ‘DU SHES DANG TSOR BA ‘GOG PA ‘GOG PA’I SNYOMS ‘JUG GI RNAM THAR GCIG GO

There are two points to the path where we remain in joy about things we have seen.  First there is the freedom of the four balanced meditations of the formless realm.  And then there is the one freedom of cessation meditation, where on the path of remaining in peace we put a stop to discriminations and feelings.



Emptiness of own quality
related to the time of the result

[3889]
,GSUM PA NI,

Which brings us to our third point from above: the own quality of things related to the time of the result.


	[3890]
[VI.210]
Suviniścita rūpāṇi balāni kathitāni ca,
Supratiṣṭhita rūpāṇi vaiśāradyāni tāyinaḥ.

,STOBS RNAMS SHIN TU RNAM PAR NI,
,GTAN LA ‘BEBS PA’I RANG BZHIN GSUNGS,
,SKYOB PA’I MI ‘JIGS PA RNAMS NI,
,SHIN TU BRTAN PA’I NGO BO YIN,

		The forces were said
To have a quality of
		Establishing one deeply.

		The forms of
		Fearlessness of
		The Protector

		Have an essential
Nature of being
Extremely steadfast.


[3891]
‘CHAD ‘GYUR GYI STOBS BCU PO RNAMS NI, SHIN TU RNAM PAR GTAN LA [f. 259a] ‘BEBS PA’I RANG BZHIN NAM MTSAN NYID CAN DU RIG PAR BYA STE, YUL RNAMS SHIN TU GTAN LA ‘BEBS PA NYID KYIS, YUL LA ‘JUG PA LA THOGS PA MED PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN YIN PA’I PHYIR STOBS ZHES BYA’O,,

As for the ten forces that we will be explaining further on, one should understand that these have a quality, or own nature, of establishing one deeply.  That is, because we have an extreme ability to establish objects, there is an own quality of being able to engage in objects without the slightest resistance—and this then is why we speak of “force” here.


[3892]
SHES BYA THAMS CAD YANG DAG PA PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR RDZOGS PAR TE MA LUS PAR SANGS RGYAS PA STE THUGS SU CHUD DO, ZHES ZHAL GYIS BZHES PA DANG, NGA ZAG PA BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA ZAD DO ZHES PA DANG, NGAS CHAGS SOGS THAR PA’I BAR DU GCOD PA’I CHOS YIN NO ZHES PA DANG, SA LAM ‘DI LA NAN TAN DU BYAS NA SDUG BSNGAL ZAD PAR ‘GYUR RO ZHES DAM BCAS PA BZHI LA DE LTAR MIN NO,

Here we have the statement about the four declarations:

It is not so with these.  First there is the declaration that “I have reached that comprehension; I am enlightened towards all the knowable things there are; I grasp each and every one of them, unerringly, and in their entirety.”

Then there is the declaration that “I have finished off all impurity, along with the deep seeds for this impurity.”

Next there is the declaration, “I assert that craving and the like are things which act as an obstacle to freedom.”

And then finally we have the declaration that “If you make devoted efforts in these levels & paths, you will come to the end of your pain.”


[3893]
ZHES PA’I CHOS MTHUN GYI RGOL BA ‘GA’ YANG MA MTHONG BA’I SKYOB PA’I MI ‘JIGS PA BZHI PO RNAMS NI, SHIN TU BRTAN PA’I NGO BO NYID DE MTSAN NYID CAN YIN TE, RGOL BA SUS KYANG GZHAN DU BYA BAR MI NUS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

What this is referring to is the four forms of fearlessness of the Protector; and we can see no reasonable opponent who could question them.  These have an essential nature, an own nature, of being extremely steadfast, in that no opponent would ever be able to say that things were otherwise.


	[3894]
[VI.211]
Pratibhānādyanāccheda lakṣaṇāḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ,
Jagad dhitopasaṃhāro mahāmaitrī nirucyate.

,SO SOR YANG DAG RIG RNAMS NI,
,SPOBS SOGS TSAD MED MTSAN NYID CAN,
,’GRO LA PHAN PA NYER SGRUB PA,
,BYAMS PA CHEN PO ZHES BYA’O,

		The perfect understandings
		Of details—confidence
		And so on—have an
		Own nature of being
		Without any extent;

		And what we call
		“Great love” accomplishes
		Help for living beings.


[VI.212]
Mahākṛpā paritrāṇaṃ duḥkhināṃ muditā khalu,
Prāmodya lakṣaṇopekṣā jñeyāsaṃkīrṇa lakṣaṇā.

,SDUG BSNGAL CAN RNAMS YONGS SKYOB PA,
,THUGS RJE CHEN PO’O DGA’ BA NI,
,RAB DGA’I MTSAN NYID BTANG SNYOMS NI,
,MA ‘DRES MTSAN NYID CAN ZHES {%SHES} BYA,

		Great compassion
		Acts to protect,
		Entirely, those
		Who are suffering.

		Great joy has
		An own nature
		Of high joy.

		Equanimity
		Should be understood
		As having an own nature
		Of being unadmixed.		


[3895]
CHOS DANG DON DANG NGES PA’I TSIG DANG SPOBS PA SO SOR YANG DAG PAR RIG PA RNAMS NI, SPOBS PA LA SOGS PA BZHI CHAD {%TSAD} PA STE GTUGS PA MED PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NO,,

Let’s consider next the perfect understandings of details, for the Dharma; meanings; different words for the same ideas; and confidence.  These four of confidence and so on have an own nature of being without any extent; which is to say, limit that they touch.


[3896]
‘GRO BA RNAMS LA PHAN PA DANG BDE BA NYE BAR SGRUB PA NI, BYAMS PA CHEN PO ZHES BYA BA’I MTSAN NYID DANG, SDUG BSNGAL CAN GYI SEMS CAN RNAMS YONGS SU SKYOB PA NI, THUGS RJE CHEN PO’I MTSAN NYID DO,,

And then the own nature of what we call “great love” is that it accomplishes help and happiness for all living beings.  And the own nature of great compassion is that it acts to protect, entirely, each & every suffering being.


[3897]
DGA’ BA CHEN PO NI RAB TU STE MCHOG TU DGA’ BA’I MTSAN NYID CAN NO,,

Great joy has an own nature of high—which is to say, supreme—joy.


[3898]
BTANG SNYOMS CHEN PO NI ‘GA’ ZHIG LA RJES SU CHAGS PA [f. 259b] DANG, ,GZHAN DAG LA KHONG KHRO BA LA SOGS PA DANG MA ‘DRES PA STE DE DAG DANG BRAL BA’I MTSAN NYID CAN DU SHES PAR BYA’O,,

And then great equanimity should be understood as having an own nature of being “unadmixed” with—which is to say, free of—feelings of attachment for some people and then anger towards other people, or anything of the like.


	[3899]
[VI.213]
Buddhasyāveṇikā dharmā daśa cāṣṭau ca ye matāḥ,
Tair ahāryo yataḥ śāstā tato’hāryasvalakṣaṇāḥ

,SANGS RGYAS CHOS NI MA ‘DRES PA,
,BCU DANG BRGYAD DU GANG ‘DOD DAG,
,GANG PHYIR STON DES MI ‘PHROGS PA,
,DE PHYIR MI ‘PHROGS RANG MTSAN NYID,

		The Dharma of the Buddhas,
		Which we assert
		Has those 18 qualities
		Of being unmixed,

		Has an own quality
		That it cannot
		Be stolen off.

		Why this is true
		Is for that reason
		That the Teacher
		Cannot be
		Stolen off.


[3900]
SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS NI, MA ‘DRES PA BCU DANG BRGYAD DU GANG ‘DOD PA DE DAG GZHAN GYIS MI ‘PHROGS PA’I RANG GI MTSAN NYID CAN TE, RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA STON PA LA MA ‘DRES PA’I MI MTHUN PHYOGS ‘KHRUL PA SOGS MI MNGA’ BAS DE RNAMS KYIS GLAGS MED PA NYID KYIS MI ‘PHROGS PA STE, THUB PAR MI NUS PA DE’I PHYIR RO,,

The Dharma of the Buddhas, which we assert has those 18 qualities of being unmixed, has an own quality that it cannot be stolen off by others.  The reason why this is true is that the Teacher has no nature of being mixed in with things like error, or ideas that would contradict their positions.  As such, their teachings cannot be “stolen off,” or defeated—for that simple reason that they cannot be defeated.


[3901]
MA ‘DRES PA BCO BRGYAD NI DRUG TSAN GSUM STE, SKU LA ‘KHRUL PA DANG, GSUNG LA CA CO DANG, THUGS LA BSNYEL BA DANG MNYAM PAR MA BZHAG PA DANG, ‘KHOR ‘DAS THA DAD DU ‘DZIN PA’I RTOG PA DANG SO SOR MA BRTAGS PA’I BTANG SNYOMS MI MNGA’ BA DRUG NI DANG PO’O,

These 18 qualities of being unmixed come in three sets of six each.  The first six consist of:

	(1) the holy actions of their body have no error;

	(2) the holy words of their speech have no chatter;

	(3-4) the holy thoughts of their heart have no forgetting, or period
		in which they are ever out of balanced meditation;

	(5-6) they have no idea that the circle of suffering, and passing
		beyond it, could ever be separate things; and they
		never go into a state of indifference, where they are
		not examining in an individual way.


[3902]
‘DUN PA DANG BRTZON ‘GRUS DANG DRAN PA DANG TING NGE ‘DZIN DANG, SHES RAB DANG RNAM PAR GROL BA NYAMS PA MI MNGA’ BA NI GNYIS PA’O,,

The second set of six consists of (7) aspiration, (8) effort, (9) recollection, (10) concentration, (11) wisdom, and (12) liberation which know no decline.


[3903]
LUS KYI LAS DANG NGAG GI LAS DANG, YID KYI LAS THAMS CAD YE SHES SNGON DU ‘GRO ZHING, YE SHES KYI RJES SU ‘BRANG BA DANG, ‘DAS MA ‘ONGS DA LTAR GYI DUS LA MA CHAGS PA DANG MA THOGS PA’I YE SHES KYI GZIGS PA ‘JUG PA NI GSUM PA’O,,

The third set of six consists of the fact that all of (13) their actions of body, (14) their actions of speech, and (15) their actions of mind are preceded by wisdom, and followed by wisdom; while they (16) have no attachment to things of the past or (17) things of the future or (18) things of the present, and engage in an unimpeded wisdom which sees into these.


[3904]
MA ‘DRES PA’I NGES TSIG NI CHOS DE RNAMS SANGS RGYAS KHO NA’I RTEN LA YOD KYI, RTEN GZHAN LA MED PAS RTEN MA ‘DRES PA’O,,

Why are these 18 called “unmixed”?  The point is that these are possessed in the person only of beings who are Buddhas, and are unmixed in the person of other subjects.


[3905]
‘DI DAG GI BSHAD PA NI ‘GREL PAR GZUNGS KYI DBANG PHYUG RGYAL POS ZHUS PA’I MDO DRANGS PA LAS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

As for a further explanation of these qualities, the autocommentary allows us to learn them through references from The Sutra Requested by the King of the Lord of Secret Words.


	[3906]
[VI.214]
Sarvākāra jñatā jñānaṃ mataṃ pratyakṣa lakṣaṇam,
Anyat prādeśikatvena na pratyakṣam itīṣyate.

,RNAM KUN MKHYEN NYID YE SHES NI,
,MNGON SUM MTSAN NYID CAN DU ‘DOD,
,GZHAN NI NYI TSE BA NYID KYIS,
,MNGON SUM ZHES BYAR MI ‘DOD DO,

		The wisdom of
		Omniscience itself
		Is something that

		We hold to have
		An own quality of
		The direct perception.

		Those other than this
		Are only partial;
		
		As such, we would not
		Refer to them
		As direct.


[3907]
RNAM PA KUN MKHYEN PA NYID KYI YE SHES NI, SHES BYA [f. 260a] THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU MKHYEN PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN DU ‘DOD DE, RNAM MKHYEN DE LAS GZHAN PA’I SHES PA THAMS CAD NI YUL NYI TSE BA TZAM LA ‘JUG PA NYID KYIS, SHES BYA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU MKHYEN PA ZHES BYA BAR MI ‘DOD DO,,

The wisdom of omniscience itself is something that we hold to have an own quality of the direct perception of all knowable objects.  All states of mind other than this omniscience are limited to engaging in their objects in only a partial way; as such, we would not refer to them as the direct knowledge of all existing entities.


[3908]
DE LTAR GZUGS NAS RNAM MKHYEN GYI BAR GYI MTSAN NYID RNAMS NI, DE RNAMS MTSON BYED KYI RANG GI NGO BO TZAM YIN PAS, RTAGS KYI DGAG BYA’I RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DANG KHYAD PAR SHIN TU CHE’O,,

All of these examples of own qualities for things from physical form on up to omniscience itself serve to typify these objects, and give only their essential nature.  As such there is a huge difference between these natures and the existence by nature or definition which is what we deny with our reasoning.



A summary on emptiness
of its own quality

[3909]
GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to our third point from before, which is the concluding summary.


	[3910]
[VI.215]
Yal lakṣaṇaṃ saṃskṛtānāṃ yac cāsaṃskṛta lakṣaṇam,
Tasya tenaiva śūnyatvaṃ sā svalakṣaṇa śūnyatā.

,GANG ZHIG ‘DUS BYAS MTSAN NYID DANG,
,’DUS MA BYAS PA’I MTSAN NYID GANG,
,RE RE KHO NAS STONG PA NYID,
,DE NI RANG MTSAN STONG PA NYID,

		The own nature
		Of those produced,

		And the own nature
		Of those which exist
		But were not produced,

		Is then for each of them
		Their emptiness
		Of that alone:

		Their emptiness
		Of some nature.


[3911]
GANG ZHIG ‘DUS BYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS KYI MTSAN NYID DANG, ‘DUS MA BYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS KYI RANG MTSON BYED KYI MTSAN NYID GANG YIN PA DE RNAMS, DE’I RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DE KHO NAS STONG PA NYID DE NI RANG GI MTSAN NYID STONG PA NYID DO,,

And then let’s consider the own nature of those entities which are produced; and the own nature which typifies entities which exist but were not produced.  Their emptiness of “that alone”—referring to existing through some nature of their own—is then their emptiness of some own nature.



Emptiness of not seeing,
and true nature

[3912]
GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to the third part from before: an explanation of both the emptiness of not seeing anything and the emptiness of true nature, beyond all things.



15) The emptiness of not seeing anything

	[3913]
[VI.216]
Asthito vartamāno’yam atītānāgataṃ na sat,
Yatraite nopalabhyante’nupalambhaḥ sa ucyate.

,DA LTA BA ‘DI MI GNAS SHING,
,’DAS DANG MA ‘ONGS YOD MA YIN,
,GANG DU DE DAG MI DMIGS PA,
,DE LA MI DMIGS PA ZHES BRJOD,

		Those of the present
		Do not remain;

		And those of the past
		And the future;
		None of these exist.

		These things cannot
		Be observed, in any.

		As such,
		We refer to them
		As “unseen.”	


[3914]
DE {%DA} LTAR BYUNG BA ‘DI RANG GRUB PA’I DUS PHAN CHAD DU MI GNAS SHING, BYUNG ZIN ‘DAS PA NI BYUNG BA DE ZHIG PA YIN PA DANG, ‘BYUNG ‘GYUR MA ‘ONGS PA NI ‘BYUNG ‘GYUR DE DA LTAR MA SKYES PA’I PHYIR, GSUM PO DER YOD PA MA YIN NO,,

Now those things which have occurred in the present time do not remain beyond the point at which they have come into being.  And things which have already occurred—those in the past time—have already stopped.  Things which are yet to occur—those in the future—are still to come, and have not yet come to start in the present.  As such, none of these three exist as those.


[3915]
BYUNG ZIN DANG ‘BYUNG ‘GYUR DANG DA LTAR BA DE DAG RIM PA BZHIN DU ZHIG PA DANG MA SKYES PA’I DUS GNYIS DANG, RANG GRUB PA’I ‘OG GANG DU MI DMIGS PA DE LA NI MI DMIGS PA ZHES BRJOD DO,,

Those things that have already occurred; and those that are yet to occur; and those in the present cannot be observed—respectively—in any of the two times of either what has already stopped or what is yet to start; nor subsequent to their having occurred.  As such, we refer to them as “unseen.”


	[3916]
[VI.217]
Yā tasyānupalambhasya tat svarūpa viyuktatā,
Sākūṭasthāvināśenānupalambhākhya śūnyatā.

,MI DMIGS PA DE RANG NGO BO,
,DE YIS DBEN PA NYID GANG DE,
,THER ZUG GNAS MIN ‘JIG MIN PAS,
,MI DMIGS ZHES BYA’I STONG NYID DO,

		This state of being
		Unseen is entirely
	
		Devoid of existing
		In that essential way.

		It is not something
		That can remain
		In some solid manner,

		Nor is it something
		Which stops.
		
		As such, it is
		The emptiness,
		We say, of
		“Not seeing anything.”		


[3917]
MI DMIGS PA DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA DE YIS DBEN PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, THER ZUG TU GNAS PA MIN PA DANG, ‘JIG PA MIN PAS NA MI DMIGS PA ZHES BYA BA’I STONG PA NYID DO,

Consider then this state of being unseen; the fact that it does not exist through any pure, essential nature of its own: the fact that it is entirely devoid of existing in that way.  This is not something that can remain in some solid manner, nor is it something which stops.  As such, it is the emptiness, we say, of “not seeing anything.”



16) The emptiness of true nature, beyond all things

	[3918]
[VI.218]
Nāsti sāṃyogikaṃ rūpaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratyayodayāt,
Saṃyogasya tu tenaiva śūnyatābhāvaśūnyatā.

,RKYEN LAS BYUNG PHYIR DNGOS RNAMS LA,
,’DUS PA PA YI NGO BO MED,
,’DUS PA PA NI DE NYID KYIS,
,STONG NYID DNGOS MED STONG NYID DO,

		The functional
		Are “brought together,”
		Because they occur
		Through conditions,

		And an essential nature
		Of it has no existence.

		The fact that these
		Same things
		Of that convening
		Are empty

		Is what we refer to
		As “the emptiness
		Beyond all things.”


[3919]
RGYU DANG RKYEN LAS BYUNG BA’I PHYIR NA, DNGOS [f. 260b] PO RNAMS LA ‘DUS PA PA STE RGYU RKYEN ‘DUS PA LAS BYUNG BA’I NGO BO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAS, DE RNAMS LA DNGOS PO MED PA ZHES BYA LA,

We refer to functional entities as “brought together,” because they are something which occurs through causes & conditions.  That is, they possess an essential nature of having occurred through the convening of causes & conditions.  And since this essence has no existence as something that could exist through some nature of its own, we refer to these as “beyond all things.”


[3920]
‘DUS PA LAS BYUNG BA DE NYID KYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID NI, DNGOS PO MED PA’I NGO BO NYID KYI STONG PA NYID DO,,

And the fact that these same things which have occurred through that convening are empty of existing through any perfect, essential nature of their own is what we refer to as “the emptiness of any perfect essential nature, beyond all things.”


[3921]
DE LTAR BCU DRUG TU BSHAD PA NI BDEN GRUB ‘GOG PA’I RIGS PA MI ‘DRA BA’I SGO NAS NI MIN TE, THAMS CAD LA YANG THER ZUG TU GNAS PA DANG ‘JIG PA MED PA’I RIGS PAS BSGRUBS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

The explanation that we make this way, into sixteen different types, is not something that is accomplished through different types of reasoning which denies that things could exist as real.  And that’s because every single one of them is proven through the logic which shows that things cannot stay in any solid way; nor can they stop.


[3922]
GANG ZAG GCIG LA SPYIR BDEN MED DU SGRUB PA YANG MIN TE, GZHI MIG SOGS NANG GI CHOS RNAMS KYI STENG DU BDEN MED TSAD MAS GRUB NA GZHI GZHAN LA BLO KHA PHYOGS PA’I TSE, GZHAN GYIS SGRUB BYED BKOD PA LA MI LTOS PAR RANG GIS RTAGS LA BRTEN NAS THE TSOM CHOD PAR ‘GYUR BA’I PHYIR RO,,

Nor is it the case that with a single individual we can establish that—in general—things have no real existence.  If we establish, with an accurate perception, the fact that nothing is real with regard to a particular locus—such as the inner entities of the eye and so on—then when we turn our minds to some other locus we are able to eliminate any doubts we may have had, based on the reason we used ourselves, and without relying upon any proof set forth by others.


[3923]
DE’I PHYIR GANG ZAG GCIG GI DBANG DU BYAS PA DANG, GZHI SO SO LA BDEN ZHEN SHAS CHE BA’I GANG ZAG SO SO’I DBANG DU BYAS PA GNYIS KA SHES PAR BYA’O,,

As such, both are to be understood with regard to a single person; and relative to each individual person who may display some strong belief in reality, for each individual locus.



The division of emptiness into four

[3924]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second more general point from above: a detailed explanation of the division of emptiness into four types.


	[3925]
[VI.219]
Ucyante bhava śabdena pañca skandhāḥ samāsataḥ,
Tair eva śūnyatā teṣāṃ yā soktā bhava śūnyatā.

,DNGOS PO’I SGRAS NI MDOR BSDUS NA,
,PHUNG PO LNGA RNAMS BRJOD PA YIN,
,DE RNAMS DE YIS STONG NYID GANG,
,DE DNGOS STONG PA NYID DU BSHAD,

		The term “things” refers,
		In a summary way,
To the five parts
To the person.

		That fact that these
		Are empty is what
		We refer to as
		“The emptiness of things.”		


[3926]
DNGOS PO STONG PA NYID CES BYA BA’I DNGOS PO’I SGRAS NI PHUNG PO LNGA RNAMS BRJOD PA YIN TE, DE YANG SO SOR MA PHYE BAR MDOR BSDUS NAS SPYIR BRJOD DO,,

When we say “the emptiness of things,” the term “things” refers to the five parts to the person.  And the reference in this case is meant in a general sense, in a summary way, without dividing out the individual components.


[3927]
PHUNG PO LNGA PO DE RNAMS DE YI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, DNGOS PO STONG PA NYID DU MDOR BSHAD DO,,

And then that fact that these five parts to the person are empty of existing through any nature of their own is, in brief, what we refer to as “the emptiness of things.”


	[3928]
[VI.220]
Abhāvo’saṃskṛtā dharmā nirdiśyante samāsataḥ,
Tenābhāvena śūnyatvaṃ tasyaivābhāva śūnyatā.

,MDOR BSDUS NA NI DNGOS MED PA,
,’DUS MA BYAS CHOS RNAMS LA BRJOD,
,DE NYID [215a] DNGOS MED DES STONG NYID,
,DNGOS PO MED PA STONG NYID DO,

		This lack of things,
		In summary,
		Refers to entities

		That are things
		Which exist but
		Were not produced [f. 215a].

		The fact that these
		Same absences of things
		Are empty is

		The emptiness of
		The lack of things.


[3929]
SO SOR MA PHYE BAR MDOR BSDUS NA NI DNGOS PO MED PA NI ‘DUS MA BYAS NAM MKHA’ LA SOGS PA DANG MYANG ‘DAS RNAMS LA BRJOD DO,,

The lack of things in summary, without dividing out the individual components, refers to empty space and the rest, and nirvana—things which exist but were not produced.


[3930]
‘DUS MA BYAS DE NYID DNGOS POR MED PA DE’I RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB [f. 261a] PAS STONG PA NYID NI, DNGOS PO MED PA STONG PA NYID DO ZHES BYA’O,,

And then when we speak of the fact that these same unproduced, existent phenomena—these absences of things—are empty of existing through any nature of their own, that is what we call “the emptiness of the lack of things.”


	[3931]
[VI.221]
Prakṛter niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ svabhāvākhyā tu śūnyatā,
Prakṛtir na kṛtetyevaṃ svabhāva iti kathyate.

,RANG BZHIN NGO BO NYID MED NI,
,RANG BZHIN ZHES BYA’I STONG NYID DE,
,’DI LTAR RANG BZHIN MA BYAS PAS,
,RANG BZHIN ZHES NI BYA BAR BSNYAD,

		What we give
		The name of
		“The emptiness
		Of any nature”

		Is an absence
		Of any real quality
		To the nature.

		This particular nature
		Is not something produced;

		As such we give it the
		Name of “the nature.”


[3932]
RANG BZHIN NI CHOS NYID KYI RANG BZHIN LA BYA STE, ‘DI LTAR RANG BZHIN DE NI NYAN THOS LA SOGS PAS MA BYAS PAR DNGOS PO’I GSHIS LUGS SU GNAS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

“The nature” here refers to the nature of the way of all things; and that’s because this particular nature is not something that the listeners and the like have ever produced—it simply remains, as the original nature of things.


[3933]
RANG BZHIN CHOS NYID DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID DO ZHES BYA BAR BSNYAD DO,,

This nature or way of all things is an absence of things existing through any nature of their own; as such, we give it the name of “the emptiness of any nature.”


	[3934]
[VI.222]
Utpāde’pi hi Buddhānām anutpāde’pi bhāvataḥ,
Śūnyatā sarva bhāvānāṃ paro bhāvaḥ prakīrtitaḥ.

,SANGS RGYAS RNAMS NI ‘BYUNG BA’AM,
,MA BYUNG YANG RUNG DNGOS SU NI,
,DNGOS PO KUN GYI STONG PA NYID,
,GZHAN GYI DNGOS POR RAB TU BSGRAGS,

		Whether the Buddhas
		Ever occur
		Or do not appear,
		It’s all the same.

		All entities will possess
		An emptiness, really;

		This is what we declare
		Is the emptiness
		Of being other things.


[3935]
SANGS RGYAS RNAMS NI BYUNG BA’AM STE ‘JIG RTEN DU ‘BYUNG YANG RUNG, MA BYUNG YANG RUNG STE DNGOS PO KUN GYI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID NI, GZHAN GYI DNGOS PO STE NGO BOR RAB TU BSGRAGS SO,,

“Whether the Buddhas ever occur”—which is to say, whether they appear in this world, or do not appear in this world—it’s all the same.  Still, in either case, all entities will possess an emptiness of any nature of their own; and this is what we declare is the “emptiness of being other things,” or essential natures.


[3936]
‘DIR NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS, MA BYUNG YANG NI RANG BZHIN NYID, CES PA DANG, GZHAN GYI NGO BO STONG PAR BSGRAGS, ZHES ‘BYUNG BA LTAR BDE’O,,

Here we find the wording of Nakto’s translation to be more convenient: “the very nature of things, even if they don’t appear,” and “what we declare as the emptiness of being other essences.”


[3937]
GZHAN GYI NGO BO’I SKAD DOD NI MCHOG DANG GZHAN DANG PHA ROL GSUM LA ‘JUG PAS, DANG PO LTAR NA MCHOG TU BYUNG BA’I DE KHO NA NYID DO,,

The original Sanskrit wording for “other essences” here can apply to three different things: to “the highest”; to “something other”; and to “the other side.”  If we take it the first way, then we can read it as “suchness which appears as the highest.”


[3938]
MCHOG TU BYUNG BA’I DON NI RTAG TU DE KHO NA NYID KYI MTSAN NYID LAS MI ‘DA’ BAR YOD PA’O,,

What “appears as the highest” implies here is that things always exist without going beyond the quality of suchness.


[3939]
GNYIS PA LTAR NA GZHAN NI ‘JIG RTEN PA LAS GZHAN ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA’I YE SHES PHUL DU BYUNG BA RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA’I YE SHES SO,,

If we follow the second connotation here, then the “something other” is “other than something of the world.”  And this would refer to the form of wisdom which is beyond the world—a form which is excellent, and no longer imagines things in a mistaken way.


[3940]
DNGOS PO STE NGO BO NI YE SHES DES RTOGS PAR BYA BA’O,,

When it says “thing” here it refers to the essential nature which is what this wisdom realizes.


[3941]
GSUM PA LTAR NA PHA ROL NA YOD PA NI GZHAN GYI NGO BO’O,,

Following the third connotation, “existing on the far side” is a reference to the essential nature of other things.


	[3942]
[VI.223]
Bhūtakoṭis tathātvaṃ ca sā parabhāva śūnyatā,
Prajñā pāramitānītāvityetāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ.

,YANG DAG MTHA’ DANG DE BZHIN NYID,
,DE BZHIN DNGOS PO’I STONG NYID DO,,
,SHES RAB PHA ROL PHYIN TSUL LAS,
,DE DAG DE SKAD RAB TU BSGRAGS,

		The ultimate end
		And, just so,
The true nature,

Are the emptiness
Of things.

This is how
They were declared
In those words

Presented in
The way of the
Perfection of wisdom.


[3943]
DE YANG ‘KHOR BA LAS ‘DAS PA’I PHYIR ‘KHOR BA’I PHA ROL NI YANG DAG PA’I MTHA’ STE MTHA’ NI ‘DIR ‘KHOR BA ZAD PA’I MYANG ‘DAS SO,,

And now since it is beyond the circle of suffering, we refer to the “far side” of this circle as “the ultimate end.”  Here, “end” refers to the nirvana in which we have finished off this circle of pain.


[3944]
DE KHO NA NYID KYI MTSAN NYID LAS RNAM PA GZHAN DU ‘GYUR BA MED PAS DE BZHIN NYID [f. 261b] DO,,

And we use the expression “the true nature” to indicate something that never displays any changing to something other type: other than the nature of suchness.


[3945]
DE NYID NI DE NYID KYI RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PA’I MTSAN NYID CAN GYI STONG PA NYID DE NI, GZHAN GYI DNGOS PO STE NGO BO’I STONG PA NYID CES BYA’O,,

This in itself is an emptiness which has an own nature of being empty of any nature of its very own; and so we speak of the “emptiness” of other things, or essential nature.


[3946]
RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID LA SOGS PA SNGAR BSHAD KYANG ‘DIR BSHAD PA MI ZLOS PA NI, ‘DIR DBYE SGO ‘BRING PO’I DBANG DU MDZAD PA’O,,

Now we have, previously, already given an explanation of things like “the emptiness of a nature of its own.”  The reason why what we have here is not redundant is with reference to the degree of division which we have here, which is middling in extent.


[3947]
BSHAD PA PHYI MA GNYIS RGYAS ‘BRING GNYIS KA’I SKABS SU YANG YANG ‘BYUNG BA NI, CHOS NYID DE DNGOS PO’I GSHIS YIN PA DANG, RTAG TU YOD PA DANG, MI RTOG YE SHES KYI GZHAL BYAR YOD PAR KHAS LEN NA BDEN PAR GRUB BO SNYAM PA’I DOGS PA GCAD PA’I DON YIN PAS DE RNAMS MI ‘GAL BAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

Now why do the latter two explanations occur over & over again in the context of both the more extensive and the middling versions?  This is because we accept that the true nature of things is their original nature; and that it exists for all time; and that it exists as that object which the wisdom beyond any mistaken perception holds under its consideration.  As such, the intent here is to prevent any mistaken idea where people think that perhaps it exists in truth.  You should understand then that we have no contradiction here.


[3948]
DE ‘DRA BA’I STONG PA NYID DE DAG NI SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’I TSUL RGYAL BA’I YUM LAS DBYE BA DANG STONG TSUL DE DAG ‘DIR BSHAD PA DE SKAD DU RAB TU BSGRAGS PA STE BSHAD DO,,

These types of emptiness then represent the divisions, and the manner in which things are empty, as the way of the perfection of wisdom is presented in the sutras of the Mother of the Victors.  We have explained them then here according to how they were declared in those words.



A concluding summary
describing the high qualities

[3949]
BZHI PA NI,

With this we have reached our fourth very general division from above: a concluding summary for the section, by way of describing the high qualities of this level.


[3950]
DA NI SHER PHYIN LA LHAG PAR MOS PA’I BYANG SEMS KYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA’I YON TAN BRJOD PA’I SGO NAS, SHER PHYIN GYI SKABS RDZOGS PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR DU BSHAD PA,

And so we will now make an explanation with a view towards wrapping up our section on the perfection of wisdom, by describing the unique personal qualities of a bodhisattva who has a special longing for this wisdom perfection.


	[3951]
[VI.224]
Iti matikiraṇa sphuṭāvabhāsaḥ
svakaragatāmalakaṃ yathaiva buddhvā,
Tribhavam idam aśeṣam ādyajātaṃ
vyavahṛtisatyavaśān nirodham eti.

,DE LTAR BLO GROS ZER GYIS SNANG BA
GSAL BYAS PA,
,RANG GI LAG NA GNAS PA’I SKYU RU
RA BZHIN DU,
,SRID GSUM ‘DI DAG MA LUS GDOD NAS
SKYE MED PAR,
,RTOGS TE THA SNYAD BDEN PA’I STOBS KYIS
‘GOG PAR ‘GRO,

		The wisdom
		From this represents
		Rays of light
		That illuminate;

		We could compare it
		To an olive
		Sitting in the palm
		Of they themselves.

		Suppose we are able
		To realize that
		There is nothing about

		The entirety
		Of these three realms
		Of existence which

		Has ever started,
		Since time with
		No beginning.

		Through the power
		Of nominal reality,
		We come to the point
		Where things are stopped.


[3952]
SNGAR BSHAD PA’I RNAM PA DE LTAR RNAM PAR DPYAD PA LAS BYUNG BA’I BLO GROS KYI ‘OD ZER GYIS DE KHO NA NYID MTHONG BA LA GEGS BYED PA’I MUN PA ‘JOMS PA’I SNANG BA GSAL BAR BYAS PA’I BYANG SEMS RANG GI LAG NA GNAS PA’I SKYU RU RA RLON PA’I ‘BRAS BU BZHIN DU,

Let us consider then the wisdom that comes from this kind of careful examination of all the different aspects we’ve described in the discussions up to this point.  This wisdom represents rays of light that illuminate the darkness which acts to block us from seeing suchness.  It lights things up so well that we could compare it to the fresh fruit of an olive sitting in the palm of the bodhisattva themselves, seen by them this clearly.


[3953]
SRID PA GSUM PO ‘DI DAG MA LUS PA GDOD MA NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PAR MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA DE YANG NI, THA SNYAD PA KUN RDZOB BDEN PA’I STOBS KYIS TE KUN RDZOB TU ‘GOG PAR ‘GRO BA STE DE LA [f. 262a] SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG GO

And so suppose that we are able to realize, directly, that there is nothing about the entirety of these three realms of existence which has ever started through any nature of its own: and it has been this way since time with no beginning.  And in this case, we have—through the power of nominal, or deceptive reality—come to the point where things are stopped, in a nominal sense.  And then we go into a balanced meditation on this very point.


	[3954]
[VI.225]
Janayati karuṇāṃ jagatyanāthe
bhavati nirodha gatāśayaḥ sadaiṣaḥ,
Jayati ca sakalān dhiyāta ūrdhvaṃ
Sugatavacaḥ prabhavāt sa madhyabuddhān.

,RTAG TU ‘GOG PAR GTOGS PA’I BSAM GTAN
YIN MOD KYI,
,’GRO BA MGON MED PA LA SNYING RJE’ANG
SKYED PAR BYED,
,DE GONG BDE GSHEGS GSUNG SKYES SANGS RGYAS
‘BRING BCAS NI,
,MA LUS PA RNAMS BLO YIS PHAM PAR
BYED PA’ANG YIN,

		It is admittedly
		The case that
		They always have
		
		A state of mental focus
		Which is taken in
		By a cessation;

		And yet
		At the same time
		They give rise to
		
		Thoughts of compassion
		Towards living beings,

		Who have no one
		To protect them.

		Beyond that,
		They defeat,
		In their mind,

		All of those
		Individuals who are

		Born of the word
		Of Those Gone to Bliss,
		And medium buddhas.


[3955]
,’GOG PA’I NGO BOR SON KYANG ‘GRO BA SKYOB PA’I BSAM PA ‘DOR BA YANG MA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA,

Here we will explain the idea that “Even though one has passed into the essence of cessation, it is not that at the same time they give up thoughts of protecting.”


[3956]
BYANG SEMS SA DRUG PA BA DE RTAG TU ‘GOG PA ‘OD GSAL DU GTOGS PA’I BSAM PA DANG LDAN PA YIN MOD KYI, ‘GRO BA MGON MED PA RNAMS LA ‘DI YI SNYING RJE’ANG SKYED PAR BYED PA STE ‘PHEL BAR ‘GYUR RO,,

Now it is admittedly the case that a bodhisattva at the sixth level is always possessed of a state of mind which is taken in by a cessation: by the clear light.  And yet at the same time they “give rise to”—which is to say, increase—their thoughts of compassion towards living beings, who have no one to protect them.


[3957]
DE’I PHYIR ‘DI’I SBYOR BA NI ‘KHOR BAR GTOGS PA DANG, BSAM PA NI MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PAR GTOGS SO,,

As such, we can say that the activities of such individuals are taken in by the cycle of pain; while their state of mind is taken in by nirvana.


[3958]
SA DRUG PA BA ‘DIS SA DRUG PA DE’I GONG DU STE PHYI NAS BDER GSHEGS GSUNG SKYES NYAN THOS RNAMS SANGS RGYAS ‘BRING PO RANG RGYAL DANG BCAS PA MA LUS PA RNAMS NI BLO YI STOBS KYIS PHAM PAR BYED PA STE ZIL GYIS GNON PA’ANG YIN NO,,

This person at the sixth bodhisattva level is also someone who “beyond that,” meaning later on, “defeats”—which is to say, outshines—in the power of their mind all of those individuals who are “born of the word of Those Gone To Bliss” (a reference to the listeners) and “medium buddhas” (self-made victors).


	[3959]
[VI.226]
Jina guṇa jaladheḥ paraṃ sa pāraṃ 
vrajati puraskṛta eṣa janmi haṃsaiḥ,
Śubha pavana balena rāja haṃsaḥ
pṛthu sita saṃvṛti tattva jāta pakṣaḥ.

,KUN RDZOB DE NYID GSHOG YANGS DKAR PO
RGYAS GYUR PA,
,NGANG PA’I RGYAL PO DE NI SKYE BO’I
NGANG PA YIS,
,MDUN DU BDAR NAS DGE BA’I RLUNG GI
SHUGS STOBS KYIS,
,RGYAL BA’I YON TAN RGYA MTSO’I PHA ROL
MCHOG TU ‘GRO,,

They are able
To stretch forth

Their broad, white,
Wide-spreading wings,

Of the deceptive
Side of things,
And suchness.

They are kings
Among the birds,

Soaring at the head
Of the geese
Of living beings.

By the strength
And power
Of good deeds,

They fly
To the highest:

To the far shores
Of the ocean of
The high qualities
Of the Victors.


[3960]
KUN RDZOB RGYA CHE BA’I LAM GYI RIM PA DANG, DE KHO NA NYID ZAB MO’I LAM GYI RIM PA’I G-YAS G-YON GYI GSHOG PA YANGS PA DKAR PO RGYAS PAR GYUR PA’I NGANG PA’I RGYAL PO SA DRUG PA BA DE NI, GDUL BYA’I SKYE BO’I NGANG PA PHUL DU BYUNG BA SKYED PA RNAMS KYIS MDUN DU BDAR NAS,

These bodhisattvas of the sixth level are able to stretch forth their broad, white, wide-spreading right and left wings—a reference to their practice of the deceptive side of things, the wide-spreading path; and their practice of sheer suchness, the path of the profound.  As such, they are like kings among the birds, soaring at the head of the geese of living beings—their disciples—whom they have created as exceptional.


[3961]
SNGON LAN MANG DU BSAGS PA’I DGE BA’I RLUNG GI SHUGS CHEN PO’I STOBS KYIS, RGYAL BA SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN GYI RGYA MTSO CHEN PO’I PHA ROL MCHOG TU ‘GRO BAR ‘GYUR BAS,

They are driven by the strength, by the great power, of the wind of the good deeds that they have, on many previous occasions, gathered together.  And with this power they are able to fly to the “highest”—to the far shores of the great ocean of the high qualities of the Victors: the Buddhas.


[3962]
DE’I RJES SU SLOB PAR ‘DOD PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG LAM RIM PA GNYIS KA’I GSHOG PAS BGROD DGOS KYI, GSHOG PA GNYIS GANG YANG MED PA DANG, PHYOGS RE BA’I LAM GSHOG PA GCIG CHAG PA LTA BUS MI TSIM PAR,

As such, those who hope to follow in their wake and learn these things must make the journey using the strong wings of both of these variations of the steps of the path.  You should not be satisfied with possessing neither of these wings; and neither should you be satisfied with a path which is only partial: where it is as if you were born with but a single wing.


[3963]
THABS DANG SHES RAB GNYIS KA [f. 262b] TSANG BA’I LAM GYIS SANGS RGYAS KYI SAR BGROD PAR BYA’O,,

That is, it is only by employing the complete path—one which includes both method and wisdom—that we will be able to make the journey to the level of an Enlightened Being.


	[3964]
[chapter number]
DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS SEMS BSKYED PA DRUG PA’O,,

This concludes the sixth wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


[3965]
DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA’I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA DGONGS PA RAB TU GSAL BA LAS, DON DAM PA’I SEMS BSKYED PA DRUG PA’I BSHAD PA’O,,

This then concludes the explanation of the sixth ultimate “Wish for Enlightenment”—or chapter—in An Illumination of the True Intent, an extensive commentary to Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 7
The Final Four Levels
 


Chapter 7
The Final Four Levels


The seventh level

[3966]
` ,,GSUM PA RING DU SONG BA SOGS BZHI BSHAD PA LA BZHI, SA BDUN PA DANG, SA BRGYAD PA DANG, SA DGU PA DANG, SA BCU PA BSHAD PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us to a third great section of our work, which is our explanation of the four levels including the one named “Gone Far,” and the rest.  Here there are four sections: an explanation of the seventh bodhisattva level; and then the eighth; and the ninth; and finally the tenth.  Here is the first of those.


	[3967]
[VII.1]
	Sanskrit unavailable

,RING DU SONG ‘DIR ‘DI NI SKAD CIG DANG,
,SKAD CIG LA NI ‘GOG PAR ‘JUG ‘BYUNG ZHING,
,THABS KYI PHA ROL PHYIN LEGS ‘BAR BA’ANG ‘THOB,

		Here at “Gone Far,”
		This one is in meditation,
		From moment to moment,
		On cessation.

		Further, they also attain
A perfection of skillful means
		Which is blazing strongly.	


[3968]
SA BDUN PA RING DU SONG BA ‘DIR NI, SA DRUG PAR THOB PA’I ‘GOG PA DE LA SKAD CIG DANG, SKAD CIG STE SKAD CIG RE RE LA BYANG SEMS ‘DI SNYOM PAR ‘JUG PAR ‘GYUR TE,

Here at the seventh level, known as “Gone Far,” this bodhisattva remains in balanced meditation, from moment to moment—in each separate moment, upon the cessation that they attained at the sixth level.


[3969]
‘GOG PA LA ‘JUG PA NI YANG DAG PA’I MTHA’ LA SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG PA YIN PAS, DE BZHIN NYID LA ‘GOG PA ZHES BRJOD DE, ‘PHAGS PA’I MNYAM GZHAG GI SKABS SU DE BZHIN NYID ‘DIR GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA THAMS CAD ‘GOG PAR ‘GYUR BA’I PHYIR RO,,

And because this engagement in the cessation is a balanced meditation upon the ultimate end, we refer to it as “cessation in the way things really are.”  And that, in turn, is because here in the very nature of things at the point of the balanced meditation of a realized being, all elaborations of duality are stopped.


[3970]
DE SKAD DU SA BCU PA LAS, KYE RGYAL BA’I SRAS DAG BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’I SA DRUG PA YAN CHAD, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’I ‘GOG PA LA SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG PA STE, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’I SA BDUN PA ‘DI LA GNAS PA’I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ NI, SEMS KYI SKAD CIG SEMS KYI SKAD CIG LA YANG ‘GOG PA LA SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG CING LDANG STE, ‘GOG PA MNGON SUM DU BYAS ZHES NI MI BYA’O ZHES RGYAS PAR GSUNGS SO,,

We see this described, in some detail, in The Sutra on the Ten Levels:

O children of the Victors, beyond the sixth level of the bodhisattva, one goes into a balanced meditation upon the cessation of a bodhisattva.  That is, a bodhisattva who is staying at the seventh bodhisattva level enters into balanced meditation upon—and then arises from—their cessation, moment by mental moment.  We do not though refer to this as having gone directly into the cessation.


[3971]
SA ‘DIR THABS MKHAS KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA LEGS PAR ‘BAR BA STE CHES YONGS SU DAG PAR YANG ‘GYUR TE, DAG TSUL NI SNGAR SA GZHAN LA BSTAN PA’I RIGS PAS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

At this level, the perfection of skillful means is blazing strongly; that is, it has further become ever more absolutely pure.  The exact manner in which it is pure is something you can understand from the reasoning we presented earlier for the other levels.


[3972]
SHER PHYIN NYID RNAM PA KHYAD PAR [f. 263a] CAN DU ZHUGS PA LA PHAR PHYIN PHYI MA BZHIR BZHAG GO

When one is engaged in an exceptional form of this very perfection of wisdom, we posit it as being the four latter forms of the perfections.


[3973]
,CHOS RAB TU RNAM PAR ‘BYED PA’I GNAS SKABS NYID NI SHER PHYIN ZHES BRJOD KYI RNAM PA GZHAN NI MA YIN NO,,

This point at which we are engaged in an extraordinary level of the discernment of entities is what we refer to as the “perfection of wisdom”; and it is no other way.


[3974]
THABS MKHAS KYI PHAR PHYIN DU ‘JOG PA’I THABS LA MKHAS PA NI BYANG SA LAS, DRUG TSAN GNYIS GSUNGS PA’I DANG PO NANG GI SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS ‘GRUB PA LAS BRTZAMS PA’I THABS MKHAS PA DRUG NI,

The kind of skillful means which we establish as the perfection of skillful means is described in Levels of the Bodhisattva.  Here we find described two sets of six.  The first set is composed of the six forms of skillful means which start off from ones inner practice of the teachings of the Buddha.


[3975]
BYANG SEMS KYIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA SNYING RJE DANG LDAN PAR LTA BA DANG, ‘DU BYED THAMS CAD KYI RANG BZHIN YANG DAG PA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU SHES PA DANG, BLA NA MED PA’I BYANG CHUB KYI YE SHES ‘DOD PA DANG, SEMS CAN LA LTA BA LA BRTEN NAS ‘KHOR BA MI GTONG BA DANG, ‘DU BYED JI LTA BA BZHIN SHES PA LA BRTEN NAS NYON MONGS PA CAN MA YIN PA’I SEMS KYIS ‘KHOR BAR ‘KHOR BA DANG, SANGS RGYAS ‘DOD PA LA BRTEN NAS BRTZON ‘GRUS ‘BAR BA’O,,

Here we have—

(1) The way that bodhisattvas view each and every living being with compassion;

(2) The way in which they comprehend the nature of all factors as pure, exactly as it is;

(3) The way in which they aspire to the wisdom of matchless enlightenment;

(4) The way in which they refuse to abandon the circle of suffering, so far as how they look upon living beings;

(5) The way in which they circle in the circle of suffering, with a mind that is free of negative emotions, all depending upon their understanding of the way that factors really are; and

(6) The way in which they set on fire the efforts they make, all due to their yearning towards enlightenment.


[3976]
PHYI’I SEMS CAN SMIN PAR BYA BA LAS BRTZAMS PA’I THABS MKHAS DRUG NI,

And then there is the second set of six types of skillful means, which are undertaken towards working to ripen the outside objects, of living beings. 


[3977]
BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYIS SEMS CAN GYI DGE BA’I RTZA BA CHUNG NGU RNAMS ‘BRAS BU TSAD MED PAR SGYUR BAR BYED PA DANG, DE BZHIN DU TSOGS CHUNG NGUS DGE RTZA CHE BA DAG SGRUB PAR BYED PA DANG, BSTAN PA LA ZHE ‘GRAS PA RNAMS KYI KHONG KHRO SEL BAR BYED PA DANG, BSTAN PA LA YID BAR MAR GNAS PA RNAMS DE LA ‘DZUD PA DANG, ZHUGS PA RNAMS SMIN PAR BYED PA DANG, SMIN PA RNAMS GROL BAR BYED PA STE 

These six then are the following:

(7) The way in which bodhisattvas take the more minor roots of virtue which living beings possess, and transform them into limitless results; and, just so,

(8) The way they act to accomplish massive roots of virtue out of minor collections of goodness;

(9) The way in which they manage to clear away the anger of those who feel some hatred towards the teachings;

(10) The way they induce those who are feeling divided about the teachings to enter those teachings;

(11) The way they act to ripen those who have already entered the teachings; and

(12) They way they act to liberate those who are ripened.


[3978]
THABS LA MKHAS PA BCU GNYIS SO,,

These then are the twelve forms of skillful means.


	[3979]
[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA BDUN PA’O,,

This concludes the seventh wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


[3980]
DBU MA LA [f. 263b] ‘JUG PA’I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA DGONGS PA RAB TU GSAL BA LAS, DON DAM PA’I SEMS BSKYED PA BDUN PA’I BSHAD PA’O,,

This then concludes the explanation of the seventh ultimate “Wish for Enlightenment”—or chapter—in An Illumination of the True Intent, an extensive commentary to Entering the Middle Way.



Special prayers,
and rising from cessation

[3981]
` ,,GNYIS PA LA GSUM, SA ‘DIR SMON LAM LHAG CING ‘GOG PA LAS SLONG TSUL, NYON MONGS THAMS CAD ZAD PAR BSTAN PA, DBANG BCU THOB PAR BSTAN PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

With this we have reached our second section from above: an explanation of the eighth bodhisattva level.  We proceed in three parts: a description of how, at this level, ones prayers are special, and how they rise out of their cessation; a description of how they finish off all their negative emotions; and a description of how they attain the ten powers.


	[3982]
	[VIII.1]
	Sanskrit unavailable

,YANG YANG SNGAR DGE LAS LHAG THOB BYA’I PHYIR,
,GANG DU PHYIR MI LDOG PA NYID ‘GYUR BA,
,MI G-YO DE LA BDAG NYID CHE DE ‘JUG
,’DI YI SMON LAM SHIN TU DAG ‘GYUR ZHING,
,RGYAL BA RNAMS KYIS ‘GOG LAS SLONG BAR MDZAD,

		They seek,
		Again and again,

		To achieve an even
		Higher degree
		Of virtue.

		These great beings
Enter “Unmoving”;

This is where
They can absolutely
Never turn back,

And special prayers
Made by them
Reach an extraordinary
Level of purity,

		While the Victors
		Undertake to
		Rouse them from
		The cessation.


[3983]
BYANG SEMS SA BDUN PA BA DE NI YANG DANG YANG DU SNGAR GYI DGE BA LAS LHAG PA THOB PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR DU, SA GANG DU BYANG SEMS DE PHYIR MI LDOG PA NYID DU ‘GYUR BAS BRGYAD PA MI G-YO BA DE LA, BYANG SEMS BDAG NYID CHEN PO DE ‘JUG GO

This bodhisattva at the seventh level seeks, again and again, to achieve an even higher degree of virtue than what they had reached before.  And so it is that these great beings—these particular bodhisattvas—enter the eighth level, Unmoving; so called because this is the level at which the bodhisattva can absolutely never turn back.


[3984]
,DE LA YANG DANG YANG DU SNGAR SA BDUN PA MAN CHAD KYI DGE BA LAS LHAG PA THOB LUGS NI,

Now just how is it that these practitioners continue, over and over again, to attain virtue which is even higher than that they reached earlier, at the seventh level on down?


[3985]
SA BCU PA LAS, KYE RGYAL BA’I SRAS ‘DI LTA STE, DPER NA RGYA MTSO CHEN POR ‘GRO BA’I GRU BO CHE NI, RGYA MTSO CHEN PO LA MA THUG GI BAR DU CHED DU BSKYOD CING ‘GRO BAR BYA BA YIN TE, GANG GI TSE RGYA MTSO CHEN PO LA PHYIN MA THAG TU RLUNG GI DKYIL ‘KHOR GYIS BSKYOD NAS, CHED DU BSKYOD MI DGOS PAR ‘GRO STE, DES RGYA MTSO CHEN PO LA NYIN GCIG CHOD PA DE NI SNGON CHED DU BSKYOD CING ‘GRO BAS, LO BRGYAR YANG DE SRID DU TSAD MED PAR PHYIN PAR MI NUS SO,,

The Sutra on the Ten Levels puts it this way:

O child of the Victors, this is the way it is.  Think for example of a great ship bound for the great sea.  It continues its journey with purpose, moving on until it reaches this massive body of water.

And then suppose that, just after it has reached that greater sea, it is struck by a hurricane.  No longer do the sailors have to make any conscious effort to advance the ship; it moves across the great sea making more progress in a single day than it had made in all their sailing up to that point.  Not even in a hundred years would they have been able to move that far, beyond all limits.


[3986]
KYE RGYAL BA’I SRAS DE BZHIN DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ DGE BA’I RTZA BA’I TSOGS SHIN TU BSAGS PA, THEG PA CHEN PO YANG DAG PAR BSGRUB PA YANG, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’I SPYOD PA’I RGYA MTSOR PHYIN NAS LHUN GYIS GRUB PA’I YE SHES KYIS YUD TZAM ZHIG LA, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES JI TZAM GNON PA DE NI, SNGON GYI CHED DU BYA [f. 264a] BA’I LAS KYIS BSKAL PA ‘BUM DU YANG, DE SNYED DU DPAG TU MED PA GNON PAR MI NUS SO, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

And it is the same, o monks, with those bodhisattvas who have made a massive collection of the roots of virtue, and who have practiced the greater way perfectly.  Once they have come to the ocean of the deeds of the bodhisattvas, then spontaneous wisdom starts to have its effect on them, in even but a single moment, during which they are set upon by the wisdom of omniscience.  And they reach a place that they had never arrived at, even after a hundred thousand eons of concerted effort.  They could never have reached this place even with countless periods of trying, for that same amount of time.


[3987]
DE LA RGYA MTSOR MA PHYIN PA’I BAR NI SA BDUN PA MAN CHAD KYI DPE’O,,

In this metaphor, the time it takes just to reach the great ocean represents the period from the seventh bodhisattva level on down.


[3988]
RGYA MTSOR ZHUGS NAS ‘GRO BA NI SA BRGYAD PA THOB NAS LAM BGROD PA’I DPE’O,,

Finally entering and then traveling upon this ocean represents our journey along the path once we have attained the eighth bodhisattva level.


[3989]
SA BRGYAD PA BA ‘DI YI SMON LAM SNGON ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA’I SEMS DANG PO BSKYED PA NA, SMON LAM CHEN PO BCU LA SOGS PA’I SMON LAM ‘BUM PHRAG GRANGS MED PA PHRAG BCU BTAB PA DE DAG ,SA ‘DI LA SHIN TU DAG PA STE SMON LAM GYI PHAR PHYIN SA ‘DIR CHES LHAG PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

There are special prayers that are made by this bodhisattva who is on the eighth level.  Back when they first gave rise to the state of mind beyond the world, they made ten groups of innumerable prayers, the groups themselves numbering in turn a hundred thousand.  At this level then, these prayers reach an extraordinary level of purity; and so here they attain an especially extraordinary level of the perfection of prayer.


[3990]
SA ‘DI NI GZHON NU’I SAR GZHAG STE, DGU PAR RGYAL TSAB ‘THOB LA, BCU PAR NI ‘KHOR LOS SGYUR BA LTAR RGYAL BA RNAMS KYIS DBANG BSKUR RO,,

This particular bodhisattva level is considered a “level of the youth.”  At the ninth level, the bodhisattva attains the status of a regent to the crown; and then at the tenth level they are finally invested with the full authority of a Wheel Emperor.


[3991]
SA MI G-YO BAR ‘GOG PA CHOS NYID LA ZHUGS PA NA, RGYAL BA RNAMS KYIS ‘GOG PA LA ZHUGS PA DE LAS SLONG BAR YANG MDZAD DE,

When these bodhisattvas have entered into cessation, true nature, at the level of Unmoving, the Victors further undertake to rouse them from the cessation entered into.


[3992]
SA BCU PA LAS, KYE RGYAL BA’I SRAS DAG DE LTAR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’I SA MI G-YO BA ‘DI LA GNAS PA’I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ SNGON GYI SMON LAM GYI STOBS BSKYED PA DANG, CHOS KYI SGO’I RGYUN DE LA GNAS PA DE LA SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN ‘DAS RNAMS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA’I YE SHES NYE BAR SGRUB PAR MDZAD DE, DE LA ‘DI SKAD CES KYANG BKA’ STZAL TO,,

The Sutra on the Ten Levels puts it this way:

Consider again, o children of the Victors, those bodhisattvas who are situated in this way, at the bodhisattva level known as “Unmoving.”  They raise the force of the prayers they had made earlier, and remain there in the flow of the entrance of the Dharma.  And then they go further and come to achieving the wisdom of the Buddhas, the Conquerors—those who have Gone That Way.  And then they are spoken to, in the following high words.


[3993]
RIGS KYI BU LEGS SO LEGS SO, ,SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS RJES SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA LA ‘DI NI DON DAM PA’I BZOD PA YANG YIN NO,

O child of noble family, it is excellent, excellent.  What you are undertaking is ultimate perseverance in coming to a full realization of the Dharma of the Buddhas.


[3994]
‘ON KYANG RIGS KYI BU GANG NGED KYI STOBS BCU DANG, MI ‘JIGS PA BZHI LA SOGS [f. 264b] PA SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS MA ‘DRES PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE KHYOD LA MED KYI, SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE YONGS SU BTZAL BA’I PHYIR SBYOR BA BYOS SHIG ,BRTZON ‘GRUS RTZOMS SHIG ,BZOD PA’I SGO ‘DI NYID KYANG MA ‘DOR CIG

And yet, o child of noble family, as yet you still do not possess the ten forces that I possess, and my four types of fearlessness, and all the other of the excellent, unadmixed qualities of a Buddha.  As such, I urge you now to apply yourself in the pursuit of the totally excellent qualities of an Enlightened Being.  Gird yourself in your efforts.  And never abandon this particular doorway of forbearance.


[3995]
,RIGS KYI BU KHYOD KYIS DE LTAR ZHI BA’I RNAM PAR THAR PA LA GNAS PA THOB KYANG, BYIS PA SO SO’I SKYE BO MA ZHI BA RAB TU MA ZHIG {%ZHI} BA, NYON MONGS PA SNA TSOGS KUN TU BYUNG BAR GYUR PA, RNAM PAR RTOG PA SNA TSOGS KYIS YID G-YON SPYO BA ‘DI DAG LA SOMS SHIG

O child of noble family, it may well be the case that you are residing in the freedom of peace.  And yet I urge you to turn your thoughts to the infants, the common beings, who have no peace—who have no peace at all.  They are still plagued by a whole variety of different negativities; and their thoughts are still corrupted by a whole variety of imaginings.


[3996]
,GZHAN YANG RIGS KYI BU SNGON GYI SMON LAM DANG, SEMS CAN GYI DON THOB PAR BYA BA DANG, YE SHES KYI SGO BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB PA DRAN PAR GYIS SHIG

Moreover, o child of noble family, I urge you never to forget the prayers you have made in times gone by; and your duty to accomplish the goals of living beings; and the inconceivable doors of wisdom.


[3997]
,YANG RIGS KYI BU ‘DI NI CHOS RNAMS KYI CHOS NYID DO, ,DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS BYUNG YANG RUNG MA BYUNG YANG RUNG CHOS KYI DBYINGS ‘DI NI GNAS PA NYID DO, ‘DI LTAR CHOS THAMS CAD STONG PA NYID DANG, CHOS THAMS CAD DMIGS SU MED PA’O,,

And I remind you, o child of noble family, that this is the true nature of all existing things.  Whether Buddhas ever appeared in this universe, or failed to appear, this realm of all things is pure reality, itself.  Which is to say, each and every existing entity is emptiness; and nothing in the entire universe is to be found here.


[3998]
‘DIS NI DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS NYI TSE RAB TU DBYE BAR BYA BA MA YIN GYI, NYAN THOS DANG RANG SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYIS KYANG RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA’I CHOS NYID ‘DI ‘THOB BO, ZHES DANG,

And this is not some outline of things which is partial; that is, which fits only Those Who Have Gone That Way.  Rather, we can say that all of them—including the listeners and the self-made Buddhas—come to an attainment of this true nature of things, beyond all thought.


[3999]
GAL TE SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN ‘DAS DE DAG GIS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ DE LA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES MNGON PAR SGRUB PA’I SGO RNAMS SU GZHUG PA MA MDZAD DU ZIN NA, DE DE NYID KYI TSE YONGS SU MYA NGAN LAS ‘DA’ BAR ‘GYUR TE, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON BYA BA YANG [f. 265a] RGYUN CHAD PAR ‘GYUR RO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

And then we have—

If it were the case that the Buddhas, the Conquerors, were to fail to set the bodhisattva to entering the doorways where they could finally achieve the wisdom of omniscience, then at that very point they would instead pass into nirvana.  And then the flow of their efforts to accomplish the needs of every living being would be cut off.


[4000]
DE DAG GIS NI SA BRGYAD PAR RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA’I YE SHES LA DBANG SGYUR THOB NAS, DE TZAM LA MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA NA, DE LAS BSLANG NAS SANGS RGYAS KYI STOBS LA SOGS PA THOB PA’I RGYUR RJES THOB TU TSOGS GSOG PA LA BSKUL ZHING,

What this is describing is a point at which we have gained mastery over the wisdom, at the eighth bodhisattva level, where we are no longer imagining any self-existence.
