If we are in a balanced meditation on nothing more than this, then when we are awakened out of this meditation it serves to incite us to amassing the collection of goodness, in the aftermath, which would serve as a cause for our attaining the forces of an Enlightened Being, and so on.


[4001]
CHOS NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA’I MI RTOG YE SHES NYAN RANG GIS KYANG ‘THOB PAR GSUNGS PAS, DE KHO NA NYID KYI RTOGS PA YOD NA TSOGS GZHAN GSOG PA LA ‘BAD PA MI DGOS KYI, DE NYID LA GOMS PAS CHOG GO ZHES PA NI MI MKHAS PA’I BAB COL DU SMRA BA’O,,

So too, it has been stated that listeners and self-made buddhas can also attain that wisdom, beyond imagining any self-existence, with which one realizes—directly—the true nature of things.  As such, it is the ravings of a person who has no mastery when someone comes and says that—if you have reached the realization of suchness—then there is no need for you to make efforts in accumulating any other collections of good deeds; and that it will then be enough for you just to get used to this very thing.



Finishing off negative emotions

[4002]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second part from above; a description of how those at this level finish off all their negative emotions.


	[4003]
[VIII.2]
Sanskrit unavailable

,CHAGS PA MED PA’I BLO NI SKYON RNAMS
DAG DANG LHAN CIG MI GNAS PHYIR,
,SA BRGYAD PA LA DRI MA DE DAG
RTZA BCAS NYE BAR ZHI ‘GYUR ZHING,
,NYON MONGS ZAD CING SA GSUM BLA MAR
GYUR KYANG SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYI NI,
,’BYOR PA MKHA’ LTAR MTHA’ BRAL MA LUS [215b]
‘THOB PAR NUS MA YIN,

		The state of mind
		Free of attachment

		No longer remains
		Combined with
		The various faults.

		As such, here at
		The eighth level

		All these impurities,
		With their roots,
		
		Are put to their
		Final rest.

		So too, we put
		A finish to the
		Negative emotions;

		And we have become
		A spiritual teacher
		For all three grounds.

		They are though
		Still unable
		To achieve

		All the riches
		Of the Buddhas,

		Which like the sky
		Are without any limits [f. 215b].


[4004]
GANG GI PHYIR SA BRGYAD PA ‘DIR RGYAL BA RNAMS KYIS ‘GOG PA LAS SLONG BA DE’I PHYIR SA ‘DIR, CHAGS PA MED PA’I BLO STE

Because here at the eighth level the Victors rouse the bodhisattva from their cessation, at this level then we have a state of mind which is free of attachment.


[4005]
YE SHES NI CHAGS SOGS NYON MONGS PA’I SKYON RNAMS DAG DANG LHAN CIG TU MI GNAS PA’I PHYIR, SA BRGYAD PA LA NI RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA’I YE SHES KYI NYI MA SHAR BAS,

At this point, our wisdom no longer remains combined with the various faults of everything involved with the negative emotions of craving and the like.  As such, here at the eighth level the sun of the wisdom that no longer imagines things in a mistaken way rises high.


[4006]
MUN PA LTA BU’I DRI MA STE NYON MONGS PA SNGAR BYUNG BA ‘KHOR BAR SKYE BA’I RGYUR GYUR BA, KHAMS GSUM NA SPYOD PA DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG RTZA BA STE SA BON DANG BCAS PA NYE BAR ZHI BA STE SPANGS PAR ‘GYUR ZHING,

And something happens then to the impurities that are comparable to darkness here in the world; that is, to everything related to the negative emotions which—earlier on—served as causes for taking rebirth here in the cycle of pain.  That is, we are also able to put to their final rest—to eliminate—all these ways of carrying on a life in the three realms, along with the roots or deep seeds for them.


[4007]
DE LTAR NYON MONGS PA THAMS CAD ZAD CING SA GSUM STE KHAMS GSUM GYI BLA MAR GYUR KYANG,

So too, in this manner, we are able to put a finish to everything involved with the negative emotions; and then we have become a spiritual teacher for all three “grounds”—referring to the three realms.


[4008]
BYANG SEMS ‘DIS NYON MONGS ZAD PA’I GNAS SKABS DER, SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYI NI YON TAN GYI ‘BYOR BA {%PA} MKHA’ LTAR MTHA’ DANG BRAL BA MA LUS PA ‘THOB PAR NUS PA MA YIN PAS, DE THOB PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR SA BRGYAD PA BA ‘DIS BSGRIM PAR BYA [f. 265b] DGOS SO,,

And let’s further consider the bodhisattva at this point, where they have finished off the negative emotions.  They are though still unable to achieve all of the riches of the high qualities of the Buddhas, which like the sky itself are without any limits.  As such, this bodhisattva at the eighth level needs to focus their efforts further, in order to achieve these riches.


[4009]
‘O NA SA ‘DIR NYON MONGS THAMS CAD ZAD PAR CIS SHES SHE NA,

One may ask: “How is it that we know that—at this level—all the negativities have been finished off?”


[4010]
SA BCU PA LAS, ‘DIR DE NYID KYI TSE YONGS SU MYA NGAN LAS ‘DA’ BAR ‘GYUR TE, ZHES GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR, SA ‘DIR KHAMS GSUM LAS SEMS ‘DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA NYID YOD PA YIN TE, NYON MONGS CHAD PA’I {%TSANG BA’I? carvings say CHAD PA’I} ‘DOD CHAGS DANG MA BRAL BA LA MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA MNGON DU BYED NUS PA MED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

The Sutra on the Ten Levels says that “here, at this point in time, one achieves total nirvana.”  As such, it is at this bodhisattva level that we find a mind which is perfectly free from desire for the three realms of existence.  And this is because a person could never have the capacity to actualize the state of nirvana so long as they were still not free of a state of desire where the negative emotions are complete.



The ten powers of the eighth

[4011]
GSUM PA NI,

Which brings us to our third point from above: a description of how the bodhisattva at the eighth level does come to attain the ten powers.


	[4012]
[VIII.3]
Sanskrit unavailable

,’KHOR BA ‘GAGS KYANG DBANG RNAMS BCU PO
THOB PAR ‘GYUR ZHING DE DAG GIS,
,SRID PA’I ‘GRO BAR RANG GI BDAG NYID
SNA TSOGS STON PAR BYED PAR ‘GYUR,

		They have put a
Stop to the cycle;

Despite that,
We attain
The ten powers.

These allow them to
Display their person

As an entire variety,
To beings of
The suffering world.
		

[4013]
GAL TE SA ‘DIR KHAMS GSUM LA ‘DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL NA ‘KHOR BAR SKYE BA ‘GAG PAS, JI LTAR NA ‘DI YIS SANGS RGYAS KYI RGYU’I CHOS MA LUS PA YONGS SU RDZOGS PA BYED PAR ‘GYUR ZHE NA,

One may begin with the following question—

If, at this bodhisattva level, one is free of desire for the three realms, then they have stopped all rebirth in the cycle of pain.  How then is it that this individual acts to complete each & every one of those things which serve as a cause for Buddhahood?


[4014]
SA BRGYAD PA BA ‘DI YI LAS NYON GYI DBANG GIS ‘KHOR BAR ‘KHOR BA NI ‘GAGS MED {%MOD} KYANG, SA ‘DI THOB PA NA YE SHES LA DBANG BA SOGS KYI DBANG RNAM PA BCU PO THOB PAR ‘GYUR ZHING,

Admitted then that this bodhisattva at the eighth level has put a stop to circling in the cycle of pain due to the power of karma and negative emotions.  Despite that, when we do reach this particular level, we attain the ten different powers of achieving power over wisdom, and so on.


[4015]
DBANG BCU PO DE DAG GIS BYANG SEMS ‘DIS DPAL ‘PHRENG GI MDO LAS BSHAD PA LTAR GYI YID KYI RANG BZHIN GYI LUS KYI SGO NAS, SRID PA’I ‘GRO BA RNAMS SU RANG GI BDAG NYID KYI LUS SNA TSOGS PA STON PAR BYED PAR ‘GYUR BAS, ‘DI’I TSOGS YONGS SU RDZOGS PAR ‘GYUR BA MI ‘GAL LO,,

These ten powers allow the bodhisattva—as described in the Sutra of Shrimala—to become able to display their personal body as an entire variety of bodies, to those beings of the suffering world.  This is done through a physical form which has the nature of the thought.  As such, it is no contradiction to say that this particular individual’s accumulation of goodness has been completed, in its entirety.


[4016]
DBANG BCU NI BSKAL PA BRJOD DU MED PA’I YANG BRJOD DU MED PAR TSE’I TSAD BYIN GYIS RLOB PAS TSE LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

Here are the ten different powers:

1) The bodhisattva has achieved power over their lifespan, since—for groups of eons beyond description consisting of individual eons which are themselves beyond description—they have received blessings related to the length of their life.


[4017]
TING NGE ‘DZIN NGES PAR SEMS PA DPAG TU MED PA’I YE SHES KYI ‘JUG PAS SEMS LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

2) They have achieved power over their mind, since they have engaged in a wisdom consisting of unimaginable instances of deep absorption in meditation.


[4018]
‘JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS THAMS CAD RGYAN BKOD PA DU MAS RAB TU BRGYAN PA’I BYIN GYIS BRLABS KUN TU STON [f. 266a] PAS YO BYAD LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

3) They have achieved power over things, because they are able to display special blessings where all of the worlds are supremely decorated with a great many adornments.


[4019]
LAS KYI RNAM PAR SMIN PA BYIN GYIS BRLABS KYIS DUS JI LTA BA BZHIN DU STON PAS LAS LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

4) They have achieved power over karma, because they are able to display karmas at any time they may wish to, by performing blessings related to the ripening of karma.


[4020]
‘JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS THAMS CAD DU SKYE BA KUN TU STON PAS SKYE BA LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

5) They have achieved power over births, since they are able to display a birth in each and every one of the worlds there may be.


[4021]
SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING DANG, DUS GANG DU CI DGA’ BAR MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR BYANG CHUB PA KUN TU STON PAS SMON LAM LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

6) They have achieved power over prayer, since they are able to display Buddha paradises, and also—at whatever point in time they may wish—their own total enlightenment.


[4022]
‘JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS THAMS CAD SANGS RGYAS KYIS RAB TU GANG BA KUN TU STON PAS MOS PA LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

7) They have achieved power over wishes, because they are able to display all worlds as filled to the brim with Buddhas.


[4023]
SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING THAMS CAD DU RDZU ‘PHRUL GYI RNAM PAR ‘PHRUL BA KUN TU STON PAS RDZU ‘PHRUL LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

8) They have achieved power over emanating, because they are able to display emanations in each and every Buddha paradise.


[4024]
DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA’I STOBS DANG, MI ‘JIGS PA DANG, SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS MA ‘DRES PA DANG, MTSAN DANG, DPE BYAD BZANG PO DANG, MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR BYANG CHUB PA KUN TU STON PAS YE SHES LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,,

9) They have achieved power over wisdom, because they are able to display the powers of Those Gone Thus; their different forms of fearlessness; the unadmixed qualities of a Buddha; the excellent signs and marks upon an Enlightened Being’s body; and total enlightenment itself.


[4025]
MTHA’ DANG DBUS MED PA’I CHOS KYI SGO SNANG BA KUN TU STON PAS CHOS LA DBANG BA ‘THOB BO,

10) They have achieved power over the Dharma, for they are able to display the shining light of the doorways to the Dharma, without ends or middle.


[4026]
ZHES SA BCU PA LAS RGYA CHER GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

Here we have followed the extensive presentation of the powers as they are described in The Sutra on the Ten Levels.


	[4027]
[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA BRGYAD PA’O,,

		This concludes the eighth wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


[4028]
DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA’I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA DGONGS PA RAB TU GSAL BA LAS, DON DAM PA’I SEMS BSKYED PA BRGYAD PA’I BSHAD PA’O,,

This then concludes the explanation of the eighth ultimate “Wish for Enlightenment”—or chapter—in An Illumination of the True Intent, an extensive commentary to Entering the Middle Way.



The ninth level

[4029]
` ,,GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to the third part from above: our explanation of the ninth bodhisattva level


	[4030]
[IX.1]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DGU PA LA NI DE’I STOBS LTA ZHIG
MTHA’ DAG RDZOGS PAR DAG ‘GYUR ZHING,
,DE BZHIN YANG DAG RIG CHOS RANG GI
YON TAN YONGS SU DAG PA’ANG ‘THOB,

		At the ninth,
		The forces are
		Beyond description;

		All of them
		Become pure
		In a way which is
		Totally complete.

		In like manner
		They also achieve

		The different
		Total purities of
		Their fine qualities—

		The qualities of
		Pure understanding.		


[4031]
SA DGU PA LA NI BYANG SEMS DE’I STOBS LTA ZHIG STE STOBS KYI PHA ROL PHYIN PA MTHA’ DAG RDZOGS PAR DAG PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

At the ninth bodhisattva level the forces of this bodhisattva are beyond description; which is to say, all of the perfections of force become pure in a way which is totally complete.


[4032]
STOBS KYI PHAR PHYIN LA STOBS BCU BSHAD PA NI THUB PA DGONGS RGYAN LAS,

This description of the perfection of the forces as being ten forces can be found as follows, in the Jewel of the True Thought of the Able Ones:


[4033]
DE LA BSAM PA’I STOBS NI NYON MONGS PA KUN TU SPYOD PA MED [f. 266b] PA’I PHYIR RO,,

1) The “force of thought” is so called because they no longer engage in anything related to the negative emotions.


[4034]
LTAG {%LHAG} PA’I BSAM PA’I STOBS NI SA’I YE SHES YONGS SU SBYANGS PA NYID KYI PHYIR RO,,

2) The “force of personal responsibility” is so called because they have, indeed, perfectly purified the wisdom of the levels.


[4035]
GZUNGS KYI STOBS NI CHOS MI BRJED PA NYID GYI PHYIR RO,,

3) The “force of words of the holding” is so called because they have a perfect ability to avoid ever forgetting the Dharma.


[4036]
TING NGE ‘DZIN GYI STOBS NI RTAG TU RNAM PAR G-YENGS PA MED PA NYID KYI PHYIR RO,,

4) The “force of deep meditation” is so called because they are always perfectly free of any kind of mental distraction.


[4037]
YANG DAG PAR ‘BYOR BA’I STOBS NI MTHA’ YAS SHING MUR THUG PA MED PA’I ‘JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS KYI SPYOD PA RNAM PAR DBYE BA LA MKHAS PA NYID KYI PHYIR RO,,

5) The “force of applying themselves perfectly” is so called because they become absolute masters in every different variation of all the activities of the realm of the everyday world, endless as these are, beyond any possible limit.


[4038]
DBANG GI STOBS NI YID LA RE BA THAMS CAD YONGS SU RDZOGS PA THOB PA’I PHYIR RO,,

6) The “force of power” is so called because they have reached a point where they have totally fulfilled each and every hope of their hearts.


[4039]
SPOBS PA’I STOBS NI SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS THAMS CAD RNAM PAR SPYOD PA RNAM PAR DBYE BA LA MKHAS PA NYID KYI PHYIR RO,,

7) The “force of confidence” is so called because they are absolute masters in all the different divisions of activity for all the different kinds of Dharma ever taught by the Buddhas.


[4040]
SMON LAM GYI STOBS NI SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYI SPYOD PA LA SBYOR BA MI GTONG BA’I PHYIR RO,,

8) The “force of prayer” is so called because they never give up applying themselves in the activities of each and every Buddha.


[4041]
PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’I STOBS NI BDAG NYID KYIS SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS YONGS SU SMIN PAR BYED PA DANG, SEMS CAN YONGS SU SMIN PAR BYED PA DANG, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA PHAN PA’I SPYOD PA MI GTONG BA’I PHYIR RO,,

9) The “force of perfection” is so called because they never give up working themselves to bring to their complete ripening all the qualities of the Buddhas; and they never give up working to bring all living beings to this ripening; and they never abandon working for the benefit of every single being.


[4042]
BYAMS PA CHEN PO’I STOBS NI SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BSKYAB PA LA MCHOG TU SBYOR BA MI GTONG BA’I PHYIR RO,,

10) The “force of great love” is so called because they never give up their efforts to bring every living being to the highest form of protection.


[4043]
SNYING RJE CHEN PO’I STOBS NI SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI SDUG BSNGAL THAMS CAD SEL BAR BYED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

11) The “force of great compassion” is so called because they work to clear away all the sufferings of each and every living being.


[4044]
CHOS NYID KYI STOBS NI SGYU MA LTA BU LA SOGS PA’I CHOS NYID MNGON DU BYED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

12) The “force of the way things are” is so called because they have brought forth all the ways that things are—such as their being like an illusion.


[4045]
DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA THAMS CAD KYIS BYIN GYIS RLOB PA’I STOBS NI RNAM PA THAMS CAD PA’I THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES LA MNGON DU PHYOGS PAR GYUR PA NYID KYI PHYIR RO,

13) And then finally the “force of the blessings of each and every One Gone Thus” is so called because they are quite surely approaching the knowledge of all things, in all the forms it may take.


[4046]
ZHES PA MDO [f. 267a] SDER BSTAN PA’I STOBS RNAMS SO, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RO,,

These then are the forces that have been taught in the collection of sutras.


[4047]
STOBS KYI PHAR PHYIN RDZOGS PA DE BZHIN DU SO SO YANG DAG PAR RIG PA’I CHOS KYI RANG GI YON TAN YONGS SU DAG PA BZHI’ANG ‘THOB STE, CHOS DANG, DON DANG, NGES PA’I TSIG DANG, SPOBS PA SO SO YANG DAG PAR RIG PA BZHI’O,,

In addition to completing the perfection of the forces, in like manner do these bodhisattvas also achieve the four different total purities of their fine qualities—the qualities of pure understanding.  These are the four pure understandings of the details of the Dharma; of meanings; of different words for the same ideas; and of confidence.


[4048]
DE LA DANG POS NI CHOS RNAMS KYI RANG RANG SO SO’I MTSAN NYID RAB TU SHES SO,,

1) The first of these refers to the perfect knowledge of all the various defining characteristics for each and every existing object.


[4049]
GNYIS PAS NI CHOS THAMS CAD KYI RNAM PA’I DBYE BA SHES SO,,

2) The second refers to a knowledge of the different categories of all existing things.


[4050]
GSUM PAS NI CHOS RNAMS MA ‘DRES PAR SO SOR STON PA SHES SO,,

3) The third refers to a knowledge of how to teach each different thing, individually, without mixing them up in any way.


[4051]
BZHI PAS NI CHOS RNAMS KYI MTHUN PA’I RGYU RGYUN CHAD PA MED PA RAB TU SHES PAR

4) The fourth refers to a perfect knowledge of the uninterrupted flow of all of the conducive conditions for the different teachings.


[4052]
RANG ‘GREL LAS GSUNGS SO,,

These are the descriptions of the four, as we find them in the autocommentary.


[4053]
GZHUNG GZHAN LAS MING GI RNAM GRANGS KYI CHOS DANG, BRJOD BYA’I DON DANG, SGRA’I NGES PA’I TSIG DANG, SPOBS PA MI ZAD PA RIG PA LA BSHAD DO,,

In other sources we see the four explained as an understanding of the different names for the same things; of the meaning being expressed; of the etymology of the term; and of never-ending confidence.


	[4054]
[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA DGU PA’O,,

This concludes the ninth wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


[4055]
DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA’I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA DGONGS PA RAB TU GSAL BA LAS, DON DAM PA’I SEMS BSKYED PA DGU PA’I BSHAD PA’O,,

This then concludes the explanation of the ninth ultimate “Wish for Enlightenment”—or chapter—in An Illumination of the True Intent, an extensive commentary to Entering the Middle Way.



The tenth level

[4056]
` ,,BZHI PA NI,

With this we have reached our fourth point: an explanation of the tenth bodhisattva level.


	[4057]
[X.1]
Sanskrit unavailable

,BCU PA’I SA LA DE YIS KUN NAS
SANGS RGYAS RNAMS LAS DBANG BSKUR BA,
,DAM PA ‘THOB CING YE SHES LHAG PAR
MCHOG TU BYUNG BAR GYUR PA’ANG YIN,

JI LTAR DE BZHIN ‘GRO RNAMS KYI,
,DGE BA’I LO TOG CHED DU RGYAL SRAS

		At the tenth level,
		This one receives

		The highest investment
		Into power,

		From all the Buddhas
		Of every corner.

		High knowledge
		Also reaches
		Its highest expression.

		The rains
		Are sent down
		From the rainclouds;

		Just so, the
		Children of the Victors
		Also let the rain
		Fall, spontaneously,

		For the crops
		Of virtue among
		Living beings.		


[4058]
SA BCU PA LA GNAS PA’I BYANG SEMS DE YIS PHYOGS BCU KUN NAS, SANGS RGYAS RNAMS LAS ‘OD ZER CHEN PO’I DBANG BSKUR BA DAM PA STE MCHOG ‘THOB BO,,

This bodhisattva at the tenth level receives the highest—the supreme—investment into power, in the form of massive rays of light, from all the Buddhas residing in every corner of the universe.


[4059]
‘THOB TSUL NI BYANG SEMS ‘DIS TING NGE ‘DZIN GRANGS MED PA ‘BUM PHRAG BCU THOB PA’I THA MA LA, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES DANG KHYAD PAR MED PAR DBANG BSKUR BA DANG LDAN PA ZHES BYA BA’I TING NGE ‘DZIN MNGON DU ‘GYUR RO,,

Just how does this happen?  This bodhisattva attains all ten groups of the hundred thousand collections of “countless” forms of meditative concentration.  And then at the end of this process, they manifest that concentration which is known as “coming to possess an investment into power which in no way differs from the wisdom of omniscience.”


[4060]
DE NAS DE MA THAG TU STONG GSUM ‘BUM PHRAG BCU’I GTOS DANG MNYAM PA’I RIN PO CHE CHEN PO’I PAD+MA RIN PO [f. 267b] CHE RNAM PA THAMS CAD KYI MCHOG DANG LDAN PA ZHES BYA BA NAS,

And then it all follows the description we find in The Sutra on the Ten Levels:

Just after that then, there appears first a precious lotus—possessed of all the highest qualities—made of precious jewel; in extent, it matches the size of ten different groups of a hundred thousand galaxies of a billion planets each.


[4061]
RGYAS PAR STONG GSUM ‘BUM PHRAG BCUR TSAD PA’I RDUL PHRA RAB KYI RDUL SNYED KYI PAD+MA’I ‘KHOR DANG LDAN PA ‘BYUNG BAR ‘GYUR TE, 

And then (as the description continues) this lotus is surrounded by a group of lotuses equal in number to all the atoms there are, and equal in extent to ten groups of a hundred thousand galaxies of a billion planets each.


[4062]
BYANG SEMS DE’I LUS KYANG DE DANG ‘TSAM PAR GNAS SO,,

And the body of this bodhisattva matches the sizes here.


[4063]
TING NGE ‘DZIN DE THOB MA THAG TU PAD+MA DE LA ‘DUG PAR KUN TU SNANG NGO,,

And just after they attain that state of meditative concentration, they make their final appearance, upon that lotus.


[4064]
DE DE LA ‘DUG PA DANG, SANGS RGYAS SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING KUN NAS GDAN ‘DZOM PA RNAMS KYI MDZOD SPU NAS, 

Here then the bodhisattva takes their seat.  And then rays of light spring forth the pores of the skin upon every Buddha in every Buddha paradise there is, as these all gather together.


[4065]
‘OD ZER BYUNG NAS BYANG SEMS DE LA DBANG BSKUR BAR MDZAD DO, ZHES BYA BA’I BAR DU SA BCU PA LAS GSUNGS PA LTA BU’O,,

And the light goes forth, and grants the bodhisattva their investment into power.


[4066]
BYANG SEMS ‘DI LA PHAR PHYIN BCU’I NANG NAS YE SHES KYI PHAR PHYIN LHAG PAR MCHOG TU BYUNG BA STE DAG PAR ‘GYUR BA’ANG YIN NO,,

So too, for this bodhisattva the perfection of high knowledge—from among the ten different perfections—also reaches its highest expression; which is to say, it comes to its highest state of purity.


[4067]
YE SHES KYI NGOS ‘DZIN DANG DE DANG SHES RAB KYI PHAR PHYIN GYI KHYAD PAR NI, ,BYANG SA LAS,

How do we identify the kind of wisdom here?  And how does it differ from the perfection of wisdom?  Here is how The Levels of the Bodhisattva describes it—


[4068]
CHOS THAMS CAD LA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RNAM PAR BZHAG PA SHES PA NI, YE SHES KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’O,,

That knowing where we have gone into a balanced meditation on the real nature of each and every existing entity is the perfection of high knowledge.


[4069]
DE LA DON DAM PA ‘DZIN PA LA ZHUGS PA’I SHES RAB NI, SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’O,,

The wisdom where we have gone into holding to the ultimate is the perfection of wisdom.


[4070]
KUN RDZOB ‘DZIN PA LA ZHUGS PA NI YE SHES KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STE, ‘DI GNYIS KYI BYE BRAG NI DE YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

When we have gone into holding to the deceptive, then that is the perfection of high knowledge.  And that expresses the difference beween these two.


[4071]
CHAR SPRIN RNAMS LAS ‘JIG RTEN PA RNAMS KYI LO TOG SPEL BA’I SLAD DU CHU CHAR ‘BAB PA JI LTA BA

The rains are sent down from the rainclouds in order to multiply the crops of those living here in the world.


[4072]
DE BZHIN DU, GDUL BYA’I ‘GRO BA RNAMS KYI DGE BA’I LO TOG SPEL BA’I CHED DU, RGYAL SRAS SA BCU PA BA ‘DI LAS KYANG LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR DAM PA’I CHOS KYI CHAR MNGON PAR ‘BAB PA STE ‘BEBS SO,,

Just so, the children of the Victors residing here at the tenth bodhisattva level also “let the rain fall”; they drop down, generously, and spontaneously, the rain of the holy Dharma.  And this is all for the purpose of multiplying the crops of virtue among those living beings who are their disciples.


[4073]
DE’I PHYIR SA ‘DI LA CHOS KYI SPRIN ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

And this in fact is why this bodhisattva level is known as “The Rain of the Dharma.”


	[4074]
	[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA BCU PA’O,,

This concludes the tenth wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


[4075]
DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA’I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA DGONGS PA RAB TU GSAL [f. 268a] BA LAS, DON DAM PA’I SEMS BSKYED PA BCU PA’I BSHAD PA’O,,

This then concludes the explanation of the tenth ultimate “Wish for Enlightenment”—or chapter—in An Illumination of the True Intent, an extensive commentary to Entering the Middle Way.



High qualities
of the first level

[4076]
` ,,GSUM PA SA BCU’I YON TAN BSTAN PA LA GSUM, SA DANG PO’I YON TAN BSHAD PA, SA GNYIS PA NAS BDUN PA’I BAR GYI YON TAN BSHAD PA, DAG PA SA GSUM GYI YON TAN BSHAD PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us to our third more general step from above: a description of the high good qualities of the ten bodhisattva levels.  We’ll proceed in three parts: an explanation of the high good qualities of the first level; an explanation of the high good qualities of the second to the seventh levels; and an explanation of the high good qualities of the three pure levels.  Here then is the first of these.


	[4077]

At that point where we attain this first level of giving rise to the ultimate wish for enlightenment, this practitioner at the first level—in but a single instant in time, in but a moment—sees a million different Buddhas.  And these million Buddhas grant their blessing to the bodhisattva, and the bodhisattva perceives this blessing.

SA DANG PO LA GNAS PA DE NYID KYI TSE NA BSKAL PA BRGYAR GNAS PAR BYED PA DANG, BSKAL PA BRGYA LA SNGON DANG PHYI MA’I MTHAR YANG YANG DAG PAR ‘JUG GO

In this very moment that the bodhisattva resides at the first level, they are able to stay there for a million eons; and they engage perfectly in this million eons in both the beginning end and the final end of the period.


[4080]
,DE’I DON NI SNGON DANG PHYI MA’I MTHA’I BSKAL PA BRGYAR YANG YE SHES KYI MTHONG BA ‘JUG PA’O,,

What this last point means is that they engage in the seeing of wisdom for a million eons in both the beginning end, and the final end, of the period.

Each of these million various forms is, further, accompanied by a group of a million children of the Victors, which they display.  As such, they are rich in a lovely circle of followers.

two through seven

When this intelligent one residing at (1) the level of Perfect Happiness has attained those twelve different groups of a hundred high qualities each, they move to the second bodhisattva level.  And then they reside at (2) this level known as “Immaculate,” just as we explained them doing at the first level.  And they attain, perfectly, this same number of groups of high qualities (twelve), except that these are now composed of a thousand members of features each.

Let’s consider then these same twelve groups of high qualities at five different bodhisattva levels: the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and the seventh.  These five different bodhisattvas come to be completed—respectively—in (3) twelve groups of a hundred thousand high qualities each; (4) twelve groups of a billion high qualities each; (5) twelve groups of ten billion high qualities each; (6) twelve groups of a trillion high qualities each; and then finally becoming complete in (7) twelve groups of a hundred quintillion high qualities each; which is to say, twelve groups of a hundred thousand groups of ten million good qualities each.

High qualities of
the three pure levels

[4094]
GSUM PA NI,

And then this brings us to our third point from above: an explanation of the high good qualities the three pure levels.


[4095]
SA BRGYAD PA NAS YON TAN DE RNAMS GRANGS KYI GNAS KYIS BGRANG BAR MI NUS PAS, RDUL PHRA RAB RNAMS KYIS YONGS SU BGRANG BAR BSHAD PA,

From the eighth bodhisattva level on, it’s not possible to count the high qualities with any kind of existing numbers; as such, we need to express the count as equivalent to that of the number of atoms in selected bodies of the galaxy.


	[4096]
[afterword.6]
Sanskrit unavailable

		Unmoving has no

Let’s start with a person who is staying at the eighth bodhisattva level: Unmoving.  This individual, who has no mistaken thoughts holding to some true existence either of the person or things, “incorporates” a thousand galaxies of a hundred billion planets each.


[4098]

Which is to say, we would have to take all the atoms that existed in the worlds of three galaxies of a billion planets each.  And then the number of fine qualities that this particular bodhisattva attains is equal to that total.

We can moreover say that when this bodhisattva undertakes to show emanations, they do so without any running of motivation involving conceptual thought. This point is summarized in the section [from the autocommentary] that includes:

The phrase “as well” in the verse here is meant to include those beings not directly mentioned.  Those that are not so listed include worldly gods such as Destroyer of the Hundred Cities; Pure One; and Protector of the World; as well as kings among the humans, listeners, and self-made buddhas.


[4111]
DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GDUL BA’I SEMS CAN RNAMS LA BRGYA BYIN LA SOGS PA’I GZUGS BZUNG NAS LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR CHOS STON PAR NUS SO, ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA’I BAR GYI DON SDUD PA’O,,

The Ones Thus Gone are able to teach the Dharma spontaneously, by taking on for those living beings they seek to tame the form of Destroyer of the Hundred Cities, or whatever it might be.


[4112]
RGYAS PAR NI SA BCU PA LAS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

For more detail on these points, please refer to The Sutra on the Ten Levels.



How we first reach enlightenment

[4113]
GNYIS PA ‘BRAS BU’I SA LA LNGA, DANG POR SANGS RGYAS PA’I TSUL, SKU DANG YON TAN GYI RNAM GZHAG ,SPRUL PA’I SKU BSTAN PA, THEG PA GCIG TU BSGRUB PA, MNGON PAR BYANG CHUB PA DANG BZHUGS PA’I DUS KYI BSHAD PA’O,,

This brings us far back, to a second section promised, for a presentation on those levels which consist of the result.  Here we proceed in five steps: (1) the way in which we first reach our enlightenment; (2) a description of the holy body, and the fine qualities, that we then achieve; (3) a presentation concerning our emanation body; (4) a proof that in the end it is all a single path; and (5) an explanation of the point at which we have become enlightened, and remain there.


[4114]
DANG PO LA GNYIS, DNGOS KYI DON DANG, RTZOD PA SPANG BA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

The first of these steps has two parts of its own: the actual point, and then refuting argument on this point.  Here is the first.


	[4115]
[afterword.10]
Sanskrit unavailable

,GANG PHYIR NAM MKHA’ ‘DRI MA MED LA
ZLA SNANG GSAL BAR GYUR BA’I PHYIR,
,SNGON TSE STOBS BCU BSKYED PA’I SA LA

		It’s all because
The moon is shining
		In a perfectly clear sky—

		They make
		Great efforts further,
		At the level where,

		Earlier,
		They created
		The ten forces.

		This is found
		By them
		In “Below None”;

		Peace, the highest
		State of being:

		The ultimate among
		All high qualities,

[4116]
JI LTAR TE DPER NA ZLA BA’I SNANG BAS NAM MKHA’ DRI MA MED PA LA ‘GRO BA MA LUS PA GSAL BAR NUS PA

Think of how—when the moon is shining—it is able, in a perfectly clear sky, to provide light for each and every living being.


[4117]
DE BZHIN DU, SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS ‘THOB PA LA GEGS BYED PA’I MUN PA SBYONG BAR MDZAD PA THUGS BSKYED PA BCU PA BRNYES PAS,

It’s just the same when we have been able to clear away the darkness that acts as an obstacle to our achieving the qualities of an Enlightened Being, and reach the tenth “level of attaining the holy Wish.”


[4118]
RANG GIS SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS BRNYES NUS PAR MKHYEN NAS, SLAR YANG STOBS BCU PA SANGS RGYAS KYI SA BSKYED PA’I SNGON GYI SA BCU PA DER SANGS RGYAS KYI SA ‘THOB PA LA ‘BAD PA MDZAD PA’AM BRTZAMS PAR GYUR CING,

Knowing that we will now be able to achieve all the qualities of a Buddha, we apply ourselves further, and so this person with the ten forces makes great efforts to work at the tenth level that we had achieved earlier, in order to attain here the level of an Enlightened Being.  That is, the bodhisattva at the tenth level is in the act of creating a level of enlightenment itself.


[4119]
GANG GI DON DU ‘BAD PA ‘DI BRTZAMS PAR GYUR PA’I GO ‘PHANG MCHOG ZHI BA BLA NA MED PA’I YE SHES DE YANG, BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS ‘OG MIN DU [f. 270a] NI STE GNAS DE KHO NAR KHYOD KYIS BRNYES PAR GYUR TO,,

And let’s consider this goal that we are working for—exerting ourselves for.  This is the matchless peace, or wisdom, of the highest state of being.  And this is found by them only at a certain place: in the paradise known as “Below None,” where the Conquerors themselves reside.


[4120]
YE SHES DE NI YON TAN MTHA’ DAG GI MTHAR THUG PA STE, DRAN PA NYER GZHAG LA SOGS PA’I YON TAN MTHA’ DAG ‘DIR MTHAR THUG CING PHUL DU BYUNG BA’I PHYIR RO,,

This particular state of wisdom is the ultimate high quality among all the high qualities there are.  And that’s because each & every one of the extraordinary qualities of the different types of close awareness, and the like, reach their fullest and most perfect expression at this point.


[4121]
DE NI MTSUNGS PA MED PA YANG YIN TE, DE DANG ‘DRA BA MED PA’I PHYIR DANG, GONG NA MED PA’I PHYIR RO,,

These achievements are, moreover, beyond all equal; because there is nothing like them, and nothing above them.


[4122]
TSIG RKANG DANG PO’I ‘GYUR NI ‘GREL PA DANG BSTUN NA SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR ‘ONG DGOS LA, TSIG RKANG GNYIS PA LA NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS, SLAR YANG STOBS BCU BSKYED PA’I SNGON GYIS DER ‘BAD BA MDZAD GYUR PA, ZHES ‘BYUNG BA LTAR LEGS SO,,

If we interpret the first part of the verse here in accordance with the autocommentary, it comes out as we have already explained it here.  As for the second part of the verse, it comes out better if we follow the translation of Naktso, which reads: “That one from before undertakes to make continued efforts here, to give birth to the ten forces.”


[4123]
‘OG MIN KHO NAR ZHES GSUNGS PAS NI SNGAR SANGS MA RGYAS PA GSAR DU ‘TSANG RGYA BA’I RTEN LA ‘OG MIN PA DGOS PAR STON LA, SNGON SANGS RGYAS ZIN GSAR DU ‘TSANG RGYA BA’I TSUL STON PA ‘DOD PA KHAMS SU MDZAD PA YIN TE, PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’I THEG PA’I LUGS SO,,

When we use the expression “only in the One Below No Other,” what we are indicating is that a person who has never achieved Buddhahood before must first attain this state in a body & mind located in the level of Below No Other.  If though a person has already achieved enlightenment, and is going to pretend to reach it anew, then they do so in the desire realm.  That is, at least, according to the way of the perfections.


[4124]
‘OG MIN DU DANG POR ‘TSANG RGYA BA NA, BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KYIS SKAD CIG GCIG KHO NA LA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES BRNYES PAR STON PA NI,

The next lines here are meant to convey the idea that—when we do first become enlightened, in the paradise Below No Other—this Conqueror attains the wisdom of knowing all things in but a single instant of time.


	[4125]

,JI LTAR SNOD KYI DBYE BAS MKHA’ LA

		There are no distinctions

		At all engendered

		With suchness,
		Being a single song.

		This is something
		That you can
		Discern perfectly;

		As such,
		Those of you with

[4126]
JI LTAR TE DPER NA BUM PA DANG ‘KHAR GZHONG LA SOGS PA’I SNOD KYI MI ‘DRA BA’I DBYE BA DU MA YOD KYANG, MI ‘DRA BA’I DBYE BA DE YIS SNOD DE DAG TU GTOGS PA STE DER KHYAB PA’I NAM MKHA’ LA NI, SGRIB PA THAMS CAD BKAG TZAM DU MTSUNGS PA’I PHYIR, DE LAS GZHAN PA’I DBYE BA MED PA

Now there are many different types of vessels, such as a water pitcher or a bronze bowl.  But let’s consider what is contained in all those different kinds of vessels: the empty space that overarches them all.  All these empty spaces are exactly the same, in the sense that each of them is the simple absence of physical obstruction.  That is, there are no other distinctions to be made here.


[4127]
DE LTAR DU GZUGS DANG TSOR BA LA SOGS PA LA DNGOS PO STE RANG GI RGYU RKYEN GYIS BYAS PA’I DBYE BA MI ‘DRA BA DU MA YOD KYANG,

The case is the same with functional things like our physical form, or our feelings.  It is true, first of all, that there are many different distinctions among these objects, from the point of view of each of them having been produced by its own causes & conditions.


[4128]
DE DAG [f. 270b] TU GTOGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA’I SKYE BA MED PA’I DE KHO NA NYID LA, DNGOS POS BYAS PA’I DBYE BA ‘GA’ YANG MED PA DE’I PHYIR DE KHO NA NYID NI RO MNYAM PA STE RO GCIG KHO NAR SHES PAR BYA’O,,

If though we consider the suchness of these objects—the fact that they are devoid of anything included into them which could exist through any nature of its own—we can say that there are no distinctions at all here that were engendered by any functional entities.  And thus it is that you should understand that, with suchness, everything “tastes the same,” meaning that it is all but a single song.


[4129]
RO MNYAM DE YANG MKHYEN PA’I SKAD CIG GCIG KHO NAS YANG DAG PAR THUGS SU CHUD PAR MDZAD PAR GYUR PAS NA, MKHYEN PA BZANG PO CAN KHYOD KYIS SKAD CIG GIS NI SHES BYA THAMS CAD THUGS SU CHUD PA’I YE SHES BRNYES SO,,

This fact of being a single song is something that even just a single millisecond of true knowledge can discern perfectly.  As such, those of you possessed of excellent understanding can—in even just a moment—come to find that wisdom which grasps, in their entirety, all the knowable things in the universe.



An argument against
how we reach enlightenment

[4130]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, PHYOGS SNGA MA DGOD PA DANG, LUGS DE DGAG PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us to our scond part from above, which is refuting argument about the way in which we first reach our enlightenment.  We cover this in two sections: phrasing the position of the other party, followed by its refutation.


	[4131]

,GANG TSE ZHI BA DE NYID YIN NA

[4132]
RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PA NI GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI DE KHO NA NYID DO, ZHES RNAM PAR ‘JOG CING DE YANG BLOS SHES PA YIN NO ZHES ‘JOG NA,

And so suppose one comes with the following objection:

You have set forth, as your position, the idea that the fact that nothing can start through any nature of its own is the essential nature of form and other types of entities.  And you have stated, in addition, that this is something that can be known by the mind.


[4133]
GANG GI TSE RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA ZHI BA NI, DE KHO NA NYID DO ZHES RNAM PAR ‘JOG PA DE’I TSE,

Now consider this point at which you have posited putting to its rest the idea that things could arise through some nature of their own, and referring to this state as the true nature of things.


[4134]
YUL DE LA RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU BLO GROS TE SHES RAB MI ‘JUG PAR KHAS BLANG DGOS TE, ‘DI LTAR RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PA’I DE KHO NA NYID LA BLO DE ‘JUG PA NA, BLO DE YUL CI’I RNAM PA CAN CIG TU ‘GYUR TE MI ‘GYUR RO,,

You would, then—at the same time—have to accept the fact that intelligence (which is to say, wisdom) could never engage in this particular object in any manner at all.  And this is because—if the mind were to engage in a true nature of things where nothing could ever grow through any quality of its own—one would have to ask the question of which object’s aspect this mind could ever assume.  Because, it could never in fact do that.


[4135]
DE’I PHYIR YUL GYI RNAM PA GANG YANG ‘CHAR BA MED PAS DE KHO NA NYID LA BLO MI ‘JUG GO

As such, we would have to say that there was no object aspect that made its appearance here at all.  And if that were true, then the mind could never engage in some true nature of things.


[4136]
,YUL CAN GYI BLO YUL LA MA ZHUGS PAR NI SHES BYA’I YUL BLOS NGES PAR RIGS PA’ANG MA YIN PAS,

The fact is though that the idea that a subject state of mind could never engage in any object of perception is not something that could ever make sense with the engagement of the mind in any of the knowable objects there are.


[4137]
DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON ‘DI YONGS SU SHES PAR ‘GYUR BAR JI LTAR ‘OS, 

And how then could it ever be appropriate to speak of coming to some thorough understanding of the meaning of suchness?


[4138]
YONGS SU SHES PA MED PA NI DE KHO NA NYID SHES PA’O, ZHES BYA BAR MI RIGS PA’I PHYIR TE,

Because the simple reason for that is that it would be inappropriate for you to come and say, “The complete absence of complete understanding is what comes and grasps the true nature of things.”


[4139]
YUL KUN NAS SHES PA MED PAR NI SHES PAR JI LTAR ‘GYUR TE ‘GAL BAR ‘GYUR BA’I [f. 271a] PHYIR RO,,

And that’s because it would be a complete contradiction to posit some state of knowing where you had no comprehension of anything!


[4140]
DE KHO NA NYID LA ‘JUG PA’I SEMS SKYE BA STE ‘BYUNG BA MED NA YANG, DE KHO NA NYID MKHYEN PA PO MED PAR ‘DI LTA BU’I MTSAN NYID CAN GYI DE KHO NA NYID NGAS THUGS SU CHUD DO ZHES KHYED KYIS GDUL BYA GZHAN DAG LA SU ZHIG GIS STAN PAR BYED PA

And so here you are, going around saying that you have comprehended, completely, a suchness like this, and that now you will have to go and teach it to anyone else—any disciple—that you can find.  That is, even though you have yet to give rise to any state of mind where you are engaging in suchness—even though it just hasn’t happened yet for you—you are going around describing some state of things with certain characteristics when as yet there is no one here who actually comprehends suchness.


[4141]
RIGS TE MI RIGS SO ZHE NA,

Is that something you’d say was logical?  Because it certainly doesn’t seem logical to us!



Refuting the idea
that realizing suchness
is mistaken

[4142]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA MI ‘THAD PA’I RTZOD PA SPANG BA, MKHYEN PA PO MI ‘THAD PA’I RTZOD PA SPANG BA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

Which brings us to our second point from above: our actual refutation of argument on the way in which we first reach our enlightenment.  Here we proceed in two steps: refuting argument which says that the idea of realizing suchness is mistaken; and then refuting argument which says that our idea about the one who gains the knowledge in this case is mistaken as well.


	[4143]

		When this is being
		Its suchness

		The mind is devoid
		Of any starting.

		At this point,
		Their resting upon

		Of suchness.

		Let’s say
		That a particular
		State of mind
		
		Has taken on
		The aspect.

		This is it
		Having a
		Comprehension
		Of the object [f. 216b].

		Just so
		We refer to
		A knowledge
		
		In reliance upon

[4144]
‘JIG RTEN ‘DI NA SHES PA YUL DE’I RNAM PA’I RJES SU BYED PA NYID ‘DZIN PA NA, SHES PA DES YUL DE RIG PAR BRJOD DE,

Now in this world, if a state of mind grasps to a particular object, through the very act of following its particular aspects, then we say that this mental state has known the object in question.


[4145]
JI LTAR TE DPER NA SEMS NI YUL SNGON PO GANG GI RNAM PA CAN DU SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA NA, SEMS DE YIS YUL SNGON PO DE YONGS SU SHES SO ZHES BRJOD PA

Let’s say for example that a particular state of mind arises which has taken on the aspect of blue.  This is itself what we refer to as “it,” the mind, having a comprehension of the object, blue.


[4146]
DE BZHIN DU YUL CAN GYI SHES PA YUL DE KHO NA NYID JI ‘DRA BA DE ‘DRA BA’I RNAM PA CAN DU SKYE BA NA, THA SNYAD KYI BDEN PA LA BRTEN NAS DE KHO NA NYID RIG PA YIN NO ZHES NYE BAR GDAGS SO,,

Just so is it when a subject state of mind arises with the aspect of suchness, reflecting the state of that object.  And then we refer to this as a knowledge of suchness which has occurred in reliance upon nominal reality.


[4147]
SHES PA DE KHO NA NYID KYI RNAM PA’I RJES SU BYED TSUL NI, GANG GI TSE RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PA YUL GYI DE KHO NA NYID YIN ZHING STE YIN PA

How is it then that the mind takes on the aspect of suchness?  Let’s consider that point in time when the object of the mind is being—or is—its suchness: the fact that things cannot start through any nature of their own.


[4148]
BZHIN DU, DE’I YUL CAN GYI BLO YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA DANG BRAL BA’I RNAM PA CAN DU CHU LA CHU BZHAG PA BZHIN DU ZHUGS PA

Just so, the subject state of mind here has an aspect of being devoid of any starting through some nature of its own.  As such, the situation is the same as when we pour water into a glass which already has some water in it.


[4149]
DE’I TSE, YUL DE’I RNAM PA STEN PA STE ‘DZIN PA NYID LAS, DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PAR ‘JOG PA’I PHYIR SNGAR GYI RTZOD PA’I SKYON MED DO,,

At this point, the resting upon or the very holding of this aspect is established as the realization of suchness.  As such, our presentation is free of the faults that you are arguing it possesses.


[4150]
NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS, DE TSE DE’I DE NYID RTOGS PA DE’I RNAM PA ‘DZIN PA NYID YIN TE, ZHES ‘BYUNG BA LTAR LTA BU MED PA DAG PA YIN NO,,

The translation of Naktso reads, “at this point, the realization of the real nature of it is quite certainly holding its aspect.”  That is, we don’t see the wording “as though” in his version.  This reading is the accurate one.


[4151]
‘DIR RANG ‘GREL LAS, [f. 271b] DE’I PHYIR BTAGS PA LAS DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS SO ZHES RNAM PAR BZHAG GI ,DNGOS SU NA ‘GA’ ZHIG ‘GA’ ZHIG GIS SHES PA NI MA YIN TE, SHES PA DANG SHES BYA GNYIS KA YANG MA SKYES PA NYID KYI PHYIR RO,

At this juncture, the autocommentary reads:

As such, the way we describe it is by saying, “Suchness is realized through labeling.”  It is not the case that some number of things are perceived by some number of things directly.  And that’s because neither the state of mind nor what it knows displays any kind of starting at all.


[4152]
ZHES GSUNGS PA’I BTAGS PA LAS ZHES GSUNGS PA’I DON NI, THA SNYAD BRTEN NAS RIG PA YIN, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS RIG PA MIN PAR BTAGS PA TZAM LAS RIG PAR ‘JOG PA’I DON YIN GYI, DE KHO NA NYID RIG PA BTAGS PA BAR ‘JOG PA MIN NO,,

How then do we understand the expression “through labeling” here?  As the line goes, “We perceive based on a term.”  That is, the meaning of “perceiving” here is established only as occurring through labeling; we do not perceive things through some essential nature of their own.  It is not though that we are here establishing the perception of suchness itself as something labeled.


[4153]
DNGOS SU NA ZHES SOGS KYI DON NI SPROS BRAL GYI RNAM PA SHAR BA CES LAS RIG PA MIN PAR SNGO SER SOGS KYI RNAM PA ‘DRA BA CIG SHAR NAS RIG PA MIN TE,

When the autocommentary mentions “directly” at this juncture, it is not the point that the perceiving occurs through an aspect of being free of all elaboration making its appearance.  It is not that we are here perceiving things in a way similar to how the aspect of blue or of yellow might make its appearance.


[4154]
YUL DE KHO NA NYID MA SKYES PA YIN PA BZHIN DU, YUL CAN YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA’I RNAM PA CAN YIN PAS SO ZHES PA’I DON NO,,

Rather, what’s being said here is that the object of suchness is something that has never started and—just so—the subject state of mind too is something with an aspect of not having started, through any nature of its own.


[4155]
DE LTAR NA PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRA BA POS BLO LA DE KHO NA NYID KYI RNAM PA ‘CHAR RGYU MED PA DANG, YUL DE’I RNAM PA MA SHAR NA BLO YUL LA MI ‘JUG PA DANG, MA ZHUGS NA YUL DE MI SHES PA DANG, MA SHES NA YUL CAN DE SHES PAR ‘GAL LO ZHES SMRA BA’I

And so what those who take the former position are saying is that the aspect of suchness is not something that could ever make its appearance to the mind.  And if the aspect of the object could never make its appearance, then the mind could never engage in the particular object.  And if the mind did not engage, then it could never perceive this object.  And if it could not, then it would be a contradiction to say that this subject state of mind were mind at all.


[4156]
YUL GYI RNAM PA MA SHAR NA BLO MI ‘JUG PA LA SOGS PA RNAMS RANG YANG DE LTAR ‘DOD PAS, DE LA LAN MI ‘DEBS PAS BLO LA DON DAM BDEN PA’I RNAM PA ‘CHAR RGYU MED PA BKAG NAS,

We as well would agree that if no aspect of the object ever made its appearance, then ideas like the mind failing to engage would indeed follow.  And so rather than offering a response to that idea, we undertake to deny the idea that no aspect of ultimate reality could ever make its appearance to the mind.


[4157]
DE’I RNAM PA BLO LA ‘CHAR BA DANG, DE SHAR BA LAS YUL DE RTOGS PAR ‘JOG CES DPE DANG BCAS PAR GSUNGS PAS,

And so what we describe is a situation where just such an aspect is indeed making its appearance to the mind, and where we establish that one perceives this object through its having made such an appearance—and we add a metaphor for this as well.


[4158]
LUGS ‘DI LA DON DAM BDEN PA RTOGS PA’I MI RTOG YE SHES MED PAR SMRA BA NI, ‘PHAGS PA’I RTOGS PA MCHOG LA [f. 272a] SKUR BA ‘DEBS PA YIN NO,,

As such, when in the system described they claim that there is no such thing as a non-conceptual state of wisdom which realizes ultimate reality, they are in fact discrediting the supreme realization of The Arya.


[4159]
‘DIR SKAD CIG GIS NI SHES BYA THUGS SU CHUD, CES SKAD CIG GCIG KHO NAS THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES BRNYES PA DANG, JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES KYIS RIG BYA RIG BYED DNGOS  SU THA DAD PA’I TSUL DU SNANG NAS MI MKHYEN PAR GSUNGS PA RNAMS LA,

Now let’s go back to the line where it said, “In even just a moment, we grasp all the knowable things in the universe”; the point being that we achieve the state of omniscience in but a single instant of time.  And what this is also saying is that it is not the case that the wisdom which realizes the way things really are achieves this realization through the object of the state of mind, and the state of mind itself, appearing directly as separate entities.


[4160]
SANGS RGYAS KYIS JI LTA BA DANG JI SNYED PA MKHYEN TSUL LEGS PAR SHES DGOS PAR SNANG BAS, MDOR BSDUS PA CIG BRJOD PAR BYA’O,,

Given such pronouncements, it would appear that we need to make a special effort to come to a really good understanding of how a Buddha knows both the way that all things are, and the total quantity of the things there are.  As such, I will describe this topic here, in brief.



How Buddhas know all things,
and the way of all things

[4161]
‘DI LA SANGS RGYAS MA THOB PAR {%BAR} DU BLO GCIG GIS SKAD CIG MA GCIG LA CHOS CAN SO SOR SNANG BA DANG, CHOS NYID GNYIS KA DNGOS SU MKHYEN PA MI ‘ONG BAS DE GNYIS MKHYEN PA RES ‘JOG TU ‘ONG NGO,,

On this point, we can begin by saying that—until such time as a person becomes a Buddha—it is not possible for their mind, in a single moment of time, to perceive—directly—both the individual appearance of selected objects and the true nature of these objects.  As such, at this point our perception of these two things has to occur in a successive manner.


[4162]
BDEN ‘DZIN GYI BAG CHAGS MA LUS PA ZAD DE SANGS RGYAS PA NAS DUS RTAG TU DON DAM BDEN PA MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA’I MNYAM GZHAG LA BZHUGS PAS, DE LAS BZHENGS PA’I MNYAM RJES RES ‘JOG MED PA’I PHYIR DANG,

Then comes a point when we are able to finish off all of the deep seeds for the tendency to hold things as being real, and reach our own enlightenment.  From this time on, we are forever in a deep meditation where we are perceiving, directly, ultimate reality.  As such, we no longer engage in a successive state, in the sense of first being in deep meditation and then coming out into what is termed the “aftermath” of that meditation.


[4163]
BDEN GNYIS RANG ‘GREL LAS,
,MKHYEN PA’I SKAD CIG GCIG GIS NI,
,SHES BYA’I DKYIL ‘KHOR KUN KHYAB CAN,

The autocommentary to The Two Realities puts it this way—

A single second
Of this knowledge

Embraces the entire globe
Of things that could
Ever be known.


[4164]
ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR YIN PAS MNYAM GZHAG GI YE SHES DE LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA’I JI SNYED PA MKHYEN PA’I RJES THOB KYI YE SHES MED PA’I PHYIR NA, YE SHES GCIG GIS BDEN PA GNYIS KYI SHES BYA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAR ‘DOD DGOS SO,,

Given that things are the way these lines describe them, there is no “aftermath” state of knowledge that perceives the total quantity of knowable things and is also essentially discrete from the wisdom of deep meditation, at this point.  As such, we would have to take the position that it is possible for a single state of high wisdom to perceive all knowable objects subsumed by both realities.


[4165]
GANG GI TSE CHOS NYID LA LTOS TE JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES SU SONG BA DE’I TSE BLO DE’I NGOR GNYIS SU SNANG BA THAMS CAD NYE BAR ZHI BAS YE SHES DE CHU LA CHU BZHAG PA BZHIN DU RO GCIG TU ZHUGS [f. 272b] PA YIN LA,

Now there is a point where, relative to the real nature of things, our state of mind becomes the wisdom which knows the way in which things are.  At this juncture, all appearances of things as being dual have been put to a complete rest.  Our high knowledge at this point has gone into the fact of a single song—like water poured into water.


[4166]
GANG GI TSE CHOS CAN LA LTOS TE JI SNYED PA MKHYEN PAR SONG BA DE’I TSE, YUL YUL CAN SO SOR SNANG BA’I GNYIS SNANG YOD KYANG, GNYIS SNANG ‘KHRUL BA’I BAG CHAGS DRUNGS PHYUNG BAS SNANG YUL LA MA ‘KHRUL BA’I GNYIS SNANG YIN GYI ‘KHRUL BA’I GNYIS SNANG MIN TE, ‘DI MA ‘KHRUL BA’I TSUL GZHAN DU LEGS PAR BSHAD ZIN TO,,

At some point, relative to the object at hand, our state of mind passes into the knowledge of all the things there are.  At this stage, there is present a duality in the sense of the object and the subject state of mind appearing as two different things.  By now though we have torn out, from its very roots, the deep seed for error involving duality.  As such, we can say that here we have a sense of duality which is not mistaken about the object which is appearing to it; but which is not that sense of duality which is in error.  The exact way in which this mental state is not mistaken is something that I have covered quite nicely elsewhere.


[4167]
SANGS RGYAS KYI SAR MNYAM GZHAG DANG RJES THOB KYI YE SHES GNYIS KA YOD PAR NI RGYUD BLA MA LAS,

The point that, at the level of a Buddha, we possess both types of wisdom—the one which is in deep meditation, and the one which is subsequent to that state—is described in The Higher Line as follows—


	[4168]
,SHES RAB YE SHES RNAM GROL RNAMS,
,GSAL DANG ‘PHRO DANG DAG PHYIR DANG,
,THA DAD MED PHYIR ‘OD DANG ZER,
,NYI MA’I DKYIL ‘KHOR RNAMS DANG MTSUNGS,

Wisdom, high knowledge,
And complete freedom

Are the same as the light,
And the shining,
And the purity;

So too because
They are nothing separate,

They are equivalent
To the light,
And the rays,
And the very disk of the sun.


[4169]
ZHES PA’I ‘GREL PAR DE LA SANGS RGYAS KYI RGYUD LA MNGA’ BA’I ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA’I SHES RAB NI, SHES BYA’I DE KHO NA NYID DAM PA’I MUN PA SEL BAR NYE BAR GNAS PA’I PHYIR, ‘OD GSAL BA DANG CHOS MTSUNGS SO,,

The commentary to these lines puts it this way:

The wisdom possessed in the mindstream of an Enlightened Being—the type which is no longer perceiving things in any mistaken way—exists in a manner where it acts to clear away that ultimate form of darkness: the one that obscures the suchness of knowable things.  As such, it is comparable to shining light.


[4170]
DE’I RJES LA THOB PA SHES BYA THAMS CAD KYI YE SHES NI SHES BYA’I DNGOS PO MA LUS PA RNAM PA THAMS CAD LA ‘JUG PAS NI ‘OD ZER GYI DRA BA ‘PHRO BA DANG CHOS MTSUNGS SO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

The state of wisdom which is attained subsequent to that first wisdom is the high knowledge of all existing entitites.  It engages in each and every knowable entity in every possible manner, and so it is comparable to the sending out of a vast net of light rays.


[4171]
‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA NI MNYAM GZHAG YIN LA, DE YANG DE KHO NA NYID LA LTOS NAS ‘JOG PA NI DE KHO NA NYID DAM PA ZHES SOGS KYI DON NO,,

That state of mind beyond the world, no longer seeing things in a mistaken way, refers to deep meditation; and where this is established relative to suchness, it is the “highest” form of suchness.  This and the like explain the wording here. 


[4172]
RJES LA THOB PA ZHES PA’I RJES KYI DON NI, MNYAM BZHAG LAS LANGS PA’I RJES ZHES DUS SNGA PHYI’I RJES MIN GYI, MNYAM GZHAG DE’I STOBS KYIS THOB PA’AM BYUNG BA’I DON NO,,

Now when we say that something is “attained in the aftermath,” what exactly is the “aftermath” here?  When we refer to “the aftermath of rising out of deep meditation,” the emphasis of the term “aftermath” is not to indicate that one thing is happening after another.  Rather, the point is that something is attained, or occurs, due to the power of the deep meditation.


[4173]
SHES BYA ZHES SOGS KYI DON NI RJES THOB KYI YE SHES DE SHES BYA JI SNYED PA THAMS CAD LA [f. 273a] ‘JUG PA’I SGO NAS ‘JOG PA’O,,

And when they talk about “existing entities” here, the point is that the wisdom attained in the aftermath engages in each and every existing entity, or knowable thing—in the exact total number that there are.


[4174]
DES NA CHOS CAN LA LTOS TE JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA MIN LA, CHOS NYID LA LTOS TE JI SNYED PA MKHYEN PA MIN NO,,

As such, the knowledge of the way that all things are is not something that is established relative to the entity with the quality; and neither is the knowledge of the total amount of things established relative to the real nature of things.


[4175]
DON ‘DI LEGS PAR SHES NA BDEN GNYIS LAS
,BRTAGS PA’I NGO BOS DBEN PA YIS, 
,JI LTAR SNANG BA ‘DI KHO NA,
,BRTEN TE SKYES PA THAMS CAD NI,
,THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAS MNGON SUM GZIGS,
ZHES DANG,

If we have a good understanding of this point, then we can grasp the import of the following lines from The Two Realities:

	Everything that arises
	Through dependence,

	And that very thing
	Where objects appear
	
	As if they were devoid
	Of being labeled

	Is seen directly
	By the state of all-knowing.


	[4176]
,GANG TSE SHES DANG SHES BYA DANG,
,BDAG NYID RJES SU MI MTHONG BA,
,DE TSE MTSAN MA MI ‘BYUNG PHYIR,
,GNAS PA BRTAN PHYIR MI BZHENGS SO,

And so too with this other verse:

	When one no longer
	Sees any combination
	Of knowing
	And what is known,

	Then the signs of things
	No longer appear.

	And because the way
	A person stays is then firm,
	They no longer arise.


[4177]
ZHES SANGS RGYAS KYIS SNANG BA JI SNYED PA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU MKHYEN PA DANG, YANG GNYIS SU SNANG BA’I TSUL GYIS SHES PA DANG SHES BYA GANG YANG MI MTHONG BAR GSUNGS PA DANG,

What this is saying is that an Enlightened Being knows, directly, the total amount of things that ever appear.  At the same time though, they see nothing—neither knowing nor what is known—in a manner where these appear in a dualistic way.


[4178]
CHEN PO GZHAN DAG GIS KYANG DE DANG ‘DRA BAR GSUNGS PA RNAMS LA, SHES PA DANG SHES BYA GANG YANG MI MTHONG BA SANGS RGYAS RANG SNANG GI DBANG DU BYAS SHING, SHES BYA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU GZIGS PA GDUL BYA GZHAN SNANG GI MKHYEN TSUL YIN PAS,

Other great thinkers too have made the same sort of statements; and then we can say about these pronouncements that not seeing any state of mind, or anything known, at all relates to how things appear to the Buddha themselves; and then being able to see all existing entities directly relates to the way in which this being sees things appearing as something other to disciples.


[4179]
SANGS RGYAS KYI SAS BSDUS PA’I YE SHES MED CES ZER MI DGOS PAR YE SHES GCIG NYID YUL GNYIS LA LTOS TE, MKHYEN TSUL MI ‘DRA BA GNYIS ‘ONG BA LA ‘GAL BA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAR SHES PA’I PHYIR RO,,

As such, there is no need for making a claim that there is no state of wisdom at all which is taken in by the level of an Enlightened Being.  That is, one should understand that there is not the slightest contradiction in saying that we can get two different ways of no more than a single state of wisdom knowing things, relative to two different objects of knowledge.


[4180]
‘O NA DNGOS KUN YANG DAG BRDZUN PA’I MTHONG BA YIS, ZHES SOGS KYIS BDEN PA GNYIS KYI MTSAN NYID BSTAN PA DANG, RNAM GZHAG ‘DI GNYIS ‘GAL BAR ‘GYUR RO SNYAM NA,

One may return here with the following assertion—

Earlier on in the root text, we had that verse about “seeing what is pure, and what is a lie,” and so forth, presenting definitions for the two different kinds of reality.  But don’t that explanation, and the one found here, contradict each other?


[4181]
MI ‘GAL TE BDEN GNYIS KYI MTSAN NYID SNGAR BSHAD [f. 273b] PA NI SPYIR BTANG LA DGONGS LA, SANGS RGYAS KYI YE SHES KYI MKHYEN TSUL NI SA BCU PA MAN CHAD DANG, THUN MONG MA YIN PA DMIGS BSAL GYI DBANG DU BYAS PA YIN PA’I PHYIR RO,,

And yet in fact there is no contradiction here.  The definition presented earlier for the two realities was meant only to be a general description; it was made only with reference to the way in which the high knowledge of a Buddha does its knowing at the tenth level on down; and so it was treating a special case, not something typical.


[4182]
DE’I PHYIR SANGS RGYAS KYI MKHYEN TSUL YANG BSDUS PA’I DBANG DU BYED NA NI YANG DAG PA MTHONG BA’I RIGS SHES TSAD MAS RNYED PA DANG, YUL DE LA RIGS SHES TSAD MA YIN PA NI, DON DAM BDEN PA’I MTSAN NYID YIN LA, DES KUN RDZOB BDEN PA’I MTSAN NYID KYANG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

And so suppose we were to give a more inclusion description of how it is that an Enlightened Being does their knowing.  Let’s think about how the knowledge that sees total purity locates its object, with an accurate perception.  And saying that this is a knowledge of that object which is an accurate perception should be understood as a definition relative to ultimate reality—but as offering a definition of deceptive reality as well.


[4183]
DE BZHIN DU JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES KYIS RNYED CING YUL DE LA JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES SU SONG BA DANG, JI SNYED PA MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES KYIS RNYED CING YUL DE LA JI SNYED PA MKHYEN PAR SONG BA’I SGO NAS, YUL SO SO LA LTOS NAS KUN RDZOB DANG DON DAM MKHYEN TSUL YANG SHES PAR BYA’O,,

In the same way, the wisdom which knows the way in which things are locates the object, and then becomes wisdom towards that object which knows the way things are.  And this wisdom that knows all the things there are finds its objects, and then becomes the wisdom towards those objects that knows all things.  We should understand then the way that we know the deceptive and the ultimate relative to the respective objects.


[4184]
‘DIR SNGAR RANG RIG ‘THAD MI ‘THAD DPYAD PA BYAS PA’I RANG LUGS KYANG DRAN PAR BYA’O,,

At this juncture, we can as well recall the position that we ourselves took back when we were examining whether the concept of apperception was correct or not.



The actual point
on gaining knowledge

[4185]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DNGOS KYI DON DANG, DE’I ‘THAD PA DNGOS BSTAN PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

With this we have come to our second point from above: refuting argument which says that our idea about the one who gains the knowledge in this case is mistaken as well.  This we present in two sections: the actual point, and then a direct demonstration of how it is correct.  Here is the first. 


[4186]
GANG YANG KHYOD KYI LUGS LTAR NA MKHYEN PA PO MED PAR GDUL BYA GZHAN LA DE KHO NA NYID NI ‘DI LTA BU’O ZHES SU ZHIG GIS STON ZHES BRJOD PA DE LA YANG LAN BRJOD PAR BYA STE,

One might start with the following question:

According to your system, if there were no one who had done the knowing, then who is it that would sit and teach someone else—a disciple—that “here is what this suchness is like”?   And we are ready to give you an answer on that point here.


[4187]
SANGS RGYAS KYI SA’I DE KHO NA NYID ‘JAL BA’I SHES PA ‘DI YUL RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PA’I DON DAM DANG RO GCIG TU ZHUGS PA BDEN MOD KYANG, ‘JIG RTEN NA DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA MI SRID PA YANG MIN NO, ,DE JI LTAR ZHE NA,

Now let’s admit that—at the level of an Enlightened Being—this knowledge that holds suchness under its consideration is engaging, in a single song, along with its object: the fact that there is nothing which ever starts through any nature of its own.  Even so, you say that it is not an impossibility—even in the everyday world—that people could realize suchness.  Just how is that?


[4188]
RTZOD PA ‘DI’I DON NI DE KHO NA NYID LA RO GCIG PA’I TSUL GYIS RTAG TU BZHUGS PA YIN NA, CHOS STON PA’I KUN [f. 274a] SLONG GI RNAM RTOG DANG BCAS PA’I STON PA PO MED LA, DE MED NA CHOS STON PA MED CES PA’I DON YIN TE,

The point of this particular argument is as follows.  There can be no one who is doing teaching who—if they are remaining at all times inside of emptiness, in the manner of a single song—could also entertain a normal thought where they were motivated to teach the Dharma.  And if they could not, then there could be no teaching of the Dharma.


[4189]
‘DI’I ‘OG NYID NAS RNAM RTOG MED KYANG CHOS STON PA ‘THAD PA’I LAN GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR,

We see then the immediately following verse, which is meant to express an answer describing how—even without having a normal thought—someone could indeed teach the Dharma.


	[4190]
[afterword.14]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DE YI LONGS SPYOD RDZOGS SKU BSOD NAMS KYIS,
,ZIN DANG SPRUL PA MKHA’ GZHAN LAS DE’I MTHUS,
,SGRA GANG CHOS KYI DE NYID STON ‘BYUNG BA,
,DE LAS ‘JIG RTEN GYIS KYANG DE NYID RIG

	The holy body
	Of this one
	
	Complete in
	Its enjoyments

	Is embraced
	By merit.

	And from
Emanated bodies

	From the sky
	And other things,

	Due to the mystic
	Power of these,
	
	The sound that
	Comes forth

	Teaches the
	Suchness of things.

	From this then
	The world

	Comes as well
	To know suchness.


[4191]
RTZOD PA ‘DI LA LAN BRJOD PAR BYA STE, SANGS RGYAS RNAMS GZUGS KYI SKU GANG LA BZHUGS NAS CHOS KYI DBYINGS CHOS KYI SKU MNGON SUM DU MDZAD PA’I SANGS RGYAS

Here then is the answer that we would give to this argument.  Here is what happens after the Buddhas have entered their holy body of form, and then make their holy body of the Dharma—the realm of all things—manifest.


[4192]
DE YI GZUGS KYI SKU NI, BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS BRGYA PHRAG DU MAS ZIN PA STE MNGON PAR ‘DU BYAS PA’I BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB PA SNA TSOGS PA’I GZUGS MNGA’ BA,

The physical body of this Enlightened Being is “embraced”—which is to say, brought together—by many millions of collections of merit.  Thus it is that they possess a form with many different variations of inconceivable good qualities.


[4193]
BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYI CHOS KYI LONGS SPYOD KYI RGYUR GYUR PA’I LONGS SPYOD RDZOGS PA’I SKU YIN PAS, SKU DE LAS SGRA GANG ZHIG ‘BYUNG BA CHOS KYI DE KHO NA NYID STON PA

This is the holy body which is “complete in its enjoyments,” in the sense that it provides the cause for the bodhisattvas to enjoy the experience of the Dharma.  The sound that comes forth from this holy body teaches the suchness of things.


[4194]
DE LAS ‘JIG RTEN TE GDUL BYA CHOS DE LTA BU NYAN PA’I SNOD DU GYUR PAS KYANG DE KHO NA NYID PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR RIG PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And it is from this then that the “world”—referring here to disciples—who are worthy vessels to listen to just such a teaching of the Dharma come as well to know suchness, in an unerring manner.


[4195]
BSOD NAMS BRGYAS BSKYED PA’I SKU LAS DE LTAR ‘BYUNG BA LTA ZHOG ,LONGS SKU DE’I BYIN RLABS KYIS SPRUL PA DANG,

And it is not only from the holy body produced by millions of good deeds that these kinds of teachings come forth.  There are further, first of all, the bodies that are emanated through the blessings of this body of enjoyment.


[4196]
DE TZAM DU MA ZAD KYI GZHAN YANG SPRUL PA DE YI MTHUS NAM MKHA’ DANG, GZHAN RTZVA DANG SHING DANG RTZIG PA DANG BRAG LA SOGS PA SEMS MED PA LAS SGRA GANG ZHIG CHOS KYI DE NYID STON PA ‘BYUNG BA DE LAS KYANG GDUL BYA RNAMS KYIS DE KHO NA NYID RIG PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And not only that.  Teachings also come forth, due to the mystic power of these emanations, from the sky and from “other things”—which includes for example the simple grass, or trees, or the walls of buildings, or caves: things without their own mind, each one making their own sound.   And these sounds give forth teachings on the very nature of all things; and from that, disciples come to understand suchness itself.



The one who gains knowledge

[4197]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second section from above: a direct demonstration of how our position about the person who gains knowledge is correct.


[4198]
YANG JI LTAR SEMS DANG SEMS BYUNG GI RNAM RTOG MED PA NI, DE LTAR STON PA’I DUS DA LTA KUN SLONG GI BYA BA MI SRID KYANG, CHOS STON PA’I BYA BA ‘BYUNG BA’I RGYUR ‘GYUR SNYAM NA,

The following question then might occur to one.  Here we have a mind, and mental functions, that are without any kind of conceptual thought; and so in the time that things like those we’ve described happen, it is impossible—in the present moment—for there to be any activity of motivation.  And yet still these mental entities act as a cause for the occurrence of the activity of teaching the Dharma.


[4199]
DE BSTAN PA’I PHYIR DPE DGOD PA NI,

In order to clarify this point, we the following metaphor is presented.


	[4200]
[afterword.15]
Sanskrit unavailable

,JI LTAR RDZA MKHAN STOBS CHEN LDAN PAS ‘DIR,
,YUN RING CHES ‘BAD PAS BSKOR ‘KHOR LO NI,
,DE’I RTZOL DE {%DA?} LTAR SKYES PA MED BZHIN DU’ANG,
,’KHOR ZHING BUM PA LA SOGS RGYUR MTHONG LTAR,

		It’s like how
		Here, a potter
		
		Possessed of great
		Strength puts forth
		Great effort.

		Even though for
		Quite some time

		They have made
		No current efforts,

		We can see it
		Still spinning,

		Acting as a cause
		For a pot or the like.


[4201]
JI LTAR TE [f. 274b] DPER NA ‘JIG RTEN ‘DIR RDZA MKHAN STOBS CHEN PO DANG LDAN PAS ‘BAD PA CHEN POS BSKOR BA’I ‘KHOR LO NI, DE ‘DAS NAS YUN RING DU SONG BAS RDZA MKHAN DE’I ‘KHOR LO BSKOR BA’I ‘BAD RTZOL DA LTA SKYES PA MED BZHIN DU’ANG, ‘KHOR LO DA ‘KHOR ZHING RDZA BUM LA SOGS PA’I RGYUR MTHONG BA LTAR,

It’s like how—here in the everyday world—a potter who is possessed of great strength puts forth great effort to spin their potter’s wheel.  And then even though quite some time may have passed during which the potter is making no current efforts to spin their wheel, even after the original effort is long gone we can see that this same wheel is still spinning, and still able to act as a cause for a new clay pot, or the like.


	[4202]
[afterword.16]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DE BZHIN DA LTA SKYES RTZOL MED BZHIN DU,
,CHOS KYI BDAG CAN SKU NYID LA BZHUGS DE’I,
,’JUG PA SKYE BO’I DGE DANG SMON LAM GYI,
,KHYAD PAR GYIS ‘PHANGS LAS CHES BSAM MI KHYAB,

		In the same way,
		There is no longer
		Conscious effort

		Which has arisen in
		The present moment;

		At the same time though
		Their engagement continues,

		Residing as they are
		In an identity

		Consisting of
		The holy body
		Of all things.

		The good deeds
		Of beings,

		And their
		Extraordinary prayers,

		Project—and
		From that, it is
		Far beyond
		Any imagining.
		 

[4203]
DE BZHIN DU SANGS RGYAS PA’I TSE DA LTA SKYES PA’I ‘BAD RTZOL GYI RTOG PA MED BZHIN DU, CHOS KYI SKU’I BDAG NYID CAN NYID LA BZHUGS PA’I SANGS RGYAS DE’I ‘PHRIN LAS ‘JUG PA NI,

In the same way, once one has reached enlightenment, there is no longer any conceptual thought, conscious effort, which has arisen in the present moment.  At the same time though the holy activity of this Enlightened Being—residing as they are in an identity consisting of the holy body of all things—continues with their engagement.


[4204]
YID BZHIN GYI NOR BU DANG DPAG BSAM GYI SHING DANG ‘DRA BAR, SANGS RGYAS LAS DE ‘DRA BA’I CHOS THOS PAR ‘GYUR BA’I LAS YONGS SU SMIN PA’I DGE BA GDUL BYA’I SKYE BOS BSAGS PA DANG,

What happens then is similar to what occurs with a wish-giving gem, or a tree that fulfils all of ones wishes.  That is, there is a certain power to the good deeds that beings who are disciples have accumulated; and there is a full ripening of their karma to hear, from an Enlightened Being, certain specific teachings.


[4205]
SANGS RGYAS KYIS SNGON BYANG SEMS GYI SKABS SU SMON LAM KHYAD PAR CAN BTAB PA’I MTHUS ‘PHANGS PA STE SHUGS LAS YIN PAS, CHES SHIN TU BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB PA YIN NO,,

Moreover, the extraordinary prayers that this Buddha has made previously—during the time when they themselves were a bodhisattva—are able to project their power.  As such, from this tremendous force, the ripening is far beyond any imagining.


[4206]
SMON LAM JI LTA BU ZHE NA,

And just what kind of prayers are the ones that are made here?


[4207]
JI LTAR ‘TSAM PAR SEMS CAN GYI DON SGRUB PA LHUR MDZAD CING, CHOS KYI DBYINGS LAS SKAD CIG KYANG MI BSKYOD LA, SEMS CAN GDUL BA’I DUS LAS KYANG MI ‘DA’ BA DE ‘DRA BAR BDAG KYANG GYUR CIG ,CES PA’O,,

In these prayers, we have said to ourselves:

There are those who are able, spontaneously, to serve the needs of all living beings, in just the right way.  And at the same time, they never budge from the realm of all things, even for a moment.  Moreover, they never shift out of that period during which they are working to tame living beings.  May I too become like them!


[4208]
‘DIR DE’I SHAS {%SHES} BYED KYI MDO DRANGS PA NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS ‘BYUNG NGO,,

If you would like to see the sutra passages that provide the source for this description, you can find them in the translation of Naktso.



The holy body of all things

[4209]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, SKU’I RNAM GZHAG DANG, STOBS KYI YON TAN GYI RNAM GZHAG GO

Which brings us to our second point from above: a description of the holy body, and the fine qualities, that we then achieve.  We proceed in two sections: a presentation of the holy bodies; and then a description of the fine qualities of the forces.


[4210]
,DANG PO LA GSUM, CHOS KYI SKU DANG, LONGS SPYOD RDZOGS PA’I SKU DANG, RGYU MTHUN PA’I SKU BSHAD PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

The first of these we cover in three parts of its own: an explanation of the holy body of all things; an explanation of the holy body complete in all enjoyments; and an explanation of corresponding holy bodies.  Here is the first of these.


[4211]
DE NI CHOS KYI SKU’I DBANG DU BYAS NAS BSHAD PA,

The next part of the root text then relates to holy body of all things.


	[4211]
[afterword.17]
Sanskrit unavailable

,SHES BYA’I BUD SHING SKAM PO MA LUS PA,
,BSREGS PAS ZHI DE RGYAL RNAMS CHOS SKU STE,
,DE TSE SKYE BA MED CING ‘GAG PA MED,
,SEMS ‘GAGS PAS DE SKU YIS MNGON SUM MDZAD,

		The dry firewood of
		Each and every one of
		The knowable objects
		Is burned;

		And the peace
From that is
		The holy body
		Of all things.

		At this point, it is
Without any starting,
And without any stopping.

They have put a stop
To the mind; as such,

		This is manifested directly
		By the holy body.


[4212]
YUL CAN YE [f. 275a] SHES KYI RANG BZHIN TE BDAG NYID CAN GYI SKU GNYIS SU SNANG BA’I SHES BYA’I YUL BUD SHING SKAM PO DANG ‘DRA BA MA LUS PA, YE SHES ME DANG ‘DRA BAS BSREGS PA LAS,

Let us consider first the two holy bodies whose identity consists of the nature of the subject state of high knowledge.  Each and every one of the knowable objects, all objects of perception, that there are make their appearance to these two, in a manner where they resemble dry firewood.  And then these are burned by that high knowledge which is like to the fire.


[4213]
SHES BYA RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PA JI ‘DRA BA DE ‘DRA BA’I RNAM PA CAN DU ZHUGS PAS, SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA DE’I RNAM PA CAN DANG LDAN PAR GYUR BA’I DE KHO NA NYID ZHI BA DE NI RGYAL BA RNAMS KYI CHOS KYI SKU’O,,

This knowledge engages in the things it knows in a manner which reflects the fact that no knowable entity ever starts through any nature of its own.  Thus then the suchness which reflects the fact that knowledge itself never began through any nature of its own—this state of peace—is the holy body of all things which belongs to the Victorious Buddhas.


[4214]
‘DI NYID KYI DBANG DU MDZAD NAS RDO RJE GCOD PA LAS,
,SANGS RGYAS RNAMS NI CHOS NYID LTA,
,’DREN PA RNAMS NI CHOS KYI SKU,
,CHOS NYID SHES BYA MA YIN TE,
,DE NI SHES PAR NUS MA YIN,

It is in this context that the Diamond Cutter Sutra says,

The Buddhas view the nature of things;
Our guides are the bodies of reality.

Those for whom this nature of things
Is beyond the things they know
Will never be able to know things.


[4215]
ZHES SANGS RGYAS RNAMS NI DUS KUN TU CHOS NYID LA LTA BA STE DE LA MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA DANG, ‘DREN PA RNAMS KYI DON DAM PA’I SKU NI CHOS KYI SKU DANG, CHOS NYID DE MKHYEN PA NA’ANG GNYIS SU SNANG BA’I TSUL GYIS SHES PAR BYA BA MIN PAR GSUNGS SO,,

What this is saying is that the Buddhas are—at every moment—"viewing” the true nature of things; which is to say, they are in deep meditation upon this nature.  We also learn that the ultimate body of these guides is their holy body of all things; and that their ability to know the very nature of things is not, however, something that does its knowing in a way where things appear in a disparate way.


[4216]
DE KHO NA NYID KYI CHOS KYI SKU ‘DI NI, DE’I TSE SKYE BA MED CING ‘GAG PA MED PA STE ‘DI’I DBANG DU MDZAD NAS, ‘JAM DPAL SKYE BA MED CING ‘GAG PA MED PA ZHES BYA BA ‘DI NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA’I TSIG BLA DAGS SO ZHES MDO SDE LAS GSUNGS SO,,

This body of all things, of suchness, is—at this point—without any starting, and without any stopping.  And it is with respect to this fact that we see in sutra the statement:

O Manjushri, the expression “nothing starts and nothing stops” is just another way of saying “Those Gone Thus.”


[4217]
DE LTAR NA SANGS RGYAS KYI SAR YE SHES KYI YUL DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON LA, RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU DE’I YUL CAN GYI SEMS DANG SEMS LAS BYUNG BA’I RNAM RTOG ‘GAGS SHING MI ‘JUG PAS, RNAM PAR MI RTOGS {%RTOG} PA’I YE SHES DANG DE KHO NA NYID GNYIS CHU LA CHU BZHAG PA BZHIN DU DBYER MED PAR ZHUGS SO,,

Thus it is that—at the level of a Buddha—the subject state of mind, and mental functions, operate in a way where they have put a stop to all conceptual states of mind, in a state of high knowledge which no longer engages in that way, in any manner at all, in the object of perception which is the fact of suchness.  As such, the Buddha enters into high knowledge “which is no longer thinking,” and suchness here—these two—engaged indivisibly, like water poured into water.


[4218]
DE’I PHYIR GO ‘PHANG DE NI DANG POR LONGS SPYOD [f. 275b] RDZOGS PA’I SKU YIS MNGON SUM DU MDZAD PA STE BRNYES PAR KUN RDZOB TU RNAM PAR BZHAG GO ,NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS DE’I SHES BYED DU PHYIR MI LDOG PA’I ‘KHOR LO’I MDO DRANGS PA SNANG NGO,,

And so this enlightened state is first “manifested” directly—which is to say, achieved—by the holy body which is complete in all enjoyments; it is established in a deceptive manner.  In the translation of Naktso, it would appear that he is referencing the Sutra of the Unstoppable Wheel in support of this description.


[4219]
SEMS ‘GAGS PA ZHES GSUNGS PA’I DON NI, TSIG GSAL LAS, MDO LAS, DON DAM PA’I BDEN PA GANG ZHE NA, GANG LA SEMS KYI RGYU BA YANG MED NA, ,YI GE RNAMS LTA SMOS KYANG CI DGOS, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,

Just what does this expression—“stopping the mind”—refer to?  A Clarification of the Verses puts it this way:

We see the following in sutra: “And just what is ultimate reality?  It is that towards which the mind never runs; and so what need to mention, as well, words?”


	[4220]
[afterword.18a]
Sanskrit unavailable

	And the holy body:
