[4221]
DE LTAR NA RNAM PAR RTOG PA MED PA YIN NO, ZHES SEMS KYI RGYU BA RNAM RTOG MED PA LA GSUNGS PA DANG,

As such, when we see the expression “there is no longer thinking,” what it’s referring to is that there is no running of the mind in a conceptual way.


[4222]
‘DIR RANG ‘GREL LAS KYANG, ZHI BA’I DON SEMS SEMS BYUNG DANG BRAL BA LA BSHAD NAS, ZHI BA DE YIN YANG SEMS CAN GYI DON MDZAD NUS PA GSAL BAR BYED PA’I DPER,

The autocommentary on this point also explains the meaning of “peace” as being free of mind and mental functions.  And then it goes on to a metaphor to clarify how it is that—nonetheless—we are still capable of acting on behalf of living beings.


[4223]
DPAG BSAM GYI SHING DANG YID BZHIN GYI NOR BU BKOD PA’I MTHAR, ‘DI RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA YIN DU ZIN KYANG, DPAG BSAM GYI SHING DANG YID BZHIN GYI NOR BU LTAR, ZHES RNAM RTOG GI SEMS SEMS BYUNG DANG BRAL BA LA GSAL BAR GSUNGS PAS,

The work first gives a description of the examples of a tree that fulfils all our wishes, or else a wish-giving gem.  And then at the end there it speaks of how—even though these objects are ones without any kind of thought—we are similar here to the tree that fulfils all wishes, and the wish-giving jewel, in that we are “crystal-clear”; meaning that we are free of any conceptual thought, in mind or mental functions.


[4224]
SANGS RGYAS LA YE SHES MED PA’I KHUNGS SU ‘DREN PA NI GZHUNG GI DON MA RTOGS PA’I SKUR ‘DEBS CHEN PO’O,,

As such, when we see people quoting this section as the source for some idea that the Buddhas possess no high knowledge, this is a grave philosophical debasement where they have failed utterly to understand the import of the text.



The holy body
complete in enjoyments

[4225]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of the holy body complete in all enjoyments.  


[4226]
SKU GANG GIS CHOS SKU MNGON DU MDZAD PA’I LONGS SKU ‘DI NI, SEMS SEMS BYUNG GI RTOG PA DANG BRAL BAS NA ZHI BA’I SKU’O,,

The body that we employ to actualize the holy body of all things is the body of enjoyments.  And because this latter is devoid of any conceptual thought involving mind and mental functions, we call it the “holy body of peace.”


[4227]
DE LTAR RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA YIN YANG SEMS CAN GYI DON MDZAD PAR NUS PA GSAL BAR BYED PA NI, DPAG BSAM GYI SHING LTA BU DANG, YID BZHIN GYI NOR BU JI BZHIN DU RNAM PAR MI RTOG PAR GDUL BYA’I ‘DOD PA’I DON SGRUB PA’I RGYU NYID DU ‘GYUR RO,,

This holy body never entertains any normal kinds of thoughts; but still we make it crystal-clear that it is still capable of working for the good of beings.  What happens is that this body acts as a perfect cause for achieving all the goals that disciples may wish for, in a way that resembles a tree which grants our every wish; or which is comparable to a wish-giving jewel.  Which is to say, there is no normal thinking process involved.


	[4228]

This body of enjoyment represents a Wish for enlightenment which is free of all elaboration; and it only makes its appearance to those individuals who have reached a level where they have attained the mirror of a completely spotless state of high knowledge, due to their accumulation of the two collections.

Everything from a single pore

With this we have reached our third part from above—an explanation of corresponding holy bodies.  This we cover in three sections of its own: their holy body, and the way in which they display all of their activities within a single pore of their body; the way in which they display all the activities of others in that location; and an explanation of how they have the perfect power to carry out their wishes.  Here is the first of these.


[4236]

The next section is meant to explain the following.  We are talking now about a holy body which will have come about through the mystic power of the holy body of all things, or else that of the physical body described earlier here.


[4237]
SNGAR BSHAD PA’I LONGS SKU LAS GZHAN DU GYUR PA SPRUL PA’I SKU’I NGO BO NYID CHOS LONGS KYI RGYU MTHUN PA STE ‘BRAS BU’I SKU GANG DAG, 

And it is something different from the holy body of enjoyment; it is the holy body of emanation, which has an essential nature where it is a resulting body, with the bodies of all things and enjoyment acting as its concordant cause.


[4238]

It has appeared due the cause of seeking to tame living beings; and as we will see here, its forms possess a certain feature of power—which is completely inconceivable.

Buddhas and bodhisattvas though know that the nature of entities is that they possess a quality of being similar to an illusion; and possess no distinction of being true or false. Thus we can say that those of you who are individuals of wisdom should neither fail to imagine that such a thing could be, nor—even when you do understand it—continue to entertain any doubts about it.  Armed with an understanding of the metaphor we have offered, you should rather increase your aspiration for these things.


	[4269]
[afterword.25]
Sanskrit unavailable

And so it is the case that these very same kinds of activities—and all the various activities of an Enlightened Being—can be displayed by these holy beings all at the same time, and from every single pore of their skin.


[4271]
DUS GSUM GYI BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’ DANG, DUS GSUM GYI RANG RGYAL ‘PHAGS PA DANG NYAN THOS MA LUS PA’I SPYOD PA DANG, DE RNAMS KYI LHAG MA SO SO SKYE BO’I GNAS SKABS KYI SPYOD PA THAMS CAD NI, BA SPU’I KHUNG BU GCIG TU DUS GCIG GI TSE STON PAR NUS SO,,

The same is the case with the activities of each & every one the bodhisattvas of the past, present, and future; and with all the realized beings who are self-made buddhas; and the listeners too.  And then we can add to these “all the rest”—referring to all the activities that they undertook during that period when they were common beings.  That is, they are able to display all of these in a single moment, within but a single pore of their body.



Carrying out their wishes

[4272]
GSUM PA NI,

Here then is our third section here: an explanation of how these beings have the perfect power to carry out their wishes.


[4273]
DE LTAR SKU GSUM PHUN SUM TSOGS PA BRJOD NAS RNAM RTOG MI MNGA’ YANG BZHED PA LA MNGA’ ‘AM DBANG BSGYUR BA PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

Now that we have described all these perfectly excellent qualities of the three holy bodies, we present lines to speak of how—even though these beings possess no conceptual thought at all—they can still carry out their wishes: they still have a perfect capacity to do so.


	[4274]
[afterword.26]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DAG PA ‘DI NI BZHED PA
‘JUG PA YIS,
,RDUL GCIG YUL LA MKHA’ GTUGS
‘JIG RTEN DANG,
,’JIG RTEN MTHA’ YAS PHYOGS KHYAB

		This thing
		Is cleaned;

		Engaging in the
		Wish to do so,

		Worlds extending
		To space are in
		A single atom.

		Admitted they can
		Display an atom
		Spreading to
		Infinite planets;

		But that atom
		Does not become
		More gross;

		Nor does that planet
		Become more fine.


[4275]
DRI MA MA LUS PAS DAG PA’I SANGS RGYAS KYI MDZAD PA ‘DI NI, BZHED PA TZAM GYI ‘JUG PA YIS TE DE’I SGO NAS NAM MKHA’ YI MTHAS GTUGS PA’I ‘JIG RTEN RNAMS RDUL PHRA RAB GCIG GI YUL GYI KHYON LA STON PAR NUS LA,

Let’s consider “this thing”: the holy deeds of an Enlightened Being, who has cleaned themselves of each & every impurity there is.  “Engaging in no more than the wish to do so”—that is, with nothing more than this, they are able to display these deeds in the “land” of but a single tiny atom of the entire quantity of worlds that extend to the very ends of space itself.


[4276]
[f. 278a] ‘JIG RTEN MTHA’ YAS PA STE MA LUS PA’I RTEN GYI KHYON, RDUL PHRA RAB GCIG GIS KHYAB PA YANG STON PAR MDZAD PA NA, RDUL GCIG PO DE RAGS PA CHE BAR YANG MI ‘GYUR LA, ‘JIG RTEN PHRA BA STE CHUNG BAR YANG MI ‘GYUR RO,,

And if they undertake to make such a display even in the space occupied by a single tiny atom upon an infinite number of planets—upon the surface of all the worlds there are—then that one atom does not become any more “gross,” any larger.  But neither as well does that planet itself become any more “fine,” which is to say, any smaller.


	[4277]

Just so do you—that being who possesses no conceptual thought at all—undertake a whole variety of activities, in every single instant of time, even up until the final moment of “existence”; referring here to the duration of the cycle of pain.

And just as you make this one display, you make the same displays upon the surface of all the planets there are—infinite in their number, for the count of your deeds is equal to that of the count of all the atoms in all worlds there are.

SNGA MA NI YUL GYI DBANG DU BYAS LA, ‘DI NI DUS KYI DBANG DU BYAS PA’O,,

The previous case was a description relative to location; and this one here is a description relative to time.



The ten forces, in brief

[4281]
GNYIS PA LA BZHI, STOBS BCU MDOR BSTAN PA{%,} DE RNAMS RGYAS PAR BSHAD, YON TAN KUN BRJOD MI NUS PA’I TSUL, YON TAN GNYIS SHES PA’I PHAN YON BSTAN PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

This brings us to our second point from before—a description of the fine qualities of the forces.  Here we cover four topics: a brief presentation of the ten forces; a more extensive explanation of the same; a discussion of how it would be impossible ever to describe all these fine qualities; and a demonstration of the benefits of understanding the two kinds of fine qualities.  Here is the first.


[4282]
SANGS RGYAS KYI SA NI STABS {%STOBS} BCUS RAB TU PHYE BA’I PHYIR NA, DE’I RNAM PAR DBYE BA CHA TZAM ZHIG BSTAN PA’I PHYIR BSHAD PA,

That is, the following verses of the root text are meant to present just some portion of the various divisions of the forces of a Buddha, in order to indicate how the level of an Enlightened Being is distinguished by the fact that there are ten different forces there.


	[4283]
[afterword.28]
Sanskrit unavailable

,GNAS DANG GNAS MIN MKHYEN STOBS DANG,
,DE BZHIN LAS RNAM SMIN BLO DANG,
,MOS PA SNA TSOGS THUGS CHUD DANG,
,SNA TSOGS KHAMS NI MKHYEN STOBS DANG,

		There is the force
		Of knowing
		What is actual,
		And what is not;

		And, just so,
		The force of mind
		Of how different
		Karmas will open.

		Then there is
		Comprehending
		The variety of wishes;

		And the force
		Of knowing
		Different propensities.


[4284]
THUB PA’I STOBS LA NI, GNAS DANG GNAS MIN MKHYEN PA’I STOBS DANG, DE BZHIN DU LAS KYI RNAM PAR SMIN PA BLO STE MKHYEN PA’I STOBS DANG, MOS PA SNA TSOGS PA THUGS SU CHUD PA’I STOBS DANG, KHAMS NI SNA TSOGS PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS DANG,

Here then are the forces of an Able One.  We start with (1) the force of knowing what is actual, and what is not; and, just so, (2) the force of the state of mind—or the understanding—where we know how different karmas will open.  Then there is (3) the force of comprehending the variety of different wishes that people might entertain; and (4) the force of knowing people’s different propensities.


	[4285]
[afterword.29]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DE BZHIN DBANG MCHOG MCHOG MA YIN,
,MKHYEN DANG THAMS CAD DU ‘GRO DANG,
,BSAM GTAN RNAM THAR TING ‘DZIN DANG,

		We have the force
		Of understanding
		Higher or lesser
		Capacities; as well as

		The paths that lead
		To different goals;

		And understanding
		Concentration,
		Freedom,
		Single-pointed focus,
		
		Staying in deep
		Meditation, and others
		Of the like.

In like manner we have (5) the force of understanding the higher or lesser capacities of individuals; as well as (6) the force of understanding the paths that lead to different goals.


[4287]
BSAM GTAN DANG RNAM PAR THAR PA DANG TING NGE ‘DZIN DANG SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG PA SOGS BLO STE MKHYEN PA’I STOBS DANG,

Then there is (7) the force of understanding—of knowing—topics such as concentration; and freedom; single-pointed focus; staying deep in meditation; and others of the like.


	[4288]
[afterword.30]
Sanskrit unavailable

,SNGON GNAS DRAN PA MKHYEN PA DANG,
,DE BZHIN ‘CHI ‘PHO SKYE BLO DANG,
,ZAG RNAMS ZAD PA MKHYEN STOBS TE,
,STOBS NI BCU PO ‘DI DAG GO

		So too there is
		The force of 
		Understanding
		Days gone by;

		And just so
		The state of mind
		Of the deaths of beings,

		And how they move on
		Or find their rebirth.

		And then finally
		There is the force
		Of understanding

		Of the impurities
		Are finished off.

		These then
		Are the ten
		Different forces.


[4289]
SNGON GYI GNAS RJES SU DRAN PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS DANG, DE BZHIN DU ‘CHI ‘PHO BA DANG SKYE [f. 278b] BA DANG GNAS PA BLO STE MKHYEN PA’I STOBS DANG,

So too there is (8) the force of understanding days gone by; and just so (9) the state of mind or knowledge of the deaths of beings, and how they move on or find their rebirth, and then their life to come.


[4290]
ZAG PA RNAMS ZAD PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS STE, STOBS NI BCU PO ‘DI DAG TU YOD DO,,

And then finally (10) there is the force of understanding when the last of the impurities are finished off.  This then brings us to a total of ten different forces that we can come to possess.



The five beginning
with knowing the actual

[4291]
GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, GNAS DANG GNAS MIN MKHYEN PA SOGS KYI STOBS LNGA BSHAD PA DANG, THAMS CAD DU ‘GRO BA’I LAM MKHYEN PA SOGS KYI STOBS LNGA BSHAD PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

Which brings us to our second point from above: more extensive explanation of the ten forces.  This we will discuss in two sections: an explanation of the five forces beginning with that of knowing what is actual, and what is not; followed by an explanation of the five forces beginning with that of knowing the paths that lead to every different kind of goal.  Here is the first.



1) The force of knowing
      what is actual, and what is not


	[4292]
[afterword.31]
Sanskrit unavailable

,RGYU GANG ZHIG LAS GANG ZHIG NGES PAR
SKYE ‘GYUR BA,
,DE NI DE YI GNAS SU DE MKHYEN
RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS,
,BSHAD PA LAS BZLOG GNAS MIN SHES BYA
MTHA’ YAS PA,
,MKHYEN PA THOGS PA SPANGS PA DE NI
STOBS SU BSHAD,

		Something has,
		Quite certainly,
		Arisen from
		A particular cause.

		Those who have
		A high grasp
		Of such things

		Have stated that
		This is the actuality.

		Anything happening
		In the opposite way
		Is not actual.

		Eliminating all stopping
		Towards knowing
		Infinite objects
		Of perception

		Is what we refer to
		As the force.


[4293]
RGYU GANG ZHIG LAS ‘BRAS BU GANG ZHIG NGES PAR SKYE BAR ‘GYUR BA’I RGYU DE NI ‘BRAS BU DE YI GNAS SU DE LTAR MKHYEN PA’I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS TE,

And so say that a particular result has, quite certainly, arisen from a particular cause.  The Buddhas—who have a high grasp of such things—have stated that this cause then is the actuality of the result.


[4294]
DPER NA MI DGE BA LAS RNAM SMIN YID DU MI ‘ONG BA ‘BYUNG BA DANG, ‘PHAGS PA SLOB PA’I LAM LAS MYANG ‘DAS ‘THOB PA LA SOGS PA’O,,

It’s like the examples of how unpleasant ripenings derive from non-virtue; or how realized beings attain nirvana from the paths of those who are still learning, and so on.


[4295]
DE LTAR BSHAD PA LAS BZLOG PA NI GNAS MIN PA ZHES BYA STE, DPER NA DGE BA LAS RNAM SMIN YID DU MI ‘ONG BA ‘BYUNG BA DANG,  MTHONG LAM THOB PAS LAS DBANG GIS SRID PA BRGYAD PA ‘GRUB PA NI GNAS MA YIN ZHING GO SKABS MED PA LTA BU’O,,

Anything that could happen in the opposite way from what we have described here then would be called what is “not actual.”  For example, it would not be actual (there would be no chance of it) if a virtuous action led to an unpleasant ripening; or if an individual had attained the path of seeing and then—due to the power of karma—were to experience an eighth rebirth afterwards.


[4296]
DE ‘DRA BA’I GNAS DANG GNAS MA YIN PA’I SHES BYA MTHA’ YAS PA MKHYEN PA LA THOGS PA SPANGS PA STE THOGS PA MED PA DE NI GNAS DANG GNAS MA YIN PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU BSHAD DO,,

Now suppose a person has “eliminated all stopping” towards knowing infinite objects of perception: these different types of reality and non-reality.  Which is to say, suppose their knowledge is unstoppable.  This then is what we refer to as the force of understanding both what is actual and what is not actual.


2) The force of knowing
    how different karmas will open


	[4297]
[afterword.32]
Sanskrit unavailable

,’DOD DANG MI ‘DOD DE LAS BZLOG DANG
ZAD DNGOS KYI,
,LAS DANG DE YI RNAM SMIN SHIN TU
SNA TSOGS LA’ANG,
,MKHYEN PA NUS MTHU THOGS MED SO SOR
‘JUG ‘GYUR BA,
,DUS GSUM SHES BYA KHYAB MDZAD DE NI
STOBS SU ‘DOD,

		There is what
		Is desirable
		And what is
		Not desirable;

		And then the
		Opposite of these.

		There are karmas
		Which are entities
		Which finish off;

		And the great variety
Of ripenings.

What we accept then
As the force is

The power of knowledge
Engaging in objects
In a way which is
Unstoppable;

Taken in by the
Past, present,
And future,

Extending to all
Knowable things [f. 217b].


[4298]
‘DOD PA STE DGE BA DANG MI ‘DOD PA STE LAS MI DGE BA STE MA ‘DRES PA GNYIS DANG,

And then next let’s consider “what is desirable”—a reference to virtuous deeds; and “what is not desirable”—referring to non-virtuous deeds.  There are instances in which these two are unadmixed.


[4299]
DE GNYIS LAS BZLOG PA STE LAS ‘DRES MA DANG, ZAG BCAS KYI LAS NGAN PA ZAD PAR BYED PA’I ZAG MED KYI DNGOS PO’I LAS RNAMS DANG, LAM DE’I RNAM SMIN SHIN TU MI ‘DRA BA SNA TSOGS PA LA’ANG,

And then there are cases of the opposite of these two; meaning that the karmas are mixed.  And then there are the karmas that represent entities which are immaculate—which in fact function to finish off negative karmas.  And then there are the great variety of different ripenings that are produced by this path.


[4300]
MKHYEN PA NUS MTHU THOGS PA MED PAR SO SOR ‘JUG PAR ‘GYUR BA, DUS GSUM GYIS BSDUS PA’I LAS DANG DE’I ‘BRAS BU’I SHES BYA [f. 279a] KUN LA KHYAB PAR MDZAD PA DE NI LAS KYI ‘BRAS BU MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU ‘DOD DO,,

What we accept then as being the force of knowing how different karmas will open is a case where the power of our knowledge engages in individual objects in a way which is unstoppable; we see the karmas and their results taken in by the entirety of the past, present, and future—and this knowing extends to all knowable things.


3) The force of knowing
   the variety of wishes


	[4301]
[afterword.33]
Sanskrit unavailable

,’DOD [217b] CHAGS SOGS KYIS ‘BYUNG BA’I STOBS KYIS
‘DOD PA NI,
,SHIN TU SNA TSOGS DMAN ‘BRING GANG YANG

,DE LAS GZHAN RNAMS KYIS G-YOGS MOS LA
MKHYEN PA NI,
,DUS GSUM ‘GRO BA MA LUS KHYAB PA

		There are
Wishes which occur
		By force of desire
		And so on—

		An extremely
		Great number
		Of different wishes;

		Those lesser,
		The inbetween,
		And those which are
		Extremely elevated.

		And there are hopes
		By those different
		From these—

		Hopes which
		Are obscured.

		Here we have
		A knowledge
		Which travels

		To the three of
		The past, present,
		And future—
		Which covers all.

		This we refer to
		As the force.
		
		
[4302]
‘DOD CHAGS DANG DES MTSON NAS ZHE SDANG LA SOGS PA’I NYON MONGS DANG, SOGS KYIS BSDUS PA DAD PA LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI ‘BYUNG BA STE SA BON GYI STOBS KYIS BSKYED PA’I ‘DOD PA NI,

Let’s consider first the occurrence of desire, and then the repulsion and other negative emotions that it represents.  Then too we have “and so on”—wishes which include faith and so on which “occur”; that is to say, are triggered, by the force of their seeds.


[4303]
SHIN TU MI ‘DRA BA SNA TSOGS PA DMAN PA DANG, ‘BRING DANG GANG YANG KHYAD PAR DU ‘PHAGS PA’I ‘DOD PA DANG,

And then there are an extremely great number of different—varying—wishes: lesser ones, inbetween ones, and those which are extraordinarily elevated.


[4304]
MOS PA DE LAS GZHAN PA’I CHOS KUN TU SPYOD PA RNAMS KYIS SNGAR BSHAD PA’I MOS PA’I SA BON G-YOGS PA STE BSGRIBS PA’I MOS PA LA’ANG,

And then there are hopes that beings have which are different from these other ones: these are hopes that are entertained by those who are trying to practice the Dharma, whose hopes are obscured, or wrapped in the seeds of the hopes mentioned so far.


[4305]
MKHYEN PA DUS GSUM DU ‘GRO BA STE ‘JUG PAS MOS PA’I SHES BYA MA LUS PA KHYAB PA NI, MOS PA SNA TSOGS PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS ZHES BYA’O,,

But here we have a knowledge which travels to the three of the past, present, and future; which covers all the different entities that one might ever hope for.  This then is what we refer to as the “force of perceiving all the various hopes.”



4) The force of knowing
     people’s different propensities


	[4306]
[afterword.34]
Sanskrit unavailable

,SANGS RGYAS KHAMS KYI RNAM PAR DBYE LA
MKHAS RNAMS KYIS,
,MIG SOGS RNAMS KYI RANG BZHIN GANG DE
KHAMS SU GSUNGS,
,RDZOGS PA’I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYI MKHYEN PA
MTHA’ YAS SHING,
,RNAM KUN KHAMS KYI KHYAD PAR LA ‘JUG
STOBS SU ‘DOD,

		Those who are masters
		In the different categories
		Of an Enlightened Being

		Have described
Those things that are
The nature of the eye
		And so on as
		The propensities.

		The infinite variations
		Of the knowledge of
		Totally enlightened beings

		Engage in the details
		Of all the different
		Categories; this is

		What we assert
		Constitutes the force.


[4307]
SANGS RGYAS KHAMS MTHA’ DAG GI RNAM PAR DBYE BA LA MKHAS PA RNAMS KYIS, MIG DANG SOGS KYIS BSDUS PA RNA BA NAS YID KYI BAR DRUG DANG,

And so let’s consider all of the different categories of an Enlightened Being.  Those who are masters of this topic have a knowledge, first, of the six of the eye and “so on”—which includes everything from the ear to the thought.


[4308]
GZUGS NAS CHOS KYI BAR DRUG DANG, MIG GI RNAM SHES NAS YID KYI RNAM SHES KYI BAR DRUG DANG, DE DAG RNAMS KYI RANG BZHIN NANG STONG PA NYID LA SOGS PA GANG YIN PA

So too they know all six from physical form up to objects; and the six from the awareness of the eye up to the awareness of the thought.  And then they know the “nature” of all these things—a reference to qualities such as being completely empty on the inside, and so forth.


[4309]
DE KHAMS SU GSUNGS PA’I KHAMS KYI RAB DBYE RNAM PA KUN GYI KHYAD PAR RNAMS LA, RDZOGS PA’I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYI MKHYEN PA MTHA’ YAS PA ‘JUG PA NI, KHAMS SNA TSOGS PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU ‘DOD DO,,

The infinite variations of the knowledge of totally enlightened beings engage in the details of all the different divisions of the categories which were here described as “propensities.”  And this then is what we assert constitutes the force of knowing the variety of propensities.



5) The force of knowing
     higher or lesser capacities


	[4310]
[afterword.35]
Sanskrit unavailable

,KUN TU RTOG SOGS CHES RNO NYID NI
MCHOG BZHED LA,
,’BRING GNAS SKABS DANG RTUL NYID MCHOG MIN
PAR BSHAD DANG,
,MIG LA SOGS DANG PHAN TSUN SGRUB NUS
CHUD PA LA,
,RNAM PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA CHAGS MED
STOBS SU GSUNGS,

		There is that
State of imagination
Which is not correct,

And so on—
What we assert
To be supreme,

In a particularly
Sharp form.
	
		And then there are
		What we refer to
		As “not supreme”:

		Only middling,
		Or quite dull.

		There are the
		Eye and the rest,
		And the way these
		Inform, or have

		The power to
		Complete, each other.

		Omniscience has
		No density
		Towards them;

		This was spoken
		To be the force.		


[4311]
YANG DAG MIN PA LHAG PAR SGRO ‘DOGS PA’I KUN TU RTOG PA NI, CHAGS SOGS SKYED PA LA DBANG BYED PAS NA DBANG PO’O,,

Next let’s consider that state of imagination which is not correct, and which has a tendency to overstate things grossly.  This is known as a “force” in that it tends to force the arisal of attachment and such.


[4312]
SOGS KYIS BSDUS PA DAD PA’I DBANG PO SOGS CHES RNO BA NYID NI MCHOG TU BZHED LA, DBANG PO ‘BRING GI [f. 279b] GNAS SKABS DANG, DBANG PO RTUL BA NYID CHUNG NGU’I GNAS SKABS NI MCHOG MIN PAR BSHAD PA DANG,

The phrase “and so on” here is meant to encompass what we assert to be supreme: the powers of faith and the like, in a particularly sharp form.  And then what we refer to as “not supreme” would be the point at which our powers are only middling, or where those powers are lesser—quite dull.


[4313]
MIG LA SOGS PA’I DBANG PO NYER GNYIS DANG, DBANG PO RNAMS KYI PHAN TSUN ‘BRAS BU CHUB PA STE SGRUB NUS PA’I RANG GI NGO BO RE RE LA RNAM PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA’I CHAGS PA STE THOGS PA MED PA DE NI, DBANG PO MCHOG DANG MCHOG MA YIN PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU GSUNGS SO,,

And then consider the 22 powers of the eye and the rest; and then the way that these powers “inform” each other, or have the power to complete each other.  Omniscience in the form of knowing the very essence of each of these has no “density” towards them here—meaning, it penetrates with the least obstruction.  This then is what was spoken to be the force of knowing both those capacities which are supreme, and those which are not.



The five beginning with
knowing the paths

[4314]
GNYIS PA NI,

This brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of the five forces beginning with that of understanding the paths that lead to every different kind of goal.



6) The force of understanding the paths
     that lead to different goals


	[4315]
[afterword.36]
Sanskrit unavailable

,LAM ‘GA’ RGYAL BA NYID DANG ‘GA’ ZHIG
RANG RGYAL GYI,
,BYANG CHUB DANG NI NYAN THOS BYANG CHUB
YI DAGS DANG,
,DUD ‘GRO LHA MI RNAMS DANG DMYAL BA
SOGS ‘GRO BA,
,DE LA MKHYEN PA CHAGS MED MTHA’ YAS
STOBS SU ‘DOD,

		Some paths lead
		To the state of a
		Victor themselves;

		Some to the
		Enlightenment of
		A self-made Buddha.

		Others lead to
		The enlightenment
		Of the listener;

		Or to a life as
		A craving spirit,
		Or an animal,

		A worldly god,
		A human,
		Or a hellbeing,

		And so on.
		What we say
		Is the force

		Is a knowledge
		Of all these
		
Which is
Without density, 
		As well as infinite.


[4316]
LAM ‘GA’ ZHIG RGYAL BA NYID DU ‘GRO BA DANG, LAM ‘GA’ ZHIG RANG RGYAL GYI BYANG CHUB DANG, ‘GA’ ZHIG NYAN THOS KYI BYANG CHUB TU ‘GRO BA DANG, YI DVAGS DANG DUD ‘GRO DANG LHA DANG MI DANG DMYAL BA RNAMS SU ‘GRO BA DANG,

Now some paths lead to the state of a Victor themselves; while some paths lead to the enlightenment of a self-made buddha.  Others lead to the enlightenment of the listener.  Still others lead to a life as a craving spirit; or an animal; a worldly god, a human, or a hellbeing.


[4317]
SOGS KYIS NI YANG DAG PA DANG LOG PAR NGES PA’I LAM LA SOGS PA RNAM PA SNA TSOGS PA STON TA {%TE}, DE RNAMS LA MKHYEN PA CHAGS THOGS MED PA NI MTHA’ YAS PA STE THAMS CAD DU ‘GRO BA’I LAM MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU ‘DOD DO,,

The phrase “and so on” here refers to a whole variety of different paths, such as those which are quite certainly pure, or mistaken—and so forth.  And so what we say is the force of knowing the paths that go to all places is a knowledge of all these which is without density, or obstruction, and is as well infinite.



7) The force of understanding
     concentration & the like

	[4318]

Then there are

Deep practitioners
On infinite

Concentration;
The eight total freedoms;

[4319]
‘JIG RTEN MTHA’ YAS PA NA YOD PA’I RNAL ‘BYOR PA’I BYE BRAG LA STE KHYAD PAR GYIS RAB TU DBYE BA THA DAD PA MTHA’ YAS PA BSAM GTAN BZHI DANG, RNAM PAR THAR PA BRGYAD DANG, GANG ZHI GNAS GANG DAG STE TING NGE ‘DZIN DANG, SNYOMS ‘JUG GI KHYAD PAR GANG DAG GCIG DANG BRGYAD DU GYUR PA STE MTHAR GYIS GNAS PA’I SNYOMS PAR ‘JUG PA DGU DANG, KUN BYANG 

And then there are the “details,” or the different divisions due to distinctions, among the activities of deep practitioners on infinite numbers of worlds.  The variations here are themselves infinite, including for example:

	 the four levels of concentration;
	 the eight total freedoms;
	 those states of quietude which are truly pure, focused meditation;
	 the nine states of deep meditation which has reached its final expression,
		whether that be in a single state or eight; and then
	 total enlightenment itself.


[4320]
DE DAG LA MKHYEN PA THOGS PA MED PA ‘DI NI, KUN NAS NYON MONGS PA DANG RNAM PAR BYANG BA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU BSHAD DO,,

And then what we describe as the “force of knowing both that which is entirely involved with the negative emotions, and that which is entirely involved with total enlightenment” is that unstoppable form of knowing all these.



8) The force of understanding
    days gone by


	[4321]
[afterword.38]

JI SRID GTI MUG DE SRID PA STE GCIG NAS GCIG TU BRGYUD PA THOG MA [f. 280a] MED PA’I SRID PAR GNAS PA NA,

We have lived then in a cycle of being that has no beginning: we have revolved from one existence to another, for the total amount of time that we have possessed dark ignorance.


[4323]
‘DAS PA’I DUS SU BDAG DANG SEMS CAN GZHAN RE RE YI SRID PA’I SEMS CAN NI, JI SNYED PA DE SNYED KYI SEMS CAN MTHA’ YAS PA,

And so think then of all the beings that we and other living creatures have each lived through, during all the time of the past: this total amount of living things—infinite.


[4324]
GZHI STE RGYU DANG BCAS PAR DRAN PA DANG, RANG DANG GZHAN RNAMS KHA DOG ‘DI ‘DRA BAR GYUR ZHES DRAN PA NI RNAM PA DANG BCAS PAR DRAN PA DANG, ‘DI ‘DRA ZHI GNAS ‘DI ‘DRA ZHIG TU SKYES SO ZHES DRAN PA NI,

And remember as well their “foundation”—which is to say, the causes that created them.  Remember too the details here: at that time, the color of my body and the bodies of those around me, was like this.  And remember as well, “This was the kind of meditative quietude that this kind of being had achieved.”


[4325]
YUL PHYOGS DANG BCAS PAR DRAN PA STE DRAN PA’I YUL DE RNAMS LA BLO THOGS PA MED PA GANG DANG GANG YIN PA DE NI, SNGON GYI GNAS RJES SU DRAN PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU BSHAD DO,,

And so here is a state of mind which is unstoppable—recalling all these things as well as the specific place where they took place.  Any type of perception like this is what we refer to as the force of understanding days gone by.

And then there is the death, and moving on, that all living beings have experienced in the form of each separate living thing; as well as the rebirth that then they took as they crossed into a new set of the parts to a person.

NAM MKHA’I MTHAR THUG PA’I ‘JIG RTEN LA GNAS PA SNA TSOGS PA’I LAS KYI BZO BOS BKRA BAR BYAS PA MANG PO DE LA DUS DER MKHYEN PA RNAM PA KUN YONGS SU DAG PAS MA CHAGS PA STE MA THOGS PAR ‘JUG PA YIS, YUL MTHA’ YAS PA MKHYEN PA

And then there are many images that have been brought to light by the craftsmen of all the different sorts of karma, located in worlds laid across infinite space itself.  When we know them in that time, in states of mind that have no attachment (which here means “unstoppable”)—for they are all entirely pure—we know a veritable infinity of objects.

‘CHI ‘PHO BA DANG SKYE BA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU ‘DOD DO,,

And this then is what we refer to as the force of the knowledge of the deaths, and passing on, and rebirth of beings.



10) The force of knowing that
       the last of impurities is finished

	[4330]
[afterword.40]
Sanskrit unavailable

,RNAM KUN MKHYEN PA’I STOBS KYIS MYUR DU
RGYAL RNAMS KYI,
,NYON MONGS DAG NI BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS
‘JIG ‘GYUR DANG,
,SLOB MA LA SOGS NYON MONGS BLO YIS
‘GOG PA GANG,
,DE LA MKHYEN [218a] PA CHAGS MED MTHA’ YAS
STOBS SU ‘DOD,

		The Victors,
		Who know all
		Things there are,

		Use these forces—
		With speed—
		To destroy the
		Negative emotions,

		Along with the
		Deep seeds.

		Those who are students,
		And the rest, put a stop
		To the negative emotions
		Using their intelligence [f. 218a];

		This then constitutes
		A state of knowledge
		Which is free of density,

		And this is what
		We refer to as the
		Force of the infinite.


[4331]
RNAM PA KUN MKHYEN PA’I RGYAL BA RNAMS KYI STOBS KYIS CHAGS SOGS NYON MONGS PA DAG NI, BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA THAMS CAD ‘JIG PA STE BCOM PAR ‘GYUR BA DANG,

The Victors, who know all things there are, use these forces to “destroy,” or conquer—“every one of them”—referring to everything involved with the negative emotions, attachment and the rest, along with the deep seeds for these.


[4332]
SLOB MA NYAN THOS DANG LA SOGS PAS BSDUS PA RANG RKYAL {%RGYAL} BA RNAMS KYIS NYON MONGS PA RNAMS BLO STE ZAG MED KYI SHES RAB KYIS ‘GOG PA STE SPANGS PA

Those who are students, or listeners, and “the rest”—which is a reference to the self-made buddhas—put a stop to, or eliminate, everything involved with the negative emotions by using their intelligence; here referring to wisdom.


[4333]
GANG YIN PA DE LA MKHYEN PA CHAGS PA STE THOGS [f. 280b] PA MED PA NI, MTHA’ YAS PA ZAG PA ZAD PA MKHYEN PA’I STOBS SU ‘DOD DO,,

This then constitutes a state of knowledge which is free of density—free of all obstruction.  And that is what we refer to as the force of the knowledge of the infinite: the ending of all impurity.


[4334]
MYUR DU ZHES PA NI BAG CHAGS LHAG MA SHIN TU PHRA BA SANGS RGYAS KYI YE SHES SKAD CIG MA GCIG GIS SPANGS PAR STON PA’O,,

Now the lines of the root text here mention “with speed.”  This is meant to indicate that the high knowledge of an Enlightened Being eliminates all the remaining deep seeds—the very most subtle ones—in but a single instant of time.


[4335]
‘DIR NYON MONGS PA’I BAG CHAGS NI, ‘GREL PA LAS, GANG GIS SEMS KYI RGYUD ‘BAGS PAR BYED CING BSGO BAR BYED LA, RJES SU BGROD PAR BYED PA DE NI BAG CHAGS TE, NYON MONGS PA’I MUR THUG PA DANG, GOMS PA DANG, RTZA BA DANG, BAG CHAGS ZHES BYA BA NI RNAM GRANGS DAG GO, ZHES GSUNGS SHING,

What does it mean when we refer here to “deep seeds for everything involved with the negative emotions”?  The autocommentary puts it this way:

What we refer to as a “deep seed” here is that thing which functions to infect the mind; to stain the mind; to trigger influences that take us on.  For everything involved with the negative emotions, we can say that the terms “final destination”; and “habit”; and “root”; and “deep seed” are all synonymous.


[4336]
NYAN RANG DGRA BCOM PAS NYON MONGS SPANGS KYANG BAG CHAGS DE SPONG MI NUS PAR GSUNGS LA,

It is also stated that—even though enemy destroyers who belong to the listeners and the self-made buddhas have eliminated negative emotions—they are unable to eliminate this deep seed.


[4337]
YANG DE NYID LAS, DE LA MA RIG PA’I BAG CHAGS NI SHES BYA YONGS SU GCOD PA’I GEGS SU GYUR PA YIN LA, ZHES SHES SGRIB TU YANG GSUNGS SO,,

The same text also says,

The deep seed for misunderstanding acts as an impediment for the final analysis of knowable things.


[4338]
LUGS ‘DI LA CHOS KYI BDAG ‘DZIN NI NYON MONGS SU BZHED PAS, SHES SGRIB KYI GTZO BO NI GNYIS SNANG ‘KHRUL BA’I BAG CHAGS LA BYA DGOS TE,

Now according to the present system, the tendency to hold that things are themselves is considered a negative emotion.  As such, we would have to say that the most serious of the obstacles to omniscience is the deep seed for the mistake of a perceptual inconsistency.


[4339]
‘DI NI ‘PHAGS PA YAB SRAS KYIS GZHAN DU SHES SGRIB KYI NGOS ‘DZIN GSAL BAR MA GSUNGS PAS, ‘DIR GSUNGS PA NYID LA BRTAN {%BRTEN} PAR BYA’O,,

On this point, the fact is that the father & son, for the Realized One, have not clearly described any identification of what an obstacle to omniscience would be like.  As such, I would advise you to rely for that upon the very statement you find here.


[4340]
YANG ‘GREL PA LAS, MA RIG PA DANG, ‘DOD CHAGS LA SOGS PA’I BAG CHAGS DE YANG RNAM PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA DANG, SANGS RGYAS KHO NA LA LDOG PAR ‘GYUR GYI, GZHAN DAG LA NI MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS 

The autocommentary further reads,

Something else, about the deep seeds for desire and the like.  They are stopped only for those who know the way of all things, and Buddhas—but not for others.


[4341]
NYAN RANG DGRA BCOM PA DANG, SA BRGYAD PA NAS NYON MONGS KYI SA BON ZAD PAR GSUNGS PA’I NYON MONGS KYI SA BON NI, ‘DIR BSHAD PA’I NYON MONGS KYI BAG CHAGS DANG MI [f. 281a] GCIG GO

As such, when it is stated that with listeners and self-made buddhas who are enemy destroyers, and from the eighth bodhisattva level on, the seeds of negative emotions are finished off, the seeds being referred to are not the same as the deep seeds for negative emotions that we are talking about here in this context.


[4342]
,BAG CHAGS ‘DI SHIN TU PHRA BA NI SA BCU RGYUN GYI THA MA’I BAR CHAD MED LAM SKYE BA LA PHYOGS PA DANG, SHIN TU PHRA BA ‘GAG PA LA PHYOGS PA GNYIS DUS MNYAM LA, DE THOG MAR SPANGS PA’I RNAM GROL LAM NI SANGS RGYAS KYI YE SHES SKAD CIG MA DANG PO YIN NO,,

As for the extremely subtle form of the deep seeds here, that point at which the uninterrupted path of the final period in the flow of the tenth level is approaching its arisal, and the point at which the stopping of these extremely subtle forms is just approaching, occur simultaneously.  And the path of liberation in which we have first eliminated these represents the first moment of the high knowledge of an Enlightened Being.


[4343]
DE’I PHYIR RNAM PA KUN MKHYEN PA’I STOBS KYIS ‘JIG PAR GSUNGS SO,,

This is why we see the statement that these are destroyed by the force of knowing all the things there are.


[4344]
DE LTAR STOBS RNAMS KYIS SHES BYA MTHA’ DAG MKHYEN PAR GSUNGS PA NI MNGON GYUR DU YIN LA, SANGS RGYAS KYI MNGON SUM LA SHUGS RTOGS MI RUNG BAS SNANG NAS MKHYEN DGOS SO,,

Thus it is that we see it spoken that the various forces allow us to know all existing entitites; and this reference is to a direct form of perception.  It wouldn’t make sense to say that the direct perception of a Buddha involved perceiving things in some incidental manner; as such, they must know things as those things make their appearance.


[4345]
DE YANG RNAM PA MA SHAR BAR MKHYEN PA ‘DI’I LUGS MIN PA NI RIGS PA DRUG CU PA’I ‘GREL PA LAS GSAL BAR BSHAD DO,,

Moreover, the idea that they could know objects without those things making their appearance is not something that this particular system would assert; this point is clearly made in the commentary to The Sixty Verses.


[4346]
DE’I PHYIR DA LTAR BA MNGON SUM DU ‘JAL BA’I SHUGS LA ‘DAS MA ‘ONGS GNYIS ‘JAL BA YANG MIN NO,,

As such as well we can say that the idea that an Enlightened Being perceives the past and the future incidental to perceiving the present directly is incorrect.


[4347]
‘DI YANG NYI MA DE RING LTA BU’I DUS DA LTA BA ‘DI’I DUS SU, DE LA LTOS PA’I ‘DAS MA ‘ONGS GNYIS MED PAS DUS DER DE GNYIS MA GZHAL YANG, DE RING GI DUS MKHYEN PA’I YE SHES DE NYID KYIS ‘DAS MA ‘ONGS THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA MI ‘GAL TE,

On this point, we could consider the present moment in, for example, today.  The two of the past and the future do not, relative to this point in time, exist.  As such, it is not the case that these two can be apprehended at that moment in time.  That does not make it a contradiction, however, to say that the very same high knowledge which perceives today could perceive everything both past and future, as well.


[4348]
DPER NA SA BON GYI DUS KYI MYU GU SA BON GYIS MI SKYED KYANG, SA BON GYIS MYU GU SKYED PA MI ‘GAL BA BZHIN NO,,

We cannot, for example, say that a sprout is grown by a seed during the time of the seed; but that doesn’t mean that there is any contradiction in saying that the seed produces the sprout.



The impossibility of describing
all the fine qualities

[4349]
GSUM PA NI,

This brings us to our third section from before: a discussion of how it would be impossible
ever to describe all these fine qualities.


[4350]
SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN MTHA’ DAG PA NI, SANGS RGYAS NYID KYIS BSKAL PA GRANGS MED PAR SKU TSE BYIN GYIS BRLABS SHING, ‘PHRIN LAS GZHAN MI ‘DA’ BAR SKYEN PA SKYEN PAR GSUNGS KYANG, YON TAN RDZOGS PAR MI ‘GYUR NA, BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYIS CI ZHIG SMOS,

The entirety of the fine qualities of an Enlightened Being constitutes a topic that the Buddhas themselves could attempt to describe at the greatest speed possible, but which—even in the lifetime of a holy form blessed to live for eons beyond any count, and even if this form had no need to pass any time in other holy deeds—they would never come to speaking of the last of the qualities.  If this is the case, then there is no need for us to speak of how a bodhisattva could ever list all of them.


[4351]
DES [f. 281b] NA RANG SANGS RGYAS DANG NYAN THOS RNAMS KYIS YON TAN MTHAR PHYIN PAR SHES PA’AM BRJOD PAR NUS PA LTA SMOS KYANG CI ZHIG DGOS, DON ‘DI NYID DPE’I SGO NAS BSHAD PA,

As such, there is no need for us even to mention how the self-made buddhas and listeners could ever comprehend, or express, these fine qualities in their entirety.  The next lines of the root text then describe this same point, in terms of a metaphor.


	[4352]
[afterword.41]
Sanskrit unavailable

,NAM MKHA’ MED PAS ‘DAB CHAGS LDOG PAR
MI ‘GYUR GYI,
,’DI NI RANG MTHU ZAD PAS LDOG PAR
‘GYUR DE BZHIN,
,SLOB MA DANG BCAS SANGS RGYAS SRAS RNAMS
SANGS RGYAS KYI,
,YON TAN MKHA’ LTAR MTHA’ YAS MA BRJOD

		It is not as though
		The winged ones
		Must eventually

Come to a stop
Because there is
No more sky;

Rather, this one flies
Until their strength
Is exhausted—

And then they
Must turn back.

The students
And those in
Their company,

And the buddhas
And the children
Are similar:

They can describe
The high qualities
Of the Enlightened Ones,

Similar to the sky
In being infinite,

But they will
Have to stop,

Without having
Listed them all.


[4353]
‘DI LTAR NA {%NAM} MKHA’ ‘DAB GSHOG YANGS PA’I RLUNG GI SHUGS KYIS, PHA ROL GNON PA YANG NAM MKHA’ LA ‘PHUR BA NA, NAM MKHA’ MED PA STE ZAD PAS ‘DAB CHAGS KYI DBANG PO DE LDOG PAR MI ‘GYUR GYI

Thus it is that a bird with the broadest of wingspans might push the air of the sky back through the power of the wind created by flapping those wings; and thus fly through that sky.  But it is not as though this lord of the winged ones must eventually come to a stop because there is no more sky: because the extent of the sky itself has been exhausted.


[4354]
‘DIR NI ‘DIR ‘PHUR ‘PHUR BAS NAM ZHIG NA RANG GI MTHU STOBS ZAD PAS LDOG PAR ‘GYUR BA

Rather, this great bird flies and flies until at some point their strength and power are exhausted; and then then they must turn back.


[4355]
DE BZHIN DU, SLOB MA NYAN THOS DANG DE DANG BCAS PA’I RANG SANGS RGYAS DANG, SANGS RGYAS KYI SRAS SA CHEN PO LA BZHUGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN NAM MKHA’ LTAR MTHA’ YAS PA MA BRJOD PAR LDOG PAR ‘GYUR BA NI,

The students—referring to the listeners—and “those in their company” (referring to the self-made buddhas), and even those children of the Buddhas residing at the highest levels, are similar.  They can undertake to describe the high qualities of the Enlightened Ones—qualities that are similar to the sky itself, in being infinite; but in the end they will have to stop, without having listed them all.


[4356]
YON TAN RDZOGS PAS MA YIN GYI RANG GI BLO’I STOBS NYAMS PAS YIN NO,,

That is, it is not as if they have come to the last of these fine qualities, and stopped there; rather, they must stop their description because the power of their own mind has been exhausted in the attempt.


	[4357]
[afterword.42]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DE PHYIR BDAG ‘DRAS KHYOD YON ‘DI DAG CI,
,SHES PA DANG NI BRJOD PAR NUS ‘GYUR RAM,
,’ON KYANG DE DAG ‘PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS,
,BSHAD PHYIR DOGS SPANGS CUNG ZHIG
TZAM ZHIG SMRAS,

		Thus how could
		Someone like me
		Ever be able

		To understand,
		And then to express,

		These high qualities
		That you possess?

		Nonetheless,
		I have thrown aside
		Any doubts,

		And boldly offered
		Just the barest list,

		Because those
		Have been described
		By The Arya,
		Nagarjuna.


[4358]
SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN RDZOGS PAR BRJOD MI NUS PA DE’I PHYIR ‘GREL PA MDZAD PA BDAG ‘DRA BAS SANGS RGYAS KHYOD KYI YON TAN ‘DI DAG NI CI SHES PA DANG NI BRJOD PAR NUS PAR ‘GYUR RAM CI STE MI NUS SO,,

The fact is then that the fine qualities of the Buddhas could never be listed in their entirety; and thus how could it ever come to be that “someone like me”—a reference to the author of this classical commentary—could ever be able to understand, and then to express, these high qualities that “you” (referring to the Buddha) possess?  In reality I would never manage to do so.


[4359]
DE LTAR BDAG LA RANG STOBS KYIS SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN SHES TZAM ZHIG SHES PA’ANG MED PA ‘ON KYANG, BDAG GIS DOGS PA SPANGS PA STE TSAM TSOM MED PAR YON TAN CUNG ZAD TZAM ZHIG SMRAS PA NI,

Thus it is that I—acting on my own accord—can say that I don’t even possess enough knowledge to grasp even some part of the high qualities of an Enlightened One.  Nonetheless, I can say that I have thrown aside any doubts—any faltering here—and boldly offered just the barest list of those qualities here.


[4360]
YON TAN DE DAG ‘PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS BSHAD PA’I PHYIR TE DE LA BRTEN NAS YIN NO,,

And I have been able to do so only because those qualities have been described by The Arya, Nagarjuna; and I have relied upon that description here.



Benefits of understanding
the qualities

[4361]
BZHI PA NI,

Which brings us to our fourth point from above: a demonstration of the benefits of understanding the two kinds of fine qualities.


	[4362]
[afterword.43]
Sanskrit unavailable

,ZAB MO STONG PA NYID YIN TE,
,YON TAN GZHAN RNAMS RGYA CHE BA’O,
,ZAB DANG RGYA CHE’I TSUL SHES PAS,
,YON TAN ‘DI DAG ‘THOB PAR ‘GYUR,

		The profound here
		Is emptiness;

		The other
		Fine features
		Are the widespread.

		When we come
		To an understanding
		Of both the profound
		And the widespread,

		We will be able
		To attain these
		Fine features.


[4363]
MDOR BSDUS NA BSTAN BCOS ‘DI LAS SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA GNYIS BSTAN PA’I ZAB MO NI STONG PA NYID CHOS KYI SKU DANG, GZHI [f. 282a] DANG LAM GYI STONG PA NYID DO,,

To put it briefly then, the fine qualities of the Enlightened Ones have been described—in this classical commentary—as being of two types: the profound, and the widespread.  The “profound” here is a reference to emptiness—referring here to the emptiness of the holy body of all things, as well as to the emptiness of the original condition of things, and to the path itself.


[4364]
DE LAS GZHAN PA SA BCU GCIG GI YON TAN DANG STOBS LA SOGS PA BSHAD PA RNAMS NI RGYA CHE BA’I YON TAN NO,,

And then when we refer to the “widespread” good qualities, we are speaking of the other ones: the fine features of the eleven levels, and the forces and so on.


[4365]
DE ‘DRA BA’I ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA’I YON TAN GYI TSUL LEGS PAR SHES PAS NI, DON DE GNYIS SHES NAS BSGOMS PAS SANGS RGYAS KYI YON TAN GNYIS PO ‘DI DAG ‘THOB PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

And suppose that we come to a good understanding of both these profound qualities, and the widespread ones.  If we learn and then practice these things deeply, then we will ourselves be able to attain these two good types of fine features.



The holy body of emanation

[4366]
GSUM PA NI,

And with this we come to our third section from above: a presentation concerning our emanation body.


[4367]
DA NI SPRUL PA’I SKU NYAN RANG DANG BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYI DON DANG THABS THUN MONG BA ‘BYUNG ZHING, SO SKYE RNAMS KYI DON YANG CI RIGS PAR ‘BYUNG BA, BDE ‘GRO LA SOGS PA’I SGRUB BYED DU GYUR PA’I DBANG DU BYAS NAS BSHAD PA,

That is, the next section here is meant to address the holy emanation body, from which are derived the goals of both the listeners & self-made buddhas, and the bodhisattvas—providing spiritual methods for both together.  From here are derived the goals of the common beings as well; with this form aiding us in our quest for a higher rebirth, and the like.


	[4368]
[afterword.44]
Sanskrit unavailable

,SLAR YANG MI G-YO SKU MNGA’ KHYOD KYIS
SRID GSUM BYON NAS SPRUL RNAMS KYIS,
,GSHEGS PA DANG NI BLTAM DANG BYANG CHUB
ZHI BA’I ‘KHOR LO’ANG STON PAR MDZAD,
,DE LTAR KHYOD KYIS ‘JIG RTEN G-YO BAG
SPYOD CAN RE BA’I ZHAGS PA NI,
,MANG POS BCINGS PA MA LUS THUGS RJES
MYA NGAN ‘DAS PAR BKRI BAR MDZAD,

		You continue on
		To all three worlds,
		Because you possess
		
		A holy form which
		Never shifts out;

		You use your
		Emanations to travel.

		And then you
		Make a display
		Of taking
		Your holy birth,

		And undertake
		To teach the Wheel
		For enlightenment
		And peace.

		Thus do you act
		Towards the world,

		Bound tightly
		In the shackles

		Of their manifold
		Hopes, sporting in
		All kinds of roles.

		Out of your compassion,
You act to lead
		Each & every one
		On to their nirvana.	


[4369]
CHOS KYI SKU BRNYES SU ZIN KYANG SLAR YANG DA {%DE} KHO NA NYID LA MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA LAS MI G-YO BA’I SKU MNGA’ BA KHYOD KYIS SA ‘OG SA STENG SA BLA’I SRID PA GSUM DU BYON NAS,

Now even though you have already completed your achievement of the holy body of all things, you continue on to making your way to all three of the worlds: to the area below the earth; upon the earth; and above the earth.  And you do so because you possess a holy form which never shifts at all out of a state of deep meditation upon suchness.


[4370]
SPRUL PA’I SKU RNAMS KYIS DGA’ LDAN NAS MI YUL DU GSHEGS PA DANG NI,

That is, you use your emanation bodies to depart from the Heaven of Happiness and travel to the lands of humans.


[4371]
BLTAMS PA LA SOGS PAS YAB YUM DANG SRAS DANG ‘GREL {%’BREL} BAR STON ZHING, BYANG CHUB PA ZHI BA MYANG ‘DAS KYI GRONG KHYER DU ‘JUG PA’I CHOS KYI ‘KHOR LO’ANG DBANG PO DANG ‘TSAM PAR STON PAR MDZAD DO,,

And then you make a display of taking your holy birth and the like: you show yourself as though you are the child in a relationship with your high father and mother.  And next you undertake to teach the Wheel of the Dharma, in a way which fits the capacities of differing individuals, helping them to enter the great city of enlightenment: peace, going beyond all grief.


[4372]
DE LTAR KHYOD KYIS ‘JIG RTEN TE SEMS CAN GYI KHAMS SPYOD PA SNA TSOGS PA CAN RE BA STE SRED PA’I ZHAGS PA NI MANG POS BCINGS PA

Thus do you act towards the world, towards those living beings of such varying natures and activities, bound tightly in the shackles of their manifold “hopes”—here referring to their desires.


[4373]
MA LUS PA GRAGS PA DANG PHAN LAN BZHED PA SOGS LA MI LTOS PA’I THUGS RJE CHEN POS MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PAR BKRI BA STE ‘GOD PAR MDZAD DO,,

And you help each & every one of them, out of your great compassion—without any hopes for some kind of fame, or idea that someone may provide you with something in return.  That is, you act to lead them on to their nirvana: you take them and place them into this state.


[4374]
G-YO BAG SPYOD CAN ZHES PA LA ‘GREL BSHAD KYI ‘GYUR LA, SNA TSOGS SPYOD CAN ZHES ‘BYUNG BA ‘GREL PA DANG MTHUN NO,,

The unusual phrase here—“sporting in all kinds of roles”—is given in the translation of the classical Explanation as “living all kinds of activities”; which fits the intent of the autocommentary.



All a single path

[4375]
BZHI PA NI,

With this we come to our fourth part from above: a proof that in the end it is all a single path.


[4376]
[f. 282b] DE LTAR SKU GSUM GYI RNAM GZHAG BSHAD NAS, THEG PA GCIG LA THEG PA GSUM DU BSTAN PA DGONGS PA CAN DU BSHAD PA,

Now that we have completed our explanation of how the holy bodies are presented as three, we come to a verse which is meant to explain why the presentation of the single path as being three paths was not meant literally.


	[4377]
[afterword.45]
Sanskrit unavailable

,GANG PHYIR ‘DI NA DE NYID SHES LAS
DRI MA MTHA’ DAG SEL BA NI,
,LHUR BYED GZHAN MED CHOS RNAMS DE NYID
RNAM ‘GYUR DBYE LA’ANG BSTEN MIN ZHING,
,DE NYID YUL CAN BLO GROS ‘DI YANG
THA DAD ‘GYUR BA MA YIN LA,
,DE YI PHYIR NA KHYOD KYIS ‘GRO LA
THEG PA MI MNYAM DBYER MED BSTAN,

Why have we taken
Our approach?

Even though there is
Nothing there
Which is our focus,

We have been presenting
Clearing away
Each & every impurity,

A topic different
From discussing suchness.

It is not the case
That we are suggesting
Further that one

Rely upon differing
Versions of the
Suchness of things—
Upon divisions.

Nor is it the case
That the insight
Which takes suchness
As its object
Possesses separate ones.

Thus it is that you
Have taught to beings
One which is indivisible,
With no equal
Among ways.


[4378]
RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA ‘DI NA CHOS RNAMS KYI DE KHO NA NYID SHES PA LAS GZHAN SGRIB GNYIS KYI DRI MA MTHA’ DAG SEL BA NI, LHUR BYED PA STE GTZO BOR GYUR PA MED LA,

Let us say something about the reason why we have taken our particular approach here.  Even though there is nothing there which is our focus (which is to say, the main thing), we have been presenting in this part of the text the topic of clearing away each & every impurity—the two obstacles; which is a topic different from discussing the suchness of all objects.


[4379]
CHOS RNAMS KYI DE KHO NA NYID KYANG MI ‘DRA BA’I RNAM ‘GYUR GYI DBYE BA STEN PA’ANG MIN ZHING STE MIN PAS,

It is not the case that we are suggesting further that practitioners need to “rely upon” differing versions of the suchness of things; which is to say, we are not focusing here upon the divisions of this reality.


[4380]
DE KHO NA NYID KYI YUL CAN GYI BLO GROS TE YE SHES ‘DI YANG YUL ‘JAL BA’I RNAM PA THA DAD PA MI ‘DRA BAR ‘GYUR BA YANG MA YIN PA

Nor is it the case that the insight or high knowledge here, which takes suchness as its object, possesses separate—disparate—aspects as it takes its objects under consideration.


[4381]
DE YI PHYIR NA, THUB PA KHYOD KYIS GDUL BYA’I ‘GRO BA LA THEG PA GZHAN GANG DANG YANG MI MNYAM PA DBYER MED PA’I THEG PA GCIG BSTAN TE,

Thus it is that you, Able One, have taught to your disciples—to beings—a single way which is indivisible, and which finds no equal at all among any other ways.


[4382]
JI SKAD DU, ‘OD SRUNGS CHOS THAMS CAD MNYAM PA NYID DU RTOGS NA MYA NGAN LAS ‘DA’ BA YIN LA, DE YANG GCIG YIN GYI GNYIS DANG GSUM NI MA YIN NO, ZHES ‘BYUNG BA’I PHYIR RO,,

We see this fact reflected in the scripture which reads,

O protector of light, if a person has a realization of the equality of all existing entities, then they will pass beyond all grief.  And this is but a single thing; it is not two, it is not three.


[4383]
‘PHAGS PAS KYANG,
,CHOS KYI DBYINGS LA DBYER MED PHYIR,
,KHYOD LA THEG PA’I DBYE BA MED,
,THEG PA GSUM DU BSTAN PA NI,
,SEMS CAN RNAMS NI GZHUG PHYIR RO,
ZHES ‘JUG PA DANG MTHUN PAR GSUNGS SO,,

The Arya has as well made the following statement, which accords with The Entrance:

	The realm of all things
	Possesses no different divisions;

	Thus it is that according to you
	The way has no divisions.

	Teaching the different ways
	As being three was only
	To allow beings their entrance.


[4384]
DE DAG GIS NI DE KHO NA NYID MA RTOGS PAR NYON MONGS THAMS CAD ZAD PAR MI NUS PA LA, CHOS RNAMS KYI DE KHO NA NYID LA MI MTHUN PA CHEN PO MED PA’I PHYIR NA,

What these references are saying is that—if one is unable to realize suchness—then they will never be able to finish off all the negative emotions; and that there are no major discrepancies between the types of suchness that existing objects possess.


[4385]
MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PAR BGROD DANG LA {%BGROD PA LA}, DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS MA RTOGS KYI RGYU’I THEG PA MI ‘DRA BA BSHAD PA DANG, NYON MONGS ZAD PA’I MYANG ‘DAS TZAM THOB NAS, THEG PA GZHAN DU MI ‘GRO BA’I ‘BRAS [f. 283a] BU’AM THEG PA ‘GA’ ZHIG BSHAD PA NI,

This leads then to the following conclusion.  We do see varying explanations of the way that acts as a cause—where we may or may not have realized suchness, in our journey to nirvana.  We see as well explanations of a number of result states where we do not travel on to some other way; that is, explanations of different ways, after we have achieved no more than nirvana in the form of eliminating the negative emotions.


[4386]
GDUL BYA RE ZHIG DRANG BA’I PHYIR GSUNGS PAR BSTAN PA ‘DI, LEGS PAR RTOGS NA THEG DMAN LA CHOS KYI BDAG MED RTOGS PA MED PAR BSHAD PA RNAMS KYI DGONGS PA RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR RO,,

If we truly grasp teachings like this—teachings which were enunciated only in order to lead on certain of the disciples—then we will come to grasp the true intent of explanations in the lower way that there is no realization of the lack of a self-nature to things in general.


[4387]
GAL TE GANG THOB NAS LAM GZHAN DU ‘GRO MI DGOS PA’I MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA GCIG KHO NA YIN LA, NYAN RANG GI THEG PAS KYANG MYA NGAN LAS ‘DA’ BAR BSTAN PA JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA,

Which may lead one to ask the following question:

If there really is only one nirvana which—when you achieve it—you no longer need to travel upon any other path, then why is it that in the ways of the listener and self-made buddhas they present a nirvana as well?


[4388]
DE LTAR BSTAN PA ‘DI DGONGS PA CAN DU BSHAD PA,

The following lines then are presented in order to explain that this particular presentation is not to be taken literally.


	[4389]
[afterword.46]
Sanskrit unavailable

,GANG PHYIR ‘GRO LA NYES PA SKYED BYED
SNYIGS MA ‘DI DAG YOD GYUR PA,
,DE PHYIR ‘JIG RTEN SANGS RGYAS SPYOD YUL
GTING ZAB LA ‘JUG MI ‘GYUR ZHING,
,BDE GSHEGS GANG PHYIR KHYOD LA MKHYEN RAB
THUGS RJE THABS DANG LHAN CIG PA,
,MNGA’ DANG GANG PHYIR BDAG GIS SEMS CAN
DGROL ZHES KHYOD KYIS ZHAL BZHES TE,

		Now there is
		A certain reason:

		Something which
Functions to trigger
Problems within
Living beings.

And that is
The presence of
Those degenerations.

As such, the realms
In which Buddhas act
Are too deep
For the world;

They cannot engage
In something
With such depths.

Because the fact is
That you, Those Who
Have Gone to Bliss,

Possess in conjunction
Knowledge and
A method consisting
Of compassion.

And further you
Made a certain
Commitment:

“I will liberate
Living beings.”


[4390]
GANG GI PHYIR ‘GRO BA RNAMS LA NYES PA STE NYON MONGS SHAS CHEN PO SKYED PAR BYED PA’I RGYUR GYUR PA LUS SEMS LAS SU MI RUNG BAR BYED PA’I SEMS CAN DANG SKAL BA DANG NYON MONGS PA DANG LTA BA DANG TSE’I SNYIGS MA LNGA PO ‘DI DAG NI YOD PAR ‘GYUR PA,

Now there is a certain reason for things here, that there is a specific cause in action which functions to trigger “problems”—meaning, an abundance of negative emotions—within living beings.  And that is the presence of those famous five degenerations: those of living beings; of their spiritual fortune; their negative emotions; their viewpoints; and their lifetimes.


[4391]
DE DAG GIS LHAG PAR MOS PA KHYAD PAR DU ‘PHAGS PA ‘JOMS PAR BYED PAS, SANGS RGYAS KYI YE SHES LA DON GNYER BYED PA ‘GOG PAR BYED PA

These factors function strongly to smash the especially high aspirations that people might entertain; as such, they act to block their aspiration for achieving the high knowledge of the Buddhas.


[4392]
DE’I PHYIR ‘JIG RTEN TE GDUL BYA SANGS RGYAS KYI SPYOD YUL ZAB PAS GTING DPAG DKA’ BA LA ‘JUG PAR MI ‘GYUR ZHING,

As such, the realms in which the Buddhas act are too deep for “the world”—for disciples.  They cannot engage in something with depths so difficult to fathom.


[4393]
GANG GI PHYIR BDE BAR GSHEGS PA KHYOD LA GDUL BYA ‘DUL BA’I THABS LA MKHAS PA’I MKHYEN RAB DANG, DE DAG GI DON LA BSNYEL BA MI MNGA’ BA’I THUGS RJE’I THABS DANG LHAN CIG PA MNGA’ BA DANG,

Because the fact is that you, Those Who Have Gone to Bliss, possess in conjunction two things.  First there is your knowledge, which is wise in the methods for taming disciples.  And then you have a method consisting of compassion, which has a quality of never overlooking their needs.


[4394]
GANG GI PHYIR SNGON BYANG SEMS KYI DUS SU BDAG GIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD DGROL BAR BYA’O ZHES KHYOD KYIS ZHAL GYIS BZHES PA DE NYID THABS KYI RNAM PA GZHAN GYIS NGES PAR BSGRUB DGOS SO,,

And further the fact is that—in times before, when you were simple bodhisattvas—you made a certain commitment: you said, “I will liberate each and every living being.”  And then just such a commitment had to be accomplished by means of yet another kind.


	[4395]
[afterword.47]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DE PHYIR MKHAS PA RIN PO CHE YI
GLING DU CHAS PA’I SKYE TSOGS KYI,
,NGAL BA NYER SEL GRONG KHYER YID ‘ONG
BAR DU RNAM PAR BKOD PA LTAR,
,KHYOD KYIS THEG PA ‘DI NI SLOB MA
NYE BAR ZHI BA’I TSUL LA YID,
,SBYAR ZHING RNAM PAR [218b] DBEN LA’ANG
BLO SBYANGS RNAMS LA LOGS SU GSUNGS,

		Thus it is
		That a master

		Who is trying to
		Dispel the fatigue

		That a group of
People might display

In a voyage to
The Isle of Jewels

Sets forth visions of
A lovely magical city,
Long before.

Just so do you
Undertake a
Certain way;

All this is meant
To attract their minds

To the way
Of total peace.

		And then separately,
		After they had 
		Trained themselves

		In thoughts of
		Total isolation [f. 218b],
		You taught them.
		

[4396]
GANG GI [f. 283b] PHYIR ‘GRO BA RNAMS THEG CHEN LA ‘JUG PA LA GEGS MANG PO YOD CING, ‘GRO BA RNAMS KYANG MYANG ‘DAS LA NGES PAR DGOD DGOS PA DE’I PHYIR,

Now it is the fact that there exist many impediments that keep living beings from entering into the greater way; while at the same time these beings must quite certainly be brought to their nirvana.


[4397]
PAD DKAR LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR DED DPON MKHAS PAS RGYA MTSO NA GNAS PA’I RIN PO CHE’I GLING DU CHAS PA’I TSE SKYE BO’I TSOGS KYIS, YUN RING POR BGROD PA’I NGAL BA NYE BAR SEL BA’I PHYIR DU

Thus it is that the Sutra of the White Lotus has a pertinent description here.  It speaks of a master ship captain who is trying to dispel the fatigue that a group of people might display when they have taken to sea, in a voyage to the Isle of Jewels—and the trip has simply been too long.


[4398]
RIN PO CHE’I GLING DU MA SLEBS PA’I BAR DU GRONG KHYER YID DU ‘ONG BA RNAM PAR BKOD PA STE SPRUL PA LTAR DU,

And this skillful captain manages to “set forth visions”—that is, to emanate—in the distance a lovely magical city, long before the ship arrives at it intended destination, of that Isle of Jewels.


[4399]
BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KHYOD KYIS KYANG THEG PA CHEN PO’I TSU ROL TU THEG CHEN DE THOB PA’I THABS SU GYUR PA ‘DI NI, NYE BAR ZHI BA’I TSUL GYI BDE BA LA YID SBYAR BA’I PHYIR DU, SLOB MA NYAN THOS DANG DES MTSON PA’I RANG RGYAL LA NYAN RANG GI THEG PA GNYIS GSUNGS SHING,

And just so do you as well, O Conqueror, undertake a certain stratagem—even before people reach the greater way—as a way of getting them to attain to this greater way.  And this is that you describe to them the two ways of the listener and the self-made buddha, to students who are described as “listeners” in a way which is meant to indicate, in addition, those self-made ones.  And all this is meant to attract their minds to the happiness of the way of total peace.


[4400]
DE NAS ‘KHOR BA’I NYON MONGS KYIS RNAM PAR DBEN PA’I BLO SBYANGS PA RNAMS LA LOGS SU STE PHYI NAS THEG PA CHEN PO KHO NA GSUNGS LA,

And then “separately,” or after that—after the point where they had trained themselves in the thoughts of “total isolation” from the negative thoughts of the cycle of pain—you taught them only the greater way.


[4401]
DE RNAMS KYIS KYANG SANGS RGYAS RNAMS LTAR TSOGS RDZOGS PAR BYAS NAS, GDON MI ZA PAR SANGS RGYAS THOB PAR BYA DGOS SO,,

And all of this was indeed necessary because you knew that—beyond any doubt at all—they too needed to attain Buddhahood, completing the necessary accumulations as other Enlightened Beings had, before them.


[4402]
THEG PA GCIG TU SGRUB PA ‘DI MDO KUN LAS BTUS PA LAS, THEG PA GCIG TU ZAD PAR NI MDO SDE DU MA LAS GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR RO, ZHES SOGS KYIS GSUNGS PA LAS SHES PAR BYA’O,,

The fact that the ways can be proven as one is something that we can understand from sources such as the Compendium of the Sutras, where it says, “We can understand this from the fact that many different sutras describe how, in the end, there is indeed but a single way.”



The point of enlightenment

[4403]
LNGA PA LA GNYIS, MNGON PAR BYANG CHUB PA’I DUS KYI DBANG DU BYAS PA’I BSHAD PA DANG, BZHUGS PA’I DUS KYI DBANG DU BYAS PA’I BSHAD PA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

Which brings us then to our fifth part here—an explanation of the point at which we have become enlightened, and remain there.  Here we proceed in two different sections: an explanation relative to the point at which one reaches total enlightenment; and then an explanation relative to the point at which one is residing in total enlightenment.  Here is the first.


	[4404]
[afterword.48]
Sanskrit unavailable

,BDE BAR GSHEGS PA MA LUS PHYOGS SHING
SANGS RGYAS YUL DAG NA,
,PHRA RAB RDUL GYI RDUL RNAMS BDOG PAR
GYUR PA JI SNYED PA,
,BYANG CHUB MCHOG RAB DAM PAR GSHEGS PA’I
SKAL BA {%BSKAL PA} DE SNYED DE,
,’ON KYANG KHYOD KYI GSANG BA ‘DI NI
BSNYAD BGYI MA LAGS SO,

		There are all the lands
		Of Enlightened Beings,
		
		Paradises in every
		Corner of the universe.

		There exist,
		In these worlds,
		
		A certain number
		Of atoms of dust.

		And the eons
That it has taken
Those Gone to Bliss

To reach that most
High, and holy, and
Supreme enlightenment

Are equal to
That very number.

Even so,
This particular
Secret of yours

Is not something
We would normally
Describe openly.


[4405]
PHYOGS BCU’I ZHING MA LUS PA SANGS RGYAS KYI YUL DU GYUR PA DAG JI SNYED PA DE NA, RDUL PHRA RAB KYI RDUL GYI GRANGS RNAMS BDOG [f. 284a] PAR GYUR PA JI SNYED PA BDE BAR GSHEGS PA KHYOD BYANG CHUB KYI MCHOG RAB DAM PAR GSHEGS PA’I BSKAL PA YANG DE SNYED DE,

Consider now all of the lands of the Enlightened Beings—the paradises that stretch through every corner of the universe.  There exist, in these worlds, a certain number of atoms of dust.  And the eons that it has taken you, Those Gone to Bliss, to “go” or reach that most holy, and high, and supreme enlightenment are as well equal to that very number.


[4406]
DE LTAR YIN PA ‘ON KYANG SNGON DGE RTZA MA BSAGS PA RNAMS MOS PAR DKA’ BA’I PHYIR, KHYOD KYI GSANG BA ‘DI NI BSNYAD PAR BGYI BA MA LAGS SO,,

And even though this is the case, the knowledge of it would make it difficult for those who had not already accumulated the requisite virtue to even hope to reach this goal.  As such, this particular secret of yours is not something we would normally describe openly.


[4407]
DE LA LHAG PAR MOS PA RNAMS LA NI BSOD NAMS GZHAL DU MED PA BSAG PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR ‘DIR BSHAD DO,,

And in fact we have spoken of it here only to assist those who already possess this special aspiration, in their quest to accumulate truly inestimable goodness.


[4408]
‘DI LA ‘GREL BSHAD BYED PAS ‘DI YANG SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYI CHOS KYI SKU GCIG YIN PAS DE LTAR BRJOD PA YIN GYI, GZHAN DU NA SANGS RGYAS GZHAN ‘BYUNG BAR MI ‘GYUR BAS SO, ZHES ‘CHAD PA NI

On this point, the author of The Explanation says—

The explanation is made as it is here is only because the holy body of all things belonging to each & every one of the Buddhas is but one body; otherwise, we could not say that other Buddhas had appeared.


[4409]
MI ‘THAD DE, ‘GREL PA LAS SPRUL PA’I SKU ‘BYUNG BA’I DBANG DU BYAS PAR GSUNGS PA’I PHYIR RO,,

This idea though is mistaken, since in the autocommentary these statements are described as relating to the appearance of the holy body of emanation.


[4410]
SPRUL PA’I SKU ‘BYUNG BA’I RGYU ZHES PA CHOS KYI SKU LA DGONGS ZHES ‘CHAD PA YANG MI RIGS TE, CHOS KYI SKUR GSHEGS PA’I TSAD DE TZAM DU ‘DOD NA GANG ZAG GZHAN SANGS RGYA BA’I SKABS MED PA’I SKYON DER YANG ‘JUG PA’I PHYIR DANG,

Nor would it be correct to say that the phrase “cause for the appearance of the holy body of emanation” was meant to refer to the holy body of all things.  If we were to accept that as the measure of what it took to reach the holy body of all things, then there arises the additional problem that there wouldn’t have been sufficient time for any other individuals to have reached enlightenment.


[4411]
SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYI CHOS SKU GCIG YIN NA SANGS RGYAS SNGA MA RNAMS SANGS RGYAS PA’I TSE, SNGAR SANGS MA RGYAS PA DANG ‘TSANG RGYA RGYU’I CHOS SKU YANG SNGON DU THOB ZIN PA SHIN TU ‘GAL BA’I PHYIR RO,,

If the holy bodies of all things belonging to each and every one of the Buddhas were all but a single body of all things, then at the point when the earlier Buddhas reached their Buddhahood, the bodies of all things belonging to those who had not earlier reached their enlightenment, and those who were still to reach their enlightenment, would already have been attained.  And that would be a total contradiction.


[4412]
DES NA BYANG CHUB KYI SNYING POR GSHEGS PA’I TSAD STON PA YIN LA, DE YANG SNGON DU SANGS RGYAS NAS KYI YUN TSAD STON PA MA YIN PAS, SANGS RGYAS NAS SLAR YANG BYANG CHUB KYI SNYING POR SPRUL SKU’I ‘TSANG RGYA TSUL STON PA’I GRANGS TSAD STON PA YIN NO,,

As such, what’s being indicated is the measure of time needed to travel to the heart of enlightenment; it is not meant to describe the amount of time passed since that earlier point when one had become enlightened.  As such, we can say that the number being described is the time it takes an emanation to pretend to reach enlightenment, in the very heart of enlightenment—all after we had already actually become a Buddha.


[4413]
DE LTAR [f. 284b] NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS,
,SANGS RGYAS YUL GYUR ZHING RNAMS
PHYOGS BCU MA LUS NA,
,PHRA RAB RDUL NI JI SNYED
YOD PA DE SNYED DU,
,BDE BAR GSHEGS PA MCHOG GYUR
KHYOD KYI BYANG CHUB KYANG,
,’BYUNG ‘GYUR
ZHES ‘BYUNG BA LTAR LEGS SO,,

Thus it is that Naktso’s translation of the root text at this point is well done:

	There are all the lands
	Of Enlightened Beings,

	Paradises in every
	Corner of the universe.

	And in them there are
	A certain number of atoms.

	This is how long
	It takes you, Highest Ones,

Those Gone to Bliss,
To reach your
Enlightenment too.


[4414]
DE LTAR MA BYAS PAR ‘GREL BSHAD LTAR BSHAD NA, RTZA BA LAS GSANG BA ‘DI BSHAD PAR MI BYA BAR GSUNGS PA’I YUL DU ‘GRO BA YIN NO,,

If we decide not to read the lines this way, and rather follow thread of the Explanation in our thinking, there is a danger that we would end up being the type of people who are being described—in the root text—as being those with whom this secret should not be shared!



Residing in total enlightenment

[4415]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to our second part from above: an explanation relative to the point at which one is residing in total enlightenment.


	[4416]
[afterword.49]
Sanskrit unavailable

,RGYAL BA JI SRID ‘JIG RTEN MTHA’ DAG
MCHOG TU RAB ZHI BAR,
,’GRO BA MIN ZHING NAM MKHA’ RNAM ‘JIG
‘GYUR MIN DE SRID DU,
,SHES RAB YUM GYIS BSKYED PA KHYOD LA
THUGS BRTZE MA MA YIS,
,TSUL LUGS BYED PAS RAB TU ZHI BAR
‘GYUR BA GANG LA MNGA’,

		A Victor remains
		Until all the world

		Reaches to that
		Highest state
		Of absolute peace,

		And also
		Until that day
		When space itself
		Comes to its
		Complete dissolution.

		They have been
		Given birth by
		The Mother,
		Wisdom, and then

		Compassion,
		Acting in the manner
		Of a wet nurse.
		
		How then could
		We ever say
		That you possessed
		Some total peace?


[4417]
RGYAL BA’I MA ‘ONGS PA’I SKU TSE’I TSAD NI JI SRID DU ‘JIG RTEN GDUL BYA MTHA’ DAG GO ‘PHANG MCHOG TU RAB TU ZHI BAR ‘GRO BA MIN PA LTE {%STE} SANGS RGYAS SU MA RGYUR PA’I BAR DANG, JI SRID DU ‘DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA’ RNAM PAR ‘JIG PAR ‘GYUR BA MIN PA DE SRID DU YIN TE, 

The length of life, into the future, for the holy body of a Victor is that it will remain until “all the world”—meaning disciples—is able to reach to that highest state of absolute peace; which is to say, until they become Buddhas themselves.  We can also say that this body remains until that day when space itself—which is nothing that was ever produced—comes to its complete dissolution.


[4418]
SANGS RGYAS NI SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA’I YUM GYIS BSKYED NAS THUGS BRTZE BA CHEN PO YI MA MA LA GTAD PA LAS SNGAR BSHAD PA’I TSUL LUGS ‘DI BYED PAS,

Now a Buddha is a person who has been given birth by the “Mother”—referring to the perfection of wisdom—and then been handed over to the wet nurse of great compassion, acting in the manner that we described before.


[4419]
DE ‘DRA BA KHYOD LA ZHI BA PHYOGS GCIG PAR ‘GYUR BA GA LA MNGA’ STE MI MNGA’ BA’I PHYIR RO,,

How then could we ever say that you possessed a peace here that was only partial?  You never could.


[4420]
GANG GIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON BSGRUB PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR DU MU MTHA’ MED PAR SEMS CAN ‘DI DAG GSO BAR BYED PA SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYI THUGS RJE DE JI ‘DRA BA ZHIG CE NA,

One may come then with the following question:

Can you describe the compassion of the Enlightened Ones, who—in order to bring about the goals of each & every living being—sustain these beings endlessly?


	[4421]

[4422]
BDEN ‘DZIN GYI GTI MUG GI SKYON GYI DBANG GIS ‘JIG RTEN PA RNAMS KHA ZAS TE ‘DOD YON LNGA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PAS ZOS PAS,

Due to the problem of the dark ignorance of grasping to some real existence, those of the world consume a specific meal—out of their craving for the five objects of desire, of the senses.


[4423]
SDUG BSNGAL RGYA CHEN PO’I RGYU BYED PA’I PHYIR DUG DANG BCAS PA ZA BA PO YI SKYE BO NYID KYI NANG MI STE BDAG GI BAR BYAS PA DE RNAMS LA KHYOD BRTZE BA SKYE BA

And there is a certain poison contained in this food that acts as a cause of massive suffering, for the one who eats it.  And so love comes into your heart for them: you treat these very people as members of your own family: you make them your own.


[4424]
JI LTA BA DE LTAR DU DUG ZOS NAS NYEN PA’I BU GCIG PU LA MA YI SDUG BSNGAL GYI [f. 285a] YID SKYE BA MIN TE, DE BAS NA MGON PO SANGS RGYAS RNAMS MCHOG TU RAB TU ZHI BA PHYOGS GCIG PAR GSHEGS PAR ‘GYUR BA MA LAGS SO,,

This is not though like the intense feelings of suffering that a mother feels for a beloved, only child who has, in a similar way, mistakenly eaten some poison.  Which means that it is not the case that the Protectors, the Enlightened Beings, have travelled only to some one part of the supreme and final peace.

And what is the reason for this?  It is all because those who are not well versed in the meaning of suchness still possess a state of mind where they have a strong craving for taking entities as existing in truth.  Because of this, they put their faith in the laws of karma and its consequences, and thus believe that rebirths as a worldly god or human do exist.


[4427]
SKYE BA DANG ‘JIG PA’I GNAS SKABS TE ‘CHI BA’I SDUG BSNGAL NGES PAR ‘THEB CING,

And because of this, in turn, they are quite certainly stricken by “periods when they are born, and periods when they are destroyed”: a reference to the suffering of dying.


[4428]
YUL SDUG PA DANG BRAL BA DANG, MI SDUG PA DANG PHRAD PA YIS BSKYED PA’I SDUG BSNGAL MYONG BAR ‘GYUR LA,

And they undergo as well all the suffering which is triggered by being torn from all those things that feel attractive to them; and meeting up with all those things that seem to them undesirable.


[4429]
RGYU ‘BRAS KYI DNGOS PO MED PAR ZHEN PA’I BLO CAN LOG PAR LTA BA DANG LDAN PAS NI, SDIG TO CAN GYI ‘GRO BA DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA’I NGAN ‘GRO DANG, SNGAR BSHAD PA’I SDUG BSNGAL YANG ‘THOB PA DE’I PHYIR DANG,

Those who are possessed of wrong view, where they feel a craving for causes & effects which are not even actual things, end up achieving no more than the “future fate of those who still have terrible deeds”—a reference to the realms of hell, and other lower rebirths, along with all the sufferings that we described above.


[4430]
‘JIG RTEN GYI SKYE BO DE RNAMS THUGS BRTZE BA CHEN PO’I YUL DU RAB TU DONG BA STE SONG BAS NA, THUGS RJE CHEN POS BCOM LDAN ‘DAS KHYOD KYI THUGS ZHI BA PHYOGS GCIG PA LA GZHOL BA LAS BZLOG PAS KHYOD LA ZHI BA PHYOGS GCIG PA’I MYA NGAN LAS ‘DAS PA MI MNGA’ BAR ‘JIG RTEN DU BZHUGS SO,,

The beings of this world have “crowded to”—have become—worthy objects of great compassion.  As such, “you”—the Conqueror—have, out of this great compassion, turned away from allowing your heart to be lost to but a partial state of peace.  That is, you remain here in the world, but without allowing yourself to go into a kind of nirvana which represents one side of the condition of peace.



How the commentary was composed

[4431]
GSUM PA BSTAN BCOS JI LTAR BRTZAMS PA’I TSUL NI,

And this now brings us to our third great division from the beginning of our text: a description of how it was that the commentary was first composed.


	[4432]

And so this presentation, which comments unerringly upon the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna, has been related by a Buddhist monk known as the glorious Chandrakirti.  My explanation has proceeded from the Root Text on Wisdom—that classical commentary of the middle way.


[4434]
NGES DON GYI MDO SDE RNAMS LUNG JI LTA BA BZHIN DANG, ‘PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI MAN NGAG NI JI LTA BA BZHIN DU BRJOD PA YIN [f. 285b] NO,,

My presentation is in complete accord with the traditional sources of the sutras which offer a literal presentation of reality; and in keeping as well with the personal advices of the Realized One himself: Nagarjuna.
