JI LTAR DBU MA’I GZHUNG LUGS ‘DI LAS MA GTOGS PAR BSTAN BCOS GZHAN NA STONG PA NYID CES BYA BA’I CHOS ‘DI NI, PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR BRJOD PA MED PA

Now there is no entirely unmistaken presentation of this teaching known as “emptiness” to be found in any classical commentary other than those which follow the description found in the system of the great books of the middle way.


[4437]
DE BZHIN DU, KHO BO CAG GIS ‘DIR LUGS GANG ZHIG BRGAL LAN DANG BCAS PAR BSNYED {%BSNYAD} PA ‘DIR ‘BYUNG BA’I LUGS KYANG, STONG PA NYID KYI CHOS LTAR BSTAN BCOS GZHAN NA NI MED DO ZHES MKHAS PA RNAMS KYIS NGES PAR MDZAD DU GSOL LO,,

And we ask those among you who are real masters to be sure of one thing.  As we’ve just said, the system which we have enunciated—the one that appears here, along with our treatment of the objections of other parties—is one that you cannot find in any of the other, different classical commentaries which purport to be teachings on the topic of emptiness.


[4438]
DE’I PHYIR DBU MA PA KHA CIG GIS MDO SDE PA RNAMS DANG, BYE BRAG TU SMRA BA RNAMS KYIS GANG DON DAM PAR SMRAS PA DE NYID, DBU MA PA RNAMS KYIS KUN RDZOB TU ‘DOD DO ZHES SMRAS PA DE NI,

As such, let us say something about statements by certain supposed followers of the middle way who have remarked that those specific items which followers of the Sutrist School, and those of the Detailist School, describe as being the ultimate are actually what those of the Middle Way school assert are deceptive reality.


[4439]
DBU MA’I BSTAN BCOS KYI DE KHO NA NYID MA SHES PAS SMRAS PA YIN TE, ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA’I CHOS NI ‘JIG RTEN PA’I CHOS DANG MTSUNGS PAR MI RIGS PA’I PHYIR RO, ZHES RANG ‘GREL LAS GSUNGS SO,,

Statements like this can only be made by those who have no understanding of suchness as it is presented in the Classical Commentary on the Middle Way.  As the autocommentary puts it, “It would be incorrect to say that things which are beyond the world were equivalent to things within the world.”


[4440]
‘DIS NI RANG GIS THA SNYAD DU RNAM PAR BZHAG PA KHAS BLANGS PA THAMS CAD RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NYID LA ‘JOG PAS, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHO NA’I STENG NAS RNAM GZHAG BYAS PA’I DON SMRA GNYIS LA SOGS PA’I GRUB MTHA’ RNAMS RANG LUGS KYI DON DAM DU MA ZAD THA SNYAD DU YANG GRUB PA MED PAR ‘DOD PA’I LUGS SO,,

All this is a reference to a system where we say the following.  Once we accept the presentation of how things are established in terms, then what we are saying is that there is nothing at all which could exist “in actuality.”  And so let’s consider the beliefs expressed by the two Functionalist schools, and the like, who can only posit their own presentations with the assumption of things that could exist “in actuality.”  The actual fact is that, according to our own system, it is not only the case that such objects could not exist in any ultimate way; neither could they exist even nominally.


[4441]
DES NA RANG GI LUGS ‘DI SEMS TZAM PA DANG YANG THUN MONG MA YIN PAR MA ZAD, MGON PO KLU SGRUB DANG ‘PHAGS PA LHA’I DGONGS PA ‘GREL BA’I DBU MA PA GZHAN GYI LUGS DANG YANG THUN MONG MA YIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG CES ‘DOMS PA PO,,

As such, what our author is actually advising us of here is the following—

Not only should we say that the system that we ourselves are presenting here is nothing held in common even with those of the Mind Only.  You must also understand the point that no one can say, either, that our beliefs are held in common with those of other systems of some thinkers of the Middle Way School who are attempting to comment upon the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna, and Aryadeva.


[4442]
[f. 286a] DE LA SLOB DPON SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS KYI ‘GREL PA NI TSAD MAR SLOB DPON ‘DI BZHED PAS, DE LA ZUR ZA BA MIN LA, RGYAL SRAS ZHI BA LHA’I LUGS DANG YANG SLOB DPON ‘DI’I LUGS GNYIS SHIN TU MTHUN PAR SNANG NGO,,

On this point, we should though understand that our Master here does accept the commentary of Buddha Palita as being accurate; as such, we can say that we have no reason to think that it may contain some error.  It would also certainly appear that the system enunciated by that child of the Victors, Shantideva, accords extremely closely to that of our present Master.


[4443]
THA SNYAD DU YANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA’I STENG NAS, BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM GZHAG MDZAD PA ‘DI LA BRTEN NAS RANG RGYUD KYI GRUB MTHA’ DANG, KUN GZHI MI BZHED PA SOGS KYI BSHAD SROL THUN MONG MA YIN PA MANG DU YOD PA NI, DRANG NGES RNAM ‘BYED LA SOGS PAR RGYAS PAR BSHAD PAS ‘DIR MA SMOS SO,,

And so it is true that—even speaking nominally—there is nothing that could exist by definition.  In addition, we have our presentation here of the two different types of reality.  Based on this, there are many different, unique, systems of explanation—such as the school of the Independent Group, and those who do not accept the concept of a storehouse consciousness.  I have explained all these at great length in works such as Distinguishing the Figurative from the Literal; as such, I will not go into them further here.


[4444]
KHA CIG ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA NI ‘JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD LAS ‘DAS PA GZHAN LUGS DANG, ‘JIG RTEN PA NI RANG GI LUGS SO ZHES ZER BA NI,

Some people have made the claim—as far as the expression “gone beyond the world”—that having gone beyond the verbiage of the world refers to the position of the other side; while “the world” here represents our own position. 


[4445]
‘GREL PA LAS ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA’I CHOS ‘DI YONGS SU SPANGS PAS ZHES GSUNGS PA DANG ‘GAL BAS NA, BZLOG STE BYA DGOS LA ‘JIG RTEN PA DANG DE LAS ‘DAS PA’I DON NI, DE KHO NA NYID JI BZHIN MA RTOGS PA DANG RTOGS PA’I LUGS SO,,

This though contradicts the autocommentary, where it says, “because they have given up, completely, this teaching which is beyond the world.”  As such, we need to take this in the completely opposite way, where the meaning of “things of the world” and “things gone beyond the world” refers to systems where we either fail to grasp suchness correctly, or do grasp it so.


[4446]
‘PHAGS PA’I DGONGS PA ‘CHAD LUGS ‘DI NI THUN MONG MA YIN PA YIN PA’I PHYIR, ‘PHAGS PA’I THUGS DGONGS MI SHES SHING, GSUNG RAB KYI DE KHO NA NYID NGES PA MED PAR,

This way of explaining the true intent of The Arya is truly unique; as such, there have been people who rejected this teaching beyond the world; this was done by those who had not grasped the true and holy intent of The Arya, and who had not yet ascertained suchness as presented in the scriptures.


[4447]
STONG PA NYID STON PA RNAMS KYI YI GE TZAM LA ‘JIGS PA RNAMS KYIS, ‘JIG RTEN LAS ‘DAS PA’I CHOS ‘DI SPANGS PAS, DE’I PHYIR DBU MA’I BSTAN BCOS KYI DON GYI DE KHO NA NYID PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR BSTAN PAR BYA BA’I PHYIR,

As such they were in fear even of the words being used by those presenting emptiness.  This led them to reject this Dharma, which is so far beyond the normal world.  Thus we have the following lines, which are meant to present—in an unerring manner—the meaning of the Classical Commentary on the Middle Way.

The fact is that people became frightened when they heard someone say, “I will now compose Entering the Middle Way”—frightened simply when they saw the shade of the ebony abyss of depths so impossible to fathom, within the vast expanse of the ocean of that mind which could plumb the deeps of Arya Nagarjuna.

SEMS TZAM DU SMRA BA LA SOGS PA’I SKYO {%SKYE} BOS KLU SGRUB KYI LUGS BZANG PO GANG DAG RGYANG RING DU SPANGS MOD KYANG,

Now it is indeed the case that individuals like those who follow the Mind Only school have only rejected the beautiful system of Nagarjuna, discarding it off to a great distance.


[4451]
DBU MA’I GZHUNG GI TSIG LE’UR BYAS PA KHA ‘BUS PA’I KU MU DA KHA PHYE BA’I CHUS KU MU DA KHA ‘BYED BYED ZLA BA GRAGS PA DA LTA YID LA RE BA RNAMS SKONG BAR BYED DO,,

But along came a refreshing flow of pure water—a classic of the middle way set in verse—which opened the blooms of a pure white water lily, whose buds had been awaiting it.  And with this liquid, the one who crafted the lily-opener—Chandrakirti—has now fulfilled all the hopes of those who had held them in their heart.

GAL TE DE LTA YIN NA GNAS BRTAN DBYIG GNYEN DANG, PHYOGS KYI GLANG PO DANG, CHOS SKYONG LA SOGS PA BSTAN BCOS RNAMS KYI MDZAD PA PO BYON ZIN PAR GYUR PA

One may then raise the following question:

If things are really the way they’re described in those last few lines, then let’s consider respected elders such as Vasubandhu, Dignaga, Dharmapala, and all the rest: those of the past who have composed their own classical commentaries.


[4453]
DE DAG GIS KYANG YI GE TZAM THOS PAS ‘JIGS TE, RTEN CING ‘BREL BAR ‘BYUNG BA’I DON PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR STON PA ‘DI YONGS SU SPANG SAM ZHE NA,

Are you saying that they too were frightened, just by hearing the words we’ve been talking about?  Are you saying that they rejected, entirely, this unmistaken teaching on the way that things occur in dependence and interrelationship?


[4454]
DE SKAD DU SMRA’O, ,DE LTAR GSUNGS PA LA DBYIG GNYEN DANG PHYOGS GLANG GI GZHUNG RTZOD MED RNAMS NAS NI, RNAM PAR RIG PA TZAM GYI LUGS SU BKRAL MOD KYANG, SLOB DPON DE DAG GI BZHED PA JI LTAR YIN PA NI BDAG CAG ‘DRA BA RNAMS KYIS SHIN TU RTOGS PAR DKA’O,,

Here then is what we would say to that.  Now it is true that the great classics of Vasubandhu and Dignaga are indisputable, with regard to these statements; that is, they have interpreted these ideas according to the school which says that everything is mind.  Nonetheless, it is an extremely difficult task for people like you and me to truly understand just what these masters really thought.


[4455]
YANG ZAB MO’I DON ‘DI SU ZHIG GIS RTOGS PAR ‘GYUR ZHE NA,

And then one might come with another question: “Well then, who is it exactly that actually did grasp this profound thought?”

Let us consider then this profound idea of suchness, which we have finished explaining here, and which is in fact likely to be frightening.  There are individuals who have, in their past—during their previous lifetimes—become highly accustomed to deep seeds created by their intense aspiration for emptiness.
