At this point, Naktso’s translation would seem preferable to Patsab’s:

Given sufficient power of the appropriate causes, even the texts of the River Schools—inferior as they are—can lead those who perceive things as real to seeing themselves come to a realization of emptiness.


[4459]
JI LTAR GZHAN SDE SNGON SEMS RGYUD LA STONG NYID LA LHAG PAR MOS PA’I BAG CHAGS MA BZHAG PA RNAMS KYIS MNGON PA NAS BSHAD PA LTAR SRID RTZE MA GTOGS PA’I KHAMS GSUM GYI NYON MONGS MNGON GYUR RE ZHIG SPANGS SHING, GRUB PA’I MTHA’ GZHAN NYE BAR SBYOR NUS PAR MTHONG YANG,

And so let’s consider members of these other groups, who may not have—at some prior point in time—planted any deep seeds inside their mindstreams that would make them feel some strong aspiration towards emptiness.  As explained in the texts on higher knowledge, they might still be able to eliminate—for a certain amount of time—different negative emotions for all three of the realms, except for that level known as the Peak of Existence.  And we might observe them being able to apply themselves to other philosophical systems.


[4460]
SANGS RGYAS KYIS GSUNGS PA’I DON DAM PA STONG PA NYID STON PA LA LHAG PAR MOS MI NUS PA DE BZHIN DU, SLOB DPON DE DAG LA GSUNG RAB MANG DU GSAN PA RGYA CHE PA MNGA’ BA YIN YANG, ZAB MO’I DON ‘DI NI GZHAN GYIS THUGS SU CHUD PAR MI ‘GYUR RO,,

Still though they would be unable to aspire, in any great degree, to the teachings on emptiness in the form of ultimate reality, as these were described by the Buddha.  Just so, it may well be the case that these other masters may possess vast learning in a great variety of the scriptures; and yet still they would not be able to grasp this profound concept.


[4461]
DE’I PHYIR DBU MA’I LUGS LAS GZHAN PA’I DON DAM PA STON PA’I TSUL LUGS SANGS RGYAS KYI DGONGS PAR MA SONG BAS RANG GI BLOS SBYAR BA ‘DI DAG MTHONG BA STE BLTAS NAS, GANG ZAG GI BDAG TU BRJOD PA STE DE GSAL BAR BYED PA’I GZHUNG LUGS RNAMS LA BYA BA LTAR,

And thus it is that we can say that any system of teaching ultimate reality which is other than that of the followers of the middle way fails to capture the true intent of the Buddha.  As such, where we “see” or consider these ideas that people have made up in their own mind, we note that they are behaving just the same as if they were following the scriptural traditions of those who “describe” or elucidate some self-nature to the person.


[4462]
SLOB DPON GZHAN GYI LUGS KYI BZHED PA’I GZHUNG DBU MA’I LUGS ‘DI LAS GZHAN PA RNAMS LA DGA’ BA’I BLO DOR BAR BYA BA STE,

As such, I would encourage you to discard that state of mind where you take some kind of pleasure in systems other than that of the middle-way approach that we have described here—give up the texts of those masters who adhere to some other school of thought.


[4463]
LUGS GZHAN RANG GI BLOS SBYAR BA LA YA MTSAN PAR MI BYA’I, RANG GI STONG PA NYID KYI LTA BA LA LHAG PAR MOS PA KHO NA LA YA MTSAN PAR BYA’O,,

That is, give up any kind of attitude where you take these other systems—which people have simply made up on their own—as being something really amazing.  The only thing you should really feel amazed at is a very strong aspiration to follow the viewpoints of emptiness that we already have in our hands.



A dedication of the good deed

[4464]
BZHI PA BSTAN BCOS BRTZAMS PA’I DGE BA BSNGO BA NI,

This brings us to our fourth section from above: a dedication of the virtue of having completed the composition.


	[4465]
[colophon.5]
Sanskrit unavailable

,SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB LUGS BZANG BSNYAD LAS
BDAG GIS BSOD RNAMS PHYOGS KYI MTHAR,
,KHYAB CING YID MKHA’ NYON MONGS KYIS SNGOR
STON KA’I RGYU SKAR STAR DKAR BA’AM,
,SEMS KYI SBRUL LA GDENGS KA’I NOR BU
DANG ‘DRA GANG ZHIG THOB PA DES,
,’JIG RTEN MA LUS DE NYID RTOGS NAS
MYUR DU BDE GSHEGS SAR BGROD SHOG,

		Thus have I
		Enunciated that
		Beautiful system
		Of the Master,
		Nagarjuna.

		And by doing so,
		I have merit enough
		To stretch to the
		Very edges of
		Space itself.

		The sky of my mind
		Had been sent into
		The gloom of the
		Negative emotions.

		But now,
		In the midst,
		Has come a bright
		White light like
		
		A major star in
		The autumn heavens.

		Or else you could say
		That here is a mind
		Which resembles
		That fabulous jewel

		Which a cobra holds
		Embedded in their hood;

		And the acquisition of such
		Will allow the entire world
		To perceive suchness;

		And then may it happen
		That—with great speed—
		Every being completes
		Their journey to the level
		Of One Gone to Bliss.


[4466]
SLOB DPON CHEN PO ‘PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI DBU MA’I LUGS BZANG PO LUNG DANG RIGS PA’I TSOGS SHIN TU GSAL BAS, BSNYAD PA STE BSHAD PA 

Thus then have I “enunciated”—which is to say, explained—that beautiful middle-way system of the great Master, The Arya, Nagarjuna; and I have done so by using perfectly clear examples of entire collections of both scriptural authority and logical reasoning.


[4467]
LAS BYUNG BA’I BDAG GIS [f. 287b] PHYOGS KYI MTHAR KHYAB PA’I RGYA CHE BA’I BSOD NAMS BSAGS PA,

And by doing so, I have myself accumulated a massive amount of merit—enough to stretch to the very edges of space itself.


[4468]
YID KYI NAM MKHA’ NYON MONGS PA’I TSOGS KYIS SNGO ZHING GNAG PAR BYAS PA’I DKYIL DU, STON KA’I RGYU SKAR LTAR SHIN TU DKAR BA’AM,

The sky of my mind, thus far, had been sent into the gloom—darkened—by an entire mass of everything related to the negative emotions.  But now, in the midst of that obscuration, something has come, shining in bright white light like a major star in the autumn heavens.


[4469]
RTZOM PA PO’I SEMS KYI SBRUL LA STE GYI GDENGS KA’I NOR BU DANG ‘DRA BA GANG ZHIG THOB PA DE YI MTHUS, SEMS CAN GYI ‘JIG RTEN MA LUS PAS ZAB MO’I DE KHO NA NYID JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RTOGS NAS,

Or else you could say that the author of our text has a mind which resembles that fabulous jewel which a cobra is said to hold embedded in their hood—which is part of their hood.  And the power of their acquisition of such mental capacity will allow the entire world—every living being, without a single exception—to perceive, just as it is, that profound truth of suchness.


[4470]
MYUR DU BDE BAR GSHEGS PA’I SA KUN TU ‘OD CES BYA BAR BGROD PAR SHOG CIG

And then may it happen that—with great speed—every being completes their journey to the level of One Gone to Bliss: the level we call “Drowned in Light.”


[4471]
,NAG TSO’I ‘GYUR LAS, KLU SGRUB LUGS MDZES PHYOGS SU GRAGS PA BRJOD LAS THOB PA’I BSOD NAMS GANG, ZHES ‘BYUNG NGO,,

Naktso’s translation at this point includes the phrasing, “The merit that I have achieved, by proclaiming that lovely system of Nagarjuna throughout every corner of the world.”



The master who composed the work

[4472]
BZHI PA MJUG GI DON LA GNYIS, SLOB DPON GANG GIS MDZAD PA DANG, LO PAn GANG GIS BSGYUR BA’O, ,DANG PO NI,

And then with this we have reached that fourth part, the meaning of the conclusion to the text.  This we cover in two sections: identifying the Master who composed the work; and then identifying the ancient translators and sages who rendered it into Tibetan.


	[4473]
[colophon.6]
Sanskrit unavailable

,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA’I TSUL GSAL BAR BYED PA SLOB DPON ZLA BA GRAGS PA THEG PA MCHOG LA THUGS GZHOL BA,

This then completes Entering the Middle Way, an illumination of the ways of both the profound and the widespread.  It was composed by Master Chandrakirti, whose holy heart had long since been lost to that highest way.


	[4474]
[colophon.7]
Sanskrit unavailable

,MI PHROGS PA’I MKHYEN RAB DANG THUGS RJE MNGA’ BA, ,RI MOR BRIS PA’I BA DRUS LAS ‘O MA BZHOS PAS BDEN PAR ZHEN PA BZLOG PAR MDZAD PAS SBYAR BA RDZOGS SO,,

He held a high level of knowledge that was never stolen away; and he possessed compassion as well.  He was known for sketching a cow that was about to give birth, and then milking real milk from it.  With this, he was able to stop others from believing that things are real.  This then is the one who completed this composition.


[4475]
DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA KLU’I LUGS KYI ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA’I TSUL GSAL BAR BYED PA

This then completes Entering the Middle Way, an illumination of the ways of both the profound and the widespread, according to the system of Arya Nagarjuna.


[4476]
YUL SA MAntAR SKU ‘KHRUNGS PA’I SLOB DPON CHEN PO DPAL LDAN ZLA BA GRAGS PA RIG PA ‘DZIN PA DANG, SGYU MA LTA BU’I TING NGE ‘DZIN BRNYES PAR GRAGS PA

It was composed by that great master, the glorious Chandrakirti, who took his holy birth in the land of India, at a place known as Samanta.  This sage was a holder of the various traditions of classical knowledge, and a person known as having achieved that level of meditative concentration we call “Like an Illusion.”


[4477]
THEG PA BLA NA MED PA’I MCHOG LA THUGS RAB TU GZHOL BA, MI MTHUN PA’I PHYOGS KYIS MI ‘PHROGS PA’I MKHYEN RAB DANG THUGS RJE PHUL DU BYUNG BA MNGA’ BA,

His holy heart had long since been lost to that highest way: the unsurpassed way.  Master Chandrakirti held a high level of knowledge that was never stolen away by mistaken ideas; and he possessed the most excellent form of compassion as well.


[4478]
RI MOR BRIS PA’I BA DRUS MA LA ‘O MA BZHOS PAS SEMS CAN GYI BDEN PAR ZHEN PA ZLOG PAR MDZAD PAS

He was known as well for one day sitting down and sketching a cow that was about to give birth; and then milking that cow and coming out with real milk.  With this, he was able to stop the habit that others around him had, for believing that things are real.


[4479]
SBYAR BA RDZOGS SO,,

This then is the one who completed this composition.



The translators who created
the Tibetan version

[4480]
GNYIS PA NI,

Which brings us to identifying the ancient translators and sages who rendered this work into Tibetan.


	[4481]
[translators.1]
,,KHA CHE’I YUL GYI GRONG KHYER DPE MED KYI DBUS, ,RIN CHEN SBAS PA’I GTZUG LAG KHANG DU, ,KHA CHE’I RGYAL PO DPAL ‘PHAGS PA LHA’I SKU RING LA,

This was translated in the middle of the Kashmiri town known as Anupama, or “Beyond All Compare,” within the temple whose name is “Hidden Jewels.”  This was during the time of the Kashmiri king whose name was Aryadeva.


	[4482]
[translators.2]
,RGYA GAR GYI MKHAN PO TI LA KA DANG, ,BOD KYI LO TZTSA BA BANDE PA TSAB NYI MA GRAGS KYIS KHA CHE’I DPE DANG MTHUN PAR BSGYUR,

The translation of the text was done according to the Sanskrit edition of the work circulating at that time in Kashmir.  The team that completed the translation consisted of the senior Indian cleric Tilaka, together with the master Tibetan translator, the Buddhist monk Patsab Nyima Drak.


[4483]
KHA CHE’I YUL GYI GRONG KHYER DPE MED KYI DPUNG STE DBUS, RIN CHEN SBAS PA’I GTZUG LAG KHANG DU

This classical text was translated “in the middle”—which is to say, in the crowded quarters—of the Kashmiri town known as Anupama, or “Beyond All Compare,” within the temple whose name is “Hidden Jewels.”


[4484]
KHA CHE’I RGYAL PO DPAL ‘PHAGS PA [f. 288a] LHA’I SKU RING LA, RGYA GAR GYI MKHAN PO TI LA KA KA LA SHA STE THIG LE BUM PA DANG, BOD KYI LO TZ’A BA PA TSAB NYI MA GRAGS KYIS KHA CHE’I DPE DANG MTHUN PAR BSGYUR,

This was during the time of the Kashmiri king whose name was Aryadeva.  The translation of the text was done according to the Sanskrit edition of the work circulating at that time in Kashmir.  The team that completed the translation consisted of the senior Indian cleric Tilaka Kalasha (whose name means “Vase of the Sacred Drop”), together with the master Tibetan translator Patsab Nyima Drak.


	[4485]
[translators.3]
,PHYIS RA SA RA MO CHER RGYA GAR GYI MKHAN PO KA NA KA WARMA DANG, ,LO TZTSA BA DE NYID KYIS NYI ‘OG SHAR PHYOGS PA’I DPE DANG GTUGS SHING LEGS PAR BCOS TE GTAN LA PHAB PA’O,,

Later on, at the Ramoche Temple in the city of Lhasa, the senior Indian cleric by the name of Kanaka Varma and the same master Tibetan translator were able to review a copy of the Sanskrit text that had been circulating in the eastern part of Bactria.  This allowed them to complete an accurate revision of the Tibetan translation, and then finalize it through their efforts to teach it to their students.


[4486]
PHYIS RA SA RA MO CHER RGYA GAR GYI MKHAN PO KA NA KA WA RMA STE GSER GYI GO CHA DANG, LO TZ’A BA DE NYID KYIS NYI ‘OG SHAR PHYOGS PA’I DPE DANG GTUGS SHING, LEGS PAR BCOS NAS ‘CHAD NYAN GYIS GTAN LA PHAB PA’O,,

Later on, at the Ramoche Temple in the city of Lhasa, the senior Indian cleric by the name of Kanaka Varma (“Armor of Gold”) and the same master Tibetan translator were able to review a copy of the Sanskrit text that had been circulating in the eastern part of Bactria.  This allowed them to complete an accurate revision of the translation into Tibetan, and then finalize it through their efforts to teach it to their students.


	[4487]
[translators.4]
‘DIR ‘GREL PA’I MDZAD BYANG DANG, ,’GYUR BYANG GI STENG NAS THUN MONG BA RNAMS BKOD PA NI, ,RTZA BA LOGS SU BSGYUR BA DANG ‘GREL PA’I NANG GI RTZA BA DE GNYIS SBYAR NAS ZHUS DAG DBANG DU BYAS PA YIN NO,,

Why then do we see one colophon for the composition of the commentary itself, and then a shared colophon for the translation?  This is because the root text was translated once on its own, and then edited as part of a combined version of the commentary and the root text presented within it.


[4488]
` ,,’DI’I ‘GREL PA’I MDZAD BYANG DANG, ‘GYUR BYANG GI STENG NAS THUN MONG BA RNAMS BKOD PA NI, RTZA BA LOGS SU BSGYUR BA DANG ‘GREL PA’I NANG GI RTZA BA GNYIS SBYAR NAS ZHUS DAG BYAS PA’I DBANG DU BYAS PA YIN NO,,

Why then do we see one colophon for the composition of the commentary itself, and then a shared colophon for the translation?  This is because the root text was translated once on its own, and then edited as part of a combined version of the commentary and the root text presented within it.



How Je Tsongkapa
composed his commentary

[4489]
,RGYAL BA’I GSUNG RAB KUN GYI SNYING PO MCHOG
,ZAB MO DBU MA MTHA’ BRAL RTEN ‘BYUNG LAM,
,MTHA’ GNYIS SPANGS TE STON PAR LUNG BSTAN BZHIN,
,JI BZHIN ‘GREL MDZAD ‘PHAGS MCHOG KLU SGRUB ZHABS,

	It is the supreme heart
	Of all the high speech
	Of the Victors;

	It is the profound path
	Of the middle way,
	Occurrence in dependence,
	Free of all extremes.

	And there was one
	Who was prophesized
	To come and teach it,
	Free of the two extremes.

	I bow at the feet
	Of that highest of all
	The realized beings:
	
	Nagarjuna,
	Who explained this path
	As it really is.


[4490]
,DE YI RING LUGS DAM PA ‘PHAGS PA LHA’I,
,DGONGS PA ‘GREL PA’I MKHAS PA’I LUGS MANG YANG,
,YONGS RDZOGS ‘GREL MDZAD DPAL LDAN SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS,
,ZLA BA’I ZHABS DANG ZHI BA LHA YI LUGS,

	Now there are many systems
	Of masters who commented
	Upon the true thought
	Of Aryadeva, who carried on
	This Arya’s system of thought.

	But the ones who explained it
	In total fullness were the systems
Of the glorious Buddhapalita,
The venered Chandrakirti,
And Master Shantideva.


[4491]
,GRUB PA’I DBANG PHYUG GSUM GYI BZHED PA’I SGO,
,GCIG TU DRIL NAS GNAD RNAMS MTHA’ CHOD PAR,
,TSIG ZUR PHYIN PAR LEGS PAR BSHAD PA YIS,
,THAL ‘GYUR LUGS MCHOG DRI MA MED PAR BYAS,

	The doorways of the positions
	Taken by these three lords
	Among the accomplished

	Were combined into one,
	Giving fine explanations
	Of the crucial points
	In a definitive way,
	Down to the last syllable.

	Thus then was the supreme
	System of the Consequence Group,
	Free of all impurity, created.


[4492]
,BYANG PHYOGS ‘DI NA LUGS ‘DIR MOS RNAMS KYANG,
,SHIN TU PHRA BA’I RIGS LAM MI BYED CING,
,ZAB MO’I DON LA SKAL BA DMAN PA RNAMS,
,RANG GIS MA RTOGS LUGS MCHOG ‘DIR [f. 288b] SMOD PA,

	Here in the Northern Land,
	Those attracted to this system
	Were however unable
	
	To follow its path
	Of extremely subtle reasoning.

	These were persons
	Who lacked sufficient fortune
	To grasp its deepest points;

	And thus did they begin
	To denigrate here
	That supreme system

	Which they themselves
	Could not grasp.


[4493]
,MANG DU MTHONG BA’I DRI MA BSAL PHYIR DANG,
,SKAL BZANG ‘GA’ LA ZAB LAM GSAL PHYIR DANG,
,BDAG KYANG SKYE BA KUN TU LAM GYI MCHOG
,’DI DANG MI ‘BRAL PHYIR DU ‘BAD PA BYAS,

	Thus it is that I myself
	Have undertaken great efforts

	To clear away the stain
	That I see here many have;

	And to bring a light
	To this profound path,
	For the sakes of just a few
	Who possess sufficient good.

	I hoped as well to assure
	That in all my lives to come
	I would never see myself
	Separated from this highest path.


[4494]
,DER NGAL BA LAS BYUNG BA’I DGE BA YIS,
,’GRO KUN ZAB MO’I GNAD RNAMS KUN RTOGS NAS,
,NYIN MTSAN KUN TU SGRUB PA LHUR LEN PA,
,RTAG TU SRAS BCAS RGYAL BA MNYES BYED SHOG

	And I pray that by
	The virtue I’ve created
	In these exhausting efforts,

	Every living being
	May come to a perfect
	Realization of every
	Crucial point of the profound.

	May they throw themselves
	Into their practice
	Always, night & day,

	And ever come to please
	The Victors and their children.
	

[4495]
,CES DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA’I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA DGONGS PA RAB GSAL ZHES BYA BA ‘DI NI, DGE BA’I BSHES GNYEN LHU LA DKA’ BCU PA LEGS PA DPAL GYIS DNGUL SRANG BZHI BCU’I MAndAL PHUL TE NAN CHER BSKUL BA DANG, 

This then is the Illumination of the True Thought, which was composed in response to urgent supplications by that spiritual friend, the Master of the Ten Classics from Hlula, by the name of Lekpa Pel—who at the same time presented a mandala offering complete with forty weights of silver.


[4496]
GZHAN YANG DGE BA’I BSHES GNYEN CHOS ‘DI LA SHIN TU MOS SHING, DON RTOGS PA’I BLO’I NUS PA MI DMAN PA MANG PO ZHIG GIS ‘GREL PA’I DKA’ GNAS RNAMS KYI BSHAD PA RNAMS TSANG BA, TSIG DON GSAL ZHING SPYI DON GYI MTHA’ GCOD PA RGYAS PA CIG GYIS SHIG CES NAN TAN GYIS BSKUL BA’I DON DU,

And there were as well others, great numbers of great spiritual friends, who had a great yearning for this teaching, and who had no little capacity of mind to grasp in full its meaning.  They urged me to the task, requesting explanations that would treat all the most difficult points in the autocommentary, in their entirety—clarifying the wording, presenting the overall meaning, and dissecting difficult points in full.  Thus have I written this work, to fulfil their insistent requests.


[4497]
DBU MA CHEN PO’I RNAL ‘BYOR PA MANG DU THOS PA’I DGE SLONG SHAR TZONG KHA PA BLO BZANG GRAGS PA’I DPAL GYIS, ‘BROG RI BO CHE DGE LDAN RNAM PAR RGYAL BA’I GLING DU SBYAR BA’O,,

This work was composed then by a deep practitioner of the magnificent middle way, a Buddhist monk by the name of the glorious Lobsang Drakpa, hailing from the east of our land, and deep in his learning.  He completed this work at the monastery known as Ganden, land of goodness, isle of the final victory, nestled below Shepherd’s Peak.





The Root Text of
“Entering the Middle Way”




Root Text of
Entering the Middle Way

This translation utilizes the edition from the Derge edition of the Tengyur, with original folio numbers noted.


	[title]
[f. 201b]
In the language of India, this book is called Madhyamaka
Avatara Nama.
In the language of Tibet, it is called Uma La Jukpa Shejawa.
In the English language, these translate as
“The Book known as Entering the Middle Way”


	[translators’ obeisance]
I bow down to glorious Gentle Voice, become young.



	Chapter 1
	Perfect Happiness

	[I.1]
The listeners, and the medium Buddhas,	
Are born from the Lords of the Able;
And Buddhas take their holy birth
From the bodhisattvas.

The causes which create
These children of the Victors
Are the attitude of compassion;
A state of mind beyond duality;
And the Wish for enlightenment.


	[I.2]
And so here at the beginning,
I shall sing the praises of compassion—

For I believe that love, and only love,
Is like the seed which produces
Those excellent crops of the Victors;

And like the water which makes them grow,
And like the ripened fruit
Which then long afterwards
Is something we can enjoy.


	[I.3]
First they want a person,
Talking about “me”;
And then they crave for things,
Talking about “mine.”

I bow down to that thing
Which is compassion for all beings—
Those who revolve here helplessly,
Like buckets on a water wheel.


[I.4-5a]
The one we call the “first” is the one
Where a child of the Victors sees every living creature
As constantly shifting, and empty
Of any nature of their own—
Like the moon reflected in shifting waters;

And where their heart becomes a slave
To thoughts of compassion,
Determined to free these beings;

Living in a place of joy,
Dedicating all they do
With the prayer of Perfect Goodness.


[I.5b]
Starting from this point,
They have attained it;
As such, they are referred to
With nothing less
Than the name of “bodhisattva.”


[I.6a]
They have also taken their birth
Into the family of Those Gone Thus,
And they have eliminated, within themselves,
All three of the bonds.


	[I.6b]
This bodhisattva holds in their hands
A supreme form of happiness;
And they are further someone
Who can shake a hundred planets.


[I.7]
They want to work their way up
From the one level to the next;
They begin to move up;

And when it happens
They block all the paths
To the realms of misery.

At this point as well
All the levels for them
Relating to normal beings
Are finished.

	They are spoken of this way
As a realized being of the eight.


[I.8a]
Even those who stay at the first
Of the visions of total enlightenment

Defeat, by the force of both good karmas,
[f. 202a] The self-made buddhas,

Along with those born from the words
Of the Lords of the Able Ones;

Then they continue to exceed them further.	


[I.8b]
This same one will also exceed them
In their state of mind,
At the level called “Gone Far.”


[I.9a]
At this point,
It is none other than giving,
The first of the causes
Of total enlightenment,
Which becomes higher for them.


[I.9b]
The fact that this person
Esteems even the act
Of giving away their own flesh

Acts too as a cause for the deduction
Of something not normally apparent.


[I.10]
All people here have a hope
For happiness;
And without things,
Human beings are not happy.

The Able Ones,
Understanding that things
Come from giving,
Thus speak of giving first.


[I.11]
Even people with little compassion,
Or those with a very cruel heart,
The ones who are only
Watching out for themselves,

Can still get the things they want
From giving, the cause which puts
Suffering to a final rest.


[I.12]
Because of these instances of giving then,
Even they at some point will quickly attain
Opportunities to meet people
Who are realized beings.

And then the flow
Of their lives of suffering
Will be stopped completely,

And those with this cause
Will come to peace.
					

[I.13a]
The giving of those
Who have resolved in their hearts
To be of benefit to living beings

Makes them feel happiness,
Not long afterwards.


	[I.13b]
And these are the reasons
Why it is none other 
Than the discussion of giving

Which is primary for both
Those who are the embodiment of love,
And those who are not this embodiment.


[I.14]
When a child of the Victors
Hears “Please give it to me,”
And thinks to themselves,

They feel a happiness
Which is even greater
Than the happiness
Of the Able Ones,
When they enter into peace.

What need then is there
To mention how they feel
When they give away everything?

				 
[I.15]
What do they do with the pain
Of cutting off & giving away
Their own flesh?

When they have seen for themselves
The pain of others—
Those in the hells & the rest—

They leap to do the deed,
In order to cut that pain.


	[I.16a]
Giving which is void
Of anything which is given;

And anyone who receives it;
And anyone who gives it

Is what we say
Is a “perfection beyond the world.”


	[I.16b]
When a person feels an attachment
To all the three of these,

This has been taught
As a “perfection of the world.”
	
			
	[I.17]
Thus does the happiness we have found
Rest, perfectly, within the mind
Of a child of the Victors;

Thus does its light, like a moonstone,
Lend great beauty to this ultimate setting;

Thus does it clear away and conquer
All the masses of darkness [f. 202b].


	[chapter number]
This concludes the first wish for enlightenment, or chapter,
	of Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 2
Immaculate

[II.1a]
Their ethical way of life
Possesses both an excellence
And high qualities;

As such, they have rid themselves
Of the stench of immorality,
Even in their dreams.


[II.1b]
Since the movements
Of their body & speech & mind
Are pure,

They accumulate all ten
Of the ultimate karmic paths.


[II.2]
They possess these same
Ten paths of goodness
In a way which is even better,
Reaching extreme purity.

They are always pure,
Like the autumn moon,
Made lovely by both
Peacefulness and light.


[II.3]
If they were to view
Following an ethical way of life purely
As something that existed by nature,
Then their ethics would no longer be pure.

Thus it is that they are always free
Of their mind running in duality
Towards any of the three.


[II.4a]
When people who have practiced giving
Enjoy their wealth in a lower realm,

It’s because the legs of an ethical life
Have failed them.


	[II.4b]
When you splurge the accumulated capital
From which you are earning your interest,

You will having nothing more
That can bring you wealth later on.
			

	[II.5]
Suppose a person
Who is free to do whatever they want
In a land that suits all their needs
Cannot restrain themselves;

They will fall into the abyss,
Living under the will of others.

And then later
Who could ever get them out?


[II.6]
This is why the Victorious Ones,
When they had discussed the act of giving,
Then afterwards discussed none other than
Living an ethical way of life.

If high personal qualities flourish
In the garden of an ethical life,
The fruits of wealth
Will never be interrupted.


[II.7]
Other than an ethical way of life,
There is no cause
That can bring normal beings,

And those born of the holy words,
And those who have confirmed
Themselves in their enlightenment,
And the sons & daughters of the Victors

The achievement of definite good
And the higher realms of life.


[II.8]
A corpse cannot coexist
With the great ocean;

The auspicious cannot coexist
With something which is ill-starred.

Just so, someone who is a great being
By virtue of their ethical life

Would never want to associate
With someone who has failed
To follow this way of life.


[II.9]
An ethical way of life
Where you see them as three—

The one who gives them up,
The ones that they give up,
And the one towards whom
They give them up—

Is one that we call
A “perfection of the world.”

And it is beyond the world
Where this way of life is empty
Of attachment to these three.
	
				
[II.10]
The light that comes from the moon
Of this child of the Victorious Ones
Is the glory of the cycle of pain,

Without being the cycle of pain—
It is immaculate, free of every stain [f. 203a].

Like the light of the moon
In the days of autumn,
It banishes the painful heat
In the minds of living beings.
	

	[chapter number]
This concludes the second wish for enlightenment, or chapter,
	of Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 3
Shining

	[III.1]
This third of the bodhisattva levels
Is called “Shining,”

Because of the light given off
By the fire that burns
Every stick of the firewood
Of all the things you can know.

At this point, a light
Of a copper color, like that of the sun,
Shines forth from the child
Of Those Who Have Gone to Bliss.


	[III.2]
Suppose some
Find their thoughts disturbed,
Not a place to go,

And they cut pound after pound
Of flesh from their body,

Along with the bone,
And for a very long time.

Even then they find
Even more powerful feelings of patience
Towards the one who is cutting
Their flesh.

				
	[III.3]
The bodhisattva, who has seen
That nothing is itself,
Also sees that these things—

What is being cut,
Who is doing the cutting,
And how they are cutting
At that moment—

Are all like a reflection in a mirror,
And for this as well
Maintain their patience.


[III.4]
Do you think that—
If a person hurts you,
And you feel enmity towards them—

Then this enmity will somehow
Prevent what’s done & gone?

We can conclude then
That feeling enmity now
Over what they did
Is without question pointless.

It also contradicts the world beyond.
	
				
[III.5]
You claim you’d like to finish off
The consequences of a negative deed
You’ve done in the past—well there it is.

Hurting the other person back,
And anger towards them,

Are precisely the karmic seed
That will bring the pain back—
How then could they be right?


	[III.6]
A moment of anger
Towards bodhisattvas

Is enough to destroy
The good karma accumulated

Over the length of a hundred eons
Through giving and an ethical life;

Thus there exists no negative deed
Which is more effective
Than losing ones patience.


	[III.7a]
Losing your patience makes your appearance unattractive,
And leads you to do things which are low.

It robs you of your capacity to distinguish
Between what is right to do, and what is not;

And it quickly throws you down
Into the lower realms.
			
	
	[III.7b-8]
		Patience brings us good qualities—the opposite
		Of what we have described so far.

		It makes us attractive in our appearance,
And we become valued & cherished

To beings who are holy.  We become well versed
In what is proper to do, and what
Is not proper to do; after that happens

We take our birth among
The worldly gods or humans;
And bad deeds done are ended.
				

	[III.9]
Common beings and children of the Victors
Should come to understand

The problems of anger
And the good qualities of patience [f. 203b].

Stop ever losing your patience,
And quickly come to rely upon,

In every situation, that patience commended
By those who are realized beings.


	[III.10]
The one where we still perceive the three
Is the one which is still of the world,
Even if it happens to be dedicated
To the enlightenment of a total Buddha.

But the one where we perceive none of them
Is the only one that the Buddhas
Have described as “That perfection
Which is beyond the world.”


[III.11]
Children of the Victors at this level
Achieve concentration and clairvoyance.

They have finished off	
Ignorant liking & disliking;

And they’re always able as well
To destroy the mistaken wanting

For the objects of desire
That those of the world possess.


[III.12]
The three practices of giving & the rest
Are recommended by Those Who’ve Gone to Bliss
Primarily for those who live the home life.

What we call the “accumulation of merit”
Is these same three; this is the cause for the holy body
Of a Buddha which is physical in nature.


[III.13]
These children of the Victors,
Standing in the Sun of Shining,

Banish the darkness within their being
Even at the first; then gain a fervent desire
To destroy the darkness of beings;

And despite their cutting light,
They never lose their temper.


	[chapter number]
This concludes the third wish for enlightenment, or chapter,
 	of Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 4
Radiance

[IV.1]
All high qualities follow after joyful effort;
It is the cause for both the accumulation
Of goodness and of knowledge.

The level at which joyful effort blazes
Is the fourth, to which we give
The name of “Radiance.”


	[IV.2a]
Here the children of Those Gone to Bliss
Practice the qualities of perfect enlightenment
Even higher; and then a light arises from this—

An exceeding light is born,
A light of a copper color.


[IV.2b]
		And then everything related
		To seeing things as themselves
		Is finished off completely.


	[chapter number]
	This concludes the fourth wish for enlightenment, or chapter,
		of Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 5
Invincible

[V.1a]
		These great beings cannot be defeated,
		Even by each & every demon;

		And so the level is known
		As “Invincible.”
					

[V.1b]
		They reach a high point
		In their practice of meditation,
		As well as an excellent mind:

		And a high degree of mastery
		In a very fine state of mind
		Comprehending the nature
		Of the truths.
				

	[chapter number]
This concludes the fifth wish for enlightenment, or chapter,
 	of Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 6
Direct Perception

	[VI.1]
A bodhisattva at the level of Direct Perception [f. 204a]
Is residing in an exceptional state of meditation.

They are directly approaching the qualities
Of a totally enlightened being,
And they have seen this one suchness:
Of how all things in the world occur.

They reside in wisdom, and have thus attained
The ending of certain undesirable qualities.
	
		
	[VI.2]
Think of how a single person with sight
Can easily lead an entire group of blind people
To a place where they would like to go.

Just so, here our intelligence
Takes up the fine qualities we possess—
Those with imperfect eyes—

And they travel to that one state
Of becoming a Victor.	


	[VI.3]
I shall now impart to you the manner
Of the true nature of things,

Following the scriptural tradition
Of the realized being Nagarjuna:

Realizing that thing infinitely profound
In just that way, utilizing the scriptures
And, beyond them, reasoning.


	[VI.4-5a]
There are certain individuals who—
Even as common beings—
Feel repeated sensations of overwhelming joy
When they hear of emptiness.

This joy brings tears to their eyes,
And they get goosebumps.

These kinds of people have the seeds
For the mind of a fully enlightened Buddha.

These people then are proper vessels
To whom you can teach emptiness;
These are the ones to whom you should teach
The reality which is ultimate.


	[VI.5b-7a]
		And they will achieve good qualities
		Which follow upon this:

They forever continue to
Observe a pure code of ethics;

		They make efforts in the act of giving;
		They dedicate themselves to great compassion;
		And they adhere to the practice of patience.

		They take all these good deeds
		And dedicate them to reaching enlightenment,
		So that they can free all living beings.

		Those who have reached total enlightenment
		Pay high respect to these bodhisattvas.


	[VI.7b]
An individual who is well versed
In both the profound & the widespread

Will, in time, attain the level
Of Perfect Happiness.

Lend then your ears to this path,
Those who aspire to reach it.
			
	
	[VI.8a]
This cannot occur through that—
And how could it occur
Through something other?

Nor could it through both.
How as well could it occur
Without a cause at all?


[VI.8b]
There would be no additional
Point at all served to this,
If it were to occur through that.


[VI.8c-VI.9a]
		If something had already grown,
		It would as well be totally illogical
		For it to grow once more.

		And suppose you fantasize
		That something already grown
		Could ever grow again;

		It would then be the case
That we could never observe
		Sprouts & such growing here.
				

[VI.9b]
The seed could only
Continue to grow,

Until the very end
Of the universe.


[VI.9c]
How could the presence
Of the one ever act [f. 204b]
To destroy the other?


	[VI.10a]
		According to you, the sprout
		Could have no shape, or color,
		Or taste or properties,

		Or ripening that was different
		From that of the seed
		Which had given it birth.


	[VI.10b]
Suppose the self-nature
In the previous one fades away,

And transforms into
The essence of the other—

And at that point,
Its is that very one.

But how could that be?


	[VI.11]
		Suppose that, as you put it,
		The seed & the sprout here
		Were not not the other.

		Then just as the seed,
		Neither could the sprout
		Be something that we held.

		Or else we could also say that,
		Since these two are the same,
		Then just as the sprout
Is something that is held,

The other too would have to be—
And so we refuse to accept this idea.			
	

	[VI.12a]
		Not even in the everyday world
		Would people accept the idea
		That they were one & the same.

		This is because,
		Even if the cause ends,
		Its result can still be observed.


[VI.12b]
		Thus it is that
		The fanciful idea
		That objects grow from themselves

		Is illogical, both in the way
		Things are, and in
		The everyday world as well.


[VI.13]
		If we accept that a thing
		Could grow from itself,
		It would be the case that

		The thing being produced;
		And the thing doing the producing;
		The very act; and the agent
		Would have to be one & the same.
	
		They are though not the same;
		And so the idea that something
		Could grow from itself
		Is not something that we
		Should ever accept.

		After all, the problems
		Described at length
		Would then result.


[VI.14]
		Suppose it were the case
		That something other
		Could grow, based on
		Something other;

		Well then we would get
		A thick darkness
		Even from flames.
	
		And all objects
		Would have to grow
		From all other objects;

		For the reason that
		Each & every thing
		That did not act
		To produce the thing

		Would be exactly the same,
		In being different.
	

[VI.15]
		Now suppose someone says
		“We specify anything
		Which can be created,
		As such, as the result.

		And anything which is
		Capable of producing
		Is a cause, even if
		It is something other.

		A rice sprout grows
		From what is incorporated
		Into a single flow,

		And from something
		That does function
		To produce it.

		As such, it is not something
		That can grow, in the same way,
		From barley or the like.”			


[VI.16]
		Take barley; and filaments;
		The flame of the forest;
		Or anything of the like.
	
These are not at all things
That we could ever agree
Act to produce a rice sprout,
Nor do they possess the capacity;

They are not included in a single flow,
Nor are they the same.

Just so, neither is the rice seed
For it; because it is entirely other.


[VI.17]
		It is not the case
		That the sprout and seed
		Exist at the same time;
	
		If they cannot be
		Totally other,
		Then how could the seed
		Be something entirely other?

		Neither, therefore,
		Is it the case
		That the birth of a sprout
		From a seed could be [f. 205a].

		As such, we implore you
		To relinquish this position,
		Where you claim that things
		Grow from something other.			


	[VI.18]
Now the others may claim:
“We can observe
How the arms of a scale
Rising & descending,

These two, are not such
That they do not occur
At the same time.

The growth & the ending
Of what is produced,
And what does the producing,
Occur too in a similar way.”

This idea though is not correct;
Even given that these two
Are concurrent,
There would not be here
Simultaneity.				


[VI.19]
		Suppose that,
		In the act of growing,
		It is still approaching growth;
		And as such it is not
		Something that exists.

		There is though that
		Which is in the act of ending;
		But we treat it as something
		Approaching its destruction.

		How then in this moment
		Could it be that these
		Were the same as the scale?

		If the agent were absent,
		Then for this growing to exist
		Would be contrary
		To the very concept of logic.


	[VI.20]
Suppose the eye and such
Which are what produce
And are simultaneous to
The awareness of the eye;

As well as the discrimination
And the like which occur
In conjunction,

Are—relative to it—
Perfectly other.

What purpose
Could possibly be served
By the occurrence of something
That already existed?

Suppose you say
That there is none;
We have already described
The problem with that case.				


[VI.21]
		Suppose something produces
		Something produced;
		And what it produces
		Is something other.

		Let’s calculate whether
		That exists; or else does not;
		Or both; or is devoid of either.

		Suppose it existed;
		Then what need would there be
		For what acted to produce it?

		And if on the other hand
		It did not exist,
		Then what would it do for it?

		If both, what would it do?
		And if it were devoid,
		What again could it do?


[VI.22]
		Those who remain
		With their own viewpoints
		Consider the world accurate;

		What could possibly be here
		The use of articulating
The point with this logic?

		What people of the world
		Perceive is that things issue
		From things which are
Other than them.

What purpose would
The logic for this be—
For the fact that things do grow
From things that are other?


[VI.23]
All objects involve
Two different natures:
Objects discovered
By seeing what is pure
And what is a lie.

It was declared that the one
Which serves as the object
When we see the pure
Is suchness;

And that seen to be a lie
Is deceptive reality.


[VI.24]
We take the position
That those which see the lie
Are also of two types:

Where the powers are clear,
And where the powers
Are defective.

We take the position
That states of mind
Belonging to those
With powers
Possessing a defect,

Relative to states of mind
With powers which are sound,
Are mistaken.	


[VI.25]
		Things which are held
		By the six senses where they

		Are not adversely affected
		Are those perceived
		By the everyday world;
 
		Relative to the world itself,
		These are real—the rest
		Are established as mistaken,
		Even just to the world [f. 205b].


	[VI.26]
The nature of the self—
As it is imagined
By those of lower views,

Inspired by the sleep
Of misunderstanding;

And those things imputed
In illusions, mirages, & the like,

Are nothing that
Could ever exist,
Even relative to the world.


[VI.27]
The perceptions of eyes
Clouded with cataracts

Cannot draw into question
A state of mind
Without such cataracts;

And there is nothing about
A mind which has abandoned
The wisdom free of stain

Which could ever draw
Into question the state of mind
Which is free of stain—

These two cases then
Are the same.


[VI.28]
Dark ignorance draws a veil
Over the nature of things,
And from that fact is deception.

		Due to this, things
		That are a false construct
		Appear as though
		They were real.

		These were described
		By the Able One to be
		A deceptive reality:

		Objects which make up
		This false construct
		To the deceptive.


	[VI.29]
	Suppose that a person,
	Due to some cataracts,
	Thinks they see something
	As different than it really is:

	They perceive a strand
	Of hair, or something of the like.

	And now suppose a person
	With clear eyes looks down
	Where those actual things
	Are supposed to be.
	
	They are the one
	Who sees the real;

	Understand the case here
	As being the same.


	[VI.30]
Suppose that people
Of the world were accurate;

These people of the world then
Would have to see the real nature.

If that were so,
Then there would be no need
For other realized beings.

And what use then
Would be served by
The path of the realized?

Neither do these simple fools
Enjoy any accurate perception
At all.


[VI.31a]
Those of the world
Are not, in any way,
An accurate perception.

For this reason,
The world cannot draw
Anything into question,

With regard to
The way things are.


[VI.31b]
Suppose that
The state of things
In the everyday world

Were itself disallowed
By the very conventions
Of this same world;

This same person
Would be contradicted
By the world.


[VI.32]
		Because the world
		Makes the declaration,

		“I was the one who
		Gave birth to this child,”

		And people think
		To themselves,
		“I planted the tree,”
		
		Things growing from things
That are other than them

Is not something that we see
Even in the everyday world.


[VI.33]
And for what reason?
A sprout is not something
Which exists as something
Other than the seed;

Therefore, by the time
Of the sprout, the seed
Has gone out of existence;
That no longer exists.

For the reason that
They are not such
That they exist
As one single thing,

Because it’s not,
We never speak of a seed
Which is present,
By the time of the sprout.


[VI.34]
Suppose they existed
By definition; if that
Were something depending,
In a manner discounting these,

Entities would have to be
Destroyed; and as such,

Emptiness must act
As a cause
For the destruction
Of the entities.

Yet neither is that
Reasonable; as such,

It could never occur
That objects could exist.


[VI.35]
In a selected case,
We might make an examination
Of these things, and then

We might not be able
To discover whether

Entities involved with suchness
Existed, in their nature,
Towards us.

As such,
In the nominal reality 
Of the everyday world,

No one undertakes
Those kinds of examination.


[VI.36]
Use the same rationale
As at the point of
	The way things are:

	That it would be illogical [f. 206a]
	To say that a thing
	Could have grown

	Either from itself,
	Or from something different.

	This very same reasoning
	Applies in nominal cases
	As well, to show that
	It could not be logical.

	What kind can you point to,
	For the growing?


[VI.37]
		Things which are empty—
		A reflection in a mirror,
		And so on—
	
		Rely upon the coming together;
		And we cannot say
		This is something
		The world itself wouldn’t say.

		It’s just the same
		As there: a reflection
		And the like are empty,

		And from these grow
		Awareness which assumes
		The likeness of it.


[VI.38a]
		All functioning things—
		Even though they are empty—

		Quite certainly grow,
Just as these, from those
Of emptiness.


	[VI.38b]
These things
Neither last forever
Nor simply discontinue.


[VI.39]
	For this reason,
	Neither does it stop
	Through any nature
	Of its own.

	As such, it has
The power for this,
Even refusing
A foundation consciousness.

In particular ones,
Karma can stop,
And a very long time
Can pass; but even then,

You should understand,
The exact consequence
Will be given forth.


[VI.40]
		One may see certain objects
		Perceived inside a dream;

		And then foolish people
		Might awake,
		And begin to feel desire.

		Just so,
		A karma which is not
		Something that exists
		With any nature of its own

		Can stop,	
		And there can be
		A consequence from it.


[VI.41]
		It’s also like objects
		Equivalent in the way
		They’re not really there;

		Those with cataracts
		Are sure they see
		Strands of hair,

		But other things
		That we don’t even see.

		Similarly,
		You should understand
		That it’s not as if
		What has ripened
		Will ripen once again.
		

[VI.42]
		As such, we can see
		That a non-virtuous ripening
		Is black karma,

		While that virtuous ripening
		Is from a good deed.

		And also intelligent ones
		Who understand
		There exists no virtue
		Nor non-virtue
		Come to be freed.

		And they undertake
		To prevent overthinking
		Karma & its consequences.


[VI.43]
	Statements as thus—
That there does exist
	One of the foundation,

	And there does exist
	A very essence of the person

	Which is only
	In and of these parts
	To the person—

	Were for those particular
	Ones who could not comprehend
	Extraordinarily deep points.


[VI.44]
	It’s like how
The Buddha is free
	From the view
	Of the destructible collection,

	But did still give teachings
	Using “me” and “mine.”

	This is a similar case:
	Things admittedly have
No nature of their own,

And yet only
In a figurative sense
It was stated
That things did exist.


[VI.45]
	They see there are no
	Objects of perception;

	And they see none
	Which act to hold
	To these—

		They come to a deep
		Realization that all three
		Realms of existence
		Are only consciousness itself.

		A bodhisattva who
		Is staying in wisdom
		Comes to a realization

		Of that real nature of things:
		That they are only consciousness.
		

[VI.46]
	It’s like the great ocean,
	Instigated by the winds [206b];

	And from there
	The waves occur.

	Just so do we have
	What we call
	“The all-foundation”

	For the deep seeds
	Of everything;

	And from that arise
	What is nothing more
	Than consciousness,

	Through energies
	Concordant with them.


[VI.47a]
	Therefore an essential nature
	To dominated things
	
	Is the cause for things
	Which exist only as
	They are given these names.


[VI.47b]
	They occur in a lack
	Of outer objects
	Which are grasped;
	
	And they exist,
	And have a nature,

	Never objects of
Any elaboration.


[VI.48]
		Where then is
		The metaphor for
		A mind where there
		Are no outer objects?

		Suppose you say
		It is the same
		As a dream—
		We need to consider this.

		Suppose that—
		Even just in a dream—
		There’s a mind;

		In ours there is
		No such existence:
		You would have no
		Metaphor that existed.


[VI.49]
	Suppose that,
	When we wake,
	We remember the dream;
	And our mind existed.

	From that then
	Outside objects
	Would be just so.

	It follows from this—
	The memory where
	You think to yourself,
	“I saw something”;

	And moreover
	Such things existed
	As outside.


[VI.50]
		If, in our sleep,
		The mind of vision
		Is impossible,

		Then those are not
		Something; rather,
		All that is present is
		The awareness of our thoughts.

		We are attached to
		An aspect of it;
		The outside world itself.

		Suppose you accept that
		It’s just the same here
		As the way in a dream.


[VI.51]
		Just the way you say
		Outside objects never start
		In a dream,

		The thought too,
		In the same manner,
		Never starts.

		The eye and
		The object of the eye,
		And the state of mind
		Triggered by them—

		All three—
Are also deceptive.		


[VI.52a]
	The extra three
	For the ear and so on
	Also have no growing.


	[VI.52b]
	Just as in a dream,
	Here in waking too
	Entities are deceptive.

	As such, this mind
	Is nothing that exists.

	None of the objects
	Of activity
	Have any existence;

	And neither do
	The powers exist.


[VI.53]
		It’s just as here,
		When we’re awake.

		And it’s the same
		For those who have
		Not yet woken;

		For that length of time,
		All three exist to them.

		When they have awakened,
		None of the three
		Exist any more.

		Just so, we can
		Finish the sleep
		Of dark ignorance;
		Such is it.


[VI.54]
	A power which has 
Cataracts, a particular
State of mind,

Sees certain strands
		Due to the influence
		Of the cataracts.

		Relative to this mind,
		Both of them are real.

		To one seeing objects clearly,
		Both are false.


[VI.55]
		Suppose a state of mind
		Were there in the absence
		Of an existing object;

		The object of that strand
		Would have an eye which
		Was connected with it;

		And one who had
		No cataracts would also
		Have a state of mind
		With a strand of hair—

		And for this reason
		It is not the case;
		It is not something
		Which could exist.


[VI.56a]
		Suppose this were
Your position:

“It is not the case
		That there would be
		Any ripening
		
		Of the potential
		For a state of mind
		With those who saw.

		For this reason then,
		It is not the case
		That a state of mind could
		Ever come with these

		Because it was devoid
		Of any entity
		Which possessed
		An existing object.”


	[VI.56b]
	Since there is no such thing
	As a potential like this
	Which exists [f. 207a],

	That is not something
	Which could be established.


	[VI.57a]
	It is not a possibility
	That there could exist
	A potential to what
	Had already grown;

	Neither could there exist
	Any potential that had
	A nature of
Not having yet grown.


	[VI.57b]
	There would exist none
	Characterized by
	A certain feature,

	In the absence of
	A feature.

	This would also
	Have to exist
	With the child
	Of a barren woman.


[VI.58]
		Suppose you assert
		That you apply a term
		To that which is
		Yet to come.

		But there cannot exist
		Any which could arise
		In the absence
		Of a potential.

These are things
Which occur in a
Codependent relationship;

The holy ones
Would say that
That is something
Which could only never exist.


[VI.59]
	Suppose that
	Some potential
	From the stopping
	Ripens, and from that
	There comes this.

	Something other
	Is arising from
	A potential which
	Is something other.

	In a case where
	Things have the flow
	There exist those
	Distinct from one another;

	In that case
	Everything would happen
	From everything.


[VI.60]
	Suppose then
	There is the composite
	Flow of those
	That are different
	From each other.

	But suppose you say
	That the flow for those
	Could never involve
	Separate things;

	And so there is
	No such problem.

	This idea though
	Is something that
	You would still
	Have to prove.

	It is illogical to say
	That there could be
	Any opportunity

	For a flow of things
	That were not separate.	


[VI.61]
	John is leaning on Joe;
	Still, they are entities
	That are essentially different;
	
As such, they are not
Sharing a single flow.

For those that were
Separate things that
Existed by definition,

It would not be logical
That they were sharing
A single flow.


[VI.62]
The growing of
Awareness of the eye
Springs forth from
That potential which
Occurs just after that.

And its consciousness
Is the support for a potential;

They think of this and say,
“This is the eye,
A physical sense power.”


[VI.63]
		Here awareness
		That arises from
		The sense powers

		Comes from
		Seeds for it
		In the absence
		Of outer objects.

		Beings though fail
		To understand that
		What arises is just

		The appearance
		Of blue and the like,
			
		Believing that
		What is mind 
		Constitutes outer
		Objects of perception.


[VI.64]
		In a dream,
		There are no physical objects
		Which are other entities.

		The potential for them ripens,
		And from that arises
		A state of mind
		With the aspects of those.

		In this very same way,
		Here when we are awake
		As well, there are none outer;
		What we have is the thought.

		Suppose you take this position.
		

[VI.65]
		In a dream,
		A state of mind
		Comes up which is
		The thought,
	
		And takes on
		An aspect of blue
		Or whatever it may be,

		Even though
		There is no sense power
		Of the eye there.

		A deep seed
		Within it ripens;

		In this case,
		Why wouldn’t a person
		Who was blind
		Come to see?


[VI.66]
		Suppose that,
		As you would have it,

		There does exist the
		Ripening of the potential
		For the sixth
		Within a dream;

		And suppose that
		This were absent
		During the waking state.

		Why then wouldn’t it be
		Correct to say that

		Here there was no ripening of
		The potential for the sixth,

		And just so no such thing
		During the dream?


[VI.67]
		As they do when
		There is no eye,
		For this they are not
		Acting as a cause.

		Just so, in a
		Dream as well,
		Sleep could not be
		The cause [f. 207b].

		For that reason,
		You would accept
That in a dream
As well as that,

There were
False entities
Having objects

As the cause
For the perception
Of the eye.


[VI.68a]
		Whatever response it is
		That these might make,
		We can see that this
		Assertion is equivalent.

		As such,
		This particular argument
		Actually clears the beliefs.


	[VI.68b]
	The Buddhas have not
	Ever taught the idea,

	In any at all, that
	Entities could exist.


[VI.69]
		There is that case
		Where high practitioners
		Follow the advice
		Of their spiritual teachers,
		
		And see the entire
		Surface of the earth
		Covered with skeletons.

		There also they see,
		In the absence
Of all three arising.

And that’s because
It has been described
As a mistaken
Bringing to the mind.
		

[VI.70]
		Suppose you have
		Objects of the awareness
		Of a sense power,
		And the same
		For all of them.

		Just so,
For certain others
There should also
Be a perception,
A mind of the repulsive,

When they direct
Their minds towards
The same objects:
The perception 
Should also occur.

Neither would this
Be deceptive.


[VI.71a]
	For cases equivalent
To a state of mind 
With a sense power
That has cataracts,

There is also
The state of mind
Of pus for those
Craving spirits

Towards a stream
Of fresh water.


[VI.71b]
	To summarize,
	There is nothing
	In the universe;

	Just so, there is
	No state of mind.

	This is the point
	We need to understand.


[VI.72]
		Suppose that there exist
		No objects to be held,
		Devoid then of any
		Holding itself;

		And that there
		Could exist
		Dominated entities
		That were empty
		Of the two.

		How is it then
		That you can perceive
		The existence of these?

		It would be wrong
To say there did exist
Something there,
Even though it wasn’t held.


[VI.73a]
		This particular one
		Is not something
		That could establish these,
		By experiencing them.


[VI.73b]
		Suppose we were
		To establish it
		From recollection
		At a later time.

		They are
		Bringing it up
		In order to substantiate
		
		That which has not yet
		Been established.

		The fact that this
		Does not exist
		Is not something
		Which serves to establish it.


[VI.74]
	In the end, your proofs
	Are going to rely upon
	It knowing itself;

	But it is still
	Not logical
	For recollection
	To recall,

	Because they are
	Other than each other.

	It’s the same as
	What could have arisen
	In the mindstream of one
	Who has not known;

	That logical statement
	Would also obviate details.


[VI.75]
		First of all, in ours
		That recollection of
		Of having undergone
		An experience

		Could never be
		Something other.

		For this reason,
		It will happen
		That there will be
		A recollection

		Where we say to ourselves,
		“I have seen this.”

This too is the way
Of the world;
The way that the world
Speaks of things.


[VI.76]
		Therefore, apperception
		Is something that
		Doesn’t exist;

		What is it then
		That holds to your
		Dominated entities?

		The agent,
		The object of the action,
		And the act
		Are not one & the same.

		As such,
		It would be inappropriate
		To say that this
		Were doing the holding.


[VI.77]
		Suppose that
		There is nothing
		Which can start,

		And that
		There does exist
		An entity which is
		A dominated one
	
		And has a nature
		Such that it is
		Not perceived.

		There is yet
		Another why
		It would be illogical
		To say that such existed [f. 208a]:

		The child of a
		Barren woman
		Has done so much damage.


[VI.78]
	At such point
That there did not exist
Even the slightest
Dominated entities,

Then how could
Something ever exist
As a deceptive reason?

If it accords to
These other ones,
Attached to thinking
Of that substance,

Then the way that
The everyday world
Posits how things exist
Is completely lost.


[VI.79]
		Those who have
		Wandered away
		From the path of
		Our master, Nagarjuna,

		Lack the method
		Needed to attain peace.

		These people have lost
		The true concepts
		Of deceptive reality
		And the reality
		Of suchness.

		Once we have lost this,
		There is no possibility
		That we can achieve freedom.


[VI.80]
		There is nominal reality,
		Which becomes a method,
		And ultimate reality,
		Which comes from the method.

		Any person who fails
		To understand the divisions
		Of these two has entered
		Into a mistaken path,
		Of mistaken ideas.


[VI.81]
	You say that
	Dominated entities
	Are real;

	And then when
	You agree to it,
	
	A deceptive reality
	Is not something
	We can accept.

		It is meant
		For a particular effect—

		That all these things
		Are not things
		Which exist.

		Nonetheless,
		What we say is
		That they exist,

		To the appearances
		Of the world.


[VI.82]
	None exists
	For those who reside
	In peace, where
	
	Enemy destroyers
	Have eliminated
	The heaps.

	Suppose that,
	In a similar way,

	There were none
	In the general
	World as well.

	I do not say that
	It would be similar;	

	That there could exist
	One like this
	For the world.


[VI.83]
		If the world
		Is not something
		That could call your
		Ideas into question,

		Then you can
		Go ahead and deny it
		Relative to
		The world itself.

		You and the world
Can go ahead
And argue with
Each other on this.

Once you are done,
I will put my support
Behind the stronger.


[VI.84]
		A bodhisattva
		Headed towards
		The manifestation

		Comes to the realization
		That these three
		Worlds of pain
		Are nothing but the mind.

		What this means
		For them is that
		They have blocked
		
The idea of an
		Unchanging self
		As the creator,

		And come to
		The realization.


[VI.85]
		Thus it is
		The Journey to Langka
		Speaks of the diamond weapon

		Consisting of speech
		Used by the Omniscient One
		To smash down
		The lofty summit
		
		Of the mountain
		Of the River Schools.

		This is the one
		Described in order
		To carve out
		The real intent.	


[VI.86]
		Look at the way
		The River Schools—

		In this or that
		Of the commentaries
		Of theirs—

		Speak of the person
		And such and such.

		The Victors though
		Do not see these
		As creators,

		And so have stated
		That it is only the mind
		Which is the creator.		


[VI.87]
	We refer to those
	Who have expanded
	Their mind
	Into suchness
	As “Buddhas.”

	In the same way,
	It is “mind only”
	In the sense of 
	The main thing.

	This is from
	References in sutra
	Which say that

	“For the world,
	There is only mind [f. 208b].”

	Here it is not the
	Meaning of sutra to be
	Some kind of denial
	Of outer form.


[VI.88]
		Suppose all these
		Were referred to
		As “only the mind,”

		And the Buddha
		Knew this, and so
		Meant in this
To deny “form itself.”

And then how
Could it be in it
For the Great Being
To state that the mind

Was born from
Dark ignorance
And karma?


[VI.89]
	This one thing,
	The mind,

	Has set forth
		The world
		Of living beings,

		And the vessel
		Of the outer world,
		With all its
		Endless variation.

		It was stated that
All the beings there are
Have been created by karma;

If we were to eliminate
The mind, then there
Would no longer be
Any karma either.	


[VI.90]
		We would
		Have to admit
		That physical matter
		Does exist;

		It is not the case
		That with this
		You find the
		One creator,

		As in the case
		Of the mind.
		
		As such, we reject
		Any creator other than
		The mind itself;

		But that is not denying
		Outer form itself.


[VI.91]
		All five do exist,
Just as they are
Spoken of in
		The everyday world:

		That part
		Can be found
		In the way things are,
		According to the world.

		In a case where
		We accept that
		There can appear
		That wisdom
		Of suchness,

		These five
		Do not occur
		For a deep practitioner.


[VI.92a]
		If there exists
		No form,
		Then you shouldn’t
		Hold that mind
		Exists either.

		And if
		Mind exists,
		You shouldn’t
Be holding that
There exists no form.


[VI.92b]
		In sutras
		On the ways
		Of wisdom,

		The Buddha
		Treated them
		As equivalent,
		In rejecting.

		He also stated this
		In the teachings
		Of higher knowledge.


[VI.93]
		Even though
These stages
		Of the two realities
		Are destroyed,

		That doesn’t mean
		That your idea
		Of the substantial
		Is established;
		For it was disproved.

		Thus it is that,
		Because of stages
		Like that,
		
		Entities have
		Never arisen,
		For all the time
		There ever was.

		It is reasonable
		To say,
		In the world,
		That they have arisen.


[VI.94]
There is that sutra
Which states that
The appearance
Of the outside
Is nothing that exists.

What this is saying
Is that the mind
Appears in a
Variety of ways.

There are those
With an extreme
Attraction to forms;

And so they put
A stop to forms
For these individuals—

And those were only intended
As something metaphorical.


[VI.95a]
	This statement was made
	By the Teacher only
	As something to be
	Taken figuratively;

	It can also be established
	That it was only meant
	As metaphorical,
	And nothing more—
	
	Through logical reasoning.


	[VI.95b]
	There are
Citations from
	The body of sutras
	Like those;

	But there are
	Even more citations

	Which these quotations
	Explain to be taken
	Metaphorically.


[VI.96]
		The Buddhas
		Have stated that
		If no objects exist,

		And then we
Clear away
The idea of a
State of mind,

		Then people can
		Come to this idea
		More easily.

		If there are no
		Objects of knowledge,

		We can deny
		Any perception,
		And establish that.

		Therefore
		At the beginning
		We focus on denying
		Objects of knowledge.


[VI.97]
		That is, we should
		Come to know
		The whole story
		Of the scriptures.

		There are certain sutras
		Which contain ideas
		That explain something
		Other than suchness.

		They were taught
		In a figurative way;
		We should realize that,
		And interpret them [f. 209a].

		And any which conveys
		The idea of emptiness
		Should be understood
		As something
		To be taken literally.


[VI.98]
		It is also not the nature
		Of clear thinking
		To say that things
		Could arise from
		A combination.

		Why is that?
		Because those same
		Problems already raised
		Would strike
		Like lightning.

		From the point
		Of the everyday world
		There are none;

		And speaking as well
		From the point of view
		Of suchness,

		Neither is this idea
		Something that
		We can accept.

		The reason
		That this is true
		Is that there
		Is no such thing

		As an arising
		Accomplished separately.


[VI.99]
		Suppose then
		That it were the case
		That arising were
		Something that happened
		
		Only without
		A cause at all.

		In that case,
		Then all there is
		Would also have to
Simply pop up.

People of the
Everyday world,
Hoping that results
Will make their appearance,

Expend hundreds
Of efforts to accumulate
The seeds and so forth;

All this would
Never go on.


[VI.100]
		Suppose that the variety
		Of living beings
		Was simply devoid
		Of any cause.

		In this case,
		They would all become
		Something totally ineffable,

		Like the scent and color
		Of a blue lotus
		That suddenly popped
		Out in thin air.

		And then it would be
		The same with this
		Entire world that
		We hold before us,
		With all its endless variety.

		As such, you must
Understand that the world
Before us is the same
As our mind,

And something
From its own causes.	


[VI.101]
		It is only constructs
		Of these elements
		Which can serve as
		The object of your mind.

		And if things
		Were not such constructs,

		Then how on earth
		Could that which is
The thick darkness
		Of your mind itself

		Ever come to grasp,
		In a correct way,
		A world beyond
		This one?


[VI.102]
		When you good fellows
		Undertake to deny
		The existence of a world
		Beyond this one,

		You are looking
		At the nature
		Of existing things

		In a way which is
		Completely mistaken.

		This is equivalent
		To a basis for that view:

		A body which is
		A basis for that
		To be possessed.

		It is similar to
That point at which
You take a position

Where you accept
The very existence
Of embodiments
Of the elements.


[VI.103]
We have long since
Explained how it is
That these elements
Cannot be something
Which exists.

And how was it?
We undertook to deny,
Previously, that things
Could grow from themselves;

From some other;
From both; or without
Any cause at all.

We have already denied
The idea in common.
Much less with these elements,

This is not something
Where we have given
No explanation.


[VI.104a]
		For the reason
		That there can exist
		No arising of a thing
		Which could occur
		From itself,

		Or from something other,
		Or from both,
		Or without relying
		Upon any cause at all,

		Entities are devoid
		Of some nature
		Of their own.


[VI.104b]
		The fact is that
		The everyday world
		Exists in a dense
		Lack of understanding

		Which is just the same
		As a huge gathering
		Of rain clouds.

		And for that reason, they have
		A mistaken impression
		Of the objects around them;

		This is how things make
		Their appearance to them.


[VI.105]
It’s possible
For some people,
By force of a cataract,

To be made to hold,
Mistakenly,

A strand of hair,
One moon as two,
The pattern
Of a peacock’s feathers,

A random fly, or
Something of the like [f. 209b].

The same sort of thing
Happens with those
Who are not wise,

Due to the problem
Of their dark ignorance.

They perceive
Various objects
Like produced things
With their intellect.


[VI.106]
		This description
		Is without doubt
		A reference to the fact

		That it is only those
		Who are not wise
		Who understand all this

		As saying that karma
		Occurs dependent upon
		Dark ignorance;

		And without
		This dark ignorance, then
		That would not occur.

		The wise grasp
		That these are
		Perfectly empty,

		Using the bright sun
		Of their fine minds
		To dispel—completely—
		That thick fog;
		And they are liberated.


[VI.107]
	If it’s the case
	That all these things
	Have nothing
	In & of themselves,

	Then they are like
	The child of
	A barren woman,
	
	And the same
	In a nominal sense:
	They really do
	Possess none.

	And then
	For that reason,
	They could exist
	Only by nature.


[VI.108]
	Strands of hair
	Or the like act
	As objects

	For a person
	Who possesses
	Cataracts or such;

	And these
	Have never started.

	So let’s assume first
	That we seek out
	The way that
	Things really are.

	After that,
	There’s the connection
	To the cataracts
	Of misunderstanding.


[VI.109]
		Now suppose there is
		A dream, along
With a city of the
Craving spirits.

Or water flowing
From a mirage—
An illusionist at work—
Or a reflection,

Or something
Of the like:
Things that
Never started.

When we come to see,
We can say that
They are equivalent

In not being
Existing entities.

And you should be
Asking, how are
All these things?

It doesn’t make sense!


[VI.110]
		Speaking purely,
		Things never start
		In any way at all.

		And yet this is not
		Something that can be
		An object that is seen

		In the eyes of the
		Everyday world,

		In the way that
		They would regard
		The child of
		A barren woman.

		And since it is not,
		This statement
		Is itself inconclusive.


[VI.111]
		The child
		Of a barren woman
		Is not something

		Which arises
		All on its own accord;

		It has no existence
		In & of itself.

		Neither is it
Something which exists,
In the everyday world.

Just so,
All these entities
Have never arisen through
		Some essential nature;

		For the world, or from
		The point of view
		Of suchness.
 

[VI.112]
		For this reason,
		The Teacher has stated
		That all the objects
		That exist consist

		Of peace from
		The very beginning;

		And are devoid
		Of arising;

		And that they have,
		By their very nature,
		Gone entirely to nirvana.

		As such,
		They have never
		Displayed any arising.


[VI.113]
		Things like
		Pitchers and the like
		Are not such that
		
		They exist
		In their essence;

		They do though
Exist as they are
Spoken of in the
World at large.

All the entities
That exist
Follow this
Very same pattern;

It is not the case
That they would
Have to be

The equivalent
Of the child
Of a barren woman.


[VI.114]
	It is indeed the case
	That these entities
	Do not arise without
	Any cause at all;

	Nor from the cause
	Of some supreme
Being, or the like.

And because
These do not arise
From themselves,

From something other,
Or from both,

Their arisal
Most definitely flows
From a dependence.


[VI.115]
		The fact is
		That entities will
		Always spring forth
		In dependence.

		Thus these notions
		Cannot stand up
		Under close examination.

		And thus things
		Occur in dependence [f. 210a];

		This logic serves
		To sever all the cables
		Of the vast net
		Of terrible viewpoints.


[VI.116]
		We have already examined,
		In depth, these notions
		That things could exist,

		And how things
		Could never be.

		In the absence
		Of things,
		These will never
		Come up;

		It’s like,
		For example,
		The way that

		Fire can never occur
		In the absence
Of firewood.


[VI.117]
		Common beings
		Are enslaved by notions;

		Deep practitioners
		Do not imagine things,
		And become liberated.

		The wise
Have presented this:

The results of
Correct analysis,
Turning away
From those notions.		


[VI.118]
		Logical arguments
		In the classical commentary
		Were not made

		Out of a love for
		Disputation.

		They were for teaching
		The concept of suchness,
		For the purpose
		Of liberating beings.

		Suppose it is the case
		That, when we undertake
		To present the details
		Of our explanations
		Of suchness,

		The texts of other
		Groups are shattered.
		You cannot fault us
		For that.


[VI.119]
	When we have attachment
	To our own viewpoints,
	And when—
	In the same way—
	
	We feel disturbed
	By views, we are
	Falling into those
	Very notions.

	In this case,
	We will be able
	To clear away

	Those tendencies
	To feel attachment
	And aversion—

	When we are able
	To analyze things,
	We find ourselves
	Liberated, with speed.


[VI.120]
		Our intellect
		Comes to see

		That each & every
		One of the troubles
		Of the negative emotions

		Comes from
		The view of destruction.

		What we come to realize
		Is that what this
Thinks it sees
Is the self;

And then the
Deep practitioner
Works to stop
The self.
		

[VI.121a]
		That River system
		Imagines a consumer
		Which is a self that is
Unchanging & functioning;

Although not
The creator.

It does not have
The qualities, and
Performs no activity.	


[VI.121b]
	Based upon various
	Minor distinctions,

	There have developed
	The different systems
	Of the River Schools.


[VI.122]
		Because things
		Are devoid of arising,
		
Like the child
		Of a barren woman,

		It is not the case
With the self—
		They are not reality.

		This cannot
		Logically be
		The basis for

		Our tendency to
		Grasp to some “me.”

		We deny
		The existence
		In a deceptive sense
		As well.


[VI.123]
		It’s because
		All the features that
		These River Schools
		Describe both in

		Those classical commentaries
		And these classical commentaries

		Are themselves
		Drawn into question
		
		By the logic of things
		Never arising
		That they declare among
		Themselves so widely.
