		A response to express
		The position about

		Contact or anything
		Of the like; so here,
		We engaged in
		Our own attack.

		There does not exist one
With further argument.

The remainder
Already described
In these words

Can be understood
From this very position.		


[VI.179]
	In order to free beings,
He stated that
	There are no objects

	Which possess
	Some self-nature;

	And that this
	Has two divisions:
	
	That to the person,
	And that to things.

	Having taught as such,
He went on to
Lay out all the
Different divisions

Of this very thing,
For different disciples.


[VI.180]
	He utilized
	Great detail,

	First explaining
	Sixteen divisions
	Of emptiness,

	And then he
	Went over the same
	In a briefer way,
	With four types.

	And he acknowledged
	As well that
These constituted
The greater way.


[VI.181]
	Why is it?  Because
	The nature of this
	Is that the eye
	Is empty of the eye.

	In the same way
	We also refer
	To the ear, the nose,
	The tongue, the body,
	And the thought [f. 213b].


[VI.182]
		They are not things
		Which remain
		In a solid manner;

		Nor do they stop
		In this way.

		The eye and the
		Rest of the six
		
		Do not exist
		Through any nature;

		What we accept
		As being emptiness
		On the inside
		Is this fact.


[VI.183]
	Form is empty
	Of existing through form,	

	Due to the fact
	That the very nature
	Of it is that.


[VI.184a]
		The fact of
The lack of a nature
		To form and the rest
		Is what we say is
		“Emptiness on the outside.”


[VI.184b]
		It is both;
		And the fact
		That it does not exist

		Through any
		Essential nature

		Constitutes emptiness
		On the outside
		And the inside.


[VI.185]
		The fact that entities
		Are without any nature
		Of their own is what
		
		Masters refer to
		As emptiness.

		We assert that
		The fact that
		They are empty

		Is in turn also empty
		Of some essential nature
		Of emptiness itself.		


[VI.186]
		We say that
		The emptiness of
		The thing which
		We refer to itself
		As emptiness is
		“Emptiness emptiness.”

		These statements
		Were made in order
		To block the tendency

		Of those whose minds
		Were grasping,
		Holding that emptiness
		Was a real thing.


[VI.187]
		Because the vessel of 
The world, or the
Living beings contained,

Extends in expanse
Over no less than
The entirety,

Our example of
The infinity has
No final edge;

And thus is massive
In the extent
Of the directions.


[VI.188]
	The fact that
	All ten directions
	Are empty is
	“Great emptiness.”

	It was taught
	In order to stop
	The holding that
	They are vast.


[VI.189]
	This is of ultimate significance,
Here, nirvana; because
This is the highest purpose.

The fact that this
Is empty of its own—

This is ultimate emptiness.
	

[VI.190]
	The goal here
	Is to help put a stop
	To the tendency

		That people have
		In their mind
		To hold this nirvana
		As actual.

		This is why
		The one who knows
		The ultimate

		Undertook to teach
		This ultimate emptiness.


[VI.191]
	The three realms
	Are referred to
	As produced things,

	Since they come
	From conditions.

	That these are
	Completely empty
	Of any was taught

	As the emptiness
	Of produced things.


[VI.192]
		Any entity
		Which is devoid
		Of any arising
		Or changing—

		And also devoid
		Of staying—

		Is what we refer to
		As “an existing entity
		Which has not
		Been produced.”

		The fact that
		This type is empty
		Of its own is

		“The emptiness of
		Things that exist
		But were not produced.”


[VI.193]
	A situation where
	There is no case of
	An extreme

	Was described as
	“Going beyond
All extremes.”

What is the
Emptiness of this,
Simply that,

Is where we use
The expression
“Emptiness beyond
All extremes.”


[VI.194]
	The cycle of suffering
	Was described as having
	
	No first beginning
	And no final end.

	This is because it has
	No beginning limit,
	Nor an ending limit.

	Coming and going
	Are devoid;
	As such, our existence
	Is similar to a dream [f. 214a].


[VI.195]
	The fact that
	This is devoid
	
	Was referred to in
	The classical commentaries

	With the description,
	“Emptiness where there
	Is no beginning,
	And no end.”


[VI.196]
		The expression “given up”
		Can be used both
		In the sense of
		“Throwing off”
		And “abandoning.”

		“Never given up”
		Means “cannot
		Be sent off”:

A reference to
No kind of thing		
		That could ever 
		Be relinquished.


[VI.197]
		It is an essential
		Never being given up;

		The fact of the emptiness
		Of this particular object
		Was then referred to
		As emptiness:

		This is because of
		Its being something
		That we should
		Never relinquish.		


[VI.198]
	The essential nature
	Of produced things
	And the like has been
	Named their “very nature.”

	And why is it so?
	The essential nature
	Of produced things
	And such is not something
	That was ever created

	By the students,
	Or self-made Buddhas,
	Or children of the Victors,
	Or Those Who Have Gone
	That Way.  The essential nature


[VI.199]
		Of produced things
		And the like
Has been named 
Their “very nature.”

This very thing
Is empty of itself;
		
		And this fact then
		Is the emptiness
		Of any nature.


[VI.200]
	There are the eighteen
	Categories of existence;
	The six forms of contact;
	And the six forms of feeling
	That arise from these.

	There is everything
	That possesses form,
	And everything
	Which does not
	Possess such form.

	In the same way,
	We have those entities
	Which are produced things,

	And those which exist
	But which are not produced.


[VI.201a]
		All of these
		Various existing entities
		Possess an emptiness

		Where they are devoid
		Of their own.


[VI.201b]
		Those things
		That can be pointed to
		As being form,

		And all the rest
		Which lack being
Things, is the emptiness
Of a thing’s own quality.


[VI.202]
		What we accept
		Is that the “own quality”
		That form possesses
	
	Is that it can be pointed to
	As being form.

	Feelings consist of
That entity which
Possesses a self-nature
Of experience.

Discrimination
Holds to features;

And other factors
Act to bring together.


[VI.203]
	The own quality
	For consciousness
	Consists of being

	A state of mind
	Which perceives
	Individual objects.

	The own quality of
	The parts to the person
	Is suffering; and

	The self-nature
Or own quality
Of the categories
Of existence is that
They are poisonous snakes.


[VI.204]
		The doors of sense
		Were described
		By the Buddhas as
		
		The very doors
		For growing.

		Its own quality for
That thing we refer to as
		A “dependent relationship”

		Is the coming together
		And contact.


[VI.205]
		The perfection of giving
		Is giving away.

		The own quality
		For the ethical life
		Is turning away
		From the torment.

		The own quality
		Of patience is
		An absence of anger;

		And for joyful effort
		It is that free
		Of disreputable actions.


[VI.206]
		Meditation possesses
		Its own quality
		Of gathering together;

		The own quality of wisdom
Is a freedom from craving.

Thus the own qualities
Of the six different perfections
Have been described as
Being these ways.


[VI.207]
		Then there are the
		Concentration levels
		And the immeasurables;

		And just so, other items:
		Those for the formless realm [f. 214b].

		These are what that
		Being of Perfect Knowledge
		Described as states

		Whose own quality was
		Beyond being disturbed.


[VI.208]
		The own quality
		Of the 37 elements
		Of enlightenment

		Is those points
		Which produce 
		Our release.

		Its own quality
		For emptiness
		Is that very quality
		
Of being devoid,
		No longer focusing.


[VI.209]
		That beyond all signs
		Has its own quality
		Of peace;

		Its own quality
		For the third
		Is a freedom from
		Suffering and
		Dark ignorance.

		The own quality
		For the freedoms
		Is that they act
		To liberate us.


[VI.210]
		The forces were said
To have a quality of
		Establishing one deeply.

		The forms of
		Fearlessness of
		The Protector

		Have an essential
Nature of being
Extremely steadfast.


[VI.211]
		The perfect understandings
		Of details—confidence
		And so on—have an
		Own nature of being
		Without any extent;

		And what we call
		“Great love” accomplishes
		Help for living beings.


[VI.212]
		Great compassion
		Acts to protect,
		Entirely, those
		Who are suffering.

		Great joy has
		An own nature
		Of high joy.

		Equanimity
		Should be understood
		As having an own nature
		Of being unadmixed.		


[VI.213]
		The Dharma of the Buddhas,
		Which we assert
		Has those 18 qualities
		Of being unmixed,

		Has an own quality
		That it cannot
		Be stolen off.

		Why this is true
		Is for that reason
		That the Teacher
		Cannot be
		Stolen off.


[VI.214]
		The wisdom of
		Omniscience itself
		Is something that

		We hold to have
		An own quality of
		The direct perception.

		Those other than this
		Are only partial;
		
		As such, we would not
		Refer to them
		As direct.


[VI.215]
		The own nature
		Of those produced,

		And the own nature
		Of those which exist
		But were not produced,

		Is then for each of them
		Their emptiness
		Of that alone:

		Their emptiness
		Of some nature.


[VI.216]
		Those of the present
		Do not remain;

		And those of the past
		And the future;
		None of these exist.

		These things cannot
		Be observed, in any.

		As such,
		We refer to them
		As “unseen.”	


[VI.217]
		This state of being
		Unseen is entirely
	
		Devoid of existing
		In that essential way.

		It is not something
		That can remain
		In some solid manner,

		Nor is it something
		Which stops.
		
		As such, it is
		The emptiness,
		We say, of
		“Not seeing anything.”		


[VI.218]
		The functional
		Are “brought together,”
		Because they occur
		Through conditions,

		And an essential nature
		Of it has no existence.

		The fact that these
		Same things
		Of that convening
		Are empty

		Is what we refer to
		As “the emptiness
		Beyond all things.”


[VI.219]
		The term “things” refers,
		In a summary way,
To the five parts
To the person.

		That fact that these
		Are empty is what
		We refer to as
		“The emptiness of things.”		


[VI.220]
		This lack of things,
		In summary,
		Refers to entities

		That are things
		Which exist but
		Were not produced [f. 215a].

		The fact that these
		Same absences of things
		Are empty is

		The emptiness of
		The lack of things.


[VI.221]
		What we give
		The name of
		“The emptiness
		Of any nature”

		Is an absence
		Of any real quality
		To the nature.

		This particular nature
		Is not something produced;

		As such we give it the
		Name of “the nature.”


[VI.222]
		Whether the Buddhas
		Ever occur
		Or do not appear,
		It’s all the same.

		All entities will possess
		An emptiness, really;

		This is what we declare
		Is the emptiness
		Of being other things.


[VI.223]
		The ultimate end
		And, just so,
The true nature,

Are the emptiness
Of things.

This is how
They were declared
In those words

Presented in
The way of the
Perfection of wisdom.


[VI.224]
		The wisdom
		From this represents
		Rays of light
		That illuminate;

		We could compare it
		To an olive
		Sitting in the palm
		Of they themselves.

		Suppose we are able
		To realize that
		There is nothing about

		The entirety
		Of these three realms
		Of existence which

		Has ever started,
		Since time with
		No beginning.

		Through the power
		Of nominal reality,
		We come to the point
		Where things are stopped.


[VI.225]
		It is admittedly
		The case that
		They always have
		
		A state of mental focus
		Which is taken in
		By a cessation;

		And yet
		At the same time
		They give rise to
		
		Thoughts of compassion
		Towards living beings,

		Who have no one
		To protect them.

		Beyond that,
		They defeat,
		In their mind,

		All of those
		Individuals who are

		Born of the word
		Of Those Gone to Bliss,
		And medium buddhas.


[VI.226]
They are able
To stretch forth

Their broad, white,
Wide-spreading wings,

Of the deceptive
Side of things,
And suchness.

They are kings
Among the birds,

Soaring at the head
Of the geese
Of living beings.

By the strength
And power
Of good deeds,

They fly
To the highest:

To the far shores
Of the ocean of
The high qualities
Of the Victors.


[chapter number]
This concludes the sixth wish for enlightenment, or chapter,
 	of Entering the Middle Way.



Chapter 7
The Final Four Levels


[VII.1]
		Here at “Gone Far,”
		This one is in meditation,
		From moment to moment,
		On cessation.

		Further, they also attain
A perfection of skillful means
		Which is blazing strongly.	


[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA BDUN PA’O,,

This concludes the seventh wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.

	[VIII.1]
		They seek,
		Again and again,

		To achieve an even
		Higher degree
		Of virtue.

		These great beings
Enter “Unmoving”;

This is where
They can absolutely
Never turn back,

And special prayers
Made by them
Reach an extraordinary
Level of purity,

		While the Victors
		Undertake to
		Rouse them from
		The cessation.


[VIII.2]
		The state of mind
		Free of attachment

		No longer remains
		Combined with
		The various faults.

		As such, here at
		The eighth level

		All these impurities,
		With their roots,
		
		Are put to their
		Final rest.

		So too, we put
		A finish to the
		Negative emotions;

		And we have become
		A spiritual teacher
		For all three grounds.

		They are though
		Still unable
		To achieve

		All the riches
		Of the Buddhas,

		Which like the sky
		Are without any limits [f. 215b].


[VIII.3]
		They have put a
Stop to the cycle;

Despite that,
We attain
The ten powers.

These allow them to
Display their person

As an entire variety,
To beings of
The suffering world.
		

[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA BRGYAD PA’O,,

		This concludes the eighth wish for enlightenment,
			or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.

[IX.1]
		At the ninth,
		The forces are
		Beyond description;

		All of them
		Become pure
		In a way which is
		Totally complete.

		In like manner
		They also achieve

		The different
		Total purities of
		Their fine qualities—

		The qualities of
		Pure understanding.		


[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA DGU PA’O,,

This concludes the ninth wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


[X.1]
		At the tenth level,
		This one receives

		The highest investment
		Into power,

		From all the Buddhas
		Of every corner.

		High knowledge
		Also reaches
		Its highest expression.

		The rains
		Are sent down
		From the rainclouds;

		Just so, the
		Children of the Victors
		Also let the rain
		Fall, spontaneously,

		For the crops
		Of virtue among
		Living beings.		


	[chapter number]
,DBU MA LA ‘JUG PA LAS, ,SEMS BSKYED PA BCU PA’O,,

This concludes the tenth wish for enlightenment,
	or chapter, from Entering the Middle Way.


The afterword

[afterword.1]
		At that point,
		This one sees
		A million Buddhas,

		And these grant
		Their blessing, and
		They perceive it.

		In this very moment
		They stay there
		For a million eons;

		And they engage
		Perfectly in this
		In both the
		
		Beginning end
		And the final end.


[afterword.2]
		This intelligent one
		Engages in,
		And then releases,
		
		A million
		Different states of
		Meditative concentration.

		They also cause a
		Million different
		Planets to tremble,

		And further have
		The capacity
		To spread light
		Over them.

		Just so, this one—
		Using their power
		Of performing miracles—

		Is able to bring
		To ripening
		A million
		Living beings.

		And they are
		Also able to
		Travel to those

		Connected in number
		To that million.


[afterword.3]
		This one acts,
		Further, to open—
		Perfectly—

		Different doorways
		Of the Dharma.

		This child
		Of the Lords
		Of the Able Ones

		Is also able
		To show their body
		Widely, in
		Different forms.

		Each of these forms
		Is, further, accompanied

		By a group
		Of a million
		Children of the Victors,
		Which they display:

		They are rich
		In a lovely circle
		Of followers.


[afterword.4]
When this intelligent one
Residing at the level
Of Perfect Happiness

Has attained those
High qualities,

Then they reside,
Just so,
At this level
Known as “Immaculate.”

And they attain,
Perfectly,

This same number,
But composed
Of a thousand members.


[afterword.5]
At five different
Levels, these come
To be completed

In groups attained of
A hundred thousand;
A billion; ten billion;
A trillion; and a
Hundred quintillion.

And then once more
Everything is multiplied,
By another thousand,
For a grand total [f. 216a].


[afterword.6]
		One staying at
		Unmoving has no
		Mistaken thoughts;

		They incorporate
		A thousand galaxies

		Of a hundred billion
		Planets each.

		Take all the atoms
		That exist
		In the worlds;

		The number
		Of fine qualities
		That they attain

		Is equal to
		That total.


[afterword.7]
		The bodhisattva
Residing at the level
Of Fine Wisdom

Possesses ten groups
Of fine qualities
Equal to the
Previously mentioned,

Multiplied by
A thousand groups
Of a hundred,

Each consisting
Of a countless number—

These attain
A number equal.


[afterword.8]
		Provisionally,
		The number of
		Fine qualities
		Here at the tenth

		Is far beyond
		Ever being expressed;
		It is nothing that
		Could ever be
		Expressed in speech.

		In sum,
		They are equal
		In count to the atoms.


[afterword.9]
		They are able
		To display,

		From the pores
		Of their body,

		The holy bodies
		Of bodhisattvas

		And totally
		Enlightened beings
		Beyond number.

		Just so, as well,
		They display—
		Moment by moment—
		
		Worldly gods,
		Demigods,
		And humans.


[afterword.10]
		It’s all because
The moon is shining
		In a perfectly clear sky—

		They make
		Great efforts further,
		At the level where,

		Earlier,
		They created
		The ten forces.

		This is found
		By them
		In “Below None”;

		Peace, the highest
		State of being:

		The ultimate among
		All high qualities,
And beyond all equal—

		This is found by them.


[afterword.11]
		Now there are
		Types of vessels,
		
		But no distinctions
		In these spaces.

		The case is the same;
		There are no distinctions

		At all engendered
		By functional entitites.

		And thus it is
		With suchness,
		Being a single song.

		This is something
		That you can
		Discern perfectly;

		As such,
		Those of you with
		Excellent understanding

		Can, in even
		Just a moment,
		Grasp all

		The knowable things
		In the universe.


[afterword.12]
		The point where
		Putting it to rest
		Is the true nature
		Of things

		Is something
		In which
		Intelligence
		Could never engage.

The idea that
A subject state of mind
		Could never engage

		Is not something
		That could ever
		Make sense

		With engagement
		In knowable objects.

		It would be a
Complete contradiction
To posit some state

Of knowing where you
Had no comprehension.

You have yet
To give rise to
A state of mind,

But you say
You will go
And teach it
Like this
To anyone else.


[afterword.13]
		Let’s consider that point
		When this is being
		Its suchness

		And, just so,
		The mind is devoid
		Of any starting.

		At this point,
		Their resting upon
		Is as though
The realization
		Of suchness.

		Let’s say
		That a particular
		State of mind
		
		Has taken on
		The aspect.

		This is it
		Having a
		Comprehension
		Of the object [f. 216b].

		Just so
		We refer to
		A knowledge
		
		In reliance upon
		The nominal.


[afterword.14]
	The holy body
	Of this one
	
	Complete in
	Its enjoyments

	Is embraced
	By merit.

	And from
Emanated bodies

	From the sky
	And other things,

	Due to the mystic
	Power of these,
	
	The sound that
	Comes forth

	Teaches the
	Suchness of things.

	From this then
	The world

	Comes as well
	To know suchness.


[afterword.15]
		It’s like how
		Here, a potter
		
		Possessed of great
		Strength puts forth
		Great effort.

		Even though for
		Quite some time

		They have made
		No current efforts,

		We can see it
		Still spinning,

		Acting as a cause
		For a pot or the like.


[afterword.16]
		In the same way,
		There is no longer
		Conscious effort

		Which has arisen in
		The present moment;

		At the same time though
		Their engagement continues,

		Residing as they are
		In an identity

		Consisting of
		The holy body
		Of all things.

		The good deeds
		Of beings,

		And their
		Extraordinary prayers,

		Project—and
		From that, it is
		Far beyond
		Any imagining.
		 

[afterword.17]
		The dry firewood of
		Each and every one of
		The knowable objects
		Is burned;

		And the peace
From that is
		The holy body
		Of all things.

		At this point, it is
Without any starting,
And without any stopping.

They have put a stop
To the mind; as such,

		This is manifested directly
		By the holy body.


[afterword.18a]
	We have peace
	And the holy body:

	We are crystal-clear,
Similar to the tree
That fulfils all wishes;

		And like the
		Wish-giving jewel,
		We have no
		Conceptual thought.


[afterword.18b]
		This is free of
		All elaboration,

		And makes its
		Appearance always

		In order to serve
		The world,
		
		Until living beings
		Are liberated.
		

[afterword.19]
		The Lord of the Able
		Has a certain
		Physical embodiment,
		Through its
		Concordant cause—

		The occasions of
		Ones past rebirths
		Come to their end.

		They are displayed
		With great clarity,
		And without
		Any jumbling,

		In every one
		Of the ways
		They occurred
		In the past;

		And so all
		Are resplendent.

		They are moreover
		Displayed all
		At the same time.


[afterword.20]
		The Buddha paradise
		Of the Lords of the Able
		Is just right;

		And the mystic
		Power and force
		Of the activities
		
		And the holy bodies
		Of these comes
		In just the right way;

		And the community
		Of the listeners
		Is in just
		The right number,

		And devote themselves
		Just right.

		And the bodhisattvas
		Possess physical forms
		In just the right manner.


[afterword.21]
	And they teach
	Just the right Dharma;

	And there are
	Just the right number
	Of eminent beings;

	And there are those
	That listen to
	The Dharma,

	And engage in the
	Various activities.

	In a single
	Holy body,
	They display

	Acts of giving
	Presenting all this
	Just right.


[afterword.22]
		In the very same way,
		They undertake

		An ethical lifestyle;
		Patience; joyful effort;
		Single-pointed focus;
		And wisdom—

		Just as they did
		Before, with no
		Single detail left
		
		Incomplete
		In their practice,
		From the beginning.

		They display—
		With utmost clarity—

		All this very same
		Activity, from every
		Single pore of
		Their holy body.				


[afterword.23]
		All of those
		Enlightened Beings
		Who are past,

		And who are
		Yet to come,
		And here in
		The present

		Teach the Dharma
		In a high song
		Which reaches to
The very ends of
Space itself [f. 217a].

They seek to bring
Comfort and relief
To beings in the
Grasp of suffering.


[afterword.24]
		From the very
		First day of
		The holy Wish,

		And up until
		They reside in the very
		Heart of Buddhahood,

		They undertake then
		All of their various
		Activities of service.

		And each one
		Of their activities
		Is repeated,

		Displayed altogether
		In every point in time,
		
		Within each & every
		Pore of their body.

		And they know
		That entities possess
		A quality of being
		Similar to an illusion.


[afterword.25]
		The same is the case
		With the activities

		Of each & every one
		Of the bodhisattvas
		Of the past, present,
		And future;

		And with all the
		Realized beings who
		Are self-made buddhas,
		And listeners too.

		And there are
		All the rest;
		All they undertook
		During that period
		When they were
		Common beings—

		All this they display
		In a single one,
		Within a pore
		Of their body.


[afterword.26]
		This thing
		Is cleaned;

		Engaging in the
		Wish to do so,

		Worlds extending
		To space are in
		A single atom.

		Admitted they can
		Display an atom
		Spreading to
		Infinite planets;

		But that atom
		Does not become
		More gross;

		Nor does that planet
		Become more fine.


[afterword.27]
You are a being
Who possesses
No conceptual
Thought at all;

And yet
You undertake
A whole variety
Of activities,

In every single
Instant of time,

Even up until
The final moment
Of existence.

Just as you make
This one display,

You make the same
Upon all the planets,
Infinite in number,

Equal in count to
		That of all the atoms.


[afterword.28]
		There is the force
		Of knowing
		What is actual,
		And what is not;

		And, just so,
		The force of mind
		Of how different
		Karmas will open.

		Then there is
		Comprehending
		The variety of wishes;

		And the force
		Of knowing
		Different propensities.


[afterword.29]
		In like manner
		We have the force
		Of understanding
		Higher or lesser
		Capacities; as well as

		The paths that lead
		To different goals;

		And understanding
		Concentration,
		Freedom,
		Single-pointed focus,
		
		Staying in deep
		Meditation, and others
		Of the like.


[afterword.30]
		So too there is
		The force of 
		Understanding
		Days gone by;

		And just so
		The state of mind
		Of the deaths of beings,

		And how they move on
		Or find their rebirth.

		And then finally
		There is the force
		Of understanding
		
		When the last
		Of the impurities
		Are finished off.

		These then
		Are the ten
		Different forces.


[afterword.31]
		Something has,
		Quite certainly,
		Arisen from
		A particular cause.

		Those who have
		A high grasp
		Of such things

		Have stated that
		This is the actuality.

		Anything happening
		In the opposite way
		Is not actual.

		Eliminating all stopping
		Towards knowing
		Infinite objects
		Of perception

		Is what we refer to
		As the force.


[afterword.32]
		There is what
		Is desirable
		And what is
		Not desirable;

		And then the
		Opposite of these.

		There are karmas
		Which are entities
		Which finish off;

		And the great variety
Of ripenings.

What we accept then
As the force is

The power of knowledge
Engaging in objects
In a way which is
Unstoppable;

Taken in by the
Past, present,
And future,

Extending to all
Knowable things [f. 217b].


[afterword.33]
		There are
Wishes which occur
		By force of desire
		And so on—

		An extremely
		Great number
		Of different wishes;

		Those lesser,
		The inbetween,
		And those which are
		Extremely elevated.

		And there are hopes
		By those different
		From these—

		Hopes which
		Are obscured.

		Here we have
		A knowledge
		Which travels

		To the three of
		The past, present,
		And future—
		Which covers all.

		This we refer to
		As the force.
		
		
[afterword.34]
		Those who are masters
		In the different categories
		Of an Enlightened Being

		Have described
Those things that are
The nature of the eye
		And so on as
		The propensities.

		The infinite variations
		Of the knowledge of
		Totally enlightened beings

		Engage in the details
		Of all the different
		Categories; this is

		What we assert
		Constitutes the force.


[afterword.35]
		There is that
State of imagination
Which is not correct,

And so on—
What we assert
To be supreme,

In a particularly
Sharp form.
	
		And then there are
		What we refer to
		As “not supreme”:

		Only middling,
		Or quite dull.

		There are the
		Eye and the rest,
		And the way these
		Inform, or have

		The power to
		Complete, each other.

		Omniscience has
		No density
		Towards them;

		This was spoken
		To be the force.		


[afterword.36]
		Some paths lead
		To the state of a
		Victor themselves;

		Some to the
		Enlightenment of
		A self-made Buddha.

		Others lead to
		The enlightenment
		Of the listener;

		Or to a life as
		A craving spirit,
		Or an animal,

		A worldly god,
		A human,
		Or a hellbeing,

		And so on.
		What we say
		Is the force

		Is a knowledge
		Of all these
		
Which is
Without density, 
		As well as infinite.


[afterword.37]
Then there are
The details among
The activities of

Deep practitioners
On infinite
Numbers of worlds:

Concentration;
The eight total freedoms;
Those states of quietude
Which are truly pure;

And deep meditation,
Whether single or eight.

What we describe
As the force is that
Unstoppable form
Of knowing all these.


[afterword.38]
		We have lived then
		In a cycle for the
		Total amount of time
		That we have possessed
		Dark ignorance.

		There are all the
		Beings that we and
		Other living creatures
		Have each lived though,

		In the past: this total
		Amount—infinite;
		And the foundation
		For them.  And so

		Here is a state
		Of mind which
		Unstoppable
		
		Towards all these,
		As well as the
		Specific place
		Where they took place.

		A type of perception
		Like this is what
		We refer to
		As the force.


[afterword.39]
		And then there is
		The death, and
		Moving on, that
		
		All beings
		Have experienced

		In the form of each
		Separate living thing;
		As well as the rebirth.

		Many are brought
		To light, located
		In worlds laid
		Across infinite
		Space itself.

		When we know
		Them in that time,
		We have no attachment,

		For they are all
		Entirely pure—
		An infinity.

		This is what
		We refer to
		As the force.


[afterword.40]
		The Victors,
		Who know all
		Things there are,

		Use these forces—
		With speed—
		To destroy the
		Negative emotions,

		Along with the
		Deep seeds.

		Those who are students,
		And the rest, put a stop
		To the negative emotions
		Using their intelligence [f. 218a];

		This then constitutes
		A state of knowledge
		Which is free of density,

		And this is what
		We refer to as the
		Force of the infinite.


[afterword.41]
		It is not as though
		The winged ones
		Must eventually

Come to a stop
Because there is
No more sky;

Rather, this one flies
Until their strength
Is exhausted—

And then they
Must turn back.

The students
And those in
Their company,

And the buddhas
And the children
Are similar:

They can describe
The high qualities
Of the Enlightened Ones,

Similar to the sky
In being infinite,

But they will
Have to stop,

Without having
Listed them all.


[afterword.42]
		Thus how could
		Someone like me
		Ever be able

		To understand,
		And then to express,

		These high qualities
		That you possess?

		Nonetheless,
		I have thrown aside
		Any doubts,

		And boldly offered
		Just the barest list,

		Because those
		Have been described
		By The Arya,
		Nagarjuna.


[afterword.43]
		The profound here
		Is emptiness;

		The other
		Fine features
		Are the widespread.

		When we come
		To an understanding
		Of both the profound
		And the widespread,

		We will be able
		To attain these
		Fine features.


[afterword.44]
		You continue on
		To all three worlds,
		Because you possess
		
		A holy form which
		Never shifts out;

		You use your
		Emanations to travel.

		And then you
		Make a display
		Of taking
		Your holy birth,

		And undertake
		To teach the Wheel
		For enlightenment
		And peace.

		Thus do you act
		Towards the world,

		Bound tightly
		In the shackles

		Of their manifold
		Hopes, sporting in
		All kinds of roles.

		Out of your compassion,
You act to lead
		Each & every one
		On to their nirvana.	


[afterword.45]
Why have we taken
Our approach?

Even though there is
Nothing there
Which is our focus,

We have been presenting
Clearing away
Each & every impurity,

A topic different
From discussing suchness.

It is not the case
That we are suggesting
Further that one

Rely upon differing
Versions of the
Suchness of things—
Upon divisions.

Nor is it the case
That the insight
Which takes suchness
As its object
Possesses separate ones.

Thus it is that you
Have taught to beings
One which is indivisible,
With no equal
Among ways.


[afterword.46]
		Now there is
		A certain reason:

		Something which
Functions to trigger
Problems within
Living beings.

And that is
The presence of
Those degenerations.

As such, the realms
In which Buddhas act
Are too deep
For the world;

They cannot engage
In something
With such depths.

Because the fact is
That you, Those Who
Have Gone to Bliss,

Possess in conjunction
Knowledge and
A method consisting
Of compassion.

And further you
Made a certain
Commitment:

“I will liberate
Living beings.”


[afterword.47]
		Thus it is
		That a master

		Who is trying to
		Dispel the fatigue

		That a group of
People might display

In a voyage to
The Isle of Jewels

Sets forth visions of
A lovely magical city,
Long before.

Just so do you
Undertake a
Certain way;

All this is meant
To attract their minds

To the way
Of total peace.

		And then separately,
		After they had 
		Trained themselves

		In thoughts of
		Total isolation [f. 218b],
		You taught them.
		

[afterword.48]
		There are all the lands
		Of Enlightened Beings,
		
		Paradises in every
		Corner of the universe.

		There exist,
		In these worlds,
		
		A certain number
		Of atoms of dust.

		And the eons
That it has taken
Those Gone to Bliss

To reach that most
High, and holy, and
Supreme enlightenment

Are equal to
That very number.

Even so,
This particular
Secret of yours

Is not something
We would normally
Describe openly.


[afterword.49]
		A Victor remains
		Until all the world

		Reaches to that
		Highest state
		Of absolute peace,

		And also
		Until that day
		When space itself
		Comes to its
		Complete dissolution.

		They have been
		Given birth by
		The Mother,
		Wisdom, and then

		Compassion,
		Acting in the manner
		Of a wet nurse.
		
		How then could
		We ever say
		That you possessed
		Some total peace?


[afterword.50]
		Due to the problem
		Of dark ignorance,

		Those of the world
		Eat a meal containing
		A certain poison.

		Love comes
		Into you for them,
		The members of
		Your own family.

		This is not
		The suffering
		That a mother feels
		For a beloved child

		Who has,
		In a similar way,
		Mistakenly eaten
		Some poison;

		Which means
		That it is not
		The case that

		The Protectors
		Have travelled
		Only to some

		Supreme and
		Final peace.


[afterword.51]
		What is the
		Reason for this?

		It is all because
		Those who are
		Not well versed

		Still possess
		A state of mind
		Where they have
		Strong craving.

		And because of this,
		They undergo
		Periods when they
		Are born & destroyed.

		They are torn
		From what feels
		Attractive, and
		Meet with
		The undesirable;

		They achieve
		The future fate of
		Those who still have
		Terrible deeds.

		The world
		Has crowded to
		Worthy objects
		Of compassion.

		As such, you—
		The Conqueror—
		Have, out of
		This compassion,

		Turned your heart
		Away from peace,

		Without allowing
		Yourself to go
		Into nirvana.	



The colophon

[colophon.1]
		This presentation
		Has been related
		By the Buddhist monk
		Known as Chandrakirti.

		It has proceeded
		From that classical
		Commentary of
		The middle way,

		And is in accord with
		The traditional sources,
		And the personal advices.


[colopon.2]
		There is no presentation
		Of this teaching
		To be found in any
		Other than those.

		Just so, real masters
Should be sure
Of one thing:

The system
		That appears here

		Is one that
		You cannot find
		In any of the other.	


[colophon.3]
		They were frightened
		By the shade
		
		Of the expanse
		Of the ocean

		Of the mind
		Of Nagarjuna.

		And so individuals
		Took the beautiful system
		And discarded it off
		To a distance.

		But the flow
Of pure water
From that one
		Set in verse

		Opened the blooms
		Of a pure white
		Water lily,

		Whose buds had
		Been awaiting it.

		And with this
		Chandrakirti has now
		Fulfilled, perfectly,
		All the hopes.
		

[colophon.4]
		The profound idea
		Of suchness

		Which we have
		Finished explaining
		Can be frightening [f. 219a].

		There are individuals
		Who have, previous,
		Become highly accustomed,
		And did have
		Such realizations.

		Others may possess
		Vast learning,
		
		And yet still
		They would not
		Be able to grasp this.

		And thus it is that
		Any system where
		We see these ideas

		That people have
		Made up in
		Their own mind

		We note that they
		Are just the same
		As if they were following

		The scriptural traditions
		Of those who describe
		Some self-nature.

		As such,
		I would encourage you
		To discard that
		State of mind where

		You take some kind
		Of pleasure in
		The texts of those

		Who adhere
		To some other
		School of thought.


[colophon.5]
		Thus have I
		Enunciated that
		Beautiful system
		Of the Master,
		Nagarjuna.

		And by doing so,
		I have merit enough
		To stretch to the
		Very edges of
		Space itself.

		The sky of my mind
		Had been sent into
		The gloom of the
		Negative emotions.

		But now,
		In the midst,
		Has come a bright
		White light like
		
		A major star in
		The autumn heavens.

		Or else you could say
		That here is a mind
		Which resembles
		That fabulous jewel

		Which a cobra holds
		Embedded in their hood;

		And the acquisition of such
		Will allow the entire world
		To perceive suchness;

		And then may it happen
		That—with great speed—
		Every being completes
		Their journey to the level
		Of One Gone to Bliss.


[colophon.6]
This then completes Entering the Middle Way, an illumination of the ways of both the profound and the widespread.  It was composed by Master Chandrakirti, whose holy heart had long since been lost to that highest way.


[colophon.7]
He held a high level of knowledge that was never stolen away; and he possessed compassion as well.  He was known for sketching a cow that was about to give birth, and then milking real milk from it.  With this, he was able to stop others from believing that things are real.  This then is the one who completed this composition.



The original translators

[translators.1]
This was translated in the middle of the Kashmiri town known as Anupama, or “Beyond All Compare,” within the temple whose name is “Hidden Jewels.”  This was during the time of the Kashmiri king whose name was Aryadeva.


[translators.2]
The translation of the text was done according to the Sanskrit edition of the work circulating at that time in Kashmir.  The team that completed the translation consisted of the senior Indian cleric Tilaka, together with the master Tibetan translator, the Buddhist monk Patsab Nyima Drak.


[translators.3]
Later on, at the Ramoche Temple in the city of Lhasa, the senior Indian cleric by the name of Kanaka Varma and the same master Tibetan translator were able to review a copy of the Sanskrit text that had been circulating in the eastern part of Bactria.  This allowed them to complete an accurate revision of the Tibetan translation, and then finalize it through their efforts to teach it to their students.


[translators.4]
Why then do we see one colophon for the composition of the commentary itself, and then a shared colophon for the translation?  This is because the root text was translated once on its own, and then edited as part of a combined version of the commentary and the root text presented within it.











Je Tsongkapa’s
Outline of the Text



Je Tsongkapa’s Outline of the Text


I. MTSAN GYI DON,
The meaning of the title [folio 2b] [title]

II. ‘GYUR GYI PHYAG
The translator’s obeisance [f. 4a]
	
III. GZHUNG GI DON,
The meaning of the body of the text [f. 4a]

	A. BSTAN BCOS RTZOM PA LA ‘JUG PA’I THABS MCHOD PAR BRJOD PA,
The offering of praise, which functions as a means of initiating the composition of this classical commentary [f. 4a]

1. SNYING RJE CHEN PO LA SO SOR MA PHYE BAR BSTOD PA,
Singing the praises of great compassion without dividing out the components [f. 4a]

a. SNYING RJE BYANG SEMS KYI GTZO BO’I RGYUR BSTAN PA,
Describing how it is that compassion is the principal cause of a bodhisattva [f. 4b]

i. NYAN RANG GNYIS THUB DBANG LAS SKYES TSUL,
How it is that listeners & self-made buddhas are born from the Lords of the Able [f. 4b] [v. I.1a]

ii. SANGS RGYAS RNAMS BYANG SEMS LAS ‘KHRUNGS TSUL, [f. 7b]
How it is that Buddhas take their holy birth from bodhisattvas

iii. BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA’I RGYU’I GTZO BO GSUM BSTAN PA, [f. 9b] [v. I.1b]
A description of the three principal causes of a bodhisattva

b. BYANG SEMS KYI RGYU GZHAN GNYIS KYI YANG RTZA BAR BSTAN PA, [f. 11b] [v. I.2]
Describing how it is that compassion is the very root of the other two causes of a bodhisattva as well

2. SNYING RJE CHEN PO LA SO SOR PHYE STE PHYAG ‘TSAL BA,
	[f. 13a]
Bowing down to great compassion while dividing out the components

a. SEMS CAN LA DMIGS PA’I SNYING RJE LA PHYAG ‘TSAL BA, [f. 13a] [v. I.3]
Bowing down to the form of compassion which focuses upon living beings

b. CHOS DANG DMIGS PA MED PA LA DMIGS PA’I SNYING RJE LA PHYAG ‘TSAL BA, [f. 15a] [vv. I-4-5a]
Bowing down to that form of compassion which focuses upon things, and upon the way in which beings are not even there


B. BRTZAMS PA’I BSTAN BCOS KYI LUS DNGOS, [f. 18b]
The actual body of the commentary which is then composed

1. RGYU’I SA, [f. 18b]
A presentation of the levels which act as a cause

a. LUGS ‘DI’I LAM NYAMS SU LEN TSUL SPYIR BSTAN PA,
	[f. 18b]
A general discussion of how it is that we put the path of this system into practice

b. BYE BRAG TU SO SKYE’I SAR NYAMS SU LEN TSUL BSHAD PA, [f. 20a]
A more specific explanation of how we practice upon the levels of common beings

c. BYANG SEMS ‘PHAGS PA’I SA’I RNAM GZHAG BSTAN PA,
A presentation on the structure of the levels for realized beings who are bodhisattvas [f. 21a]

	i. SA BCU’I THUN MONG GI RNAM GZHAG, [f. 21a]
	A combined presentation of the ten levels

ii. SA SO SO’I RNAM GZHAG [f. 23b]
A separate presentation for each one of the ten levels

	a) RAB DGA’ SOGS SA LNGA BSHAD PA, [f. 23b]
An explanation of the five levels beginning with Perfect Happiness

i) SA DANG PO RAB TU DGA’ BA BSHAD PA,
An explanation of the first bodhisattva level, Perfect Happiness [f. 23b]


*  *  *


a1) KHYAD GZHI SA’I NGO BO MDOR BSTAN, [f. 23b]
A brief presentation of what it is which possesses a certain feature—that is, the level itself

b1) KHYAD CHOS SA’I YON TAN RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA, [f. 24b]
An expanded explanation of the feature which the level possesses—that is, specific high personal qualities

	a2) RANG GI RGYUD MDZES PAR BYED PA’I YON TAN BSTAN PA, [f. 24b]
A description of the high qualities where our being is made beautiful

	a3) YON TAN SO SOR PHYE STE BSHAD PA, [f. 24b]
	An explanation of these high qualities, made by
separating them out individually

a4) DON LDAN GYI MTSAN ‘THOB PA’I
YON TAN, [f. 24b] [v. I.5b]
The high quality where we earn a very significant name

b4) RIGS SU SKYE BA SOGS BZHI’I YON TAN,
	[f. 25a] [vv. I.6a, I.6b]
The high quality with the four characteristics
	that begin with taking birth into a royal family

c4) SA GONG MA GNON PA SOGS
GSUM GYI YON TAN [f. 26b] [v. I.7]
			The high quality with three characteristics,
				beginning with surpassing the levels before

Appendices





About the translator,
and the translation

Geshe Michael Roach was born in Los Angeles and grew up in Phoenix, Arizona.  He graduated with honors from Princeton University, and is a recipient of the Presidential Scholar medallion from the President of the United States at the White House.  He has also received the McConnell Scholarship Prize from the Princeton School of Public & International Affairs, as well as an honorary doctorate in the Congress of Mexico from the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM).

Michael is the first foreigner in the 600-year history of Tibet’s Sera Mey Monastery to receive the title of Geshe (Master of Buddhism), after 25 years of study.  After graduation, he founded the Asian Classics Institute (ACI), translating over 20,000 pages of the geshe program and designing 36 courses of studies in English, for modern people of all walks of life.

At his teacher’s directive, Michael—in order to confirm that the principles of the ancient texts could be used in modern life—helped in 1981 to found the Andin International Corporation, which became one of the largest diamond jewelry companies in the world, and was purchased by super-investor Warren Buffett in 2009.  Michael used the majority of his income from the business to found and run the Asian Classics Input Project (now called ALL, or Asian Legacy Library), starting in 1987.  This is the largest free, online searchable database of ancient Asian literature in the world.

Michael also helped found the Three Jewels Outreach Center of New York; DCI Global; the Sedona College of International Management; the Yoga Studies Institute; Green Stretch Pen; Diamond Mountain Retreat Center; The Knowledge Base; Diamond Cutter Press; DSEU University; Classics Soft Power; Innovation Retreats; Dragonshead; and the Diamond Cutter Classics translation center.  Each of these institutions helps preserve and make available the precious wisdom of ancient Asia, in the modern world.

Michael is the author of some 100 books and major translations.  His most popular works include The Diamond Cutter: The Buddha on Managing Your Business & Your Life; and How Yoga Works.  He lives in the small town of Rimrock, Arizona, with his wife Veronica, whom he first met some 50 years ago.  Together they enjoy gardening, charitable work, and running their small Peach Tree Café, for local cowboys & cowgirls.

Just a few technical notes about the translation.  For the Sanskrit you find here, our "codex
unicus” is the manuscript from Tibet of the Madhyamakāvatāra Bhāṣya by Master Chandrakirti, which includes the verses of  the Madhyamakāvatāra as well.  This is the sole extant and only recently available Sanskrit manuscript, which had been preserved for centuries in the Potala Palace in Lhasa, but which is not yet available to the larger scholarly community. 

For the first five chapters, we have the critical and diplomatic editions published in 2022 based on the microfilm copy of this  manuscript, kept in the China Tibetology Research Centre (CTRC) in Beijing, with collaborative work performed by the Austrian Academy of Sciences (IKGA). 

For the sixth chapter we have the critical edition published by Xuezhu Li in 2014, who extracted the Madhyamakāvatāra Kārikā verses from the same manuscript.  Chapters 7 through 13 have not yet been published by the IKGA & CTRC, and were not available for our research.

As for the presentation of the Sanskrit here in situ, you will see that we normally present the entire Sanskrit verse together, and then in specific cases split its Tibetan counterpart into pieces below it.  This is necessary because of the difference in word and line order within verses between the two languages.

Scholars will note that our DCC standard is to separate out the Sanskrit words where this is practical, since our goal for adding the Sanskrit in the first place is to help students, rather than scholars, of Sanskrit—since the latter will be able to access the verses with combined words easily in the same published sources that we availed ourselves of.

As for the Tibetan edition here, the text was early on input from the only edition available at the time, published by Guru Deva Rinpoche and sponsored by the wonderful Khen Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tharchin.  This edition had many problems with it, due to the fact that it was printed off of film retouched by inexpert scribes.  We have in the meantime worked hard to correct it, but no doubt a few problems remain.

Where our corrections to the Tibetan manuscript might be questioned; are particularly difficult to detect; or may bring out interesting historical variants, we have added a note of the original and the correction in the format of {%..}.  More obvious corrections are made silently.

The original here was the Shul Parkang (Zhol par-khang) edition.  We have inserted into this edition the root text from the Derge edition of the Tengyur, which explains for the scholar the differing folio numbers in situ seen in some cases.

We may finally note that we have not included in this introduction the typical biographical information for the author, Je Tsongkapa, since we have already previously published his definitive biography under the title of King of the Dharma: the Illustrated Life of Je Tsongkapa, Teacher of the First Dalai Lama, with the Complete Paintings and the Original Text of the All-Knowing One, Jamyang Shepay Dorje (1648-1721).



Acknowledgements

Here at the Diamond Cutter Classics project, we often refer to the process of translating a new book as “snow on the mountain,” meaning that the entire process of putting out a new work closely resembles the way in which snow falls upon a high mountain peak; gradually melts; and then wends its way down the mountain to the valleys—and from there inevitably to feed the ocean.

Our thanks to all the people whose hard work to make our translations possible follows the same pattern.

First, at the peak of the mountain, is the snow-treasure of the Asian Legacy Library’s free online database of ancient Asian books.  Millions of pages have been scanned or input in searchable form, under the leadership of executive director John Brady, over the last 35 years.  He is assisted by—just to name a few—Emma Lewis, Aisha Maria Nguyen, Christine Vimala Sperber, Christina Kasica, Joel Crawford, Arina Garcia, Osiris Luciano, Ben Ghalmi, Ven. Phil Baker, and Alona Stoliarchuk.

The massive labor of inputting all of the Tibetan works in the database over all of these years has been completed by the ALL Input Operator Team, headed now for many years by Ms. Sonam Lhamo.  At the National Library of Mongolia, the catalog team has been led by the Library Director, Ms. Bayarkhuu Ichinkhorloo; and the Project Manager, Dr. Sainbileg Byambadorj.  The new cataloging project at Gandantegchinlen Library is led by Ven. Munkhbaatar Batchuluun.

ALL’s Sanskrit materials are input at the Varanasi ALL Input Center, under the direction of Dr. Santosh Dwivedi; the Kathmandu ALL Input Center, directed by Drs. Miroj & Milan Shakya; and the Kerala ALL Input Center, directed by Dr. N.V. Ramachandran.  Thank you all for your endless work!  

We are very grateful for Aisha Maria Nguyen, who tirelessly searches every corner of the web for any and all Sanskrit materials that we may need input; as well as David & Nancy Reigle, for helping to define and provide us with the most accurate, high-quality editions possible of any work in the Sanskrit language.  We also thank Stanley Chen for his advice on Chinese-language sources.

The cataloging and input work cannot be accessed without the priceless subject cataloging by the Diamond Cutter Classics team dedicated to this 35-year effort, now led by Nicholas Lashaw, Ben Kramer, and Geshe Michael Roach—along with Dr. Word Smith, Oscar Leon, and Anatole Nguyen.  Nick & Ben also manage the DCC translator team, including all our fellow translators, and we would like to share deep gratitude with every one of them—you keep us going!

We are also infinitely indebted to all those who support the work of DCC, around the world; including our tireless and deeply dedicated sponsors.

We rely heavily upon the fine work of the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (BDRC) for obtaining original scans of the many source works our translations require.  The Head Librarian, Karma Gongde, has offered us years of wonderful service and advice; and BDRC Executive Director Dr. Jann Ronis and Chief Technology Officer Élie Roux continue to give all of us really excellent support.

The next step in translation is the manuscript editing, which for technical books like this one is always a massive effort.  We would especially like to thank Anatole Nguyen, Bets Greer, Nick Lashaw, and all the other editors contributing their time.  We are in awe of the work by the Diamond Cutter Press staff, who get all these translations out into the world—especially in the new ebook formats, and dedicated DCP app.  Thank you DCP director Rosa van Grieken, Ven. Elizabeth van der Pas, Katey Fetch, and master artist Gina Rivera.

Our entire translation team would have no central place to meet and conduct the many hundreds of translation sessions that books like this require, without the offices in Sedona, Arizona, supplied through years of effort by John Brady; Connie O’Brien; Tim Lowenhaupt; and Gail Deutsch.  Thanks as well to the wonderful staff of the Peach Tree Cafe of Rimrock, Arizona, for countless happy hours of meetings there.

We are also extremely grateful for the special sponsorship of the entire Diamond Cutter Classics translation team.  Recently, the expenses of our team have in addition been covered through the Good Night Book Club project, led by Lindsay Jilk and regional directors Inna Ivanina (Europe & North America); Tina Lyu (mainland China); Olga Van-Dick (Latin America); Nguyen Cong Binh (Vietnam); and Sugeng Shi & Xintian Ie (East & Southeast Asia).

Our grateful thanks to all of you, and to everyone else who has contributed to our work.  Your trust in us is a big part of the reason why we can complete projects—like the present volume—which require quite nearly a decade each.

The Diamond Cutter Classics Series

The book you are reading is one of over 100 volumes in the Diamond Cutter Classics Series.  For those who are interested in furthering their study of the great ideas of ancient Asia, we provide the following list of titles in the series.  They cover both original translations of the ancient classics; courses for modern life based upon them; and popular titles conveying the same information to a more general audience.
The titles marked with an asterisk (*) are completed and published, as of May 2026; printed and ebook versions are available from online booksellers worldwide, such as Amazon, as well as from the Diamond Cutter Press at DiamondCutterPress.com.  Publications from specific organizations listed, such as the Diamond Cutter Institute Global (DCIG), are available through those organizations.
For more information, to follow the translation of these great books live, or to make any inquiry about our work, please visit the Diamond Cutter Classics Series website at DiamondCutterClassics.com.  We would love to hear from you.
